articleTitle: ‘Apni maa ki kasam khao’: When Nana Patekar refused to hear Anees Bazmee’s Welcome script
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nana Patekar
description: Nana Patekar’s portrayal of Uday Shetty in Welcome remains one of his most loved performances. The film offered a refreshing change for fans who were used to seeing Nana play intense characters on screen.
body_raw: Veteran actor Nana Patekar, who died on Thursday morning at the age of 75 after suffering a heart attack, had a long and successful career in films and theatre. Over his decades-long career, he delivered several memorable performances, but his portrayal of Uday Shetty in Anees Bazmees Welcome 2007 remains one of his most beloved roles. Interestingly, the actor had initially turned down the role. During an appearance on The Kapil Sharma Show Season 2, Anees Bazmee recalled how he approached Nana Patekar for the role in Welcome. He shared, I called him and told him I want to meet you. He replied, Kaai ko? Why? I told him that I want to narrate a film to you. The director recalled that when he visited Nana Patekars house to narrate the script, the actor refused to hear it and said, Mujhe kahaani nahin sunni Aneez. Tum apni maa ki kasam khao aur batao ki mujhe ye karna chahiye I dont want to listen to the story, Anees. You swear on your mother and tell me whether I should do this film or not. However, Anees insisted that Nana hear the entire story, and the actor listened attentively to the three-hour narration. The director recalled that after hearing the script, Nana hugged him and said, Main kachhi mitti hoon. Tere set pe aayega, jis roop mein dhalna hai dhaal lena I am raw clay. When I come to your set, mould me into whichever shape you want. Also Read When Nana Patekar said he never found time to live Zindagi udhar ki hai On the show, Anees Bazmee also refuted industry rumours about Nana Patekar being difficult to deal with on sets. The entire film finished, and from his side, there wasnt even an issue the size of a dust particle. There is no work easier than working with him if you are honest with your script, said Anees. In a 2017 Filmfare interview, Anees also shared that Nana thanked him after the release of Welcome. After Welcome released, he told me, Anees, thanks for this film. Because my kids would always get scared of me. They never came near me. But Welcome changed my image in their minds. Now they come and sit on my lap. That was a very nice compliment for me. Nana Patekars portrayal of Uday Shetty in Welcome remains one of his most loved performances. The film offered a refreshing change for fans who were used to seeing Nana play intense characters on screen. His dialogue, Control, Uday. Control, became hugely popular and continues to be used by fans in everyday conversations. Another memorable line, Aloo lelo, kanda lelo, continues to inspire memes and jokes on social media.

articleTitle: When Vidhu Vinod Chopra tore Nana Patekar’s kurta on set, late actor spoke about ‘bad memories’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nana Patekar and Vidhu Vinod Chopra's infamous feud during Parinda
description: Nana Patekar once recalled his 'bad memories' from Parinda. Director Vidhu Vinod Chopra admitted that he tore the late actor's kurta on set.
body_raw: Late actor Nana Patekar was known to be quite temperamental on film sets and during one of his best-known films, Parinda, he had a scuffle with director Vidhu Vinod Chopra. In an interview, Nana recalled the memories of shooting for Parinda and said that he had bad memories from the film. Vidhu, in another interview, admitted that the argument on the set got heated up to such an extent that he tore Nanas kurta after they started swearing at each other. Nana Patekar has no control over his anger Nana Patekar shared his side of the story in an interview with The Lallantop and said that he did not like Vidhu Vinod Chopra. He accepted that even back then, he could not control his anger, which resulted in a tiff between the two. I dont like Vidhu Vinod Chopra. I have no control over my anger. I am still the same. That aspect of my life hasnt changed yet. Every scene has its setting, tune, and note, there is a way to talk. Now, I dont know if you watched Parinda, I was in the character, so when the director says, Lights, camera, clap, if you aggressively say action, it starts to linger in your ears. It echoes and hurts your ears. ALSO READ  Nana Patekars wife financially supported him son died at the age of 2 I never cried Nana said that since Vinod would yell out action, it would distract his performance just before the take. Let us be in our character please. What happens, when someone shouts, we forget the note that is required for the scene and unknowingly pick directors note. Just say action calmly. Let us get into our character and note. It is because of this we must have had a tiff. I have very bad memories of him Vidhu Vinod Chopra and his habits, he said. Nana then looked into the camera to address Vidhu directly. He said, Vidhu, please hear this. I want to tell you all this to your face and not behind your back. When Nana was asked about his last meeting with the director, he said, Every time I meet him, I wish it to be the last meeting. No, seriously, he added as his response made the studio audience laugh. Vidhu Vinod Chopra claimed Nana Patekar would hurl abuses Vidhu Vinod Chopra shared his side of the story during an appearance on the singing reality show Sa Re Ga Ma Pa in 2023 where he said that he was a very well-behaved young man from Kashmir but it changed after he met Nana Patekar. Vidhu said that Nana would hurl abuses at him when he directed the actor. I wondered how I would direct him at all. So, thats when I started abusing him back. I started swearing only because I had to direct Nana, he claimed. Vidhu shared that their first fight happened over food. Since the film was being made on a tight budget, all the actors were told to bring their own food, but Nana did not adhere to these directions. The first fight we had was over food, because he asked for lunch. I asked him, Ghar se nahi laaya khaana Didnt you get food from home?, he recalled. ALSO READ  Nana Patekar Death Updates Last rites to be held with full state honours, relatives gather at Goa hospital Sachin Tendulkar, Alia Bhatt, Kiara Advani mourn actor Vidhu Vinod Chopra tore Nana Patekars kurta Recalling their infamous scuffle where the director tore Nana Patekars kurta, Vidhu Vinod Chopra shared, Theres a scene in the film where Nana asks if he has tears in his eyes after his wife has died. Wed been shooting all day, and it was late in the evening. Nana declared that he was too tired to continue and that he was going home. I told him, Sure, you pay for the overheads then. He started swearing at me, I swore back, and in the scuffle, I tore his kurta. The cops on set said, Were here to protect you, and youre fighting among yourselves. Vidhu said that when they filmed the scene, Nana was just wearing a vest as Vidhu had destroyed his kurta. If you watch the scene, hes wearing a vest in it because his kurta had just been torn. The tears that you see in his eyes are real because wed just fought. Later, we hugged it out and he told me, I was nervous about the scene. Thats how Parinda was made, he shared. Nana Patekar won the National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor for his work in Parinda. Nana and Vidhu never collaborated again. About Nana Patekars death Nana Patekar died on Thursday, October 8, at his residence in Goa. He was 75. His son Malhar shared with The Indian Express, Yes, the information is true. I am in Pune right now and reaching Goa. I will come up with detailed statement. He died due to natural reasons.

articleTitle: Delhi Police bans gatherings at Rajghat after Congress announces protest against EC
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Delhi Police detain Congress supporters during a protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. (ANI)
description: Delhi Police bans gatherings at Mahatma Gandhi memorial after Congress announces protest against EC
body_raw: Congress and other INDIA bloc MPs began arriving for a second consecutive lunch meeting in Delhi on Thursday, with leaders expected to march to Rajghat afterwards to protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The meeting is being hosted by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge. Congress MP Kodikunnil Suresh said the Opposition would continue its protest and demanded Gyanesh Kumars resignation. He said the next strategy would be decided at the meeting, with Rahul Gandhi, Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other INDIA bloc leaders expected to lead the subsequent protest. The meeting comes a day after Delhi Police stopped an INDIA bloc march towards Jantar Mantar and detained several Opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi. Police said three FIRs have been registered over the protest, including allegations of assault and manhandling of police personnel, obstruction of government work and misbehaviour. Sources in the INDIA bloc told The Indian Express that MPs from the alliance will meet for lunch at Moets restaurant in Connaught Place, a day after a lunch gathering turned into a street protest. Those expected to attend include TMCs Derek OBrien and Mahua Moitra, CPIMs John Brittas, IUMLs ET Mohammed Basheer, CPIs P Sandosh Kumar, and Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Mallikarjun Kharge. The Samajwadi Party has sent two representatives for the lunch being hosted by Mallikarjun Kharge.Ghosi MP Rajeev Rai and Rampur MP Mohibbullah Nadvi will be in attendance. Rai confirmed to The Indian Express that the two MPs have been told by the party to attend the lunch. We are going there, said Rai. This comes a day after the SP skipped Wednesdays lunch and protest led by the Congress in Delhi demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumars resignation.

articleTitle: Texas executes 46-year-old, first US execution since Christa Pike survived lethal injection
articleFeaturedImageAlt: This photo provided by the Texas Department of Criminal Justice shows Jamaal Howard on Oct. 28, 2022.
description: Before the drugs were administered, Jamaal Howard apologised repeatedly to members of his victim’s family, who were watching from a room just a few feet from the execution chamber.
body_raw: Texas executed Jamaal Howard on Wednesday evening putting the 46-year-old to death for killing a convenience store clerk during a robbery in 2000. According to Associated Press,Howard was pronounced dead at 8.03 pm at the state prison in Huntsville after receiving a lethal dose of pentobarbital. He became the 30th person executed in the United States this year and the first since Tennessees failed attempt to execute Christa Pike last week. Before the drugs were administered, Howard apologised repeatedly to members of his victims family, who were watching from a room just a few feet from the execution chamber. He said, I wish that you accept my apology and I wish for your forgiveness.Im sorry for what happened. I wish you can learn to forgive me one of these days. He thanked his family and friends and said he was ready to find peace and the Lord. He ended his final statement by telling those watching to enjoy life. Jamaal Howards execution As the pentobarbital began flowing, Howard took several breaths and gasped. He then began making snoring sounds, coughed and resumed breathing heavily before the sounds gradually became quieter. Within 30 seconds he stopped moving and was pronounced dead 19 minutes later. Howards sister, who was among those watching the execution, became distressed and said, Get me out of here. And then officers helped her leave the witness room. How Jamaal Howard was caught Howard was sentenced to death for killing 42-year-old Vickie Swartout during a robbery at a convenience store in Silsbee, a small town about 100 miles northeast of Houston. Howard was 20 when he entered the store in 2000 and shot Swartout once in the chest. According to court records, he took 114 and a carton of cigarettes. Surveillance footage of the shooting was taken as evidence at his trial. His lawyers made several last-minute attempts to stop the execution, including arguments that Howard was intellectually disabled and that Texas use of pentobarbital posed concerns similar to those raised by the failed execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee. The Texas Court of Criminal Appeals rejected two late challenges over the states execution drugs. His lawyers also appealed to the US Supreme Court, arguing that he should not be executed because of an intellectual disability. The Supreme Court declined to intervene late Wednesday, clearing the way for the execution, as per AP reports. Latest development in Christa Pikes case Tennessee inmate Christa Pike was expected to die last week in a Tennessee execution chamber. Instead, after surviving two lethal injections, the 50-year-old death row prisoner has begun speaking from a hospital bed, leaving her family, lawyers and doctors shocked and raising questions about what happens now. According to one of her lawyers Randy Spivey, Pike was declared brain dead on Monday. Her team was told that life support would be removed the next day. But then on Tuesday morning everything changed. To the shock of everyone, including me, including her team and including the medical team, Christa woke up and began talking, her lawyer Spivey said at a press conference on Wednesday. Her first words after waking up was, Where am I? And who are you? Pike is now conscious but seriously ill. Her lawyers said she has pneumonia and a blood clot in one arm. She cannot swallow or move, while both her hands and arms are severely swollen. There is a long road to recovery, Spivey said. Her lawyer said she is angry and confused and is trying to understand what has happened to her. She has asked about her legal team and about the victim Colleen Slemmers family, Pike was convicted of killing in 1995. Despite her condition, Pike remains physical restraint to her hospital bed, her lawyers said. Medical staff have reportedly asked prison officials to remove the restraints, but those requests have been denied. What happened after the lethal injections failed Pike was taken from Tennessees execution chamber to hospital last Wednesday after prison officials administered two doses of the barbiturate pentobarbital, intended to kill her. Witnesses said Pike appeared to struggle after the first injection, with her heavy breathing. She was later taken to hospital after the second dose also failed to kill her. Spivey said that the execution attempt was cruel and torturous. He said seven needles had been used in Pikes left arm and that one appeared to have been bent when it was removed. Pike had also complained during the procedure that her arms were burning. Her lawyers had warned before the execution that finding a suitable vein could be difficult and that the process could cause her severe pain. Medical experts have since speculated that some of the drug may have entered tissue rather than a vein, that a vein may have ruptured, or that there could have been a problem with the drug itself. The exact reason for the failed execution remains unclear. A new legal battle in Pikes case While Pike fights to recover, her lawyers have begun preparing for another battle in court. During a hearing in Nashville on Wednesday, Judge IAshea Myles ordered Tennessee officials to preserve evidence from the attempted execution, including anything that was inside the execution chamber. Pikes legal team accused state officials of secreting away evidence that could become important if the state seeks to execute her again. According to her another lawyer Luke Ihnen, The motion that we filed is just to preserve evidence. Its the very first step of what will be a long legal battle we presume. Ihnen said the state had not promised that Pike would not face another execution. He argued that preserving evidence was therefore crucial to any future legal challenge.

articleTitle: ‘You don’t want me’: Alia Bhatt’s decade-old response to Ranbir Kapoor on love and career
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ranbir Kapoor and Alia Bhatt shared an interesting conversation about love, marriage, and career ambitions over a decade ago
description: Ranbir posed a thought-provoking question: “Would you get married to somebody who didn’t want you to act?” Without hesitation, Alia responded, “No.”
body_raw: Long before they fell in love and married, Ranbir Kapoor and Alia Bhatt shared an interesting conversation about love, marriage, and career ambitions. The discussion occurred during a promotional interaction with director Imtiaz Ali, when Alia was still finding her footing in the industry. Ranbir, who had already established himself as an actor, asked her, Whats your take on love? Right now, youre one of those girls whos like, My career is the most important. Before he could finish, Alia cut in, Ive never been in love before. Ranbir then posed a thought-provoking question Would you get married to somebody who didnt want you to act? Without hesitation, Alia responded, No. She explained, I probably wont act all my life, but I want to act for as long as I want. And if someone doesnt want that for me, then you dont want me. You want somebody else, and that person isnt here, sorry. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. A decade later, she married Ranbir in 2022, proving that staying true to her values was non-negotiable. But how do such conversations shape relationships, and what does this say about modern love and career ambitions? Love vs. career The importance of mutual respect in relationships Psychologist Rasshi Gurnani tells indianexpress.com that Alia Bhatts response to Ranbir Kapoors question - whether shed marry someone who didnt want her to act - highlights key aspects of relationships, especially the balance between love and career. She made it clear that if someone couldnt accept her work, they didnt truly want her. This reflects how important career compatibility is in a long-term relationship, Gurnani explains.   View this post on Instagram   A post shared by Alia Bhatt  aliaabhatt She emphasises that love alone isnt always enough mutual respect and understanding of each others ambitions matter too. If one partner expects the other to sacrifice their career for the relationship, it can lead to resentment and emotional distance. A supportive partner will encourage personal and professional growth, not limit it, she adds. Navigating relationships and professional success despite stereotypes Ranbirs question also reflects a common stereotype - that women often prioritise their careers over love. Gurnani notes that this assumption puts unnecessary pressure on women, making them feel guilty for being ambitious. Society still expects women to adjust their professional goals around relationships, while men rarely face the same scrutiny. These outdated beliefs make it harder for women to balance both aspects of their lives, she says. She points out that the healthiest relationships are those where both partners support each others dreams instead of forcing sacrifices. Career and love dont have to be at odds. A partnership thrives when there is equal encouragement and respect for personal choices, she adds. The power of personal choice in relationships Alia also mentioned that while she may not act forever, she wants that decision to be hers. Gurnani believes this underscores the importance of autonomy in a relationship. Especially in high-profile careers, where public and personal expectations can be overwhelming, having the freedom to make career decisions without pressure from a partner is crucial, she explains. A relationship should never feel like an ultimatum between love and ambition - it should be a space where both can coexist, she concludes. articleTitle: Sonali Kulkarni says a scolding on Taxi No. 9211 set launched lifelong bond with Nana Patekar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sonali kulkarni Nana Patekar death
description: In an exclusive conversation with SCREEN, actress Sonali Kulkarni spoke about her friendship with Nana Patekar.
body_raw: Actor Sonali Kulkarni, who has shared screen with veteran actor Nana Patekar is unable to process his loss. Nana, 75, died after suffering a cardiac arrest in Goa early on Thursday morning. Nana was at his family home when his health deteriorated. He was rushed to the hospital, where doctors tried to revive him for 45 minutes. The senior actor was declared dead at 520 am. In an exclusive conversation with SCREEN, the actress spoke about their friendship, and shared some beautiful memories from their time together. Sonali Kulkarni on Nana Patekars death Sonali and Nana have worked together in several Marathi films, and also shared screen space in Taxi No. 9211. Talking about their friendship, Sonali expressed her sadness and said, I still cant process what I have heard. What would it mean, Nana sir, not being with us? I dont know. I will take time to process this. We have worked on three projects Taxi No. 9211, Deool, which won the National Award for Best Film, and the third was Dr Prakash Baba Amte. Nana sir had also come for my book publication and spoke so fondly about it. I have seen the change - from me being scared of someone called Nana Patekar to him becoming so close to me and my family. I have had a beautiful friendship with him. I knew him well enough to the extent of making fun of him. He was a dear friend who had complete authority to call me anytime. Also Read Hours before death, Nana Patekar messaged friend at 230 am he was unwell   View this post on Instagram   A post shared by Nana Patekar nanapatekarfc I am happy for him he would have hated to be ill or hospitalized, and recover. He was always fit, passionate, and easy. Now, he will meet his dear mother, and all the farmers who committed suicide I am sure he will scold all of them. I am still not able to believe that we are talking about a man who won a Padma Shri award not being there, Sonali Kulkarni added. Sonali on working with Nana Patekar in Taxi No. 9211 Recalling a memory of working with him in Taxi No. 9211, Sonali said, I have seen him act in a very unscripted manner. I remember a scene from Taxi No. 9211 where I leave him, he comes to meet me, and the train has already gone. The kind of longing, pathos, and loss he had on his face said a lot about him as an actor. He was so funny in films like Welcome I always appreciated his comedy, and he enjoyed that compliment. He lived life on his own terms. One thing he did very nicely was give love, splurge money, and give compliments abundantly he never counted these things. She also recalled, Taxi No 9211 was my first film with Nana sir. I was a little scared because Id never worked with him. He and John Abraham were already shooting when I was called for a look test. When I wore the costume and exited my vanity van, Nana sir saw me. He said, Makeup utaar. Itna make up nahi chalega I just said impromptu, Maine makeup kia bhi nahi hai, sir My hairdresser said, Kisko jawab de rahi hai Take it easy. But it somehow set the tone for what our characters shared in the movie. It was a very nice nok-jhok throughout the film.   View this post on Instagram   A post shared by SCREEN ieentertainment Sonali went on to praise the actor and said, I got a lot of screen time to understand this person and actor. Hes so nice. He only wants some love and a chocolate. If you give a good shot, thats a good chocolate for him. He thrives on his co-actors performance. Hes a very performance-hungry actor. He told me about his journey, and I agreed with him. He had no looks or glamour that industry demanded, but thrived on his performances. His struggle was his struggle, but I enjoyed all three films with him. Our chemistry is totally different in all of them. Its hilarious in Deool. In front of other people, Im a decent wife. But in front of him, Im like, Tu kaun hai re? laughs. Sonali on Nana Patekars philanthropic work and memories from Deool Speaking fondly about Nana Patekar, Sonali also mentioned his philanthropic work and said, His heart was beating for the farmers who were thinking of committing suicide. He worked a lot through the NAAM Foundation. As much as he gave to society and farmers, he didnt get back the same amount of love. He never bothered about what he got in return he loved everyone unconditionally. He lived life without any worries, so it will take us some time to fill that void. She even recalled their bond when they worked on the Marathi film Deool. I have a beautiful picture of Nana sir when he came to meet me after I delivered my daughter Kaveri. It was hilarious. When we were promoting Deool, I was pregnant throughout the film. From the day he learned I was pregnant, first he got upset that I didnt tell him, then he took so much care of me. For the films launch, I had gone to PVR with my mother I was eight and a half months pregnant, and he was laughing. He said it was the first time he was posing with a heroine who was heavily pregnant. Deool was released on my birthday, and it was my first outing after my daughter was born he insisted and made sure I saw the film with my husband, Nachiket. Once he had come to see my daughter when she was two months old, he came in an auto. The auto driver didnt realize that Nana Patekar was sitting behind until Sir got off and asked him to wait for 30 minutes. When he figured it was Nana Patekar, he started trembling. When Nana sir was leaving, the auto-driver was unable to drive, so he told him, itna darta kyun hai, main chalau kya? and we laughed a lot. He has always loved me a lot, Sonali added as she got emotional. While the industry has been mourning Nana Patekars loss, the veteran actor will be laid to rest with state honors. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, CM Devendra Fadnavis, Amit Shah, Smriti Irani, and many others have also expressed their grief on Nana Patekars demise.

articleTitle: INDIA bloc lunch at Delhi’s Connaught Place, a hat-trick of SIR protest
articleFeaturedImageAlt: INDIA bloc, Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi
description: Sources said there'll be a protest after lunch, just like Wednesday. "It will be decided during lunch where we will protest and how," said a source
body_raw: A day after the INDIA bloc MPs lunch meet at Sagar Ratna in Janpath became the prelude to a dramatic street protest, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge has again invited Opposition MPs for lunch, this time at Moets in Connaught Place on Thursday. I invite your good self and all your members in both LS and RS for lunch today i.e. 8 October 2026 at 1.45 pm at Moets K-14, Outer Circle, Connaught Place, New Delhi, the invite from the Congress chief said. The back-to-back invites suggest that the Congress and its allies want to keep the pressure on the government as it steps up its campaign for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation over issues linked to the Special Intensive Revision SIR of voter rolls. Sources said therell be a protest after lunch, just like Wednesday. It will be decided during lunch where we will protest and how. More MPs and parties, including the Samajwadi Party, are scheduled to join us, said the source. The Samajwadi Party had skipped Wednesdays lunch. Protest timeline MPs of the INDIA bloc took out a march to the Election Commission on Tuesday. Police stopped them midway, but Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi and his sister and Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra managed to enter the Akashvani Bhavan premises and stayed there for hours. The sit-in, which the Congress said was an impromptu plan, eventually ended when police detained the siblings and the Congress leaders with them and shifted them to a police station. They were released later. On Tuesday, a lunch hosted by Congress chief Kharge became a rendezvous for INDIA bloc MPs, who then headed to Jantar Mantar. The Gandhis, Mamata TMCs Derek OBrien, CPIMs John Brittas and CPIs Sandosh Kumar were among the MPs who joined the protest on Wednesday. Police stopped them near Windsor Place, leading to dramatic scenes. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra lay on the road, clutching a copy of the Constitution. And Rahul Gandhi said the protests wont stop till Gyanesh Kumar resigns. The protesting MPs were detained on Wednesday, too, and later released. Wednesdays lunch plan will be attended by more MPs, and a much larger protest than Tuesdays may follow, sources in the Opposition have said. Also, the Cockroach Janta Party, which led the mega protest against paper leaks in Jantar Mantar in July, has called for another agitation on October 10. This will then be a week of protests in Delhi on the same issue. A unity message through lunch The lunch invites, besides becoming a rendezvous for Opposition MPs, are also sending a message of unity in the INDIA bloc. The Gandhis sit-in at Akashvani Bhavan had grabbed headlines, but left some Opposition parties grumbling. The Indian Express reported that some Opposition leaders felt the INDIA bloc protest on Tuesday became a Rahul Gandhi show because of the siblings sit-in while other Opposition leaders were detained. Senior Congress leaders then reached out to INDIA bloc allies and told them that the Akashvani Bhavan sit-in was an unplanned move. Some questions, however, remain. DMK, which broke up with Congress after the Tamil Nadu poll results, and AAP have stayed away from the INDIA bloc protests. The DMK, however, is blowing hot and cold, with one of its spokespersons praising Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday. The AAP faces a poll fight against the Congress in Punjab and will weigh its options before deciding on joining the INDIA bloc campaign. The Samajwadi Party joined the march on Tuesday, but was conspicuously absent on Wednesday. Party MPs have blamed Congresss poor coordination for this. The allies are also locked in a tussle over seat-sharing for the Uttar Pradesh election, but party leaders say that was not why they skipped Wednesdays lunch. They pointed out that many of them had left Delhi by the time the lunch was planned. Congress leaders, too, downplayed the Samajwadi Partys absence, saying that the lunch was planned late.

articleTitle: Nana Patekar saved Rs 1.5 cr to buy car, TV report changed his life; helped 77 lakh farmers
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nana Patekar
description: Nana Patekar helped over 77 lakh farmers, 51,000 disaster-relief families and supported nearly 5,000 widows through the Naam Foundation. The actor died on Thursday at the age of 75.
body_raw: With the death of Nana Patekar, fans lost their favourite actor. But for lakhs of people, they lost something more a ray of hope. Nana Patekar wasnt just an exceptional actor he had also become a source of hope for thousands of farmers and their families. Over the past decade, through the Naam Foundation, Nana helped over 77 lakh farmers, 51,000 disaster-relief families and supported nearly 5,000 widows through its widow welfare programme. It all began after the agricultural region of Marathwada in Maharashtra suffered devastating crop losses and farmer deaths in the summer of 2015. Maharashtra recorded 3,228 farmer suicides that year, with Marathwada alone accounting for 1,130. At the time, Nana was preparing to buy a luxury car. But one night, something he saw on television changed the purpose of his life forever. I had saved up Rs 1.5 crore with the intention of buying a new car. In the evening, I was sipping my drink and watching television. They were playing an interview with the family members of a farmer who had died by suicide. More than the mourning for the dead, I could feel their starvation. It was visible in their eyes, the actor told The Lallantop. The images and their pain unsettled Nana, who was living a vastly different, more privileged life at the time. Suddenly, the luxury he had been accustomed to felt meaningless. That scared me and made me think Why do I need this car? I decided to donate Rs 15,000 each to 1,000 farmers. However, my friend advised me to first meet the women who had lost their husbands before distributing the cheques, and that changed my life, he recalled. ALSO READ  Nana Patekar Death Updates Nana Patekar will be accorded state funeral, PM Narendra Modi remembers his intensity, individuality The experience prompted Nana, along with actor Makrand Anaspure, to start the Naam Foundation. Nana soon realised that handing out a single cheque of Rs 15,000 would not solve the larger problems faced by farmers and their families. What began as an attempt to help a few families soon grew into a much larger movement. Within two months, the foundation collected Rs 60 crore. And these are not some big industrialists, but the middle class and lower middle class people who helped, Nana said. Speaking to The Indian Express in 2016, Nana said the response had been overwhelming. We have set up an account for NAAM Foundation and in a day nearly Rs 80 lakh was collected. Its not true that people are not willing to help those affected, its just that theyre not assured if their money goes to the right place or not. But now they have faith in us that were doing honest work. Nana didnt just raise money to support farmers he also became their voice and advocate, repeatedly speaking about the circumstances that pushed many of them towards suicide. Speaking to NDTV in 2016, Nana said, When I see the farmers, I dont see them, I see myself. I understand why they take such drastic steps. I can see that they cannot afford to buy medicines for their family, food for their children, hay for their cattle. I can see their hopelessness, their shame in it. And for a man, that is a horrible feeling. He feels as if theres nothing left for him. He feels helpless, and thats when his hand goes towards the noose. He also urged people not to look away from the crisis and encouraged them to take responsibility for the welfare of farmers. Speaking at an event at Sanjay Ghodawat University, Nana said, When one accepts the reality of death, life becomes beautiful. Dont look away from farmer suicides or other crises. Face the hard truths. Thats when you start living with real purpose. Even as he continued to act, Nana maintained his association with the foundation and its work. In May this year, while addressing the Jal Kranti Parishad in Nagpur, he spoke about how the work had changed his own understanding of happiness. The happiness Naam Foundation has given me is greater than all awards and money from cinema, he said. Naam Foundation also made headlines for providing financial assistance to the families of Army and paramilitary personnel. Nana, in association with the Army, also participated in initiatives aimed at improving educational opportunities for children living in remote areas near the Line of Control following the abrogation of Article 370. For Nana Patekar, acting may have given him fame, awards and recognition. But his work beyond cinema gave him something he valued even more a sense of purpose. And for the millions who saw him as more than an actor, his loss is not merely the loss of a familiar face on screen. It is the loss of someone who chose to turn his privilege into a lifeline for others.

articleTitle: Nana Patekar’s wife financially supported him; son died at the age of 2: ‘I never cried’

The first thought that ran through my mind when Id see him like this was, What will people think about me, that my son looks like this. Imagine what a terrible man I am. My first worry was what people would say about me, not him, he said. Opening up about the tragic incident, Nana said, He died at the age of two-and-a-half, but he taught me so much. Hes the triggering point. It happens. he said and added that he never wallowed in grief. Ive always had a chin-up attitude. I dont cry. I cry only in the movies, and I do that for money, he said. Nana shared that after his son passed away, he started smoking excessively and would even smoke while in the shower. He recalled, At that time, I used to smoke about 60 cigarettes a day. I even smoked while bathing. But its a very bad thing. No one would sit in my car because of the foul smell. I never drank alcohol much but I smoked a lot. articleTitle: ‘Clean South Mumbai doesn’t mean clean Mumbai’: Bombay High Court’s reality check for BMC
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Mumbai filth bombay high court
description: Blasting the Mumbai civic body over 'filth' in the city, the Bombay High Court remarked that a 'clean South Mumbai doesn't mean entire Mumbai is clean'.
body_raw: Expressing displeasure over inadequate waste management measures across the city, the Bombay High Court on Wednesday pulled up the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation BMC, observing that cleanliness in some parts of South Mumbai did not mean similar steps had been taken across the city. Everywhere there is filth. Only because Worli is clean or South Mumbai is clean, or Nariman Point is clean, that doesnt mean entire Mumbai is clean, a bench of Justices Girish S Kulkarni and Neela K Gokhale orally remarked. The bench was hearing a plea raising concerns about waste disposal at the Kanjurmarg landfill, as well as garbage dumping on city streets and beaches. Once the system is in place and the citizens are also sensitised, one day will come that they will stop doing throwing garbage on streets. And we are looking at Mumbai to be converted into that kind of city where people themselves will go and throw everything in the dustbin. That will happen as we do it when we go abroad, because there are deterrents, there are cameras, but here in Mumbai there is absolutely no worry, Justice Kulkarni said. Even as senior advocate Anil Sakhare, appearing for the BMC, claimed that the situation had improved, the HC said it did not find a very high progress by BMC ward officers in addressing problematic areas related to health and hygiene at public places, hill slopes, pavements and streets. The HC sought a comprehensive affidavit detailing the steps taken by ward officers to ascertain the correct position on the ground, as well as measures taken on Gandhi Jayanti as part of the Swachhata Abhiyan. The judges also said that while travelling to the Maharashtra Judicial Academy in Uttan, Bhayander, they had noticed a plastic-strewn hill near a municipal school in Jogeshwari. Can we believe that this is Mumbai? Simple cleaning will take no more than one day. Nothing has happened. It is unbelievable, Justice Kulkarni said, seeking immediate corrective measures. The bench indicated that it may call ward officers from a few western suburban wards during the hearings, citing a lot of chaos related to waste management in their areas. The judges further indicated that they may soon visit the Kanjurmarg facility for a second round of inspection. The bench will also hear submissions on redressal of complaints regarding odour and environmental pollution from the site at the next hearing on October 22.

articleTitle: Amazon layoffs: E-commerce giant cuts jobs in Stores business amid AI spending push
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Amazon has cut jobs again as the tech industry continues to see layoffs and restructuring. (Image for representation/Magnific)
description: Amazon has cut a small number of jobs in its Stores business as the company continues to reduce costs while ramping up spending on AI.
body_raw: The tech industry is witnessing another round of layoffs. E-commerce giant Amazon, on Wednesday, October 7, said it was cutting some jobs in its Stores business, which works with its main website. The announcement comes close on the heels of Amazons biggest shopping days. The fresh round of job cuts at Amazon is part of a larger round of layoffs that began last year and affected around 30,000 employees, with the latest cuts reportedly affecting fewer than 1,000 employees. Reportedly, affected employees wrote in an internal Slack channel that they received emails informing them that their roles were being eliminated. According to a report in Business Insider, the channel with 37,000 members subsequently saw queries about severance, internal job postings, and if more notifications were in the offing. The messages on Slack indicated job cuts across multiple business units, including marketplace support, customer service, and engineering roles in retail business, in both India and the UK. The layoffs suggest that Amazons cost-cutting drive is continuing to reshape its corporate workforce. This is coinciding with the companys plans to dramatically increase spending on AI. The e-commerce giant slashed around 30,000 jobs in late 2025, and it is now looking at a mammoth 220 billion investment in data centres, chips, and other AI infrastructure. Meanwhile, an Amazon spokesperson confirmed that the company cut a small number of jobs on Tuesday, mainly in its stores business. The company said it had changed the structure of the business to better support its priorities and that the affected employees would receive support during the transition. The tech sector continues to see significant job cuts. Amazon is not the only tech giant cutting jobs while increasing its focus on AI. Meta laid off around 8,000 employees in May while moving 7,000 other workers to new AI-focused initiatives. Microsoft has cut 5,300 jobs so far this year, including 4,800 in July and another 500 in September. According to Layoffs.fyi, 131,382 tech employees have been laid off across 314 companies so far in 2026. In September, companies including Uber, Oracle, Microsoft, Workday, Apple, Expedia, Thinkific and Trustly announced job cuts. Uber announced one of the largest rounds, affecting about 3,300 employees, while Workday cut 525 and Microsoft 500. The cuts reflect a mix of restructuring, cost reduction and changing business priorities, with AI increasingly influencing how major technology companies organise their workforces.

articleTitle: ‘Baseless and misconceived’: Centre after Elon Musk claims ‘oligarchs’ blocking Starlink in India

description: The Centre said India’s satellite communication policy is fair and non-discriminatory. The statement came after Elon Musk alleged that “certain oligarchs” were blocking Starlink’s plans in the country.
body_raw: The Ministry of Communications on Thursday said Indias regulatory framework for satellite communication services is fair and non-discriminatory. This comes a day after SpaceX CEO Elon Musk alleged that certain oligarchs were blocking Starlinks plans in India. The Centre said that any suggestion of Indias regulatory framework for satellite communication services is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived. In a statement issued by the Press Information Bureau, the Ministry said that licences have been granted to three satellite communication companies and all are required to meet security conditions. Their security assessments are currently underway. Under the terms and conditions of license, every such licensee is required to demonstrate compliance with security conditions. This is aimed at ensuring that services provided meet various security requirements to ensure safety of all users and their data, the statement read. As and when this security process is completed for a licensed entity, it may proceed to the next step of seeking assignment of spectrum. At present, all the three entities are at broadly the same regulatory stage, the Ministry further said. At present, all the three entities are at broadly the same regulatory stage, the ministry said, calling claims of discrimination baseless and misconceived, a statement issued by the Press Information Bureau said. Earlier, Elon Musk had alleged on X that Starlink was being blocked to protect a monopolistic chokehold over Indian consumers. His comments came in response to a post arguing that Starlink could provide high-speed internet to underserved and remote communities. Unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people. You can guess who they are . This is a crime against the people of India - Elon Musk elonmusk October 7, 2026 Starlink has a licence to offer satellite internet services in India, but it is still awaiting security clearances and spectrum band allocation before it can start commercial services, Bloomberg reported. India has given satellite communication licences to three companies Starlink, Jio and OneWeb. None of them has yet switched on a full commercial service, Bloomberg said. At the India Mobile Congress on Wednesday, Starlink vice-president Lauren Dreyer said the company had built 20 gateway sites in India and developed India-specific security controls. She said Starlink was keeping Indian users data within the country and had invested in ground infrastructure to begin commercial services. Dreyer also said Starlink had been working with Indian regulators and industry stakeholders for five years. In June, she had denied reports that the approval process had been frozen, saying the company remained in talks with the government over its commercial launch.

articleTitle: Nana Patekar, the actor who redefined the tough cop, the psychotic villain, and Hindi cinema
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Film star Nana Patekar in film WAJOOD. Express archive photo
description: In a film industry that traditionally handed out important roles to clean-cut, chocolate-box heroes, Nana Patekar stood out in both appearance-- rough-hewn, son-of-the-Maratha-soil who could pull bombast with believability.
body_raw: Apne ko sochne ka allowed nahin hai, apne ko sirf ungli hai, ghoda kheechne ka. That single dialogue, in a 2004 film filled with snappy one-liners, cemented the image of the encounter cop in Hindi cinema. Scenery-chewing tough-talking cops had always been a Bollywood staple, with Amitabh Bachchan giving his Vijay in the 1973 Zanjeer the kind of smouldering swag we hadnt encountered before. But when Nana Patekar came swinging out in Shimit Amins 2004 Ab Tak Chappan, owning the part of a Maharashtrian cop in his own way, he became equally unforgettable. Patekar didnt have to act the part of his iconic Inspector Sadhu Agashe, based on a real-life figure  he just became the man so obsessed with cleaning up crime that all semblance of balance disappeared. His other, even more iconic line that everyone remembers, belongs to another cop he played in the 1991Yashwant  ek machchar saala aadmi ko hijra bana deta hai, delivered in that distinctive voice, rumbling out from the screen. Its one of those lines that became viral before virality was a thing, and it is as resonant today. In a film industry which had traditionally handed out important roles to clean-cut, chocolate-box heroes, Nana Patekar stood out in both appearance- rough-hewn, son-of-the-Maratha-soil-who-never-forgot-his-roots, as well as his ability to pull off bombast with believability. While he did lean into socialist-realist-middle-of-the-road cinema and broad comedy  Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman, Natasamrat, Welcome, his most striking streak saw him both in villain and hero roles, a tough divide to straddle  think Vidhu Vinod Chopras 1987 Parinda, in which Patekars psychotic crime lord Anna Seth ruled the roost, right up there with the 1991 Prahaar in which he plays the righteous armyman Major Pratap Chauhan, which he directed himself without making it a vanity project  interestingly, both films had Madhuri Dixit in the lead. ALSO READ  Nana Patekar Death Updates Nana Patekar will be accorded state funeral, PM Narendra Modi remembers his intensity, individuality Craggy looks and the crime landscape goes hand in hand, especially when it comes to hidebound casting choices in Bollywood  his first appearance that brought him recognition was Mira Nairs 1988 Salaam Bombay, in which he plays Baba, the hard-nosed drug dealer without an ounce of empathy for the women he pimps out. And he could have got typecast in such roles, especially after Parinda, a film which gave him a maniacal laugh as his signature mannerism. But Patekar refused to get boxed in. There were a clutch of other roles that he will be remembered for, especially the 1994 Krantiveer, in which he got to play his own brand of angry young man, fighting against injustice and corruption. And then there came a time when his film appearances dwindled- in 2018, he was faced with a sexual harassment charge- but even when he remained on the periphery, his unshakeable stature as one of the most popular actors in Maharashtra, ensured that his Ganapati celebrations continued to be crowded with netas and abhinetas alike. Speaking of, Patekars reluctance to join active politics was an enduring mystery. Given his constant, almost bordering on reverence, connection with Marathi manoos, he could easily have become a mascot of parties like the Shiv Shena that spoke to Marathi asmita, or of BJPs brand of nationalism. But he stayed far away, almost as if it was an area he didnt want to have anything to do with it. One of those reality-is-stranger-than-fiction things, even more ironic because he played, with great conviction, savvy king-makers in highly-political films like Prakash Jhas 2010 Rajneeti. His being at the right place at the right time ensured he became one of the busiest actors of the era. With his powerful performances, and stylised delivery, he cemented a place in the post-Satya late 90s world, giving us a clutch of characters we could enjoy and take home with us. Patekar never tried to be anything he couldnt channel with authenticity, even when doing loud nationalistic dramas like the 1993 Tiranga. Corrosive anger and a kind of derision, which felt, often, self-directed, as well as slung out at the audience, was a quality that ran through his highly-performative roles, the ones his fans loved him for. But he could also underplay. One of my most favourite performances of his in Bollywoods only true musical, the criminally forgotten Amol Palekar-helmed Thoda Sa Roomani Ho Jaaye, in which he plays the rare romantic hero who spreads joy without being cheesy. His other hatke part was in 1996 Sanjay Leela Bhansali Khamoshi, in which he plays the deaf-mute Joseph Braganza as a husband-and-parent, to Seema Biswas and Manisha Koirala respectively. This was the film in which Patekar channelled his softer, vulnerable side, and he was quite wonderful in it  no clutches of dialogue, just pure performance, the hallmark of a true actor.

body_raw: The Delhi Police has increased security deployment outside Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars residence following fresh threat inputs, officials said. However, in view of the latest intelligence inputs and ongoing protests in New Delhi, additional police personnel have been deployed outside his residence, a senior police officer said. Local district police have also been asked to increase the deployment of personnel. As protests are already underway in the New Delhi district, all security agencies have been directed to coordinate closely to prevent any untoward incident, the officer said. Z-plus is the second-highest security category in the country after the Special Protection Group cover for the Prime Minister and immediate family members. In the Z-plus category, around 50 personnel work in shifts with enhanced arrangements for the protectees residence and cavalcade. The enhanced security arrangements come amid protests by INDIA bloc leaders, led by Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, over alleged irregularities in the Election Commissions Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls. The Opposition has demanded Kumars resignation. Meanwhile, in one of the largest deployments of central forces for law and order duties in the national capital during a protest, the Ministry of Home Affairs has made 221 companies of the Central Armed Police Forces-around 23,000 personnel-available to Delhi Police from October 8 to 12. For the deployment, CRPF companies are being brought in from Jammu and Kashmir, West Bengal and Chhattisgarh. The additional forces will help Delhi Police manage the protests, secure key government buildings, and maintain law and order in central Delhi.

articleTitle: Nana Patekar served with the army during Kargil War for 60 days: ‘Part of Quick Reaction Team’

body_raw: Actor Nana Patekar, who passed away on Thursday, October 8, in Goa, was one of the most respected actors in the country. But apart from being a stellar actor, Nana was also a true patriot as he served the country during the Kargil War in 1999. Nana had previously discussed the subject in an interview in 2024 and shared that he was a part of the QRT Quick Reaction Team in Kargil. In a chat with The Lallantop, Nana recalled, George Fernandes was the defence minister and I wanted to go to Kargil. He was discouraged initially but after he had a word with the Defence Minister, he was sent to the warfront the same day. I was there for 60 days, he recalled. When asked what he was doing there, the actor said, Dont ask that. I cant tell you. He added, Eventually, I became a member of QRT, Quick Reaction Team. When I went, I was 76 kgs, and when I came back, I was 56 kgs, in just two months. Itna sa toh kuch hum kar sakte haim desh ke liye At least we can do this for the country. The report said that Nana had undergone intense training with the Maratha Light Infantry for his film Prahaar, which starred him and was also directed by him. The actor was quoted saying, Our greatest weapon is not the Bofors, nor the AK, but our jawans. About Nana Patekar death Nana Patekar died in Goa at his residence at the age of 75. His son Malhar told The Indian Express, Yes, the information is true. I am in Pune right now and reaching Goa. I will come up with detailed statement. He died due to natural reasons. His first award was the Best Supporting Actor award for Parinda. He won another Best Supporting Actor award for Agni Sakshi. His sole Best Actor award came for Krantiveer. articleTitle: Hours before death, Nana Patekar messaged friend at 2:30 am he was unwell
articleFeaturedImageAlt: nana patekar
description: The veteran actor's friend saw the late-night message only later and reached his Goa home around 4 am to find him sweating and gasping. He was declared dead at 5.20 am. Maharashtra will give him a state funeral in Pune.
body_raw: Actor Nana Patekar messaged a friend around 2.30 am on Thursday to say he was unwell. Less than three hours later, the veteran actor, one of the most distinctive performers in Hindi and Marathi cinema, was declared dead after a cardiac arrest, according to the hospital where he was taken. He was 75. Patekars son, Malhar, confirmed the death to The Indian Express. Yes, the information is true. I am in Pune right now and reaching Goa. I will come up with detailed statement, Malhar said. He added that the funeral would be held in Pune. Patekar will be given a state funeral today, Maharashtra Cultural Affairs Minister Ashish Shelar announced, citing his unparalleled contribution to Marathi theatre and to Marathi and Hindi cinema. The decision was taken by the state government headed by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Shelar said. Patekar was at the familys house in Goa. His friend saw the message late, Dr Shekhar Salkar, chief of the oncology department at Manipal Hospital, Goa, told the media. From information that we have received, he Nana messaged his friend that he was not feeling well somewhere around 2.30 am.that he was feeling uncomfortable.but since it was late night time, I think his friend could not get the message properly on time, Salkar said. He friend reached his Patekars house around 4 am when he was sweating and gasping.then his caretaker came here, took the ambulance and went to the residence, which is nearby. When our ER team went there, they started cardiac massage because he was totally unresponsive. By the time, they reached he was unresponsive, they started CPR in the house, shifted him on CPR to the hospital, but by the time it was too late and he was declared dead at 5.20 am, Salkar said. Nana Patekar was brought dead at our hospital at around 4.20 am. We tried our best to give him CPR, he added. Salkar said the hospital did not know whether Patekar had a history of heart trouble. It is a case of cardiac arrest, but the cause we dont know, whether he was a known case of cardiac or he was on any tablets.that we dont have an idea. Because he was brought dead, the hospital registered a medico-legal case. The police came and the body has been shifted to Goa Medical College for post-mortem. After the post-mortem, the body will be handed over to the relatives, Salkar said. Tributes poured in from the film industry, from politicians and from his fans. Fadnavis said, Nana was as great-hearted as he was great on screen. He gave Marathi and Hindi cinema an entire era. From Krantiveer to Natsamrat, there is no parallel to the powerful and accomplished range of his acting. His death is a great loss to the film industry. Fadnavis also recalled Patekars work with farmers and drought-hit communities through the Naam Foundation. Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant wrote, Shocked and deeply saddened to learn about the demise of veteran actor Shri Nana Ppatekar Ji. With his remarkable journey across theatre, Hindi and Marathi cinema, his powerful performances and distinctive artistry left an indelible mark on Indian cinema.My heartfelt condolences to his family, friends, admirers and the entire film fraternity. Actor Riteish Deshmukh wrote, I am shocked beyond words. Feels like a truck has hit me. Deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Nana Patekar ji. An actor par excellence, incomparable to anyone, he carved his place in peoples hearts with his own unique style and brand of acting. There wasnt a role or a character he couldnt perform. He aced it all - a larger-than-life hero, a terrifying villain or be it his poker-faced comedy. He was a hero off screen too, and worked tirelessly through his charity for the good of the people. Patekar started out in theatre and made his film debut with Gaman 1978. He rose to prominence with Parinda 1989, which won him the National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor. Krantiveer 1994 won him the National Award for Best Actor, and Agni Sakshi 1996 brought a third, for Best Supporting Actor. His other acclaimed films include Khamoshi The Musical, Ab Tak Chhappan, Apaharan and Raajneeti. He also showed a gift for comedy as the gangster Uday Shetty in Welcome 2007, a role he reprised in Welcome Back 2015. In Marathi cinema, he played a retired stage actor in Natsamrat 2016, one of his most celebrated roles. He also directed, wrote and starred in Prahaar The Final Attack 1991, and received the Padma Shri in 2013. Away from films, Patekar worked with drought-hit farmers through the Naam Foundation, which he set up with actor Makarand Anaspure in 2015. His career spanned nearly five decades.

articleTitle: Crispy, creamy and Indian: Malai kofta makes the World’s Top 10 Deep-Fried Dishes
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Malai Kofta, with crisp, rich koftas served in a creamy gravy, has become a familiar favourite at Indian restaurants and celebrations.
description: Malai Kofta has ranked No. 10 among TasteAtlas' 50 best deep-fried dishes in the world. A chef explains the history of this indulgent Indian dish and shares tips for making crisp, soft koftas and a silky gravy at home.
body_raw: Indian gravies are known for their creamy texture and spice, and few dishes make a deep-fried vegetablecottage cheese dumpling feel as indulgent as malai kofta. The soft, rich koftas, usually made with potatoes, paneer and other ingredients, are paired with a creamy gravy to create a dish that has long been a favourite on Indian restaurant menus and at celebratory meals. Beyond being the go-to dish at weddings and other gatherings, Malai Kofta now has another reason to be celebrated - it ranked No. 10 among Taste Atlass 50 best deep-fried dishes in the world. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. But behind its familiar, restaurant-style appeal is a dish with an interesting culinary history, and getting it right at home isnt always as easy as it looks. We asked a chef to share the history of this lip-smacking dish, and he also shared common mistakes people make when preparing it at home.   View this post on Instagram   A post shared by TasteAtlas tasteatlas History of Malai Kofta Malai kofta, to Chef Ishijyot Surri, Executive Chef and Founder of Mulk  SJI Hospitality, is a beautiful example of how food travels but eventually finds a new home. The kofta has roots in Persian and Central Asian culinary traditions, where it was traditionally made with pounded or minced meat. As these influences entered the Indian subcontinent and became intertwined with Mughal-era cooking, the kofta began taking on a distinctly Indian identity. Over generations, Indian kitchens adapted it to paneer, potato and vegetables, pairing the kofta with rich, aromatic gravies, he says. Malai kofta has a unique contrast of textures. Unlike many other classic Indian dishes that derive their rich texture from ghee, Sukhi Singh writes in her blog, malai kofta is fully vegan-friendly with a cashew base chock-full of healthy plant-based fats. And this is what makes it special crisp outside, almost melting within, surrounded by a silky gravy, says Chef Ishijyot. How to make restaurant-style malai kofta at home For restaurant-style results at home, Chef Suri believes the biggest secret is restraint. Keep the potatoes dry, grate the paneer finely and use very little cornflour, just enough to bind. Too much binding is why homemade koftas often become dense. The gravy also needs patience. Cook the base properly, blend and strain it. Use cashew and cream to create the body rather than heaviness. Following this, the kasuri methi and cardamom should be added as gentle finishing notes, he says. He also mentions common mistakes people make when preparing Malai Kofta at home. People mostly use wet potatoes, excessive flour, fry at the wrong temperature and almost drown the dish in cream. Sharing a tip, he says that it is important never to leave the koftas sitting in the gravy. The kofta and gravy should meet only at the last moment. Apart from malai kofta, the other dishes that made to the cut are Chicken 65 at rank 32 and Papdi Chaat at rank 40. articleTitle: India is signing bilateral investment treaties again. What changed after the 2016 reset?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Modi UAE treaty
description: India is revisiting its bilateral investment treaty framework after terminating dozens of pacts a decade ago. New agreements show greater flexibility on when foreign investors can seek international arbitration.
body_raw: A decade after unilaterally terminating multiple bilateral investment treaties BITs signed between 2016 and 2017, India has kicked off a significant overhaul of its investment treaty network. There are now expectations that the government would seal 4-5 agreements by year-end. Following the 2025-26 Union Budget announcement of undertaking the review of 2016 model BIT to make it more investor-friendly and attract sustained foreign investment, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Monday said the new BIT template would be approved by the Cabinet shortly. However, a number of fresh agreements, including with Saudi Arabia, Israel and the UAE, have already been signed keeping this new framework in mind. So, what is a bilateral investment treaty? A bilateral investment treaty or a BIT is an agreement between two countries which spells out the rules governing private investment in either nation from companies in the other. As such, they help promote, protect, and provide clarity to foreign investments. Amid sharp slowdown in net inflow of investments, the new pacts show the countrys readiness to a higher degree of flexibility when it comes to exhaustion of local remedies ELR - a rule which requires a foreign investor to seek redress in the host states domestic courts or administrative bodies before bringing an international claim. While India agreed to a three year ELR rule in its BIT with the UAE in 2024, an investor from Saudi Arabia, as per the deal finalised last week can approach international arbitration in two years. The deal comes amid expectation of Saudi investment in Indian refineries. Cautious approach to BITs This comes as trade partners have even sought a one year ELR rule under the treaty, but India has not agreed to such demands so far. After the conclusion of BIT with Saudi Arabia, a government official said India-Saudi Arabia BIT would provide legal certainty and protect the interests of investors of either country in the territory of another. The 2-years exhaustion of local remedies requirements provides investors enhanced access to the Investor State Dispute Settlement ISDS mechanism. At the same time, the agreement carefully balances investor protection with the States right to regulate in the public interest, thereby preserving sufficient policy space for sovereign governance, the official said. Investor State Dispute Settlement is a mechanism designed to protect foreign investments by allowing investors to bring claims against host states for alleged treaty violations. Indias insistence of a five-year ELR after terminating BITs in 2016-17 had been a major challenge flagged by foreign investors. Prabhash Ranjan, Professor at Jindal Global Law School said that India should have a uniform treaty practice on this issue. The model BIT should provide for a one to two year period for pursuing local remedies, and no more. Furthermore, the overall limitation period to bring an ISDS claim should not be too strict. It should be something that is workable for foreign investors, Ranjan said. State vs investors While several partners have criticized Indias decision to terminate scores of BITs unilaterally, balancing state and inventors rights has been a key challenge for India and several other developing nations after a spate of adverse orders from international courts. India was not the only country to terminate BITs in the past. Developing countries like South Africa and Indonesia also did the same to preserve policy space as the decisions by international tribunals were seen to be encroaching on domestic policy space. Jos Miguel Ahumada and Ha-Joon Chang in their research report titled A New International Economic Order said that the Global South economies face significantly tighter constraints and often their efforts to establish regulatory frameworks that compel technology transfer from FDI to domestic productive networks are obstructed by the legal architecture of BITs and ISDS mechanisms. Ahumada and Chang pointed out that there is compelling evidence that the tribunals tend to favor foreign corporations over state rights, impose substantial legal defense costs on states, establish strict limitations on national policy space, and generate a regulatory chilling effect on host countries. Indeed, recent actions by the rich economies are proving the limitations of the current system. The EU has withdrawn from the Energy Charter Treaty because its ISDS is considered incompatible with the Paris Agreements. Similarly, the United States and Canada removed ISDS clauses from the USMCA United StatesMexicoCanada Agreement, and New Zealand has opted out of ISDS provisions in the CPTPP Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership. In this sense, a new order should institutionalize this wave of exits and reestablish the national level as the primary scale for regulating FDI foreign direct investment, the reports said. Arbitration at the heart of BIT debate RV Anuradha, Partner at Clarus Law Associates said that rule mandating specific time periods for exhaustion of local remedies can be a way for the government to effectively assess the nature of the dispute and try to resolve genuine investor grievances - thereby pre-empting the move to ISDS arbitration. But any provision such as this in our BITs will be effective only if there is a fast-tracking of investor disputes. Such fast tracking will need a statutory basis. Practically speaking, it would not be possible to deal with investor concerns based on the investors nationality. The judicial process will treat all investors on equal footing. A foreign investor cannot claim preference to be heard by Indian courts based on a BIT provision, Anuradha said. What we need, therefore, is a statutorily backed mechanism which is available for all investors - regardless of whether they are Indian or foreign investors, Anuradha said, adding that timely grievance redressal can in fact potentially have a dispute preventionmitigation effect. Before the 2016 model, India had signed bilateral investment treaties with 83 countries based on the model BIT of 1993, and as amended in 2003. Out of these, 74 were ratified. Among these 74 BITs, notice of termination was issued to 68 countries with request to re-negotiate based on the 2016 model, according to government data shared in the Parliament in March 2023. Since the revised 2016 model, India has signed BITs with Belarus, Kyrgyz Republic, Investment Cooperation and Facilitation Treaty ICFT with Brazil, the UAE and Uzbekistan, a Lok Sabha reply from April 2025 showed. In the BIT with the UAE, the window for exhaustion of local remedies was reduced to three years from five. A Bilateral Investment Agreement has also been signed between India Taipei Association and Taipei Economic and Cultural Centre, it said.

articleTitle: JD(U) vs JD(U) in MLC polls: How a feud handed Prashant Kishor a chance
articleFeaturedImageAlt: JD(U) vs JD(U) in MLC polls: How a feud handed Prashant Kishor a chance
description: Mokama MLA Anant Singh, who has a long-standing rivalry with JD(U)’s official candidate Neeraj Kumar, has thrown his weight behind Jan Suraaj Party’s Anuj Singh.
body_raw: Even as elections to eight MLC seats in Bihar are set to be held on October 23, the Patna Graduate constituency has emerged as the most closely watched contest not because of a conventional face-off between political rivals, but due to the fight effectively turning into a JDU versus JDU battle. The Janata Dal Uniteds official candidate, Neeraj Kumar, is facing an open challenge from fellow party MLA from Mokama, Anant Singh, who is campaigning for the Jan Suraaj Party JSP nominee, Anuj Singh. Neeraj, who is also the JDU chief spokesperson, is seeking a fourth-consecutive term from the Patna Graduates seat. But Anant, who shares a long-standing rivalry with Neeraj, has been campaigning for Anuj. What has made the situation particularly awkward for the JDU is the reluctance of its top leadership to intervene. Both Neeraj and Anant are from Mokama and their rivalry predates their association with the JDU. In the 2015 Assembly elections, Neeraj had unsuccessfully contested against Anant, who won as an Independent. Singh, who has faced several criminal cases, had also drawn criticism from Neeraj in the past. Now, with Singh openly campaigning against the partys official candidate, the JDU has so far stopped short of taking disciplinary action against him. The rebellion has given JSP founder Prashant Kishor an opening. Kishor has thrown an open challenge to Neeraj, saying the JSP would withdraw its candidate if former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar issued an authentic video message backing Neerajs candidature. If Neeraj Kumar gets Nitish Kumar to issue an authentic video message supporting his candidature, we will withdraw our candidate from the Patna Graduates seat, Kishor said, stressing that the video should not be AI-generated. Kishor smells chance Kishor has stepped up his campaign, making education the centrepiece of his pitch. He has also promised job guarantees, drawing on his campaign in Bankipur, where he had promised to facilitate at least 10,000 private-sector jobs over five years. The JSP believes Anants support could significantly alter the dynamics of the contest. With Union minister Rajeev Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh and JDU national working president Sanjay Kumar Jha refusing to intervene and Anant fully backing us, who knows, we could do a Bankipur in the Patna Graduate seat, a JSP source said. For Neeraj, the contest is a sharp departure from his earlier elections. The Patna Graduates seat, covering parts of Patna, Nalanda and Nawada and around 80,000 registered graduate voters, was virtually a cakewalk for him in the 2008, 2014 and 2020 MLC elections. Neeraj, once considered close to Lalan Singh, is now fighting the election without the organisational backing he might have expected. A source close to him said the partys inaction over Anant Singhs campaigning was difficult to understand. It is not rocket science to understand who is goading Anant. It is also surprising that the party has not initiated any disciplinary action against him for anti-party activities. However, Neeraj has faced party infighting in past elections and still won, the source said. Anant, for his part, remains unapologetic about backing the JSP candidate. Neeraj has opposed me in at least four of my elections despite being a fellow JDU member. I faced the Ladma Arms Act case because of him. There is no question of backing out of my support for the JSP candidate, he said. Not my battle Jha, meanwhile, sought to distance himself from the dispute. It is a matter concerning areas under the Lok Sabha seat Munger of Lalan Singh. It is up to him to see how the matter can be sorted out, he said. Lalan Singh, however, also ruled out direct intervention. We heard what our national working president said. But Anant has his own concerns. It is not for me to intervene in such matters, he told reporters. There are, nevertheless, factors that could work in Neerajs favour. Anants influence remains largely confined to pockets of Mokama and parts of Nawada. Neeraj has also played a significant role in enrolling graduate voters. Besides Lalan Singh, senior JDU leaders, including Jha, Bihar minister Shravan Kumar and Nishant Kumar, have campaigned for him. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary is also expected to campaign for Neeraj in the final phase. The RJD has fielded Dilip Kumar, who contested the previous election as a Congress candidate. The internal JDU battle is creating confusion among voters and will definitely help our candidate. It also tells a lot about the internal problems within the NDA and JDU, RJD national spokesperson Subodh Kumar Mehta said. The elections to four Graduates constituencies - Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut and Kosi - and four Teachers constituencies - Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut and Saran - cover 30 districts and around 150 Assembly constituencies. A total of 164 candidates are in the fray across the eight seats, the results for which will be declared on October 27. The Bihar Legislative Council has a strength of 75.

articleTitle: ‘I settled 8 wars’: Trump renews Nobel Peace Prize bid ahead of Friday announcement
articleFeaturedImageAlt: US President Donald Trump renewed his pitch for the Nobel Peace Prize
description: Donald Trump renewed his Nobel Peace Prize pitch, claiming he settled eight wars and prevented global destruction during remarks at the Oval Office.
body_raw: US President Donald Trump renewed his pitch for the Nobel Peace Prize at the Oval Office, claiming he had settled eight wars and done stuff that nobody else has ever done. Trump made the fresh bid at the Oval Office on Wednesday afternoon, ahead of Fridays announcement of the coveted award by the Norwegian Nobel Committee. Ive done stuff that nobody else has ever done. Im not bragging, Im just telling you the facts. No president has probably ever settled any wars. I settled eight wars, Trump told reporters here. He then said that it would be a great discredit to the Nobel Committee not to honour him. They have a reputation for maybe not giving it to people like me. But, whether I get it or not, I have done far more. And I think it would be a great discredit to them. And Im not saying that out of scorn, Im saying that when you settle eight wars, and nobodys never, the US president said. He said that his peacemaking efforts were continuing and hinted that he was on course to settle another war, apparently referring to the US-Iran conflict, which has now entered its eighth month. Look, Obama got it, and he didnt do anything, says Trump Trump then moved on to criticise former US President Barack Obamas 2009 Nobel Peace Prize win, claiming Obama did not know why he had received the award. Look, Obama got it, and he didnt do anything. He still doesnt know what he got it for. He got it when he got elected, right at the beginning, and he had no idea why he got it, the US President said. He further recalled that last years Nobel laureate, Venezuelas Maria Corina Machado, handed her peace prize to him during a meeting at the Oval Office. Last time they gave it to a young lady whos a fabulous person, and she said she didnt deserve it, that I deserved it, and she gave it to me, the US President said. I was very honoured to receive it indirectly. Last time by the recipient, who said nobody in history deserves it more than President Trump, he said. POTUS then repeated that in the past year he had settled eight wars, secured the return of all hostages and used tariff threats to prevent conflicts.
