He said, I congraulate every one on this very first institution of innovation and theater. There is such an illustrious team Vijaya Veda, Dr Laagu, Tendulkar, Sulbha Deshpande, Arvind, Vrundavan Dandawatre. They are all one voice. I remember when I did Tendulkars first play the writer, director, all of them together were such a brilliant group. Their plays would go on for weeks at an institute. I appreciate that they bring all artists in the city together this institute will only flourish this way. In theatre and cinema, anything new gets appreciated, so always seek newer ideas. Your values wont change you, in fact, others will inculcate them sic. Also Read Nana Patekar, who commanded every screen, dies of cardiac arrest at 75 VIDEO  Goa Actor Nana Patekar attended and addressed the Samraat Club International installation ceremony in Dona Paula. Full video available on PTI Videos -   - Press Trust of India PTINews October 4, 2026 He also said, We all have to go someday. I dont know whether I will be here tomorrow or not. Every persons life will eventually reach that point. But before that happens, I have to ask myself am I able to do what I want to do? I have to ask myself whether I have tried. If my world is limited to my children, my wife, and my home, then what is my purpose? I have to give something back here, dont I? I like some of Narendra Modis ideas, and I dont like some of them. We should learn to say that. He does not always get everything wrong. What is a protest ultimately? It is when something does not feel right to us, when something is not happening the way it should. The definition of protest should change with age, shouldnt it? Dont speak in public with anger and abuse. Among friends, we may fight, grab each other and say things to one another, but that should remain between us. When we speak publicly, there has to be some basic decency. That has to be maintained otherwise, there is no meaning to it. Expressing grief, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis recalled the actors contribution to cinema and said, Nana was as great-hearted as he was great on screen. He gave Marathi and Hindi cinema an entire era. From Krantiveer to Natsamrat, there is no parallel to the powerful and accomplished range of his acting. His death is a great loss to the film industry. Nana Patekar transitioned from theater to the screen in 1978 he made his acting debut in films with Gaman. His film Parinda 1989, brought him the National Film Award, and Krantiveer 1994 earned him the National Award for Best Actor. His other projects include Agni Sakshi, Khamoshi The Musical, Ab Tak Chhappan, Apaharan, Raajneeti, Welcome, Natsamrat, and many more. Nana Patekar was also a director and writer. He was honored with a Padma Shri in 2013. Nana Patekars very recent appearance on the big screen was in Housefull 5, ORomeo, and Subedaar. On the web space, he was seen in Prakash Jhas show Sankalp in March this year.

articleTitle: 3 FIRs against Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka for ‘assaulting cops’ during Delhi protest
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra during INDIA bloc MPs' protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Windsor Place near Jantar Mantar, in New Delhi on Wednesday. (ANI Photo/Amit)
description: Both leaders were detained by the police for the second consecutive day during their protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar
body_raw: At least three FIRs have been registered against Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra for allegedly assaulting officers during the INDIA bloc MPs protest on Wednesday, Delhi Police sources have said. According to police officers, the FIRs were registered under sections pertaining to assault and obstructing police officers in conducting their duties. Wednesday was the second consecutive day when opposition MPs had protested, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner CEC Gyanesh Kumar. It was also the second consecutive day when Rahul, Priyanka and several other senior leaders were detained by the police. Lunch, protest, then detention The MPs had initially boarded a bus after lunch at Sagar Ratna restaurant in Connaught Place, but were stopped from going towards the Election Commission office near Windsor Palace by security forces. The parliamentarians led by Rahul Gandhi got off their buses and attempted to begin an impromptu sit-in. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra lay on the road with a copy of the Constitution, shielded by other MPs and party workers, while her brother stood guard, pushing back the police personnel attempting to break up the protest. This is my sister, the LoP had shouted at the police. A scuffle followed with the police, with some purported videos showing Priyanka Gandhi allegedly elbowing a woman police officer. In another clip, a police officer was allegedly kicked in the back by a protester. Constable Ankit Kasana also sustained bruises during the scuffle with the MPs. Is it my mistake, doing my duty, he told mediapersons later. Both the LoP, Priyanka Gandhi, and other Opposition leaders were eventually pushed into police buses amid allegations that the police used force on them. Trinamool MP Mahua Moitra sustained injuries to her face and hands, and was seen showing her counterparts that she had been left bloodied. The Congress has called for more protests at state, district and block levels on Thursday.

articleTitle: ‘No one believed in Hanuman Ansh, declared flop on day 8’: Producer on miracle that saved it
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Hanuman Ansh sequel update by Anupriya Nagar
description: In an exclusive conversation, Anupriya Nagar shared an update on the second instalment of Hanuman Ansh, she even spoke about start a production house.
body_raw: After successfully running for 62 days at the box office and earning over Rs 425 crore, Hanuman Ansh has emerged as more than a film - it has become a moment in Indias cinematic history, a lot like Jai Santoshi Maa that once gave competition Sholay back in the day. The devotional film, based on Neem Karoli Baba, was made on a budget of a shade less than Rs 2 crores. Amid its massive commercial success, SCREEN spoke to its co-producer, Anupriya Nagar, about its trajectory at the ticket windows, and how that Hanuman Ansh has been planned as a trilogy. It has also become the catalyst for Anupriya, who is 22, to write a book on it and set up a production house. Anupriya Nagar on the success of Hanuman Ansh The film, which started its journey with Rs 10 lakh collection, has emerged as the best return on investment seen in the Hindi film industry in decades. Talking about this feat, Anupriya shared, To be very honest, I didnt become a part of this film for it to become a financial project, for me it was an emotional project. There were no expectations. Even the team never expected the film to do so well. We just wanted the devotees and kids to watch the film and learn about Indian culture. The first two weeks, the film didnt work at all, and on the eighth day, the industry declared the film a flop. We became a little nervous and thought, If devotees are not supporting us, how will the rest of the audience watch the film? Also Read A 21-year-old gave up Zurich job to fund Hanuman Ansh, earned Rs 50 cr on Rs 50 lakh share We knew that this film would only work through word-of-mouth since it had no known faces, a first-time director. While Maharajji is the biggest superhero of the film, from a general perspective, this was the thought. Even before I came on board, people never believed in the film. They asked how this film would work. While people were craving this kind of content, not too many films were made like this. When the screens went down from 300 to 30, we were told that only a miracle could save the film from being pulled down at theaters. I couldnt sit with my hands tied, I did whatever I could, Anupriya Nagar added. I gave all my savings for Hanuman Ansh Talking about how the film has been loved for its simplicity, Anupriya shared they initially thought of releasing the film on OTT. Hanuman Ansh doesnt align with the formula in which films are made these days. Its a simple period film, so its normal to question if the audience will relate to it. Everyone thinks before the release they have made a Mughal-e-Azam, its only when it releases do you understand how the film is received. There were also conversations about taking the film to OTT first. But we wanted to build a community, so we went with a theatrical release, she said. Giving up a job opportunity at Zurich was not the only risk Anupriya took she even invested her lifes savings in Hanuman Ansh. When Ragini Sona told me they needed funds, I decided to give what I had saved. I used to work during Christmas holidays and get extra salary so I could invest it I thought I would go to Zurich and live a comfortable life. Later, I used all of those savings for Hanuman Ansh, Anupriya shared. Sharing what she plans to do with the profit of Hanuman Ansh, she said, After Hanuman Ansh, people started calling me Chasmewali Producer bespectacled producer fame has come my way. But I am still the same. Everyone is telling me to get a holiday house with the money Hanuman Ansh has made. I am not going to gift myself anything. I have everything I want. It is only because of the people that the film is doing so well, so I just want to give it back to society. I want to help children and provide proper education and health facilities and I am in the process of starting my foundation. It will be my greatest gift. I celebrated the films success with my family and we all went to Kaichi Dham after a really long time. It was the best celebration. Hanuman Ansh would be a trilogy While Anupriya shared how the film and political industry have come to support the film now, she recalled a conversation she had with Premanand Maharaj. Anupriya shared, I met Premanand Maharajji after the film released and was doing well. I thought he wouldnt recognize me. But he was so happy to see me. He told me, main bohot khush tha ke aap aaye, film ke pehle, aur uske baad bhi. Apne santo ke liye bohot bada kaam kiya hai He told me I am very happy you came here before the film and after its success. You have done a great service to the spiritual leaders. It was such a huge thing to say. Sharing that Hanuman Ansh is supposed to be a trilogy, Anupriya added, I am writing a book on my journey with Hanuman Ansh and with Maharajji. I am in the process of establishing my own production house, where I can tell these wonderful stories. We will take the film to OTT now. Regarding the rest of the stories, even 10 films will not be enough for it. From the very beginning, we thought of making a trilogy, this is the first part. We have to sit and plan the second film, and now the responsibility is greater. We need to decide the timeline. Right now we are trying to do justice to the film. The numbers are increasing, and we are still trying to reach more and more people. The film has now gone global as it was released overseas on September 11. Hanuman Ansh was released in theaters on 7 August 2026.

articleTitle: Ted Lasso season 4 review: Jason Sudeikis and women’s team coach each other
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ted Lasso season 4 review: Jason Sudeikis returns to coach a women's football team.
description: Ted Lasso season 4 review: Jason Sudeikis' titular character returns to Richmond to coach a women's football team -- only to learn life lessons in return.
body_raw: Ted Lasso season 4 was an afterthought. Ted Lasso, having hung his UK boots and relocated back to his home turf of the US, is summoned back to Richmond, this time to coach a womens team. The premise was enough for the Indian audience to churn out memes of Ted Lasso delivering the climactic sattar minute speech in the womens locker room, a la Shah Rukh Khans hockey coach Kabir Khan in Shimit Amins 2009 seminal Bollywood sports drama Chak De India. But Ted Lasso is no vindictive, defamed coach trying to get back his lost glory. Hes just an average American Joe pulled back to a land thousands of miles apart to do what he does best - live. Fish out of water - two times over Co-creator and lead actor Jason Sudeikis had signed off as the titular buoyant football coach after season 3 of Apple TVs Emmy Award-winning show before he had an epiphany. As he returns to Richmond to coach its second-division womens football team - he faces resistance, particularly from their coach Alice Chilton Tanya Reynolds. And just like that, its like season 1 all over again. A soccer player roped in to train a British football team? Heck, he doesnt even like tea. But thats not important. Whats key here is how Lasso makes his way in, not by blending into the British way of life, but by dialling up his infectious, charming self. Hes inherently a team player, so divisions - whether theyre nationality or gender - have little bearing on his being. Not that he vowed to, but instead of relishing tea, he ends up getting Rebecca Welton Hannah Waddingham, the uptight AFC Richmond owner, addicted to shortbread biscuits. Coach Alice is too messed up and amour-propre to exchange her head position with a man - however ebullient and chivalrous he may be - for the womens football team. The way episode 1 ends, one does feel that the male wagon of creators and showrunners - Sudeikis, Bill Lawrence, Brendan Hunt, and Brett Goldstein - are using the audiences unabating love for Ted to shortchange Alice. Take it or leave it with a shrug of shoulders - that seems to be Teds tone, even though hes trying to be as unobtrusive and friendly as possible. So, when Alice caves in - and doesnt accept Teds farewell gift - it feels like feminism just walked backwards by a few steps. Its natural then that Alice feels a strong surge of jealousy when she sees Ted warm his way into the womens locker room - even though it was she who handheld him and Coach Beard the first time, making them close their eyes and wait until the women are dressed. Ted isnt even the most abhorrent of men who mansplain women into learning football. Hes considerate, patient, and most crucially, in touch with his feminine side. He urges his players to cry out their emotions - theres crying in football - and not bottle them up like Alice. Hes also as conscientious - cleaning up a bar with the women after they make a mess out of it during an impromptu brawl with a bunch of men did Kabir Khan and the Chak De India girls clean up the McDonalds? No. Learning from life - and everything that it throws at you But theres something that Ted is bound not to get as a man. In an affecting and strikingly relevant episode, we see members of the team deal with personal crises - from taking up odd jobs to make ends meet since second-division womens football doesnt exactly pay handsomely, or doubling up as a mother of two because your husband treats her ambition as inconvenience. Teds go-to magic word - Believe - doesnt exactly cut it here, as thats easier said than done. It then takes an Alice to step in and make a tiny addition to get the women all pumped up - Believe. and win. Its this added adrenaline and call to action that season 4 of Ted Lasso needed to make it as effective as its predecessors. The individual arcs of all the women players couldve made for a far more impactful and well-rounded season than wasting it on side plots like a secret investor buying their way into AFC Richmond. Not all side plots are as tepid though. Rebecca giving new love a chance, before sabotaging it, and then giving it yet another lease of life, couldve made the most patient of men run out of the virtue. But it makes the audience comfort her like Phil Dunster does in his memorable cameo. Roy Goldstein and Keeley Juno Temple are arguably the Ross and Rachel of Ted Lasso, though even the Friends pair couldnt pull off the downright adorbs football commentary scene with a makeup set, including what Roy calls a squishy pencil makeup brush, as Keeley corrects him. Also Read - When Jeffrey Archer called Bollywood bunch of thieves for stealing his bestseller plots The strength of Ted Lasso, thus, remains in the quiet, slow change it brings about, just like its central character and his constant nudging towards a fair, equal, and kinder world. The audience is invited into the heads of all characters as they struggle with their feelings. But when they finally let them out to the ones theyve been wanting to confide in, were gently drawn out. That not only prevents the show from getting preachy, but also helps us come to terms with leaving the beloved characters to their lives, if this is indeed the last season. A voiceover from the grave - one for the ages - by the shows old guard surely helps you tug it into the bed like its a child you want to kiss goodbye - I think of each name as a comfortable music in the mouth. tending, as all music does. towards silence.

articleTitle: Digger: Tom Cruise and Hollywood are done saving the world; time to embrace the end
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Tom Cruise in Digger
description: Digger could be seen as the age-old story where a wealthy industrialist has destroyed the world but unlike those stories which often ended with someone saving the day, there are no heroes anymore.
body_raw: Tom Cruise has been single-handedly saving the world for decades, and now, with Digger, he has single-handedly destroyed everything. Of course, this is not Tom Cruise the person or the actor, but the characters he has played that have dominated Hollywood, and by extension, the rest of the world. Digger can easily be labelled as Toms best performance, but it also makes you wonder how the American soft power that Tom peddled for decades is now a thing of the past and they seem to have accept the fact in the film. Tom Cruises Digger is a cartoonish, but equally conniving villain Alejandro Inarritus Digger has Cruise playing Curtis, an actor whose daughter is the center of his life. And in the play within the film, he is playing Digger, the oil magnate who one might imagine runs the Illuminati and controls everything that goes on in the world from his garish mansion. Presidents of major countries are at his beck and call as Digger makes decisions that destroy the world, without any supervision whatsoever. Such characters have traditionally been cartoonish villains in films, and here too, Cruise plays Digger like a caricature. He knows how to gaslight the audience into feeling that they are equally responsible for the climate crisis that was triggered by him. He puts on an exaggerated performance just so he can trap them in a web of self-reflection and get away with his crimes, one more time. Digger is the obvious villain of the story here for he brought the entire world to a halt. But the film goes a step further when it introduces Jesse Plemons Kenny, who is a wolf in sheeps clothing. Kenny reveals he is Diggers nephew in the third act and this is when we also find out that the play is based on a real-life chapter from recent history where millions of people lost their lives and livelihoods, all because of Digger and the many governments who chose to look away while he was running the show. Kenny, like his uncle, gives an impassioned speech where he paints Digger as the biggest villain there ever was, and claims that he is producing this hyper-realistic play so the people can process their grief, with a dash of laughter. Just like Digger made the people self-reflect, Kenny does too, and thats where he, like his uncle, wins again. Kenny is fooling the world, just like Digger It is only at the end of the film that we actually see the reality of how the climate apocalypse triggered by Digger has changed the reality of the world. The cities are literally falling apart as people walk around the ruins of a civilisation wearing giant masks that cover their faces, for all the necessities of life have ceased to exist. And Kenny, the nephew of the disgraced oil tycoon, residing in his ivory tower, is using his immense wealth to put on expensive plays. Kenny thinks of himself as a supporter of the arts in a world where human life cant survive anymore he has fooled the people into believing that he is the good guy, the man who hates Digger just as much as anyone. Of course, Kenny is self-aware and knows that he cant be seen singing praises of his uncle anymore, even though he was the guy who set him up for life rather, set the family up for generations. So he does the next best thing turn into a hypocrite and dictate how the public must feel. Putting up plays is not his sole job duh, as he also runs some secret Mossad-like organisation where he can trace any individual in any part of the world but Curtis, who is playing Digger, cant see through the farce of this man because, just like the rest of us, he too is busy putting food on the table and worrying about his familys survival. Kenny, meanwhile, is gathering more wealth through the many businesses he continues to run as the world slowly comes to an end. Industrialists have been running the world ever since the Rothschilds formalised banking systems. Digger, surely, does not tell us anything new in that department, but it surely does tell us that we, the masses, are too gullible for our own good. What else could explain our fascination with the uber-wealthy people who have the resources to actually help millions around the world, but choose not to? And no, this isnt about them doing charity work to keep their conscience clean, but about taking steps to stop harming the world. ALSO READ  Is Chris Hansen a hero or villain? Primetime explores his god complex to get to the answer Digger could be seen as the age-old story where a wealthy industrialist has destroyed the world but unlike those stories which often ended with someone saving the day, there are no heroes anymore. The Tom Cruise-like saviour who could have ended the tyranny of someone like Digger no longer exists, because the situation is so far in the dumps that the Kennys of the world are now pretending to be our new saviours.

articleTitle: Death toll in Delhi building collapse rises to 4, more feared trapped
articleFeaturedImageAlt: delhi building collapse
description: Delhi building collapse in Seemapuri: Four-storey building developed cracks during Tuesday's earthquake
body_raw: A day after a four-storey building collapsed in Northeast Delhis New Seemapuri Wednesday afternoon, police officials said one more body was recovered in the wee hours of Thursday, taking the death toll to four. On Tuesday, when Delhi experienced earthquake tremors in the evening, the building had developed cracks, officials said. Rescue operations still continue at the site, with officials saying that they fear that 1-2 people might still be trapped. A Municipal Corporation of Delhi MCD official said that 75 of the debris has been cleared but it might be a couple of hours more before the area could be fully cleared The collapse took place near the Idgah Machhli Mandi area. Four fire tenders were rushed to the spot. Within minutes of the collapse, residents started pulling people out of the rubble and took them to hospitals. The building measured 225 sq ft. Some people have been rescued and sent to hospitals, but we suspect that two to three people are still trapped under the debris. They are talking. rescue operation is underway, DCP Northeast R P Meena said. In a statement, the MCD described the structure as a ground-plus-three-floor building located in a jhuggi jhopri area on about 25 square yards of DUSIB land. It said the building was around 20-25 years old and occupied. The building stood next to the mosque in the densely packed locality. The boundary wall of the mosque also collapsed in the impact, while walls of an adjoining building were damaged, the MCD added. Officials said demolition work was being carried out in the adjoining building. Three- and four-storey structures surround the mosque on three sides, leaving little open space. Much of the debris fell inside the mosque compound, said local residents. The building was owned by Anwar. His family members who stayed on the first three floors included his wife Salma, 50 son Rehman, 28, and wife Sakeena his daughters Nushrat and Ameena as well as Nushrats three-year-old son Abdaan. While Anwar, Ameena and Rehmans wife were not at home when the building collapsed, Nushrat is stuck under the debris, officials said. A tenant, also named Sakeena 35, lived on the upper floor, according to relatives.

articleTitle: Why Elon Musk has slammed ‘certain oligarchs’ for Starlink’s India launch delay
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Elon MUsk, Starlink
description: Starlink’s India launch remains delayed amid ongoing security concerns. Elon Musk has accused “certain oligarchs” of blocking the satellite internet service.
body_raw: Billionaire Elon Musk, whose satellite communications company Starlink is yet to receive final approvals from Indian authorities to launch its services in the country-more than a year after securing necessary licences from the government-has blamed certain oligarchs for blocking Starlink in the country. He called it a crime against the people of India. Unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people. You can guess who they are. This is a crime against the people of India Musk said in a post on social media platform X. Starlink in India would enable high-speed, affordable Internet connectivity for those who cant afford current prices or who dont have a connection at all he added in another post. However, in a clarification in response to Musks allegations, the Indian government said the countrys regulatory framework for satcom services is fair and non-discriminatory. The Government has put in place a fair and non-discriminatory authorisation framework for all telecommunication services, including satellite communication services. Under this, telecom licences have been granted to three Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite services based on non-geosynchronous satellite orbit based satellite communications, as part of its commitments to enable provision of satellite communication services in India. Under the terms and conditions of license, every such licensee is required to demonstrate compliance with security conditions. This is aimed at ensuring that services provided meet various security requirements to ensure safety of all users and their data, the Ministry of Communications said in a statement without explicitly naming Musk. Security assessment as part of this process is currently under way in respect of all the three licensees. As and when this process is completed for a licensed entity, it may proceed to the next step of seeking assignment of spectrum. At present, all the three entities are at broadly the same regulatory stage. As such, the suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived, it added. Musks comments come amid continued regulatory delays to Starlinks launch in India, primarily over security concerns, even though the company says it has tailored its operations to meet the countrys security and regulatory requirements. At the India Mobile Congress Wednesday, Lauren Dreyer, vice-president of Starlink Business Operations at SpaceX, said, Weve built our Starlink operations specifically for India in recognition of Indian security requirements and other regulations, establishing controls at every layer for India and keeping India user data within India. Were standing ready to serve India once India is ready. Were ready to work with the government, ready to work with operators, ready to work with industry to this end. Were ready to help Prime Minister Modi achieve his vision of 100 connectivity throughout India, she added. Satellite communication services rely on an array of satellites in orbit to offer connectivity to homes and businesses on the ground. They are an alternative to ground-based communication, called terrestrial networks, such as cable, fibre, or digital subscriber line, and they dont require wires to transmit data. Starlink operates the worlds largest satellite constellation, with around 7,000 satellites in orbit. Why the delay in Starlinks India launch Musks Starlink is among the operators that have secured GMPCS global mobile personal communication by satellite licences and other statutory approvals needed to launch satellite communication, or satcom, services in the country. Others who have received it include Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb, and Jio Satellite Communications Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Jio Platforms. Jeff Bezos-owned Amazon Leo is also in contention for a licence. Last July, Starlink had received what industry executives said was the last regulatory approval needed to launch the service in India from the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre IN-SPACe granted authorisation to the satcom company for its satellite constellation. Before that, the company had received an operator licence from the Department of Telecommunications DoT, three years after first applying for one. Despite the regulatory clearance, it is understood the government is yet to green-light formal launch of these services over security concerns. The concern particularly stems from anxieties around foreign satcom operators potentially bypassing Indian gateways to offer their services, an event when the government might lose control over the service. In satellite communication, Indian gateways refer to Satellite Earth Station Gateways physically located within Indian territory that interface between space-based satellite constellations and domestic terrestrial telecom networks. All traffic originating or terminating in India must process entirely through these local ground facilities. The delay in Starlinks final security clearance comes as Reliance Jio is building a sovereign low earth satellite constellation in India, and is considering a 1,6001,650 satellite network costing an estimated 1015 billion. DoT guidelines for satcom companies Last May, the Department of Telecommunications DoT had released guidelines for satellite communication companies. The norms call for companies to set up local manufacturing, data localisation, use domestic navigation systems, implement a blocking mechanism, and cooperate with law enforcement agencies. According to the guidelines, satcom companies will have to share with the government a year-wise phased manufacturing plan aiming at indigenisation to a level of at least 20 of their ground segment of the satellite network that is established at the end of five years after launching commercial operations. The companies should also ensure provisioning of NavIC-based positioning systems in their user terminals on best effort basis, along with a transition plan to implement NavIC in a time-bound manner by 2029. NavIC, or Navigation with Indian Constellation, is Indias regional satellite navigation system, similar to GPS, which is a global system developed by the US. Companies will have to provide real-time monitoring to ensure that no user traffic originating from, or destined for India is being routed through any gateway outside Indian territory. They will also have to submit an undertaking that they will not copy and decrypt Indian telecom data outside India. Operators would need to implement service restrictions to any individual, group of subscribers or certain geographical areas during hostilities, the guidelines said. These companies will have to seek separate clearance from security angle for voice service and data service. Satcom operators will also have to ensure that their data centres are based within the geographical boundary of India and shall make provision to provide Domain Name System resolution within its territory.

articleTitle: When Nana Patekar said he ‘never found time to live’: ‘Zindagi udhar ki hai’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nana Patekar
description: Commenting on the life of an artiste, Nana Patekar said, “Humari zindagi udhar ki hai na (Our life belongs to others, doesn’t it?)". He said the applause will stop the day one dies.
body_raw: Veteran actor Nana Patekar died at the age of 75. The actor, who dedicated nearly five decades to the film industry, first took up acting to grab the attention of his father, Dinakar Patekar. Initially juggling theatre and work, Nana eventually chose to pursue theatre full-time. The actor, whose death has shocked the entire country, once admitted that he had never really found the time to live for himself. Speaking in an interview once, the actor said, Humari zindagi udhar ki hai na Our life belongs to others, doesnt it?. Nana Patekar Death Updates Actor Dies at 75 in Goa, Death Reason, Tributes and Funeral Updates Speaking to The Lallantop just two years ago, Nana, who was 73 at the time, said, Our life belongs to others, doesnt it? When do we ever get to live our own life? We never really found the time to live for ourselves. Today, we are living the life of one character tomorrow, it will be another character. Maybe the day we finally stop and pause, we will realise it. We will think about ourselves. But that day never comes. It becomes a habit. He added, I have said this before-when you are performing on stage, theres darkness in front of you, isnt there? We are on the stage. And perhaps that is simply the nature of an artist we have to find our own happiness in that darkness. And the echo of applause becomes an addiction. We cant break away from it. He concluded, That is life for us. The day that voice-the sound of applause-stops, that is the day we die. After that, you wont cast us anymore. You wont even take us. While many actors enter the profession driven by their passion for acting, for Nana, the journey began with a much more personal motivation he simply wanted to impress his father. He once participated in a school play about the saint Valmiki. I was one of his henchmen, Nana Patekar recalled. His performance had such an impact on him that his father travelled from the city to their village to watch him perform. I assumed that my father loved my brothers more than me. After all, I wasnt very good-looking. But when I did the Valmiki play, even though I was playing the henchman, my father travelled to our village to see me perform. I thought this was a great way to pull his attention towards me, he said. That journey continued until his final years. Nana Patekar remained actively involved in films over the years. From The Vaccine War in 2023 to the Marathi film Ole Aale in 2024, Vanvaas in the same year, Housefull 5 in 2025 and ORomeo in 2026, the veteran actor continued to remain a familiar presence on screen. He was last seen in the Anil Kapoor-starrer Subedaar, where he made a special appearance as Nana Waghmare. articleTitle: ‘Bhakti is getting lost’: How Durga Puja at Delhi’s CR Park has changed
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Chittaranjan Park, Chittaranjan Park Durga Puja, durga puja, durga puja celebrations, Durga Puja pandals, delhi Durga Puja pandals, delhi news, India news, Indian express, current affairs
description: From door-to-door chanda to corporate sponsorships, CR Park’s Durga Puja has grown into a large-scale operation — and not everyone is happy with what that has brought.
body_raw: Devyani Rudra, 60, recalled her earliest memories of Durga Puja from Chittaranjan Parks J Block helping her mother, cutting vegetables for bhog - the traditional community meal offered to the Goddess and distributed as prasad - and joining the neighbourhoods cultural programmes. Earlier, only 50 to 100 people would turn up for the pujas, she said. Rudra and her family moved to CR Park from Delhi Cantonment in 1975. Back then, it was known as the East Pakistan Displaced Persons Colony, established as part of the governments rehabilitation efforts for those uprooted by Partition. It housed only 15-20 families, mostly government officials. The celebrations later shifted to Mela Ground and the Shiv Mandir in 1976, now known as Kali Mandir. Five decades later, Durga Puja has become a much larger affair. The colony now has nearly 50,000 residents and hosts around 10 major community pujas, besides several private household celebrations. Lakhs of visitors from across Delhi-NCR descend on the neighbourhood. But as the festivities kick off on October 16 this year, some of CR Parks old residents feel the celebrations have moved away from the intimacy of a festival once centred on the community. What does a puja cost? At Kali Mandir, the annual Durga Puja budget is around Rs 1 crore to Rs 1.5 crore, while other major CR Park pujas have annual budgets of around Rs 80-90 lakh. The temporary pandal and tent structure at Kali Mandir alone costs around Rs 25-30 lakh, said Jaya Ray, a member of the Kali Mandir Society and its Durga Puja organising committee. The bhog operation costs Rs 30-40 lakh. The kitchen serves at least 7,000 people within about four hours on a single afternoon, with 300-500 kg of food prepared on 10 wood-burning stoves, Ray added. The five-day cultural programme, featuring dance, music, orchestras and other performances, costs another Rs 5-10 lakh. The Mandir committee also spends on printing, decoration, logistics and the salaries of priests and support staff who work through the year. At other venues, the scale is similarly large. Narayan Dey, secretary of the Mela Ground Durga Puja Samiti, said during the festival, the committee runs a daily langar serving around 10,000 meals. Its pandal has expanded to around 180 feet by 85 feet. Saurav Chakravorty, General Secretary of K-Block Cooperative Ground, said that they see a daily footfall of around 1-1.5 lakh people during the festival while cultural shows feature artists who fly in from Kolkata and Mumbai. Who pays for the celebrations? Ray said the celebrations were once funded almost entirely by residents. In the 1970s and 80s, the celebrations relied entirely on personal resident contributions. We would go door to door collecting chanda. Back then, the pandals cost Rs 1 lakh or Rs 2 lakh. But now, that will not cut it, she said. The major shift came in the early 2000s, when corporate houses and public sector undertakings began sponsoring the pujas. At Kali Mandir, corporate sponsorships now account for around 70 of the Durga Puja budget, according to the organising committee. Individual resident contributions make up the remaining 30. Sponsors are given visibility through stalls at the venue, LED screens, backdrops and flexes at the gates. At Mela Ground, Dey said the committee puts up panels within the pandal area carrying the names of sponsors. The ecosystem behind the pujas The scale of the celebrations has also created a wider ecosystem around the festival. Kali Mandirs idol-making workshop, which began in 1972, produced only around three to five idols a year in its early days. By the late 1980s and 1990s, production had risen to around 100 idols. Today, the Kali Mandir workshop, along with its second workshop at Chandralok Cinema in G Block, produces more than 800 idols every year for puja committees across Delhi-NCR, other parts of India and overseas. The idols are made on commission and sold to other puja committees, providing the temple with an additional source of income. While commissioned idols generally cost around Rs 40,000 to Rs 80,000, larger and more elaborate custom installations can cost more than Rs 10 lakh. The workshops also employ artisans and other workers, allowing traditional idol-making expertise to remain within the community. At K-Block, Chakravorty said the idols are constructed completely in-house, from scratch, inside the pandal. At Mela Ground, 250-300 artisans and staff come from outside Bengal to craft the idols on site. But what is lost? The transformation has also brought criticism from some long-time residents. Rudra called it a commercialisation of the festival. Earlier, there were just a small number of food stalls. And that too, they were set up at no cost. But now the puja venues charge you in lakhs to put up stalls. She added that cultural programmes used to be conducted by the locals, and then film screenings. But now, if you see, popular reality show stars and singers fly in for the event, and local talent is no longer promoted. It is more entertainment than the puja itself. The growing crowds and high footfall have also raised safety concerns, Rudra claimed. The bhakti of the festivities is getting lost, and the present generation no longer understands that, she added.

His performances never felt like acting, but life unfolding on screen. A remarkable artist whose contribution to Indian cinema will be remembered for generations. Heartfelt condolences to his family and loved ones. Om Shanti. Nana Patekar made his film debut with Gaman 1978 after starting out in theatre. He rose to prominence with films such as Parinda 1989, for which he won the National Film Award, and Krantiveer 1994, which earned him the National Award for Best Actor. He went on to deliver acclaimed performances in films including Agni Sakshi, Khamoshi The Musical, Ab Tak Chhappan, Apaharan, Raajneeti, Welcome and Marathi film Natsamrat. He was also a director, writer and recipient of the Padma Shri 2013. Patekar also displayed a different side of his acting in the hugely popular comedy Welcome 2007, in which his portrayal of gangster Uday Shetty became one of his most remembered performances. He reprised the role in Welcome Back. In Marathi cinema, Patekar delivered one of his most acclaimed performances in Natsamrat 2016, playing a retired stage actor. He also appeared in Dr. Prakash Baba Amte-The Real Hero, for which he received the Filmfare Award for Best Actor Marathi. He was also a director, making Prahaar The Final Attack in 1991, besides acting in and writing the film. Patekar received the Padma Shri in 2013 and was a recipient of three National Film Awards. Patekar was also associated with social work through the Naam Foundation. His death marks the end of a career spanning nearly five decades in Indian cinema.

articleTitle: 2026 Chemistry Nobel: Mirror-image molecules and the chemistry of life
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026, Nobel Chemistry Prize 2026, Chemistry Nobel 2026, Nobel Prize Chemistry winners 2026, Nobel Chemistry winners, Chemistry Nobel winners, Nobel Prize in Chemistry explained, Nobel Chemistry history, first Nobel Prize in Chemistry, Nobel Prize Chemistry discoveries, Nobel Prize Chemistry predictions, Nobel Chemistry from India, Chemistry Nobel Prize winners, Nobel Prize winners 2026, Nobel Prize Chemistry facts, indian express, express explained
description: Certain molecules exist in two forms — like your left and  right hands. But the building blocks of life use only one. The scientists Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai showed how to make just that form in labs — something crucial for the manufacturing of medicines.
body_raw: Certain molecules exist in two forms, each a non-superimposable mirror image of the other - like the left and right hands of human beings. Chemically, the two forms are the same in the sense that they are composed of the same set of atoms, connected in the same order. The difference is only in the relative three-dimensional arrangement of those atoms, such that one happens to be the mirror image of the other. This structural asymmetry, called chirality, becomes particularly interesting in biology. Many of the fundamental molecules in biology, like the amino acids that make up proteins or the sugars in DNA, appear in only one form. The mirror image versions of these amino acids or the sugars do exist, but they are rarely used in these biological settings. This preference for homochirality in life forms has intrigued scientists for long. This years Nobel Prize in Chemistry has been awarded to two scientists, Henry Kagan and Kenso Soai, for demonstrating how this homochirality can emerge. The normal chemical processes used to produce a chiral molecule results in the production of both forms, called enantiomers. Kagan developed a way of manipulating these processes in such a manner that one form was produced in much greater proportion than the other. Soai took a step further and designed the first chemical reaction in which only one of the enantiomers was produced. Outside of biological processes, such a result had never been achieved. The first breakthrough The propensity of biochemistry to prefer one particular enantiomer over the other was initially thought to be something unique for life forms. After all, when chiral molecules were produced in laboratories, a mixture of both enantiomers was obtained in almost even proportions. However, way back in the early 1900s, German chemist Willy Marckwald had been successful in carrying out a chemical reaction in which the proportion of the yields of the two enantiomers was slightly asymmetric. Marckwald had used a catalyst - a chemical that speeds up the reaction without itself getting consumed into it - which itself was chiral. And this had led to one mirror-image form being produced more than the other. However, subsequent attempts to increase the asymmetry in the yields of the two enantiomers remained unsuccessful. Besides, scientists still did not understand how the use of a chiral catalyst was affecting the reaction in a manner that one enantiomer was produced in greater quantity. It was Kagan, working in the 1980s, who eventually answered these questions. Before him, it was believed that there was a linear relationship between the catalysts chirality and the proportion in which the two forms of the product were produced. In other words, if the catalyst itself contained a disproportionate amount of one form, this would get reflected in the proportions of the final product as well. Kagan was able to show that this was not true, and that much greater asymmetry in production could be achieved even if the catalyst was only mildly chiral. In the process he was also able to demonstrate the internal dynamics of how this was happening. The next step This breakthrough created a new excitement in the field. While studying one of the chemical reactions that had produced one particular enantiomer in large quantities, Soai realised that there were significant similarities in the catalyst used and the final product. That prompted him to explore autocatalytic reactions - chemical reactions in which the final products themselves act as catalysts. None of the autocatalytic reactions known at the time Soai started experimenting with them in the 1990s were known to produce asymmetric formation of enantiomers. After about a decade of trying, he finally succeeded in carrying out an autocatalytic reaction that resulted in the production of one particular enantiomer, which then formed copies of itself in a self-replicating process. The final product contained 99.5 of one enantiomer, a result comparable to the kind of preference seen in biological processes for a particular version of a chiral molecule. Mysteries of life The work of Kagan and Soai has demonstrated that homochirality can be obtained in the laboratory as well. It was not exclusive to nature. Their work does not solve the origin of the puzzle of life - how biological processes themselves preferred homochirality. But it did open up fresh avenues for scientists to try and understand the chemistry of life. Possibly the biggest practical implication of their work has been in the pharmaceutical industry. Many drug molecules are chiral, and it matters immensely which particular enantiomer has to be used. This is because the human bodies prefer only those enantiomers. The other variety of molecule might not just be ineffective, they can even be harmful. Before this Nobel Prize-winning work showed how one single enantiomer could be produced, pharma companies had been manufacturing the drug molecules as a mixture of both enantiomers, and then the desirable enantiomer was separated through a separate process. This was an expensive, wasteful and often technically difficult way of achieving the final result. The asymmetric synthesis of a particular enantiomer, as shown by Kagan and Soai, is already being used widely by the pharmaceutical industry. This is relevant for the manufacturing of all other substances that are meant to interact with living organisms, including flavours, fragrances and agricultural chemicals like pesticides.

articleTitle: What if your cooking gas came from water? Meet India’s hydrogen stove
articleFeaturedImageAlt: hydrogen stove
description: As LPG supply chains face fresh vulnerabilities, companies are experimenting with hydrogen-powered stoves — but high costs, efficiency and the lack of long-term data remain hurdles
body_raw: Vikash Kumar grew up in a house where cooking was always cumbersome-it meant either getting bundles of firewood or cow dung arranged, or running around for LPG cylinders. For the 33-year-olds household in Bihars Vaishali district, the LPG crisis in the aftermath of the West Asia conflict magnified the problem severalfold the family had to shell out Rs 8,000 per cylinder. We had to stand in a queue for hours, he says. So, I thought of a solution - let me make a one-time investment so that we dont have to stand in line for gas again and again every month. Thats when he came across hydrogen stovetops on Instagram and YouTube from a Faridabad-based, research-driven company that aims to revolutionise carbon neutrality with cutting-edge green technologies. The stovetop uses water and separates H2O into hydrogen fuel, which can then be used for cooking roti sabzi every day. The stovetop is one of several experimental products that strive to optimise hydrogen-the most abundant element in the universe. Companies hope to push hydrogen as a clean-energy replacement for fossil fuels-not only because of the ongoing climate crisis and the decarbonisation problem that electricity and batteries cant easily solve, but also, more recently, the West Asia conflict, which has caused cooking gas prices to spiral. For millions of Indians like Vikash, the technology could be significant - the country imports almost 60 of its LPG, with over 90 coming via the Strait of Hormuz. The West Asia conflict significantly impacted LPG supply - Indias monthly imports dropped from two million tonnes to less than a million, a decline of over 50. Globally, approximately 2.1 billion people still cook using biomass, coal, or kerosene, with severe health consequences, particularly for women and children. LPG, while cleaner than solid fuels, remains dependent on fossil supply chains with volatile pricing. Hydrogen cooking - where the only combustion product is water vapour - eliminates indoor air pollution and carbon emissions, provided the hydrogen source is renewable. For companies exploring this avenue, the possibilities are immense-but so are the challenges. At the World Hydrogen Summit in Rotterdam in May 2026, Indian deep-tech company Vision Mechatronics and Netherlands-based HyCooker BV signed a strategic cooperation agreement for international commercial sales of hydrogen-burning cooking stoves. The agreement positions India as the manufacturing base for hydrogen cookstoves under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat programme, with the partnership targeting industrial-scale production to bring costs down. Among those exploring the field is Prakash Chandra Ghosh, a professor in IIT Bombays Department of Energy Science and Engineering, who is collaborating with Powai-based Zest Clean Power Pvt. Ltd to take hydrogen cooking stoves to villages using indigenously developed and internationally patented technologies. Ghosh, who has a PhD in hydrogen technology from Germany and over two decades of experience, is developing hydrogen cooking systems using alkaline electrolysis, with a focus on community-scale solutions. A 25 kW solar-powered green hydrogen production unit was demonstrated at IIT Bombay during the recent West Asia crisis. We showed that it was capable of producing 2.53 kg of green hydrogen a day to prepare 200250 meals. IIT Bombays canteen relied on the system for daily meal preparation, Ghosh says. Strategically, this technology reduces dependency on imported fossil fuels and strengthens national energy security. Our research highlights that this technology eliminates indoor air pollution, reduces heat stress by lowering cooking temperatures, and advances gender equality. Users believe that while these products are somewhat pricey at the moment, the investment could be worth it. Vikash bought the domestic double-burner model from GreenVize a few months ago-and believes the investment was worth it. Its design and operation are very simple. Its not bulky and doesnt take up space. I dont have to worry about gas running out or becoming expensive, he says. How it works Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe, but on Earth, it exists almost entirely bound to other atoms - most commonly in water. It is an energy carrier, not an energy source, meaning it must be produced. When produced using renewable electricity, it is called green hydrogen, and when burned, its only by-product is water vapour. Its this that GreenVize hopes to leverage through its hydrogen cooking stove, which uses an integrated on-site generation process. Co-founder Sanjeev Kumar, a mechanical engineer by qualification with an M.Tech in design engineering, says he began looking for a sustainable alternative to standard cooking gases, and that search led him to hydrogen energy-based products. As you see nowadays, there is a huge dependency on LPG, fossil fuels, and Gulf countries, so we were looking for an alternative for a long time. Two years ago, we started with the thought that nothing needs to be imported and we shouldnt be dependent on foreign countries, Sanjeev says over a call on a sunny Monday afternoon. We wanted to build a practical hydrogen-based system so that we could easily adopt things and wouldnt need to source things from anywhere else. The mechanics are fairly straightforward. You add water to the stoves internal tank, which a built-in Proton Exchange Membrane PEM electrolyser splits into hydrogen and oxygen using electricity. Hydrogen then passes through safety and conditioning stages, including a bubbler, a buffer tank and a multi-stage flame back arrestor, before reaching the catalytic burner, where it combusts to produce a clean, smokeless flame. Electrolysis, the process at the heart of the stove, typically operates at 6286 efficiency depending on the technology used. PEM electrolysers use a polymer membrane to split water and are known for their compact design and ability to operate at varying loads, though they require high-purity water. Once the system is switched on and the required operating conditions are reached, hydrogen generation starts within 30 seconds. The only by-product of this combustion is pure water vapour, says Sanjeev. Oxygen is also released into the air, which is good for indoor air quality improvement, Sanjeev says, adding that the company also has other variations, the Hydrooxy and Alkaline electrolysers, which serve the same purpose. Sanjeev says he first conceived the idea of a company in 2024. But why hydrogen? He says it was because of its versatility. We wanted to explore how hydrogen could be converted from an emerging clean-energy concept into a usable solution for everyday energy applications. Cooking and industrial heating are two areas where LPG, PNG and other conventional fuels are still used. If hydrogen can be used as a clean fuel here too, why should it be limited to large industrial plants, laboratories or mobility applications? he asks. The device is expensive at the moment - a domestic model with a 3-litre tank costs Rs 1,05,000 for a single burner and Rs 1,50,000 for a double burner, while the commercial stove is priced at Rs 3,50,000. For an average user like Vikash, the 3-litre tank lasts about a month. GreenVize estimates this translates to approximately 3 tons of CO savings per year and eliminates the need for external hydrogen storage or LPG cylinders. The company was officially registered in January 2025. Two years and several safety trials later, GreenVize made its first sale of the stove in March 2026 - to the Indian Army. The armys stove is being used in the high altitudes of Jammu right now, says Sanjeev. They also sell hydrogen dispensers, hydrogen fuel-cell systems, biomass power plants, and pressure swing absorption PSA oxygen and nitrogen generators. Future of hydrogen cooktops Under its National Green Hydrogen Mission, India aims to produce 5 million tonnes of green hydrogen by 2030, install 10100 GW of electrolyser capacity, and create 5 lakh new green jobs. The Centre has allocated Rs. 17,490 crore until 2030 to incentivise electrolyser and green hydrogen production. GreenVize has also applied for the Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme BIG, which supports young start-ups in biotechnology innovation and research. Sanjeev believes the grant will help the company scale up as well as improve quality. We aim to integrate smart tech and AI to make a smart stove. That would mean your stove could be connected to your Wi-Fi network, controlled by your phone via an app, and even have voice integration, he says. At a workshop organised by the Bureau of Indian Standards BIS in collaboration with Standards Australia SA under the Australia-India Standards Trade Enabling Project AI-STEP in August, GreenVizes hydrogen cooktops were presented as a case study. The company is also planning to distribute the hydrogen stovetop across other countries, starting with the Maldives. For now, however, there are limitations, chief among them the high cost. Sanjeev knows that this could be a challenge but believes theres some way to go. If anything is exclusive, it tends to be expensive. To make it affordable, we need to make it non-exclusive. Once it goes into mass production, we will bring the cost down, he says. Then there are the repair and replacement costs. While the company says that it depends on individual products, theres no data on long-term use yet. Sanjeev understands he has a long way to go, especially if he wants to scale up production. The company has still not broken even yet, he says. The priority right now is to establish it as a commercially viable product first, and then scale up manufacturing. His clients agree. At their restaurant in Khliehtyrshi, a small town in Meghalayas West Jaintia Hills, Alpana Bareh and her husband, Marphalangki Chyrmang, have been using GreenVizes commercial hydrogen stove for the last few months and now swear by it. This stove is quicker than the LPG one we had before, and the safety of the valves is built into the system itself, which is a plus. We bought two commercial single-burner cooktops after the LPG crisis hit, and found it to be very cost-effective, Alpana says.

articleTitle: WhatsApp chats to CBI raids: How Punjab’s ‘graft network’ with CMO links unravelled
articleFeaturedImageAlt: WhatsApp chats to CBI raids: How Punjab's 'graft network' with CMO links unravelled
description: CM Mann’s OSD, a former health official, and a businessman among people CBI has booked following Punjab and Haryana High Court's directions.
body_raw: Following a directive from the Punjab and Haryana High Court to register an FIR and conduct an impartial probe into the alleged corruption network linked to Chief Minister Bhagwant Manns office, the CBI zeroed in on six individuals, including Rajbir Singh Ghuman, Manns Officer on Special Duty OSD. On Tuesday, the CBI booked Ghuman and five others in connection with the case. An FIR has been registered to investigate the allegations of corruption against OSD to Punjab Chief Minister and his associates for influencing and manipulating postings of officers including that of IAS and IPS officers, departmental proceedings, matters pertaining to policy formulation, administrative approvals, tender conditions, licensing matters, land use conversion matters, property disputes, revenue and land related issues in lieu of pecuniary benefits, the agency said in a statement. The move has triggered sharp reactions from the ruling AAP, which has accused the BJP of tarnishing Manns image by misusing central agencies ahead of the 2027 Assembly polls. Mann himself on Wednesday said he was not scared of any probe. Here is a look at the six people who are under CBIs scanner and the allegations against them. Despite repeated attempts by The Indian Express, all six remained inaccessible. Rajbir Singh Ghuman Manns longtime aide Ghuman is among Manns closest aides. An engineer by qualification, he worked as an assistant professor at a private engineering college in Sangrur before joining Mann. He hails from Gharachon village, around 40 km from Manns native village Satoj. His association with Mann dates back to the Chief Ministers days as Sangrur MP and has continued even after the AAP came to power in 2022. The ED has alleged that Nitin Gohal, another of the accused, routed requests for transfers, postings and other matters through Ghuman. The OSD has denied the charges, saying Gohal is an old friend and that he would not break ties with him over fear of the ED. The High Court noted that despite being at the centre of the allegations, Ghuman was not part of the preliminary inquiry of the Punjab Bureau of Investigation. Nitin Gohal The intermediary The ED describes Gohal, who owns Fortec Web Solutions Private Limited, as a key intermediary in the alleged chain. In his statement to the agency, Gohal said he has known Ghuman for over two decades and visited his office. On being asked why he was approached for transfers and postings despite not being the competent authority, Gohal said he merely prepared lists and forwarded them to the concerned people. The ED said Gohals seized phone revealed 21 WhatsApp chats relating to transfers and postings of officials between September 2023 and March 2026. Another 11 chats were interpreted as concerned with policy formulation, departmental rule changes, administrative approvals, tender conditions, licensing and other government decisions. Other conversations allegedly involved land transactions, change of land use, Greater Mohali Area Development Authority GMADA approvals and property disputes. The ED also cited 11 chats which it interpreted as showing payments, kickbacks or other benefits for official favours. Jitin Gohal The Markfed link Jitin Gohal alias Raja, Nitins brother, is a Markfed manager posted in Jalandhar. His premises were searched by the CBI. Officials said he had been attached to the CMO and worked from the CMs camp office. The ED alleges Nitin facilitated Jitins placement in the CMO through Dr Mahajan and Ghuman. It cited a January 23, 2026 WhatsApp conversation, besides chats in which lists of officers and draft transfer-related material allegedly moved between the brothers. Dr Romi Raja Mahajan Retired officer with political links Dr Romi Raja Mahajan retired in September as Deputy Medical Commissioner at Gurdaspur. An MBBS doctor, he had served at Civil Hospital, Gurdaspur, before becoming Deputy Medical Commissioner. Officials said he too had been attached to the CMO. A senior bureaucrat described him as very active, saying he frequently called officials regarding transfers. The ED cited alleged communications between Mahajan and Nitin Gohal concerning postings and linked Mahajan and Ghuman to Jitin Gohals alleged placement in the CMO. Mahajan allegedly had political links across parties in Gurdaspur. He was allegedly close to former Congress MLA Sukhbans Kaur Bhinder and later served an adviser to BJP leader Swaran Salaria before differences allegedly cropped up between them. He subsequently came to know Ghuman through AAP leader Jagrup Singh Sekhwan of Qadian. Bir Devinder AAP leader Bir Devinder hails from Ballan village in Morinda and is associated with the AAP youth wing. He is known for organising the partys programmes against drugs. The ED material records Nitin Gohal saying he had known Bir Devinder since 2004 and that the duo were partners in a company. Citing a travel agents ledger, the agency also alleged that Nitin Gohal arranged air tickets and hotel accommodation for Ghuman and Devinder, with payments allegedly made in cash. R S Nagra Businessman Hailing from Patialas Nabha Road area, Nagra runs a rice-shelling business. His alleged link to the network largely runs through Nitin Gohal, who allegedly told the ED that he met Nagra in 2022-2023 through a common friend. Nitin Gohal also allegedly told the agency that following the meeting Nagra sent him requests concerning transfers and postings on WhatsApp. The ED cited requests involving officers in the police, taxation, food and civil supplies and other departments, besides references to foodgrain transport policy, tenders, licences, land and GMADA approvals. The CBI also raided premises linked to Nagra. How ED probe led CBI to them The EDs material emerged from its investigation of builder Ajay Sehgal and associates of the Indian Cooperative House Building Society. Searches of Nitin Gohals premises led to the seizure of his phone and examination of WhatsApp chats, call records and documents following which the agency sent its dossier to the Punjab DGP. The Punjab Police examined the material and issued notices but did not register an FIR. The High Court subsequently held that the material disclosed cognisable offences and ordered a CBI probe. It described the state police process as a journey with all travel and no reaching and said an FIR ought to have been registered. The CBI then registered the FIR and searched eight locations across Chandigarh and Punjab, including Manns camp office and premises in Mohali, Gurdaspur, Ludhiana, Patiala, Sangrur and Jalandhar. Laptops, mobile phones and documents were seized. The ED allegations remain under investigation. The CBI probe will now determine whether the personal relationships, administrative access and communications cited by the ED amount to the organised corruption network.

articleTitle: Kerala’s IUML picks Hindu leader as state vice-president. Why it matters
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Kerala’s IUML picks Hindu leader as state vice-president. Why it matters
description: The elevation of C Syam Sundar, a former DYFI state leader who has been with the IUML since 2010, comes as the party navigates allegations of communal polarisation from the Left and pressure from Muslim clerics over its positions.
body_raw: At a time when it faces Opposition allegations of communal polarisation and a push towards conservatism from within the Muslim community, Keralas United Democratic Alliance ally has made an unprecedented move - elevating a Hindu leader to one of its top positions. On Wednesday, the IUML announced that 61-year-old C. Syam Sundar was its new state vice-president as part of its organisational reshuffle. A former state leader of the Democratic Youth Federation of India, the youth wing of the Communist Party of India, Syam Sundar, a prominent Nair leader from central Keralam, has been with the IUML since 2010. The decision comes after the IUML divested all ministers and legislators of various organisational roles. Speaking to the media after his elevation, Syam Sundar said he was happy with the new responsibility. Im the first non-Muslim to become the state vice president of the IUML. I have been with the party since 2010 and started my journey with the IUML as a local party worker. Over the last 15 years, the party has given me various roles, which I have discharged with utmost sincerity, he said. For the party, picking Syam Sundar for one of its top positions assumes significance, especially given the timing. The party finds itself in a difficult position - while the CPI M accuses it of communal polarisation, the IUML is also having to defend conservative positions amid growing pressure from Muslim clerics. Who is C Syam Sundar Syam Sundar belongs to a prominent upper-caste Hindu Nair political family from Alappuzha - the states first Assembly Speaker, R Sankara Narayanan Thambi, was his uncle. At the IUML, Syam Sundar has been given charge of the Idukki and Pathanamthitta districts, where the party does not have a significant presence. Although this is the first time a Hindu leader has taken a prominent position in the IUML, the party has had non-Muslim leaders and electoral candidates in the past. Last year, the outfit inducted Jayanthi Rajan, a Dalit woman, as a national assistant secretary, with the party even fielding her from the CPIM stronghold of Koothuparamba in this Assembly election. Although Jayanthi lost the election, she had managed to put up a formidable fight against the Left. The IUML also backed a young Christian leader from the Congress, V S Joy, in the election in Thavanoor in Muslim-majority Malappuram. The support helped Joy beat the CPIM-backed independent and four-term MLA K T Jaleel in a seat where the Christian vote bank accounted for only 1.4 per cent of the total electorate. For the election, IUML put its organisational machinery behind Joy, a non-Catholic Christian who had earlier struggled to find acceptance in Catholic-dominated constituencies when the Congress decided to field him there.
