This is my sister, the LoP shouted at the police. He became a shield, said a Congress MP. But as it unfolded on Tuesday, both the LoP, Priyanka Gandhi, and other Opposition leaders were eventually pushed into police buses amid allegations that the police used force on them. Trinamool MP Mahua Moitra sustained injuries to her face and hands, and was seen showing her counterparts that she had been left bloodied. As the police bus carrying Rahul Gandhi made its way to the Barakhamba police station, some Congress workers punctured one of its tyres, bringing it to a screeching halt. As the police waited for backup, the LoP sent out a video message saying the fight would continue till Gyanesh Kumar resigns. This is a fight to protect the most sacred thing in this country, he said. We are not going to stop protesting till Gyanesh Kumar resigns. This is a fight to protect the most sacred thing in this country. There is nothing that Narendra Modi and Amit Shah can do that will stop us.  - Rahul Gandhi RahulGandhi October 7, 2026 Priyanka and other MPs and Opposition leaders were taken to far-off Chhatrasal Stadium in Model Town. Eventually, all were released after hours of dramatic scenes. The INDIA bloc is learnt to be planning another protest on Thursday and has kept the details under wraps, sharing them with only a few select leaders, to catch the police off guard. More MPs, more parties will come on Thursday, claimed a senior MP.

articleTitle: Stabbed 7 times while sealing petrol pump, IOC officer’s killing echoes 2005 Manjunath case
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Indian Oil official stabbed to death while sealing petrol pump, 4 held
description: The IOC officer was identified as Mahesh Shelke, 37. He worked as Manager (Retail Sales) and Field Officer with IOC and was posted in Nanded North.
body_raw: In a case bearing striking similarities to the 2005 Manjunath murder case in Uttar Pradesh, an Indian Oil Corporation IOC field officer was allegedly stabbed seven times during an altercation while he was attempting to seal a non-functional petrol pump in Hingoli district on Tuesday evening. Kurunda police have arrested four people, including a mother and her son, in connection with the murder and are searching for a fifth suspect. The deceased was identified as Mahesh Shelke, who worked as Manager Retail Sales and Field Officer with IOC and was posted in Nanded North. According to police, Shelke, along with three to four members of his team, went to the Sai Umesh petrol pump in Ambachondi village in Basmat tehsil on October 6 to officially take over and seal the retail outlet. The pump had remained closed for nearly three months but recently resumed operations. Police said the petrol pump owner was not present at the spot. However, his wife, son and some others were present when the IOC team arrived. An argument broke out, and the situation escalated when the group allegedly began pelting stones at the officials, a senior IPS officer said. During the confrontation, Umesh Pandvir, 24, allegedly attacked Shelke with a knife and stabbed him seven times in the abdomen, chest and back. Shelke died on the spot, and the accused allegedly fled the scene, another officer said. Four persons, identified as Umesh Pandvir his mother, Lata Sahebrao, 46 Shravan Gangadhar Wakude, 24 and a family friend, were arrested within 12 hours. A team is moving to trace a fifth accused. The Indian Oil Officers Association IOOA and IOC have demanded a swift investigation and strict action against the accused. The issue has been taken up with the senior-most officials of the Maharashtra Government and Police to ensure swift and strict action against those responsible, in accordance with law. The safety, dignity and security of our energy-sector personnel, who work tirelessly to serve the nation, remain paramount, Petroleum Minister Hardeep Puri said on social media platform X. Shanmugam Manjunath, a 27-year-old IOC sales officer, was allegedly shot dead in Uttar Pradesh. Manjunath was killed after he conducted a surprise inspection of one of the outlets allegedly involved in selling adulterated fuel that had resumed operations despite the action.

articleTitle: Punjab: Supreme Court sets aside polls in 50 wards, orders re-elections in six weeks
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Supreme Court, Punjab ward elections, Punjab ward re elections, Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, Punjab and Haryana High Court, Indian express news, current affairs
description: To ensure that re-elections are conducted in a free, fair, and transparent manner, the top court asked the Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court to appoint, within one week, a monitoring committee comprising a retired judge of the HC to oversee the process.
body_raw: The Supreme Court has set aside the elections to 50 wards in Punjab after a fact-finding commission appointed by it found widespread obstruction during the nomination process, whereby nomination papers were snatched, torn or destroyed, and candidates were assaulted, detained or threatened in the local body polls. A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana ordered fresh elections in 50 wards - 28 in Patiala district and 22 in Moga. .the Commission found 50 ward elections to be vitiated and deserving of being set aside. We accept the recommendations and direct that fresh elections be conducted in the relevant 50 wards.The entire process of re-election shall be completed within 6 weeks, the bench ordered. In the September 28 order, which was made available Wednesday, the bench took note of the fact that Kapil Sibal, appearing for the State of Punjab states that the State has no objection to the acceptance of the recommendations made by the Commission. To ensure that re-elections are conducted in a free, fair, and transparent manner, the top court asked the Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court to appoint, within one week, a monitoring committee comprising a retired judge of the HC to oversee the process.

articleTitle: Second day, second Opposition protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, detentions again
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Second day, second Opposition protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, detentions again
description: Samajwadi Party absent at Kharge lunch for INDIA bloc leaders; Cong for more protests today
body_raw: Pressing for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Opposition leaders staged a protest for the second consecutive day in the heart of the Capital Wednesday before they were stopped and detained by police. The Samajwadi Party, however, stayed away from the INDIA bloc protest. On Tuesday, after the Opposition protest, Congress allies had expressed concern that it had been turned into a Rahul Gandhi show. The SP skipped the lunch hosted Wednesday by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge at the Sagar Ratna restaurant on Janpath. From the restaurant, Opposition MPs, including Gandhi, Mamata TMCs Derek OBrien, CPIMs John Brittas and CPIs P Sandosh Kumar, boarded three buses to head towards Jantar Mantar. Over the next couple of hours, as the buses crawled forward, Congress workers walked alongside. Police, however, blocked the way and the march came to a halt near Windsor Place. Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra lay on the road, clutching a copy of the Constitution, along with other women leaders. Later, police forcibly removed Congress workers and detained the Gandhi siblings and other senior leaders. Kerala Chief Minister V D Satheesan was among those who had joined the protest. We are not going to stop protesting till Gyanesh Kumar resigns. This is a fight to protect the most sacred thing in this country. There is nothing that Narendra Modi and Amit Shah can do that will stop us, Gandhi said. He thanked all INDIA bloc MPs standing firm in defence of our democracy-in Parliament, outside on the streets, and today near Jantar Mantar. The Congress called for more protests at state, district and block levels on Thursday. The party also played down the absence of SP MPs from Wednesdays lunch meeting, saying they had left Delhi the night before or early Wednesday. The SPs absence, it is learnt, also came up during the discussions over lunch. Later in the day, INDIA bloc leaders reached out to the SP, which agreed to send its representatives for the protest Thursday, sources said. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh, in a post on X, said all alliance parties were invited to the lunch. But the decision for lunch had been taken late last night and communicated. It was therefore natural that some parties could not be represented. There is needless comment in some sections of the media on it. INDIA and other Opposition parties are united and stand in solidarity against Vote Chori, SIR and Delimitation, he said. SP leaders whom The Indian Express spoke to blamed the patchy coordination by the Congress. A party MP said, The Samajwadi Party did not attend the lunch by the Congress because of lack of proper coordination from the Congress side. Samajwadi Party MPs left for their constituencies on Tuesday evening after the protest against the CEC ended. Until then, there was no information about the lunch. Sources in the SP said the party leadership and the MPs were upset with the Gandhi siblings for stealing the show Tuesday. It is true that we are not happy with the poor coordination by the Congress regarding the protest at Akashvani Bhavan. It was supposed to be a joint protest by the INDIA bloc, and not by the Gandhis. The next big election in the country is in Uttar Pradesh, where the Samajwadi Party has a bigger stake than the Congress. Akhilesh Yadav raised the concerns about SIR in Uttar Pradesh more aggressively and effectively, while the Congress leadership only took symbolic steps during the SIR in UP earlier this year. But the Congress in Delhi tried to portray that only it was serious about SIR, an SP leader said. The developments are playing out against a key backdrop the UP Assembly elections early next year. In the politically significant heartland state, the SP and the Congress are allies and as the polls approach, a tussle over seat distribution has begun.

articleTitle: Up to 30% of cotton area under ‘illegal’ GM hybrids, finds study
articleFeaturedImageAlt: GM cotton hybrids, GM cotton varieties, cotton area under illegal GM hybrids, cotton, cotton production, cotton farmers, FSII-NSAI study, Indian express news, current affairs
description: Farmers planting hybrids incorporating unapproved herbicide-tolerant and Vip3 Bt genes.
body_raw: More than a quarter of the total area cultivated under cotton in India comprises illegal hybrids incorporating unapproved genetically modified GM traits, including resistance to glyphosate herbicide. Out of the 114.8 lakh hectares lh area sown under cotton by Indian farmers in 2025-26, an estimated 26.2-29 lh, i.e. 24-30, was of hybrids containing unauthorised herbicide-tolerant HT or Bacillus thuringiensis Bt genes, according to a field-based study commissioned by the Federation of Seed Industry of India FSII and National Seed Association of India NSAI. India currently allows farmers to grow GM cotton hybrids varieties containing only two genes - cry1Ac and cry2Ab - that are isolated from Bt, a soil bacterium. These genes code for proteins toxic to certain bollworm insect pests. But the FSII-NSAI study shows farmers are also planting the seeds of hybrids that contain cp4-epsps and Vip3A genes. Both these are alien genes, whose harbouring in any crops has not been approved by the government. The cp4-epsps gene, sourced from another soil-dwelling agrobacterium, makes cotton plants tolerant to glyphosate. This herbicide cannot be sprayed on normal cotton, as the chemical does not distinguish between the crop and weeds. The Vip3A gene is derived from Bt, but works differently from the cry1Ac cry2Ab genes and is said to effectively control a broader spectrum of bollworm larvae. The FSSI-NSAI study has been based on 227 geo-tagged seed leaf samples collected from fields of 984 farmers across 16 districts of Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh AP and Rajasthan. The 16 hotspot districts were identified using a combination of secondary data sources, including glyphosate sale trends, farmer interactions and seed market intelligence. The testing of the samples for gene identification was conducted using dipstick lateral flow assays and ELISA enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. We found the HT cp4-epsps gene to be present in 72.69 of the field samples, with this as high as 88.64 for Telangana, 70.92 for Maharashtra, 62.86 for AP and 57.14 for Rajasthan. It indicates widespread adoption of HT technology by farmers for weed management, despite the government not authorising this GM trait, said Bhagirath Choudhary, director of the Jodhpur Rajasthan-based South Asia Biotechnology Centre that undertook the study. The demand for the unapproved HT gene technology has been driven by the acute shortage of labour and high manual weeding costs. Farmers have decisively shifted towards glyphosate-based weed management enabled by illegal HTBt cotton technology. They are typically applying 2-3 sprays per season that costs Rs 750-850 per acre, as against Rs 12,000-15,000 through manual weeding, Choudhary noted. Laboratory analysis of samples apart, the decline in sales of legal Bt cotton hybrid seeds - from 596 lakh packets in 2022-23 to 463 lakh packs in 2025-26 each packet contains 450 grams of seeds - is also proof of the high acceptance of HT hybrids by farmers. This has been accompanied by a significant 29 jump in imports of glyphosate, from 27,721 kilolitres in 2024-25 to 35,642 kilolitres in 2025-26. The FSSI-NSAI study has estimated the unauthorised HTBt seed market in India to have expanded from around 35 lakh packets in 2017-18 to 82-88 lakh packets in 2025-26. At an average price of Rs 1,000 per packet, this market would be conservatively valued at Rs 820-880 crore. Equally interesting is the planting of cotton hybrids expressing the Vip3 Bt gene. We found 53.74 of our 227 field samples testing positive for this next-generation insect-resistance gene. Its presence was 58.16 in Maharashtra, 54.29 in AP, 57.14 in Rajasthan and 38.64 in Telangana. The driver here seems to be effectiveness against pink bollworm, with the first-generation Bt hybrids becoming vulnerable to this insect pest, said Choudhary. Simply put, the market for illegal GM cotton seeds is growing, with both farmers and a sophisticated supplier network bypassing the countrys established biosafety and regulatory approval system.

articleTitle: Caught cheating? Let student finish exam: IIT Bombay panel after suicide
articleFeaturedImageAlt: IIT-B student dies by suicide, iit Bombay student dies by suicide, IIT Bombay, IIT Bombay students protest, ChatGPT, examination question paper on ChatGPT, Mumbai news, Maharashtra news, Indian express, current affairs
description: The aim was to have guidelines in place before the remaining mid-semester papers are held this weekend. The committee presented its interim report at a special meeting of the IIT Senate on Wednesday.
body_raw: If a student is caught cheating during an exam, the invigilator should take away the related material and record the incident, but allow the student to complete the paper with a fresh answer booklet. The quick response team QRT helpline should be alerted so the student has support after the exam. These are among the proposals put forward by a committee, set up after the recent student suicide at IIT-Bombay, in its interim report, The Indian Express has learnt. IIT Director Shireesh Kedare had set up the eight-member commitee - four faculty members and four students - to revisit exam conduct rules, days after Sahil Wakode, a Second Year BTech student who was allegedly found using a cellphone during a mid-semester exam, died by suicide on September 18. The aim was to have guidelines in place before the remaining mid-semester papers are held this weekend. The committee presented its interim report at a special meeting of the IIT Senate on Wednesday. The Senate has also decided to go back to the institutes2015 punishment rules until a new set is drafted, putting on hold the stricter rules it adopted this year. Under the July rules, a student found carrying a phone into an exam got an FR or fail and repeat grade and suspension for a semester. Under the 2015 rules, carrying a phone in the exam hall would mean loss of one grade, and using it would mean an FR. A student caught talking to another during an exam got a straight FR under the July rules. In 2015, it meant loss of one grade unless there was other evidence, such as identical answers. The interim report proposes that the invigilator should record the incident in a prescribed form, give the student a chance to give their version, and alert a quick response team QRT so the student has support, it has said. Seized items such as phones may be photographed. The report proposes limits to the invigilators role. An important point to note When a suspected unauthorised academic practice is noticed, the invigilators responsibility is to stop that activity, collect related material and record details to the extent possible. Further proceedings will be carried out later by the Disciplinary Action Committee as per norms, it says. Protesting students have alleged procedural lapses in how Wakodes case was handled. The invigilator is to seize the material with as little conversation with the student as possible. If there is doubt about the students identity, the invigilator can photograph them at the desk, the report says. When the exam ends, the invigilator should fill a form describing the incident and the evidence collected. The student can record their version on another form, at a designated venue with additional staff present. The forms, which the report is prescribing for the first time, are meant to keep a complete record of each case, sources said. These will be sent to the head of the department conducting the course, along with the seized material and the original answer book. When the student leaves the exam hall, the invigilator must alert the QRT helpline, giving the students name, roll number, course and venue, the report says. The idea is to ensure the student isnt alone after such an incident, sources said. Until now, the institute followed procedures framed in 2015, which had a single paragraph on what an invigilator should do. With no central monitoring, each department handled cases in its own way, sources said. The committee has also proposed stricter exam hall rules. No phones, smartwatches, earphones or other gadgets, and no bags, notes or books will be allowed inside the exam building. Teaching assistants cannot bring phones into the hall. Halls are to be monitored through CCTV, only one student can step out at a time for bio-break, and entry will close 30 minutes after the exam begins. According to sources, members broadly agreed with the report but made several suggestions, and a final version will be prepared once these are considered. Senate meetings are usually open only to members, but given the importance of the matter, all faculty members were invited, sources added.

articleTitle: GST Council meeting today: Cutting across divide, 5 big states oppose end of taxmen’s arrest powers
articleFeaturedImageAlt: GST regime, GST regime Arrest powers, GST Council meeting today, GST defaulters, Goods and Services tax (GST), GST, GST rates, GST returns, GST impacts, GST Council meeting, Indian express business, business news, current affairs
description: Back provision for ‘civil arrest’ in serious GST violation, warn of ‘toothless’ regime
body_raw: As states and the Centre converge in Delhi for the 57th Goods and Services Tax GST Council meeting Thursday to discuss process reforms that include a proposal mandating the removal of the arrest provision, at least five major states are learnt to have expressed concern over any sweeping curtailment of the taxmens powers. Maharashtra, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh are among states that have expressed reservations regarding the scrapping of arrest powers under GST in multiple meetings held between the state and Central government officials in the run-up to the Council meeting. A key demand by states has been that the indirect tax regime should not be rendered toothless, and pre-prosecution arrests should be graded with an additional layer enabling civil arrest in cases of serious violations, a state minister told The Indian Express. While the proposal entails removal of arrest altogether, except for prosecution, states are asking for an additional layer of arrest powers even in the pre-prosecution stage. Many states feel that taking away such powers will make it completely toothless. While there can be a provision for no arrest in normal cases, there can be a provision for civil arrest in cases of serious violations under GST, the minister said. The Council meeting got deferred by a day to Thursday, and the additional day in between is learnt to have been utilised by Union government officials to reach out to GST chief commissioners across zones to iron out residual issues, especially concerns over the no-arrest proposal. On Thursday, the Council, in a bid to boost investor sentiment and allay concerns about overreach by tax authorities, is set to take up the proposal to decriminalise offences including removal of arrests, as was reported by The Indian Express last Sunday. The underlying intent, an official said, is to make enforcement work through money rather than custody, and through a system that detects fraud rather than a provision that deters it. As per the proposal to be discussed at the Council meeting, tax disputes are aimed to be resolved through civil consequences, namely recovery of tax, interest for the delay, and penalty, while keeping prosecution available for a higher threshold of Rs 5 crore as against Rs 1 crore at present. The idea is to focus on detection and not deterrence. The proposal is to remove pre-prosecution arrests and the Council will debate it. In the last 8-9 months, several rounds of discussions were held between states and the Centre, including three national coordination meetings. So far, 3-4 states have expressed their concerns, especially about how they will get to trace offenders. The Council will take a final call on the form that the arrest powers should take, keeping in mind the criticism regarding threats of criminalisation, the official said.

articleTitle: ‘They ask me over and over’: Bengal BLOs fear tribunal questions in special drive
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bengal BLOs fear tribunal questions, Bengal sir, Bengal sir special drive, SIR of electoral roll, nationwide SIR, Special Intensive Revision (SIR), Assembly elections, Assembly polls, nationwide Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, nationwide SIR of of electoral rolls, Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, SIR of of electoral rolls, Election Commission, Election Commission of India, Indian express news, current affairs
description: CEO notice says BLOs should refer to list of those deleted on grounds of being absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, hints tribunal cases not covered; BLOs wait for clarity
body_raw: An organisation representing Booth Level Officers BLOs has expressed apprehension that they may face the ire of deleted voters. Others wonder how long the latest turn in the Special Intensive Revision SIR exercise, of re-checking those voters left out, will keep them away from their day jobs. Some point out that it entails them doing an exercise done by them once already. However, the biggest question hanging over BLOs in West Bengal as they set out again is this how do they tackle questions regarding those whose cases are hanging fire in appellate tribunals? They also hope that clarity will be forthcoming in training sessions to be held for them after the Durga Puja holidays. With questions swirling, the state CEOs office put out a notice Tuesday saying that the special drive announced by the Election Commission of India ECI applies to left out eligible voters, adding that BLOs should refer to the list of ASDD Absentee, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate voters. Any person in this list may submit Form 6 online or through BLO for inclusion of hisher name in the Electoral Roll, the notice said, apart from first-time voters who have now reached 18 years of age. As reported by The Indian Express first, under fire over the scale of voter deletions, the ECI directed on September 29 that in the 20 states and Union Territories where the SIR was completed, a special drive will be held to enrol voters left out of the rolls. At a subsequent video conference with all state Chief Electoral Officers, the Deputy Election Commissioner present said pre-SIR and post-SIR rolls should be compared to draw up the list of those deleted, and identify any who may have been left out, as per officers who attended. In the final electoral roll of West Bengal published on February 28 this year, 63.66 lakh voters were deleted, nearly 1.9 lakh added, while the cases of 60.06 lakh were listed as under adjudication. Of these, while 33 lakh-odd voters were restored to the electoral roll, cases of 27 lakh were referred to tribunals, which also took up around 16 lakh applications against inclusion. Speaking to The Indian Express over the phone, Md Sahabuddin Mondol, a BLO of Barasat, North 24 Parganas, said Before the SIR, there were 1,279 voters in my booth. During the SIR, we found 120 either absent, shifted or dead. I think now there is a chance for such voters to apply again. Additionally, from his booth, 586 cases were referred to the tribunals. Of these, 86 have been deleted so far, Sahabuddin says. I am not sure whether these 86 can apply again, and I dont think those whose cases are still being heard by tribunals can apply either. But I am waiting for the training session. The ECI also said in its September 29 order that the Form 6 for enrolment of voters now will no longer require them to show linkage to the 2002 SIR. Sahabuddin says he has heard of this change, but is waiting for clear instructions. Pinki Jaiswal, a BLO at Kolkatas Narkeldanga, says of the 191 voters deleted in her booth, 100 were removed as they are dead. The rest I will re-check. Basically, we have to check the shifted and absentee voters. In my case, I had found that most of them were now in Bihar. Jaiswal adds The main problem is with the cases referred to tribunals. I have 28 in my booth who appealed, but there is no news regarding their hearings. The BLO believes they cannot be included in the exercise. Khurshid Anwar, a BLO from Srirampur in Hooghly district, says he has heard that we will have to visit and re-check the documents. He mentions that it will take time, and adds But the main problem is the tribunal cases. People are stuck there, and they ask me about it over and over. Habibur Rehman, a BLO from Deganga in South 24 Parganas, says All I am hearing is that there will be training. Only after that can I tell you anything. A BLO from Central Kolkata who did not want to be named expresses his frustration. After completing the SIR and then helping with the Assembly elections, we have now been enrolled for Census. That itself is a mammoth task, and the process will only be completed next February. Meanwhile, this special ECI drive has started. When will we do these jobs and when do we do our school duties? Earlier, an organisation representing BLOs called Votekormi and BLO Aikya Mancha wrote to the Bengal CEO seeking appropriate measures for complete security. for BLOs working in sensitive areas. where a huge number of voters have been deleted during SIR. Referring to South and North 24 Parganas, Howrah, parts of Hooghly and Kolkata, Malda, Murshidabad and Uttar Dinajpur, the letter said In these districts, a huge number of voters were deleted for no reason. They the BLOs may be the target of attacks by furious deleted voters. The BLOs themselves had no role in the mass deletion, the letter said, blaming it on the ECI system flagging logical discrepancies that had raised the question of credentials of these deleted voters. Then Chief Minister Mamata Banerjees decision to go to court led to their cases coming under adjudication and finally being referred to tribunals, the organisation wrote. The entire process was faulty and then we drew the attention of the concerned authority, but without result. Asked about the BLOs fears, a senior ECI official said, In this process, they dont have to go to every applicants house. All District Electoral Officers will organise camps where applicants can apply through Form 6. They can also apply online. Then, if an Electoral Registration Officer or District Electoral Officer thinks that in a particular case physical verification is needed, in only those, BLOs would have to go to the applicants residence. On the tribunal cases, the official said No applicant who was deleted after hearing in a tribunal or whose case is under tribunals jurisdiction can apply because the Calcutta High Court earlier said that such cases can only go to an appellate court. The ECI has no role in their cases.

articleTitle: First hike in over 3 years may not be last; repo rate can rise by another 75 basis points
articleFeaturedImageAlt: RBI repo rate, RBI repo rate hike, RBI monetary policy, RBI MPC, Monetary Policy Committee, RBI policy stance, calibrated tightening, RBI interest rate hike, India interest rates, India inflation, CPI inflation India, WPI inflation India, retail inflation India, wholesale inflation India, core inflation India, inflation expectations, inflation generalisation, RBI inflation forecast, RBI GDP forecast, India GDP growth, India economic growth, Sanjay Malhotra RBI, RBI policy October 2026, RBI policy August 2026, hawkish RBI, dovish RBI, interest rate cycle India, rate hike India, inflation and interest rates, El Nino India inflation, weak monsoon inflation, memory chip prices India, West Asia war inflation, US Federal Reserve rate hike, global interest rates, bank rate India, policy repo rate, Express Explained,
description: RBI is likely to tighten the monetary policy with a series of rate hikes if the situation on the price front doesn’t improve in the coming months. This means interest rates on loans will increase further, which in turn can dampen  the demand conditions in the economy.
body_raw: THE 25 basis points hike in key policy rate, the first in more than three years, may not be the last. A shift in the monetary stance from neutral to calibrated tightening is a clear warning that the central bank will tighten the screws if inflationary pressures refuse to ease. Bankers and economists are now expecting another 50-75 basis points hike in the policy rate in the coming reviews. In other words, the RBI is likely to tighten the monetary policy with a series of rate hikes if the situation on the price front doesnt improve in the coming months. This means interest rates on loans will increase further, which in turn can dampen the demand conditions in the economy. It MPC underscored that given the current conditions, rate cuts are off the table in the near term and policy action ahead can only be a rate hike or a pause, depending on the evolving conditions and the outlook, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said after the MPC meeting. With borrowing costs already elevated, another rate hike would exert additional pressure on households, businesses and an economy trying to sustain momentum in a challenging external environment. The RBIs message leaves little room for complacency. By signalling further tightening, the central bank has effectively chosen to prioritise inflation control over the immediate concerns of growth and credit demand. The consequences could be particularly punishing for consumers and businesses carrying existing debt, as higher interest rates translate into steeper EMIs, costlier working capital and weaker investment. If the MPC follows through on its hawkish stance, the next round of tightening could expose just how much economic pain the RBI is willing to tolerate in its battle to bring inflation under control. Malhotra said the duration and extent of the rate hike cycle would be contingent on the actual growth-inflation developments and outlook, especially that of underlying inflation, the extent of broadening of price pressures and second round effects of the supply shock, as also the impact of demand impulses. The MPC observation clearly indicates that another rate hike might be in the offing in the December policy review, depending on the economic conditions, analysts said in initial reactions. HDFC Bank economists expect the RBI to hike rates by another 50-75 bps over the coming meetings expect back-to-back increases in consecutive meetings instead of a staggered approach. The need for a more aggressive rate hike cycle greater than 100-125bps hinges on how the West Asia conflict progresses from here on how durable and strong is the second order impact of inputs costs increases on retail inflation evolution of El Nino conditions and impact on winter crop and finally and how growth and demand impulses hold up in the face of global volatility and rate increases, the bank said. Given these factors, while a longer and higher rate hike cycle cannot be ruled out completely at this stage, we see it as a lower probability event, it said. While ICRAs baseline GDP growth projection 7.1 per cent for FY2027 is in line with the MPC, it believes that there are risks to the outlook arising from deficient monsoon rainfall, impact of rising global energy prices on corporate profits, and an adverse base owing to GST rate cuts in September 2025. ICRAs baseline estimate pencils in the CPI inflation at 5.0 per cent in FY2027, lower than the MPCs forecast. However, elevated crude oil prices could push inflation to 5.3-5.5 per cent, with the GDP growth moderating to 6.8 per cent in the fiscal. At present, we expect another rate hike of 25 bps in the December 2026 meeting, and a pause thereafter, unless there are sizeable negative surprises on the inflation front, ICRA said. Our estimates suggest that headline inflation will remain above 5.5 per cent YoY for three consecutive quarters starting in Q3 FY27, significantly above the RBIs medium-term target of 4 per cent YoY. As inflation accelerates, real policy rates are likely to turn negative, necessitating a recalibration of monetary policy, UBS Chief India Economist Tanvee Gupta Jain said. We expect a cumulative 50-75 bps rate hike cycle, with another 25bps hike likely in the December policy. Namrata Mittal, Chief Economist, SBI Funds Management, expects another cumulative 75 bps of hikes through the cycle, potentially taking the repo rate to 6.0 per cent, though she highlights that the global environment remains highly fluid. Malhotra further observed that in light of available data, it is clear that inflation and its outlook are not benign as they were last year, with headline CPI inflation expected to average almost 5.8 per cent in the next three quarters and core inflation projected at 4.4 per cent this financial year. In this milieu, recalibrating the policy rate is imperative, he said.

articleTitle: DDA begins process to rehabilitate 45 slum clusters housing 1 lakh people
articleFeaturedImageAlt: DDA begins process to rehabilitate slum clusters, delhi slum clusters, rehabilitate delhi slum clusters,Master Plan for Delhi, Delhi Development Authority (DDA), Indian express news, current affairs
description: The slum clusters in Badli, Shahdara, Pitampura and Tilak Nagar house the largest number of households to be considered for rehabilitation.
body_raw: The Delhi Development Authority DDA on Wednesday initiated the process of rehabilitation of more than one lakh slum dwellers, in what is seen as one of the first big movements under the Master Plan for Delhi MPD-2047. The agency floated Request for Proposals RFP for appointment of three Transaction Advisors for preparing feasibility reports for 15 projects covering 45 slum clusters across the city. The clusters comprise approximately 21,229 households spread over 135.74 acres of land. The slum clusters in Badli, Shahdara, Pitampura and Tilak Nagar house the largest number of households to be considered for rehabilitation. The move comes over three months after Union Home Minister Amit Shah chaired a meeting on slum rehabilitation in the city and directed the DDA and the Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board DUSIB to issue tenders for five slum clusters within 45 days, and to float tenders for at least five public-private partnership PPP-based rehabilitation projects every month. A DDA spokesperson said that the transaction advisors will assess rehabilitation requirements, development potential, infrastructure needs, financial viability and suitable implementation models for systematic and sustainable implementation of the projects. The government claims that there are about 675 slums in the Capital. Of these, around half are set up on land owned by various Central agencies, such as Railways, Land and Development Office LDO, and the DDA. The nodal agency for rehabilitation of these slums is DDA. The rest are located on land owned by the Delhi government, where the nodal agency is the Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board DUSIB, which comes under the Urban Development Department. The rehabilitation process has progressed at an excruciatingly slow pace over the past decade, with only two in-situ projects - Ashok Vihar and Kalkaji, together providing around 4,700 flats - completed so far, both by DDA. Under the PPP model, which the government says it will use, private developers come in to construct housing to rehabilitate slum dwellers on a part of the slum land while the remaining land is commercially developed. The underlying rationale is that the developer recovers the cost of building units for slum dwellers by making profits from the free sale component. The model was expected to work well since slums are typically located on high-value land. However, the DDA has struggled to attract private developers who cited small land parcels, difficult locations near drains and railway tracks, and frequent litigation. Recent changes to rehab framework How Delhi handles slum rehabilitation has undergone big changes over the past couple of months. Amendments were made to the citys slum policy, making slum dwellers eligible for getting a flat in place of their current home. Changes were also made in the MPD-2047. In a bid to attract participation of private developers in slum rehabilitation, developers were allowed to build taller buildings on slum land parcels and sell a higher proportion of that land for profit. Transferable Development Rights TDR were also introduced in the MPD-2047. In the free sale component, a developer may not be able to use all the development rights available to build flats, shops, or offices for profit because of the size or location of the land parcel in question, or due to height restrictions. Under the new TDR mechanism, these unused development rights can be used on another plot, or sold to another developer. TDR has been used extensively in Mumbai, particularly to accelerate slum rehabilitation and redevelopment.

articleTitle: Centre approves Rs 65 crore for geo-spacial based survey of unauthorised colonies
articleFeaturedImageAlt: geo-spacial based survey of unauthorised colonies, unauthorised colonies, Delhi Revenue and Imaging Survey, Spatial Technology Initiative, DRISHTI, GIS-based survey, Rekha Gupta, Manohar Lal, Indian express news, current affairs
description: Delhi government is implementing the PM-UDAY (Pradhan Mantri-Unauthorized Colonies in Delhi Awas Adhikar Yojana), aimed at granting property rights to residents of the city's over 1,500 unauthorised colonies.
body_raw: Nearly three months after Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta wrote to Union Housing and Urban Affairs Minister Manohar Lal requesting an assistance to regularise unauthorised colonies, the Centre has approved Rs 65 crore under Delhi Revenue and Imaging Survey, Spatial Technology Initiative DRISHTI for GIS-based survey and mapping of such colonies. Delhi government is implementing the PM-UDAY Pradhan Mantri-Unauthorized Colonies in Delhi Awas Adhikar Yojana, aimed at granting property rights to residents of the citys over 1,500 unauthorised colonies. Moreover,PM-UDAY cells in 13 districts, and a headquarter, will be set up to expedite registration of properties in unauthorised colonies. The geographic information system GIS survey is required under PM-UDAY scheme to verify, map and authenticate property boundaries and geo-coordinates within Delhis notified unauthorised colonies. The technology-driven survey will make mapping of properties more transparent, systematic and time-bound. The project has an estimated total cost of Rs 65 crore, of which Rs 52 crore, or 80 per cent, will be provided as a grant from the Urban Development Fund UDF of the Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, the CMO said. The remaining Rs 13 crore, will be contributed by Delhi governments revenue department that will be responsible for implementing the project, it said. The initiative will help make the mapping and documentation process related to properties under PM-UDAY scheme more systematic and time-bound. The chief minister said the PM-UDAY scheme is not merely a process of issuing property-related documents but also an important means of providing legal security over homes and property rights to lakhs of families living in Delhis unauthorised colonies.

articleTitle: I&B Ministry notifies names of 13 journalists as Press Council members
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ministry of information and broadcasting, Press Council of India operating at half strength, Press Council of India, Press Council of India (PCI) staff, Press Council of India (PCI) strength, Indian express news, current affairs
description: The Indian Express reported on Wednesday that the I&B Ministry has not yet notified the names of 13 of the 28 PCI members, despite nominating them earlier this year and the council sending three reminders to the government.
body_raw: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting IB on Wednesday officially notified the names of 13 journalists as members of the Press Council of India PCI - Indias key media watchdog. The names comprise six newspaper editors and seven working journalists other than editors. The Indian Express reported on Wednesday that the IB Ministry has not yet notified the names of 13 of the 28 PCI members, despite nominating them earlier this year and the council sending three reminders to the government. The gazette notification has been long pending, with the PCI operating at half its sanctioned strength for nearly a year and without a single working journalist or newspaper editor. The PCI operates under the Press Council Act, 1978, which stipulates that the Council must consist of a chairperson and 28 members, each serving a three-year term. So far, only 14 of the 28 members have been appointed five MPs, three nominees and six from among newspaper owners and management, aside from the chairperson. Earlier in the day, the Editors Guild of India also demanded the immediate reconstitution of the 15th Press Council in conformity with the Press Council Act, 1978, including the prompt filling of all 13 seats reserved for professional journalists.

articleTitle: Microsoft, Nvidia unveil new AI PCs with RTX Spark chip at San Francisco event
articleFeaturedImageAlt: microsoft, Nvidia, Microsoft unveil new AI PCs with RTX Spark chip, Nvidia unveil new AI PCs with RTX Spark chip, Nvidia unveil new AI PCs, Microsoft unveil new AI PCs, Nvidia’s RTX Spark chipset, Satya Nadella, Jensen Huang, Indian express news, current affairs
description: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella was joined by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on stage alongside Windows and Devices head Pavan Davuluri.
body_raw: Microsoft launched a new class of Windows-powered laptops featuring Nvidias RTX Spark chipset, in an effort to take on Apple Inc.s MacBook Pros. The new laptops are aimed at developers and creators who want high-end machines capable of running demanding AI workloads locally rather than in the cloud. At an event on Wednesday in San Francisco, Microsoft and Nvidia unveiled a new category of laptops, headlined by the new Surface Laptop Ultra with RTX Spark, alongside new features in Windows 11 that leverage the new system chips capabilities. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella was joined by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on stage alongside Windows and Devices head Pavan Davuluri. It took more than 4,000 engineering years. This is a massive project. We have reinvented the personal computer. For the first time, we took all the capabilities that used to be in a gaming laptop, a workstation, a supercomputer or the cloud, unified the architecture and made it run on one superchip, Huang said. For the first time, Microsoft showed the Surface Laptop Ultra, the companys new 15-inch premium laptop featuring Nvidias RTX Spark chip. Pricing for the Ultra starts at 2,599, with up to 128 GB of unified memory. The Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, a device designed for hardcore developers and creators, starts at 5,999.They, along with PCs from Asus, Dell, Lenovo, HP, and MSI will ship next Friday, October 16. The new Surface Pro Ultra has been marketed as the most powerful Windows computer designed for everything from local AI computing, creative workloads, and ray traced gaming and its all thanks to Nvidias new CPU the RTX Spark. Davuluri showed the Surface Laptop Ultra running GitHub Copilot and playing Gears of War E-Day at 60 frames per second. He said that hundreds of AAA and indie titles will be available on day one, and that Call of Duty will come to RTX Spark in 2027. The laptop has the brightest peak HDR display on a laptop, Duvuluri said. The system also features a magnetic USB-C charger called Magnetic Connect. The connector plugs in similarly to Apples MagSafe, except that it uses a standardised port. Microsoft compared the Spark with the M5 Pro in the MacBook Pro, promising performance of up to 2.1 times faster time to first token, 4.3 times faster image generation, and 6.2 times faster video generation. Microsoft gave a video demo using multiple local and cloud models across Blender, Photoshop, ComfyUI, and Unreal Engine. The demo showed a workload that took hours instead of days. Hybrid Intelligence With new high-performance laptops, Microsoft is bringing an updated Windows 11, adding new quick actions in the Search menu in the Task Bar, making quick changes to settings, taking screenshots, or arranging windows using natural language. Microsoft also pushed hybrid intelligence, which allows Copilot to access your files, take actions and use local AI models as well as those on the cloud. In this new structure, Copilot will only tap into the cloud for difficult AI tasks, while running local models to save your precious tokens. Beyond Copilot, Windows 11 will be able to host multiple AI agents locally including Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Perplexity, and even Facebook Muse. Nadella describes the event as building the frontier ecosystem, centered on Agent 365, Microsoft IQ, and Copilot. Davuluri described Windows 11 as the most secure platform for AI agents, emphasisng built-in containment. The writer is in San Francisco on the invitation of Nvidia

articleFeaturedImageAlt: MPSC protests continue, MPSC paper leak, MPSC protests, MPSC protests intensify, MPSC chairman Vivek Bhimanwar, Pune news, Pune, Maharashtra news, Indian express, current affairs
description: At SM Joshi bridge, six protesters have been on hunger strike for the past four days—Shivraj More and Priyanka Chaudhari of the Youth Congress, Nitin Gite, Omkar Patil, Rushikesh Gangurde, Gajanan Shelke and Somnath Chavan.
body_raw: Two of the three protests ongoing in Pune demanding reforms in the Maharashtra Public Service Commission MPSC are ongoing while one protest has been withdrawn after the Bombay High Court on Monday suggested that students should go home and study as the court was seized of the matter. The larger protest ongoing at SM Joshi bridge, completing seven days, is being forefronted by Nationalist Congress Party-Sharadchandra Pawar NCPSP MLA Rohit Pawar. This group has been demanding the resignation of MPSC Chairman Vivek Bhimanwar. The other protest is ongoing at Lal Bahadur Shastri Road, while the protest at Alka Talkies has been called off by the third group. At SM Joshi bridge, six protesters have been on hunger strike for the past four days-Shivraj More and Priyanka Chaudhari of the Youth Congress, Nitin Gite, Omkar Patil, Rushikesh Gangurde, Gajanan Shelke and Somnath Chavan. The court was hearing a Public Interest Litigation filed by two residents of Pune citing inconvenience to Punes public due to the protest. Pawar said that the petitioners in court were connected to a BJP corporator. In its order the Court found substance in the argument by agitators that accountability has to be fixed in the paper leak case and the matter requires consideration. Maybe the police had self-confidence as the case was in the High Court that the hearing would begin at 11 and at 1115 the decision would be in their favour. That is why there was a huge police force here in the morning, Rohit Pawar said after the hearing. The HC bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait M Sethna remarked orally that the protesters should continue with police permission and relocate if need be. Referring to the court order, Pawar said, Now in Pune city there is no dedicated protest place. The police check whether there are any homes, buildings, schools, hospitals, and if not then there is no problem giving permission. We have chosen this spot because there is nothing other than trees here, it is in between two crematoriums, Pawar said. Meanwhile Pawar also said one of the protesters on hunger strike, Rushikesh Gangates sugar had dropped to a dangerous level, and that no government doctors had visited the site throughout the day. Pawar added that discussions had taken place between him and the state government on Wednesday, and that the government might send some ministers for discussions with the protesters in Pune. We will not go to Mumbai, he said. Congress MP Praniti Shinde, Samajwadi Party MLA Rais Shaikh, Sujat Ambedkar of the Vanchit Bahujan Aghadi, and satire singer Neha Singh Rathore were some others who joined the protest on Wednesday night and spoke to the students.

articleTitle: KPSC chairman Sahukar, member Geetha took bribes to leak answer keys
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka Public Service Commission job racket, KPSC recruitment scam, Shivashankarappa Sahukar, Karnataka KPSC scam, KPSC chairman daughter recruitment, Suma Sahukar income certificate case, KPSC veterinary doctor paper leak .Karnataka veterinary recruitment scam. Shivashankarappa Sahukar CID probe, KPSC question paper leak, Karnataka High Court KPSC case, KPSC corruption allegations, Basavaraj Kannale KPSC scam, Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar arrest, 400 veterinary doctors recruitment scam, Karnataka government job scam, Express investigation, KPSC recruitment controversy
description: Sahukar reportedly leaked the keys to an aspirant for a Rs 10 lakh advance, who subsequently secured the third rank, while Geetha allegedly provided them to the first-rank winner for a Rs 20 lakh advance.
body_raw: An Enforcement Directorate ED probe has revealed that the now-suspended Karnataka Public Service Commission KPSC chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar and KPSC member B V Geetha allegedly leaked answer keys for the January 6 veterinary doctors recruitment exam in exchange for bribes. Sahukar reportedly leaked the keys to an aspirant for a Rs 10 lakh advance, who subsequently secured the third rank, while Geetha allegedly provided them to the first-rank winner for a Rs 20 lakh advance. They were arrested by the ED on Tuesday following a probe into allegations of money laundering by KPSC officials through job frauds in the Commission with a specific reference to the fraud in the recruitment of veterinary doctors for Karnataka. The EDs findings with respect to Sahukar and Geetha were presented in court on Wednesday, where the agency submitted that the two had obtained the answer keys for 80 questions prepared for the entrance exam from the now-arrested KPSC Controller of Exams and IAS officer, Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar, and supplied it to as many as six candidates. Incidentally, Gangwar and a middleman Basavaraj Kannale were earlier arrested for allegedly leaking up to 80 questions to as many as 11 aspirants for bribes ranging from Rs 20 lakh to Rs 40 lakh. In the case of the previous arrests, it was the questions that were leaked. Here, in this case, it is the answer keys, the ED counsel Madhu N Rao told the court. This is a different modus operandi from the first cases, he added. The ED probe has found that four other candidates - the eight, ninth, 11th and 12th rank winners - were also given access to answer keys by Sahukar and Geetha. The probe found that Geetha gave the names of six aspirants to Exam Controller Gangwar and he, in turn, looked at the seating arrangement for them in the exam hall and then provided the answer keys for the specific set of question papers they would receive on the exam day, the ED counsel said. Only 80 answers For 100 questions were given, and the candidates were asked to memorise them. This is why these candidates have all got the same answers wrong in the exam, the counsel added. The ED has shown prima facie that the two accused were misusing their positions for leakage of answer keys to the two candidates for consideration of illegal gratification of Rs 20 lakh and Rs 10 lakh respectively, the special court said while remanding Sahukar and Geetha to EDs custody till October 19. The ED probe also prima facie discloses that Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar, VH the third rank candidate, her father, NB the first rank candidate and his father, and Shivashankarappa Sahukar and B V Geetha were connected with monetary transactions. the court observed. The ED has taken the two accused into custody until October 19 to probe transactions with other selected candidates and to find the money trail from the bribes.

articleTitle: Pregnant woman, 2 children among 3 killed as building collapses in Delhi
articleFeaturedImageAlt: delhi news, Seemapuri Building Collapse, Seemapuri Building Collapse news, Delhi Seemapuri Building Collapse News, Delhi Seemapuri Building Collapse latest News, Breaking news, latest news, top news today, top news, big news break, indian express, india news, world news
description: “The building measured 225 sq ft. Some people have been rescued and sent to hospitals, but we suspect that two to three people are still trapped under the debris. They are talking... rescue operation is underway,” DCP R P Meena said.
body_raw: A pregnant woman and two children were killed and eight people, including a three-year-old, injured after a four-storey building collapsed in Northeast Delhis New Seemapuri on Wednesday afternoon, trapping people under the rubble. On Tuesday, when Delhi experienced earthquake tremors in the evening, the building had developed cracks, officials said. Within minutes of the collapse, residents started pulling people out of the rubble and took them to hospitals. Among those who rushed between the collapse site and hospitals looking for their loved ones was Reshma 24. She was looking for her younger sister Gulfisha 22, who was four months pregnant. Gulfisha had been walking through E Block with her four-year-old daughter Zoya when the building came crashing down around 3.10 pm. Her father received a call from Gulfisha after the collapse. She told him she was stuck under rocks. And she cant breathe, Reshma said. Reshma rushed to Rajiv Gandhi Hospital after being told that Gulfisha had been taken there. At the hospital, they say she is here at the collapse site. I came back, she said. Gulfisha was later identified as the pregnant woman who died. The identity of the two deceased children, one of whom is 12-years-old, had not been established by Wednesday evening. Zoya was among those initially feared trapped. Another one trapped was Hazra Khatun 42. She had been taking a walk near the building when it collapsed. She was just taking a walk here. Then I heard that a building had collapsed. When she didnt return, I came here, Haseena, her daughter, said. The collapse took place near the Idgah Machhli Mandi area. Four fire tenders were rushed to the spot. The building measured 225 sq ft. Some people have been rescued and sent to hospitals, but we suspect that two to three people are still trapped under the debris. They are talking. rescue operation is underway, DCP R P Meena said. In a statement, the MCD described the structure as a ground-plus-three-floor building located in a jhuggi jhopri area on about 25 square yards of DUSIB land. It said the building was around 20-25 years old and occupied. The building stood next to the mosque in the densely packed locality. The boundary wall of the mosque also collapsed in the impact, while walls of an adjoining building were damaged, the MCD added.Officials said demolition work was being carried out in the adjoining building. Three- and four-storey structures surround the mosque on three sides, leaving little open space. Much of the debris fell inside the mosque compound, said local residents. The building was owned by Anwar. His family members who stayed on the first three floors included his wife Salma 50 son Rehman 28 and wife Sakeena his daughters Nushrat and Ameena as well as Nushrats three-year-old son Abdaan. While Anwar, Ameena and Rehmans wife were not at home when the building collapsed, Nushrat is stuck under the debris, officials said. A tenant, also named Sakeena 35, lived on the upper floor, according to relatives. Ameena said the family had moved into the house around four months ago. My father has a junk shop on the ground floor, while my brother has another shop in a lane almost half a kilometre away. All of them were inside the house when it collapsed, she said.

articleTitle: Firing distance raised suspicion: How an ‘accidental’ shooting in Lonavala turned into a murder case
articleFeaturedImageAlt: accidental shooting in Lonavala, Lonavala accidental shooting, Lonavala police murder case, Motiram Marathe arrested, Advocate Abhay Manik Marathe, Lonavala lawyer shooting, Bhushi village property dispute, Hotel Motiram Lonavala, Sassoon Hospital post mortem, Sandeep Singh Gill SP, Lonavala city police station, family property dispute murder, 12 bore gun shooting Lonavala
description: Lonavala City police have arrested Motiram Marathe for allegedly shooting dead his 33-year-old grandson, advocate Abhay Manik Marathe, at Hotel Motiram in Bhushi village on Monday.
body_raw: A shooting initially reported as an accidental firing at a hotel in Lonavala turned into a murder investigation after the post-mortem examination found that the bullet had been fired from a distance of around 30 centimetres, police said. The investigation subsequently revealed a property dispute between the deceased and his 83-year-old grandfather, who later allegedly confessed to shooting him. Lonavala City police have arrested Motiram Marathe for allegedly shooting dead his 33-year-old grandson, advocate Abhay Manik Marathe, at Hotel Motiram in Bhushi village on Monday. Police have also booked four other family members for allegedly attempting to destroy evidence and conceal the crime. Family initially claimed accidental firing According to police, Motiram, who holds a valid licence for a 12-bore rifle that he used for hunting, was at the hotel when the incident took place. Motiram Marathe holds a valid arms licence for a 12-bore gun, which he used for hunting. The family said that the incident took place on Monday. They told police that Abhay was cleaning his grandfathers gun when the trigger was accidentally pulled and a bullet hit him in the chest, Superintendent of Police Sandeep Singh Gill said at a press conference on Tuesday. Lonavala City police initially registered the case as an accidental death after reaching the spot. However, officers began to suspect that the familys account did not match the circumstances at the scene. Police examined the firearm, the injury to Abhays chest and the bloodstains on the wall, and sent the body to Sassoon Hospital for a post-mortem examination. The post-mortem findings further raised suspicion. Police said doctors found that the bullet had been fired from a distance of around 30 centimetres, making the claim of an accidental firing while cleaning the rifle difficult to establish. Property dispute emerges during probe As part of the investigation, police questioned family members as well as the hotel manager and staff. They found that Abhay and his grandfather had been involved in a dispute over land and its development. Motiram wanted to sell their land and distribute the money among family members however, Abhay had different plans for the land development, which led to the dispute, Gill said. Gill said the nature of the firearm also added to the suspicion. Also, a 12-bore rifle, which is around 4 to 4.5 feet long, so using it to fire towards self is difficult. So the suspicion increased. Even when inquired with the hotel staff and manager, they also said that for quite some time there have been quarrels between the two regarding financial and land-related matters, he said. Police said the two were at the restaurant counter of Hotel Motiram around 11 am on Monday when they had a heated argument. During the argument, Motiram allegedly took his licensed 12-bore rifle and shot Abhay in the chest. The bullet proved fatal. Police said the two had a history of disagreements over land and financial matters. Police allege attempt to destroy evidence The investigation also led police to suspect an attempt to cover up the shooting. According to Gill, CCTV cameras near the spot were allegedly removed and the DVR containing the footage was taken away. Police also alleged that hotel staff were threatened against speaking about the incident. The body was displaced to a different location and even the weapons were taken away to a different location. So we have booked five of the family members, Gill said. Police said that while it was initially difficult to determine whether the shooting was accidental or deliberate because family members maintained that it was an accidental firing, the post-mortem findings and subsequent investigation strengthened the murder suspicion. Police said Motiram later confessed to the crime. Initially the family members denied but the accused Motiram confessed to the crime. The three family members-Motiram Marathe, Hiraman Motiram Marathe, and Manoj Hiraman Marathe-have been granted police custody till October 12, Sachin Patil, senior police inspector, Lonavala City police station, told The Indian Express. Police have also booked Kavita Hiraman Marathe and Rajashree Dashrath Pawar, sister of Hiraman Marathe. Marathe familys business  political links Abhay was the son of Manik Marathe, a former councillor of the Lonavala municipal council. The Marathe family owns Hotel Motiram and Manik Moti in Bhushi village and is involved in the beer bar business. The family also runs a petrol pump in Lonavala, according to people familiar with the family. Macchindra Kharade, former Shiv Sena Pune district chief and a close associate of Manik Marathe, said the family had been living together for several years. The Marathe family has always been involved in business. Motiram Marathe has three sons and a daughter-Rajashree, Hiraman, Manik, and Ratan, the youngest son. All the family members, even Motirams brother, used to live together. It was rare to see such a huge joint family still living together, Kharade said. He said Manik had been active in local politics while also managing the family businesses. According to Kharade, Manik had contested the Lonavala municipal council election on an NCP ticket in 2011 and later won as a Shiv Sena candidate in 2016. He contested the 2025 election from Shiv Sena UBT but was defeated. Ratan is currently the Bhushi ward chief of Shiv Sena UBT, Kharade said. Though Manik had been in politics, he had limited presence as he also used to manage family businesses. Abhay was married and also used to help in their family business. And it was shocking for Lonavala residents that such an incident had happened, Kharade said. A tea stall owner in Lonavala said, The Marathe family had been prominent in the area for several decades and had also been associated with religious and community activities during the annual Kanifnath Maharaj yatra held in Lonavala during Rangpanchami.

articleTitle: The hidden crisis in Indian classrooms: Why teachers are quitting before year five
articleFeaturedImageAlt: World Teachers' Day 2026
description: UNESCO lists attractive career pathways with equitable access to professional development as a key to keep teachers motivated. Does it mean that primary school teaching is not considered an attractive pathway?
body_raw: World Teachers Day is held annually on October 5, exactly a month after we celebrate our teachers and their work. UNESCO commemorates the anniversary of the adoption of the Recommendation concerning the Status of Teachers in 1966, which set the benchmarks regarding the rights and responsibilities of teachers, and standards for their professional preparation and employment. In 2026, while we mark its 60th anniversary, UNESCO brings to our attention the new difficulties that have emerged for teachers from digital technologies, climate change, migration and displacement. These pressures adversely affect teachers work and status, which have always been insufficiently valued in all systems. Their lower status is marked by limited professional autonomy and voice in policymaking. UNESCOs Global Report on Teachers 2023 warned us that teachers are leaving the profession within the first five years of practice, especially at the primary level. The report classified teacher shortage as a pervasive phenomenon, which is a result of several factors including low motivation, sluggish recruitment practices, weak professional preparation, difficult working conditions, and low status. These, in turn, have consequences including increased workloads on the remaining teachers, compromised sense of well-being, and discouragement of prospective teachers. The UNESCO report mentions a shortage of 7.8 million teachers in South Asia, including India. Let us pay attention to two factors, namely teacher motivation and preparation, to understand why teachers are leaving, especially at the primary level. UNESCO lists attractive career pathways with equitable access to professional development as a key to keep teachers motivated. Does it mean that primary school teaching is not considered an attractive pathway? Well, it is not even a pathway because it is one of the most stagnant recruitments in our system. The experience of teaching at the primary level is not counted in the eligibility to become a school principal. Secondary teachers who get appointed as principals make further progress by playing a role in policymaking as they eventually join the bureaucracy. More than 70 years after Independence, we realise that in educational policymaking, school-based decision-making and administration, the wisdom of primary teachers has remained absent. The wisdom and knowledge that they must be gaining by teaching and managing the beginners - which include millions of first-generation learners - simply get lost. The loss is two-fold, as the system loses out on a resource and has to pull on with a large number of teachers whose enthusiasm and aspirations dissipate. Let us turn to the factor of teacher preparation, an Achilles heel for the Indian system. It is a connecting point between school and university systems but a weak one. Indian universities have shown persistent reluctance in playing a catalyst role in teacher preparation, especially for the primary level. A small-scale but major breakthrough was made in the 1990s when Delhi University DU institutionalised its first-ever four-year integrated professional degree programme of elementary teacher education, namely, Bachelor of Elementary Education B.El.Ed.. It marked DUs attempt to locate teacher preparation for elementary level, earlier a constitutional dream, later a commitment, within the ambit of a central university. B.El.Ed. graduates emerged as elementary teachers who drew their identity from being the teachers of children rather than transmitters of a school subject. B.El.Ed. thus became a landmark as its graduates developed professional commitment and resilience to remain in the system and improve it, highlighted by the UNESCO report as an important means to address teacher shortage. This small achievement brought to the fore a dilemma that teacher preparation encapsulates in India. Should we train teachers or educate them? In educational discourse, training has been associated with tricks of the trade that the trainees acquire by practising certain actions such as modulation of voice while explaining something. Training emphasises trainee-teachers dependence on being trained by others in skills and practices, but remains weak on the important principle of autonomous pursuit of knowledge. The emphasis in teaching is upon a relationship between the teacher and their students in a carefully developed learning ethos. Teaching demands from the teacher a persistent interest in the learning process of their students, which involves command over knowledge and recognition of the specificities that the students bring with them. The specificities emerge from disparities involving caste, poverty, gender, language, tribal affiliations, and so on. Teaching emphasises the focus on interaction between the minds of a teacher and their students. Approaching teacher preparation as training has its origins in the colonial system of education centred on the limited purpose of the transmission of textbook content. The roots of training orientation have proved strong, as one notices its presence even in the reports of progressive commissions. The term teacher education gained mild popularity as it was used in the recent policy documents, but the system retained the training orientation as the basic features of the programs of teacher preparation remained intact. The recent changes in teacher preparation, made under the framework of NEP 2020, reinforce the colonial format of training. The policy aims at extreme homogenisation by replacing all the teacher education programmes with the Integrated Teacher Education Programme ITEP, which is a new name for yesteryears BA As the university system in India moved to a four-year UG degree programme, the teacher education programmes received a casual and unspecialised treatment. The general higher education prescriptions are being applied to them. Thus, ITEP is wobbling between the tedious and meandering calculations of credits and dual degree arrangements, giving structural priority to content rather than specificities of the learners and teachers autonomy. With inadequate preparation and the pressure of new challenges, the teachers find it difficult to meet the demands that teaching a group of young minds poses. They quit early or remain demotivated. No wonder that the UNESCO report does not include India in the list of hopeful countries that could address the teacher shortage by 2030. Honouring a few teachers is not enough. We need to modernise their preparation and take policy-level steps to address the lower status of primary teachers. The writer teaches education at Delhi University

articleTitle: ‘3 ICC trophies, 2 Asia Cups, back-to-back Asian Games gold’: BCCI lauds outgoing selector Agarkar

body_raw: The Board of Control for Cricket in India BCCI has lauded outgoing chairman of selectors Ajit Agarkar for his commitment, conviction and contribution over the last three years, as his tenure officially came to an end. Agarkars term concluded last month, and the BCCI on Tuesday invited applications to fill the vacant post, following weeks of speculation over whether he would be considered for an extension. A tenure marked by some truly special moments for Indian cricket - three ICC trophies, two Asia Cup titles and back-to-back Asian Games Gold medals, along with a run to the 2023 ODI World Cup final, the BCCI posted on its official X account. Thank you, Mr Ajit Agarkar for your commitment, conviction and contribution as Chairman of the Mens Selection Committee. Wishing you the very best for the journey ahead, the apex cricket governing body added. A tenure marked by some truly special moments for Indian cricket - three ICC trophies, two Asia Cup titles and back-to-back Asian Games Gold medals, along with a run to the 2023 ODI World Cup final. Thank you, Mr Ajit Agarkar imAagarkar, for your commitment, conviction and contribution as Chairman of the Mens Selection Committee. Wishing you the very best for the journey ahead. - BCCI BCCI October 7, 2026 India won the 2024 and 2026 T20 World Cups, along with the 2025 Champions Trophy, during Agarkars tenure. He also oversaw a significant transition that involved the T20 and Test retirements of batting greats Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma. History would be kinder The BCCIs message followed head coach Gautam Gambhirs note of thanks to Agarkar earlier in the day. Gambhir said history would be kinder to Agarkar, whose conviction in the team first theory was crucial to India winning three ICC trophies during his tenure. Dear Ajit Bhai, an absolute honour to work with you. Those 3 ICC trophies are a testimony of your conviction Team first  Team ahead, always. I must say, History will be kinder to you. articleTitle: Khushbu Sundar’s skincare routine at 56: ‘I do it every day for half an hour or so’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Actor Khushbu Sundar
description: The actor has a simple approach to starting her day and caring for her skin
body_raw: Tamil actor and politician Khushbu Sundar, 56, recently revealed her everyday routine, including waking up early and a few skincare hacks. I am an early riser. I wake up by 4.30 am-5 am. I make tea for everyone at home in the morning. So, I put raw milk on my face. Sometimes, I use saffron strands and use the water on my face. Sometimes, I just massage with coconut oil or almond oil.depending on my mood. I do it every day for half an hour or so, the Aranmanai 4 actor told Maalai Malar in a video interview. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. Is this skincare routine safe for anyone to follow? Traditional skincare practices such as applying raw milk, saffron-infused water or natural oils have been followed for generations, and many people enjoy them as part of their morning routine. However, it is important to understand that natural does not always mean suitable for every skin type. Raw milk, for instance, can contain microorganisms and may not be ideal for direct application, particularly on sensitive or acne-prone skin, pointed out Dr Shareefa Chause, dermatologist, Dr Shareefa Skin Care Clinic, Mumbai. Similarly, coconut oil and almond oil can moisturise some people, but they may feel heavy or clog pores in those prone to acne or folliculitis, Dr Chause remarked. Saffron-infused water is generally used as a traditional beauty practice, but there is limited scientific evidence to suggest that it can change the skins appearance, said Dr Chause. She also mentioned to indianexpress.com that regular massages may make the skin feel relaxed and temporarily improve circulation, but vigorous rubbing should be avoided as it can irritate the skin, stressed Dr Chause. Dr Chause also noted that you should do a patch test before applying these ingredients. A simple routine with a gentle cleanser, moisturiser and broad-spectrum sunscreen remains the foundation of good skin health. So, make sure to consult an expert before trying any home remedies, said Dr Chause. Rather than treating every wrinkle or change in facial appearance as something that needs correcting, accepting that skin and the body naturally change with age can take some of the pressure out of beauty routines, remarked consultant dietitian Garima Goyal. At the same time, taking care of the skin and seeking professional dermatological advice when needed can coexist with ageing naturally, said Goyal. And this fits into a broader picture of health. Khushbus recent weight loss journey has also involved walking, yoga and dietary changes over several years, rather than relying on a quick transformation. Whether it is waking up early, caring for your skin, or staying physically active, the real benefit comes from sustainable habits. Healthy ageing is less about chasing perfection and more about taking care of yourself consistently, said Goyal.
