articleTitle: How Amitabh Bachchan & Amish Tripathi are taking Indian mythology global through gaming
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The Age of Bhaarat - Visual (1)
description: The Age of Bhaarat is a dark fantasy action adventure game that draws on Indian epics and traditions.
body_raw: Ancient India is a land of noble heroes and glittering cities. But, where heroes rule, villains will attack. Where wealth is plentiful, plunderers will pillage, says Amitabh Bachchan in the trailer of the game, The Age of Bhaarat. Your time has come to declare war, he says as the screen crackles with images of fire bursting out of the ruins of grand sculptured pillars. Bachchan is the co-founder of Tara Gaming Ltd, gamemakers for PCs and consoles that features mythical landscapes and magical characters and stories drawn from the Indian epics. The other eminent founder is Amish Tripathi, author of Shiva Trilogy. Tara Gamings vision is a large franchise that is aimed at telling Indian stories in a way that resonates worldwide. The Age of Bhaarat, for instance, is a dark fantasy action-adventure game that draws on Indian epics and traditions to inspire an international audience to undertake a journey of an ordinary person who becomes a powerful Forest Warden armed with magical capabilities. This is possibly Indias first AAA action adventure game, which is the hallmark of a high profile, big-budget game of top production capability. The game is currently under development and is expected to hit the markets in a couple of years. The studio where the game is being developed is in Pune. There is an immense combination of the richness of mythology, their novelty to the West, their relevance in India and the talent in India and, particularly, in Pune. When we started, the first thing we did was hiring a head for a studio in Pune, Siddharth Singh. In about 18 months, we grew the studio to 85 people, says executive chairman Nicolas Granatino. Gaming has caught the interest of the Central government as well. In the Union Budget this year, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman had spoken of the rapid growth of Indias animation, visual effects, gaming and comics AVGC sector, he added. Singh said, a lot of times, the Indian industry has worked as vendors or outsourcers for foreign companies. They come in and give us a part of the work. Not a lot of companies in India have done this kind of large-scale execution, from the initial ideation and concept phase all the way through to the final launch. So, not many people have actually seen or experienced the entire lifecycle of game development in India, and thats where Tara Gaming is different. We have also managed to bring together the right kind of talent, says Singh. While Tripathi is responsible for crafting the lore of the game, Bachchan is involved in the creative process and provides the voiceover for the games trailer. The rest of the team is equally rooted to the story. Success is not only bringing a successful game and these stories to the world. For us, success is that some of the people in the studio in Pune will leave a few years from now and create their own studio, because they will have seen the production of the game from scratch. Thats a very different way to train and upskill and work with talent in India, says Granatino.

articleTitle: Sujeet Kalkal wants the mat, not the functions, before the World Championships
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sujeet
description: The Asian Games champion, who has won 19 bouts in a row, says the ground game is what he must fix before Kazakhstan
body_raw: Wrestler Sujeet Kalkal has had a great week. He brought the mens 65 kg freestyle gold home from the Asian Games after defeating Olympic champion Kotaro Kiyooka of Japan in the semi-final and winning the final from 2-9 down. He also won the Raja Randhir Singh award for the best Indian male athlete at the Asian Games 2026. However, the 23-year-old from Charkhi Dadri doesnt want to lose himself in the celebrations right now.After winning the Asian Games medal, there are some distractions like functions and everything. But I want to go back to the mat as soon as possible, Sujeet said at an interaction organised by SAI Media. He is right to want to get back to the mat a tough World Championships awaits him in Kazakhstan, starting October 24. Sujeet is on a dominant run in the mens 65 kg category. He is the reigning U23 World Champion, Asian champion and Asian Games gold medallist. Since losing the bronze-medal match at last years World Championships, Sujeet has won 19 bouts in a row and is unbeaten at the national level too. The World Championships will bring new challenges the Iranian powerhouse Rahman Amouzadkhalili, to whom Sujeet lost last year, and the American prodigy Bowen Bassett, who beat Worlds bronze medallist Real Marshall Ray Woods in the US trials. The competition level in the World Championships is very tough and it is not going to be easy for me. It is certainly more competitive than the Asian Games and that is what makes it more exciting. This is the most important competition for me, Sujeet said. But he has a few things to fine-tune before he goes for a world title. I need to learn from the mistakes that I made in the past competitions. So, I am going to focus on that, he said.  Sujeets Asian Games campaign was near flawless, but he gave away easy points at the start of bouts, especially in positions played out on the mat. One of the reasons that Sujeet trailed in the final was that he gave a more advantageous position to the opponent on the ground. That is something we are going to work on in this small time frame we have got, his coach Kuldeep Singh told The Indian Express. Sujeet agrees. Both my coaches Kuldeep and Shako have asked me to take a strong position on the ground. I am working on it. Right now, I need to attack on the ground well and also defend if I lose the attacking position, he explained. The other thing he has to do more of is attack, something national coach Bentinidis Shako also insists on. Before the Asian Games, I had played a tournament in Russia. I won that tournament and every bout in it. But coach Shako was not happy with it, Sujeet said. He told me to attack more as I have a variety of attacks. He did that at the Asian Games, but will need to do more of it at the World Championships. I worked on it and executed it during the Asian Games. That is why I was able to score so many points. I think I will need to continue doing this at the World Championships, said Sujeet. Shako, who also coached Bajrang Punia to an Olympic medal, has brought attacking changes to Sujeets game. One of the highlights of Sujeets Asian Games campaign was his use of the dhobi pachad in the bout against the Iranian wrestler. It is a classic Indian kushti technique that uses the opponents momentum and a tight upper-body grip to lift and arc them over the shoulder or back. I have to thank coach Shako for that. I used to try the technique in practice but never really executed it on the mat. But coach Shako made some corrections to it. He asked me to practice it over and over. I think I executed it because of the regular practice of the move, said Sujeet. Sujeet has less than 15 days to finish with the functions, work on his ground wrestling and head to Astana, Kazakhstan, where he could become only the second Indian to win a wrestling world title.

articleTitle: In Andhra, poll officers told to make videos of voter recertification exercise
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The ECI has also said that anyone whose name is left out during or after SIR, including young and first-time voters, can apply for inclusion through continuous updation.
description: Authorities said this was meant to ensure transparency, with the CEO also directing DEOs to keep their social media handles active and post at least two photos and two videos each day.
body_raw: Andhra Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer Vivek Yadav has asked District Election Officers to post photos and videos of the re-verification of Absentee, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate and Others ASDDO category electors, officials said - a development that comes as election officials embark on an exercise to re-verify the status of the electors not included in the draft electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision process. According to officials, DEOs have been asked to record photos and videos of BLOs testimonials during the door-to-door re-verification exercise, as well as those of young and first-time voters, and voters whose names were deleted from the draft rolls but eventually added after the notice phase. Testimonials relating to claims, objections and the notice phase, videos of Electoral Registration Officers EROs briefing BLOs, and those of DEOs campaigns in colleges for first-time voters are also to be recorded. Authorities said this was meant to ensure transparency, with the CEO also directing DEOs to keep their social media handles active and post at least two photos and two videos each day. The posts must tag the CEO and the ECI, mention the names of polling stations, the Assembly constituency and district, and carry the tagline No eligible voter is left out. The CEO said that from October 8, BLOs will conduct door-to-door visits with lists of electors who were not included in the draft roll for verification. The lists include 44,89,512 electors who were not found at their given addresses during the enumeration phase from June 15 to July 24 this year, as well as another 1,73,071 electors found ineligible during the notice phase. Eligible voters whose names were inadvertently left out will be facilitated to submit Form 6 for inclusion in the electoral rolls. The final roll will be published on October 16. Any voter left out of the final October 16 roll and voters becoming newly eligible to vote can submit Form 6, the office of the chief electoral officer said.

articleTitle: Even if Gyanesh Kumar resigns, we won’t stop: CJP, students on Jantar Mantar protest
articleFeaturedImageAlt: AISA National President Neha Bora addresses a joint press conference at the Press Club of India, New Delhi on Wednesday. CJP Chief spokesperson Sourav Das, SFI and ASAP representatives also present. (ANI Photo)
description: Saurav Das, CJP co-convener, reached the Parliament Street police station in the morning to submit the letter to the DCP's office.
body_raw: Announcing a joint protest at Delhis Jantar Mantar on October 10 against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, the Cockroach Janta Party CJP and several student organisations on Wednesday submitted a formal intimation letter to the Delhi Police informing them about the proposed agitation. Saurav Das, CJP co-convener, reached the Parliament Street police station in the morning to submit the letter to the DCPs office. Asked whether they sought permission for the protest, Das said, Please dont use the word permission. Who is Delhi Police to give us permission? Maintaining that intimation is sufficient, he added that they provided undertakings to the police. We will cooperate with Delhi Police and we hope Delhi Police will cooperate with us, he said. After handing over the letter, Das, along with All India Students Association AISA president Neha Bora and others, held a press conference at the Press Club of India. The press conference brought together CJP, AISA, All India Students Federation AISF and Students Federation of India SFI. The Aam Aadmi Partys student wing, Association of Students for Alternative Politics ASAP, also participated. Das urged people across the country to travel to Delhi and to come prepared for a prolonged agitation. This fight is not going to be easy. I appeal to everyone across the country to join us, book train and flight tickets, he said. Even if Kumar resigns, the protesters will not step back because the electoral system needs to be cleaned up, he added. We not only demand the removal of Gyanesh Kumar but also the appointment of a new CEC in a democratic manner. It is high time that democratic reforms are carried out in the electoral roll system so that no other Gyanesh Kumar can commit vote chori in the future. He also demanded that a criminal case be registered against Kumar for allegedly carrying out irregularities in the electoral roll process. Das alleged that they had received information that Delhi Police personnel were harassing female protesters and that right-wing groups were being mobilised to disrupt the October 10 protest. Citing a September 23 report in The Indian Express, Bora said, Whatever our suspicions regarding the electoral rolls were found to be correct. The report had revealed that two of the three Election Commissioners - Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi - had recorded at least 14 objections over 10 months, including controversial changes made to Form 6 and handling of voter deletions during the Special Intensive Revision SIR process, among others. Since then, we have been seeing protests on the streets demanding the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar. The call given by people like Yogendra Yadav, Manoj Jha, Prashant Bhushan and Anjali Bhardwaj proved that, in the coming days, the fight needs to be carried out in a consolidated and united manner. That is how we fought and showed our unity during the July education-related movement, she added. The October 2 protest called by AISA in Delhi and CJP in Mumbai witnessed a huge participation of people, she said. This shows that vote theft is the biggest issue in this country right now. Backing the INDIA bloc MPs who tried to march towards the EC office on Tuesday demanding Kumars resignation, Bora said elected representatives have a duty to take to the streets to raise peoples issues and defend their rights. Thats what the MPs of the INDIA bloc did, she said. Meanwhile, Delhi Police officers said the protest would not be allowed as prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita were in force across Parliament Street and adjoining areas. In July, a CJP-led agitation over the NEET paper leak had forced Dharmendra Pradhan to resign as Union Education minister.

articleTitle: ‘Charles Sobhraj of Kashmir’ sold land he didn’t own, tracked via newspaper subscription
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Kashmir: The Crime Branch sleuths got alerted. “Why would someone tap on a door with no one inside?” said an official connected with the probe. (File Photo)
description: J&K Police arrested an 80-year-old former Ayurvedic doctor accused of cheating buyers in fake land deals using multiple identities and forged documents.
body_raw: In hot pursuit of this man, JK Police arrived at a house in Zewan area in Srinagars outskirts on September 24. A woman who answered the door told them that he had already left. The personnel asked her to show them the room where he stayed. The woman led them and, gingerly, tapped on the door. This was when the Crime Branch sleuths got alerted. Why would someone tap on a door with no one inside? said an official connected with the probe. The team instinctively spread out some barged into the room, others secured the windows. Inside,an elderly man sat under a dim light, his favourite Urdu newspaper in hand, with little knowledge that it was this love for the broadsheet that landed police at the door of the house where he had been hiding all this while. He is Somnath Koul. Or Mohan Lal Dhar. Or Brijnath Bhat. Or Hadinath Dhar. It depends on whom you ask, or which identity document he chooses to produce. But the police department in the Union Territory already had a moniker for him Charles Sobhraj of Kashmir. Police say that for almost a decade now, Koul, now 80, had been swindling Valley residents with promises of selling them land left behind by Kashmiri Pandit migrants like himself. To some, he would pose as an attorney facilitating the sale. In other cases, he would pose as the owner himself, beguiling the potential buyers with his story of having to leave his home due to the onset of militancy in the 1990s. None of the land that he wanted to sell belonged to him in the first place, said a police officer. Koul would identify the land left behind by the Pandits, strike a deal with prospective buyers with forged documents, collect the money and disappear, the officer added. That was until January this year when police found Kouls photograph affixed to one of the fake sale documents. It set off a nine-month-long hunt that eventually uncovered a trail of fraudulent land deals dating as far back as 2017. The hunt In November last year, a south Kashmir resident approached the Economic Offences Wing EOW of the Crime Branch, stating that he had bought five kanals a little over half an acre of land at Drusoo village in Pulwama and 300 poplar trees planted on a parcel of land in Bijbehara after paying Rs 93 lakh. The complainant said that when he went to court for ratification of Agreement to Sell, he was told that the land doesnt belong to the person shown as seller in the agreement. On April 1 this year, the Crime Branch registered a formal FIR against Koul, setting off an investigation in motion. It was a piece of land belonging to a migrant Kashmiri Pandit and Koul had posed as the owners attorney. In the case of the Bijbehara property, he claimed to be the owner himself, said an investigating officer. When we contacted the actual owner, he told us he had not given anyone a power of attorney.  The Agreement to Sell listed Koul as a resident of a locality in Jammu with an alternate address in Bengaluru. But when police teams reached the two addresses, Koul was nowhere to be found. But the so-called agreement offered police a crucial clue. The witness Ghulam Mohidin Dar, a resident of Budgam in central Kashmir, had signed the document as a witness. In August, Crime Branch sleuths reached his house. Dar told the officials he would change his clothes and accompany them. We were waiting for him when his family members attacked us, an officer said. In the melee, Dar managed to escape. On September 17, after a 10-kilometre chase from Rajbagh to Kanipora, Dar was nabbed. Police investigations revealed that Dar, himself an influential land broker, would lure the buyers for Koul. This is when police started learning about Kouls multiple identities. Said to be a retired Ayurvedic doctor, Kouls name in his service records is Brijnath Bhat. He owns two Voter Identity cards and two Aadhaar cards each. In one voter card, he is Brijnath Bhat. In the other, he is Hadinath Dhar. His two Aadhaar cards identify him as Somnath Koul and Mohan Lal Dhar, respectively. Of the four documents, only one could be genuine. We checked with the Aadhaar database, his name was recorded as Somnath Koul, says an officer. It was a mystery for us. If his name in so-called service records was Brijnath Bhat, how could he make an Aadhaar in the name of Somnath Koul? Finger tips damaged, iris altered As the mystery about his identity deepened, police decided to go for biometrics. It threw up more surprises. He had destroyed his fingertips. When we asked him about it, he said he had accidentally burnt them, the officer said. His iris scans too failed many times. The official at the Aadhaar centre said he most likely had an eye surgery. We really had a hard time getting one of his iris scans matched. The officials went through his Aadhaar records and were left befuddled once more. In 2016, Koul applied for an Aadhaar card in the name of Brijnath Bhat, a resident of Muthi in Jammu. The name matched his service records. In 2022, he, however, changed the name on his Aadhaar to Somnath Koul. We are checking how it happened, the officer said. The Agreement to sell also showed his name as Somnath Koul. The man himself, though, remained elusive, prompting JK police to liken him with Charles Sobhraj-the famous con artist. But interrogating Dar, police came upon a curious piece of information. Koul was an avid reader of newspapers. Apart from his favourite one published from the Valley, he would also subscribe to a bunch of newspapers from Jammu. Police began keeping a track of this unique bunch of reading material, which finally landed them at the house of his acquaintance in Zewan. Back at the Crime Branch, officials went through its own database to check cases against different identities assumed by Koul. They found at least four other cases, the oldest one dating back to 2017 and registered at the EOW of the Crime Branch. The three other cases were registered in the EOW and Special Crime Wing from 2021 to 2026. Past cases The complainant in the first case, police said, knew him as Brijnath Bhat. In his complaint, a villager stated that Koul posed himself as an attorney for a piece of land at Goshabugh in Pattan, Baramulla. A deal was done for 11 kanals and 3 marlas, a little less than one-and-a-half acre, for Rs 55 lakh. The parcel included some pieces of land belonging to Kashmiri Pandit migrants. After the complainant paid Rs 9.17 lakh in advance, Koul disappeared without a trace. In 2021, Koul again posed as an attorney, out to sell one-and-a-half kanal of Pandit land at Gulab Bagh Pandach in Srinagar. This time, he again identified himself as Brijnath Bhat. After allegedly taking Rs 47 lakh from the buyer, he disappeared. Police filed a chargesheet in absentia. Two years later, police received two more complaints. Koul allegedly promised the same piece of land to two different buyers at Humhama near the Srinagar airport. To one man, he identified himself as Brijnath Bhat. To the other, he was Hadinath Dhar. He took a combined total of Rs 1 crore from the two men and disappeared, said police. In the latest case, he had taken Rs 15 lakh from his buyer before doing the vanishing act, and being arrested months later. With his arrest, JK Police have finally learnt that the man they compared with Charles Sobhraj, a criminal known for his flamboyance, is a frail former Ayurvedic doctor with a penchant for the good old newspaper. Koul, or Bhat, is now in Srinagar Central Jail serving judicial custody. It was his love for the newspapers that finally proved to be his undoing, said an officer connected with the probe. SSP Speaks Senior Superintendent of police, Crime branch Economic Offices Wing Kashmir Abdul Waheed Shah said that they are taking the activities of this land mafia very seriously because it has been ruining lives and families. We ensure that every such complaint is investigated thoroughly so that the perpetrators of such crime are brought to justice. When a family buys a piece of land, they spend most of their hard earned savings. Once they are defrauded, it completely ruins that entire family, he said. We are taking strict action against the brokers as well as any officials involved in such frauds. We have been focused on exposing these fraudsters and dismantling their networks. Our law enforcement also helps raise awareness among public to stay vigilant against such fraud.

articleTitle: Inside Gukesh’s transformation from ‘lone wolf’ to being the life of team meetings at Chess Olympiad
articleFeaturedImageAlt: World champion D Gukesh on a sail boat during the Norway Chess Games day in Oslo during the recent Norway Chess tournament. (Express Photo by Amit Kamath)
description: At the Chess Olympiad, the world saw a different side of Gukesh. As Vidit Gujrathi and Sankalp Gupta, who have been with the Indian team for multiple Olympiad editions say: “On-the-board Gukesh and off-the-board Gukesh are almost like two different people.”
body_raw: During the recent Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, world champion Gukesh D did something he had rarely ever done in public before. He cracked a joke. Sitting at the airport on his way back after helping Indias open section team to a silver medal, Gukesh shot a video with Praggnanandhaa where he told his teammate that a fan had approached him for a photo but could not recollect his name, before eventually mistaking him for Pragg. Guys remember, this is Gukesh, he said cheekily pointing at Pragg, . and Im Pragg, Gukesh joked, while his compatriot smiled good-naturedly. In that short, one-minute clip, Gukesh had shown the world a glimpse of his other side the goofier, 20-year-old version of himself that fans have seldom seen during chess tournaments. On-the-board Gukesh and off-the-board Gukesh are very different, explains Vidit Gujrathi, who was also a part of the Olympiad team. Sankalp Gupta, who has also been a coach with the Indian team for multiple editions and has seen Gukeshs fun-loving side first hand during the Turkish League in 2023, adds On-the-board Gukesh and off-the-board Gukesh are almost like two different people.  But even those who have seen both sides of Gukesh were pleasantly surprised by the version of him that they saw at this Olympiad. For the past 18 months, the 20-year-old looked like he was struggling under the twin burdens of dwindling form and the weight of expectations. At the Chennai Grand Masters, his last tournament before the Olympiad, he did not win a single match. Then, something changed. Around August, after he played the Chennai Grand Masters, I started seeing a change in Gukesh. He was learning surfing, doing a bit of skating, trying all these new things. He was spending some time away from chess trying to have fun. The same thing carried over to the Olympiad as well. He was having a lot of fun. When we had our online training camp for the Olympiad, as soon as Gukesh joined, the vibe got lighter, says Srinath Narayanan, the captain of the Indian mens Olympiad team. ALSO READ  Gukeshs coach Gajewski Good for him to be reminded he can play really well Srinath traces how Gukesh changed over successive Olympiads. Theres been an incredible difference with Gukesh every year. In 2022, when I was not captain of the team Gukesh was in India 2, the story I heard was that Gukesh wouldnt participate in team meetings. He would just turn up to play and win his individual games. In 2023 during the Asian Games, the players were not the best of friends. But before the Budapest Olympiad, I had a chat with the players. I felt something changed in Gukesh internally, that he really wanted to get along with the team and spend time with everyone, indulge in banter, attend team meetings, which became a ritual starting from the Budapest Olympiad, says Srinath. Sankalp Gupta adds At the 2022 Olympiad, Gukesh used to be completely different than he is currently. Im not saying this approach is better or that one was. Its just a different approach. He used to be like a lone wolf back in 2022. He would eat meals by himself, stay by himself. But in 2024, he would join team meetings. We had great team bonding that time, but Gukesh was still a bit reserved. Srinath explains that the distance that the players kept from each other a few years ago was understandable. For most of the year, they would be fighting for the same titles, facing off against each other repeatedly, and chasing the same opportunities. It was a scenario that previous members of Indias Olympiad teams had not faced. Bond between players But since Budapest 2024, the camaraderie and the banter in the India camp grew as have the bonds between players. Helping solidify the bond were multiple game-day rituals, like team walks, long meetings and a player-of-the-round award which Srinath points out was also an idea from Gukesh. At Samarkand, the banter was unparalleled, say Srinath and Sankalp. Much of it was initiated by Gukesh, who the coaches say was the funniest member of the Indian mens team at this edition, taking over the baton from Pentala Harikrishna, who would lighten the mood in previous Olympiad teams. Team meetings had a vibe that you would find in a typical boys hostel, says Srinath. At Budapest Olympics, the team meetings for initial rounds were just 5-10 minutes. By the time we played USA in round 10, meetings would just go for 40-45 minutes with a lot of casual banter, says Srinath. Srinath says at the ongoing Olympiad, Gukesh was professional when discussion turned to chess, but he also knew when to switch off. Gukesh felt that we should be more chill as a team. Players keep certain things, like opening preparation, personal. But they can still hang out together as friends outside of that, says Srinath. The biggest surprise came at the traditional Bermuda Party held after the 6th round. The team atmosphere was a bit gloomy that day because India had lost to Uzbekistan. Gukesh had taken a draw and Nihal had lost a game that he could have won. That evening, Gukesh and Vidit turned up at the Bermuda Party and Gukesh did another thing you would not expect him to do in the middle of a tournament. He danced. He even did an impression of Michael Jacksons moon walk. With the amount of cameras and attention on him, it was difficult for Gukesh to be able to do that in the past. But in Samarkand, he made a conscious decision that he is not going to care about all those things and he will just have fun like a normal 20-year-old, says Srinath.

articleTitle: New role for actor Mithun Chakraborty in Bengal government, with cabinet rank
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Mithun Chakraborty
description: The administrative circles believe that the scope of his responsibilities and his specific role as an advisor would become clear in the next steps.
body_raw: The West Bengal government on Wednesday appointed veteran actor and BJP leader Mithun Chakraborty as a cultural advisor with the rank of a Cabinet Minister. He has been appointed as an advisor in the Information and Culture Department with immediate effect, as per a recent notification issued by the Personnel and Administrative Reforms Department. The notification stated, The Governor is pleased to appoint Shri Mithun Chakraborty as Advisor to the Government of West Bengal in the rank of Cabinet Minister in the Information and Cultural Affairs Department, with an immediate effect and until further order. The administrative circles believe that the scope of his responsibilities and his specific role as an advisor would become clear in the next steps. According to sources in Nabanna, Mithun will take charge of the new post very soon. At present, the veteran actor is in Alipurduar for a shooting assignment. From there, Mithun has thanked Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari for entrusting him with this new responsibility. Recently, at the stage of the foundation-laying ceremony for the Uttam Kumar Film Centre in New Town, the Chief Minister had announced that Mithun Chakraborty would be appointed as the state governments cultural advisor, owing to his contributions to the film industry as well as his connection with West Bengal. The Suvendu Adhikari-led state government had also sought his advice during the centenary celebrations of Uttam Kumar, apart from several areas such as tourism. The veteran actor had joined the BJP in 2021. He also had a brief stint with the Trinamool Congress when Mamata Banerjee had nominated him for Rajya Sabha in 2014. However, he resigned from the Upper House in 2016. The veteran actor had joined the BJP in 2021. In a stellar career spanning five decades, Mithun has acted in and produced several films, earning the moniker Mahaguru The Great Teacher in the Bengali cinema world.

articleTitle: ‘They have come for me’: Kashmiri filmmaker Arfat Sheikh ‘detained by ICE agents’ at US airport
articleFeaturedImageAlt: arafat sheikh
description: Arfat grew up in the Valley and moved to the US as a student in 2019. As per a campaign seeking his release, he filed for asylum in 2020 and has been living in Virginia.
body_raw: A Kashmiri-born filmmaker, Arfat Sheikh, has allegedly been detained by the Immigration and Customs Enforcement ICE agents in the United States. Sheikhs film, Saffron Kingdom, has won several awards at American film festivals, and his storytelling is widely acclaimed. In a statement, filmmaker Tara Dorabji, who was accompanying Sheikh, said they were travelling together from San Francisco International Airport to Dulles on September 24. When we landed at Dulles, I was sitting towards the back of the plane, and Arfat exited before me. As I got off the plane, I walked by Arfat, without realising that he had been pulled aside on the jetway. Dorabji says that Arfat called out to her, and as she turned around, he was surrounded by numerous men. Arfat said to me, Tara, Tara. This is ICE. They have come for me. The men were in plain clothes and not wearing any uniforms that indicated that they were federal agents. During the entire interaction, I never saw any of the men present a warrant or say why they were taking Arfat. They took Arfat Sheikh off the jetway onto the tarmac. He did not resist. I was shaking and could barely move, she claimed. Dorabji is an author and filmmaker. Her documentary film series on human rights defenders in Kashmir won awards at more than a dozen film festivals in Asia and the US. The two were on their way to Washington, DC, for the Art as Resistance event at Busboys and Poets. A campaign to free Arfat has been launched by friends and acquaintances. In her statement, Dorabji emphasised that Arfat dedicated his life to speaking truth and defending human rights He is one of the kindest and most courageous people I know. He came to the United States legally as a film student to share about the human rights atrocities in Kashmir. She also talked about his film, Saffron Kingdom, created as a form of collective memory and truth-telling to tell the story of his people. It is devastating that someone who spent years bringing stories of human rights violations in war-torn regions to international audiences is in ICE detention, facing the conditions Arfat has dedicated his life to end, she said. The 42-year-old filmmaker is the son of Ghulam Nabi Sheikh, a celebrated Kashmiri folk singer. Sheikh died in 2003 from falling off a train when he was travelling from Jammu to Delhi with his daughter. Over the years, the family has called the official version of the events surrounding his death into question. Arfat grew up in the Valley and moved to the US as a student in 2019. As per the campaign, he filed for asylum in 2020 and has been living in Alexandria, Virginia.

articleTitle: Justice Jalan recuses himself from hearing Gymkhana Club’s plea against eviction
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Delhi Gymkhana Club (Image: Wikimedia Commons)
description: Delhi High Court Justice Prateek Jalan recused himself from the Delhi Gymkhana Club eviction case, citing concerns over his own judgement.
body_raw: Delhi High Court judge, Justice Prateek Jalan, on Wednesday recused himself from hearing a civil suit over the Centres proceedings against the Delhi Gymkhana Club for its eviction from the 27.3-acre premises on Safdarjung Road. I am going to recuse myself from this matter. I would be more comfortable if somebody else hears this, Justice Jalan orally remarked. There are matters where one does not trust ones own judgement. There is too much personal involved, he said without elaborating, reported PTI. Justice Jalan directed that the lawsuit by the Delhi Gymkhana Club Ltd Staff Welfare Association be listed before another bench on Friday. Several suits have been filed challenging a May 22 notice by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs MoHUA, initiating re-entry in the Club premises in the heart of Lutyens Delhi. The Centre, invoking Clause 4 of the perpetual lease deed that allows such re-entry by the government, had stated that the land is critically required for strengthening and securing of defence infrastructure and other vital public security purposes. In May, Justice Avneesh Jhingan had issued summons in the suit while refusing any interim relief by staying the governments proceedings against the Club. The government had assured the court that no eviction shall be undertaken at the Club without adhering to due process of law. Apart from seeking re-entry through the conditions of the lease deed, the Union government has also initiated eviction proceedings against the Club under the Public Premises Act.

articleTitle: From ITIs to AI: Why India needs to rethink skill development
articleFeaturedImageAlt: NITI Aayog, India, skilling, vocational education
description: NITI Aayog's report calls for reimagining India’s skilling architecture to address the gap between labour market needs and workforce skills. What does India’s skilling journey reveal about this mismatch, and how can the country strengthen its skilling system to keep pace with changing demands of job markets? See infographics for quick key insights.
body_raw: - Ritwika Patgiri Students from Class 9 onwards can choose Kaushal Tracks for specialised vocational training based on local and national job demand, proposed a NITI Aayogs report. The report also calls for universities to offer courses that focus on high-growth areas, such as green industries and electric vehicles, and help workers reskill for changing job markets. These recommendations made in Reimagining Skilling for Viksit Bharat2047 point to a challenge facing India a large section of young people are not making a direct transition from education to employment or skill development. It underscores the urgent need for a shift from generic degrees to applied, industry-aligned specialisations. But what does skilling mean in the context of a changing labour market? Is it simply about acquiring a set of skills or does it involve upskilling, reskilling and adaptation to new technologies and occupations? What does Indias skilling journey reveal about the gap between labour market needs and workforce skills? First, a brief overview of the NITI Aayogs report? Why NITI Aayog calls for reimagining skills The report says that more than 7.67 crore people have undergone skill-based training since 2014-15, adding that the Union Budget for 2025-26 allocated Rs 34,000 crore towards skilling-related expenditure across multiple central ministries. Despite this, outcomes remain uneven, says the report. Based on data from the 78th round of the National Sample Survey, the report maps workforce and learners into five segments, together representing approximately 60 crore citizens i schooling, ii tertiary education, iii formal and informal work, iv not in education, employment, and training NEET youth, and v women. The report underlines the significance of establishing stronger links between education, skills and actual employment, as only 8.25 per cent of graduates are employed in roles aligned with their qualifications. Skill training can happen through both institutions, like Industrial Training Institutes ITIs and on-the-job training. However, close to only 8 of the Indian firms provide on-the-job training, according to the NITI Aayogs report. The cost of providing on-the-job training for firms is often higher and they prefer trained individuals. This makes the role of skill institutions important. Therefore, the report proposed to incorporate vocational education and employability skills from schools to universities, with a stronger focus on applied, industry-aligned specialisations, along with greater use of apprenticeships and work-integrated degree and diploma programmes. The report also called for greater focus on sectors expected to generate demand, including green industries and electric vehicles, while providing reskilling for workers in declining occupations. Investing in human capital These recommendations hint at a broader shift towards viewing education and skill development as an investment in human capital. India has the largest youth population in the world, about 65 of its people under the age of 35, representing the potential of the demographic dividend. According to the human capital investment theory, economist Gary Becker argued that the various ways to invest in human capital include schooling and on-the-job training. He argued that earnings increase with age at a decreasing rate, and this increase is positively associated with the level of skills. Unemployment rates, in turn, are negatively associated with the level of skill. Similarly, Theodore Schultz argued that investment in education and training of young people yields returns over a longer period of time. In India, skill development has been perceived as a way to enhance employability and minimise the gap between labour market needs and workforce skills. For instance, according to data from Employment and Unemployment Surveys of National Sample Survey Office NSSO and the Periodic Labour Force Survey PLFS, formal training increased from 1.6 in 2011-12 to 4.1 in 2023-24, non-formal hereditary training from 1.8 to 11.6, non-formal self-learning from 1.8 to 11.6, and non-formal on-the-job training increased from 1.7 to 9.3. However, close to 65 of people aged 15-59 remain without any form of training.This points to a significant skill deficit in India and a gap between skill workers possess and those required by the labour market. A 2022 study by the National Skill Development Corporation NSDC estimated a significant deficit of 29 million between the demand and supply of skilled workers in India, particularly in sectors like IT, BFSI, healthcare, semiconductor manufacturing, and green jobs. This has been attributed to the failure of the countrys education sector as well as the performance of the numerous ITIs. Indias skilling push Skilling can be defined as a process through which individuals gain a particular skill or set of skills. However, the nature of skills required in the labour market keeps evolving with technological advancements and changing occupational demands. Upskilling refers to acquiring relevant advanced skills within a field or occupation to keep pace with changing technologies, roles, and responsibilities. Reskilling, on the other hand, involves learning new skills for different areas or roles. Economist Amit Basole notes that in India, the definition of skill is entangled with notions of dignified work. First, jobs that require mental skills are often considered more prestigious than those that prioritise manual skills. Second, the nature of caste hierarchies has influenced the allocation and social valuation of occupations and skills based on them. Finally, certain skill-based institutions are considered more prestigious than others, reflected, for instance, in the distinctions between IITs and ITIs. The 11th Five-Year Plan 2007-2012 marked a shift in policy focus on skill development. The National Skills Policy was introduced in 2009, followed by the launch of the National Skill Development Mission by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship MSDE in 2015, which targeted training 400 million individuals by the end of 2022. During this time, vocational training institutes grew exponentially and a number of schemes were introduced, including the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana, Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Kaushalya Yojana, and the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme. Despite this, the country spends only around 3 of its educational budget on vocational education. The number of ITIs, established in 1950 under the Craftsmen Training Scheme, increased from 9776 in 2014 to 13888 in 2026. The number of National Skill Training Institutes, Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Kendras, and Jan Shikshan Sansthans also increased. However, Basole notes that the character of the expansion changed because new ITIs were mostly private in nature, compared with the initial years till the 1980s when the government played a dominant role in their administration and expansion. More importantly, the expansion has not necessarily translated into comparable improvements in the quality and market-relevance of training. Why many ITIs seats are vacant It has also been found that students entering ITIs are more likely to have completed Class 10 and come largely from OBC, SC, and ST communities. Basole cautions against interpreting this pattern as a sign of inclusivity. Students from marginalised backgrounds face barriers in accessing educational opportunities and are more likely to drop out after Class 10 and 12. While relatively better-off students are more likely to pursue degree programmes or other forms of better or higher education, the caste-representation in ITIs is more likely a fallback option rather than an aspirational choice. The challenge is compounded by the large number of vacant seats in ITIs. According to NITI Aayogs 2023 Transforming Industrial Training Institutes report, in 2021, more than 50 seats in Andhra Pradesh and 58 in Assam stayed vacant, while only 47 of seats were occupied in Delhi. The reason for the large number of vacant seats has been attributed to a range of factors. The trade mix offered by ITIs remains heavily concentrated in manufacturing and technical occupations. For instance, the trade of electrician is offered by almost all ITIs, followed by the trade of fitter. Yet, around 65 of electrician seats and nearly 72 of fitter seats across ITIs are unoccupied, according to NITI Aayog. Notably, Indias growth story is largely driven by service, and ITIs have not been able to expand training relevant to service sectors, including financial services and information technology. Similarly, relevant trades such as AI, automation, and green technologies have not received much emphasis. As of 2022, only 0.09 of all the ITI students were placed, according to the NITI Aayog report. This represents a very dismal picture. Moreover, the gendered nature of trades offered by ITIs and a very distinct gendered pattern in the type of trades men and women apply for constitute other factors behind the vacant seats at ITIs. In addition, the shortage of instructors at ITIs is yet another constraint. What India can do to strengthen its skilling system So, what can be the way out for India to enhance its skill development? The evidence points towards several areas for reform. For instance, studies reveal that ITIs located near industrial belts are more likely to create employment. Trade mix and curricula need to evolve in keeping with the changing requirements of relevant industries and service-sector jobs, as well as emerging areas like AI and green skills. The gendered nature of ITIs also requires a transformation. This requires a more structural change where changing gendered roles and perceptions can lead to changes in gendered occupational trades. Other structural changes include greater spending on both general and vocational education. There has also been a rapid decline in the duration of skill development courses. As more people are completing their degrees and earning their certificates, these training programmes sometimes as short as 10 days have not resulted in acquiring gainful skills. Finally, international experiences can provide useful insights. For instance, Germany introduces an early vocational education model at the upper secondary level. Post read questions 1. What explains the persistent mismatch between the skills acquired by Indias workforce and those demanded by its labour market? Suggest measures to bridge this gap. 2. The expansion of Indias vocational training infrastructure has not necessarily translated into better employment outcomes. Discuss with reference to Industrial Training Institutes ITIs. 3. How can India move from a degree-centric education system towards an education model that integrates vocational training, apprenticeships and work-based learning? 4. How can India make its vocational education system more responsive to the growth of the services sector and emerging areas such as artificial intelligence, automation, electric vehicles and green technologies? 5. Gender and caste continue to shape participation and outcomes in Indias vocational education system. Discuss the structural factors responsible and suggest measures for making skill development more inclusive. articleTitle: How RBI’s rate hike turns homeownership dream into bigger debt burden
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra and MPC members at a press conference on its Monetary Policy announcement and repo rate hike from 5.25% to 5.50%, (RBI/ANI Video Grab)
description: When RBI raises the price of money, borrowers pay — through higher EMIs, longer loan tenures, bigger down payments, and delayed dreams of home ownership. How is that? We explain.
body_raw: A 25-basis-point bps repo rate hike may seem insignificant on paper, but for a homebuyer, it is anything but small. On a Rs 50 lakh home loan taken for 20 years, a 25-bps increase can mean roughly Rs 780 more in monthly equated monthly installment EMI, and nearly Rs 1.88 lakh in additional interest outgo over the life of the loan, experts say. For a household already struggling to make the down payment and qualify for a loan, the Reserve Bank of Indias RBIs rate decision can turn an affordable home into an unaffordable liability. Loans linked to the marginal cost of funds-based lending rate MCLR may also become more expensive. Banks, however, have flexibility in revising MCLR-based rates depending on their funding costs, liquidity conditions and deposit mobilisation. Heres how a repo rate hike feeds into home-loan costs - and why first-time buyers often feel the impact the most. How repo rate affects borrowing costs The pain does not stop with the EMI. The RBIs repo rate is the price at which banks borrow from the central bank. When that rate rises, borrowing costs across the financial system tend to move up. Floating-rate home-loan borrowers are particularly exposed because their interest rates are linked, directly or indirectly, to benchmark rates-the repo rate. The increase can either push up the EMI or force the borrower to stay indebted for longer. According to experts, banks may choose to increase the loan tenure rather than allow the EMI to jump sharply. That may soften the immediate monthly shock, but it is hardly a free lunch. A longer tenure means the borrower remains in debt for more years and can end up paying considerably more interest. Why first-time buyers bear more For first-time homebuyers, the problem is even more severe. Loan eligibility is determined partly by the borrowers income and repayment capacity. Higher interest rates reduce the amount a household can borrow for the same EMI. The buyer is then forced to either settle for a cheaper property, arrange a larger down payment or postpone the purchase. In the countrys already expensive urban housing markets, that is a serious blow. Many real estate companies are saddled with unsold stocks in cities such as Mumbai. The blunt reality is this when the RBI raises the price of money, borrowers pay - through higher EMIs, longer loan tenures, bigger down payments, and delayed dreams of home ownership. For the countrys aspiring middle class, that is not a statistical footnote, but a direct hit to affordability. RBIs rate hike after over 3 years  a shift in policy Along with the hike in its key policy rate, which is the first rate hike since February 2023, the central bank has also signaled a shift towards tighter monetary policy amid rising inflationary pressures, elevated crude oil prices and a challenging global interest-rate environment. The Monetary Policy Committee MPC has changed the policy stance to calibrated tightening from neutral indicating further hike in the interest rates is a likelihood. The policy panel has also hiked the growth projection from 6.7 to 7.1 in FY27 in the wake of the higher economic activity in the country. The panel also raised the inflation forecast to 5.2 for FY27 from 5 previously. The six-member MPC headed by RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra has sent a hawkish message the era of easy money is almost over, and borrowers should brace themselves for more pain. The MPCs decision to shift its stance from neutral to calibrated tightening is not a mere change in terminology - it is a clear warning that the central bank is prepared to tighten the screws if inflationary pressures refuse to ease.

articleTitle: ‘Ma’: The Japanese philosophy that says healthy marriages need personal space
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Japanese concept of Ma in marriage and the importance of personal space
description: The Japanese concept of ‘Ma’ encourages couples to create intentional space within marriage. Could spending time apart actually strengthen connection, individuality and emotional intimacy?
body_raw: Marriage is often associated with closeness, shared routines, and spending as much time together as possible. But could deliberately creating some space within a relationship actually make partners feel more connected? A Japanese concept known as Ma offers an interesting way of looking at this balance. In Japanese culture, Ma refers to an intentional interval or space. In a marriage, the idea is not about ignoring a partner, withdrawing affection or giving them the cold shoulder. Instead, it is about allowing two individuals enough breathing room to retain their own identities while remaining part of a relationship. The concept challenges the Western idea of two-become-one marriage by recognising the importance of the two within the one. DISCLAIMER This article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. This can play out in small, everyday ways. One partner may go to a book club while the other takes a long solo walk, treating separate social lives as a way to recharge rather than evidence that the couple is drifting apart. Ma can also mean allowing a pause during emotionally charged conversations - for instance, when someone says, Im having a hard day, rather than immediately offering advice or responding with me too. Even physical space can matter giving a partner room while they are cooking, reading, or simply spending time in their own thoughts can be a form of respect. The idea also sits alongside Japans cultural emphasis on Gaman, or emotional endurance. While constant proximity can sometimes contribute to irritation and familiarity that breeds contempt, intentional space may create opportunities for partners to miss each other, appreciate one another and return to the relationship with renewed energy. But whether this philosophy can genuinely strengthen modern marriages - and where healthy space ends and emotional distancing begins - requires some nuance. The psychological benefits of personal space Counselling psychologist Athul Raj tells indianexpress.com, Personal space is important in a marriage because being close to someone does not mean giving up your individuality. When partners maintain their own friendships, interests and routines, they continue to have a sense of who they are outside the relationship. This becomes particularly important over time, when work, children, finances and family responsibilities can make the marriage the centre of almost everything. He adds that having some experiences that are your own can give you mental space and also something different to bring back into the relationship. It reduces the expectation that one person has to provide all companionship, emotional support and stimulation. Silence can serve a similar purpose. After a difficult or exhausting day, someone may simply need time to settle before they can be present with their partner. That does not automatically mean there is a problem between them. Healthy space vs emotional withdrawal The difference becomes clearer when we look at the pattern and what happens afterwards. A healthy request for space usually comes with some indication that the person intends to return to the conversation. Avoidance is more likely when I need space repeatedly appears whenever there is conflict, accountability or emotional vulnerability. If conversations are constantly postponed, one partner is left waiting, or the same unresolved issue keeps coming back, then the space may actually be functioning as withdrawal. At the same time, taking a break during an argument is not necessarily unhealthy. When emotions are very high, stepping away can prevent the conversation from becoming more hurtful. The important part is whether the person eventually comes back and is willing to deal with what happened. If they keep using distance to avoid the conversation altogether, that is a different issue, shares Raj. Bringing Ma into everyday married life Quick Quiz See if you can answer this What is the healthiest way for couples to create personal space in married life? A. Spend all free time together to maintain closeness. B. Give only one partner regular personal time when they need it more. C. Build small, reciprocal periods of personal time into everyday routines while maintaining emotional connection. D. Avoid personal hobbies and friendships after marriage. Reveal the answer Correct answer C Raj mentions that personal space does not require a separate room or hours of free time. It can include quiet time after work, individual friendships, hobbies, solo walks or simply doing separate activities. With children, partners can take turns giving each other uninterrupted time, even for 30 minutes. The key is reciprocity, so one partner is not left carrying most of the childcare or household responsibilities. Healthy relationships allow partners to have different needs for solitude and interaction while maintaining enough closeness to feel secure. articleTitle: Was Cathy born evil? Netflix’s East of Eden rewrites Steinbeck’s most notorious villain
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A still from East of Eden. (Source: Netflix)
description: Netflix’s East of Eden, starring Florence Pugh as Cathy Ames, gives John Steinbeck’s infamous ‘psychic monster’ a traumatic past, reigniting a decades-old debate over whether she was born evil or made monstrous.
body_raw: Are monsters created, or is one born evil? In East of Eden, future Nobel laureate John Steinbeck backs innate evil through Cathy Ames, one of the most ruthless femme fatales ever written. Now, a woman screenwriter has challenged his take on that chicken-and-egg ouroboros in Netflixs seven-episode adaptation of the American classic. Steinbecks Cathy is a serpent-tongued Eve who leads men astray, leaving only death and regret in her wake. Zoe Kazan-granddaughter of Elia Kazan, who directed the 1955 adaptation starring James Dean-tells the story from the villains perspective. To the delight and dismay of Steinbecks readers, Kazan gives Cathy, played by Florence Pugh, a villain-origin story. Here is what you should know about how Steinbeck wrote Cathy, what the series changes, the split verdict on the adaptation, and the novel itself. Steinbecks Cathy I believe there are monsters born in the world to human parents. From the outset, Steinbeck describes Cathy as something inherently evil, calling her a psychic monster with a malformed soul. He says Cathy learns early to use sex as power. In Steinbecks telling, she gets two older boys punished for assaulting her.As a teenager, she seduces her Latin teacher, who kills himself. She sets fire to the family home with her parents inside, empties her fathers safe and fakes her own death. She sleeps with her husbands brother on her wedding night, tries to end her pregnancy, takes over a brothel by poisoning its owner, and turns it into a house of sadomasochism and blackmail. With such a litany of crimes, she is portrayed as a soulless monster, a seductress, with Steinbeck reaching for Satanic descriptors to describe her her feet are small and stubby, with fat insteps almost like little hoofs, and on one occasion, her tongue flickers like a serpent. What the series changes In the Netflix adaptation, Cathy commits nearly all the same crimes, but Kazan tries to rationalise it as a traumatic response of a child violated. The aforementioned carriage-house frame-up is replaced with a scene in which an older boy lures Cathy with candy when she is but a child. In her teens, her lovesick teacher becomes a predator, and her timid father is portrayed as a tyrant who whips her and treats her as his property. In Kazans telling, Cathy is a woman exposed to the worlds cruelty at a young age, and rather than be exploited, she decides to manipulate the world and be cruel in turn. Her ambition to be free from the restrictions of society and family spurs her to escape all kinds of bonds, often through murder. She takes over a brothel through underhanded means, and uses it to gather blackmail. This is a perverted rebellion against the ambition of her contemporaries, motherhood and marriage, which in the mid-20th century would make her villainous even without the murders. Pugh told Radio Times that despite the empathetic treatment granted to a woman who in the original text is an irredeemable psychopath, Cathy is not given absolution she does not get away scot-free. For better or worse Many commentators have argued that the changes defang Cathy and reduce her to a traumatised victim, when she actually is an unrepentant perpetrator. It also robs the story of its originality by allowing a female villain with criminal tendencies who isnt driven by a moment of desperation or a last resort. As the influential critic Louis Owens, who wrote in John Steinbecks Re-Vision of America, says, Cathy is evil thats simply the way it is. Many of Steinbecks detractors believe the changes to be an improvement, as they prevent Cathy from staying a one-dimensional character, the archetypal personification of the original sin that cost Adam Paradise, or even Lilith, who refuses to bend. The change allows the character to be more than an unflattering caricature of his ex-wife Gwen, with whom he had an acrimonious split, with allegations of infidelity thrown on either side. Besides the novels central idea, timshel, the Hebrew word Steinbeck translates as thou mayest, gives the male characters the luxury of choosing their own path, but denies the same to Cathy, who is sentenced to be a monster from birth to death. Sarah Appleton Aguiar also argues in a 2005 essay that Cathys malevolent nature tends to present itself only when she is feeling cornered or trapped. Does Steinbeck hint at abuse Bibliophiles who have already watched the adaptation point out that Steinbeck himself writes that Cathy learned very young that sexuality is the most disturbing impulse humans have. In chapter 17, the narrator doubts himself, admitting that without knowing what Cathy wanted, it is easy to call her bad and hard to say why. In the letters to his editor later published as Journal of a Novel, Steinbeck went further To that extent I am a monster like Cathy. And when a correspondent told him that Cathy only became believable at the end of the book, he replied that this was when, through fear, she became like us. What is East of Eden? Published in 1952, East of Eden is a 600-page American saga, which Steinbeck wrote for his two sons. Reception was mixed, with some calling Steinbeck moralistic, melodramatic, and misogynistic, but it quickly became a bestseller within two months. The book has never gone out of print, and it saw another burst of popularity in 2003, when Oprah Winfrey chose it to relaunch her book club. The Trask story retells the biblical tale of the rival brothers Cain and Abel twice first through Adam and his violent half-brother, Charles, then through Cathys twins, gentle Aron and moody Cal. Villain or antihero, Cathy remains its most argued-over character. Whatever ones view of good versus evil, or nature versus nurture, a book that still sparks this much debate almost a lifetime after publication has earned its place among American classics.

articleTitle: Ashwin predicts Bumrah and Bhuvneshwar will play together at World Cup: ‘Sitting together on that flight…’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bhuvneshwar Kumar
description: "He is going to New Zealand now. I am telling you, if he does well, everyone will immediately say, just take him for the ODI team as well. The selectors will be watching very closely," Ashwin said
body_raw: Bhuvneshwar Kumar played a key role in helping India win back-to-back titles for the Royal Challengers Bengaluru. He scalped 45 wickets during the phase and was quite lethal in all phases of the game, and his remarkable performances earned him an India call-up for the upcoming T20I series against New Zealand. Former Indian cricketer R Ashwin said that Bhuvneshwar and Jasprit Bumrah might play together in the World Cup next year in South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe. I am very excited and happy for Bhuvneshwar Kumar because he is a very unassuming guy. And yes, I am once again putting my neck on the line to say this if he had worked a little harder, if the timing had been right and if he had avoided those injuries, with the skill set he possesses, he could have been a king for India across all formats, Ashwin said on his YouTube channel. Do you want swing? He has swing. If you want it to move one way, he can do that. If you want it to move both ways, he can do that too. And then he has decent pace, he added. Recalling his performances in Australia in the past, Ashwin noted that the 36-year-old struggled at that stage in his career, partly due to injuries. Yes, when he played a couple of games in Australia, he was also finding it a little difficult, but he had some fitness issues. With the bat, he could contribute really well. He has very, very good hands and is a good catcher, Ashwin said. He is going to New Zealand now. I am telling you, if he does well, everyone will immediately say, just take him for the ODI team as well. The selectors will be watching very closely. If he swings the ball and shows decent fitness, nobody can stop Jasprit Bumrah and Bhuvneshwar Kumar from sitting together on that flight to the World Cup, with Bhuvneshwar bowling the first ball of the World Cup, hoped Ashwin.

articleTitle: After Janhvi Kapoor’s deepfake controversy, Peddi producer says ‘youth is polluted’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Janhvi Kapoor
description: Peddi producer has condemned the misuse of AI following the Chuttamalle deepfake targeting Janhvi Kapoor, saying the youth have become polluted.
body_raw: Days after deepfake content featuring actor Janhvi Kapoor was widely circulated on the internet, Mythri Movie Makers co-founder Y Ravi Shankar has spoken out against the growing misuse of artificial intelligence AI to generate deepfake content. Janhvi was last seen in Peddi, which was produced by the same production house. It has become really easy to sling mud at each other on social media. On top of that, they are now misusing AI, and no one knows whats real or fake, Ravi Shankar said. The youth have become polluted, be it online or otherwise. It is at a time like this that we need films with divine power that instil a fear of God. It is only beneficial to society. The deepfake that prompted his remarks was an AI-manipulated version of the Chuttamalle song from Jr NTRs Devara Part 1, in which Janhvi Kapoors likeness was digitally altered to create sexually explicit imagery. Jr NTR and Janhvi Kapoor both issued public statements against such videos. It is to be noted that his own film Peddi was also severely criticised for sexualising Janhvis character and normalising assault. Some of the scenes featuring her character were changed after viewers raised objection. Also Read Janhvi Kapoor calls her Chuttamalle AI video with NTR assault Reality of being a woman Talking about Hanuman Ansh, the Neem Karoli Baba biopic whose Telugu release was being announced at the same press event, he said, We are very happy that this film not only conveys a message and shows God and reality, but has also become a commercial superhit. Rs 400 crore for Rs 2 crore is a slap in the face Ravi Shankar announced that Hanuman Ansh will release in Telugu on October 9. Made on a budget of less than Rs 2 crore, the film has already earned Rs 425 crore worldwide at the box office, and is continuing to make money at the ticket counters. It is like a slap in the face to see a film with a Rs 2 crore investment gross Rs 400 crore in collections, he said. We are spending crores of rupees with not much to show for it. But to get Rs 400 crore for Rs 2 crore, thats a real pan-Indian film. He urged producers across the industry to ensure the film reaches every possible audience. Wherever possible, if you have skipped releasing it in any language, please release it in all languages. This film is a massive hit, not just revenue-wise. Its a much-needed film, he said.

articleTitle: ‘Peace and closure’: Mirabai Chanu on a medal that took four Asian Games cycles
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Mirabai
description: A coach's remark in a Manipur gym set the target. Chanu and Vijay Sharma needed years, a changed plan for the Commonwealth Games and a Paris miss to reach it
body_raw: When Mirabai Chanu first walked into a gym in Manipur to try weightlifting, a coach looked her up and down and made a casual remark that would stay with her for over a decade You could win a medal at the Asian Games. She surpassed that remark in nearly every way but the one it named. Chanu, who can lift three times her bodyweight, won medals at the World Championships, the Commonwealth Games and, in 2021, a historic silver at the Tokyo Olympics. That consistency, chiselled over years of work and protected through countless injuries, had one gap the Asian Games. Something always kept happening during or around the Asian Games. It reached a point where I would constantly wonder why this was happening, says Chanu. Her longtime coach Vijay Sharma, sitting next to her, chimes in I wont call it a psychological barrier. You can say that it happened by chance. We have discussed this many times. We realised if we attributed it to bad luck, we wouldnt be able to do anything about it. So they did something about it. It started with how they approached the Commonwealth Games. Training loads were kept with Chanus past injuries in mind, and the duo chose not to chase a Commonwealth Games record. A gold with minimal effort was the call. It left her fresh to push at the Asian Games, for the one medal that would complete her. Weightlifting asks for unflinching trust between coach and athlete. Even at these Asian Games, Chanu did not know what weights she was supposed to lift, or where she stood on the medal table. It was Vijays split-second permutations and combinations that ensured a silver arrived while keeping her limits in mind. Vijay was there in Sydney in 2000 when Karnam Malleswari won a bronze medal. Malleswaris gripe since has been that if her Russian coach had trusted her, a better medal could have been Indias. When youre in the arena, you need to make decisions in a fraction of a second. Whatever decisions we take are for the best of the players, says Vijay. He did not allow that breakdown of trust, which he saw with Indias first Olympic weightlifting medal, when he started training Chanu. That trust is essential. In life, whether with a life partner, in business, or in coaching, without trust, there is no bonding, and without bonding, there are no results. The trust that she has in me, even after she has won medals at the World and Olympic level, she still asks me what sets to pick up, says Vijay. I didnt even know that I didnt need a third lift in Japan, admitted Chanu. Sir told me that the silver medal was assured and that we wouldnt need to risk another lift. Once the medal was assured, Chanu could finally feel the weight lift off. It was a collective sense of wrong, felt by both her and Vijay, that was corrected in Nagoya. The fourth-place finish at the Paris Olympics had rankled deeply for both of them, more than two years on, until Nagoya came along. Winning this medal after so many years, across four Asian Games cycles, feels like a dream come true for both me and Vijay sir. It helps cover up the pain of missing out on the medal in Paris. Every time we looked at photos or videos from Paris, it reminded us of what we missed. This medal brings us peace and closure, said Chanu. Their next challenge is the LA Olympics, and a jump to the 53 kg category. Chanu admits that a higher weight class feels more comfortable. Now with the weight increase, itll give some relief from injuries, so we can focus even more on performance and everything else. Whenever I win a medal, I immediately look ahead to the next competition what I need to do, what changes to make. I learn from every medal and championship, and thats where I get my motivation, says Chanu.

articleTitle: Watch: Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka hauled away again after lie-in on Delhi road
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The Congress leaders were detained by cops in dramatic circumstances
description: The showdown erupted after Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge hosted lunch for INDIA bloc MPs at a restaurant on Janpath, less than 2 km from the Jantar Mantar protest site.
body_raw: Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were dragged away by Delhi Police Wednesday evening as opposition leaders launched Day 2 of their protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The Congress leaders were detained by cops in dramatic circumstances - Rahul Gandhi was manhandled and bundled into a police bus, the second time in as many days. An angry-looking Priyanka Gandhi, who lay on the road with her arms crossed, was hustled away minutes later. She held on to a copy of the Constitution, her arm outstretched outside the moving vehicle. Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were dragged away by Delhi Police-for a second time in as many days-after opposition MPs kick-started Day 2 of protests demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar quit over irregularities in the SIR process. Read   - The Indian Express IndianExpress October 7, 2026 The showdown erupted after a lunch meet organised by Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge for INDIA bloc MPs. The venue was the all-vegetarian Sagar Ratna restaurant on Janpath, less than 2 km from the Jantar Mantar protest site. Earlier, Rahul Gandhi was trolled online by a section of X users for allegedly having a non-vegetarian roll from Khan Chacha eatery during his eight-hour sit-in at the Akashvani Bhawan on Tuesday. After about one-and-a-half hours, the MPs streamed out of the eatery and went and sat in three buses parked on Janpath Road and headed towards Jantar Mantar. Interestingly, the Samajwadi Party skipped the lunch meeting. Sources in the Congress said that most of their MPs had left Delhi by this morning and couldnt attend the meeting and the subsequent protest. Today, we feel that we will protest at Jantar Mantar, which is a designated protest site, and tell the country that for us Gyanesh Kumar is not a legitimate Election Commissioner.As I said yesterday, around 300 Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha MPs wanted to meet Election Commissioners, but they did not meet us. An impromptu sit-in took place at the roundabout in front of the Shangri-La hotel. The police soon moved to detain the protesters who countered the security officials. Rahul kept resisting police attempts to put him inside a van for detention. The INDIA bloc leaders jostled with security personnel who tried to detain them and clear the area. The entire Windsor Place roundabout was jammed with buses, cars and Congress youth outfit workers. While he was taken away to the Barakhamba police station, Rahul released a video message, continuing to engage through his social media platforms, besides his on-ground presence. We are not going to stop protesting till Gyanesh Kumar resigns.This is a fight to protect the most sacred thing in this country.There is nothing that Narendra Modi and Amit Shah can do that will stop us, he wrote in a post on his X handle along with a video message. We are not going to stop protesting till Gyanesh Kumar resigns. This is a fight to protect the most sacred thing in this country. There is nothing that Narendra Modi and Amit Shah can do that will stop us.  - Rahul Gandhi RahulGandhi October 7, 2026 Later, the Congress said, The bus in which Rahul Gandhi ji was being taken was punctured by Congresss Babbar lions near Agrasen ki Baoli. The leaders were then taken to a police station in central Delhi. In a video attached to an X post, Rahul Gandhi said that Prime Minister Modi, Amit Shah, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and Gyanesh Kumar can do all this, but we are going to bring them to justice. My guarantee that all four of them will be brought to justice. This is all a panic reaction. This is all fear. They are going to be brought to justice, mark my words, he said.
