articleTitle: Hamas calculus, Israel’s gamble: How October 7 reshaped the region, 3 years on
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Hamas
description: Why did Hamas plan the attack, and three years later, where do Israel and Palestine stand? An Expert Explains.
body_raw: On October 7, 2023, a Hamas-led attack in Israel killed around 1,200 people, while 251 were taken hostage. Israels response in the three years since has utterly devasted Gaza and sparked off three other linked wars in Iran, Lebanon, and Yemen. Why did Hamas plan the attack, and three years later, where do Israel and Palestine stand? The Hamas attack on October 7, 2023 UN investigations detail that the complex attack comprised an assault from the land, sea, and air in conjunction with the launch of a large-scale rocket and mortar attack towards cities, towns and villages and military bases in southern and central Israel. Executed across the day, the October 7 operation also saw attacks on several Israeli kibbutzim and the Nova music festival, assaults on Israeli beaches and arterial roads, and triggered the evacuation of nearly 150,000 people from their homes. Three years since, all Hamas-held hostages both dead and alive have been released, with the last batch of releases occurring as a result of a US-induced January 2025 ceasefire. On the other hand, Israels continuing military offensive in Gaza since October 2023 has killed over 70,000 Palestinians by conservative estimates, with Israeli actions characterised as a genocide by several states and human rights agencies, as well as a UN Commission of Inquiry. Israel is presently headed into its first elections since the attack, with the countrys longest-serving PM, Benjamin Netanyahu, seeking yet another term. What was Hamas strategic logic for October 7? Hamas October 7 attack occurred when it did as a result of two specific strategic conditions. First, in the 15 years before October 2023, Israels security calculus vis-a-vis Hamas had settled into a quiet for quiet approach. Besides the broader strategic goal of repelling Israeli occupation, Hamas own focus with Israel prioritised sub-strategic goals such as the lifting of Israels stringent economic blockade on Gaza since 2007 and the release of over 5000 Palestinian prisoners in Israel. There were new unwritten rules of the game in both IDF and Hamas parlance, which would be determined by acceptable and unacceptable acts. Moreover, Hamas own ability to deter a large Israeli offensive in Gaza had been proven by its intense exchanges of rocket fire most prominently for 51 days in 2014. By 2018, Hamas abilities to threaten hinterland Israeli targets had grown sufficiently for its leader Yahya Sinwar to assert that whatever rockets hit Tel Aviv for 51 days in 2024, would be launched within five minutes if Israel carried out any offensive. Since 2018, Israel had also let conditional aid trickle into Gaza as a result of negotiations with Hamas through Egypt, further contributing to Hamas perceptions of a vindication of its posture. This balance was sustained by an Israeli political interest in playing off Hamas against Fatah in the West Bank especially under Netanyahu, who fiercely defended allowing Qatari financial sustainment of Hamas across 2019 and 2020 as necessary to prevent the creation of a Palestinian state. Even hard-right politicians such as Bezalel Smotrich presently Israels Finance Minister and West Bank administrator argued in 2015 that Hamas is an asset, and Abu Mazen Mahmoud Abbas of Fatah is a burden. Second, Israels approach to removing the possibility of a Palestinian state alongside an expansion of its settlement project in the West Bank had taken on a regional character especially since 2020. Both the Abraham Accords of that year as well as subsequent Arab signaling of a de-prioritisation of the Palestinian issue brought the fundamental logic of resistance back to Hamas. Hence, as far as six months before October 7, Hamas then second-in-command Saleh al-Arouri had publicly declared that Palestinians had between two to three years before Israeli settlers in the West Bank increased to two million, making a decisive, multi-front war necessary in the near term. A more specific window of opportunity was created due to Israels then ongoing domestic crisis featuring a tussle between the Netanyahu-led executive and the judiciary. This logic was supplemented by Hamas having increasingly integrated itself into Irans Axis of Resistance. But this architectures functioning was complicated. Irans Axis was built on a non-sectarian strategic logic but with deterrence and not war as the principal objective a regional threat-in-being to counter Israels own regional approach to countering Iran. It became categorically evident on October 7 that Hamas wrested agency from the rest of the Axis, most of whom were then faced with a now or never scenario to fulfill their long-standing objective of defeating the Israeli state. However, even as Hezbollah became the only principal Shia force that initiated rocketmissile exchanges following October 7, then Hezbollah Chief Hassan Nasrallah repeatedly rationalised a limited approach and the rest of the Axis remained hesitant to act until the Yemeni Houthi blockade in early 2024. Hence, immediately after the attack, Hamas returned to seeking sub-strategic concessions from Israel. Consequently, as the Qatari PM has stated on the record, Hamas was willing to release all hostages on the first day of the war. How did October 7 affect Israels security outlook? The October 7 attack dealt a huge dent to Benjamin Netanyahus image as Israels Mr Security. However, in retrospect its domestic political effects were more complicated. Israels security architecture was already working with a long-set outlook vis-a-vis Hamas that had been politically blessed by successive Israeli governments, including Netanyahus. However, Netanyahus domestic political crises and threats from the judiciary incentivised inaction before the attack despite warnings from both Egypt and UAE, while the attack itself necessitated aggressive action instead of accepting Hamas offer for hostage return. This latter posture was further supported by the hard-right lawmakers who propped up his government. Now, Netanyahus electoral gamble is that his post-October 7 aggressive regional approach has yielded successes that have been long necessary for Israeli security. This includes significant dents to Irans Axis Hezbollahs operational decimation in south Lebanon and northern Israels expanded security perimeter a longstanding Israeli priority Bashar al Assads fall in Damascus and a free rein for Israeli military operations in Syria, which has led to an expanded Israeli occupation of the Golan Heights a US war on Iran and Arab restraint in punitive actions against Israel. However, it is the continuity in regional conflict of which these successes are a part that has enabled his opponents to keep the focus on October 7s security failure. Nonetheless, the scale of regional shifts now means that beyond Netanyahu, there is a normalisation of an aggressive security posture. This is a security logic that combines past and future. Regardless of whether Netanyahu survives politically, this assertive outlook now arguably pervades Israels politico-security establishment at large, while Israel continues to resist international pressure against its continuing occupation and expansion of settlements in Palestinian territories.

articleTitle: ‘Special camps’ for voters cut after recent demolitions: Delhi poll body chief
articleFeaturedImageAlt: SIR survey in Delhi's Sangam Vihar. (Express Photo by Gajendra Yadav)
description: Delhi election officials will hold special camps to help eligible voters left out after recent demolitions enroll in the electoral rolls during SIR.
body_raw: The Delhi Election Commission on Wednesday said it would ensure that no eligible elector is left out of the electoral roll. The commission said special camps would be organised to facilitate the enrolment of all eligible electors who have been left out of the rolls. Every eligible elector is added and no ineligible entries remain in the electoral roll, the statement issued by the Election Commission of Delhi said. With the objective of maximising the enrolment of young electors, special camps were organised at various colleges and universities across Delhi from October 7 and will continue till October 8, 2026, the statement said. Booth Level Officers BLOs present at the camps will guide students in filling out the forms, collect the completed forms and address their queries related to the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls. As per the instructions issued by the Election Commission of India on October 1, a special drive is being conducted to enrol all eligible electors left out of the electoral rolls. BLOs will conduct house-to-house visits to identify eligible persons and facilitate their enrolment through Form 6, wherever applicable. Special camps will also be organised on October 9 and 11, 2026, at all polling station locations across the National Capital Territory of Delhi to enrol eligible electors left out of the rolls. In Delhi, the Special Intensive Revision SIR data showed that 29.86 per cent of electors were marked as absent, shifted or under the others category, while 1.95 per cent were listed as deceased and 0.98 per cent were found enrolled at multiple places. articleTitle: Ahead of CJP’s October 10 protest, Delhi Police puts 2,800 ‘criminals’ on radar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: According to sources in the Delhi Police, all those with criminal antecedents who were spotted by the Facial Recognition System (FRS) during the July protests will be tracked by their local police stations. (Express Photo)
description: 2,873 people who took part in the CJP’s July Jantar Mantar protests were flagged for criminal records, with police now working to stop them from reaching Delhi ahead of October 10.
body_raw: The Delhi Police had identified 2,800-odd people with a criminal background who took part in the Cockroach Janta Partys July protests against the NEET paper leak at Jantar Mantar. Efforts are on to ensure none of them reach Delhi on October 10, senior officials told The Indian Express. The CJP has announced that the Jantar Mantar 2.0 protest, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner CEC Gyanesh Kumar, will start on October 10. According to sources in the Delhi Police, all those with criminal antecedents who were spotted by the Facial Recognition System FRS during the July protests will be tracked by their local police stations. Permission to protest has not been granted yet. So police stations will track if people with a history of serious offences, especially the ones who came last time, are heading towards the protest site. The idea is to not let them come here and disrupt law and order in the area, said a police officer on condition of anonymity. At least 2,873 people with criminal records had been flagged by the FRS 989 of them were accused in heinous cases, 101 named in murder cases, and at least 42 were involved in two or more murders. The Indian Express reported that at least 25 of them, accused of serious crimes such as murder, attempted murder, rape and child abuse, were even supposed to be in jail. Students told to keep away Apart from tracking criminals, police are also looking to inform students that any assembly on October 10 in the New Delhi area would be unlawful, said a senior police officer. Public meetings with members of Residents Welfare Associations RWAs in areas with dense student populations are usually a regular feature. Now, a senior officer said, PG owners are specifically being made aware of the law and order situation in the capital in these meetings. We are asking PG owners to inform students that Section 163 of the BNSS is in force in the New Delhi district. So any protest in the area is illegal and students should be considerate of that, said a senior cop. Focus on city borders The border areas are also a focus for the Delhi Police. Another senior officer told The Indian Express that police will be on a lookout for large groups of people who are looking to enter Delhi before Saturday. The main focus areas will be the Uttar Pradesh border, which touches East Delhi and Shahdara, Haryana border, which touches Dwaraka, and the Rajasthan border, which touches Southwest Delhi. Any mass movement will be tracked through borders. We will be putting up barricades for checks on routes going towards New Delhi, so that large groups of people dont assemble, said a senior police officer. Earlier in the day, Saurab Das, co-convener of the CJP, reached Parliament Street police station to submit a letter saying they have the right to protest at the designated site at Jantar Mantar. Das, along with All India Students Association AISA president Neha Bora, held a press conference at the Press Club of India in the afternoon where they announced a joint call to citizens to gather at Jantar Mantar to save the democracy of the country. Speaking to the media, Das said he did not seek permission from the Delhi Police but informed them that they would hold a protest against the Special Intensive Revision SIR and CEC Kumar.

articleTitle: Flydubai Omani co-pilot trained in UK, New Zealand, Australia: How Hamam al-Hammami slipped through aviation safety nets
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Flydubai Dubai-Tel Aviv Flight News
description: The Omani co-pilot, identified as Hamam al-Hammami, 29, is believed to have attended one of the UK’s biggest flight schools between 2018 and 2019.
body_raw: Flydubai flight FZ1073s Omani co-pilot, who allegedly stabbed Indian captain Smit Machchhar in a midair cockpit brawl last week in an apparent attempt to crash the Dubai-Tel Aviv plane, reportedly trained to become a professional pilot in Britain. The Omani co-pilot, identified as Hamam al-Hammami, 29, is believed to have attended one of the UKs biggest flight schools between 2018 and 2019, The Telegraph reported. The report added that Hammami received the training from England-based L3 Airline Academy, a pilot training firm that is a part of Acron Aviation. Acron Aviation declined to say whether Hammami had trained with the company, citing its policy of not publicly commenting on individual current or former students. The company said it would assist authorities with any investigation.  Crash axe attack on Indian pilot The Omani co-pilot, who attacked Machchhar with a crash axe that is usually kept in the cockpit in case of emergencies, reportedly trained at one or more centres of L3 Airline Academy in England, which includes major training facilities in Southampton and Bournemouth, as well as a simulator centre near Gatwick. Israeli passenger Yaniv Hayoun, with blood stains on his shirt, who was aboard a Flydubai aircraft that made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia, is welcomed at the arrivals gate at Ben Gurion International Airport near Tel Aviv, Israel. AP Photo The co-pilot of flydubai flight FZ1073, which had been bound for Israel from Dubai, attacked the pilot with an emergency crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said, calling the incident a terrorist attack. Co-pilots New Zealand training stint The co-pilot was in New Zealand from November 2018 to May 2019 on a six-month student visa, according to New Zealand Police. Police said he was there to complete part of his flight training for a UK-based company that no longer operates in New Zealand. Australia links investigated The Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team, comprising the Australian Federal Police, Victoria Police and the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation ASIO, is investigating the mans links to Australia, the Australian Federal Police said. Melbourne University connection Reuters, citing sources, reported that the co-pilot had studied at RMIT University in Melbourne. RMIT separately confirmed that a former student alleged to be involved in the Flydubai incident had been enrolled at the university but did not complete an engineering qualification. The university did not identify the former student.

articleTitle: Rural consumer confidence worsened for six straight months: RBI survey
articleFeaturedImageAlt: market
description: RBI’s Current Situation Index — which captures perceptions of the economy, employment, prices, income and spending — fell to 90.6 in September, from 91.7 in July
body_raw: Rural consumer sentiment in India has weakened steadily through 2026, with households becoming increasingly pessimistic about the economy, jobs and their own incomes, even as they continue to expect spending to rise. The Reserve Bank of Indias RBI September 2026 Rural Consumer Confidence Survey RCCS points to a widening gap between how rural and semi-urban households view their current circumstances and what they hope will happen over the next year. The RBIs Current Situation Index CSI, which captures perceptions of the economy, employment, prices, income and spending compared with a year ago, fell to 90.6 in September, from 91.7 in July. This is the sixth consecutive decline from 100.5 in January, and marks a sharp deterioration from 100.9 in September 2025. The deterioration is broad-based. The net response on the general economic situation declined from -11.9 in July to -14.1 in September. On the employment front, the net response worsened from -8.0 to -10.5, while the income measure slipped from -8.7 to -9.9, the survey shows. These figures mean that the share of respondents who felt conditions had worsened exceeded those who saw an improvement by an increasingly large margin. Income data, inflation The income data is particularly revealing. In September, only 20.6 of respondents said their income had increased compared with a year earlier, while 30.5 said it had decreased. A year earlier, the corresponding figures were 24.5 and 26.5. The net response has consequently moved from -2.1 in September 2025 to -9.9 now. Inflation is another major source of pressure. Rural households median perception of current inflation rose to 6.8 in September, from 6.1 in July and 5.9 in May. Their one-year-ahead inflation expectation also climbed to 7.9, from 7.4 in July and 6.8 in March. The September reading is particularly striking because it is 70 basis points bps higher for current inflation and 50 bps higher for future inflation than in July. The price-level responses underline this anxiety. As many as 93.2 of respondents said prices had increased compared with a year earlier, up from 91.6 in July. For the next year, 85.9 expect prices to increase. Net spending improves, squeeze on household confidence Yet the survey does not point to a collapse in household spending. The spending net response improved to 79.6 in September, from 77.4 in July. Spending on essential items remained particularly strong, with a net response of 84.2, while the corresponding figure for non-essential spending rose to 39.3. The disconnect between weak present sentiment and relatively strong expectations is captured by the Future Expectations Index FEI. Although it eased to 112.8 from 113.6 in July, it remains firmly above 100, indicating optimism about the year ahead. However, this too has declined substantially from 129.3 in January. What the survey shows, therefore, is not simply rural pessimism but a squeeze on household confidence. Rural consumers are spending, but their perceptions of incomes, employment and economic conditions are deteriorating while inflation expectations are rising. The fact that future expectations remain optimistic provides some cushion. But if weak income growth and elevated price expectations persist, that optimism could come under further pressure. The September RBI survey, based on 8,799 responses collected across rural and semi-urban India, thus offers a cautionary signal the rural economy may still be supporting consumption, but households increasingly feel that their financial position is not keeping pace with the cost of living.

articleTitle: Vidyut Jammwal sits still for 16 minutes as tears roll down his face: ‘You need to stop’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vidyut Jammwal
description: Vidyut Jammwal’s unusual meditation has expert looking at what happens when we simply stop
body_raw: Actor Vidyut Jammwal is receivingwidespread online love formeditating for 16 minutes without blinking, holding his breath, and remaining remarkably still even as tears rolled down his eyes at theStreet Fighter trailer launch event.He also had a message to share for the younger generation, urging them to pause and take a breather. You need to stop. Stay still. It will take you places, said Jammwal. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. That statement is worth examining, especially at a time when almost every aspect of modern life encourages the opposite. We are taught to move faster, achieve more, consume more information, respond immediately and remain constantly available. Even our empty moments have almost disappeared. A lift ride, a traffic signal, a waiting room or two quiet minutes before a meeting are quickly occupied by a screen. Yet there is an important distinction we rarely discuss meditation and stillness are not necessarily the same practice, and each can teach us something different about ourselves, reflected Delnna Rrajesh, psychotherapist and relationship breakthrough coach. Delnna noted that meditation itself is a vast field, and many traditions include open-eyed, walking and movement-based practices, so it would be inaccurate to define meditation simply as sitting with ones eyes closed. It sounds easy until we try it. Within minutes, the body begins issuing instructions. Shift your leg. Move your hand. Look over there. Scratch that itch. Check the time. Pick up the phone. Speak. Do something. The mind joins in How much longer? What is the point of this? I am bored. I cannot do this. Suddenly, what seemed like an exercise in doing nothing becomes an extraordinary opportunity to observe how continuously we are pulled by sensation, thought, and impulse. Stillness makes restlessness visible, described Delnna. To the expert, that is one of its greatest values. We often assume that because we are constantly moving, the movement is voluntary. Stillness lets us see how much of our behaviour may actually be automatic. A sound occurs, and our attention follows it. Something moves, and our eyes chase it. A notification appears, and the hand reaches for the phone almost before a conscious decision has been made. An uncomfortable thought arises, and we immediately look for distraction. Stillness introduces a tiny but psychologically important possibility I can notice an impulse without immediately obeying it. Meditation can therefore help us observe what is happening within us stillness can help us discover that not everything happening within us requires an immediate response. The two practices can meet beautifully, but their emphasis can be different, expressed Delnna.         View this post on Instagram   A post shared by Varinder Chawla varindertchawla For most people, the experiment can be much simpler. Sit comfortably for a few minutes. Keep the eyes naturally open and blink normally. Allow the gaze to remain soft. Put the phone away. Minimise unnecessary movement without turning discomfort into punishment. Then observe what happens. Notice the urge to move, look, check, speak, plan or escape. Instead of judging the impulse, become curious about it, said Delnna. Meditation can then be practised separately and intentionally perhaps closing the eyes, depending on the method, settling attention and allowing yourself to go inward. We do not need to choose between meditation and stillness. We can train both. One can deepen our relationship with our inner world the other can strengthen our ability to stay steady while the outer world continues around us. The real test of either practice, however, begins when we leave the meditation room. A person can sit peacefully for an hour and still become completely reactive during an argument. We can have profound experiences with our eyes closed and still lose access to that awareness when somebody criticises us, our child refuses to listen, our partner touches an old wound, or anxiety begins constructing frightening possibilities. The deeper question is whether practice gradually changes what happens in those moments. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine.

articleTitle: Tracing Uttarakhand’s 8.27 lakh ‘missing’ voters: What EC’s camps, house visits will check
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The exercise, details of which were presented to all district election officers this week, will begin with three-day camps at all 12,543 polling stations from October 8 to 10, followed by house-to-house verification between October 12 and 20.
description: Days after the final rolls were published, the Election Commission of India will trace voters missing from the final roll, verify their status and enrol eligible electors through Form 6
body_raw: The Election Commission has launched a special drive to trace and verify 8.27 lakh electors who were marked ASDD uncollectible during Uttarakhands Special Intensive Revision SIR, with officials now being instructed to identify those whose names figured in the pre-SIR electoral roll but are missing from the final list. The exercise, details of which were presented to all district election officers this week, will begin with three-day camps at all 12,543 polling stations from October 8 to 10, followed by house-to-house verification between October 12 and 20. The drive is aimed at correcting omissions after the SIR rather than undertaking another revision officials will specifically trace people who were on the pre-SIR roll, verify their current status and enrol them through Form 6 if they remain eligible. The data presented by the Chief Electoral Officers office shows that 8,26,977 electors were marked ASDD during the SIR. The highest number was recorded in Dehradun 1,86,008, followed by Udham Singh Nagar 1,77,673, Haridwar 1,30,203, Almora 55,485, Pauri Garhwal 51,359 and Tehri Garhwal 43,625. The development comes days after Uttarakhand published its final electoral roll on October 3, with 71,58,949 electors - around 8 lakh fewer than the electorate before the SIR. Chief Electoral Officer BVRC Purushottam said Wednesday that the exercise would specifically look for people who were on the pre-SIR roll but are absent from the current roll. BLOs shall compare the current electoral roll with the pre-SIR electoral roll and identify such electors whose names were there in the pre-SIR roll but who are not included in the current electoral roll and prepare a list of such electors. House-to-house verification Following the three-day camps, BLOs will visit the homes of identified electors between October 12 and 20 to ascertain their present status and facilitate enrolment through Form 6 wherever they are found eligible. The exercise will also cover other left-out voters and first-time voters who became eligible with reference to October 1, 2026. Purushottam said the BLOs would also assist those who turned 18 on October 1 in filling Form 6, and that the exercise will involve not just election officials but also representatives of political parties. During the three-day camps, BLOs, Booth Awareness Group BAG members and Booth Level Agents BLA-2 will be present at polling stations. During house-to-house visits, BLOs will be accompanied by BAG members and, as far as possible, BLAs. The lists prepared by BLOs will be shared with BLAs of recognised political parties. At the end of the exercise, Electoral Registration Officers will again share booth-wise lists with political party representatives, giving them another opportunity to identify eligible voters left out of the roll. 8 lakh-plus drop after SIR The fresh exercise assumes significance against the scale of deletions during the revision. According to data by the CEOs office, Uttarakhand had 84,29,459 electors on the January 6, 2025 roll. Between January 2025 and August 13, 2026, there were 4,01,276 additions but 17,05,130 deletions across the revision process. The final roll published on October 3 contained 71,58,949 electors. During the claims-and-objections period between July 14 and August 13, 1,29,872 additions and 1,04,708 deletions were recorded. The Indian Express had earlier reported that 1,30,382 Form-7 applications seeking deletion of names were filed during the claims-and-objections period, with more than 85 percent of these coming from Udham Singh Nagar, Haridwar, Dehradun and Nainital. The Electoral Registration Officers will process the applications under the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. The presentation also draws their attention to Rule 20, which provides for a summary inquiry into claims and objections and an opportunity for the concerned persons to be heard.

articleTitle: Karan Johar says ‘no cricketers’ amid demand for Virat Kohli on Koffee With Karan Season 9
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Despite huge fan demand for Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma, Karan Johar has confirmed that no cricketers will appear in Koffee With Karan Season 9.
description: Despite huge fan demand for Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma, Karan Johar has confirmed that no cricketers will feature as guests in Koffee With Karan Season 9.
body_raw: Ever since director-producer Karan Johar announced that he is all set to return with his widely popular chat show, Koffee With Karan, for the ninth and last time, social media has been abuzz with speculation about who all will show up as guests. Meanwhile, one section of netizens has been strongly demanding that power couple Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma be brought on as guests in one of the episodes. Unpacking Koffee With Karan Season 9s latest teaser Now, the producers of the show have unveiled a new teaser, categorically denying the presence of any cricketers this time. The clip features Karan speaking on the phone with various unnamed people, hinting at his plans for Koffee With Karan Season 9. Reiterating that this will be the final time he hosts the chat show, the director insists, Im not acting, Im not pretending this will be my last. Must Read  Lost Rs 250 cr in 13 years Rajpal Yadav to SC, hints at film on cheque-bounce cases Karan then slips into his signature wit with, What? What do you mean it should have ended 10 years ago? How rude In conversation with another person, he says, Thank you for asking, but I havent invited you for eight seasons. So, I dont plan to invite you for the ninth either. Sorry, are you crying? Karan Johar puts end to Virat Kohli rumours Indirectly refuting speculations about Virat Kohlis presence on the show, he notes, Cricketers are not invited. Theyre also not coming. Theyre actually refusing. As the conversation continues, someone on the other side of the phone asks the director for the couch cushions as a gift. He wonders, Isnt that creepy? He then quips to someone else, I wont be calling her at all. God knows what else will come alive if she comes. Next, he is shown speaking to his mother, who worries he is being sacked from Koffee With Karan. No, Mumma, theyre not cutting my money. Its my decision to end the show. I will buy you that diamond, I promise, he tells her. Teasing what to expect from the show this time, he assures someone, You can manifest a relationship. But no, it doesnt help with divorce. Although Karan maintains that this season will be controversy-free, he ends the promotional video with a wink, suggesting he will wrap up his beloved chat show with a bang. ICYMI  Salman Khan hosts BJP youth leader at Mumbai home Touched by your warmth, simplicity While Virat Kohli has never been on the show, Anushka Sharma has appeared three times. She made her Koffee With Karan debut in 2011 during Season 3, alongside her Band Baaja Baaraat 2010 and Ladies vs Ricky Bahl 2011 co-star Ranveer Singh. She made her comeback the very next season, sharing the floor with veteran director Anurag Kashyap. Anushka Sharmas last Koffee With Karan appearance was in December 2016, when she arrived on Season 5 of the show with her Jab Tak Hai Jaan 2012 co-star Katrina Kaif. Why Karan Johar avoids inviting cricketers now In a conversation with Sania Mirza on her podcast last year, Karan had admitted that hes never actually invited Virat to be on the show. I have never asked Virat. And now, I am not asking any cricketers after what happened with Hardik Pandya and KL Rahul. There are many who I just felt wouldnt come, so I never asked them in the first place, he said. Karan had previously hosted KL Rahul and Hardik Pandya on the show, and Pandyas comments during the episode recieved a lot of flak. Both players also faced a suspension by BCCI. Soon after, the episode was pulled down from the streaming platform.

articleTitle: Account aggregator ‘interoperability’: What RBI’s move means for your asset statement
articleFeaturedImageAlt: RBI investments
description: Account aggregators are NBFCs that act as a secure bridge for banking data, allowing lenders to access all relevant data swiftly for faster loan disbursements, or manage consent for other companies attempting to fetch your data.
body_raw: Dematerialised accounts have made it easy for investors to track their investments across financial markets, be it stocks, mutual funds, debt instruments, or commodities. This has made investing quite hassle-free for the common man, eliminating the need to track statements through different apps or depositories. The Reserve Bank of Indias RBI move to now allow interoperability between financial account aggregators AAs could also get your bank holdings into the singular consolidated statement, eliminating the need to track different bank statements to keep a check on deposits. The central bank on Wednesday October 7 allowed interoperability among NBFC Account aggregators, enabling aggregation of financial information through all account aggregators from one account aggregator. What RBI said about account aggregators After the monetary policy statement, Governor Sanjay Malhotra said, We are also facilitating SEBI regulated depositories to include information related to deposit accounts in their consolidated account statement CAS. The measures will be implemented by December 31, 2026. Account aggregators are non-banking financial companies NBFCs who store and move the users banking data without having the permission to access it. They act as a secure bridge for banking data, allowing lenders to access all relevant data swiftly for faster loan disbursements, or manage consent for other companies attempting to fetch your data. The account aggregators are basically people with whom banks enter into a contract for the purpose of sharing information. You can basically get onboarded as a bank customer, consenting to provide your information. And on the basis of your information, they will be able to pull data, explained Vivek Iyer, Partner and National Leader for Financial Services at Grant Thornton Bharat. What changes for you Currently, a consolidated account statement gives an overview for either your banking assets such as deposits, or for demat holdings like stocks, mutual funds, and bonds. There are around 17 account aggregators registered under the RBIs NBFC-AA categorisation, each separately operating in these two spaces. With the RBI opening the door for interoperability between these aggregators, investors will now get a single CAS capturing fixed deposits, recurring deposits, mutual funds, and all other financial instruments regulated by the RBI and the Securities and Exchange Board of India SEBI. This will simplify tracking investments for an average investor. The bottomline, thus, is a comprehensive overview of all investments across the banking and financial markets. On the banking side, this consolidated overview will only be limited to the assets you hold like deposits, and not your loans. Currently, they account aggregators do not have permission to view bank deposits. Why? Because bank deposits sit under banking, the regulator for whom is RBI. And depositories sit under SEBI. So, what RBI has done with this reform is they have spoken to SEBI and told them that this is the reform we will implement. I will handle the aggregators from the banking end, you handle them from the depositories end, explained Iyer. This interoperability may also help smaller businesses that need loans, which are hampered by the lack of standardisation of information across different AAs. A more interoperable AA ecosystem can materially reduce this friction by enabling consent-based access to verified financial data and making the underwriting process faster and more efficient, according to Varoon Naidu, Co-founder of Capital Stack. This can be particularly meaningful for MSMEs and smaller businesses. Better access to banking and other financial data can allow lenders to assess actual cash flows and financial behaviour rather than relying predominantly on traditional bureau scores, collateral or borrower-submitted information. Over time, this should improve both the availability and quality of credit, reduce turnaround times and potentially allow lenders to price risk more accurately, said Naidu. Further scope for interoperability While the central bank has taken initial steps towards a comprehensive asset overview for each person with the announcement on Wednesday, there is further scope going ahead. For example, the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India IRDAI could also come on board so that an individuals CAS also reflects the insurance policies they hold. This can be done through cooperation between the RBI, SEBI, and IRDAI. See, for that, the insurance market needs to be matured. So, one step at a time. They SEBI and RBI said let us just first integrate the bank deposits with the investments. And then we can get into the whole insurance aspects also. At some point in time, you will see an integration of your insurance also coming into it, said Iyer. So, the goal is basically a single comprehensive list of assets held by each investor. And the RBIs permission for interoperability between AAs marks an important step towards achieving this.

articleTitle: Gukesh’s coach Gajewski: ‘Good for him to be reminded he can play really well’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gukesh
description: Chess-wise the recent Olympiad was 'good' not 'great' for Gukesh but mentally he was strong, which is a good thing, says his coach Grzegorz Gajewski
body_raw: One of Indian chesss biggest positives at the recent Chess Olympiad was the uptick in form of world champion D Gukesh, who had seven wins and three draws in the first 10 rounds at a staggering performance rating of 2,797, before he lost his final round clash with Hungarian GM Gleb Dudin. The tournament was likely the world champions last appearance in an over-the-board tournament before he hunkers down to prepare for his upcoming World Chess Championship battle against the Uzbek challenger Javokhir Sindarov. For Gukesh, the Olympiad proved to be a slump-buster. Since he has become the world champion in December 2024, hes not won a tournament, coming close at the Tata Steel tournament in Wijk aan Zee in January 2025 and then the Norway Chess tournament that same year. But in recent tournaments, his form has dwindled, at Norway Chess in 2026, he was last in the six-player field, while at the Chennai Grand Masters, he did not taste victory in a single game. These Olympiad results are definitely good for the confidence, its good for Gukesh to be reminded that he can play really well, Gukeshs coach, Polish grandmaster Grzegorz Gajewski, tells The Indian Express in an interview. Before the tournament began, there was some criticism about Gukesh playing on Board 4 for India with Praggnanandhaa on Board 1, Arjun Erigaisi on Board 2 and Nihal Sarin on Board 3. In the previous two Olympiads, Gukesh had excelled on Board 1. Later, Gukesh had revealed that it was his call to play on the fourth board, which in hindsight looks like a masterstroke. I wouldnt call it this way a masterstroke. His teammates performed better in some of the previous events and they were also higher rated so it just seemed like the right thing to do, says Gajewski. Ask Gajewski for his assessment of Gukeshs form at the recent Olympiad, and he says Chess-wise the Olympiad was good but not great. Gukesh can definitely do better. Mentally he was strong and thats the most important thing right now. Chess-wise the recent Olympiad was good not great for Gukesh but mentally he was strong, which is a good thing, says his coach Grzegorz Gajewski The world also saw a different side of Gukesh at the Olympiad. A much easy-going side. He made jokes with the rest of the team. He posted a hilarious video with Praggnanandhaa about a fan mistaking the both of them. He was even at the Bermuda Party an Olympiad tradition where players from all nations come together for an evening party just before the only rest day of the tournament despite the Indians having lost to Uzbekistan that day, a result which more or less ascertained that the Indians would not be able to defend gold. Ask Gajewski whats changed about Gukesh, and he replies For sure his routines during the Olympiad werent as strict as they used to be and I think its a positive thing. The last year was really difficult for Gukesh and in general achieving so much comes with a price. I think that he managed to figure it out and indeed he seems really happy now

articleTitle: Why DMK is blowing hot and cold on Rahul Gandhi over protest against CEC
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gyanesh Kumar resignation, rahul gandhi, priyanka gandhi vadra, gyanesh kumar, election commission of india, cec resignation protest, india bloc protest new delhi, voter list deletion row, parliament street protest, akashvani bhavan detention, vote chori allegations, india bloc, election commissioner dissent report, akashvani bhavan, election commission news
description: While DMK spokesperson Saravanan Annadurai has sharpened his attacks on the LoP, senior leader TKS Elangovan has “defended” Gandhi’s right to protest.
body_raw: Months after the Congress walked into the C Joseph Vijay-led TVK camp to form the government in Tamil Nadu, the DMK is blowing hot and cold on Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi over his campaign against the Election Commission EC. While a section of the DMK has sharpened its attacks on Gandhi, a marked contrast that reflects the changed relationship between the two parties, another section has defended the LoPs right to protest. DMK spokesperson Saravanan Annadurai on Wednesday cited a media report on the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls to question why Gandhi, who has forcefully raised allegations of electoral manipulation elsewhere, had not spoken similarly about Tamil Nadu. Daro Mat Dont be scared, Annadurai wrote, claiming that constituencies with large numbers of deletions disproportionately went to Vijays TVK. According to Annadurai, the TVK won 84 of the 135 constituencies where more than 20,000 voters were deleted and all 10 constituencies where deletions exceeded 80,000. He asked Gandhi whether he believed the SIR had affected Tamil Nadu and the DMK, and whether the EC had acted fairly. The figures and the claim about their electoral effect were cited by Annadurai from the media report-the inputs provided do not include an ECs response to them. Measured criticism Even as Annadurai attacked Gandhi, senior DMK leader TKS Elangovan defended the Congress leaders right to protest. It is the right of citizens to fight against the governments wrongdoings. That is what Rahul Gandhi did yesterday, Elangovan said on Wednesday. He also demanded Kumars removal and fresh elections in states where, he alleged, the electoral process had been compromised. The apparent contradiction is partly explained by the political rearrangement since Tamil Nadus April election. The DMK subsequently left the Congress-led INDIA bloc. The TVK now governs with support from Congress and other smaller parties. That has given the dispute over electoral rolls another layer. The DMK and Congress may still attack the same institution over the SIR, but they now approach Tamil Nadu from opposite sides of the political field. The DMK leaders reactions came as Gandhi and other Opposition leaders intensified their confrontation with the EC in New Delhi. On Tuesday, Gandhi was detained at Akashvani Bhavan after police stopped Opposition MPs from marching to the poll bodys office. He subsequently staged a nine-hour sit-in. The Opposition has demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar following Express report last month that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally recorded objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions they said had been taken without their knowledge, including matters relating to the SIR. Afraid of Vijay Annadurai had been even more personal a day earlier. While Gandhi was staging his Delhi protest, the DMK spokesperson asked whether he was reluctant to raise Tamil Nadus deletions because he was afraid of Vijay. He also called Gandhi duplicitous and used the phrase Once a skunk, always a skunk. He further questioned why Gandhi had not endorsed what he described as Congress president Mallikarjun Kharges position that state governments elected after the SIR should be dissolved. For the DMK, the argument is therefore no longer simply whether electoral-roll revisions deserve scrutiny. It is why Gandhis campaign against the SIR, in the partys telling, appears to stop when it reaches a state governed by his new ally.

articleTitle: The Narendra Modi I saw up close
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Prime Minister Narendra Modi
description: That combination of intellectual rigour, decisiveness, accountability and an unwavering focus on outcomes is what, in my view, distinguishes Narendra Modi
body_raw: There are leaders remembered for their soaring political rhetoric, others for electoral victories, and some for the institutions they leave behind. Narendra Modi, in my experience, is best understood through something less obvious His method. Over the years, I had the opportunity to observe him closely, first as an administrator and later from within government. What struck me most was not any single policy decision, but the way he approached problems. Whether the issue was a sweeping national reform or an administrative bottleneck, his first instinct was always diagnosis. He rarely accepted a summary at face value. Instead, the questions would come quickly. What is happening on the ground? Why is it happening? What have you done so far? What exactly is preventing a solution? The questions were not designed to test people. They were designed to test assumptions. Once he understood the reality of a situation, the shift from diagnosis to action was remarkably swift. I saw this most clearly during demonetisation. The decision brought enormous logistical and economic challenges. Long reviews became routine. Every aspect of implementation was being monitored closely. Yet even while dealing with immediate pressures, Modi was already looking beyond the crisis itself. He saw an opportunity to accelerate digital payments across India. He did not view the challenge purely through a technological lens. He understood that ordinary citizens would not embrace digital transactions if commissions and transaction costs remained barriers. Rather than treating those costs as unavoidable, he pursued the issue directly with the Reserve Bank of India. The logic was simple. If friction was preventing adoption, then the friction had to be reduced. Even a vegetable vendor should be able to accept a digital payment. There were, of course, many other questions around currency circulation, cash holdings, gold purchases and the extent to which money returned to the banking system. Yet what I remember most vividly is the relentless focus on solutions. That was characteristic of his approach Identify the obstacle. Understand what sustains it. Remove it. What began as a period of disruption went on to become a major catalyst for Indias digital economy. The same mindset shaped his expectations of those who worked with him. Modi places extraordinary value on preparation. A proposal might appear flawless on paper, but within minutes his questions would reveal whether the presenter truly understood the issue. He expected policymakers to know not only the contents of a brief, but also the larger ecosystem around it The administrative realities, institutional constraints, political implications and impact on citizens. As a result, even routine meetings often became rigorous working sessions. I experienced that standard from the very beginning of my association with him. My first interaction with Modi was brief. Carrying a bouquet, I remarked that I was meeting a Yug Purush, a defining figure of our times. He laughed immediately and brushed aside the compliment, putting me at ease. The more consequential encounter came in May 2014. I was driving home from the NGO I was then running when the late Arun Jaitley called and asked me to report immediately to Gujarat Bhawan. True to form, Modi dispensed with formalities and moved straight to the task at hand. He asked me to examine the political structure of the Union government and recommend which ministries could be merged, streamlined or newly created to improve governance, particularly in the energy, skill and infrastructure sectors, core to Indias future. Working out of a quiet desk in Gujarat Bhawan, I focused on the assignment. Modi was looking for an answer Will this improve governance? That became the lens through which every recommendation was tested. I noticed a fleeting look of disappointment at my presentation. He had expected graphics and presentation, not a stack of paper. It was an early indication of how naturally he gravitated towards technology, visualisation and contemporary tools one could touch, feel, and experience. Shortly afterwards, the Prime Minister conveyed to me that he intended to appoint me as his Principal Secretary. When I raised concerns about restrictions arising from my previous role at TRAI, Jaitley Ji dismissed them with characteristic confidence. Dont bother the Prime Minister with technicalities. The demands of the office became clear almost immediately. Traditionally, the Principal Secretary accompanies the Prime Minister on official foreign visits. I suggested instead that I remain in Delhi, believing I could contribute more by overseeing matters at home while he travelled. His response surprised me. You have lifted a heavy burden off my chest. Modis work ethic recognises neither geography nor time zones. Wherever he travelled, he remained deeply engaged, often calling to review developments, track pending matters and push decisions forward. He was also a keen observer. Ideas encountered abroad, whether in urban infrastructure, public spaces or museum design, often found their way into discussions about governance back home. That same instinct is visible in initiatives such as Yuge Yugeen Bharat. To Modi, a museum is not merely a repository of artefacts. It is a living institution that connects future generations with Indias civilizational journey. Even in matters of culture and heritage, his focus remained on how institutions could educate, engage and endure. Perhaps more than anything else, Modi has little patience for inertia. If an obstacle exists, whether technological, financial or bureaucratic, his instinct is to look for a solution rather than an explanation. That expectation creates pressure, but it also creates clarity. What has earned him the trust of many who work with him, however, is something else his willingness to assume responsibility. During the prolonged opposition against the land acquisition laws, I eventually recommended that the legislation be withdrawn in the larger interest of the agricultural sector. The reforms had arrived ahead of their time and early in his first tenure. He looked at me with a knowing smile. Aap ye keh rahe hain? You are saying this? Yet he agreed. The ordinance lapsed. He is equally quick to acknowledge the contributions of others. Several years before the pandemic, I had suggested distributing surplus grain stocks rather than allowing them to deteriorate in storage. The proposal did not move forward because of fiscal constraints. When Covid-19 struck, however, he immediately saw its relevance. Moments before announcing the programme that would eventually support nearly 80 crore beneficiaries, he was convinced that poverty elimination is a strong argument. Looking back, it is not any single reform, programme or policy decision that best explains Narendra Modi to me. It is a habit of mind. He begins by asking what stands in the way. He refuses to accept cannot as an answer. He presses relentlessly until a solution emerges. Over the years, I have seen that instinct applied to governance, technology, national security, foreign policy, welfare, culture and institution-building alike. The question he returned to repeatedly, whether discussing ministries, digital payments or public policy, was always the same Will this improve governance? That combination of intellectual rigour, decisiveness, accountability and an unwavering focus on outcomes is what, in my view, distinguishes Narendra Modi. It is also why, when I first met him many years ago and referred to him as a Yug Purush, it did not feel like just praise. Time and experience have only reinforced that impression. As a man who continues to redefine our era, Prime Minister Modis mark will remain indelible in the annals of history. The writer is Chairperson, Prime Ministers Museum and Library, Chairman, Temple Construction Committee, Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. He served as Principal Secretary to Prime Minister Narendra Modi during 2014-2019

articleTitle: Bihar court convicts police officer of contempt for flouting orders, fines him Re 1
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rohtas court ias ips training bihar sp police officer dig contempt case kidnapping
description: The court observed that the Superintendent of Police, Rohtas, had habitually, deliberately and intentionally failed to comply with court orders, despite being given repeated opportunities.
body_raw: A Bihar court has found a senior police official guilty of contempt for flouting its orders and slapped a symbolic Re 1 fine. The court also directed the Ministry of Personnel and Training to overhaul the training system for IAS and IPS officers in alignment with the democratic system. Additional Sessions Court Judge Anil Kumar had iniciated contempet proceeding against the then SP Rohtas, Raushan Kumar, on August 17, under the provision concerning wilful disobedience of court orders, after observing that the SP had failed to comply with its directions and had not responded to a show-cause notice. Criticising his conduct, the court directed the fines recovery from his salary and ordered that the conviction be entered in his service record. The opposite party has not only failed to comply with the court orders habitually, deliberately and intentionally but also tried to overawe and overpower the court by approaching several eminent persons. His antecedent conduct as well as conduct during trial, especially not appearing for his evidence, shows his haughty, arrogant and egoistic attitude and thereby deprives him of any sympathy of this court, the court observed while convicting the then Rohtas SP. Directing its office to send a copy to the Ministry of Personnel and Training to draw attention to the need to overhaul the training system for IAS and IPS officers so that it is aligned with the democratic system, the order said, This problem is not confined to Bihar only. In an execution matter, Namakkal Tamil Nadu D.M. was sent several orders, including show-cause notices, but he did not reply even once. Then, the petitioner was asked to withdraw it and approach the Madras High Court under Article 227 of the Constitution of India. He did the same. Unconditional apology of DM, Namakkal sent to this court. Drawing reference from various instances and pointing out serious flaws in the training of such IPS officers, Justice Anil Kumar said, Even this court has no good experience with IAS officers, especially district magistrates. In the Periyamal Case, the Supreme Court directed that execution cases must be disposed of within six months. Noting that even after the issuance of notices and disciplinary action recommendation against the then Rohtas SP, the court said, Till date, neither the DGP nor the chief secretary sent even a single chit of paper This shows the apathy, indifference and respect of the Bihar Administration for the District Court While initiating the contempt proceedings, the court remarked, As the court found the whole administration unresponsive, it was compelled to launch a proceeding for wilfully disobeying the court orders, lowering the dignity of the court and flouting the majesty of law. The court highlighted that, on the states request, four dates were given, i.e., on August 28, September 7, September 11, September 14, and September 22, but he did not appear to give his evidence. Rather, he used this time to pressurise the court to drop the proceedings by approaching an eminent person. A kidnapping case and order to SP The court made these observations while dealing with a case related to kidnapping. The Rohtas District Court had convicted the 10 persons, noting that even when the victim and his complainant son turned hostile. The court had subsequently directed the then Superintendent of Police, Rohtas, Raushan Kumar, to obtain the accused persons latest criminal antecedents, register an FIR and initiate action against the victim for alleged perjury. According to the court, the victim was allegedly kidnapped for a ransom of Rs 1.5 crore and had then turned hostile after allegedly receiving Rs 20 lakh. The court also directed an inquiry into the victim and his son after evidence suggested their involvement in illegal activities. During the trial of the Session Case, it has come on record that the victim was involved in the business of Ganja Cannabis and became rags to riches from that illegal business, it said. It added that just before the incident of kidnapping, his informant-son won one crore rupees in gambling before the Diwali Puja, which was cited as the immediate reason for his fathers kidnapping. Expressing displeasure, the court said that the then SP did not realise the urgency and submitted the report a month after the disposal of the case that, too, was merely a formality because his report was just copied from the case diary. No recent criminal antecedents were provided. The court later found that the SP had failed to comply with these directions and did not respond to a show-cause notice issued in July. It therefore initiated contempt proceedings, alleging wilful disobedience of court orders and conduct lowering the dignity of the court.

articleTitle: 32-year-old man with two stents says heart attacks know no age: ‘Don’t miss out on this particular test’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: heart attack
description: A 32-year-old heart attack survivor has urged people not to assume they are healthy based on their appearance or fitness levels. A cardiologist explains what actually matters for heart health.
body_raw: A 32-year-old heart attack survivor, Shaumit Biswas, recently shared a list of things he believes people should do to protect their heart health. In a video on Instagram, Biswas, who said he has two stents in his heart, urged people not to assume that being young, fit, or appearing healthy means they are protected from heart disease. Heart attacks know no age, no fitness, he said, emphasising the importance of regular health checks. He also highlighted Lipoproteina, or Lpa, a largely inherited cardiovascular risk factor, along with sleep, nutrition, physical activity and stress management. Dont miss out on this particular test, he stressed. But how much of this advice holds up medically? Dr Anup Taksande, Clinical Director - Cardiology and Cardiac Interventions, KIMS Hospitals, Thane, explains what people should know. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. Looking fit does not mean your arteries are healthy According to Dr Taksande, a common misconception is that someone who exercises regularly and has no symptoms must have healthy arteries. Heart disease doesnt always give warning signs, he said. Conditions such as high blood pressure, diabetes and abnormal cholesterol can remain undetected for years. Genetics can also influence cardiovascular risk, particularly when there is a family history of heart attack or stroke at a young age. Fitness can be seen while risk is generally not visible, Dr Taksande explained. For most adults, he said, it is more useful to track basic health measurements than to undergo multiple tests without a clear reason. These include blood pressure, blood sugar or HbA1c, and a lipid profile. These checks should begin in early adulthood, with the frequency depending on a persons age and individual risk factors. People with symptoms, several cardiovascular risk factors or a strong family history may need a more detailed evaluation. ECGs, stress tests, echocardiography or coronary calcium scans can be useful in certain people, Dr Taksande said, but these should not automatically be treated as routine tests for every healthy adult. The appropriate test is the one which provides an answer to a significant clinical question, he added. What is Lipoproteina? One of Biswas key recommendations was getting Lpa tested. Dr Taksande said this is worth knowing because it represents a cardiovascular risk factor largely determined by genetics. Lpa, or lipoproteina, is a particle which carries cholesterol and the amount of it is mostly inherited, he said. Unlike several conventional cardiovascular risk factors, lifestyle changes have only a limited effect on the amount of Lpa produced by the body. Elevated Lpa can increase the risk of plaque formation and cardiovascular events, including premature heart attack and stroke. It is also associated with calcific aortic valve disease. Importantly, a person can have an apparently acceptable conventional cholesterol profile and still have elevated Lpa. Present guidance on cardiovascular health recommends that Lpa should be measured at least once during adulthood, Dr Taksande said, particularly in people with a family history of premature cardiovascular disease or cardiovascular disease that cannot be adequately explained by their usual risk factors. Because Lpa levels are largely genetic and generally remain stable, repeated testing is usually unnecessary unless there is a specific clinical reason. However, an elevated Lpa does not mean a heart attack is inevitable. It simply means that you should take the other risk factors which can be modified-particularly LDL cholesterol, blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, and lifestyle-much more seriously, Dr Taksande said. Should you cut out sugar and oil completely? Biswas suggested reducing sugar and oil as two key dietary changes for better heart health. Dr Taksande, however, cautioned against reducing cardiovascular nutrition to a single ingredient. Nutrition topics are frequently made unnecessarily polarising, he said, noting that describing sugar as a poison or presenting one cooking oil as universally harmful and another as universally protective oversimplifies nutrition. Excessive sugar intake, particularly from sugary drinks and highly processed foods, can contribute to weight gain, insulin resistance, diabetes and high triglyceride levels. These factors can, in turn, increase cardiovascular risk. Cooking oil also needs to be considered for both quality and quantity. Dr Taksande recommends limiting saturated and trans fats while favouring unsaturated fats. He also advises avoiding heating and reusing cooking oil.   View this post on Instagram   A post shared by Shaumit Biswas hustlemuscle.sb The heart doesnt react to a single ingredient rather, it reacts to the way our diet is patterned over a period of years, he said. Instead of searching for one perfect cooking oil, Dr Taksande recommends an overall eating pattern that includes vegetables, fruits, whole grains, pulses and nuts where appropriate, along with sufficient protein and a moderate amount of suitable cooking oil. For maintaining heart health, sticking to a moderate approach is generally better than adopting extreme dietary measures, he said. How much exercise do you need? Biswas recommended 30 to 45 minutes of movement four to five times a week and suggested that people do not need to run marathons to protect their hearts. Dr Taksande agrees that regular movement is an important part of cardiovascular prevention. Physical activity can improve blood pressure, insulin sensitivity, lipid profile, weight control and cardiorespiratory fitness. Adults should generally aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity physical activity a week, along with appropriate muscle-strengthening activity. This means that activities such as brisk walking can contribute meaningfully to the weekly target. The key is consistency rather than extreme exercise. Sleep and stress matter, too Biswas also emphasised getting seven to eight hours of sleep every night and incorporating stillness through breathing exercises or meditation. Dr Taksande said these are not merely lifestyle extras. They form part of cardiovascular prevention, he said. For most adults, he recommends aiming for around 7 to 9 hours of good-quality sleep. Consistently getting too little sleep is associated with poorer metabolic and cardiovascular health. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine.

articleTitle: Indian-origin woman arrested in Canada after confrontation with pedestrian turns physical
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Indian origin woman arrested in Canada
description: In the video, the woman is seen getting out of the passenger side of the vehicle and confronting the pedestrian. She appears to tell him that recording her was illegal before reaching for his phone.
body_raw: An Indian-origin woman was arrested in Calgary, Canada, after a confrontation with a pedestrian, who filmed the act on his phone and later circulated it online. The incident reportedly started when the vehicle carrying the woman allegedly failed to give way to a pedestrian crossing the road. The man began filming the encounter on his phone, after which the situation appeared to escalate. In the video, the woman is seen getting out of the passenger side of the vehicle and confronting the pedestrian. She appears to tell him that recording her was illegal before reaching for his phone. Its not legal to make a video, she can be heard saying in the footage. The confrontation then turned physical, with the woman allegedly grabbing the mans backpack and dragging him across the pavement. The police arrived at the scene soon after and arrested her. In the video, the man at the receiving end of the assault claimed that the womans husband, who was behind the wheel, was driving without valid insurance. Authorities have not publicly provided further details about the viral video or the circumstances surrounding the arrest. Watch the video   View this post on Instagram   A post shared by BodyCamDDE bodycamdde   The footage has since been viewed thousands of times on social media, prompting a debate over the confrontation and whether a person can legally record an incident taking place in a public space. Before you mess with people, make sure your papers are legit, one user commented. Why do they always think that theyre above the law? Probably because they usually get away with it, another wrote. You have no right to act superior in a country that isnt yours, a third user said, while another added, She forgot that shes not in India anymore. The Calgary incident comes weeks after another case involving an Indian-origin woman in Canada also drew attention online. Raj Tiwana was arrested following a confrontation with her tenant, who later posted a series of videos alleging that his landlady had repeatedly harassed him and interfered in his life. articleTitle: Bethlehem Kudumba Unit effect: Arvind Swamy-Sridevi’s shelved film to be revived after decades
articleFeaturedImageAlt: After 'Yavanakathayil' went viral in Bethlehem Kudumba Unit, Joshiy's shelved film Anna is set for revival.
description: After 'Yavanakathayil' went viral in Bethlehem Kudumba Unit, producer Tomichan Mulakuppadam has acquired the rights to revive director Joshiy's shelved film Anna, originally starring Arvind Swamy and Sridevi.
body_raw: Movies getting shelved isnt a new phenomenon in Malayalam cinema. From Randamoozham, Swarnachamaram, Australia, and Karnan to Dhanushkodi, Kaaliyan, and Antichrist, several films never progressed beyond the initial stages. Recently, director Girish ADs blockbuster romantic comedy Bethlehem Kudumba Unit brought one such film, Anna, back into the spotlight. Now, the movie is finally set for revival, with a new team taking over. Veteran producer Tomichan Mulakuppadam - best known for bankrolling blockbusters such as Pulimurugan, Pokkiri Raja, and Ramaleela - recently announced he has acquired the rights to Anna and is gearing up to give it a new lease of life. Taking to social media, he expressed his elation at the endeavour and stated he would announce the cast and crew details later. Also Read  No one is to blame Kalaranjini lost her voice after consuming fake blood containing acid Tomichan Mulakuppadam acquires rights to shelved film Anna I am happy to share that I have acquired the rights to the film Anna, which started in the 1990s but was shelved for various reasons. Years later, when the song Yavanakathayil from the film became a sensation again through Bethlehem Kudumba Unit, there were many enquiries and discussions about Anna, he wrote. Tomichan added, It is with the desire to bring the story and associated memories of that film to the new generation through new writers that I have taken over the production rights of Anna. A new beginning for a film that stopped midway three decades ago. More details, including the director and cast, will be announced later. Anna is coming back to the silver screen through Mulakuppadam Films. What happened to Anna? For the unversed, master filmmaker Joshiy was set to helm the film in the 90s, with Arvind Swamy and superstar Sridevi in the lead roles. According to Onmanorama, veteran writer and novelist N Mohanan originally scripted Anna, and Balram of Ambu Films was supposed to produce it. The movie centred on the love story of Hari Arvind Swamy, a Brahmin boy, and Anna Sridevi, a Christian girl. Anna was envisioned with music given the utmost prominence, and legendary composer Ouseppachan and veteran lyricist Shibu Chakravarthy were brought on board for the same. They crafted eight songs for Anna and completed their recordings even before the filming began. ICYMI  Fahadh Faasil says wont get half of Rs 300 cr as Bethlehem Kudumba Unit earns Rs 326 cr However, the project soon ran into scheduling problems, as the makers couldnt match the dates of Arvind Swamy and Sridevi. Team Anna even considered replacing Sridevi with Meena. Yet, Arvind Swamys availability remained an issue, further delaying the project. Joshiy also had other movies lined up. Thus, Anna was shelved without any of its scenes being filmed. Nevertheless, the movies music found its way to the public in 1995 when Magna Sound released a cassette containing all eight songs recorded for Anna. Yavanakathayil was one of those songs, which director Girish AD included in Bethlehem Kudumba Unit, allowing Anna to rise from the ashes like a phoenix. Must Read  Bethlehem Kudumba Unit review Nivin Pauly leads a sweet, non-creepy age-gap rom-com About Bethlehem Kudumba Unit Featuring Nivin Pauly and Mamitha Baiju in the lead roles, Bethlehem Kudumba Unit opened to rave reviews and emerged as the highest-grossing Malayalam film of all time, earning Rs 330.89 crore worldwide, according to industry tracker Sacnilk. Also starring Sangeeth Prathap, Suresh Krishna, Vinay Forrt, Roshan Shanavas, and Shyam Mohan, the romantic comedy was bankrolled by Dileesh Pothan, Fahadh Faasil, and Syam Pushkaran under the banner of Bhavana Studios.

articleTitle: Mary Kom’s ex-husband files defamation suit against her amid Bigg Boss stay: ‘It’s a strong case’

description: Mary Kom's ex-husband Onler has filed a criminal defamation suit against the boxer. She is currently a participant on Bigg Boss 20.

Onler confirmed that he was pursuing the matter and told the publication, I have a strong case. I have faith in the judicial system of India. The matter is sub judice, so I wont comment any further.
