description: This will be the first time since 1984 that the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has auctioned attached properties to recover pending tax dues.
body_raw: In a major move to recover tax dues and boost revenue, the Mumbai civic body has put three commercial Mumbai properties, including the famous Imperial Grand Palace Hotel at the Royal Palms in Aarey Forest, up for auction. This will be the first time since 1984 that the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation BMC has auctioned attached properties to recover pending tax dues. This is also the first time the BMC has attached a property linked to the contentious Royal Palms project to recover property tax. In total, the BMC will be auctioning three properties to recover Rs 74.98 crore. According to civic records, the Imperial Grand Palace Hotel auction shall recover pending dues of Rs 41.52 crore. The Royal Palms project, a contentious project that took off in the 1990s, aimed to transform a portion of the Aarey Forest into a luxury venue for leisure activities by constructing a chain of hotels, restaurants and a golf course. The project, however, nosedived after the properties got entangled in several financial cases. The current outstanding tax from this property stands at Rs 41.52 crore. The proprietors have been sent multiple notices, and we have had meetings with them. However, despite multiple deliberations, they have failed to pay the pending dues. Therefore, we have attached the property and will be putting it up for auction soon, a civic official told The Indian Express. The property has a carpet area of 38,143 square meters and has 422 rooms. It is located in a quaint corner of the Aarey Forest. The Imperial Palace was a five-star hotel listed as part of the Royal Palms project. In the early 2000s, this hotel was a preferred venue for luxurious activities however, its popularity dwindled after 2012. At present, the property lies unused and in a dilapidated state. Civic officials said the last conference recorded in this hotel was in 2012. Besides this hotel, the civic body will auction another commercial property in Malad Kurar for Rs 3.46 crore and another in Bandra for Rs 30.6 crore. In February, civic authorities attached 12 properties to recover pending dues up to Rs 269.62 crore. Civic officials said that after these properties were listed, some of their owners reached out and settled their claims while the remaining owners approached the court. The civic body put them up for auction after the owners of these three properties didnt make any effort to save them. Of the 12 properties that were listed, management of six properties settled the bill while six properties are still listed as default subjects. Of these six properties, two are open land parcels. Since the court has ordered us to revise the existing method of calculating the tax rate on land, we will be sending them a fresh bill. One of the remaining owners approached the court, and the case is sub judice. As a result, we will be putting out these three properties for auction, the official said. The civic authorities levy property tax on all real estate and commercial properties located within the BMC jurisdiction. Once the property owners default on paying taxes, the civic authorities send them notices, adding penalties. If owners still do not pay the taxes, these properties are seized or attached temporarily and put up for auction after legal proceedings. Property tax is one of the highest sources of revenue for the BMC, and this year, it has collected Rs 7,611 crore against an annual target of Rs 7,341 crore till March 31.

articleTitle: Why does a university in Gujarat celebrate Gandhi Jayanti on Oct 7?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Mahatma Gandhi spinning the charkha, a symbol of Swadeshi, self-reliance and resistance to British rule (Wikimedia Commons)
description: Gujarat Vidyapith, which the Mahatma established in Ahmedabad in 1920, celebrates ‘Rentiya Baras’ every year – Gandhi’s birthday in accordance with the Vikram Samvat. This Oct 7, it took the charkha to 350-odd schools across Ahmedabad.
body_raw: Five days after the people and government of India observed Gandhi Jayanti, the university the Mahatma founded in Ahmedabad celebrated his birthday on Wednesday October 7. Gujarat Vidyapith traditionally observes Gandhijis birthday in accordance with the Hindu Vikram calendar. As part of this years celebration, it took the charkha to around 350 municipal schools across Ahmedabad to spread Gandhijis message of swadeshi. When was Gandhiji born according to the Hindu calendar? Gandhi was born on Bhadarva Vad Baras, that is, the 12th day dwadashi of the sixth month of the Hindu lunisolar calendar, known as Bhadrapada, in the year 1925 of the Vikram Samvat, which corresponds to October 2, 1869 of the Gregorian calendar-the date universally recognised as his birthday. The Vikram Samvat, which is used by many Hindus to determine the dates of religious rituals and festivals and for making astrological calculations, started in 57 BCE-that is, 57 years before the Gregorian calendar, which is the standard international civil dating system in use around the world. 2026 corresponds primarily to Vikram Samvat 2083, which began on March 19-20 of this year. The official Indian national calendar follows the Shaka Samvat, which began in 78CE. The Gujarat Vidyapith has been celebrating Gandhis birthday by the Hindu Vikram Samvat calendar as Rentiya Baras for the past 90 years. Why is the Mahatmas birthday called Rentiya Baras? Rentiya means spinning wheel in Gujarati, which Gandhi used to spin khadi. He had wanted to dedicate his birthday to the charkha, and desired that the day should be celebrated as Rentiya Baras. Ravindra Pancholi, associate professor of Social Work at Gujarat Vidyapith, told The Indian Express When a demand was raised by his Gandhis followers to celebrate his birthday, Gandhiji said that he did not like it, and that this day his birthday according to the Vikram Samvat could instead be observed as Rentiya Baras. So, from around 1929-30 began this tradition of celebrating Gandhis birthday as per the Vikram Samvat calendar as Rentiya Baras, and not as Mohan Jayanti or Gandhi Jayanti, Pancholi 55, who is grandson of the late Gujarati writer and educationist Manubhai Pancholi Darshak, said. Why did Gandhi want to use the imagery of the charkha? For Gandhi, the charkha or spinning wheel was the most potent symbol of Indian self-reliance. He saw the charkha as an instrument of economic, political, and moral resistance against the British. Gandhi first wrote about the symbolism of the charkha in Hind Swaraj in 1909. After he started living in the Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad in 1917, he started to experiment with spinning and weaving by hand, and promoted khadi hand-spun, hand-woven cloth as an alternative to cloth made in the mills of Lancashire in Britain. Gandhi saw khadi and the charkha as a path to Indian self-sufficiency and non-violent resistance to colonialism. Besides the political and economic imperative of Swadeshi, he also encouraged the act of spinning to promote the dignity of labour and to identify with the poor. How has the Gujarat Vidyapith taken this message forward on Gandhis birthday? As part of the Non-Cooperation Movement that he launched in August 1920, Gandhi called for a boycott of schools and colleges under the control of the British government. In opposition to Lord Macaulays colonial education system that worked to sustain the interests of Empire, Indian nationalists established five Vidyapiths to provide anti-colonial education to Indian youth. Gujarat Vidyapith, which was founded on October 18, 1920 by the Mahatma himself, was one of these five Vidyapiths. Today, it is one of the national universities with a charter from the Government of India and seeks to promote Gandhijis ideals of service-oriented education, the Gujarat Vidyapith says on its website. To this end, the university has been celebrating Rentiya Baras in different ways every year, Advaita Dave, Public Relations Officer of the Vidyapith, said. Last year, our staff and students spun charkha at the Sabarmati Riverfront for around an hour and a half. Apart from Swadeshi, the idea was to spread the message that spinning the charkha is a kind of yoga as well, which helps one to improve concentration, Dave said. Pancholi said that in earlier years, students of the Vidyapith have taken part in Akhand Kantan or non-stop spinning on the occasion of Rentiya Baras, taking turns to spin the charkha continuously for 12 hours in batches of 20-25, with each batch spinning for two hours. What happened on Rentiya Baras this year? The Gujarat Vidyapith organised a special program on October 7 to take Gandhis ideals of Swadeshi, self-reliance and khadi to students of schools run by Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation. Around 200 volunteers and more than 1,800 students of Gujarat Vidyapith will visit 351 schools across 48 wards of Ahmedabad city. They will demonstrate the spinning wheel before school students and explain its significance, along with Mahatma Gandhis ideas of Swadeshi and self-reliance. Through this program, the message of the spinning wheel will reach more than 1,35,000 students, the Vidyapith said in a statement issued ahead of Rentiya Baras.

articleTitle: Bengaluru gym trainer likely died of strangulation after party: Police
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bengaluru gym trainer death
description: The police on Monday arrested three fellow gym trainers who were with the victim on Saturday night
body_raw: A preliminary investigation into the death of a gym trainer in North Bengaluru early on Sunday suggested that the 25-year-old man allegedly died of strangulation following a violent altercation with three other gym trainers in the bathroom of a flat, the police said on Wednesday. However, the police are awaiting the final post-mortem report to establish the precise cause of death of M Nandan, who worked at Masiv Gym in Sahakaranagar. The police on Monday arrested three fellow gym trainers - Vishwanath, 22, Sharath, 27, and Nishanth, 24, who were with Nandan at the flat on Saturday night - and booked them for murder. According to police sources, a group of four gym trainers, including Nandan, gathered at a flat in Kempapura following the gyms first anniversary celebrations on Saturday, where they reportedly consumed alcohol and drugs. Investigators suspect the men were heavily intoxicated when an altercation broke out inside the bathroom, escalating into a physical brawl. The police noted broken mirrors and fittings in the bathroom, along with injuries on the victim and the accused. Nandan sustained injuries to his face, while the other trainers also had injuries to their hands and knees, said an officer. Nandan was also found to have several bite marks on different parts of his body. The police are examining the injuries to determine how and when they were caused. Prima facie, authorities suspect Nandan died of strangulation, though final post-mortem and forensic reports are awaited. The police said Nandan was seriously injured after the fight but was not taken to hospital immediately. The men allegedly remained at the flat and attempted to pacify the situation. Nandan subsequently lost consciousness and was taken to hospital, where he was declared dead. Anush Shetty, owner of the flat where the gathering was held, was among those initially detained. The police have issued him a notice for inquiry and are examining his role in the incident. Gym trainers version A senior police officer said the accused gave investigators their account of what happened inside the bathroom. According to their version, Nandan vomited in the bathroom and suffered seizures, and that the injuries and bite marks occurred while attempting to prevent him from biting his tongue-a claim police are verifying against medical evidence. They have told us that Nandan was attempting to bite his tongue, and that they tried to prevent him from doing so by slapping and biting him, the officer said. Police rule out sexual act angle The police are also examining an allegation that Nandan and one of the men may have been involved in a sexual act during the gathering. However, investigators have not found evidence so far to establish that a sexual act took place, a senior police official said. The bite marks and other injuries are being examined as part of the investigation, but the police have not established that they were connected to any sexual activity. The police are also awaiting forensic reports, including the results of samples collected from the accused, to establish whether they had consumed narcotic substances and to corroborate their account of the incident. The arrested men are being questioned to establish the sequence of events inside the flat. The flat owner has told police that he was sleeping in another room and woke up later in the morning, when he found Nandan injured and unconscious. He then contacted a doctor and called an ambulance.

articleTitle: Rate hike: Behind the RBI’s pivot, a need to safeguard price stability
articleFeaturedImageAlt: rbi rate hike
description: The interaction between persistent supply shocks and strong demand warrants particular attention. Economic history suggests that when supply-driven price pressures coincide with robust growth, inflation often broadens beyond a narrow set of categories
body_raw: The shift in stance by the RBIs Monetary Policy Committee MPC, accompanied by a rate hike in its October review, was hardly unexpected. Monetary policy is shaped principally by domestic growth and inflation dynamics, with global developments playing a secondary role. Recent developments on both fronts increasingly pointed towards a recalibration of policy. This year was marked by an unusual combination of shocks and uncertainties. Yet, despite the conflict in West Asia and unresolved tariff-related turbulence, Indias economy has remained remarkably resilient. Growth has stayed robust, while inflation, particularly core inflation, has thus far been relatively contained. However, the balance of risks has begun to shift. Since the MPCs August review, upside risks to inflation have become more pronounced. Three factors stand out. First, the conflict in West Asia, marked by repeated cycles of escalation and de-escalation, has kept commodity markets volatile. Recent developments have pushed up crude prices again, with the Indian crude basket, as estimated by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell, returning to its April peak. Reflecting this, we now expect crude prices to average 88-93 per barrel this fiscal, compared with our earlier forecast of 82-87 per barrel. Even if geopolitical tensions ease, crude prices may remain elevated as damaged infrastructure is repaired and depleted inventories rebuilt. In such a scenario, another round of pass-through to domestic petrol and diesel prices appears likely. While higher pump prices could temper demand and ease pressure on oil marketing companies, they would also raise inflation through both direct and indirect channels. Food inflation represents a second major source of vulnerability. Food prices are the most volatile component of Indias inflation basket, and recent increases reflect both base effects and emerging supply concerns. To be sure, the relationship between monsoons and food inflation is not linear. Not every rainfall-deficient year has led to higher food inflation, and the governments free food programme for nearly 800 million people, alongside healthy rice buffer stocks, provides an important cushion. Nevertheless, the 2026 monsoon has ended with rainfall 13 per cent below the long-period average and over 42 per cent of districts in India classified as deficient. More importantly, the problem extends beyond the aggregate shortfall. The spatial distribution and timing of rainfall have been particularly unfavourable, making this one of the most disrupted monsoon seasons of the past decade. The implications extend beyond the current kharif season. Weak monsoons can impair rabi production by reducing soil moisture and reservoir levels. As of October 1, reservoir storage was 12.2 per cent below normal and 20.4 per cent lower than a year earlier. Crisils Deficient Rainfall Impact Parameter DRIP points to broad-based stress, with cotton, tur and bajra among the most vulnerable crops. Intensifying El Nino conditions, combined with supply disruptions linked to the West Asia conflict, are exerting upward pressure on food prices worldwide. Particularly notable is edible oil inflation, driven by weather-related disruptions in Southeast Asia and rising biofuel demand. According to the World Meteorological Organisation, the probability of a strong El Nino extending into early 2027 is close to certainty, raising the risk of extreme weather events and supply disruptions. Given that India imports over 55 per cent of its edible oil requirements, elevated global prices and currency weakness continue to keep domestic edible oil inflation elevated at around 20 per cent. The impact of the monsoon on agricultural output and food prices, then, will remain one of the most important variables for policymakers to monitor this year. Inflation risks, however, are no longer confined to supply-side shocks. Demand-side pressures also appear stronger than previously anticipated. GDP growth in the first quarter was not only above trend but also exceeded previous expectations, and the second quarter is also doing well. Reflecting this momentum, the RBI has raised its growth forecast for this fiscal to 7.1 per cent from 6.7 per cent earlier. Crisil likewise expects growth of 7.0 per cent. The interaction between persistent supply shocks and strong demand warrants particular attention. Economic history suggests that when supply-driven price pressures coincide with robust growth, inflation often broadens beyond a narrow set of categories. Early signs of such generalisation are becoming visible in core inflation, with price pressures gradually spreading beyond food and fuel. Global developments reinforce the need for caution. Bond yields in advanced economies have risen much more sharply than in India, reflecting persistent inflation and growing concerns over fiscal sustainability. Consequently, the spread between US and Indian 10-year government bond yields has narrowed to roughly 200 basis points, compared with over 400 basis points a few years ago, reducing the relative attractiveness of Indian government securities for foreign investors. At the same time, major central banks remain in tightening mode. The US Federal Reserve raised rates by 25 basis points in September, and markets continue to price in further tightening. The European Central Bank and the Bank of Japan have also maintained a tightening bias in response to persistent inflation pressures. Indias liquidity situation adds another layer of complexity. The RBIs efforts to mobilise foreign currency non-resident deposits have been highly successful, strengthening foreign exchange reserves and improving balance-of-payments resilience. However, these inflows have also injected substantial liquidity into the financial system. Consequently, financial conditions eased through August, and liquidity remains abundant. This creates a degree of tension, albeit transitory, between prevailing monetary conditions and the tightening bias increasingly warranted by growth and inflation dynamics. Taken together, these developments explain the RBIs policy shift. Inflation risks are becoming more broad-based, growth remains resilient, global monetary conditions continue to tighten, and domestic liquidity remains ample. Policymakers will need to remain highly vigilant on price developments. While future actions will remain data-dependent, the possibility of another rate hike this year can no longer be ruled out. The writer is chief economist, Crisil

articleTitle: Man weighing 144 kg loses over 60 kilos: What transformation may mean for his health
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Niraj Jha
description: The journey brought changes that went well beyond his physical transformation
body_raw: How does it feel to be over 60 kgs lighter? Sometimes the end is just life making room for a different beginning. At 144 kg, I knew something had to change. What followed was a journey that transformed far more than my body. I lost 60 kilos, but somewhere along the way, I also discovered a version of myself I did not know existed, expressed Niraj Jha in a post on Instagram. Looking back, what once felt like the end was actually where everything began. 144 kg to 79 kg. 60 kilos lighter. And still evolving, the man added. A mans transformation from 144 kg to 79 kg has drawn attention online, with his journey documenting a weight reduction of more than 60 kg and, in his words, a change that went far beyond his physical appearance. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. From a health perspective, consultant dietitian Garima Goyal said that a reduction of this magnitude represents a major change in body weight. At a higher starting weight, losing excess body fat can potentially improve several obesity-related health risks, including metabolic health, blood pressure, physical mobility and cardiovascular risk. However, the health impact of any transformation depends on factors such as the individuals medical history, body composition and how the weight was lost, Goyal told indianexpress.com. One of the most important considerations in a major weight-loss journey is preserving lean muscle while reducing fat mass. A very large reduction on the weighing scale should not be viewed simply as a race to reach a smaller number. Adequate protein, resistance training and sufficient nutrition can help support muscle preservation, while physical activity can improve strength and functional capacity, said Goyal. Long-term weight management also has an important psychological dimension. When someone has lived at a higher body weight for years, the changes may extend into everyday experiences walking becomes easier, movement becomes more comfortable, clothes fit differently and activities that once felt exhausting may become more manageable, said Goyal. At the same time, a transformation reel cannot show the complete journey. It doesnt reveal the persons exact diet, medical history, training programme, setbacks, or whether the weight loss was entirely intentional. That context matters, particularly when a large amount of weight has been lost, mentioned Goyal.   View this post on Instagram   A post shared by Niraj Jha fitwithnbj And reaching 79 kg does not necessarily mark the end of the process. Maintaining weight loss requires a sustainable approach to nutrition, physical activity, sleep, behaviour and ongoing health monitoring. The goal ultimately needs to be more than simply maintaining a number on the scale, said Goyal. Weight loss can be one chapter of a much larger change in health, confidence and daily life, added Goyal. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine.

articleTitle: ‘80% NDA, 20% PDA’: Yogi Adityanath back with claim ahead of Assembly polls
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Yogi Adityanath 80-20 UP Assembly polls
description: Since the Samajwadi Party has not fielded a third candidate, there will be no contest between it and the BJP in the Rajya Sabha polls.
body_raw: After the Samajwadi Party SP decided not to field a third Rajya Sabha poll candidate from Uttar Pradesh, paving the way for the unopposed election of its two and the ruling BJPs eight candidates to the Upper House, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said on Wednesday that the state would again see an 80-20 fight in upcoming Assembly polls. Adityanath said in Lucknow that the Rajya Sabha elections would predict the Assembly election results. Yeh ladaai 8020 ki fir aa gai hai. 80 per cent NDA me, aur 20 per cent PDA me. Aur PDA ka kya haal hone wala hai, yeh aapke saamne fir aane wala hai The fight has again become 80 and 20. Eighty per cent in NDA and 20 per cent in PDA. PDAs fate will be before everyone, he said at the Seva Jyoti Yatra-Viksit Bharat Sankalp Sabha, which marks Prime Minister Narendra Modis completion of 25 years in elected office. Since the SP has not fielded a third candidate, there will be no contest between it and the BJP in the Rajya Sabha polls. The SP has renominated veteran leader Ram Gopal Yadav, uncle of party president Akhilesh Yadav, and fielded Reliance executive Dhanraj Nathwani as its second Rajya Sabha candidate. The party has enough strength in the Assembly to get its two candidates elected to Rajya Sabha. The SP chief first floated the abbreviation PDA-Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak backward classes, Dalits, and minorities-in June 2023. The formulation was projected as the SPs social coalition against the BJP-led NDA, with Akhilesh repeatedly claiming, PDA hi NDA ko harayega it is the PDA that will defeat the NDA. Ahead of the 2022 Assembly elections, Adityanath had remarked that the Assembly election contest would be an 80 per cent vs 20 per cent fight, with the 20 per cent interpreted as a reference to the population of the minorities in the state. Adityanath later defended his 80 vs 20 remark. In an interview with ANI, he said, Its a reaction to an action. I spoke about 80 vs 20. Eighty per cent support the Bharatiya Janata Party BJP, while 20 per cent always oppose. We havent spoken about caste or religion.

articleTitle: Kenya reports first Ebola death after traveler from Congo via Uganda dies in Nairobi
articleFeaturedImageAlt: People put on masks at the entrance of The Nairobi Hospital where Kenya's first Ebola virus patient was treated and died, Tuesday, Oct. 6, 2026. (AP Photo/Andrew Kasuku)
description: Kenya Ebola Case: Kenyan authorities have placed border points on high alert and launched contact-tracing efforts to identify people who may have been exposed to the virus.
body_raw: Kenya Ebola Case Kenya has reported its first confirmed case of Ebola and the countrys first death from the disease, after a man who had been living in Congo for seven years travelled to Nairobi via Uganda, authorities said Tuesday. The man, who had fallen ill about a month ago, was treated at several hospitals before travelling by road to Kampala and later taking a flight to Nairobi. He arrived in the Kenyan capital on Saturday and was admitted to Nairobi Hospital, where he was isolated and tested positive for Ebola. He died late Monday. Kenyan authorities have placed border points on high alert and launched contact-tracing efforts to identify people who may have been exposed to the virus.

articleTitle: Is Trump’s ‘forever war’ a liability in the US midterm elections?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: us midterm elections
description: Contrary to Trump’s expectations, the prolonged war in Iran has gradually crept into domestic prices
body_raw: President Donald Trump seems anxious about the upcoming US midterm elections-voting is on November 3. So much so that he confused Brazil with India in a recent social media post when comparing the vote-counting process, an issue that has seen intense debate in the current American political zeitgeist. Since Trumps loss to Joe Biden in the 2020 election, which the former has called rigged, he has repeated the claim more than 100 times publicly and has taken the fight to the US Supreme Court. At the heart of the issue is the vote-by-mail provision that Trump has railed against. At least four developments have riled up Trump Early and mail voting are already underway in more than 40 states almost one-third of American voters vote by mail Trump is reeling under one of the lowest approval ratings on the back of rising energy prices and a new forever war in Iran there is a sense that the Democrats may just edge out the Republicans in both the House and the Senate, and finally, the Supreme Court has just begun a new term with the anticipation that it may take up new cases on election issues like gun control, immigration and religious issues. In March 2026, Trump issued an Executive Order that sought to limit how Americans could vote, particularly through mail, and vowed to do away with voting machines. Consequently, the Supreme Court struck down Trumps attempts to restrict mail ballots. More than 23 states came together to appeal against Trumps Executive Order, which now remains blocked by a nationwide injunction and will almost certainly not apply this November. Then, there is the question of nationwide popularity. Trumps average approval rating fell to 38 per cent in late September, the lowest in his second term. A little over 35 per cent of Americans believe the country is headed in the right direction. On the generic congressional ballot, Democrats average 52 per cent against 43 per cent for Republicans, the widest margin since Trump returned to office. If the numbers and the sentiment do translate into votes, Democrats may likely win. To Trumps advantage, however, the actual voting may vary state-wise, altering some of these expectations. For the Democrats, the historical record may be more favourable. Since the 1950s, the presidents party has lost an average of more than 25 House seats in midterm elections, with losses plummeting further when the presidential approval rating is below 50 per cent. In his first term, Trump himself lost 40 House seats in 2018 Barack Obama lost 63 in 2010 and Bill Clinton 54 in 1994. Perhaps the exceptions are 1998 and 2002, which are attributed to the popularity of a president or an era-defining post-911 rallying of sentiments. Trump, on the contrary, has been sucked into a war abroad and is struggling to keep price rises at home under control. The economy, along with the cost of living, lies at the heart of the political contestations. Contrary to Trumps expectations, the prolonged war in Iran has gradually crept into domestic prices. While rising petrol prices gas and electricity bills are affecting households, a spike in diesel prices is impacting the truckers supply chain and farming, adding pressure on Republicans. Republicans hold a narrow House majority, and Democrats need a net gain of only three seats to win it-making the House win a stronger possibility than the Senate. What has complicated the picture is a gerrymandering war between the two parties. The process, which can happen once every decade, could give the Republicans an edge with new maps in Texas, Florida, Ohio, North Carolina, Missouri, among others, which could yield Republicans around 16 seats on paper, against roughly six for Democrats, mostly from California. What may prove decisive in the end is how many Republican-held seats turn Democrat, if any. In the Senate, the current Republican lead may prove to be a steeper climb for the Democrats. Republicans hold 53 seats, so Democrats need a net gain of four for an outright majority, along with the two independents who caucus with the latter. Although international issues tend to weigh less in midterms, given the prolonged nature and continued US commitments to the Middle East, this November could be different. On October 1, Trump ordered a third carrier strike group, led by the USS Theodore Roosevelt, and another 10,000 troops to the region. The carrier is not expected to arrive until late November, after the polls have closed, but the political signalling has been dire. The deployment follows the virtual collapse of efforts to secure a workable ceasefire or any modus vivendi with Tehran. The war has also spread beyond Iran with the Houthis renewing missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, drawing Riyadhs ongoing response. China adds a layer of contradiction in US politics. As Trump has sought constructive strategic stability with China, extending their trade truce to January 2027, many see the stability as structurally incongruent. For the soyabean farm-state Republicans in Iowa and Nebraska, the truce with China is a lifeline, but for China hawks, it looks like accommodation. For Americas partners, including India, the more consequential question is not who wins in November but what follows. The writer is Deputy Director of the Strategic Studies Programme at ORF

articleTitle: Gurgaon woman spends 50% of salary on rent to live close to work: ‘Saving my peace’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gurgaon woman rent
description: Shakti Dharni Pandey said she could have chosen a cheaper home farther from her school but decided the time spent commuting was not worth the savings.
body_raw: A Gurgaon woman has explained why she is willing to spend more than half her salary on rent to live just a four-minute walk from her workplace, saying the arrangement gives her something she values more than the money she could save-time, energy, and peace of mind. Shakti Dharni Pandey, who works at a school in Gurgaon, shared her experience in an Instagram video and said she has no intention of moving to a cheaper area, despite knowing many would consider her rent a poor financial choice. More than 50 of my salary goes into my rent, and I am not going to change it. I live in a spacious 1RK that is just a 4-minute walking distance from this school, she said. Living so close to work has allowed Pandey to return home during breaks. And though Im able to come home during class breaks, have a piping hot lunch, and complete my pending work, it costs me way too much. More than half of my school salary goes into rent every single month, which anyone would call a completely bad decision financially, she said. Why she chose a costly home over cheaper rent Pandey said she could have chosen a cheaper home farther from her school but decided the time spent commuting was not worth the savings. I choose this instead of saving money because, from here, I am saving my peace, my energy, and my time, she explained. For Pandey, the benefits go beyond avoiding a daily commute. I dont have to rush in the morning to get ready. I dont have to be in an auto or Metro for long hours to reach home. I also dont have to spend any money on commuting, though it doesnt compensate for the rent, she said. Watch the video   View this post on Instagram   A post shared by Shakti Dharni Pandey shaktidharni   Rather than putting the money in some SIP Pandey described the decision as a way of spending her 20s on herself rather than simply maximising her savings. But the thing is, rather than saving money and putting it in some SIP, I am making my adulting easier, she added. The extra time, she said, gives her room to learn new skills, make videos, and focus on her mental well-being. Pandey also pointed out that her additional income from side projects has helped make the higher rent more manageable. Its not the rent I am paying more than 50 of my salary for it is saving my time, feeling safe and calm, and preserving energy to work on things I want to work on. Thats what I am paying this rent for. And I am not going to change it, she concluded. Pandey shared the video with the caption, Will you do something like this? Pandeys take on rent and convenience prompted a mixed response online. While some Instagram users said they understood her decision, others felt that spending more than half of a salary on housing could create financial difficulties. Just do what makes you happy. Everyone have a different life arc. You go girl, one user wrote. Another said, I can completely relate to it and agree with the perspective that you shared because I Travel almost 2 hours to reach my clg to study. If you are saving money on the commute, food and having enough time. Its worth it, a third user commented. What about those relying on a single income? However, one user pointed out that Pandeys circumstances may make the decision easier to manage than it would be for someone relying on a single income. I think its also important to consider the overall context. Since you have other sources of income, putting 50 of your school salary towards rent may be more manageable for you. For someone who is just starting out with one income source, it might be helpful to first build an emergency fund and some financial stability before allocating such a large portion towards comfort. Just a reminder that everyones financial situation is different, so what works for one person may not work for another, the user wrote.

articleTitle: Rules for body-worn cameras by cops: Court asks Centre to decide in 6 months
articleFeaturedImageAlt: delhi police
description: The Delhi High Court refused to pass any directions on a PIL seeking an SOP on such cameras used by police personnel
body_raw: The Delhi High Court Wednesday refused to issue directions on a public interest litigation PIL seeking a standard operating procedure SOP for use of body-worn cameras by police personnel. It, instead, directed the government to consider the plea as a representation and take a decision on it within six months. A bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Arun Bhardwaj was hearing the PIL by advocate Chahat Raghav. The lawyer sought an SOP on use of body-worn cameras by the Delhi Police, its operation, and the memory and storage of data collected through such cameras. Senior advocate Akhil Sibal, representing the petitioner, argued, There has to be an SOP, until there is some sort of law. it is different from facial recognition technology which has concerns about surveillance, profiling, privacy. if we have a mechanism or defined way of using it, then it will go a long way in addressing some of these concerns. Time and again, we are left with allegations and counter allegations. The question is ultimately of accountability. body-worn cameras are used, but it is all sporadic, no SOP, no chain of custody, preservation or access. Purpose is to rather than having this chaos. there has to be some way for accountability.There has to be some procedure that needs to be laid down, it will benefit the whole process, Sibal added. He also referred to media reports stating that amid allegations of police excesses during the SIR protests, Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force RAF deployed at the protest site have been issued directions to wear body cameras. Meanwhile, Additional Solicitor General ASG Chetan Sharma, representing the Centre, suggested to the court that the PIL can be treated as a representation. Sibal resisted the proposition, urging that it is not the governments case that they are unaware of the use of body-worn cameras. He urged, Let them place some reply before the court. representation will serve no purpose, its not something that they are not aware of. The court recorded in its order, The use of body-worn cameras by police can be inferred from not only tender issued but also use of the same by the traffic police. The SOP is informed to not be in existence. In such an event, there might not be any provision in the police manual. However, since the statement is made from ASG, we deem it appropriate to take the same on record. We direct the respondents to communicate the decision on framing of SOP regarding use of body-worn cameras within six months.

articleTitle: ‘We rushed things’: Nani on why The Paradise, his Rs 150-cr film, got polarised reviews
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nani admits his team could've done a better job of The Paradise.
description: Nani heaped praises on The Paradise director Srikanth Odela, while admitting that he got "carried away" by the scale and expectations riding on the film.
body_raw: Srikanth Odelas period action film The Paradise scored the biggest opening of Nanis 18-year career, and also emerged as his first film to earn over Rs 100 crore at the domestic box office. However, the actor recently responded to the polarizing reviews and reactions to the film, admitting that if his team had more time during post-production, they couldve turned in a better product. Nani on The Paradises polarizing response Were in a place where were just thinking backwards, given the reactions. Were also aware of the timing. With the less post-production time, we rushed things a little bit. It was always there on the back of our mind whether well be able to achieve everything in time, confessed Nani to The Hollywood Reporter India. However, he didnt want to buy more time by pushing the film, since he had already done that twice. The Paradise was initially scheduled to release on March 26 earlier this year. It was then pushed to August 21, before finally seeing light of the day on September 25. In the process, it averted major clashes with Ranveer Singh-starrer blockbuster spy thriller Dhurandhar 2 The Revenge and Yashs action thriller Toxic A Fairytale for Grownups respectively. This was the third release date. The audience was so excited about the film that we didnt want to give up on them because of the postponement that happened so many times. So, we had an extremely tight deadline. More things would have made sense narratively with the edit and the score, if we had more time. We couldve smoothened it out, explained the actor. He acknowledged the little glitches that the audience are complaining about, like the fact that parts of The Paradise feel a little jumpy. We couldve made all of that better, but well never know I guess. We dont know if it wouldve worked better had we pushed the film, said Nani, adding,We all get carried away and do mistakes. But if we understand and learn from them, thats the best way we can go ahead. Nani lauds Srikanth Odela The Paradise also carried tall expectations given it marked the reunion of Nani and director Srikanth Odela after their 2023 action film Dasara, which amassed Rs 121 crore at the worldwide box office, on a budget of Rs 65 crore. On the other hand, the budget of The Paradise is somewhere between Rs 150 crore and Rs 200 crore, but its garnered only Rs 169.15 crore globally yet, within 13 days of its box office run. With The Paradise, Srikanth had great ideas. But when the span of the film went up, when the expectations went up, the focus shifted from storytelling to set pieces. So, the connectivity wasnt there. If he just sticks to his heart, and focuses on just telling the story, I still believe hes one of the best talents we have, said Nani. Further heaping praises on the director, Nani added, In these many years, if I have to really bet on someone, hed be on the top of the list. Hes a very, very original guy. He has a lot of ideas, but after stitching them together, his bigger vision somewhere got a little diluted. He admitted that since the expectations were sky high from him and Srikanth, the polarizing reactions hurt even more. The Paradise also stars Raghav Juyal as the chief antagonist, along with Sonali Kulkarni, Mohan Babu, and Easwari Rao among others. Set in a Secunderabad slum of the 1980s, it stars Nani plays a tribal leader called Sarakka. It opened at Rs 11.60 crore from 900 screens at the domestic box office, but has slipped down to even below Rs 1 crore - at Rs 93 lakh - by its second Tuesday day 13. Also Read - Sanjay Dutt says his cant feel peace in India remark a scripted conversation, Shekhar Suman comments The Paradise has earned Rs 138.10 crore gross and Rs 117.13 crore net at the domestic box office. Its major chunk comes from the native Telugu version, followed by the dubbed Hindi version, though Nani refused to label it as a pan-India release. Having collected Rs 31.05 crore internationally, its earned Rs 169.15 crore globally so far. Keeping all the reactions and numbers aside, we know we couldve done better, Nani reiterated.

articleTitle: Punjab Kings teammate decodes change in Iyer’s hitting technique: ‘When Shreyas came at the start…’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Iyer
description: Recalling his own bowling experience against Iyer, the bowler said: "When I bowled to him in the nets, I had to bowl wider, or else he used to easily hit me over cover for a six
body_raw: One standout aspect of Shreyas Iyers century on Tuesday was his ability to accelerate after reaching his half-century, which he reached in 26 deliveries, and scoring the next 50 runs in just 16 deliveries. His power-hitting and technique seemed quite flawless against the spinners. His Punjab Kings teammate, Yuzvendra Chahal, decoded what has changed in Iyers approach to his innings. Definitely, attacking the mind. When Shreyas came at the start, he used to go back and play the cut. Now he comes across, and if the midwicket fielder is up, he has that option as well. If you bowl outside the off-stump, his reach is so good that he plays over cover and mid-off. So, the bowler gets slightly stuck there as to what he should do when he is not getting any help from the wicket, the Punjab Kings PBKS bowler said on Star Sports. Recalling his own bowling experience against Iyer, Chahal said When I bowled to him in the nets, I had to bowl wider, or else he used to easily hit me over cover for a six. One or one-and-a-half years ago, he used to hit hard, but nowadays he times the ball, and thats the specialty because of which his batting has improved so much, he added. Batters go back and across toward the off-stump, but he was going outside the off-stump because he knew Shepherd would try to bowl only outside the off-stump. Thats why he played the lofted extra cover drive and lofted off-drive. He read the bowlers mind, and thats why he was able to get into those positions. Brilliant batting, sensational batting, former batting legend Sunil Gavaskar elaborated on the same show. Iyers century helped India beat West Indies by eight wickets, chasing a target of 172 runs in 14.4 overs. If its your day, make sure that you win the match for the team. And today it was me. Previous couple of games, it was the batsmen who finished off the game. So yeah, overall I feel it was a comprehensive performance, and I think if we continue with the same mindset, we will be one of the destructive teams in T20s, Iyer said.

articleTitle: Ajay Devgn doesn’t rule out Drishyam 4, says Mohanlal film ‘most suited for their audience’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ajay Devgn says Mohanlal's Drishyam 3 is "most suited" for the Malayalam audience.
description: Ajay Devgn reveals the Hindi and Malayalam teams of Drishyam 3 discussed their scripts with each other, before going in completely different directions.
body_raw: Abhishek Pathaks Bollywood crime thriller Drishyam 3 took a different route from Jeetu Josephs Malayalam counterpart, which released earlier this year, marking a departure from the previous two instalments of the franchise. That risk seems to have paid off, with the Ajay Devgn-starrer now crossing Rs 340 crore at the worldwide box office. But the actor maintains that it was a natural chain of events, instead of a cinematic rebellion, to tread a different path than the Mohanlal-starrer, which didnt get the rave reviews the franchise is otherwise known for. Ajay Devgn says Hindi and Malayalam teams discussed their stories After Abhishek and his father Kumar Mangat Pathaks production house Panaroma Studios acquired the Drishyam franchise from the Malayalam makers, the Hindi and Malayalam teams began working in tandem. Honestly speaking, they had not decided to make a third one. We were toying with the idea, and I think all the writers worked out some ideas and they didnt work. And finally, things fell into place, Devgn revealed in a recent interview. We spoke to them, and we were like, Lets make it, we have a script. And then they said that theyre also working on something, and they had a script. So we thought, lets hear each ot her out and decide what to do, Devgn told Gulf News. After that, Drishyam 3 Hindi co-writers Abhishek, Aamii Keeyan Khan, and Parveez Shaikh, and Drishyam 3 Malayalam writer Joseph exchanged scripts. Finally we came to the conclusion that this is a fabulous script, but it is most suited for their audience. And we were very confident about our script. So, then we decided that we will go ahead, recalled Devgn. When you work hard and then you get something which is to the point, then youre confident enough to make it the way you want to make it, he added. Ajay Devgn hints at Drishyam 4 After the underwhelming response to the Malayalam version of Drishyam 3, Joseph seems to be developing the fourth instalment. Though Drishyam 3 was billed as The Conclusion of the epic trilogy, Devgn hinted that like his deceptive character Vijay Salgaonkar, the makers may have a trick up their sleeve as well, hinting at the remote possibility of Drishyam 4. At the moment, it is a conclusion, he said, before adding, I cant predict it. However, when pressed about the possibility of another instalment in the blockbuster franchise, Devgn didnt deny it outrightly. The decision was, this is the conclusion. The decision right now is that this is the conclusion. Right now, he added. Spoilers ahead In the Malayalam version of Drishyam 3, when Siddiques character, troubled by his wifes depression treatment in the US, vows to finally get back at Georgekutty Mohanlal and his family, the protagonist ends up having the last laugh yet again, even though that comes at the grave cost of physically hurting his elder daughter. Also Read - Drishyam 3 Box Office Collection Day 5 Updates Ajay Devgns film makes it to top 5 highest-grossing Bollywood films of 2026, earns Rs 341 crore worldwide However, the Hindi version of Drishyam 3 avoids taking that road, and instead uses Salgaonkars influence in the Goan Catholic community and his love for making movies as his weapons of choice. Also starring Tabu, Rajat Kapoor, Shriya Saran, Ishita Dutta, Jaideep Ahlawat, Prakash Raj, and Kamlesh Sawant among others, Drishyam 3 has earned Rs 217 crore at the domestic box office within just five days.

articleTitle: ‘I won’t stop’: In PM’s Viksit Bharat pledge, a message for Opposition
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Narendra Modi
description: The Prime Minister has often spoken about his vision for India becoming a developed country by 2047, when it celebrates 100 years of Independence. But these remarks are significant against the backdrop of political developments
body_raw: Contrasting the gloom and immense challenges under the UPA era with the energy, enthusiasm, self-confidence of India in the current global order, Prime Minister Narendra Modi Wednesday coined the mantra of we will do it, saying the country will not stop, nor tire, nor waver on the road to a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Speaking at the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Sabha-Seva Jyoti Yatra, organised at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi to mark 25 years of his continuous leadership as head of government, first as Chief Minister of Gujarat and then as Prime Minister, Modi said, Even today, I consider myself a student. I try to learn something new each day. That is why today, I prayed. that my power to learn does not wane. The more I learn, the more my capacity to do something for the nation will increase. I am beholden to every person and every incident which taught me something or the other. What brought me victory taught me to be humble, and what made me stumble made me learn how to stand up. Well-wishers encouraged me and critics taught me to look within. Those who supported me showed me the strength of belief. Whoever opposed me taught me the power of democracy. Every crisis was a test of my patience, every success expanded my sense of responsibility. Everything I accomplished gave me the strength, the drive to move towards larger goals, he said. Stating that he began his day with a visit to the Shri Vinayak temple where he prayed for the nation and its 140 crore citizens, he said, I express my gratitude to all of you and to all my fellow countrymen. When I took the oath as Chief Minister of Gujarat on October 7, 2001, I never imagined that this milestone would also come. Today, I have completed 25 years of continuously serving as head of government. This is the result of the continuous blessings of the janata janardan. I express my gratitude to all political colleagues of the BJP, NDA and all those who hold immense reverence for democracy. I bow my head at the feet of the people of the nation, he said. He said the Morbi floods inculcated in him a spirit of service and showed him the path to round-the-clock relief and service work, the Bhuj earthquake taught him to remain steadfast on reconstruction, and the Chandrayaan taught him to rise after failure. Similarly, the Covid pandemic, he said, underlined the importance of the nations collective consciousness, and the media gave him the inspiration to move forward through both bitter and sweet experiences. Praising the RSS swayamsevaks, whom he called the guardians of the countrys cultural soul, he said he never felt alone on his journey of selfless service. Modi said the occasion was not one of merely recalling memories but also of adding new energy to predetermined goals and commitment. Hum kar ke rahenge we will do it. Viskit Bharat by 2047, we will do it. Top three economies, we will do it. Aatmanirbhar Bharat, we will do it. Global manufacturing hub, we will do it. Organising the Olympics, we will do it. Steps in outer space, we will do it. This energy, this enthusiasm, this self-confidence is incredible, he said. That we have been born in this timeless land of Bharat is amrit itself, he said, saying while high office can be obtained anywhere, there is no sacred land such as Bharat. Taking a swipe at the UPA years, he said, In 2014, the nation expanded my responsibility as Pradhan Sevak. The nation was confronting immense challenges, only problems were visible. Each citizen was seeking a new path. Regarding Bharats economy, the world had begun saying its a gone case, growth was nowhere to be seen. Adding that a nation facing such severe disappointment needed a new confidence, he said he responded by doing the only thing he knows I urged the janshakti, repeated to them we will do it. And today, 12 years later, the picture has changed entirely. Earlier, when a crisis used to emerge, Indias economy jolted. When a crisis comes now, Bharats perseverance is discussed. Its resilience is discussed, he said. Back then, policy paralysis used to be discussed. Now the Reform Express is discussed. Back then, new avenues of imports used to be discussed. Today, records of exports are established. Back then, we used to import mobile phones even for our own use. Now, there is a jalwa of Made-in-India mobile phones, he said. Referring to flydubais Indian pilot Smit Machchhar, hailed as a hero for averting a catastrophe despite being attacked and wounded in the cockpit, he said, There will come a time when Made-in-India planes will be discussed. There are problems in our country, but we also have 140 crore solutions. This time is not to rest, but to move forward with enthusiasm. Today, the youth of Bharat have a huge opportunity. I want to tell the youth Your children will not go through the trials that your grandparents and parents were put through. That is what I am working for, he said. Asking the gathering to take a pledge, Modi said, Nation First will be my commitment. Serving the nation will be my goal. And the mantra of nagrik devo bhava will be my mantra, karma will be dharma, delivering on my responsibilities will be my commitment. Until Bharat become viksit, I will not stop, nor tire, nor waver.

articleTitle: Rate hike was expected. But RBI reinforces hints that more are coming
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Members of the Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra (centre); and (from left) Deputy Governors Shirish Chandra Murmu, Swaminathan Janakiraman, Poonam Gupta, and Rohit Jain in Mumbai on October 7. (PTI)
description: The RBI has tightened its stance from "neutral" to "calibrated tightening". But neither inflation figures nor the central bank’s own forecasts have changed dramatically since August. So what explains the shift?
body_raw: It was almost a foregone conclusion that the Reserve Bank of India RBI would increase the policy repo rate by 25 basis points bps to 5.5 on Wednesday. What was not as widely expected was that the RBIs Monetary Policy Committee MPC would also make the policy stance more restrictive - from neutral to calibrated tightening. This shift is important. As Governor Sanjay Malhota pointed out, the change in the stance means interest rate cuts are off the table in the near term and policy action ahead can only be a rate hike or a pause, depending on the evolving conditions and the outlook. According to Madhavi Arora, Chief Economist at Emkay Global Financial Services, the change in the stance feels more like a forward guidance and the RBI has clearly prepared markets for a higher-for-longer interest rate environment. While some economists did and continue to predict only a shallow rate hike cycle of 50 bps one basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point or so, financial markets had - even before the MPC decision to increase the repo rate for the first time in more than three-and-a-half years on Wednesday - already priced in a long-ish hiking cycle of at least 100 bps. This was despite the MPCs unexpectedly dovish statement and language on August 5, when the central bank said there were little signs of generalisation of price pressures so far. Generalisation of inflation means higher prices spreading to other parts of the CPI basket. We have already seen a stark example of this generalisation with commercial cooking gas getting expensive after the start of the West Asia war, restaurants and cafes sharply increased their menu prices. Consider the following the number of items in the CPI basket whose inflation was more than 4 was 65 in January and rose to 110 in August. Moreover, prices of 314 of the 358 items were higher in August compared to July. In February, this number was 236. Data for September, which will be released next week, may show more of the same. Little change in data When the MPC last met, it had with it the Consumer Price Index CPI inflation data for June, which had risen to 4.38 from 3.93 in May. Meanwhile, Wholesale Price Index WPI inflation had edged up similarly to 9.87 from 9.68. Since then, inflation developments on both fronts have not been outsized while retail inflation has risen to 4.82 in August, wholesale prices rose by 9.92. The RBI is mandated to target a CPI inflation rate of 4 in the medium-term in a band of 2-6. Of course, the MPC must be forward-looking and cant decide interest rates based on data for two months ago - it needs to take a view on what it thinks inflation might be a year or so down the line because interest rate changes impact growth and inflation in the economy with a delay of 9-12 months. However, the RBIs own projections have not moved dramatically, as the chart below shows. Governor Malhotra said in his statement on Wednesday that recalibrating the policy rate is imperative because headline inflation is seen averaging almost 5.8 over the next three quarters and core inflation is projected at 4.4 in 2026-27. The Governors statement emphasising that average Inflation of 5.8 over the next three quarters with core inflation projected at 4.4 needs policy recalibration reinforces the hawkishness, said Puneet Pal, PGIM India Mutual Funds Head of Fixed Income. Pal expects incrementally 75-100 bps of rate hikes over the next nine months. But even back in August, these forecasts were not markedly different CPI inflation or retail inflation was expected to average almost 5.6 in the three quarters starting October, while the RBI had predicted an average core inflation rate of 4.3 this fiscal. But it is only now that the MPC sees some evidence of elevated inflation expectations and generalisation of inflation after saying in August that there were little signs of the same. Economists were not convinced by the assessment made in August. On the monsoon front, the rain deficit this season has been 13, not very far off from 11 or so at the time of the August policy. And the West Asia conflict has never really shown crystal-clear signs of resolution, with matters remaining uncertain. New developments What has materially changed is the growth outlook, with the GDP seen expanding 7.1 this fiscal versus 6.7 in August following the unexpectedly high 7.8 growth in April-June. However, the MPC has noted on Wednesday that there is limited evidence of demand side pressures, although risks in view of strong growth in monetary and credit aggregates exist. Apart from faster-than-anticipated domestic growth, what has also changed since August 5 is that central banks around the world have increased their policy rates, including the US Federal Reserve, which last month raised the federal funds rate target range by 25 bps to 3.75-4 - its first rate-hike in three years. Like the MPC now, all 12 voting members of the Fed favoured this rate hike. Another one is expected in what remains of 2026. Other central banks to have raised interest rates last month include the Bank of Japan, the European Central Bank, and the Reserve Bank of Australia, among others. But the RBI focuses on domestic inflation and growth developments. And signs have been apparent for a while now that price pressures are spreading due to weak rains, the El Nino, and higher memory chip prices, among others. The reasons behind the MPCs turn between August and now may explain what lies ahead.

articleTitle: Indian student Pratyush Prabhakar elected VP of Academic Affairs at Harvard Kennedy School
articleFeaturedImageAlt: pratyush prabhakar harvard kennedy school
description: Before joining Harvard, Prabhakar also worked with India's Ministry of Education, apart from the Ministry of Railways. His work with the ministries covered government and public-sector issues.
body_raw: A public policy professional, Pratyush Prabhakar, who previously worked as a policy and communications adviser to the Minister of Railways, with the Union Government has been elected Vice-President, Academic Affairs of the student government at the Harvard Kennedy School HKS. Students from more than 96 countries, studying across multiple programmes at the school, took part in the election. As Vice-President, Academic Affairs, Prabhakar will co-chair the HKS Academic Affairs Committee with the Dean. The role involves representing students on academic matters, including curriculum, advising and other issues related to their academic experience at the school. The committee provides a forum for student concerns to be raised with the schools leadership. Prabhakar is pursuing a Masters in Public Administration at HKS as an Edward S Mason Fellow. The Mason Fellowship is aimed at public-sector professionals and leaders from developing countries. His current programme focuses on public administration and policy, and follows his earlier work in the Indian government. Also Read Harvard Executive Education programmes to launch in Hyderabad from December Before joining Harvard, Prabhakar also worked with Indias Ministry of Education, in addition to the Ministry of Railways. His work with the ministries covered government and public-sector issues. He has also founded two organisations, Communeeti and thriWe, alongside his government work. During the campaign, Prabhakar cited Mahatma Gandhi as an inspiration. The results were announced on October 2, which is observed as Gandhi Jayanti in India, and Prabhakar referred to the date in a message following the announcement. Also Read Chinese universities surge in global rankings as US schools slip The election brings Prabhakar into a student representative role that will involve working with the schools academic leadership. The Academic Affairs Committee deals with issues concerning students academic experience, giving student representatives a role in raising concerns and contributing to discussions on curriculum and advising. For Prabhakar, the position combines his studies at HKS with the public-sector experience he brought to the school. It also gives him a platform to bring the perspectives of a diverse student body, drawn from more than 96 countries, into those conversations. Harvard Kennedy School is Harvard Universitys graduate school focused on public policy and government. It offers graduate programmes in areas including public policy, public administration, international development and political governance. The school is named after former US president and Harvard alumnus himself, John F Kennedy.

articleTitle: Nothing left in democracy if institutions are undermined: Former judge Sanjib Banerjee
articleFeaturedImageAlt: sanjib banerjee supreme court election commission of india form 6 gyanesh kumar democracy SIR
description: Former Chief Justice of Meghalaya and Madras high courts, Sanjib Banerjee says the Supreme Court does not go by public perception or any wave, but by what is constitutionally correct and it will apply the same in the case of Form 6.
body_raw: At the heart of the controversy over the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls is a simple question-who must prove that a person has the right to vote in a democracy like India? In an exclusive discussion with The Indian Express, former Meghalaya High Court Chief Justice Sanjib Banerjee says the Election Commission has fundamentally got it wrong by placing the burden on voters. Underlining that this requires a course correction, he says the poll panel must instead follow Articles 325 and 326 of the Constitution, where every citizen who has attained the age of 18 is entitled to vote unless disqualified. While hearing petitions against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and examining the functioning of the poll panel, the Supreme Court recently clarified that it had not approved changes to Form 6, which new voters are required to fill. Banerjee, who has also served as the Chief Justice of the Madras High Court, argues that the dispute over Form 6 is part of a wider concern about constitutional safeguards and public trust in electoral institutions. He adds that while the apex court had affirmed the SIR process, it had not examined or approved the specific forms or other modalities of the exercise. Edited excerpts What is the significance of the Supreme Courts statement? Sanjib Banerjee My information is based on news reports, both in the print and digital media, and I havent actually seen the order of the Supreme Court. But from what Im given to understand, the Supreme Court wanted clarity on whether the critical decisions were taken by the Election Commission unanimously or whether they were taken only by the Chief Election Commissioner. The Supreme Court, apparently, also indicated that the majority rule had to prevail as far as the Election Commission was concerned, and said that it would not stop overturning decisions that may not have been taken by the majority. Finally, the Supreme Court said that it had not expressly approved or upheld the changes made to Form 6. A press release had been issued by the Election Commission prior to the hearing, probably a few days ago, to the effect that the Supreme Court had upheld the changes made to Form 6. Probably what was misleading about the press release was that the Supreme Court affirmed the process of SIR, but did not go into the nitty-gritty of the forms or the other things, and that was sought to be kind of presented as the Supreme Court having upheld or approved the entire modality of the exercise. From what I have been given to understand from press reports, particularly the report published in The Indian Express, is that the two other election commissioners pointed out to the Chief Election Commissioner that it was within the governments domain to prepare the form, and the Election Commission could not suo motu alter its contents. And that primarily appears to be the bone of contention. The modified Form 6 is a cause for real heartburn and is at the heart of what we are calling disenfranchisement of a large number of the citizens of this country, because if youre a citizen, youre entitled to vote. The most important thing which has happened, and which requires course correction, is the Election Commissioner or the Election Commission, quite wrongly and illegally putting the burden on the citizen to prove that he has a right to vote, rather than following Articles 325 and 326 of the Constitution, where every citizen whos attained the age of 18 is entitled to vote unless disqualified by the Constitution or by any law brought by the appropriate legislature. The Supreme Court stressed on Article 324 and Section 21 3 of the Representation of the People Act to uphold the SIR exercise. Can that be invoked for any changes in Form 6, or can only the government do it? Sanjib Banerjee Every judgment has a ratio decidendi reasoning, which is the exact issue or the point of law which is decided in that case. And the long and short of the Supreme Court judgment on the SIR was that the Election Commission had due authority to conduct such an SIR so that the integrity of the voting system could be maintained. Nowhere in that judgment is the procedure actually adopted, the questions which have been put up, the various forms nowhere in that judgment is there any discussion regarding this or any approval of the forms or the modalities. It was only on the process, and that process the Election Commission has due authority to do. Theres no doubt that the Election Commission has the authority to do it. But if it is in the governments domain to indicate what the contents of any form would be, then, as the two other election commissioners have reportedly pointed out to the Chief Election Commissioner, the Chief Election Commissioner should probably have waited for the government to make that change and not gone by a unilateral kind of exercise of his position to bring about that change in the form. This is particularly harsh. What happens now? Sanjib Banerjee There are many other aspects which have to be taken into consideration. You cant expect a verdict coming out on day one when the petition is lodged or taken up for the first time. We are not talking about any other office. Its an institution which is a watchdog, and we are talking of the head of that institution. Before the Supreme Court takes any step, it has to be absolutely sure it has to go through the records, and that is exactly what the Supreme Court is doing. Now, we cannot analyse every days hearing and say that this is what ought to be done, this is what should have been done. The court functions on the basis of records and after giving reasonable opportunity to all concerned to be heard. That process takes time. Its not a quick-fix solution. Its not AI coming in, and you press a button, and you get the answer. This will take time, and the Supreme Court has taken up the matter. Im sure that all aspects will now be looked into. There are certain other features, such as the split verdict, which has been referred to, or has been required to be referred to a Constitution bench. There are certain disturbing features pertaining to that, but I am confident that at the end of the day, the Supreme Court will deliver as it has in the past and uphold what is right. The Supreme Court does not go by public view or public perception or by any wave. It goes by what is constitutionally and legally correct, and that is the approach that should always be there. If those other little things, niggles were not there, it would have been better. But when question marks are raised regarding people in high places, you cannot always be sure because sometimes its motivated, and at other times they may even be genuine. We dont have those levels of kind of morality or high conduct that ought to be expected of people in such places. The less controversy about that office, which is the watchdog, its the basic thing for a democracy the right of the people to choose their own government. On Bengal elections. Sanjib Banerjee If theres anything like what is being said about the West Bengal election, that the number of people who were left out may have changed the course of elections. I know in my home constituency of Bhabanipur, where the margin was only 15,000, there were about 40,000 or 44,000 voters left out. Some may genuinely have been non-existent voters, or dead persons, or other people, but the number of people was so large that it could have made a difference if all had participated. More disturbingly, in that constituency, more than 40 per cent of the voters excluded belong to the Muslim community, though the overall percentage of the Muslim community in that constituency is 24 per cent. These do raise some pertinent questions. They raise some other things that are not good optics. For instance, some Electronic Voting Machines EVMs were burnt when a government building in Kolkata caught fire in June, and there was a fire on the fourth and fifth floors. The other floors escaped. There was a fire on the ninth and tenth floors, and between 2,500 and 4,000 EVM machines were burnt. That evidence is lost. The chief electoral officer was catapulted to the states chief secretary, and one of the election observers became a special advisor to the chief minister. These are not good for democracy. People should eschew such steps that erode confidence in the system. We are all a sum of the systems and the institutions that are there to govern us. They are there to care for us. They are there to uphold the laws and the Constitution, and these do not augur well for the future. Im not imputing any motives to anybody if these were not there, it would have been much better. We have taken great pride despite being a new republic. Despite all the problems that we have had-the poverty that we inherited at Independence-we were not a banana republic. We have never had a coup we have never had this kind of rigging on a mass scale. Accidental omissions are there, but the system is being kind of taken over this feeling of the possibility. Im not saying it happened. It may not have happened. God willing, it never happens. But if some people get this feeling, that by itself is not good for a democracy. Most importantly, when we talk of our institutions, we must be respectful. We must use temperate language and not let emotions or anger or anything get the better of us. At the end of the day, if these institutions are undermined, there is nothing left in democracy.

articleTitle: Two heads, one body: Rare turtle hatchling found on Cape Cod
articleFeaturedImageAlt: turtle
description: A rare two-headed diamondback terrapin hatchling has been discovered on Cape Cod, Massachusetts. Here’s what bicephaly means and why it occurs.
body_raw: A tiny turtle hatchling with two heads has been discovered on Cape Cod, Massachusetts, in a rare case that has caught the attention of wildlife experts. Researchers monitoring diamondback terrapins, a turtle species native to the salt marshes and coastal areas of the eastern United States, found the unusual terrapin. What made this hatchling different was immediately visible it had two distinct heads attached to a single body. The condition is known as bicephaly, a form of conjoined development in which an embryo develops two heads. It happens when an embryo doesnt fully separate during early development. While two-headed animals are exceptionally rare, this is not the first such turtle to turn up on Cape Cod. According to Live Science, the newly discovered hatchling is the third bicephalic terrapin found on Cape Cod in the past five years.  The discovery is particularly unusual because researchers already closely monitor diamondback terrapins in the region. Finding multiple hatchlings with the same rare developmental abnormality has therefore raised questions about what might be happening during their development. A two-headed turtle does not necessarily have two completely separate bodies. Instead, the hatchling generally shares organs and other body structures, even though the two heads may function independently. That can make movement, feeding and other basic behaviours more difficult. The survival of such animals can also be uncertain. Depending on how extensively they share internal organs and other structures, some may struggle to survive long, while others can live considerably longer. For researchers, however, unusual hatchlings such as this one offer a rare glimpse into how development can sometimes take an unexpected turn. And while the sight of a tiny turtle with two heads may look almost otherworldly, the phenomenon itself is a developmental abnormality rather than evidence of a new or separate species.
