articleTitle: Virat Kohli refutes claim he visited Premanand Ji Maharaj for Rs 5 cr: ‘Out of deep faith’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Anushka Sharma and Virat Kohli visit their guru Premanand Ji Maharaj in Vrindavan
description: In a letter to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Dinesh Sharma alleged that a Rajasthan-based private company and a property builder lobby had spent Rs 5 crore to facilitate Virat Kohli’s first visit to the ashram in 2023.
body_raw: Cricketer Virat Kohli has dismissed claims that he first visited the ashram of spiritual leader Premanand Maharaj in exchange for money, calling the allegations baseless and factually incorrect. He emphasised his deep faith as the reason for his visits, along with actor wife Anushka Sharma, to the ashram. The allegations began after the death of a disciple of Premanand Ji Maharaj, Rasik Dulari, under mysterious circumstances at his Radha Keli Kunj Ashram. Falahari Maharaj Dinesh Sharma, president of the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Sangharsh Nyas, claimed that Virat Kohli was paid Rs 5 crore to visit the ashram for the first time. Kohlis team, however, has categorically refuted the claim. The cricketers spokesperson issued an official statement saying, We would like to categorically state that the claims made by Falahari Maharaj Dinesh Sharma in regards to Mr Virat Kohli are completely false, baseless and factually incorrect. The statement further read, Mr Virat Kohli visits Premanand Maharaj Ji purely out of his deep faith and reverence for Maharaj Ji. It concluded, We strongly refute these claims and urge the media to exercise due diligence, verify facts before reporting or amplifying such statements, and report responsibly. What sparked the controversy? Following Rasik Dularis death, Sharma alleged that the builder lobby and land mafia had been using the name of Premanand Maharajs ashram for public relations and running an alleged extortion racket. ALSO READ  Soundarya Rajinikanth says parents changing male-dominated dynamic at home My rocks during divorce In a letter to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Dinesh Sharma alleged that a Rajasthan-based private company and a property builder lobby had spent Rs 5 crore to facilitate Kohlis first visit to the ashram in 2023. He alleged that the motive was to boost the popularity and reach of the ashram. The investigation into Rasik Dularis death is underway. When Virat-Anushka first visited Premanad Maharaj Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma first visited Vrindavan on January 4, 2023, to seek the blessings of Premanand Maharaj. Since then, the couple has made several visits to meet the spiritual leader, including before and after IPL matches and during their trips to India from London. Multiple videos from the couples visits to the spiritual leader often go viral on social media. Their most recent visit was on July 22, 2026, when they visited Premanand Maharaj at his ashram in Vrindavan. The couple made headlines after they were seen walking barefoot through the drizzle to seek his blessings.

articleTitle: College withholds security money over lost receipt, MBBS student wins Rs 2.40 lakh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Medical college security money refund MBBS student
description: A man who took admission in a private medical college and deposited refundable security money was later shifted to another college after the institute was closed for administrative reasons.
body_raw: A Rohtak consumer commission ordered a private medical college to pay Rs 2.40 lakh to a former MBBS student after it withheld his refundable security and library deposits because he could not produce the original receipt. The commission held that the mere failure to produce the original receipt was not, by itself, sufficient ground to permanently deny the refundable security amount, especially when the payment was supported by documentary evidence. President Nagender Singh Kadian, along with members Dr Tripti Pannu and Dr Vijender Singh, was hearing a complaint filed by a 26-year-old man who had completed his MBBS degree, including internship, in January 2019. The mere non-production of the original receipt, in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case, cannot by itself be treated as sufficient ground to permanently deny the complainant the refundable security amount, particularly when the payment is otherwise supported by documentary evidence and the respondents colleges have not established that the said amount was adjusted, refunded or otherwise utilised towards any lawful liability of the complainant, the September 24 order read. Shifted to another college The man claimed that he took admission in the private medical college in 2012 and deposited Rs 2 lakh as refundable security and Rs 25,000 as refundable library security with the institute on September 15, 2012. The man added that the said Institute was subsequently closed due to administrative reasons and its students were shifted to various medical colleges in Haryana. The complainant, along with other students, was shifted to another college at Hisar in 2017, where he completed his MBBS degree, including internship, in 2019. However, the man added that the security money was lying with the said college and he submitted a request letter in 2019 to the principal of the said colleges seeking refund of the security amount of Rs 2.25 lakh and enclosed a copy of the receipt. However, he was asked to produce the original receipt, which the complainant stated had been lost and was not traceable. Despite repeated requests, the security amount was not refunded, and the colleges ultimately refused to release the amount. Aggrieved, he moved the commission seeking refund and compensation for deficiency in service, causing him mental agony and harassment. The complainant was represented by advocate Anurag Malik before the commission. Colleges defence The college submitted that the complainant has not produced or furnished the original receipt of depositing the said security amount with the college, and in the absence of the original receipt of the security amount, it cannot be refunded, as the college is non-functional. It was further submitted that it was also instructed to all the candidates of each batch to submit the original fee receipts, but the complainant has not deposited the original fee receipt despite the direction to do so. Some students got refund The commission noted that it was an admitted position that the complainant had been a student of the erstwhile college and was subsequently shifted to another college. It also highlighted that the colleges themselves admitted that security amounts of other similarly situated students had been refunded pursuant to the government decision. The documents placed on record further show that even some students who subsequently submitted their receipts were thereafter granted refund, it noted. The commission further noted that the record demonstrates that the said security amount was refundable and that the university had undertaken the process of refunding the same to similarly situated students. In these circumstances, withholding the refundable security and library security amount of the complainant merely on account of non-production of the original receipt, despite the availability of a copy of the receipt and the affidavit furnished by him regarding its loss, amounts to deficiency in service on the part of the respondents colleges, it added. The commission also found that the colleges had not established that the amount had been adjusted, refunded or used towards any lawful liability of the complainant. Accordingly, the commission directed that said college pay Rs 2.25 lakh to the complainant along with Rs 10,000 towards compensation for mental agony and harassment and Rs 5,000towards litigation expenses. Takeaway This ruling highlights that non-production of the original receipt cannot, in the particular circumstances of the case, by itself justify denial of a refundable security amount when payment is otherwise supported by documentary evidence. articleTitle: Supreme Court to consider hearing plea to recall split verdict on law to appoint CEC
articleFeaturedImageAlt: CEC appointment law Supreme Court, Supreme Court CEC appointment law, Chief Election Commissioner appointment law, Election Commissioners appointment law, 2023 CEC law, Constitution Bench CEC case, Supreme Court election commissioners case, Justice Satish Chandra Sharma, Election Commission appointment case, CEC EC appointment law challenge, SC Constitution Bench reference, judicial propriety plea, Supreme Court news, EC news, Indian Express news
description: The applicants have said Justice Satish Chandra Sharma did not disclose that his son is EC’s standing counsel in Madhya Pradesh.
body_raw: The Supreme Court said Wednesday it would consider a request to list for hearing an application seeking to recall or modify its September order referring petitions challenging the 2023 law on the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners to a Constitution Bench. The application contends that the son of one of the judges who delivered the order is a standing counsel for the Election Commission before the Madhya Pradesh High Court. Appearing for the applicants, Senior Advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan mentioned the plea before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant. We will examine and then take a call, the CJI said. A two-judge bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma delivered a split verdict on September 23 on the Centres request to refer the matter to a Constitution Bench. While Justice Datta rejected the prayer, Justice Sharma favoured the reference. Unable to reach a united view, the bench finally agreed to refer it to the CJI for a Constitution Bench. What the plea says The application said it is seeking recall of only Justice Sharmas opinion and recall or suitable modification of the common order on account of coming to light of a subsequent and material circumstance bearing upon judicial propriety, disclosure and the touchstone of impartial adjudication. The plea said that after the judgment was pronounced, news reports said Justice Sharmas son, Siddharth Sharma, is the standing counsel for EC before the Madhya Pradesh High Court. The applicants said they independently verified the information with the High Court and found that Siddharth Sharma has been engaged as EC counsel since July 10, 2024. The plea said this information.makes it clear that.Siddharth Sharma.was appointed.after the appointment of Gyanesh Kumar.and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu as Election Commissioners and engagement has continued since the elevation of.Kumar as CEC and appointment of Vivek Joshi as EC. It is prudent to assume that the incumbent members of EC and specifically.Kumar and.Sandhu had a direct role andor had direct knowledge about the appointment of.Sharma.as the standing counsel for the ECI before the Madhya Pradesh High Court, it said. Despite the appointment of.Gyanesh Kumar and.Sukhbir Singh Sandhu being directly under challenge before a bench in which.Justice Satish Chandra Sharma was a member, the appointment and engagement of Mr Siddharth Sharma was continued, it added. What petitioners want The applicants said this information was not disclosed to the parties by Justice Sharma at any point in time during the 5 hearings in the matter and that if it was disclosed during the hearings, they would have requested that.Justice.Sharma recuse from the hearing. The question is whether the established circumstances, viewed objectively, give rise to a reasonable apprehension concerning impartiality, the plea said, adding that proof of actual bias or of prejudice in the decision is not necessary for that purpose. The application said it does not impute actual bias, motive or want of good faith to Justice Sharma and the grievance is much narrower whether in view of an existing professional engagement of an immediate family member of the Honble Judge concerned with the institution whose statutory composition and with the functionaries of such institution whose appointments were directly under challenge, the Honble Judge ought to have disclosed the fact of such engagement to the parties when the proceedings were ongoing? The applicants added that they make no allegation concerning the manner in which Siddharth Sharma was engaged or his conduct as counsel. They also said they are not seeking a recall of Justice Dattas opinion. Madhya Pradesh Congress leader Jaya Thakur has also filed a curative petition seeking recall of the September 23 verdict.

articleTitle: Travel firm ‘denies refund’ as Australia tour cancelled amid Covid, man wins Rs 2.3 lakh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: travel tour firm agency australia covid pandemic
description: The complainant had booked a 15-night, 16-day Australia–New Zealand tour with the agency in 2020 and paid an advance of Rs 2 lakh, but it was cancelled due to the Covid-19 pandemic.
body_raw: A West Bengal consumer commission has directed a travel company to refund Rs 2 lakh paid for an Australia-New Zealand tour cancelled during the Covid-19 pandemic, noting that it deliberately failed and neglected to refund the advance amount to the complainant. A bench of president Manoj Kumar Rai and member Ashoka Guha Roy Bera of the Kolkata District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission also awarded Rs 20,000 compensation and Rs 10,000 litigation costs, holding that failure to refund the advance despite repeated requests amounted to deficiency in service. The complainant had paid Rs 2 lakh for the tour package but did not avail the services of the opposite party due to cancellation of the proposed tour. Though several requests, reminders, and personal visits were made to the opposite party by the complainant from time to time regarding refund of the advance amount, the opposite party deliberately failed and neglected to refund the advance amount to the complainant, the September 29 order read. The ruling highlighted that the conduct and irresponsible attitude of the travel company caused significant disruption and financial loss to the complainant. The said act of the opposite party proves the fact that the opposite party is deficient and negligent in rendering service to the complainant, it said. 2-week Australia, NZ tour The complainant had booked a 15-night, 16-day AustraliaNew Zealand tour with an international travel and tourism agency, scheduled to begin on October 14, 2020, and paid an advance of Rs 2 lakh. However, the tour was cancelled due to the Covid-19 pandemic and international travel restrictions. After the cancellation, the complainant sought a refund from the travel company and was assured that the amount would be returned. However, despite repeated requests and a legal notice dated February 10, 2022, the company did not refund the money. The complainant then approached the consumer commission in May 2022, alleging deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. The travel company contested the complaint, arguing that under the contract the complainant was not entitled to a refund and that it had offered a credit voucher for future services after the tour was cancelled because of Covid-19 restrictions. Company failed to refund Order The commission found that the complainant had paid Rs 2 lakh for the AustraliaNew Zealand tour and was therefore a consumer of the travel companys services. It noted that the tour was cancelled because of the Covid-19 pandemic, cancellation of international flights and travel restrictions. Despite the cancellation, the travel company did not refund the Rs 2 lakh even though the complainant had made repeated requests, reminders and personal visits, the commission observed. It further observed that the company had failed to take any positive steps towards refund, which it described as a primary duty of a service provider. Takeaway The order underscored that travel companies cannot retain customers money after cancellation of services, even when disruptions arise from extraordinary circumstances. It reinforces consumers right to timely refunds and holds service providers accountable for financial loss and harassment caused by failure to return advance payments. Consumers facing similar grievances may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states West Bengal 1800-345-2808 or dial the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: ‘Only rate hike or pause ahead’: RBI Governor rules out rate cut in near-term
articleFeaturedImageAlt: rbi governor
description: The MPC’s shift to ‘calibrated tightening’ signals that the RBI is prepared to act if inflationary pressures persist
body_raw: After hiking the repo rate by another 25 basis points bps to 5.50 on Wednesday, the Reserve Bank of Indias RBIs Monetary Policy Committee MPC has sent a hawkish message the era of easy money is far from over, and borrowers should brace themselves for more pain. The MPCs decision to shift its stance from neutral to calibrated tightening is not a mere change in terminology - it is a clear warning that the central bank is prepared to tighten the screws if inflationary pressures refuse to ease. It MPC underscored that given the current conditions, rate cuts are off the table in the near-term and policy action ahead can only be a rate hike or a pause, depending on the evolving conditions and the outlook, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said after the MPC meeting. With borrowing costs already elevated, another rate hike would pile additional pressure on households, businesses and an economy struggling to sustain momentum. The central banks message leaves little room for complacency. By signalling further tightening, the RBI has effectively chosen to prioritise inflation control over the immediate concerns of growth and credit demand. The outcome could be particularly punishing for consumers and businesses carrying existing debt, as higher interest rates translate into steeper EMIs, costlier working capital and weaker investment. If the MPC follows through on its hawkish stance, the next round of tightening could expose just how much economic pain the RBI is willing to tolerate to bring inflation under control. Malhotra said the duration and extent of the rate hike cycle would be contingent on the actual growth-inflation developments and outlook, especially that of underlying inflation, the extent of broadening of price pressures and second round effects of the supply shock, as also the impact of demand impulses. The MPC observation clearly indicates that another rate hike might be in the offing in the December policy review, depending on the economic conditions, analysts said in initial reactions. Recalibrating policy rate, supply side inflation He further observed that in the light of available data, it is clear that inflation and its outlook are not benign as they were last year, with headline CPI inflation expected to average almost 5.8 in the next three quarters and core inflation projected at 4.4 per cent this financial year. In this milieu, recalibrating the policy rate is imperative, Malhotra said. As regards supply side inflation, the MPC noted that monetary policy primarily acts by curtailing second round effects inflation expectations and firm level pricing behaviour, etc., which take time to manifest and are difficult to extract from available data. Apart from data related to inflation expectations and firm level pricing behaviour, indicators of generalisation of inflation like core inflation and diffusion indices are used for this purpose, he said. According to him, it is difficult to distinguish between the second-round effects and the indirect impact of supply side pressures in production cost through energy and other inputs as both are present in these indicators. While there is some evidence of elevated inflation expectations and generalisation of inflation, there are limited signs of supply side pressures getting embedded in pricing behaviour. Similarly, while there is limited evidence of demand side pressures, risks in view of strong growth in monetary and credit aggregates exist, he said. Considering all these factors, the MPC unanimously voted to increase the policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50, he said. Global uncertainty, supply chain disruptions Looking ahead, global economic uncertainty and supply chain disruptions are expected to have some bearing on domestic economic activity, he said. Furthermore, weak southwest monsoon along with strong El Nino conditions may impact the upcoming rabi season and rural demand, he said. The near-term outlook on inflation points towards continued pressures from the supply side, on account of the deficient Southwest monsoon, El Nino conditions and high volatility in international oil prices. Price pressures are increasingly becoming visible across a range of commodities within the food component, apart from oil, he said. In addition, early signs of inflation becoming generalised are also evident from the increase in core inflation and higher inflation across a larger segment of the CPI basket. Further tightening of global financial conditions, uncertainty about fair valuation of AI stocks, and an elusive resolution of the West Asia conflict pose significant downside risks to the global economic outlook, Malhotra said.

articleTitle: Pune records hottest October day since 2002
articleFeaturedImageAlt: According to the forecast of the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the maximum temperature is expected to stay around 35 degrees Celsius in Shivajinagar, Pashan and NDA till October 12. (Express File Photo)
description: The maximum temperature is above normal across Maharashtra
body_raw: Shivajinagar recorded a maximum temperature of 35.7 degrees Celsius on Tuesday, 4.4 degrees above normal, and the highest temperature to be recorded in October since 2002. Pune and its suburbs sweltered throughout the day with Lohegaon recording 5.3 degrees above normal during the day, at 36.6 degrees Celsius. In Wadgaonsheri, Chinchwad, NDA and Hadapsar, the maximum temperature was above 35 degrees Celsius. Pashan and Magarpatta recorded their maximum temperature at more than 34 degrees Celsius on Tuesday. The maximum temperature has been rising over several days. In Shivajinagar, the daytime temperature was 34.8 degrees Celsius on October 3, when the southwest monsoon withdrew from Pune. According to the forecast of the India Meteorological Department IMD, the maximum temperature is expected to stay around 35 degrees Celsius in Shivajinagar, Pashan and NDA till October 12. In Lohegaon, Chinchwad, Magarpatta, the temperature is expected to touch 36 degrees Celsius. According to IMD, no rain is expected and the skies are expected to remain clear, possibly turning cloudy, for the next few days. This is a part of the seasonal transition and it is due to an anticyclonic circulation, ie, the development of a high pressure area, which is pushing temperatures higher than normal, an expert from the organisation Vagaries of the Weather said. The maximum temperature is above normal across Maharashtra. In Amravati, the hottest place in the state, the mercury touched 39.6 degrees Celsius on Wednesday, which was 7 degrees above normal. On Wednesday, the minimum temperature was 21.8 degrees Celsius in Shivajinagar, which is 1.2 notches above normal. Lohegaon recorded 22.2 degrees Celsius. These temperature readings have been rising, but marginally, over the past few days. IMD expects the minimum temperature to continue rising till it reaches 23 degrees Celsius in Shivajinagar, Pashan, Lohegaon and Koregaon Park and upto 25 degrees Celsius in Magarpatta and Chinchwad.

articleTitle: Food safety scandal in Mumbai to blackmail: Extortion bid behind ‘rat in dosa’ video
articleFeaturedImageAlt: rat in dosa tukaram mundhe FDA
description: Mansi Acharya and her sister Kinjal allegedly came to collect the money. However, instead of arresting them, the police served them notices, a police officer said.
body_raw: The Borivali Police have booked two sisters for allegedly threatening hotelier Jai Kishore Shah with a police case over a viral video of a rat allegedly found in a dosa unless he paid them Rs 25 lakh. According to the complaint, the amount was negotiated down to Rs 7 lakh, of which Shah allegedly paid Rs 1 lakh in advance on September 30. On October 5, Shah allegedly agreed to meet the sisters and pay the remaining Rs 6 lakh. Acting on his complaint, the Borivali police arranged for the meeting to take place at the same hotel. Mansi Acharya and her sister Kinjal allegedly came to collect the money. However, instead of arresting them, the police served them notices, a police officer said. According to the police, on September 24, Acharya, along with a child and two men, visited Radhakrishna Hotel-Banquet-Fast Food on L T Road in Borivali West to eat Mysore Masala Dosa and other dishes. While eating about half a dosa, a person accompanying her, identified as Amit Trivedi, allegedly found a rat in his dosa. Acharya created a ruckus at the hotel, called the police, and made a video. According to Shahs complaint, the video went viral on September 26, after which the Food and Drug Administration FDA suspended the hotels licence on September 28, forcing it to shut down. Shah alleged that Acharya threatened to lodge a police complaint against him and circulate the video further unless he paid her money. He approached the Borivali police on September 29, alleging that he had been threatened with further circulation of the video and a police case if he did not pay. He further alleged that between October 1 and 5, Acharya repeatedly contacted him on WhatsApp and demanded the remaining Rs 6 lakh, threatening to approach the police and circulate the video. Police booked both under Section 308 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for extortion.

articleTitle: Citing postpartum psychosis, court acquits mother sentenced to life for killing infant
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gauhati High Court mother infant baby postpartum psychosis
description: The woman allegedly told the police that she did not like her daughter from the day she was born, but the court said her statement was inadmissible as it could have been made under police pressure or influence.
body_raw: A case in which a mother was convicted for killing her 38-day-old daughter took a different turn before the Gauhati High Court, which found that she may have been going through the rare mental health condition of postpartum psychosis.The court acquitted the woman in the 2016 case, holding that her confession was inadmissible as it raised concerns of police pressure. Justices M Zothankhuma and Rajesh Mazumdar, on October 6, allowed the womans appeal against her conviction and life imprisonment by the trial court in September 2023. The court mentioned that postpartumpsychosis is a severe mental condition which develops following delivery, and scientific research has pointed out that childbirth is a potent trigger for severe mood disorder. The woman had allegedly told the police that she did not like her daughter from the day she was born. Her confessional statement is to the effect that she was mentally unwell and that she did not like her daughter from the day she was born. On trying to understand the case where a mother does not like her newborn child, we have come across rare cases of infanticide due to Postpartum Psychosis, the court said. Postpartum psychosis is a rare and severe mental health condition that can develop after childbirth and is distinct from postpartum depression. The court added that women with this health issue can lose touch with reality, and its symptoms may include delusions, hallucinations, severe mood symptoms and cognitive symptoms. The court, however, said it was not required to decide whether the woman actually had postpartum psychosis, but noted that the trial court should have considered the issue before convicting her. Infant goes missing The womans husband lodged a complaint in 2016 stating that his daughter, who was one month and eight days old, had gone missing during the night. During questioning by the police, his wife allegedly confessed in the presence of local witnesses that she had killed the child on October 14, 2016, and thrown the body into the Dikhow River. The husband, however, said that when he had inquired about the missing infant, the wife stated that she did not know where the baby was. The woman was represented by advocate D Baruah. Can put mother, child in danger The court pointed out that some symptoms of postpartum psychosis can be fleeting and changeable. It noted that there is a risk to babies in around 35 per cent of postpartum psychosis cases, as mothers going through the condition may act on false beliefs, incorrectly handle their babies, become severely confused or behave unusually. The court added that such behaviour can be temporary and is caused by the effect of postpartum psychosis on the brain. The National Library of Medicine in the National Centre for Biotechnology Information states that postpartum psychosis is rare, affecting one and two per one thousand women. However, postpartum psychosis can develop rapidly and place the life of the mother and infant in danger, the court mentioned. It noted that the mothers confessional statement was signed by a woman head constable who was present when it was recorded. The same makes the said confessional statement inadmissible as evidence, as the accused cannot be said to be completely free from police pressure or influence at the time of making her confession, it added. The court held that the womans conviction could not be sustained solely on the basis of the inadmissible confession and that an admission made during the hearing on sentence could not be treated as additional evidence for conviction. It thus set aside the conviction and acquitted her of the charge of murder.

The campus is expected to begin admissions for its first cohort of students in August 2027. The Hyderabad campus will offer programmes in high-demand areas including business, computing, engineering and analytics. Additional programmes are expected to be proposed to the UGC from the second year onwards. The academic model will combine subject-based learning with practical and experiential learning. Students will be expected to develop both knowledge of their chosen discipline and skills that can be applied in workplace settings. The campus will also focus on interdisciplinary learning, allowing students to work across different subject areas and apply problem-solving approaches to real-world situations. The emphasis will be on preparing students for changing workplace requirements rather than only academic study. CU Denver was established in 1973 and is governed by the University of Colorado Board of Regents. It has around 14,000 students and more than 100,000 alumni across over 100 countries. The university is classified as an R1 research institution by the Carnegie Commission on Higher Education, a classification for institutions with very high research activity, a statement notes. articleTitle: ‘Your computer is hacked’: India-based scam targeting US seniors via Bitcoin ATMs
articleFeaturedImageAlt: bitcoin
description: The CBI said a syndicate operating from Punjab and Delhi posed as tech-support staff and sent US seniors to Bitcoin ATMs, routing crores through crypto wallets into India.
body_raw: In 2022, several senior citizens in the US began receiving calls and emails from men claiming to be Microsoft employees. Their computers had been hacked, the callers warned, and their bank accounts compromised. The callers then directed the seniors to Bitcoin ATMs - a physical kiosk that lets you buy or sell cryptocurrency using cash or a debit card, connecting directly to your digital wallet - where they were coerced into depositing cash to buy software that would supposedly fix their computers. Fearing that their money and personal information were at risk, the victims followed the instructions. They realised only later that they had been scammed. Some of them complained last year to authorities in the US, and the Central Bureau of Investigation CBI was alerted. On July 27 this year, the CBI lodged an FIR under sections of criminal conspiracy and Section 66D of the IT Act, 2000, which punishes cheating by personation using a computer resource. In August, three scammers, including alleged mastermind Saurabh Rana, were arrested by the central agency. Investigators said the accused were part of a syndicate operating from Punjab and Delhi that allegedly targeted American nationals through an organised tech-support scam by impersonating representatives of technology companies, financial institutions and law-enforcement agencies. How scam money reached India According to the CBI, the extorted money was converted into cryptocurrency and moved through a chain of crypto wallets before being consolidated into accounts controlled by the accused. The proceeds were then routed into the Indian banking system. The victims were allegedly defrauded of hundreds of crores of rupees, it said. During Ranas bail hearing last month, the agency told the court that the cryptocurrency trail provided a direct link between at least one victim and Ranas account. The CBI, in its submissions before the court, mentioned the name of a victim, Joanne Maalouf. The agency said the cryptocurrency exchange account operated by Rana received proceeds directly from the wallet associated with Maaloufs kiosk deposits on December 13, 2022, thereby establishing a direct nexus between the accused and the proceeds of the fraud. Investigators said Rana operated a Binance account linked to his Aadhaar card. The account allegedly received the largest share of the fraud proceeds - 203.30 Bitcoins, then valued at approximately 6.53 million, or over Rs 50 crore. The CBI also alleged that the fraud was operationally controlled from Delhi. It said Rana had accessed his cryptocurrency exchange account from Delhi-geolocated IP addresses on multiple dates during the period the fraud was active. Investigators also recovered incriminating WhatsApp chats between Rana and the co-accused, which, they said, pointed to his role as the main conspirator and mastermind of the fraud. Bail denied Arguing for bail before Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate ACJM Jyoti Maheshwari of the Rouse Avenue Courts Complex, Ranas counsel pointed to the delay, saying the offence dates back to 2022 while the case was registered after a four-year gap. The counsel also argued that the prosecution had failed to establish the necessity of his arrest. In an affidavit filed before the court, Ranas brother, Rishav, made allegations of torture and harassment during the investigation. He alleged that an employee, Ms S, was called to the CBI office in Chandigarh on August 22 and 23 for interrogation, where she was categorically subjected to torture and harassment by the investigating officer. The affidavit further claimed that the Investigation Officer IO had told Ms S that the court had already convicted Rana and would deny him bail, and that the court had conveyed this to the IO. Rejecting the bail plea, the ACJM held  . it is apparent that the applicantaccused spearheaded the operations of the alleged cyber-fraud syndicate. Recovery of multiple digital devices from the premises connected with the applicantaccused is also indicative of his complicity in the alleged offence. . Moreover, this Court cannot turn a blind eye to the submissions on behalf of the investigating agency that various incriminating chats have been recovered from the mobile phones used by the applicant, which also reveal the modus operandi of the alleged offence, the court said. It said the offence has transnational ramifications and involves the cheating of several senior citizens of USA. .. This Court cannot turn a blind eye to the seriousness of the present offence and the alarming rise in cases of such nature, which have time and again warranted for a cautious approach, by the Honble Apex Court. Such an offence taints not just the people complicit in the crime, but also the entire country, she added in her order dated September 22. The CBI was represented in court by Public Prosecutors Saloni and Anoop Kumar. Recoveries made During simultaneous searches conducted in Delhi, Ludhiana and Mohali, Rana and co-accused Jappandeep Singh were arrested from Ludhiana, while a third man, Indermohan Singh, was arrested from Mohali. Officials said Ranas father owned the flat in Mohali from where the scam was being run. Other persons allegedly involved in the syndicate are yet to be apprehended, and the full conspiracy is still being unravelled, officials said. About 30 digital devices, including mobile phones and laptops, were seized from the Mohali premises. Digital evidence - mobile data and crypto wallets among them - form crucial evidence in the case, as per the CBI. This is still being examined.

articleTitle: Ola, Uber banned in Chandigarh. Drivers have a workaround. So do cops
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Chandigarh bike taxi ban, Chandigarh taxi ban, Chandigarh bike taxi crackdown, Chandigarh Police taxi crackdown, Uber ban Chandigarh, Ola ban Chandigarh, Rapido ban Chandigarh, inDrive ban Chandigarh, banned bike taxis Chandigarh, app-based taxis Chandigarh, Chandigarh transport rules, Bharat Taxi Chandigarh, Chandigarh news, Indian Express news
description: The crackdown has so far resulted in action against 915 vehicles in Chandigarh, making it the authorities’ biggest drive yet against unauthorised app-based transport services.
body_raw: The ride may be banned, but getting one is still surprisingly easy. In Chandigarh, drivers of app-based taxis and bike taxis linked to Uber, Ola, inDrive, and Rapido are finding new ways to stay on the road - and the police are finding new ways to catch them. From switching phones to airplane mode to cancelling bookings just before the ride begins, drivers are adopting tactics to evade enforcement, while Chandigarh Police are booking rides themselves on banned platforms to catch them in the act. The cat-and-mouse game has so far resulted in action against 915 vehicles - 812 challaned and 103 impounded - in what authorities describe as their biggest crackdown yet on unauthorised app-based transport services. Modus operandi The drivers allegedly put their phones on airplane mode, ask passengers to pay the amount shown, cancel the ride just before starting, and go offline while plying routes where police are not normally deployed. Drivers also allegedly ask passengers to tell the police they found the cab parked and hired it directly. When the police catch the driver, he quickly puts his phone on airplane mode. Meanwhile, the Chandigarh Police book cabs through the banned apps themselves to catch drivers red-handed. After stopping a vehicle, they check the drivers phone and apps to establish whether the cab is being operated through a banned platform. More bikes than cabs According to State Transport Authority STA data, bike taxis accounted for the bulk of the violations, with nearly 70 per cent of all vehicles found operating in Chandigarh, underlining the scale of their continued operation in the city. Data shows as many as 569 bike taxis were challaned and 67 impounded, taking the number to 636. Among the 208 taxis, 194 were challaned and 14 impounded. Despite the ban, app-based two-wheeler services and taxis both have a significant presence on city roads, a STA senior officer told The Indian Express. The Chandigarh Administration had also written to the Centre seeking a GPS-based mechanism to restrict the operation of the suspended aggregator apps within Chandigarh. The move was proposed as the apps remain accessible despite suspension of their licences, allowing drivers to continue accepting bookings. The ban Earlier this month, Chandigarh Administration suspended the licences of Uber and Rapido for six months. STA said the two companies had failed to comply with mandatory requirements covering driver insurance and training, fares, vehicle eligibility, safety and other operational norms, despite being given several opportunities to meet the conditions. The action followed the Union Territory administrations earlier suspension of Ola and inDrive over alleged violations related to driver welfare and training. However, the ban has made commuting difficult for passengers, with fewer options and, at times, higher fares due to reduced competition. Although the Bharat Taxi app is an alternative, many commuters still dont know about it, leaving them struggling to find affordable rides.

articleTitle: ‘Imaandaar CM’ hoardings flood poll-bound Punjab. But why are people upset?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bhagwant Mann hoarding
description: Ludhiana residents have questioned why honesty "needs an announcement or publicity", and why crores of taxpayers' money was being spent to issue a "self-certified honesty declaration".
body_raw: With less than six months to go for the Punjab Assembly elections, the ruling Aam Aadmi Party AAP in Punjab is fighting a paradox. While the Punjab and Haryana High Court has ordered a high-level CBI probe into the serious corruption allegations linked to Chief Minister Bhagwant Manns office, the roads, highways and streets in the state, especially in the states largest city, Ludhiana, are speaking otherwise. Huge hoardings declaring CM Mann as imaandaar honest have flooded Ludhiana at intervals of every few meters across the city- from highways, chowks, roadsides to streets. Not just Ludhiana, but the imaandaar CM hoardings have cropped up across the state -- drawing sharp reactions from the Opposition parties as well as residents. Residents in Ludhiana have questioned why imaandaari honesty needs an announcement or publicity, and why crores of taxpayers money was being spent to issue a self-certifiedhonesty declaration for the CM when polls were just months away, and people would be the only judge. The critics are also pointing to CM Manns own words, before he became the CM, when he had flayed other parties for advertising false claims. In Ludhiana, huge hoardings declaring Mann as imaandaar CM have been installed on Ferozepur Road, with his smiling face and a caption Imaandaar CM 90 households getting 600 units of free power. The honesty hoardings have also been put prominently in posh locations of Ludhiana West constituency such as Pakhowal Road near Hotel Park Plaza, Aggar Nagar locality on Ferozepur Road, near Sidhwan Canal Pakhowal Road, etc apart from highways and roundabouts. Ludhiana-based RTI activist and an environmentalist Kuldeep Singh Khaira said it is high time linguists update the definition of honesty. After the High Court order, even the word imaandaar must be thinking, What do I really mean? Now it feels we have to update the definitionof honesty. Those who are really honest never really sing about it. They dont need to announce it. Harjot Benipal, a worker of Akali Dal Waris Punjab De, said This has also probably happened for the first time in 70 years that a CM is declaring himself as honest. Sandeep Singh, a resident, said If a CM has to scream through hoardings that he is honest, there is something fishy. Moreover, can the AAP issue a White Paper on who has paid for this flood of hoardings in the city? Residents question why crores have been spent just to portray him as clean. Polls are a few months away. Let the people decide, said another resident, Kanav Sharma. Harminder Taneja, another resident, said Why is so much advertising needed if you are really honest?From where is so much money coming to spend on advertising? From the pockets of people. Echoing the view, Rashpal Singh, a student, said What kind of honesty is that when you have to shout about it through billboards?Taxpayers money is being used to promote the CMs honesty this is also a first in 70 years. With the AAP heavily banking on its kattar imaandaar a die-hard honest party pitch for the election campaigns, and the phrase repeatedly used by AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal to describe his party leaders, the residents are also taking a dig at the party for omitting kattar in the billboards. The AAP government must sue the creators of these hoardings. How dare they miss the word kattar and write onlyimaandaar for the honourable CM, said a resident, requesting anonymity. Another resident, Prince Vij, said Bhagwant Mann is such an Imaandaar CM that he has to waste taxpayers money to tell everyone that he is honest. What a waste of public funds Pulling out an old video of Mann criticising previous governments for wasting money on billboards and hoardings, senior Congress leader and MLA Sukhpal Singh Khaira highlighted the splurge of the Imaandaar CM. He alleged that CM Mann and AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal used to trap others with their word power. Now, theygot caught in their own words today Once they made fun of banners, and today they are running the government based on flexboards themselves. Claims are of honesty, but development exists only on paper and hoardings Before taking over as the CM, Mann had criticised previous governments for wasting public money on banners and hoardings. What kind of development is this that has to be advertised via banners? Had hospitals actually been built, they would be visible. After 9.5 years, this is fake development being shown on banners, Mann was heard saying in the video. CMs corruption stench has reached Delhi SAD Senior SAD leader and former minister Bikram Singh Majithia also took potshots at Manns honesty hoardings. Chief Minister keeps walking around holding a board that says, I am honest, while corruption in his offices has been simmering so long that its stench has reached DelhiPeople have started reading the boards and writing underneath Yeah, we got it OK, TATA, BYE BYE he wrote on X. Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon said What kind of honesty is this that advertisements are required to publicize it? Ludhiana BJP president Sunil Moudgill, in a statement issued on Tuesday, said that the Punjab government has put hoardings of Honest CM across the state, but they should be replaced with Dishonest CM. The High Court has ordered a high-level CBI probe into corruption allegations in the working of the Chief Ministers Office CMO and his Officer on Special Duty OSD Rajbir Singh Ghuman, but the CM is protecting corrupt individuals. Despite the ED writing to the Punjab Government three times, they did not get it probed. What does this prove?  he asked. Imandaar CM exposed Ravneet Singh Bittu Former union minister and BJP leader Ravneet Singh Bittu posted on X Bhagwant Mann, who has put up billboards across Punjab proclaiming himself as Imandaar CM, has been exposed today.Acting on the direct orders of the Honble Punjab and Haryana High Court and an ED report, the CBI has registered an FIR against the Punjab CMs OSD along with 5 others, conducting coordinated raids across 8 locations.Behind the self-promoted billboards of integrity lay severe allegations of institutionalized corruption-from auctioning IASIPS transfers and manipulating government tenders to fixing land CLUs and leaking confidential policy drafts for pecuniary gain.Integrity was confined to advertisements, while power was blatantly abused behind closed doors. Hoardings are part of routine campaign However, Ludhiana AAP president urban Jatinder Singh Khangura said that such hoardings are a part of the routine campaign of the party that we run from time to time. CM Mann is the most popular face of our party, and he will lead our election campaign for 2027. His honesty doesnt need any proof. We have no idea who has paid for these hoardings-the party or the government. However, AAP Punjab spokespersons - Malwinder Singh Kang, Baltej Singh Pannu, and Neel Garg - were not available for comments.

articleTitle: ‘Can a fatty liver return to its normal size?’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: liver
description: Can a fatty liver return to its normal size? A hepatologist explains what affects recovery, how much weight loss may help and when fatty liver can become more serious.
body_raw: A fatty liver diagnosis can leave you wondering how much of the change can actually be undone. If you start eating better, exercising and losing weight, can the liver return to its normal size too? This is what an internet user was also curious about and posted the query on Quora Can a fatty liver return to its normal size? We dug deeper and reached out to Dr Ameet Mandot, Director-Hepatology, Gleneagles Hospital Parel, to understand how reversible fatty liver is and what determines whether the liver can recover. DISCLAIMER This article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. Can a fatty liver return to its normal size? Fatty liver can often improve significantly, particularly when it is identified early, and the underlying causes are addressed, Dr Mandot tells indianexpress.com. Reducing excess liver fat can allow the liver to return closer to its normal size and function. In many people, lifestyle changes such as weight management, healthy eating and regular physical activity can make a meaningful difference. However, reversibility varies from person to person. The degree of reversibility depends on how advanced the liver disease is and whether complications are already present. What determines how well the liver can recover? The amount of fat in the liver, presence of inflammation or fibrosis, body weight, and metabolic health all influence recovery, the hepatologist notes. Conditions such as diabetes, high cholesterol and insulin resistance can also contribute to ongoing liver fat accumulation. Similarly, alcohol intake, medications and other underlying liver conditions may also affect the course of the disease. Earlier intervention generally provides a better opportunity to reduce liver fat and prevent further damage, Dr Mandot notes. How much weight loss can help? Even modest weight loss can help reduce liver fat and improve metabolic health in people who are overweight or obese, the hepatologist reveals. Losing around 5 of body weight can reduce liver fat, while greater weight loss may provide additional benefits. The focus, however, should be on sustainable changes. Weight loss should be gradual and achieved through sustainable changes in diet and physical activity. The appropriate target can vary depending on a persons current weight, health conditions and medical advice. What lifestyle changes can reduce liver fat? Diet and physical activity are important parts of managing fatty liver. A balanced diet with fewer sugary drinks, refined carbohydrates and highly processed foods can help reduce excess liver fat. Regular physical activity, including aerobic exercise and strength training, can improve liver and metabolic health even without major weight loss. Maintaining a healthy weight and controlling conditions such as diabetes, cholesterol and high blood pressure are also important. Alcohol intake should be discussed with a doctor, particularly when there is existing liver disease. How long does it take for fatty liver to improve? Improvement can begin within weeks to months after consistent lifestyle changes, although the timeline varies from person to person, he clarifies. Liver fat may decrease before noticeable changes in liver size or other measures of liver health occur. The extent of improvement depends on weight loss, diet, physical activity and control of underlying metabolic conditions. Regular medical follow-up can help assess whether the liver is responding to treatment and lifestyle changes. Does fatty liver always mean an enlarged liver? Not necessarily. Fatty liver does not always result in an enlarged liver, and some people can have significant liver fat without obvious enlargement. Liver size can vary depending on the amount of fat, inflammation and the stage of liver disease. This means a normal-sized liver does not necessarily rule out fatty liver. Imaging and appropriate blood tests are often used together to assess liver health rather than relying on liver size alone. When does fatty liver become more serious? The condition becomes more concerning when excess fat is accompanied by inflammation and ongoing injury to liver cells. This is because Persistent inflammation can lead to the development of fibrosis, or scarring, over time. The risk is higher in people with conditions such as obesity, diabetes, insulin resistance and other metabolic problems. If fibrosis progresses significantly, it can eventually lead to cirrhosis. Timely evaluation and management are important. So yes, fatty liver can improve, especially when it is identified early and the driving factors are addressed. But whether the liver can return completely to normal depends on the stage of the disease and whether inflammation or fibrosis has developed. DISCLAIMER This article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine.

articleTitle: INDIA allies not happy with Gandhis’ ‘impromptu’ protest, Congress firefights
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi, with Congress MPs Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Deepender Singh Hooda, stages a sit-in protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Akashvani Bhawan, in New Delhi on Tuesday. (AICC/ANI Photo)
description: Voices from among the allies feel what was a joint Opposition protest turned into a “Rahul Gandhi show”. Some also questioned the Congress leaders’ insistence on meeting the Election Commission when the protest was against them.
body_raw: Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra stole the show at the INDIA bloc march to the Election Commissions office in Delhi on Tuesday with the sit-in at Akashvani Bhavan. But this has upset Congresss allies, many of whom feel Tuesdays mega protest eventually became a Gandhi siblings show. The Gandhis, they feel, grabbed the spotlight with the sit-in at Akashvani Bhavan, the All India Radio headquarters, while other Opposition leaders were detained and taken away to police stations. Sources said KC Venugopal, Congresss general secretary organisation, told other INDIA bloc parties that the Congress leadership acted in the moment and that he regretted the mistrust created because the allies were not kept in the loop. Voices from among the allies feel what was a joint Opposition protest turned into a Rahul Gandhi show. Some also questioned the Congress leaders insistence on meeting the Election Commission when the protest was against them. What happened on Tuesday About 200 Opposition MPs gathered at Parliaments Makar Dwar on Tuesday before marching to the Election Commission office to demand the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar, the Chief Election Commissioner, over issues linked to the Special Intensive Revision of voter rolls. Delhi Police had cordoned off all roads leading to the poll panels office, and as the Opposition march reached Akashvani Bhavan, senior Opposition MPs, including Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, were detained, put on buses and taken to police stations. An impromptu move In a move the Congress described as impromptu, the Gandhi siblings entered the Akashvani Bhavan and staged a sit-in for hours. According to Congress sources, Rahul Gandhi planned to enter the Akashvani Bhavan complex and exit through the back gate, right opposite to the Election Commission office. But when police locked the back gate, the Gandhi siblings and other party leaders, including Venugopal, Pawan Khera and Imran Pratapgarhi, staged a sit-in at the Akashvani Bhavan, demanding a meeting with the Election Commission. The Gandhi siblings and Congress leaders with them were detained late in the evening and released later. An FIR has now been filed. Congress leaders said the Akashvani Bhavan sit-in was not part of the plan and that the Gandhi siblings pulled off a surprise move. The Congress leaders didnt know about the protest, so the allies also didnt know, said a Congress leader. Congress leaders defended the decision to protest at Akashvani Bhavan, calling it spontaneous. How could we have predicted this? And the MPs of other parties could have come back, and some of them did. The Congress has ensured all allies feel included, said a Congress leader. Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge will be hosting a lunch for INDIA bloc MPs at Sagar Ratna restaurant in Janpath. Why allies are not happy Todays protest was an INDIA bloc protest. But eventually it became a Congress and Rahul Gandhi protest, said a source in the INDIA bloc parties. Some senior leaders of the allies also said that the Congresss decision to demand a meeting with the Election Commission was not something the allies would have agreed to. Why would we meet the Election Commission when we are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar? If this had been discussed with the allies, we wouldnt have agreed, said a Left MP. Not the first time The Congress had done something similar during the Monsoon Session of Parliament when allies were not told about Rahul Gandhis plan to stage a sit-in outside Prime Minister Narendra Modis residence, demanding then Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhans resignation over paper leaks. Then, Congress leaders such as Venugopal reached out to allies, and Akhilesh Yadav and Supriya Sule, among others, joined Rahul Gandhi at the protest.

description: Through this scheme, beneficiaries will receive Rs 17,000 in their first year and second year of the degree, while Rs 16,000 will be provided to them in the third year, taking the total assistance to Rs 50,000.
body_raw: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday announced that the Cabinet has approved the Bhagini Nivedita Scheme, under which monetary assistance of Rs 50,000 will be provided to unmarried women pursuing higher education for three years. The scheme will be implemented across the state from January 2027, he said. In addition to the scheme, Suvendu also announced that recruitment will be made to 14,454 government posts within six to eight months. articleTitle: Grinding your teeth at night without knowing it? Here’s what it does
articleFeaturedImageAlt: teeth
description: From worn enamel and sensitive teeth to jaw pain and headaches, sleep bruxism can cause damage before you realise there is a problem
body_raw: Lisa Shah, in her late 40s, frequently complained of morning headaches and increasing tooth sensitivity. She did not realise she was grinding her teeth at night until dentists noticed characteristic wear patterns during an examination, recalls Dr Bibhakar Ranjan, a Germany-based dentist and preventive oral health advocate. After wearing a custom-made night guard and addressing contributing factors, her teeth were protected from further wear and there was an improvement in jaw discomfort, he says, underscoring why bruxism, or teeth grinding, needs greater attention and awareness among patients as well as dentists and doctors so that it can be identified early. In India too, experts associated with the Indian Dental Association IDA, say several studies have reported an increasing prevalence of the condition across different population groups. According to estimates across various studies, sleep and awake bruxism collectively affect approximately 10 to 30 per cent of the general Indian population, with varying degrees of severity, from occasional to frequent episodes. There is also a high correlation with anxiety, academic or occupational stress and modern lifestyle habits, says Dr Jayesh Rahalkar, consultant orthodontist and past president of the Indian Dental Association, Pune. Studies have shown that the rates can rise significantly in high-stress or physically demanding environment. For instance, studies in India show awake bruxism rates as high as 68 per cent among professional weightlifters and elevated levels among dental students facing academic and clinical stress, Dr Rahalkar says. The Indian Dental Association traditionally observes Oral Health Month during October and November to promote better oral hygiene and preventive care across India. What is bruxism? Grinding or clenching of teeth? Bruxism is the medical term for the involuntary or subconscious clenching, grinding or gnashing of teeth, which can happen during waking hours or while sleeping, Dr Rahalkar says. Symptoms can range from morning headaches, dull pain around the temples, sore or tight jaw muscles and facial pain to increased tooth sensitivity and enamel wear. According to Dr Rahalkar, several factors have been linked to bruxism, including psychological stress, anxiety, sleep disorders and lifestyle habits such as heavy alcohol consumption, tobacco use and high caffeine intake. Over time, dentists say, persistent grinding can make teeth increasingly sensitive to hot and cold, while also causing cracks, fractures and, in severe cases, significant pain. Dr Ranjan says patients may not even realise that they are clenching or grinding their teeth while asleep. It is only when there are jaw pain, headaches or worn teeth that dentists often identify the signs during a check-up, he says. Bruxism is on the rise due to increased stress and sleep disorders. It is known to affect 20 per cent of the population, says Dr Mohit Kheur, consultant at Deenanath Mangeshkar Hospital and professor at M A Rangoonwala Dental College, Pune. Types of disorder Bruxism can broadly be classified as sleep bruxism and awake bruxism. While sleep bruxism occurs during sleep and may involve rhythmic or sustained clenching and grinding, awake bruxism is more commonly characterised by clenching or holding the teeth together while a person is conscious. Experts say awake bruxism may be associated with periods of stress, anxiety or intense concentration, while sleep bruxism may occur alongside other sleep-related problems. In many cases, however, people may be unaware of the habit, particularly when it occurs during sleep. Rise in use of night guards, but they do not address the underlying cause With growing awareness of bruxism, dentists are seeing greater use of night guards, which are designed to separate the upper and lower teeth and reduce the damage caused by repeated clenching and grinding. According to Dr Ranjan, a custom-made guard can provide an important layer of protection, particularly in patients who have already developed signs of tooth wear. By creating a barrier between the teeth, it can help limit further enamel loss and reduce the risk of cracks, fractures and damage to existing dental restorations. However, a night guard is primarily a protective measure and does not eliminate the factors responsible for bruxism. A custom-made mouthguard doesnt cure the underlying cause of grinding, Dr Ranjan says. Identifying and addressing triggers such as stress, anxiety or sleep-related problems therefore remains important. In cases where prolonged bruxism has already damaged the teeth, restorative treatment may also be required. Worn-down teeth due to grinding can be restored with dental fillings or crowns, Dr Ranjan says.

articleTitle: How JEE Advanced AIR 1 toppers’ scores have shifted over 10 years: From Aman to Shubham
articleFeaturedImageAlt: iit delhi placement
description: JEE Advanced 2026 topper Shubham Kumar leads ten years of AIR 1 rankers, showcasing mark variations from 314 to 355 and popular choices like IIT Bombay Computer Science.
body_raw: Every year, over a million students compete for a place in the JEE Advanced merit list, but only a fraction qualify for admission to the IITs. In 2026, a total of 1,79,694 candidates appeared in both papers and 56,880 qualified. At the top was Shubham Kumar, who scored 330 out of 360. Kumar was followed by Kabeer Chhillar at AIR 2 with 329 marks, a one-mark difference between the two. Chhillar had also secured a 100 percentile in JEE Main and had been among the six candidates who scored a perfect percentile in the exam. The two were also hostel-mates in Kota and had prepared together for the IIT entrance exam. From Aman Bansal in 2016 to Shubham Kumar in 2026, these are the students who have topped JEE Advanced over the past 10 exam seasons. JEE Advanced 2016 topper Aman Bansal Aman Bansal from Jaipur topped JEE Advanced 2016 with 320 marks out of 372. He scored 113 in Physics, 105 in Chemistry and 102 in Mathematics. At the time, Bansal said he wanted to pursue Computer Science at IIT Bombay. The official JEE Advanced report lists him as AIR 1 and the IIT Bombay zone topper. JEE Advanced 2017 topper Sarvesh Mehtani Sarvesh Mehtani from Panchkula topped JEE Advanced 2017 with 339 out of 366 marks. He scored 104 in Physics, 115 in Chemistry and 120 in Mathematics. Mehtani subsequently studied Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bombay, where he was part of the 201721 BTech batch. JEE Advanced 2018 topper Pranav Goyal Pranav Goyal from Panchkula secured AIR 1 in JEE Advanced 2018 with 337 out of 360. His subject scores were 117 in Physics, 114 in Chemistry and 106 in Mathematics. Goyal chose Computer Science at IIT Bombay after topping the examination he had also scored 97.2 per cent in his Class 12 CBSE examination. JEE Advanced 2019 topper Kartikey Gupta Kartikey Gupta from Ballarpur, Maharashtra, topped JEE Advanced 2019 with 346 out of 372 marks. He scored 113 in Physics, 112 in Chemistry and 121 in Mathematics. Gupta had studied at Allens residential programme in Mumbai and said after the result that he wanted to pursue Computer Science at IIT Bombay. JEE Advanced 2020 topper Chirag Falor Chirag Falor topped JEE Advanced 2020 with 352 out of 396 marks, scoring 110 in Physics, 118 in Chemistry and 124 in Mathematics. Unlike most JEE toppers, Falor had already secured admission to the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and appeared for JEE Advanced primarily for the experience. He subsequently chose MIT over the IITs. JEE Advanced 2021 topper Mridul Agarwal Mridul Agarwal of Jaipur topped JEE Advanced 2021 with 348 out of 360 marks. He scored 120 in Physics, 112 in Chemistry and 116 in Mathematics. Agarwal appeared from the IIT Delhi zone and had also been among the candidates who secured a 100 percentile in JEE Main that year. JEE Advanced 2022 topper R K Shishir R K Shishir of the IIT Bombay zone secured AIR 1 in JEE Advanced 2022 with 314 out of 360 marks. His scores were 96 in Physics, 109 in Chemistry and 109 in Mathematics. The result year saw a substantial gap from the previous editions topper score Shishirs 314 was 34 marks below Agarwals 348 in 2021. JEE Advanced 2023 topper Vavilala Chidvilas Reddy Vavilala Chidvilas Reddy topped JEE Advanced 2023 with 341 out of 360 marks, emerging as the AIR 1 from the IIT Hyderabad zone. He later enrolled at IIT Bombay the institutes academic records list him among its 2023 undergraduate students. JEE Advanced 2024 topper Ved Lahoti Ved Lahoti from the IIT Delhi zone produced the highest JEE Advanced score recorded up to that point, with 355 out of 360 marks. He scored 118 in Physics, 120 in Chemistry and 117 in Mathematics. Lahoti subsequently chose Computer Science at IIT Bombay, according to reports following the result. He emerged as AIR 1 from the IIT Delhi zone and was reported to be aiming for Computer Science at IIT Bombay. His 332 was also tied with AIR 2 Saksham Jindal, with Gupta taking the top position on the tie-breaking criteria. He had already secured the 100th percentile in JEE Main, where he ranked sixth nationally. Kumar has said he hopes to join IIT Bombay for Computer Science. His AIR 1 result came one mark ahead of his Kota hostel-mate Kabeer Chhillar.
