articleTitle: Eva Marie Saint dies at 102: Legendary actor won Oscar for debut role in On the Waterfront
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Eva Marie Saint dies at 102: She won an Oscar for her debut role opposite Marlin Brando in On The Waterfront.
description: Eva Marie Saint, whose acting work lasted well into her 90s, died at her home in Los Angeles on Tuesday, confirmed family representative Jeff Sanderson.
body_raw: Eva Marie Saint, the pale, willowy actor who won an Academy Award for her first movie, On the Waterfront, and starred opposite Cary Grant in the Alfred Hitchcock thriller North by Northwest, has died. She was 102. Saint, whose acting work lasted well into her 90s, died at her home in Los Angeles on Tuesday, confirmed family representative Jeff Sanderson. Eva Marie Saints memorable debut Saint had one of the most spectacular debuts in Hollywood history, as the love interest of Marlon Brandos tormented Terry Malloy in On the Waterfront, and her first trip to the Academy Awards was memorable too. Pregnant with her first child, Saint accepted her Oscar from Frank Sinatra and smilingly murmured a unique winners speech I think I may have the baby right here. Her son, Darrell, was born two days later. The award for the 1954 classic made her an instant star, but she soon astonished Hollywood with a firm independence that would mark her career. She refused offers of studio contracts and declined chances to follow up on her great success, explaining that she was taking time off to become acquainted with her new son. A daughter, Laurette, was born in 1958. In her first decade in Hollywood, Saint appeared in a mere seven films. She declined such top-level productions as The Man in the Gray Flannel Suit with Gregory Peck, Summer and Smoke with Laurence Harvey, and The Rainmaker with Burt Lancaster. She credited her husband, TV and stage director Jeffrey Hayden, with persuading her to star in Hitchcocks North by Northwest, the classic 1959 thriller in which Saint plays a spy who seduces Grant, but ends up falling for him. I vividly remember him saying, Honey, I think you should find a quiet spot. Ill take care of the children and I want you to really think about this and reread this script, she told Vanity Fair in 2014. He was so right. And thats what husbands are for. Instead of being put off by her selectivity, studios continued offering her starring roles in such films as Exodus with Newman, Raintree County Elizabeth Taylor, Montgomery Clift, and All Fall Down with Warren Beatty. She turned more to television in the 1970s and enjoyed renewed popularity in the 1980s as the mother of Cybill Shepherd in the hit sitcom Moonlighting and as Tom Hanks mother in the comedy Nothing in Common. She won an Emmy for the 1990 miniseries People Like Us, and had roles in such 21st century movies as Because of Winn-Dixie, Superman Returns, and Winters Tale, adapted from Mark Helprins novel of the same name. In 2021, she played Marisa Tomeis aunt in the brief audio play The Bus Ride, part of The Pack Podcast. Saint was married to Hayden for 65 years, until his death in 2016. Eva Marie Saints life before becoming an actor When Saint emerged in the public consciousness, many believed her theatrical-sounding name must have been invented. She was born with it on July 4, 1924, in Newark, New Jersey. The family moved to Delmar, a small town near Albany, New York, where her father was a Goodrich Rubber Co. manager. Evas goal was to become a third-grade teacher like her mother, but at Bowling Green State University in Ohio, she tried out for a play and won the leading role. After graduation, she lived with her parents and began hunting for acting jobs in Manhattan. After a fruitless year, she landed a two-line role as a telephone operator on a radio drama, and was soon working steadily on soap operas and nighttime dramas, appearing for two years as Claudia on One Mans Family. Network television was booming in the early 1950s, and her looks and dramatic sense made her a favourite with casting people and producers. A critical turn in Saints career came when she auditioned before Elia Kazan, and was accepted into the Actors Studio, which shaped a generation of method-actor stars. She credited acting coach Lee Strasberg with helping her overcome her shyness. Lee Strasberg, when he got to know me a little bit, gave me a scene to do where I had to cry in front of my peers, she told The Santa Barbara Independent in 2009. I worried about it, I worked on it, I tried to use what I was learning at the studio. I finally did the scene, and I cried, and my peers were crying with me. It was just an incredible moment for me. Saint was rejected for the single female role in the play Mister Roberts, but was hired to understudy the actor chosen, Jocelyn Brando, Marlons sister. In six frustrating months Saint never got to substitute for Brando. She finally made it to Broadway in A Trip to Bountiful, which she had played on television. Also Read When Jeffrey Archer called Bollywood bunch of thieves for stealing his bestseller plots Kazan invited her to try out for the female lead in On the Waterfront by improvising a scene with Brando. She was told to try to stop a young man from entering her apartment. She told the Los Angeles Times in 2001 All I know is that Marlon got in the door and turned on the music. We started dancing. He flicked my skirt. Kazan saw the sparks fly, and thats how I got the part.

articleTitle: IIT Bombay puts ceiling fans to a vote after student’s suicide
articleFeaturedImageAlt: IIT-B student dies by suicide, iit Bombay student dies by suicide, IIT Bombay, IIT Bombay students protest, ChatGPT, examination question paper on ChatGPT, Mumbai news, Maharashtra news, Indian express, current affairs
description: The survey is part of a wider wellness overhaul after Sahil Wakode's death, as his parents, who allege caste discrimination, continue their hunger strike
body_raw: As part of ongoing efforts to improve student safety, comfort and hostel living conditions, feedback is being collected regarding possible alternatives of ceiling-mounted fans in hostel rooms, the form states. Its purpose, it adds, is to understand students preferences regarding fan type, quantity and placement, so that practical and effective configurations can be evaluated. Wakode died by suicide on September 18, hours after he was allegedly found using a mobile phone during a mid-semester examination. His death triggered massive student protests, after which Director Prof Shireesh Kedare held an open house to hear students concerns. The survey offers four alternatives to the ceiling fan wall-mounted, pedestal, table or desk, and tower fans. Students can also choose no alternative if they prefer to keep the existing ceiling fan. They are asked to pick from configurations such as two wall-mounted fans, one wall-mounted and one table fan, or two table fans, and to give the main reason for their choice. The options include better air circulation, cooling while studying or sleeping, space efficiency, convenience and safety. Students can also raise concerns about their safety, well-being or hostel experience if they wish. The survey is part of a wider overhaul of student wellness at the institute. The new measures, to be rolled out in phases from this week, include wellness secretaries in hostels, more play areas in residential areas, deterrents against exam malpractice and a new associate dean for student wellness. They were communicated to students in an email from the Dean of Students Affairs on behalf of Prof Kedare. According to the email, the institute drew up the plan after discussions with students and their representatives on academic, career and well-being concerns. It urges students to take part in surveys and consultations, with more to follow. On fans, the email says options have been identified, but a final decision will be taken after student feedback. Under the plan, the institute is working on a system to appoint wellness secretaries at the hostel level and to identify committees where student participation can be increased. Meetings with heads of departments have also focused on greater student participation at the department level and on strengthening support for students. For the play areas, general secretaries, sports councillors and wardens will be consulted to identify suitable spaces, understand residents concerns and assess access. Wakodes parents, Ravindra and Sonali Wakode, have alleged that their son was a victim of caste-based discrimination on the IIT Bombay campus. They are continuing their hunger strike at Mumbais Azad Maidan, demanding the arrest of those they hold responsible for his death.

articleTitle: Messi’s farewell speech: ‘I don’t want to leave, not being with Argentina hurts’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Messi shared an emotional speech after his final Argentina appearance in Buenos Aires. (AP Photo)
description: His international debut 21 years ago against Hungary lasted 90 seconds. After 90 minutes on Tuesday night, Messi capped his Argentina career as its top goal-scorer and highest assist-provider.
body_raw: Messi had one final chapter of gilded magic left in his boots Tuesday night. In his farewell appearance in an Argentina shirt in a packed El Monumental stadium in Buenos Aires, the 39-year-old produced a goal and two assists to lead the hosts to a 3-0 win over Benin. Emotions, expectedly, ran high. The tears of not wearing the sky-blue and white shirt again and the ecstasy of blasting the ball into the net one final time, nearly conjuring up another free-kick pearler, the Rosario-born superstar had it all one final time. The eight-time Ballon dOr winner, Argentina received a raucous applause in the 10th minute, the number that glittered on the back of his shirt, as it did in another era with Diego Maradona. His international debut 21 years ago against Hungary lasted 90 seconds after a red card. After 90 minutes of passionate football on Tuesday night, Messi capped his career as the second-highest international goal scorer 126 and the most assists 67, the last of which came in the 48th minute as he provided for Nicolas Otamendi. ALSO READ  Messi shines in Argentina farewell, ends 21-year career with goal and assist I have nothing left to do but thank this shirt. For 20 years, even through the worst moments, I never stopped fighting, pushing forward, giving everything I had and wanting to be here, Messi said in an emotional post-match speech. Not coming here anymore and no longer being with the Argentina National Team is going to hurt a lot. If it were up to me, I would love to be here for my entire life, because playing for Argentina is the most beautiful thing there is.  Messi Not coming anymore will be very painful. I swear, I would like to come here all my life because playing for the Argentine national team is the most beautiful thing that can happen to you.  - Kalshi FC KalshiFC October 7, 2026 I think Im talking more than ever today because I simply dont want this moment to end, Messi said. After the World Cup dream eluded him on four occasions in 2006, 2010, 2014 and 2018, Messi and Co. produced a month of superlative football en route to the crown in Qatar in 2022. Messis men nearly secured a dream title defence earlier this year, only to be stopped at the hurdle against a rugged Spanish contingent. Age or the enduring American heat did not deter Messi until then, having recorded eight goals and four assists. But I think the time has come for me to retire. The last World Cup took a lot out of us after everything we went through. We arrived in the final with just enough left in us, but we fought until the very end, like we always did. We came very close to winning it again, and despite everything that was said about us, nothing strange happened. The match against England took a lot out of us because we gave absolutely everything. Messis Last Tango was played with members of Argentinas FIFA World Cup 2022-winning squad and their families on hand to mark the occasion. In 2022, we had the dream of fulfilling not only my dream, but the dream of an entire country becoming world champions again. And we did it. We won the World Cup, the Copa Amrica, the Finalissima. Im incredibly grateful for everything I experienced with this National Team, Messi added. The Argentina captain hailed the warrior-mindset of his teammates that powered back to world football dominance this decade and helped him fulfill his childhood World Cup dream. But this journey wasnt only about 2022 or this last World Cup. So many teammates fought alongside me for this shirt long before we finally became world champions. Never doubt how much every one of them fought and gave for Argentina. It was a privilege and an honor to share the pitch with all of my teammates and to share so much of our lives together away from football. Every time we stepped onto the pitch, I knew we could compete against anyone because I had warriors beside me who were willing to leave absolutely everything out there. To achieve the biggest things, you need a strong group. And its during the most difficult moments that you truly discover what kind of team you have. Thats one of the biggest reasons we were able to achieve everything we did. ALSO READ  Most goals in international football Messi ends Argentina career as second highest scorer And especially to this group Thank You. They helped me fulfill the dream I had since I was a child. They helped me become a world champion. I also want to thank the people. I was lucky enough to play in so many cities across Argentina, and everywhere I went, I received an incredible amount of love. Here, in this stadium, I experienced one of the happiest days of my life our first match at home after becoming world champions. It was beautiful. And today might be one of the saddest because Im standing here saying goodbye. Im going to miss all of you so much, but Ill always be on your side. Ill be supporting these boys and everyone who comes after them. Messi also remembered his father, Jorge, who passed away last month. There are so many emotions today, but the first person I think about is my father. There are so many emotions going through me right now. Im surely forgetting many things I would like to say because this is a very difficult moment for me. The first person who comes to my mind is my dad. Im going to miss playing here so much. I love you all, and Im proud to be Argentine, Messi added. I leave grateful, proud and at peace. Thank you for everything.

articleTitle: Claude comes to Google Workspace: Here’s how to edit Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Claude for Google Workspace
description: With the new feature, users can easily access Claude by opening a sidebar next to their Google file.
body_raw: Anthropic on Tuesday, October 6, announced an expansion of its Claude AI-powered services into Google Workspace, enabling users to work with the AI chatbot on Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides. It also lets users create and edit Google files directly from their Claude chat window. Claude for Google Workspace has been released in public beta for all paid Claude plans. What is Claude for Google Workspace? With the new feature, users can access Claude by opening a sidebar next to their Google file. This eliminates the need for users to constantly switch between apps or browser tabs when they are working. Once Claude is accessed, it can read the Google Doc, Sheet, or Slide that is open, see which text, cells, or slides have been selected, and make changes directly in the file. Google Docs In Docs, Claude can fix a sentence or restyle a heading in place without changing the formatting. It can also propose edits to larger docs as suggestion cards in the sidebar. Claude can also be used to generate executive summaries and create tables. Google Sheets In Sheets, Claude can write formulas, build pivot tables, and native Sheets charts, and add new tabs. Users can also attach source files and, for instance, ask for a Q3 budget vs. actuals report with a tab for each team and a summary chart. Google Slides In Slides, Claude can build new slides matching the rest of the decks layouts and themes, so they match the rest of the deck. It can also flag elements that overlap or run off the slide, or text thats hard to read. There are two modes under which Claude works with Google files. In the default Ask before edits mode, each change appears as an approval card with a summary and Claude waits for the users approval to make the edit. In Accept all edits mode, Claude works through the task and applies changes without stopping. How to access Google files within Claude When a user signs into their Claude account, the sidebar will have the same models, connectors, and skills they use in Claude. This is helpful for those who, for instance, save a quarterly business review QBR deck as a skill by pulling data from Salesforce and recent call notes from Google Drive. Their team can then build the next deck following the same format and steps. Users also now have in-chat access to Google files. To use this feature, Paste a Google file link or ask for a Google doc, sheet, or deck. On supported setups it will open in a pane beside the users conversation. Claudes access matches a users existing Google sharing permissions, as per Anthropic. How to use Claude for Google Workspace If you are a Claude subscriber and want the AI assistant to work better with your Google files, follow these steps -Install Claude for Google Workspace from the Google Workspace Marketplace, -Open a file and go to Extensions  Claude  Open Claude. -Admins can deploy it to their domain or selected groups from the Google Admin console. -To edit Google files from Claude, turn on the Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides connectors. -On Team and Enterprise plans, an owner or primary owner needs to enable the connectors first.

articleTitle: Arvind Swamy says wife Aparna is ‘bubbly and energetic’: ‘I am introverted, need my space’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: arvind swamy photo with second wife aparna
description: Arvind Swamy opened up about his marriage to Aparna, saying she is extroverted while he is introverted, and explained how they make their differences work.
body_raw: Actor Arvind Swamy has opened up about his marriage, his equation with his wife Aparna Mukerjee and the understanding that keeps their relationship strong. Describing himself as an introvert and his wife as an outgoing, bubbly and energetic person, the Meiyazhagan actor spoke about how they have learnt to respect each others differences, give each other space and trust each others judgement. He also opened up on parenting, saying that children may remember how their parents treated them far more than the sacrifices they made for them. She knows that I need the space In a conversation with Gobinath, Arvind Swamy said Aparna is very different from him when it comes to their personalities. While he considers himself an introvert, he described his wife as someone who is naturally social and comfortable around people. My wife knows me. She talks a lot. She is a very extroverted person. She is friendly with everyone. Everyone likes her. She is a very bubbly and energetic character. I am very introverted. I am extroverted when it comes to my friends otherwise, I am a very quiet person. I dont engage a lot, he said. According to Arvind, understanding this difference has helped them give each other the space they need. He said Aparna does not force him to attend social gatherings when she knows he would rather stay away. She knows that I need the space, so she wont force me to come. This usually happens. There is not much pressure, he said. However, there are times when she tells him that it would be nice if he accompanied her. The actor said he trusts her enough to understand that such a request usually has a reason behind it. At times, she says that it would be nice if I come. I trust her that she has put a lot of thought into it. I trust that it is important to her, so I would go, he said. The actor said he can also recognise when his presence is important at a family function, birthday or another occasion. I have analysed it, and there seems to be an obligation or a requirement behind wanting me to come, either for a function, event or a birthday. If they call me to meet family or anyone, I have that trust. I wont say that I wont come, he said. Arvind said such requests should not become a source of resentment or something partners keep track of. We must not register it like an obligation. If you want to go, you can go. If not, you can tell them. There should not be any issue because of this. Similarly, I would be happy. She can be happy only if I can be happy I can be happy only if she is happy, he said. Arvind Swamy believes that partners need to complement each other and be willing to acknowledge their mistakes. Both must complement each other. When you make a mistake, you must have the courage to admit it. There must be a positive contribution, where you suggest an alternative to the other person. Similarly, they must be understanding of each other as well, he said. ALSO READ Salman Khan hosts BJP youth leader at Mumbai home Touched by your warmth, simplicity Arvind Swamy on parenting The actor also spoke about how stress from work and other responsibilities can affect family relationships. He admitted that there was a point when the pressure he carried would spill over into his interactions with his children. At one point, due to a lot of tension and pressure, when I am with my kids, the tension and pressure gets translated into the relationship, he said. He explained that people can unconsciously transfer their stress to those around them. When she sees me, I would either be irritated or preoccupied, or I might be in a situation where I have to address a few important things. We will unconsciously transfer it. The kids or people around us will feel that, he said. Arvind said he eventually realised that taking care of himself was important not just for his own well-being but also for his relationships. Only if I take care of myself and be happy can I transfer this happiness. I understood that after a long time. The actor, however, does not believe that being responsible towards a family means giving up every personal need. The mindset of having to sacrifice everything - Let me work out for an hour or I have to get some fresh air - all this is important for sanity. When you come back from this, your interaction will be better with the people around you. If you constantly live in tension, how will your interaction be? Everything will be work-related problems, everything will be an interference. You will be giving out these messages, he said. Your kids will only remember how you spoke to them Arvind Swamy went on to speak about what children eventually remember about their parents. He said parents may spend years thinking about the sacrifices they made, while children may remember something much more basic - how their parents spoke to them. Thirty or 40 years will pass by quickly. At that point, you might not be working. At that point, your kids will only remember that whenever they tried to speak to you, you only spoke out of irritation, he said. He pointed out that parents can become focused on the hard work they put in for their children without realising that their children may have a very different memory of those years. You will be thinking of all the hard work you put in. You will be thinking that you sacrificed your happiness for them. This disconnect - you would have worked and done stuff, but could have spoken to me with a smile. Isnt that what makes them happy? According to Arvind, this difference in perspective is often at the heart of the disconnect between parents and children. So this disconnect happens because people have different perspectives. How much I have sacrificed is not whats important. Do what is important to you, he said. He believes making time for things that bring personal happiness or peace is important because otherwise that frustration can spill over into relationships. For that, do whatever makes you feel better. You have to allocate some time to it. If not, you will be transferring all that to others, he said. Arvind Swamys first marriage, children and custody Arvind Swamy married Gayathri Ramamurthy in 1994. The couple have two children, daughter Adhira and son Rudra. They separated in 2003 and later sought divorce by mutual consent. During the divorce proceedings, the couple agreed that their children would remain in the actors custody, while Gayathri would have visitation rights. Their divorce was granted in 2010. Arvind married lawyer Aparna Mukerjee in 2012.

articleTitle: Jonathan Bailey as Dracula: Mary Lambert talks casting the ‘Sexiest Man Alive’ as vampire
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jonathan Bailey voices Dracula in Mary Lambert's Audible adaptation.
description: In an exclusive interview with SCREEN, Dracula director Mary Lambert talks about casting Jonathan Bailey as Dracula in Audible's adaptation, and using her experience on Pet Sematary and Madonna's "Like A Prayer" to tell the horror tale.
body_raw: There couldnt have been a more apt name than Mary Lambert to helm the new Audible Original adaptation of Bram Stokers 1897 seminal Gothic novel Dracula. Shes no stranger to horror, having helmed films like Pet Sematary 1989, an adaptation of Stephen Kings 1983 bestseller. Shes also been an aficionado of sound, music, and aural effects, having directed trailblazing music videos of pop stars like Madonna and Janet Jackson. And shes certainly not new to the cocktail of spirituality and sex that is Dracula, having collaborated with Madonna in the highly controversial 1989 video Like A Prayer. Mary Lambert on the cocktail of sex, religion, and horror Why not a Black Jesus?, Lambert recalls suggesting to Madonna when the Grammy winner pitched making out with a Black guy at the altar in the music video of Like A Prayer. It invited the ire of a lot of fundamentalist Christians and other people who want to use religion to control people, instead of connecting people, claims the director in an exclusive interview with SCREEN. She believes that unlike the extremely conservative Americans, Indians have historically been far more open to the idea of embracing sex, a la the Kamasutra. Indians deal with sexuality much better. They acknowledge that sex and sexual desire are religious experiences. Religious ecstasy is very close to what people experience as sexual ecstasy. And I dont mean that in a religious way, but as something like being consumed by desire to a point that youre not limited to your body, argues Lambert. So, when she had Peoples Sexiest Man Alive of last year - Jonathan Bailey - cast as Dracula, she could use his magnetic persona to make the audiences imagination run wild, despite the obvious setback of them not being able to watch Bailey in all his glory as the mythical vampire on screen. Jonathan is an extremely attractive man, and not just physically. Hes so charming. Sexiness is much more than that. It definitely helps to have a gorgeous face, beautiful hair, and lovely skin, but theres something else that makes someone sexy - its their personality and humanity. You really feel theres a lovely, thoughtful, and funny person inside there. He really responds to you in that moment, says Lambert. Beyond not projecting Baileys visual as the sinister, otherworldly aristocrat, directing an audio show was a challenge for Lambert because as a painter, shes also a very visual person. Thats what I enjoy most about movies - making paintings that move, she says, adding, But with sound, you can leave people to their own imagination. When you listen and visualize, the sunlight feels more real and the castle more frightening, instead of watching a movie, where the castle just looks like a hotel On learning horror storytelling from Stephen King Lambert is an advocate for whipping out of imagination than consumption on a platter also because shes a book nerd. Thats also what led to her helming Pet Sematary, which she confesses was difficult to adapt. Stephen King uses the characters voice as the singular point of view, and the readers read their thoughts. For instance, when you read Pet Sematary, you know what Louis Creed is thinking. He wants to kill the cat. He hates his daughter. These are things people dont share. But we understand thats what drives him in order to bring his son back to life, says the filmmaker. Dracula, starring Jonathan Bailey, is now available on Audible   - best of jonathan bailey badpostjbailey October 1, 2026 But with Dracula, the job was made slightly easier by multiple characters points of view. They write diaries and letters, and they tear them off sometimes. More often than not, the first letters they write are what they actually think. Its a difficult thing to visualize what someone is saying to themselves. Sometimes, its conveyed through narration, but I feel its best done through performance. Its easier in an audio drama because there are no visuals to distract from it. Sometimes, wed do a sequence over and over again until we were on the same page. Because there are no cameras, sets, hair, and makeup to take care of after every shot, adds Lambert, heaving a sigh of relief. Fallout star Ella Purnell, who voices Mina Murray in Dracula, is not designed as his hapless victim, as has been the trope in several previous iterations. Lambert feels she was able to achieve that because of two key changes in the three decades since Pet Sematary. Studios and financiers realized that women were making up a large percentage of the audience for certain horror movies. Also, more young women began directing horror movies, pointed out the director. The female nature - and men can have a female nature - is more in touch with instinct, spirituality, and the invisible world. So, this worked well in movies like The Others 2001, The Ring 2002, Insidious 2010, The Conjuring 2013, A Girl Walks Home Alone At Night, and The Babadook 2014, says Lambert, adding, Women could even be villains Like Amy Madigan, who totally changed the face of horror in Weapons, my favorite movie of 2025, largely because of her performance and its implications.

articleTitle: Drishyam 3: Ajay Devgn’s Vijay is like any political leader who uses religion to get his way
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ajay Devgn plays Vijay Salgaonkar in Drishyam 3
description: Ajay Devgn's Drishyam 3 is the representation of the moral decay of our society because here, good does not win over evil, and justice is never served.
body_raw: Drishyam 3 The Conclusion released in the theatres this past weekend and if you, like many others, were waiting for the promised conclusion at the end of Vijay Salgaonkars story, this must have been a disappointment, for the story never really ends. The loose ends still exist, the decade-old crime is still unsolved, and those who committed the accidental killing are still walking around, scot-free. In the first film, back in 2015, the chain of events begins after Vijays daughter Anju and wife Nandini accidentally kill a boy named Sam, who sexually harassed Anju and is now blackmailing her. Vijay then makes it his lifes mission to save his family from getting imprisoned. He forges evidence, coaches the family to lie, and befriends any potential pawn who could help him in his scheme. He succeeds. The film projects Vijay as the family man, the hero, who will do anything for his family, while completely dismissing the fact that, in this attempt, they are villainising those who are trying to seek justice for the dead son. Vijay lies like a sociopath and trains his family like he is running a sleeper cell so no one gets caught for a crime that was indeed committed by them. Of course, the man was killed in an accidental altercation, but he did end up dead, and someone was responsible, but the film is not interested in that conversation. There is no concept of justice in the Drishyam universe. The film only cares about worshipping the family man Vijay Salganokars family values, and not examining how those values come across as completely hollow. Vijay incites religious hatred, and believes its completely okay In many ways, Vijay is the exact representation of the political leaders of our times, which also explains his popularity amongst the masses. He claims to be an uneducated man who has supposedly become street smart from working at a cable TV shop and watching a bunch of movies. This somehow explains his warped idea of morality, as its entirely derived from fictional films, but it also explains why he lives his regular life like a main character where everyone else is just background noise. ALSO READ  Is Chris Hansen a hero or villain? Primetime explores his god complex to get to the answer In the new film, Vijay even uses religion as a weapon to save his family because his political smarts tell him that this tactic, if used correctly, cannot fail. This has worked for many political leaders, and it works perfectly for him as well. The authorities watch his plans unfold while being fully aware of how he is manipulating a mob, and just end up being mute spectators. There is even a scene where Prakash Raj lists the qualifications of those trying to put Vijay behind bars. He points out that a chauthi-fail Vijay has left even Harvard graduates scratching their heads but the film fails to acknowledge that a conniving, sly man doesnt really need a degree to fool the world. Fooling the system for ten long years is not a cause for celebration. For over a decade, Vijay has spent hours and days befriending those who are in a weaker position than him so he can take advantage of their situation and save his family. And all this while, the film has never bothered to actually reflect that his morally corrupt practices have turned him into a hate-inciting criminal. Daughters scarred for life but Vijay believes he has saved them Amid all the damage that he has been inflicting on those around him, there has never been even the slightest pause to actually ponder over how deeply he has damaged his own daughters, whom he is supposedly trying to save. In this film, when he pushes his older daughter to get married, he simply talks about moving on, as if she is not still scarred by the act of killing a man with her bare hands. The woman has been living a nightmare that led to seizures, and Vijays solution is just to get an arranged marriage match so she can move on. Its almost as if he truly believes that he saved his family, and did not create a monster that would never be tamed. The family is constantly looking over their shoulder and cant even breathe peacefully without Vijays nod, for they dont know what awaits at the next corner. The younger daughter, who must have been just 7-8 years old when Sam was killed, has lived with the burden of this case all her life. Vijay has coached her into believing that he is her saviour but the poor girl doesnt know that normal families arent hiding bodies and murders for family time. He has created an elaborate scheme for everything, and the family is playing along. Do they think they are saved? Because it definitely doesnt look like they are living a good life. Drishyam 3 is the representation of the moral decay of our society because here, good does not win over evil, and justice is never served. Vijays family faces no consequences for taking the life of a young man but Vijay is celebrated for being a mastermind criminal who can fool the masses by manipulating them.

articleTitle: India News Highlights, 7 October 2026: Maharashtra CM meets Amit Shah in Delhi to seek special assistance for drought

articleTitle: 90 lakh cheque, fake threat, cheap flat bait: How Yuvraj Manchanda was trapped, killed
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Yuvraj Singh Manchanda murder Gurugram drain, Anya Vats Sanyam Sachdeva Yuvraj Manchanda case, Yuvraj Manchanda Adani Realty manager murder, Badshahpur drain body recovery Gurugram, Anya Vats cheating racket ED notices, Lajpat Nagar missing person Gurugram murder.
description: The Delhi Police claimed the accused, Anya Vats, was trying to raise the money to settle a cheating case when she allegedly devised a plan to kill her former colleague, Yuvraj Manchanda, with her live-in partner.
body_raw: On September 2, Yuvraj Manchanda, a manager at Adani Realty, was sitting at Roots Cafe in Gurugrams Sector 29 with Anya Vats, a former colleague who now worked as a freelance real estate agent. Yuvraj, 31, was getting married in October and was looking to buy a home. Anya had told him about some flats in Gurugrams Pyramid Society in Sector 70 that were available at throwaway prices. They met to discuss finances, said a Delhi Police officer. A source with the Delhi Police said Anya was also finding out exactly how much money Yuvraj could put together how much he had in his accounts, how much he planned to borrow from banks, and how much he was taking from friends and family. She then asked for his phone to check something. She wanted to see his password. She had already accessed his bank account statements and bank balance in the name of formalities for the sale of the plot, said a police officer. Four days later, Yuvraj was dead. Police alleged that Anya and her live-in partner, Sanyam Sachdeva, shot him dead on September 6 inside their white Creta in Gurugrams Sector 70. His body was later dumped in a drain. A police officer said the murder was linked to a post-dated cheque of Rs 90 lakh that Anya had issued to settle a cheating case involving a senior Punjab National Bank PNB official. With the money unavailable, investigators alleged, she targeted Yuvraj and fabricated a threat to draw her partner into the plan. From colleagues to partners Yuvraj, Anya and Sanyam had all worked at real estate developer Emaar, said police. Anya was allegedly fired in 2022 over financial mismanagement, while Yuvraj later left the company. She had been bringing clients to Emaar, but was also making side-deals, along with Sanyam, for extra money. When the company learnt of it, she and Sanyam were fired, said a police officer. Anya and Sanyams relationship had also begun at Emaar, said police. When she first met Sanyam in 2022, he had been married for six years and had a daughter. A police officer said she allegedly texted his wife, claiming that Sanyam was making romantic advances towards her. She also allegedly created a fake profile of his wife and showed it to Sanyam, trying to prove that she was also keeping secrets from him. Ultimately, Sanyam left his wife and daughter and started living with Anya. After being let go from Emaar, the couple went to Dehradun for over one and a half years before returning to Gurugram. Anya and Sanyam had a son. By September, Anya was facing another problem. She needed money. A cheating case According to a police officer, Anya had two cases of cheating registered against her. One of them involved the high-level PNB official, whom Anya and Sanyam had allegedly cheated of Rs 1.25 crore between 2025 and 2026. A case was registered against them at Parliament Street police station in August this year. In the FIR lodged on August 16, the PNB official said he had been served fake ED notices by Anya and Sanyam. Police said Anya then claimed strong connections in the government, and allegedly took more than Rs 1.25 crore from him, saying the money was being paid to get his name cleared. But when they demanded more money, the official examined the notices and allegedly found them forged. Anya feared further action, so she proposed an out-of-court settlement to the complainant. He demanded that she start by paying him a post-dated cheque of Rs 90 lakh, said a police officer. But Anya didnt have Rs 90 lakh in her account. Thats when Yuvraj got in touch with her, she told the police during questioning. She claimed Yuvraj had texted her about some work earlier. She knew he was doing well from his social media, said a police officer. Her plan, a police officer claimed, was to take Yuvrajs money and clear her dues with the PNB officer. The fake threat Police said Anya needed help to put her plan into motion. Police said she allegedly showed Sanyam some messages from a senior officer, threatening her to return his money. The only way to pay him back, she allegedly told Sanyam, was to kill their former colleague Yuvraj and take his money. But there was no senior officer. It was Anya posing as one she had allegedly been sending messages to herself since April from a different number to make Sanyam believe she had influential connections, said a police officer. She asked Sanyam to get a gun and two bedsheets and keep them inside their SUV. On September 6, she called Yuvraj. He was having a late lunch with his sister, Karishma, at the Golden Dragon restaurant in Lajpat Nagar, K Block. According to a police officer, Anya told Yuvraj that there was a client who was willing to invest with Adani Realty. But the deal could only be sealed if Yuvraj came then and there. Yuvraj drove his MG Astor to the location and then got into Anyas car, police said. Inside, Anya and Sanyam allegedly shot Yuvraj dead, covered his body with bedsheets and kept it in the vehicle for two days. Messages that kept a family waiting Karishma, a doctor based in Faridabad, had told The Indian Express, that her brother rushed off after the call. We were shopping for his wedding. Then he got a call and left abruptly, saying he had a meeting in Gurugram and would return by 10 pm. But Yuvraj did not return home that night. Karishma received a text from him saying he was fine and in an important meeting. The next day, I got another text. he repeated that he was fine and that he might have to go to Bengaluru, she said. Police alleged that Anya was sending the messages from Yuvrajs phone, using the password she had seen him enter during their September 2 meeting. She even sent Karishma a ticket to Bengaluru, said Sahil, Yuvrajs childhood friend. But after September 8, his phone was switched off. By then, police alleged, Anya and Sanyam dumped the body in a drain in Badshahpur. The couple then travelled to Vrindavan and several other places before reaching Kainchi Dham in Uttarakhand, where they stayed in a paying guest accommodation. They were later arrested from Kainchi Dham after their vehicle was traced. A gun was recovered from them along with Yuvrajs car and phone, a police officer said. On September 11, Karishma approached the Lajpat Nagar police station and filed a complaint. On September 16, the Delhi Police learnt that a body had been found days earlier in Gurugram Sector 70 by their counterparts in the city who later cremated it after failing to identify it. The body was Yuvrajs.

articleTitle: RBI repo rate news HIGHLIGHTS: RBI raises GDP growth forecast to 7.1 per cent for FY27
articleFeaturedImageAlt: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra, RBI MPC meeting
description: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra has announced that the MPC had voted to increase the repo rate to 5.5%, a hike of 25 basis points amid West Asia tensions and inflation concerns.
body_raw: RBI Repo Rate News The Reserve Bank of Indias Monetary Policy Committee MPC kicked off its three-day bi-monthly review meeting in Mumbai on October 5. RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra has announced that the RBI will hike the interest rate by 25 basis points and change stance to tightening amid rising global energy supply concerns and inflation. This is likely to translate into hiked EMIs for retail consumers. Financial markets were bracing for the hike in interest rates amid mounting global and domestic headwinds. A hike in the short-term lending rate repo by the RBI in its upcoming monetary policy would mark a stance reversal, following four rate cuts totalling 125 basis points in 2025 and a prolonged pause thereafter, the agency reported. The last repo rate hike was in February 2023, when the RBI raised the rate by 25 basis points to 6.50 per cent. Markets fall ahead of MPC decision, rise later Equity benchmarks began Wednesdays trading session on a weak note as investors remained cautious in anticipation of a rate hike. Sentiments remained cautious as investors sought clarity on the central banks review on economic growth and inflation. The BSE Sensex slipped 102.43 points, or 0.14 percent, to open at 72,965.38, while the Nifty 50 shed 85.65 points, or 0.38 percent, to start at 22,690.45. Selling pressure intensified shortly after the bell across both benchmark indices. However, soon after the repo rate announcement, markets marginally picked up. Global instability, rising CPI big concerns The central banks MPC review comes at a time when the economic policy faces fresh pressures from geopolitical instability and rising prices. Key drivers influencing the committees stance include geopolitical tensions, rising Consumer Price Index CPI, and increasing domestic food price pressure, among other factors. The prolongedconflict in West Asia and higher crude oil costs are stoking broader macroeconomic concerns with microeconomic consequences they are pinching the common mans pocket every day. Moreover, concerns over persistent food inflation have kept retail price growth volatile.

articleTitle: Google fights 1 billion UK lawsuit over app store fees in latest Big Tech case
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The logo of Google is seen outside Google Bay View facilities during the Made by Google event in Mountain View, California, US, August 13, 2024. (Image: Reuters/Manuel Orbegozo)
description: The trial at London's Competition ‌Appeal Tribunal follows similar cases against Apple and Sony over their App Store and PlayStation Store.
body_raw: Google was accused of abusing its dominance to levy excessive commissions on app developers, as a mass consumer lawsuit worth over 1 billion 1.33 billion began in London on Tuesday. The case - brought on behalf of around 20 million consumers who bought apps through Googles Play Store, or paid for in-app purchases and subscriptions between 2015 and this July - is the latest brought in Britain against Big Tech. Lawyers representing consumer advocate Liz Coll, who is leading the claim, say Google used its dominant position to charge commissions of up to 30 on purchases of apps through its Play Store, as well as on in-app purchases and subscriptions. They argue that those excessive commissions were passed on by app developers to consumers, citing as an example that when Google sold YouTube Premium through Apples App Store it also decided to pass on the commission it was charged. But Googles parent Alphabet is fighting the lawsuit, which a spokesperson said ignores the degree of choice the Android platform gives consumers and that it charges some of the lowest fees in the market. The tech giants lawyers, who said Colls case was unfounded, argued the Play Store faces strong competitive constraints both on the developer and consumer sides, including from Apples App Store and other alternative platforms. The trial at Londons Competition Appeal Tribunal follows similar cases against Apple and Sony over their App Store and PlayStation Store, both of which cited commissions of up to 30. Colls case also comes after years of regulatory scrutiny and litigation over Googles app store practices, including a long-running battle with Fortnite maker Epic Games, whose London lawsuit was due to be heard alongside Colls. In March, Google and Epic reached a worldwide settlement under which Google said it would expand billing options and cut developer fees. Last month, Google also settled another lawsuit for 260 million, which was brought on behalf of app developers, without making any admission of liability or wrongdoing.

articleTitle: Nearly 2 lakh fewer voters: Meet Chandigarh residents missing after SIR
articleFeaturedImageAlt: martyr mother
description: Chandigarh’s final electoral roll has 4,60,209 electors, against 6,59,805 in the 2024 General Election roll — a net reduction of 1,99,596 electors, or 30.25 per cent.
body_raw: A mother lost her only son following an encounter in Jammu and Kashmir. Another family has spent three decades serving chai and paranthas to generations of Chandigarh students and voted for decades here. Yet, after the Special Intensive Revision SIR, all of these and more have found their names absent in the electoral roles of a city they have called home for decades. Chandigarhs final electoral roll has 4,60,209 electors, against 6,59,805 in the 2024 General Election roll - a net reduction of 1,99,596 electors, or 30.25 per cent. Notices have been sent to people with a call for personal hearing. Veena Sharma, 86, lost her only son, Captain Rohit Kaushal, who was killed while fighting militants in an encounter in Doda district of Jammu and Kashmir on November 11, 1995. Captain Kaushal was awarded the Shaurya Chakra for gallantry. The 86-year-old was flagged for deletion during the SIR after a discrepancy was found in her surname in older electoral records. A notice was served by the jurisdictional Booth Level Officer BLO, asking her to appear for a personal hearing. Sharma has been staying in Vrindavan for the past several months following the death of her husband and was not in Chandigarh when the notice was issued. Her son-in-law, Vinod Vashisht, then stepped in. In the 2002 electoral rolls, she had Sharma as her surname. At that time, they were staying in Sector 22 and after having moved to Sector 43, her vote showed the surname Kaushal. But the change had not been made in her older electoral record. And she was served a notice with calls that she has to personally attend the hearing, Vashisht told The Indian Express. What troubled the family was that Sharma was being asked to travel to Chandigarh despite being 86 and having several government documents establishing her identity. She is 86 years old and has been a voter in Chandigarh for more than 40 years. She is currently staying in Vrindavan and could not simply be asked to travel to Chandigarh again and again just to establish something that is already supported by her documents, Vashisht, who is also patron of the Shaheed Capt Rohit Kaushal Charitable Trust, said. He said Sharmas Aadhaar, PAN, pensioner card and passport all carry her present surname and are linked to her registered mobile number. I had to repeatedly approach the election authorities and explain that this was an elderly woman and the issue was only a surname mismatch. She was being asked to appear in person in Chandigarh, but why should an 86-year-old woman have to undertake such a journey when her Aadhaar, PAN, pensioner card and passport were already there, he said. Vashisht eventually appeared before the BLO and local election officials are now examining the case. But the episode, he said, raises a larger question about elderly voters who may not have family members to pursue such cases. She had already given her only son to the nation. It was painful to see that today she was being made to struggle to establish her right to vote. The process makes us wonder about elderly voters who may not have someone to take up their case, he said. 30 years of serving chai, paranthas, now an entire family missing from the rolls For more than three decades, the chai-parantha stall in Sector 35-D has been part of Chandigarhs student life. Generations of students, PG residents and college-goers have spent time there over steaming cups of tea and plates of parathas. But for the family that has run the stall since 1997, that three-decade connection with Chandigarh has not translated into their names remaining on the electoral rolls. Manoj, 35, who lives with his family in Sector 42-B, Attawa, said his wife, brothers Anil and Krishna, and mother have all been left out of the rolls. His father, too, had been a Chandigarh voter. We came here for work and the BLO told us that our house was locked and they could not find us. They have struck off the names of our entire family - my wife, my brothers Anil and Krishna and my mother. My father also voted here only. This stall was started by him in 1997, Manoj said. For him, the deletion is difficult to understand because voting in Chandigarh has been part of the familys life for decades. I am born here. my brothers are born here.. we have been voting since we were 18. My father also voted here, he said. Manoj, who currently lives on rent, questioned why being a tenant should become a reason for exclusion from the electoral rolls. Just because we stay on rent does not mean we should be excluded from the rolls. We have been living and working here for years. I have asked the BLO to come and verify us at our home, but he does not come, he said. He said he also has documents to establish his address. My government license that is given to me for this stall, my Aadhaar Card and all my documents have my address. Still, our name has been struck off. Why were all the names removed? They should come and verify us, he said. How can they ask us for the 2002 roll? I was just six For Karanbir Singh - a lawyer - the demand to establish an electoral link to a 2002 roll when he was just six, has turned into a family ordeal. Karanbir, 30, his wife Rupal Trivedi, sister Harkriti Singh, domestic help Neema Rawat and her son Pankaj Rawat were all asked to undergo verification. He said all five members had submitted the required documents before the BLO and filed their SIR forms within the stipulated time. He said he submitted his own form on June 24. Yet, he later received a notice stating that his vote had been cancelled and was called for a hearing on August 4, where he had to submit documents again to get his name restored. What particularly puzzled him was the demand to establish the familys electoral link with the 2002 roll. I was six. My sister wasnt even born. How can they ask us for the 2002 roll, he asked. The family was later called to Sector 17 for cross-verification of their documents. For Karanbir, the process meant taking time off work, travelling to the designated centre and waiting in long queues - despite having already submitted the required paperwork. There was hardly any clear information about where to go or what exactly had to be done. The place was severely understaffed and people were standing in queues for hours, he said. Describing the scene at Sector 17, Karanbir said, It honestly looked like a complete fish market.

articleTitle: Navratri 2026: Start and End Date, Navratri Colours With Calendar, Significance and Importance
articleFeaturedImageAlt: navratri
description: Navratri 2026 Start and End Date: Know the significance of Navratri 2026, its start and end dates, nine-day colour calendar, and the traditions associated with each day.
body_raw: Sharad Navratri 2026The term Navratri or Navaratri is a combination of two distinct words-nava, which stands for nine, and ratri, which signifies night. When brought together, the name literally translates to nine nights. Spanning nine consecutive nights and ten days, Navratri ranks among the most sacred and widely observed festivals in the Hindu tradition, typically taking place during the autumn months. At its core, the celebration emphasizes devotion to Goddess Durga, also revered as Shakti, the embodiment of universal cosmic power honouring her through her nine distinct manifestations. While four different Navaratris are observed across India over the course of the year specifically Chaitra Navratri, Paush Navratri, Magha Navratri, and Sharad Navratri, it is Maha Navratri, also known as Sharad Navratri, that is held as the most sacred and significant of them all. According to the Hindu calendar, the festival is celebrated in the month of Ashvin, which typically falls in September and October as per the Gregorian calendar. This year, Navratri will be observed from October 11 to October 20, 2026, and the 10th and last day will be celebrated as Dussehra. Importance and Significance of Navratri Regarding the significance of Navratri, it shares the fundamental theme central to all major Indian festivals, the ultimate triumph of good over evil though the underlying legends and mythologies vary significantly. Across Indias diverse regions, the festival manifests in unique ways eastern and northeastern states observe these dates as Durga Puja, whereas communities across the northern and western regions celebrate the nine-night festival to commemorate Lord Ramas victory over the demon king Ravana. According to tradition, Goddess Durga engaged in a fierce battle against the demon Mahishasura, ultimately emerging victorious over him. The festival is observed to honor and worship the Goddess in celebration of this triumph of divine light over darkness. The festivities officially commence on Mahalaya, the first day of the festival, which is dedicated to invoking and remembering Goddess Durga while signifying the conclusion of Pitru Paksha, the sacred fortnight of Shradhh honored by ancestors. On the sixth day of the festival, Goddess Durga is formally welcomed into family homes and elaborate public pandals. These festive observances stretch across the subsequent days until the tenth day, known as Vijayadashami, when the deitys idol is immersed in a body of water. Throughout this period, communities gather to go pandal-hopping, partake in sanctified feast meals called bhog, and distribute food to those in need-an act that celebrates and honors the spirit of goodwill in everyone. Across Northern India, the nine-day occasion centers on commemorating Lord Ramas historic triumph over the demon king Ravana. Over the course of nine nights, theatrical stage plays known as Ramlila perform dramatic adaptations of the ancient Hindu epic Ramayana. On the tenth and concluding day, which depicts Lord Rama slaying Ravana with a bow and arrow, the celebrations culminate in the ceremonial burning of massive effigies representing Ravana alongside his brothers, Meghnad and Kumbhakaran. Observers throughout the region dress in traditional attire, keep ritual fasts, and gather for group prayers. Intricate stage decorations, storytelling recitals, dramatic reenactments of ancient legends, scripture chanting, devotional prayers, and vibrant folk dances like dandiya and garba are performed to embody the energetic spirit of the festivities. Friends and families unite to explore pandals and participate in local gatherings. On the ultimate day, the festivities conclude either with the immersion of the Goddesss idol in water-as practiced during Durga Puja-or through the dramatic burning of effigies during Dussehra. articleTitle: Divorce, isolation, extremist videos: Inside the chargesheet of Mumbai ‘lone wolf’ case
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Mira Road stabbing case, lone wolf attack Mumbai, Mira Road stabbing case, Devendra Fadnavis self-radicalisation, Zaib Zubair Ansari arrest, self-radicalisation India, Maharashtra ATS probe, Devendra Fadnavis statement, religious hate crime Mumbai, Zaib Zubair Ansari arrest, Thane security guards attack, ISIS radicalisation suspicion, online extremism India, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita charges, Mumbai crime news, Indian express
description: Zaib Ansari, accused of stabbing two guards after asking their religion, was radicalised by videos of preachers like Anwar al-Awlaki, says the ATS. His lawyer says he has schizophrenia
body_raw: A recent divorce, being asked by his landlord to leave his rented home, and his obsessive food habits, including a distrust of food cooked by strangers, drove a US-returned man to further despair before he carried out a lone wolf attack in Mumbais Mira Road, stabbing two security guards near his residence on April 27 after asking their religion, says the nearly 2,500-page chargesheet filed by the Anti-Terrorism Squad ATS last week. Zaib Ansari 31 had been self-radicalised by watching online videos of extremist preachers, the chargesheet says. The two guards were injured and later discharged from hospital. The ATS has invoked the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act UAPA against Ansari, who is in jail, and claimed that a note found at his home said lone wolves will pounce on you. Investigators first examined whether anyone had guided Ansari but found no such evidence, an official said. Based on his interrogation and other evidence, we have ruled out any outsider being involved in this. Ansari was mentally disturbed, the official said, and watching videos of preachers such as Anwar al-Awlaki on social media radicalised him. Al-Awlaki was a radical American Muslim cleric of Yemeni descent linked to a series of terror attacks globally. He was further disturbed by reports of killings of children in Palestine, the official said. Ansari moved from the US in 2019. In the US, he made money coaching students in tennis, but he had no regular source of income in India, the agency found. After his divorce, he was living alone, and his landlord asked him to leave because she did not want to rent to bachelors. These factors, along with the attacks on Palestine, drove him to extreme content online, which radicalised him over six to eight months, an officer said. While his family members are based in the US, we have recorded the statement of his mother who had come down to visit him and his Kurla-based uncle with whom he was initially staying, the official said. During earlier court proceedings, Ansaris lawyer told the court that he has schizophrenia and was previously on medication. The lawyer also said Ansari eats only vegetarian food that he prepares himself, and never eats food cooked by others, not even at a relatives home or a family gathering. Police officials too initially faced trouble over his food while he was in custody.

articleTitle: UPI, government salaries may be used to measure growth in health, education services
articleFeaturedImageAlt: upi payments
description: Currently being released by the statistics ministry on a trial basis, the Index of Services Production is the services sector counterpart to the Index of Industrial Production, which is a key gauge of industrial activity in the country.
body_raw: The statistics ministry is considering using UPI payments data and salaries paid by the government to help measure the growth of education, health, and public administration and defence services. This would increase the services covered by the new Index of Services Production ISP, the ministry said on Tuesday. The proposed use of UPI data for the ISP comes despite a sub-committee of the ministrys Advisory Committee on National Accounts Statistics deciding against it as an input in the calculation of Indias GDP, noting that payments transaction data is not yet stable, with many people yet to move to UPI from cash. Once the UPI transaction data get stabilised, it may be explored for possible inclusion as an indicator in the estimation of PFCE, the report of the sub-committee, released in February, had said. PFCE is Private Final Consumption Expenditure and the biggest component of GDP when its measured as the sum of various types of spending. However, the statistics ministry said on Tuesday the UPI is entering a new phase of market maturity and growth in transaction values and volumes is showing a clear stabilising trend after several years of hyper-growth. Looking forward, the trend strongly suggests that UPI is transitioning into a highly mature and resilient utility. Future growth is likely to flatten into a stable band, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation MoSPI said. UPI completed 10 years of existence earlier this year. In an approach paper to widen the ISPs coverage-released on an experimental basis starting July-MoSPI said payments made by UPI for various types of schools, universities, other educational and health and medical services can be used to gauge the private sector aspect of these two categories. Meanwhile, these services provided by the public sector are proposed to be measured by the salaries paid by the government for various staff. Comments on the approach paper are invited by October 16. Identification of UPI payments for these categories will be done by the Merchant Category Codes. For instance, the merchant code for taxi cabs and limousines is 4121. Meanwhile, salaries for relevant government staff are to be taken from the Public Financial Management System PFMS, which captures budget provisions and expenditures incurred by the government under different heads. For public administration and defence, which are not market activities and hence cant be measured through their transaction values, MoSPI has proposed adding together the compensation paid to relevant employees and operational expenses incurred in the provision of these services. According to data from the National Payments Corporation of India NPCI, Rs 25,635 crore was spent via UPI on education in August, while the figure for the hospitals segment was Rs 16,976 crore. Meanwhile, Rs 17,487 crore was spent on government services. These three categories constituted 2.9, 1.9, and 2, respectively of the entire months Person-to-Merchant UPI payments of almost Rs 9 lakh crore. These three sub-sectors made up almost a fifth of the entire services sectors Gross Value Added GVA in 2024-25 education around 7, human health and residential care around 3, and public administration and defence almost 11. The ISP is the service counterpart to the Index of Industrial Production and currently comprises 19 sub-sectors covering approximately 60 of the sectors GVA in 2024-25, which is the base year for this new data series. Health, education, and public administration and defence were not initially included in the index as MoSPI hadnt finalised a method to measure their output. Following their inclusion, the ISP will cover around 78 of the services sectors GVA. The remaining 22 or so comes from ownership of dwellings, the Reserve Bank of India, and gambling and betting, among other activities. These will continue to be excluded from the index. The ISP aims to fill a key gap in Indias official statistics until now, there has been no official monthly measure of the services sectors performance, with private sector firm SP Globals services Purchasing Managers Index being the only one. This is despite services being the largest contributor to Indias economy, making up more than half of it for the last decade and a half or so. Industry, meanwhile, makes up less than a third of the GVA.

articleTitle: Naman Dhir had barely bowled in IPL. Then came his 3/31 on India debut
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Naman Dhir
description: Despite limited IPL bowling under the Impact Player rule, Naman Dhir showed on his T20I debut that he remains a genuine bowling option, taking 3/31 against West Indies in Lucknow.
body_raw: For a player who had bowled just 8.4 overs without a wicket in his IPL career, Naman Dhir could hardly have made a stronger case for his bowling. The Impact Player rule may have reduced his opportunities at Mumbai Indians, but the 26-year-old insisted he was ready. Ive been bowling for a long time. Its not like Ive just started. In IPL, yes, theres an impact player rule, so you see me bowling less. But its not like I havent bowled, Ive bowled a lot and Ive had a great experience here too. Ive got wickets, I hope Ill keep doing well in the future, he said after taking 331 on his T20I debut against West Indies in Lucknow. IPL prepares you for international cricket. Theres a lot of competition there. So I guess if youre playing IPL with a team like Mumbai Indians, then youre prepared for a big level, so you dont feel so much pressure coming here, as I feel right now, he added. His performance also showed that the lack of bowling in the IPL had not left him short of match practice. Dhir said he has continued to bowl regularly in practice and is comfortable handling different workloads. Theres an impact player rule in IPL. Its not like I dont practise I practise there too. Its the same here too. So theres nothing new for me if I get 4 overs, 2 overs, if I get 6 or 7 overs in one-day, theres nothing new for me. Its a normal thing for me. I just have to focus on my plans and try to execute them. Dhirs three wickets came after he watched Axar Patel bowl in the powerplay and felt the slower pace was helping him on the turning pitch. I saw Axar bhai bowling in the powerplay, so he was bowling a little slow. It was turning. And in my mind, I thought if I bowl a little slow with the wicket gripping, I can get them out. So I just stuck to my basic plans and bowled, and I got good results, he said. There was a personal side to the call-up too. Dhir was at the Ranji Trophy camp in the PCA when he got the news, having just come off a good tournament for himself and his team. Obviously, it was a great feeling when I got the call. I was in the Ranji Trophy camp, in PCA, our tournament had just ended, a very good tournament had gone for me, for our team, so it was a surreal feeling. I was with my friends, so right away I called my father, he was emotional I got a little emotional. Obviously, every kid has a dream to play for the country, so if you represent the country, if your name is mentioned in the team, its a big deal, especially, I am from a small town, so especially for me, no one has played from there yet, so its a big deal for me, its a big deal for the area around us. Dhir also made it clear that while his batting may get more attention, he has continued to work hard on his bowling. Even if you havent seen me bowl, but Im bowling as much as Ive come here Ive practised as much as Ive come here, so its not like Im a batting all-rounder or a bowling all-rounder, yes, my batting is a plus point, but at the same time, Im working as hard as Im bowling.

articleTitle: TV damaged ‘during shifting’, Delhi man wins Rs 50,000 payout from packers and movers
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Delhi Consumer Commission TV Packers and Movers Delhi TV Gurgaon Consumer News
description: A Delhi consumer commission was hearing the complaint alleging deficiency in service after household goods, including a TV and shoe rack, were damaged during shifting.
body_raw: A Delhi consumer commission has ordered a packers and movers company to pay Rs 50,000 after a customers TV was allegedly damaged when its box fell during packing, and a shoe rack was also found damaged on delivery. It held that the companys own records and the consumers documents supported the claim. President Suresh Kumar Gupta and member Harshali Kaur of the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, South-West Delhi were hearing a complaint filed by one Rajnish Kumar Ahuja, who had paid Rs 18,050 to the company for packing and transporting his household goods from Naraina Vihar to Gurgaon. We have no reason to disbelieve the complainants averments, the commission said in the September 16 order, considering the documentary evidence produced by him, and added that the evidence had remained unrebutted and uncontroverted. The dispute began on October 16, 2023, when four employees of the company arrived at Ahujas residence to pack his household goods. The company prepared a list of 50 items, including their values, as informed by the consumer. The goods were delivered the next day. TV box fell during packing According to Ahuja, the Sony LED TV was checked and found to be working before it was packed. He said the box containing the TV fell while the employees were making space to place it with the other goods. The delivery acknowledgement carried his handwritten note, stating that the TV box had fallen during packing and the screen was damaged, while the TV had been found in working condition before packing. The note also recorded that the shoe rack was damaged during unpacking. Photographs of the damaged items were placed before the commission. Ahuja then approached the companys customer care and shared photographs of the damaged TV. The authorised Sony service centre initially estimated the repair cost at Rs 29,618. It later informed him that it could not arrange the display panel and offered an exchange model for Rs 44,788. Ahuja forwarded the communication to the company. The company initially closed the claim as No Claim, stating that its scrutiny showed the TV had not been damaged by its employees. It later offered Rs 10,000. After Ahuja wrote to the companys chairman, its legal department offered Rs 15,000 through a letter dated February 6, 2024. He rejected the offer and pursued the consumer complaint, seeking Rs 90,000. Commission rejects valuation argument Before the commission, the company described the complaint as false and baseless. It argued that the TV had not been declared or valued and that its liability was restricted under the Carriage by Road Act. The commission rejected the valuation argument, pointing out that the companys own document listed the value of the LED TV as Rs 30,000. It also found that the consumers documentary evidence supporting his allegations had remained unrebutted and uncontroverted. The commission also noted that the companys defence had been struck off after it failed to file its reply within the legal period despite appearing before it. The commission did not accept Ahujas separate allegation that the company delayed delivery. He claimed that delivery had been promised on October 16 and that the delay caused inconvenience. However, the commission found no mention of the alleged delay in his handwritten delivery acknowledgement, the emails exchanged with the company or his National Consumer Helpline complaint dated December 2, 2023. It therefore declined to rely on the allegation. The commission allowed the complaint and held the company deficient in service. It directed the company to pay Rs 50,000 towards the damaged TV and shoe rack, inclusive of litigation costs. Takeaway Document the condition and value of your belongings before shifting, and record any damage on the delivery receipt itself. Keep photographs, emails, repair estimates and other supporting documents, as these can be crucial when seeking compensation for damage during transportation. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Delhi1800-11-4000 or call the National Consumer Helpline at1915for assistance.
