articleTitle: Three years later, in West Asia, a peace still out of reach
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Three years later, a peace still out of reach
description: No lasting settlement is possible without Israel's participation, or without Hamas giving up arms in Gaza
body_raw: The horrific terror attack on Israel by Hamas three years ago, in which almost 1,200 were killed and 251 taken hostage, set in motion a war that continues to ripple far beyond Gaza. The devastation that followed has left Israel isolated internationally, with several Western nations formally recognising the State of Palestine. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahus decision to conduct joint military operations with the US against Iran, perceived to be weakened by internal turmoil and the decimation of its proxies, has plunged West Asia into further chaos. No lasting settlement in Gaza is possible without Israels participation, or without Hamas giving up arms - peace still doesnt look within reach. The situation in Gaza, where more than 70,000 people have been killed in the last three years, continues to be enormously disturbing. The humanitarian crisis remains acute, with shortages of supplies, displacement and military strikes by the Israel Defence Forces IDF despite the ceasefire that began almost a year ago. The much-touted peace plan of US President Donald Trump has made little progress. Only two weeks ago, the Board of Peace announced a 2.45 billion recovery plan for the Strip - a fraction of the 71.4 billion that the UN estimates will be required for recovery and reconstruction over the next decade. Hamass disarmament remains an issue locked in an impasse Israel says reconstruction cannot proceed without disarmament, while Hamas, which prolongs the stalemate and the suffering of Gazans, resists disarmament without a full Israeli withdrawal first. The first phase of the Trump plan envisaged Israel retaining control of 53 per cent of Gaza since then, however, IDF forces have expanded their presence to two-thirds of the Strip. The power to enforce meaningful progress lies ultimately with the White House, but the US President seems consumed by the political fallout of the war with Iran. At the same time, the once-unbreakable US-Israel alliance is fraying Public support for Israel in America has fallen to historic lows, and the bipartisan consensus around military aid shows signs of weakening. Within Israel, the Gaza war has exposed deep divisions over the governments conduct - especially in light of revelations that Netanyahu ignored warnings from Egypt and the UAE about an impending Hamas attack - and the countrys entanglement in regional conflicts, including in Lebanon and Syria. In 20 days, Israel will hold an election, giving citizens their first chance since the terror attack to pronounce a verdict on Netanyahu. The coalition that emerges after October 27 will help shape not only the future of Gaza, but also Israels trajectory. It will indicate whether three years of militarism can give way to a path that leads away from war.

articleTitle: Parmeet Sethi takes post-dinner indoor walk, does standing calf raises: ‘They are good for your sugar levels’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Parmeet Sethi Archana Puran Singh
description: Working on them regularly can improve stability and endurance in your lower legs, said Dr Sarang Deshpande, consultant, orthopedics and joint replacement, KIMS Hospitals, Thane
body_raw: Actor and director Parmeet Sethi, 59, was recently seen taking an indoor post-dinner walk and then doing some calf raises. They are good for your sugar levels, he told son Aaryamann Sethi on his YouTube vlog, even as his wife and actor Archana Puran Singh asked, Thats soleus muscle, na? DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. Taking a leaf out of Parmeets routine, we asked an expert on the benefits of doing standing calf raises post-dinner. Dr Sarang Deshpande, consultant, orthopedics and joint replacement, KIMS Hospitals, Thane, concurred that standing calf raises are a simple but effective exercise for strengthening the calf muscles, especially the gastrocnemius and soleus. These muscles are important for activities like walking, climbing stairs, and keeping your balance. Working on them regularly can improve stability and endurance in your lower legs. Its one of those basic exercises that seems easy but provides steady results when performed correctly, said Dr Deshpande, adding that it also helps lower blood sugar levels, which is why they are called the second brain. Dr Deshpande noted that for a significant impact on blood sugar control, calf raises should be paired with other types of exercise, such as walking, resistance training, or aerobic workouts. For people with diabetes or prediabetes, staying active consistently, along with a good diet and medical advice, is much more important. Calf raises are a helpful addition, particularly for those with limited mobility who want simple ways to stay active, said Dr Deshpande. Do they offer any functional or long-term benefits? Yes, they do more than just tone muscles. Strong calves support the ankle joint and lower the risk of injuries such as strains or sprains. They also help with better posture and walking. For active people, whether running, playing sports, or standing for long periods, having strong calves is essential. Over time, this can lead to improved mobility and less fatigue in the lower legs, mentioned Dr Deshpande. Is this exercise safe for everyone? For most people, yes, but using the right technique is important. The movement should be slow and controlled, rising onto the toes and lowering the heels smoothly. However, individuals with existing ankle, Achilles tendon, or knee problems should be careful. If you feel pain while doing the exercise, its best to stop and get it checked out instead of pushing through discomfort, mentioned Dr Deshpande. Common mistakes to avoid A very common mistake is rushing through the repetitions. Quick, bouncy movements reduce effectiveness and increase the chance of strain. Another mistake is not using the full range of motion many people dont lower their heels all the way, limiting muscle engagement. Also, gripping support too tightly can lessen the load on the calves. Keeping proper posture and activating the muscles throughout the movement makes a significant difference, elaborated Dr Deshpande. How can someone make calf raises more effective? Once you feel comfortable with the basic repetitions, you can progress. This might include trying single-leg calf raises, adding weights, or gradually increasing the number of repetitions. Consistency is key. Doing them a few times a week is enough to see benefits. Combining them with stretching exercises for the calves can also help maintain flexibility and prevent stiffness, added Dr Deshpande. articleTitle: Goa’s anti-BJP coalition teeters as AAP ally makes a case for ‘grand unity’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Goa’s anti-BJP coalition teeters as AAP ally makes a case for 'grand unity'
description: Goa Forward Party says alliance cannot work if Congress is targeted; AAP says BJP-Congress “joint venture” destroyed state.
body_raw: Weeks after the Aam Aadmi Party AAP and the Goa Forward Party GFP announced a joint alliance for the 2027 Assembly elections in the coastal state, the alliance seems to be fracturing in less than a month. The AAP and the GFP had announced the Goa First alliance on September 13, calling it a non-BJP, non-Congress platform, which would offer an alternative to the BJP-Congress collusion in the state. In the days leading up to the alliance, hoardings bearing the AAP and GFP symbols came up along the national highway in the state. The hoardings targeted the BJP and the Congress over the issue of defections, saying, Congress and BJP cheated you twice. Dont let them cheat you the third time. On Tuesday, some of these hoardings were pulled down. In the past few days, GFP president Vijai Sardesai has reiterated that the people of Goa want a grand alliance of all the parties to defeat the BJP, leading to speculation of allying with the Congress. On Tuesday, Sardesai said, In politics, the voter is the King. From Goan voters, I can hear only one call.that a grand alliance is necessary. They want a grand alliance of all parties coming together to defeat the BJP. This echo is such that even if you are hard of hearing, you will be able to hear it. If you brought mangoes to Goa and instead of Mancurad, you begin selling Alphonso or Dasheri from Delhi, will that sell? It wont. Because Goans dont like their taste. What do the Goans want? They want a Mancurad, be it a Cardozo Mancurad or a Bardez Mancurad. But they want an original Mancurad, he said. Sardesai said no final decision was taken though. There is a call for a greater unity of all those who are genuinely opposed to the BJP. So, if this alliance is to be brought together, it cannot be through targeting the principal Opposition party. This is what the people feel. And we have to do what the people feel. AAP seeks clarification The AAP has now asked Sardesai to clarify his stand on the alliance. In a statement on Monday, the partys core committee said the BJP-Congress joint venture had destroyed Goa in the last decade and that Sardesai must decide whether he stands with the BJP-Congress joint venture or with the people of Goa. AAP Goa president Valmiki Naik said it was clear and agreed upon from the start that there would be no place for the Congress in the Goa First Alliance. Naik said Congress candidates had deep roots in the BJP and all the signs point to a hat-trick of defections by the Congress. On Tuesday, the AAP reiterated that Goa First is a non-BJP non-Congress platform. In 2022, the BJP emerged as the single-largest party, winning 20 of the states 40 seats, while the Congress returned with 11. The GFP contested the 2022 Assembly polls in alliance with the Congress and won one seat, represented by Sardesai, the Fatorda MLA. The AAP won two seats. Subsequently, in September 2022, eight Congress MLAs defected to the BJP, bringing the Congresss tally down to three. Earlier, in 2019, 10 Congress MLAs had defected to the BJP.

articleTitle: Chasing illicit liquor traders, cops land in Bihar village. 50 locals jump into river, 2 drown
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Chasing illicit liquor traders, cops land in Bihar village. 50 locals jump into river, 2 drown
description: Police said 39 accused, including women, were arrested while around 1,000 litres of illicit country-made liquor were seized, along with equipment allegedly used for liquor production.
body_raw: It was supposed to be a massive crackdown on alleged illicit liquor trade, coming two days after a police party was allegedly attacked and five liquor traders were freed by local residents. On Sunday, police came better prepared. Teams from four police stations along with armed police forces descended upon Beherawan Chakia Musahri village, looking to arrest those allegedly involved in the case. What they didnt anticipate was this In order to evade arrest, around 50-60 people jumped into the Punpun river. Next day, the bodies of two of them were recovered. Locals claimed some of the villagers were still missing. The incident took place under Pipra police station in Patna district. In a video statement, Masaurhi Sub-divisional police officer-1 SDPO-01 Raghav Dayal said that on October 1, five alleged liquor traders were freed after a police team conducting an anti-liquor operation in Beherawan Chakia Musahri was attacked. Three policemen were injured and a case was registered, he said. According to Dayal, on Sunday, a large-scale search operation was initiated during which the police team was again attacked and several vehicles were damaged. Police said 39 accused, including women, were arrested while around 1,000 litres of illicit country-made liquor were seized, along with equipment allegedly used for liquor production. About 61,00 litres of mahua-based fermenting mixture was destroyed, and a country-made pistol and three live cartridges were recovered from the house of one accused, Dayal claimed in the video. For their part, local residents alleged that the police operation triggered panic in the village due to which 50-60 people jumped into the Punpun river while attempting to evade the police. They alleged that stones and bricks were thrown during the confrontation and that police also hurled stones towards people in the river, making it difficult for some of them to reach the opposite bank. Residents further alleged that police entered homes and took away several belongings. Repeated calls and messages to SDPO Dayal and Patna SSP Kartikeya K Sharma, seeking their response to the allegations, went unanswered. The two deceased were identified by local residents as Akash Manjhi, around 25, from Dhibra in Phulwari Sharif, and Ram Manjhi, around 60. Police confirmed receiving information on October 5 about the deaths of two people by drowning in the Punpun river but did not disclose the circumstances in which they drowned. Villagers place bodies on roads After the bodies were recovered, local residents placed them on the Bihta-Sarmera road, blocking traffic and creating a law-and-order situation, police said. Officers reached the spot, eventually persuaded the protesters to clear the road and sent the bodies for post-mortem examination. Local residents said the road remained blocked for hours as protesters demanded the release of those arrested, compensation of Rs 4 lakh for each deceased persons family, and a search for people they alleged were still missing.

articleTitle: Scheduled call with Putin to discuss possible case of pneumonic plague in Russia: Trump
articleFeaturedImageAlt: United States President Donald Trump. (Photo: AP)

body_raw: President Donald Trump on Tuesday said he has a call scheduled with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss a possible case of plague at a Siberian research institute. Speaking to reporters at the White House, Trump said he would be talking with Putin about the case very soon. Health authorities are investigating after the death of an employee at an anti-plague institute, which authorities attributed to pneumonia with an unknown cause. Asked what the U.S. intelligence community was saying about the case, Trump said the U.S. is in very deep discussions on the topic. Well be able to report about it, probably tomorrow, Trump said. The World Health Organization on Tuesday said the case presents a very low risk outside Russia. The United Nations agency said it was in contact with Russian authorities following reports of the death last week of a woman who worked at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East. On Monday, Trump said the U.S. would be willing to help Russia with the situation. Its a rough disease. You know, thats a disease we used to be able to control, but somehow those microbes have gotten stronger and smarter. Theyre like an army, Trump told reporters at the White House. The call also comes as the Trump administration faces an Oct. 18 deadline to decide which Russian entities, if any, it will sanction under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, which Trump signed into law on Sept. 18. Ukraine has given the administration and Congress a wish list of Russian companies, vessels and individuals it would like to see hit with U.S. sanctions under that law.

The EC said it still proposed to send its most senior officer on duty to the meeting venue to receive the memorandum, which in itself would have been an unprecedented step. However, this offer was also declined by the Honble MPs, the Commission said. ECI respects the parliamentary and democratic processes of the country, as well as its own protocols and conventions, which are of utmost importance. Any political party may, at any time, request for a meeting with the Election Commission and the Commission, keeping in view the suitability of time, schedules a date and time for the meeting. This is a regular practice, it said. It pointed to the procedure laid down in 2025 for meetings with political parties. All political parties had been informed of the same and they follow this procedure. Whenever a delegation of a political party, or a joint delegation of several parties, wishes to meet the Commission, it seeks an appointment through its duly authorised representative. The meeting is thereafter held at a time mutually agreed upon by both sides, it said.

articleTitle: Sexual assault at Bagheshwar Dham: Case takes turn after DNA test

description: The MP High Court has now directed the Chhatarpur Superintendent of Police to constitute a special team and conduct a fresh investigation into the case.
body_raw: The case of alleged sexual assault on a 16-year-old girl at Bageshwar Dham in Madhya Pradesh has taken a turn after a forensic examination established the man accused of raping her was not the biological father of the foetus she was carrying. The MP High Court has now directed the Chhatarpur Superintendent of Police to constitute a special team and conduct a fresh investigation into the case. However, the court did not treat the forensic finding as sufficient ground to grant bail to the accused. It noted that the girl was a minor and that the material before the court indicated that she had been subjected to sexual harassment. Justice Ajay Kumar Nirankari, while dismissing the second bail application of the accused, directed the police to identify the person who allegedly sexually assaulted the minor and establish the identity of the biological father of the foetus. The court ordered that the investigation be completed within two months and appropriate action be taken. The case came up before the court after the minor, who was found to be around two months pregnant when she was medically examined during probe, subsequently underwent termination of pregnancy. The foetus was preserved and its samples, placenta tissue, and blood were sent to the State Forensic Science Laboratory, Sagar. The forensic report, dated August 29, 2026, found that the accused was not the biological father of the foetus. The HC took note of the contradiction between forensic evidence and the minors statements during trial. While the victim had initially alleged in statements the accused had forcibly raped her at Bageshwar Dham in Chhatarpur, she later did not support the prosecution case when examined.

articleTitle: Delhi cops had protest under control, then Gandhis walked into All India Radio
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra are detained by police during a protest against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls at Akashvani Bhawan in Delhi on Tuesday. (Express Photo by Gajendra Yadav)

body_raw: As the INDIA bloc tried to make it to the Election Commission, its leaders ran into police barricades metres from the poll panels office. Soon afterwards, Opposition leaders started getting detained and herded into police buses. The march seemed all but over, and only a handful of Congress leaders remained. Just then, the Gandhi siblings pulled off an impromptu move, upending the script and taking police and their fellow Opposition leaders by surprise. Around 8 pm, police moved in to detain the Gandhis and other Opposition leaders. It all kicked off around noon when Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi climbed a barricade near the NITI Aayog office at Sansad Marg, a few hundred metres from the ECI headquarters of Nirvachan Sadan, and waved the Tricolour as cameras clicked him. Rahul then climbed down as police began detaining MPs sitting on the road. Minutes later, he dashed back towards a bus parked near Akashvani Bhavan, the headquarters of All India Radio, where his sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra was seated, catching many Opposition MPs, including some from the Congress, by surprise. As Rahul was about to get into the bus, the siblings locked eyes with each other. Priyanka got down and, along with her brother, walked past policemen towards Akashvani Bhavan, leaving the cops also surprised. Though the Akashvani staff tried to stop them, leading to a tense stand-off, the two eventually made their way inside. We dont know what happened. This was not part of the plan, said a Congress leader. A Congress MP outside Akashvani said, Only the two of them know what they had in mind when they walked in. Congress leaders credited the Gandhis with derailing polices attempts to end the protest. The protest would have been over had they not done this, said a leader. Congress leaders said Rahul made the plan on the fly to use Akashvani as a shortcut to Nirvachan Sadan, which is located near the back gate of the broadcasters headquarters. However, police closed the gate, leaving the Congress leaders to camp on Akashvanis premises. Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force personnel have been stationed outside the Bhavan. While Opposition sources claimed Priyanka was leading negotiations with senior government officials - insisting the protest will continue until they are allowed to meet Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi - the Home Ministry dismissed it as fake. Around 2.30 pm, as reporters pushed their microphones through the grille, Rahul told them from inside the premises, I dont care what the BJP says. Im standing here to protect democracy. What has been done to the country is treason. Be it PM Modi, Amit Shah, the RSS chief, or Gyanesh Kumar, none will be spared. Until reports last came in, Congress leaders led by the siblings were carrying on with the sit-in, with Opposition MPs such as Derek OBrien and Mahua Moitra of the Mamata Banerjee-led All India Trinamool Congress also joining them at the Bhavan. Unmoved. Unfazed. We will not budge until our demands are met. We will not rest until our democracy is saved from the Vote Chors, K C Venugopal posted on X.

articleTitle: Parliament street shuts down for much of the day; opposition parties step up protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, leaders held

description: Demand CEC’s resignation as Rahul alleges ‘vote chori’
body_raw: Escalating the bitter political fight over the special intensive revision of electoral rolls by the Election Commission, INDIA bloc MPs, led by Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, staged a protest Tuesday and attempted to march to the Commission headquarters, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The standoff with the police through much of the day ended in the evening with the detention of Gandhi and several leaders including Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. Among those who joined the march from Parliament towards Nirvachan Sadan-it was the second such joint street protest since the rollout of the SIR-were SPs Akhilesh Yadav, TMCs Abhishek Banerjee, NCP SPs Supriya Sule, RJDs Manoj Kumar Jha and CPMs John Brittas. Gandhi and Congress MPs including Vadra, K C Venugopal, Pawan Khera, Imran Pratapgarhi, Charanjit Singh Channi, Praniti Shinde and Deepender Hooda forced their way into the premises of the Akashvani Bhavan, situated next to the EC headquarters, where they staged a sit-in there for several hours before being detained by police. All roads leading to the Nirvachan Sadan were heavily barricaded by police. The standoff began when Gandhi and others were stopped by police near Akashvani Bhavan. Gandhi, who climbed atop the barricades, was detained and was seen walking towards a parked police bus. He then spoke to his sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and they, along with some Congress MPs, entered the Akashvani Bhavan complex. All I want to do is meet the Chief Election Commissioner and tell him that he has done vote chori. I can continue to sit here. I am comfortable here. If they dont want us to sit here, give us some other site, Gandhi said. Targeting the Prime Minister, Union Home Minister and the RSS chief, he alleged that the country had been hijacked with the vote chori. What has been done to our country is treason. Nobody is going to escape, he said. In a post on X as the march began, Gandhi said, Gyanesh its done bro. Time to resign. The standoff ended eight hours later when police detained the leaders after several rounds of discussions, and heated exchanges. Posting a video of his detention, Gandhi said, To save the traitors of democracy, the remnants of democracy have been dragged. There will be a reckoning-not a single traitor will be spared. Late in the evening, the detained leaders were taken to the Kingsway Camp police facility. After one set of leaders were taken inside, police had to close the gate as scores of Congress workers reached the spot. Vadra, who was in another bus, could not be taken inside because of the surging crowd. She was seen climbing the gate after which the police opened the gates to let her in. The Opposition stepped up its demand for CEC Kumars resignation after an investigation by The Indian Express last month revealed that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected on record 14 times in 10 months to steps taken by the Commission under the CEC, from keeping them in the dark to adding new voters and deleting names. While the DMK, which was part of the protest last year, was missing Tuesday, the Opposition camp got unexpected support from the BJD. The Naveen Patnaik-led Odisha party sent two of its MPs to participate in the march. For many years, the BJD had maintained equidistance from the NDA and the INDIA bloc. But there were rumblings within the INDIA bloc after the protest. Some allies of the Congress felt mistreated because the Gandhi siblings stole the show by sitting in protest at Akashvani Bhavan. Around noon, all INDIA bloc MPs were in buses and were subsequently taken to different police stations, but the Gandhis and their close aides stayed back. Sources said Congresss Venugopal later conveyed to the INDIA bloc parties that the party leadership had acted on the spur of the moment, and that he regretted the mistrust that had been created by not keeping allies in the loop. Only after calls from the Congress did the TMC leaders reach the AIR office later. Some Opposition leaders also said that the Congresss decision to demand a meeting with the Election Commission was not something that the allies would have agreed to. Why would we meet the ECI when we are demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar? If this was discussed with the allies, we wouldnt have agreed, a Left MP said.

articleTitle: Press Council of India operating at half strength, without a single working journalist or newspaper editor
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Press Council of India
description: I&B Ministry says notification of names nominated by the PCI in final stage, expected to be issued shortly
body_raw: THE COUNTRYS key media watchdog, Press Council of India PCI, has been operating at half its sanctioned strength for nearly a year now and without a single working journalist or newspaper editor. The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting IB has not yet formally notified the names of 13 of the 28 PCI members, six of whom should be newspaper editors and seven should be working journalists other than editors, despite the PCI nominating them earlier this year. Ironically, the PCI remained without a chairman for nearly four months until Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai, a retired Supreme Court judge, was reappointed to the post in April this year. Justice Desai had completed her previous tenure in December last year, resulting in a prolonged vacancy before her reappointment. Responding to queries from The Indian Express on the matter, the IB Ministry said it is informed that the notification of the names of the 13 members is currently at the final stage and is expected to be issued shortly, upon completion of the requisite formalities. The PCI operates under the Press Council Act, 1978, which stipulates that the Council must consist of a chairperson and 28 members, each serving a three-year term. The members include six newspaper owners, one representative from news agencies, five Members of Parliament and three persons with special knowledge or practical experience in education, science, law, literature and culture, nominated by the University Grants Commission, the Bar Council of India and the Sahitya Akademi, respectively. In addition, the Council includes six newspaper editors and seven working journalists. The Act therefore mandates the appointment of 13 newspaper editors and working journalists. However, after the 14th Press Council completed its term in October 2024, the 15th Press Council has yet to be fully constituted. At present, only 14 of the 28 members have been appointed five MPs, three nominees and six from among newspaper owners and management, aside from the chairperson. Documents accessed by The Indian Express show that the PCI has nominated the 13 members from its side in batches since last year, under Section 53a of the Press Council Act. In December last year, the PCI nominated six newspaper editors, followed by six working journalists in May this year. The seventh working journalist was nominated in July. The documents further show that the PCI sent three communications to the IB Ministry separately - dated May 25, July 2 and September 9 - requesting it to issue the Gazette notification under Section 55 of the Act. The section states that the Central Government shall notify the names of persons nominated as members in the Official Gazette, and that each nomination shall take effect from the date of notification. In its latest communication to the Ministry, dated September 9, the PCI requested that the Gazette notification for the 13 members be issued at the earliest. It said it had received communications from nominees expressing concern over the delay in officially notifying their appointments as PCI members. In the earlier communication dated July 2, the PCI asked the Ministry to expedite the notification of the 12 individuals it had nominated to the Council by that date. This is essential to enable the 15th term of the Council to become fully representative and functional so that it can discharge its regular responsibilities, the letter stated. The matter, it is learnt, is under process at the Ministrys end. The PCI has continued to hold meetings despite functioning with half its sanctioned strength. It held its last meeting in June, and another is scheduled for later this month. The issue was also raised in Parliament in February by BJD legislator Sasmit Patra, who highlighted the serious implications of the absence of a duly constituted Council and a chairperson. He urged the government to treat the matter with the seriousness it deserved and take immediate steps to appoint a chairperson and constitute the 15th Press Council. Restoring the full functioning of the PCI is essential to uphold democratic values, strengthen media accountability and reaffirm the governments commitment to a free, fair and responsible press, he said.

articleTitle: Karnataka Public Service Commission job racket: ED arrests suspended KPSC chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar, another officer
articleFeaturedImageAlt: KPSC recruitment scam, Karnataka KPSC scam, KPSC chairman daughter recruitment, Suma Sahukar income certificate case, KPSC veterinary doctor paper leak .Karnataka veterinary recruitment scam. Shivashankarappa Sahukar CID probe, KPSC question paper leak, Karnataka High Court KPSC case, KPSC corruption allegations, Basavaraj Kannale KPSC scam, Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar arrest, 400 veterinary doctors recruitment scam, Karnataka government job scam, Express investigation, KPSC recruitment controversy
description: A Bengaluru Zone official of the ED confirmed the arrest of Sahukar and Geetha on Tuesday. “Their custody will be sought after production before a special judge,” the official said
body_raw: The Enforcement Directorate on Tuesday arrested suspended chairman of Karnataka Public Service Commission KPSC Shivashankarappa S Sahukar and a member of the Commission, B V Geetha, in connection with its money laundering probe into the recruitment of veterinary officers through KPSC. The arrests came in the wake of a fresh round of searches on Tuesday at a flat where Sahukar lived in Bengaluru, and statements given to the ED in recent weeks by arrested IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar and a middleman, Basavaraj Kannale, about corruption at the KPSC. A Bengaluru Zone official of the ED confirmed the arrest of Sahukar and Geetha on Tuesday. Their custody will be sought after production before a special judge, the official said The Karnataka High Court and a special court for CID cases had earlier rejected anticipatory bail pleas of the suspended KPSC chairman while pointing out that he was the custodian of the KPSC and hence responsible for all illegal activities that occurred under his watch. Sahukar was suspended by Karnataka Governor Thaawar Chand Gehlot on August 25 over illegal recruitment of his daughter to a state government job through KPSC. He was being investigated by the Karnataka Police in connection with multiple complaints of fraud in KPSC recruitment, but had not been arrested by the state police so far. Sahukar has been accused in two specific cases of fraud the KPSC recruitment of veterinary officers for 400 vacancies in the state and the recruitment of his daughter as an industrial officer on the basis of a fake income certificate. Sahukar and KPSC were at the centre of a series of investigative reports by The Indian Express on the recruitment scam during the tenure of Sahukar, who was picked by the BJP for the KPSC chairman post in 2019 and retained by the Congress, which came to power in Karnataka in 2023. The EDs arrest of Sahukar and B V Geetha comes following statements by Gangwar on KPSC officials using preliminary selection lists to extort aspirants during multiple job recruitments done by the Commission in the last two years. Arrested middleman Basavaraj Kannale also claimed to have given crores of Rupees to KPSC officials after collecting bribes from candidates for various job recruitments, said sources. According to the sources, Gangwar told the ED during questioning that when the 13 merit list for the veterinary doctors recruitment was published on February 4, 2026, KPSC officials, including Sahukar, Geetha, Shanta Hosmani, Elfreda D Silva, among others, approached him with candidate names to seek information about their prospects, and he divulged the information. Once the merit of a candidate was known, the concerned member, official or middleman contacted the candidate and negotiated the bribe amount the higher the candidates chance of selection, the higher the amount demanded, the ED informed a special court last week.

articleTitle: Karnataka Public Service Commission job racket: Flat purchased in name of family of arrested IAS officer under ED lens
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka Public Service Commission job racket, KPSC recruitment scam, Karnataka KPSC scam, KPSC chairman daughter recruitment, Suma Sahukar income certificate case, KPSC veterinary doctor paper leak .Karnataka veterinary recruitment scam. Shivashankarappa Sahukar CID probe, KPSC question paper leak, Karnataka High Court KPSC case, KPSC corruption allegations, Basavaraj Kannale KPSC scam, Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar arrest, 400 veterinary doctors recruitment scam, Karnataka government job scam, Express investigation, KPSC recruitment controversy
description: Gangwar, 41, who served as KPSC’s controller of examinations from January 2024 to March 2026, has been suspended by the Karnataka government.
body_raw: AN APARTMENT purchased in the name of family members of arrested IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar near Bengaluru airport has come under the scrutiny of the Enforcement Directorate, which is probing money laundering allegations in the recruitment for 400 veterinary officers through the Karnataka Public Service Commission KPSC. Gangwar, 41, who served as KPSCs controller of examinations from January 2024 to March 2026, has been suspended by the Karnataka government. He is alleged to have leaked the questions of the KPSC entrance exam for veterinary officers - held on January 8 and 9 this year - along with the answers to around 20 candidates who paid Rs 20 lakh to Rs 40 lakh through an arrested middleman, Basavaraj Kannale. During the investigation by the CID unit of the Karnataka police and the ED, Kannale, 36, allegedly revealed that Gangwar received around Rs 1.30 crore of Rs 1.52 crore taken from candidates as bribes for leaking the questions of the exams, said police sources. While the investigations have tracked Rs 52 lakh in bribes being funneled back to Gangwar through bank accounts of associates of the middleman, for purchase of expensive gold and diamond jewellery for a female friend of the officer from Bhima Jewellery showroom in Bengaluru, the remaining amount of bribes is still untraced, said the sources. The CID and the ED have indicated, following the arrest of Gangwar on August 29 and September 18, respectively, that some of the proceeds of the crime were used for the purchase of an apartment in the name of the brother of the officer at Godrej Royal Woods complex in the vicinity of the Bengaluru International Airport at Devanahalli. The IAS officers brother and family are unaware of the flat purchased in their name in Bengaluru. They never visited or used the property. It was used by the officer for parties and other activities since it provided privacy, said a police source familiar with the probe. The ED has indicated during court proceedings that the apartment at Devanahalli was bought with the proceeds of the KPSC recruitment racket. The funds were routed through Kannale and his associates for purchase of immovable property in the name of his brother, purchase of gold jewellery in the name of his friend, and payment of personal expenses, a special court for PMLA cases noted last week following an ED submission. Gangwar has reportedly told the ED that a part of the amount he received from Kannale for the KPSC veterinary officer job fraud was used to purchase a flat in the name of his brother, apart from the use of funds for buying gold jewellery for his female friend. The ED has also reported that an unexplained amount of Rs 26 lakh was deposited in cash between January 2025 and August 2025 in the bank accounts of a brother and sister-in-law of the IAS officer. The ED is also probing immovable assets acquired by the IAS officer - a semi-constructed house in Bareilly in 2025 for Rs 25 lakh and a real estate construction business launched by his older brothers in 2025 in UP.

articleTitle: Supreme Court agrees to hear Punjab government’s plea challenging HC’s order for CBI probe into corruption allegations
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Supreme Court, Supreme Court CBI probe into corruption allegations, CBI probe into Punjab corruption allegations, Punjab corruption allegations, Punjab AAP, Prevention of Money Laundering Act, Indian express news, current affairs
description: Senior Advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the state, mentioned the matter before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, seeking an urgent hearing on Tuesday itself. The CJI, however, said the court will consider listing the matter for hearing on Wednesday or Thursday.
body_raw: PUNJABS AAM Aadmi Party government on Tuesday approached the Supreme Court challenging the Punjab and Haryana High Court order directing the CBI to register a case and investigate allegations made by the Enforcement Directorate ED against people linked to Chief Minister Bhagwant Manns office. Senior Advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the state, mentioned the matter before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, seeking an urgent hearing on Tuesday itself. The CJI, however, said the court will consider listing the matter for hearing on Wednesday or Thursday. Singh explained that in the case, under 662 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, information was given by the Enforcement Directorate to the Punjab Director General of Police DGP towards the end of July. He said that in the Vijay Madanlal Chowdhary case, in which the SC had upheld EDs powers of arrest and seizure, it was made clear that police have to act only if there is a cognizable offence, and that too only in a situation where a large amount of cash is found and not in any routine instance. However, on October 5, the HC asked the CBI to register an FIR, he said. Seeking urgent listing, he said the CBI cant be directed to register an FIR. Singh said its a case regarding transfers, postings, etc. During election time, these kinds of cases are being trumped up. I have no problem if criminality is involved, he said. To a query as to what is the urgency, the senior counsel said There is urgency. Its a state going to polls. Its a clear case of the federal structure which is. being violated. The Punjab and Haryana HC on Monday directed the CBI to conduct a fair and transparent investigation into allegations raised in an ED communication to the police and submit its report within two months. The case is scheduled to come up before the High Court on December 7. The ED had sought registration of a case against Manns Officer on Special Duty Rajbir Singh Ghuman and his alleged associates Nitin Gohal and Bir Devinder. In its communication to the DGP under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act on July 30, the ED sought registration of a criminal case on the basis of material allegedly indicating cash-for-transfers and postings, influence over government policies and tenders, leakage of confidential government documents and other favours. According to the allegations cited by the ED, Ghuman, Gohal and Devinder had allegedly interfered in transfers and postings of government officials, government work and tender processes. The agency had also referred to material purportedly indicating attempts to influence postings, access confidential government documents and interfere in administrative approvals and other official processes. The High Court order came on a PIL filed by advocate Nikhil Saraf, based on the ED communication sent to the DGP. The court noted that the communication was received in the DGPs office on August 3 and was marked to the Punjab Bureau of Investigation, but no FIR had been registered even after two months. While directing the CBI to register a case, the HC division bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor said the allegations would have to be tested during investigation and trial.

articleTitle: Christa Pike is conscious and speaking after Tennessee failed execution, her attorneys say
articleFeaturedImageAlt: christa pike, Tennessee, world, christa pike alive, christa pike execution, christa pike survives, christa pike awake, Indian express news, current affairs
description: Her attorneys said they are grateful for the first responders and the medical team at the hospital “who treated Christa like a human and have provided exceptional care to her.”
body_raw: Yuvraj Manchanda murder, Christa Pike, a Tennessee inmate who survived Tennessees attempt to execute her, is awake and speaking as she receives treatment at a hospital, her attorneys said Tuesday. Against all odds, Christa Pike is conscious, speaking, and continues to receive critical medical care. Despite the severe damage she endured to her arms, she is still handcuffed and shackled to the bed. Her recovery is medically unprecedented. Her prognosis remains unclear but, at a minimum, we expect a long recovery, attorneys for Pike said in a statement. Her attorneys said they are grateful for the first responders and the medical team at the hospital who treated Christa like a human and have provided exceptional care to her. The statement was the first indication that Pike has improved since an ambulance carried her away from a Nashville prison last Wednesday. A spokeswoman for the Tennessee Department of Correction said she could provide no information other than that Pike remained hospitalized Tuesday. Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital as they attempted to put her to death for the 1995 beating and stabbing death of classmate Colleen Slemmer. The lethal injection drug didnt kill her, but her lawyers said her arms were left burned and blistered. Dr. Joel Zivot, a professor of anesthesiology and surgery in Atlanta who consulted as an expert for Pikes legal team, said the development bodes well for a good recovery. But, he added, it could be weeks or months before anyone knows exactly what her recovery might look like, and whether her competency could be restored to a level that might enable the state to try again to execute her.

articleTitle: Woman held for abducting homeless infant, planned to sell baby to UP man for Rs 6 lakh: Ahmedabad Police
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Woman held for abducting homeless infant, Woman arrested for abducting homeless infant, abducting homeless infant, homeless infant abduction, Ahmedabad news, Gujarat news, Indian express, current affairs
description: Although Parmar intended to hand over the abducted child to another individual, they panicked, abandoned the infant in the New Ranip area and attempted to flee. The child was soon reunited with the relieved parents.
body_raw: AT 315 am on October 2, a homeless couple reached Sabarmati railway station in Ahmedabad, requesting the police to find their 37-day-old child who was allegedly abducted from their sleeping spot on a footpath outside Ahvadiya lake in the citys New Ranip area. Several teams of the local police, including the crime branch, were coordinated, and the first step of investigation, checking the CCTV footage, showed a female suspect, now identified as Jinal Govind Parmar 21, abducting the child from its bed. Checkpoints were established at all railway stations, bus terminals and the airport to apprehend her. Although Parmar intended to hand over the abducted child to another individual, they panicked, abandoned the infant in the New Ranip area and attempted to flee. The child was soon reunited with the relieved parents. Once the child was identified, we tracked the movements of the female accused and apprehended her, said Ahmedabad City Commissioner of Police Anupam Singh Gahlaut at a press conference on Tuesday. Jinal Parmar, a resident of Wadhwan, Surendranagar, was apprehended near Sabarmati Railway Station and subjected to detailed interrogation. Following the emergence of preliminary facts confirming her involvement, legal action was taken against her she was handed over to the Sabarmati Police Station and scheduled to be produced before the local court, said a statement from the Crime Branch. Plot Unravels From Kidnapping to Trafficking Police said, Interrogation of the arrested female accused revealed that two individuals from Uttar Pradesh, who were juveniles in conflict with the law, had assisted in the crime. Before they could flee back to their hometown in Uttar Pradesh, the Crime Branch team, acting on the basis of photographs found on the female accuseds mobile phone, conducted searches at bus and railway stations, promptly apprehended both juveniles, and handed them over to the Sabarmati Police Station. The police also claimed that Jinal Parmar told them that an individual from Uttar Pradesh, a former colleague from a quick commerce platform, lured her with a financial reward of Rs 6 lakh to illegally arrange for a child under the age of 1 years, on behalf of a person named Bhuvaneshwar alias Bhanu. She had thus allegedly executed the crime with the help of the two juveniles in conflict with the law. To carry out the child abduction, the arrested female accused had initially conducted reconnaissance in the New Ranip area and its surroundings, as well as in the vicinity of Sola Civil Hospital, said the police. The Source of the Demand Since the man who has contacted Jinal Parmar and the man who had contacted him in turn, were both located in Uttar Pradesh, a Crime Branch team was dispatched to apprehend them. The team successfully arrested the accused-identified as Bhuvaneshwar alias Bhanu Jatav a resident of Badaun currently residing in Noida - who was involved in the childs abduction and had offered Rs 6 lakh for the child. Interrogation is underway to trace the prime conspirators, said the police.

body_raw: A woman from Nagaland was allegedly harassed and forcibly pulled towards a Mercedes car by three men in the parking lot of a five-star hotel in Chanakyapuri early Sunday. When her friends intervened, the men allegedly assaulted them with hockey sticks and iron rods, police said. The incident took place around 3.30 am Sunday, police said. According to a complaint filed by the woman, she had visited the hotel with friends. While they were leaving, three men, who were travelling in a white Mercedes, allegedly approached them, tried to stop the woman and attempted to pull her into the vehicle. Police said the womans friends intervened, following which the accused allegedly attacked them with hockey sticks and iron rods. One of the friends suffered injuries to his teeth., an officer said. The accused allegedly fled from the spot in their car after police reached the location. The complainant had noted down the cars registration number, which helped investigators trace the men, police said. The three accused were booked at Chanakyapuri police station. The woman was taken to RML Hospital, where she underwent a medical examination. Police said the case was registered on the basis of her complaint and the medical report. Police are examining CCTV camera footage from the hotel and other evidence to establish the sequence of events. articleTitle: Tamil Nadu Assembly privilege case: Supreme Court closes proceedings; keeps questions of law open
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Tamil Nadu Assembly privilege case, TN Assembly privilege case, Supreme Court, Supreme Court Tamil Nadu Assembly privilege case, Tamil Nadu Assembly privilege case proceedings closed, Indian express news, current affairs
description: Disposing of the matter as having become infructuous, the bench, however, said that the questions of law would remain open to be decided in appropriate proceedings in the future.
body_raw: WITH THE 2003 Tamil Nadu case that triggered a reference to its seven-judge bench on the question of legislative privileges vis-a-vis free speech having been withdrawn, the Supreme Court on Tuesday closed proceedings in the matter, while leaving the question of law open to be decided on a future occasion. The bench presided by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant noted that the 2003 resolution of the Tamil Nadu Assembly, which formed the basis of the reference, was withdrawn by the Assembly in 2004. The bench, also comprising Justices Aravind Kumar, P K Mishra, Joymalya Bagchi, Vipul Pancholi, Shree Chandrashekhar and V Mohana, said that the July 30, 2004 Assembly resolution withdrawing the earlier resolution of November 7, 2003 was not specifically brought to the notice of this Court. It also escaped notice when it made the reference to the seven-judge bench. Disposing of the matter as having become infructuous, the bench, however, said that the questions of law would remain open to be decided in appropriate proceedings in the future. The sequence of events dates back to a 2003 article in the The Hindu newspaper, criticising the then CM J Jayalalithaa and her government. Taking offence, the Assembly concluded that it amounted to a breach of privilege of the House. Soon after the November 7, 2003, resolution, police arrested The Hindu Editor N Ravi, Executive Editor Malini Parthasarathy, Bureau Chief V Jayant, Special Correspondent Radha Venkatesan and Publisher S Rangarajan. The journalists challenged this before the Supreme Court, which stayed the arrest on November 10, 2003. But with the matter raising significant constitutional questions of the privilege of the House vis-a-vis right to free speech, the top court in December 2003 referred it to a five-judge bench. The five-judge bench in turn referred it to a seven-judge bench, noting that there were conflicting views on the issue.

body_raw: Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and other senior Election Commission officials have postponed their two-day visit to Chhattisgarh, scheduled for October 7 and 8. Kumar was scheduled to visit the popular Danteshwari Mata temple in Dantewada district, the Chitrakoot waterfall in Bastar, and the Bhoramdev temple in Kawardha district. As per a letter issued Tuesday by the office of the Chief Electoral Officer in Chhattisgarh, Kumar had been declared a State Guest for the duration of his visit, and instructions had been issued to make the necessary protocol arrangements for him. Stating that the visit has now been postponed, the letter read, It is informed that the Election Commission has postponed the Chhattisgarh visit programme of Shri Gyanesh Kumar, Honble Chief Election Commissioner, and other senior officials of the Commission, due to unavoidable reasons. The revised date of the visit will be communicated separately once it is received from the Commission. The rescheduling of his visit comes after the intense standoff between Opposition leaders and the police in Delhi. The day-long standoff followed the detention of Congress MPs Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi late on Tuesday. They were later released. articleTitle: ‘Fake PCS officer’ bride dupes AAP leader in Punjab; 6 booked
articleFeaturedImageAlt: aap leader wife
description: Couple got married in February. 6 months on, he alleges that his wife lied to him about being a PCS officer and also has a child from a previous marriage
body_raw: An Aam Aadmi Party AAP leader from Punjabs Fatehgarh Sahib district was allegedly duped by his wife, whom he married in February after she introduced herself as a Punjab Civil Services PCS officer posted in Jalandhar. However, over six months after their wedding, the AAP leader claimed in a police complaint that his wife was not a PCS officer and that she had lied to him. He alleged that his wife lied about her age, and that she has a teenage son from her previous marriage. The complainant, AAP leader Amrinder Singh, 33, from Mandofal village, alleged, She falsely claimed that she was posted as an ADC in Mohali. She had created a fake Instagram ID, introducing herself as a PCS officer, with the caption Serving the nation is not a post, its a purpose. Amrinder, an advocate by profession, is the market committee chairman of Sirhind and zila parishad member of Fatehgarh Sahib. He has served the AAP, Punjab, as a joint secretary and was among the founding members of the AAP in Fatehgarh Sahib. Based on his complaint, police on Monday booked Amrinders Manwinder Kaur and five other members of her family, including brother Tarlochan Singh, mother Varinderjit Kaur, cousin Narinder Singh, sister-in-law Rupinder Kaur Tarlochans wife and former sarpanch Surinder Singh Rana - residents of Sur Singh village in Tarn Taran district - under sections 318 4 cheating, 336 3 forgery, 338 forgery of valuable security, 61 2 criminal conspiracy and 340 2 using a forged document of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita BNS at the Fatehgarh Sahib police station. According to the FIR, Amrinder, in his statement, told police that both families had met at Hansali Sahib, and their wedding was fixed. He said that Manwinder and her family claimed that she was a PCS officer, with a posting in Jalandhar. He said that the bride had claimed that she was posted as PCS executive in Jalandhar. He further said that Manwinder had also claimed that her parents had died, but later he got to know that her mother was alive. Amrinder said that Manwinders family had claimed that she was 34 years old, and that their wedding was solemnised at Hansali Sahib on February 10. According to the FIR, Amrinder said that after the wedding, Manwinder would often go out, claiming that she was going to her duty. Amrinder said, When I asked her about her current posting, she said that she was posted as the Additional Deputy Commissioner in Mohali, but had been suspended due to some reasons. When I asked her to provide more details so that I could help her. I asked Manwinder to provide me with a copy of her suspension order, but she did not, Amrinder said, alleging On August 27, she left the house with 14 tolas of gold and Rs 1 lakh in cash. He further said, When I repeatedly asked her for a copy of the suspension order, she sent me a document on WhatsApp in September. According to the document, she was posted as the ADC, Mohali, in April 2022. However, the document was found to be forged later. Amrinder said that after getting suspicious, he started his investigation and found that Manwinder had never cleared the PCS, nor was she ever posted as an ADC in Mohali or Jalandhar. I found that Manwinder was 46 years old and not 34, and that she was not unmarried as claimed. Manwinder has an 18-year-old son, whom she hid. Fatehgarh SSP Shubham Aggarwal said, A probe has been initiated. The opposite party will be called to record their statement. Further proceedings will be done accordingly. The complainants allegations are yet to be verified. Amrinder did not respond to repeated calls and messages. An AAP worker from Fatehgarh Sahib said, We had attended their wedding Amrinder was really happy. Its shocking that it ended this way.

articleTitle: Buying medicines at a UP hospital? The price will be on display from Nov 1
articleFeaturedImageAlt: UP government, UP government hospital pharmacies, UP government hospital pharmacies display prices of medicines, prices of medicines, Uttar Pradesh Food Safety and Drug Administration (UPFSDA), Lucknow news, Uttar pradesh news, Indian express, Current affairs
description: The move is aimed at improving price transparency, particularly for patients buying medicines from hospital pharmacies where they may have limited alternatives
body_raw: The Uttar Pradesh Food Safety and Drug Administration UPFSDA has directed pharmacies operating from hospitals across the state to display price lists based on the actual procurement and sale rates of medicines from November 1. This comes after an inspection by the Uttar Pradesh Food Safety and Drug Administration UPFSDA found a staggering gap between the procurement prices of medicines and the maximum retail prices MRPs printed on their packs, with the MRP of some drugs found to be several times higher - as high as 67 times-than the price at which hospitals procure them. The department has also directed all retail pharmacies to create public websites displaying their licence number, appointed pharmacist, licensed premises and stock details. The information will have to be updated on weekly basis, it is learnt. The move is aimed at improving price transparency, particularly for patients buying medicines from hospital pharmacies where they may have limited alternatives, officials said. The department has pointed to the cost-plus model followed in some government medical colleges for expensive medicines, including cancer drugs, high-end antibiotics and costly injections. Under this model, the price charged to patients is linked to the hospitals actual procurement cost rather than simply the printed MRP. Seeks action against drug overpricing The UPFSDA also sought action by the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority NPPA on drug pricing after inspections found that patients at some hospitals were being charged up to 67 times the procurement price of medicines. The department has written to the NPPA, seeking a review of drug trade margins, MRP fixation and price controls on high-margin medicines and medical devices. The findings followed inspections of more than 200 pharmacies in 22 medical colleges and 30 government and private hospitals across the state. The UPFSDA said the wide gap was found between the price to retailer PTR paid by hospitals and the price ultimately charged from patients. It argued that patients should receive the benefit of the high discounts the hospitals often get from manufacturers and suppliers. Under the present system, the MRP is printed on the package while institutional purchases are often negotiated on the basis of the highest discount. This could leave patients unaware of the actual procurement cost, reads the letter written by UPFSDA Commissioner and Secretary Roshan Jacob. The UPFSDA also flagged instances where medicines of the same brand and manufacturer carried different MRPs for different institutional supplies. It has raised concerns over contract-manufactured brands supplied to hospitals that may not be readily available in the general retail market. The UPFSDA has asked the NPPA to consider capping trade margins on high-MRP medicines and medical devices after reviewing margins across the supply chain. It has also sought a rationalised system for fixing MRPs that factors in manufacturing costs and permissible post-manufacturing expenses. The department has further suggested bringing high-margin medicines supplied to hospitals under the price-control framework of DPCO-2013. It has also sought stronger enforcement of DPCO provisions, including consideration of bringing violations within the ambit of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act. The department argued that the issue is not merely about pharmacy margins but also about transparency in the drug supply chain and ensuring that the benefit of institutional procurement reaches patients.

articleTitle: Congress’s Satej Patil says BJP deliberately fielded his niece from Pune MLC seat: ‘Will ensure victory of  MVA candidate’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Satej Patil, Smita Jadhav, Congress MLC Satej Patil, Pune MLC, State Legislative Council polls, Pune MLC seat, Pune news, Pune, Maharashtra news, Indian express, current affairs
description: Smita Jadhav of BJP will face challenge from Harshada Deshmukh of NCP(SP) in the Pune Graduates constituency.
body_raw: Congress MLC Satej Patil Tuesday said that the BJP fielded his niece Smita Jadhav from Pune Graduates constituency for State Legislative Council polls deliberately to out him in a bind. If the BJP and the Chief Minister have so much affection for the Jadhav family, they should have appointed my niece Smita Jadhav directly as an MLC through the Governors quota. But they didnt. Instead they fielded her from Pune seat to put me in a bind, Patil told The Indian Express. The Congress leader, however, said the nomination of his niece Smita Jadhav by BJP wont change his political stand. Though BJP has deliberately played the ploy, it will not change my political stand. My conviction is very strong. I have my political career to look after. I will campaign hard and ensure victory of the Maha Vikas Aghadi candidate, he said. Smita Jadhav of BJP will face challenge from Harshada Deshmukh of NCPSP in the Pune Graduates constituency. Smita Jadhav is the daughter of P D Patil, chancellor of Dr D Y Patil Vidyapeeth, Pimpri and wife of Yogesh Jadhav, director of Pudhari. Harshada Deshmukh is the daughter of Prabhakar Deshmukh, former Pune divisional commissioner. After she was nominated as the candidate by BJP, Smita Jadhav had said that she has the blessings of her uncle. To this, Patil said, A maternal uncle looking out for his niece is a family bond. However, political positions and personal relationships are distinct. Besides, the MVA has renominated Jayant Asgaonkar from the Teachers constituency in Pune. Patil said that the MVA will fight this election with full force without any internal rift and win both seats. If anyone from our party or other constituent parties is upset or has filed a nomination, we will have a constructive discussion with them and request them to withdraw their nomination, he said. Congress city president Prashant Jagtap said the MVA is not facing any rebellion in both the seats in Pune. The Congress has renominated Asgaonkar from Teachers constituency and we are confident of his victory, he said. Meanwhile, Patil also spoke about the speculations surrounding Kolhapurs Gokul Dairy election. News claiming the Gokul election would be held unopposed due to the drought was intentionally leaked. If you argue for an unopposed Gokul election because of drought, then why are you conducting the Legislative Council and District Central Cooperative Bank elections?, he asked.

articleTitle: Congestion ahead: Accurate Google Maps update on Barapullah traffic expected soon
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Google Maps, Google maps app, Google Maps accurate traffic update on Barahpullah, Google maps app accurate traffic update on Barahpullah, Google Maps accurate traffic update, Google maps app accurate traffic update, Delhi Traffic Police, delhi news, India news, Indian express, current affairs
description: Police also examining the possibility of regulating or diverting traffic towards NH-24, wherever feasible
body_raw: The Delhi Traffic Police is coordinating with Google Maps to ensure that the traffic situation on the newly opened Barapullah Phase-III corridor is accurately reflected on the app, officers said on Tuesday. This comes a day after the Delhi Traffic Police on Monday said in a post on X that with the app showing the route as relatively clear, commuters are being directed towards the already congested stretch.A drone survey had identified a major bottleneck at the Sundial Park merger near Sarai Kale Khan where lanes merge into the existing Barapullah corridor. Traffic Police officers said this is adding to the traffic load as vehicles that would otherwise use DND or NH-24 turns towards the new corridor, choking it further. The newly opened corridor is attracting substantial traffic that would otherwise use NH-24 and DND, thereby increasing the traffic load, an official said. The Traffic Police said the issue on the navigation app will be sorted out in a few days. PWD flags misinformation Public Works Department PWD officials have also blamed Google Maps for feeding misinformation to commuters, exacerbating the lockjam. There is some misinformation on Google Maps apparently, it is not updating real-time traffic information for commuters to properly navigate, causing more congestion on the stretch, PTI quoted an official as having said. Officials also said that despite a recent meeting with the Traffic Police and the National Highways Authority of India NHAI, no solution has been reached so far. Appropriate traffic-control measures and signals at suitable merging points may also be considered to regulate the inflow of vehicles and prevent excessive accumulation, Traffic Police officers said. The Traffic Police is also examining the possibility of regulating or diverting traffic towards NH-24, wherever feasible. Officers, meanwhile, also pointed to a traffic signal on the corridor that has no electricity connection yet, stating that once functional, it is expected to help regulate traffic entering the corridor. A request for an electricity connection has been sent to the BSES, the official said. Barapullah Phase-III flyover was inaugurated on September 29 and opened to commuters on September 30. The corridor has since witnessed heavy traffic and congestion. Senior Traffic Police personnel and PWD officials had on October 1 conducted a joint aerial inspection using drones. It was attended by Joint Commissioner of Police Traffic Sanjay Tyagi, Additional Commissioner of Police Traffic Dinesh Kumar Gupta and Deputy Commissioner of Police Southern Range Sandeep Gupta. The survey identified a sharp, almost rectangular geometry at the merger, resulting in an abrupt convergence of traffic and a bottleneck. There is a significant mismatch in lane capacity at the merging point. Multiple streams of traffic are converging towards the existing Barapullah corridor, which has comparatively limited lane capacity, an official had said. A senior traffic police officer said that they had asked the PWD to work on the curvature near Sundial park patch of the Barapullah flyover. The Traffic Police said it was closely monitoring the corridor and coordinating with PWD and other agencies to address the ongoing issues. Commuters have been advised to follow traffic advisories and directions of traffic police personnel and use alternate routes wherever advised. With PTI inputs
