articleTitle: Police issue notices to MPSC protesters, coaching classes; Commissioner calls protest ‘illegal’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: MPSC paper leak, MPSC protests, MPSC protests intensify, MPSC chairman Vivek Bhimanwar, Pune news, Pune, Maharashtra news, Indian express, current affairs
description: Protest enters Day 6, AAP's Sanjay Singh joins protesters
body_raw: Terming the ongoing protest in Pune over the MPSC paper leak illegal, Police Commissioner Amitesh Kumar said that police issued over 70 notices to protesters, coaching classes, and Telegram channels in connection with the protest. The notices were issued two to three days ago, he added. The protest is illegal, there is no permission to do it. It is causing inconvenience to the general commuters and the leaders are coming and giving provocative speeches inciting students. This is not proper and not within the legal framework. So please withdraw from the agitation is what we have said in the notices, Kumar told The Indian Express. On the future course of action of the police and whether the protesters had been given any time period to withdraw the protest, Kumar said, Time period, not really. But we are keeping a close watch on the developments and we have been exercising extreme tact and patience so as to not let a conflict situation happen. We are hoping that the agitating students realise that they are doing something illegal and in contravention of rules and regulations. But well intervene appropriately as and when required. Leaders including Rohit Pawar, who has been leading the protest, had not been issued any notice, the commissioner added. He said that no FIRs had been filed, other than an FIR filed by a journalist who was allegedly attacked by a person at the protest. The protest demanding resignation of Maharashtra Public Service Commission MPSC chairperson Vivek Bhimanwar continued for its sixth day on Tuesday. Students gathered at the SM Joshi bridge in large numbers at night as various political leaders addressed them. Earlier in the day, the protesters carried out a symbolic last rites ceremony targeting the MPSC Chairman. Aam Aadmi Party MP Sanjay Singh joined the protesters on Tuesday. I have been told that along with MPSC, papers of talati, drugs inspector, health recruitment, PMC, BMC, teacher recruitment, MMRDA, and MH-CET, all papers have been leaked. And the paper leak that got the whole country on the ground, NEET paper was also leaked. This is a paper leak government, Sanjay Singh alleged. He added, When I asked why is Vivek Bhimanwar MPSC chairperson not resigning, I was told that Bhimanwar and Devendra Fadnavis jodi is like Jai and Veeru. There is a lot of love between them. And he is not ready to take his resignation. Beware of the poision of Hindu-Muslim that they try to fill in your brain during elections. And remember, those who could not be of God Ram referring to the Ram Mandir donation theft, they can never be yours either, said Singh. The protesters are occupying the area near SM Joshi bridge. Two other protest spots have also emerged at Lal Bahadur Shastri Road, and Alka Talkies chowk, with all groups having different demands. Protesters have been demanding the resignation of the MPSC chairperson over the leak of the Drug Inspector examination held in March this year.

articleTitle: Shreyas Iyer finds perfect timing for his first T20I century
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shreyas Iyer couldn't have timed his maiden T20I ton better. (Express photo by Vishal Srivastav)
description: India were in trouble at 35/2 when the skipper came to bat, but with an unbeaten 102 from 43 balls, he ensured they would be only one winner
body_raw: The last time Shreyas Iyer scored a T20I half-century before Tuesday was nearly three months ago - an unbeaten 80 against England at Bristol. Since then, he had not crossed 30 in 10 matches, with Indias top three often taking the pressure off him. The script changed dramatically at the Ekana Stadium in Lucknow. Chasing 172, Iyer walked in with India 35 India had lost both openers inside the first 21 balls. Roston Chase and Akeal Hosein had found early rhythm with the ball. Iyer absorbed the early pressure before turning the game decisively in Indias favour. The opening came in the sixth over. Shamar Joseph needed to build on the spinners start. Instead, he gave Iyer and India a release. He conceded 12 runs as Iyer went aerial over cover before repeating the treatment against Romario Shepherd. The West Indies kept bowling outside off, but on a pitch offering little movement, Iyer was able to free his arms and find the gaps. AS IT HAPPENED  INDIA VS WEST INDIES 1ST T20I HIGHLIGHTS It forced the bowlers to go short. That had been regarded as a weakness in Iyers game. On Tuesday, he repeatedly brought out the pull against the rising delivery and found success. He reached his fifty in 28 balls, but the acceleration was only beginning. After seeing off the pacers, Iyer turned his attention to spin. Hosein was brought back in the 13th over and Iyer gave himself room before launching him over extra cover. The next over brought an assault on Forde, as Iyer struck two sixes before pulling another delivery over the boundary. He was given a reprieve when Joseph could not hold on to a miscued shot towards long-on. He reached his maiden T20I hundred with a six before India completed the chase in just 14.4 overs. Kishans role At the other end, Ishan Kishan found himself playing a different role. Walking in at No.3, he did not try to match Iyers aggression. Instead, he played the perfect supporting act, rotating the strike and waiting for opportunities to attack. His first boundary came when he went back to a slightly short delivery from Chase and whipped it through the leg side. Against Joseph, he then found the boundary through cover before taking advantage of another hit-me delivery from the pacer. He pulled Shepherd for a boundary and later cut Hosein through the off side, while his running kept the chase moving. There was one moment of drama when Kishan miscued a full toss towards deep cover. Forde appeared to have taken the catch, but the TV umpire ruled that the ball had touched the ground. By then, however, the partnership had taken complete control. Kishan stayed unbeaten as he and Iyer added 137 for the third wicket, allowing India to race home with 32 balls to spare. Earlier, Indias spin trio did the heavy lifting after the West Indies threatened to set a daunting score in good batting conditions. After Arshdeep Singh and Mayank Yadav failed to hit their straps early, Axar Patel, Kuldeep Yadav and Naman Dhir combined to take seven wickets for 90 runs, recovering from a middle-overs assault by Shai Hope and Sherfane Rutherford to keep the total manageable. After Shimron Hetmyer was run out, Axar dismissed Rovman Powell for nought to leave the West Indies 443 after six overs. But Hope and Rutherford then shifted the momentum, taking on Kuldeep and forcing Iyer to look elsewhere. Kuldeep, playing his first T20I since February, conceded 24 in his first two overs as Rutherford lofted him over cover and Hope swept him over wide long-on. Iyer brought him back after Hopes dismissal at 107 Then came the turnaround. Kuldeep found his lengths and Roston Chase fell lbw, going back to a delivery he should have played forward to. His final two overs cost only nine runs and brought two wickets, including Matthew Forde. Dhir, meanwhile, made an immediate impact on debut. After being handed the ball, he dismissed Hope for 52 before returning to remove Romario Shepherd and Shamar Springer. His three wickets gave India the control they needed. Axars miserly spell, Kuldeeps comeback and Dhirs three wickets ensured India recovered despite the pacers indiscipline. The late 36-run stand between Rutherford and Akeal Hosein gave the West Indies something to defend, but the spinners had already done enough to keep the target within reach. Brief Scores West Indies 171 all out in 19.1 overs Sherfane Rutherford 56, Shai Hope 52 Naman Dhir 331, Axar Patel 226, Kuldeep Yadav 233 lost to India 1722 in 14.4 overs Shreyas Iyer 102 not out, Ishan Kishan 37 by 8 wickets.

articleTitle: Anirudh Thapa scores but Uruguay run away 6-1 winners in friendly against India
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Anirudh
description: Maxi Araujo scores a brace as two-time world champions show more ruthlessness than Brazil on Saturday
body_raw: At around the 22nd minute, Anirudh Thapa found himself in the Uruguay penalty box. His eyes suddenly lit up. Goalkeeper Thaigo Cardozo had spilled a Ryan Williams shot and the ball was bobbing on the ground. Its almost as if time stood still. And sped up in real time as Thapa pounced, saw the resignation in Cardozos eyes and put the ball in the Uruguay net. The Salt Lake Stadium exploded. 138th-ranked India had pulled one out of the hat. The goal mattered little in the context of the 1-6 rout at the hands of the South Americans. But when the final whistle blew, 37,000 spectators seemed content as Thapas goal had allowed them to dream bigger for a while. Ahead of the clash, India coach Khalid Jamil and defender Akash Mishra had stressed on maintaining focus and not conceding early against the 20th-ranked team. With India managing to restrict Brazil in the initial stages, a Uruguay team which had just one win in their last nine international fixtures didnt seem an insurmountable barrier. Especially when they were playing without their star player Federico Valverde, ruled out due to injury. While the hosts couldnt prevent an early goal after Pramveer Singhs errant challenge resulted in a penalty that Darwin Nunez duly converted in the 10th minute, it prompted them into action as India managed to level matters through Thapa. Soon after, inclement weather and lightning forced the match to be stopped for around 35 minutes. That interruption hurt Indias cause as Uruguay struck right after when a low cross by Nahitan Nandez was met by Maxi Araujo and stroked into the India net in the 28th minute. Uruguay had more chances to surge ahead but Araujo shot one over the bar before Nunez, who was through one-on-one with goalkeeper Gurpreet Singh Sandhu, had his attempted chip blocked. That must have felt good for the custodian after his two individual errors led to goals for Brazil on Saturday. India brought on Sahal Abdul Samad and Bijoy Varghese in the second half while Uruguay added some more steel to their midfield and defence with Lucas Torreira and Guillermo Varela. It made a difference straight away as Torreiras ball was nodded into Rodrigo Zalazars path, who slammed one into the bottom corner to make it 3-1 in the 53rd minute. The proverbial floodgates had opened and Uruguay slotted in another in the 59th minute when Araujo caught Abhishek Singh Tekcham flat-footed. Substitute Juan Manuel Sanabria finished calmly after a superb transitional play to make it 5-1 in the 70th. That was followed by a well-placed goal by Rodrigo Aguirre in the 87th minute as Uruguay showed a more ruthless streak than Brazil managed against the Blue Tigers. Indias best chances in the second half came from Mohammed Sanan, whose check-back left Torreira in his wake but the shot was saved by Cardozo, before the Uruguay keeper was called to action once again when he saved Williams first-time volley.

articleTitle: How to test whether a compostable bag breaks down at home
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Consumers should check whether a compostable bag is certified for home or industrial composting.
description: Not every compostable bag can break down in a home compost bin. Here's how to check the certification, test the bag and dispose of it correctly.
body_raw: Compostable bags appear to be more environmentally friendly than plastic bags. But compostable doesnt necessarily mean something breaks down quickly in a home compost pile. Decomposition conditions may depend heavily on the material and the products certification. Test to ensure the bag is compostable at home Not all compostable bags decompose properly at home. Some bags need high-temperature, commercial-scale operations to break down properly. So consumers should look for the right certification on a product for use in their compost bin. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Maninder Singh Nayyar, Founder  CEO, CEF Group, suggests an experiment that can help consumers determine whether bags work as expected in their compost. First, cut a piece of the bag, note its size and shape, and bury it about 10 to 15 cm deep in a well-aerated compost bin. The compost should include a combination of wet green stuff, like fruit and vegetable waste, and dry brown stuff, like leaves and shredded cardboard. It should remain damp but not soggy. Inspect the pile every four weeks and keep notes on changes. A truly compostable material should show signs of breaking down under proper conditions over time, which can take several months and depends on climate and season. Comparing it to a conventional plastic bag could help, as long as neither sample is used to make compost for food later. Consumers need to know that breaking into pieces does not equate to full biodegradation. If the bag doesnt fully decompose within the time specified by the manufacturer, it may require industrial composting. Consumers must dispose of the bags as required locally and not put them in recycling bins, as they may contaminate regular plastics. What consumers need to ensure Dr Sujit Paul, Group CEO of Zota Healthcare Ltd Davaindia, says consumers need to check the packaging carefully. Pay attention to the clear information on whether the product is home compostable or industrially compostable, instead of the labels of eco-friendly or biodegradable. Any certification testing details that may be available can also give added assurance about the claims, he adds. Dr Sujit also advises to follow manufacturers instructions for disposal, as well. A bin meant to be used for industrial composting may be aggressively managed with controlled temperatures, humidity and microbial environment which would not exist within a typical home compost pile, he says. If consumers know they should opt for certified products and know what to do with them no matter which they pick, they can make more informed environmental choices. articleTitle: Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi detained after hours-long anti-CEC protest, released later
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were detained by Delhi Police on Tuesday evening
description: INDIA bloc MPs alleged 'vote chori', and demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
body_raw: Led by Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, leaders of INDIA bloc Tuesday stepped up their attack on the Chief Election Commissioner, demanding his resignation before they were detained late in the evening after staging a protest for hours near the Election Commission office in the heart of New Delhi. The leaders were released later in the night. Parliament Street shut down as Gandhi and others tried to march towards the EC office with their supporters, and climbed atop police barricades, before finding their way into the Akashvani Bhavan premises. Through much of the day, Gandhi and Vadra were holed up inside the AIR premises, demanding they be allowed to meet the CEC. They were joined by SPs Akhilesh Yadav, TMCs Abhishek Banerjee and Derek OBrien, and CPIMs John Brittas. All I want to do is meet the Chief Election Commissioner and tell him that he has done vote chori. I can continue to sit here. I am comfortable here. If they dont want us to sit here, give us some other site, Gandhi said. The march was the latest in a series of protests to press for CEC Gyanesh Kumars resignation in the wake of a report in The Indian Express that the two Election Commissioners had objected on record 14 times in 10 months to steps taken by the Commission under the CEC, from keeping them in the dark to adding new voters and deleting names. Targeting the Prime Minister, Union Home Minister and the RSS chief, Gandhi alleged that the country had been hijacked with the vote chori. What has been done to our country is treason. Nobody is going to escape, he said. The day-long protest began with the march being stopped soon after it started from Parliament House around 10 am, following which the opposition MPs sat on the street outside Akashvani Bhavan, very close to the EC office. As MPs were being detained, Gandhi spoke to his sister seated inside one of the buses and both went inside the Akashvani Bhavan, taking all by surprise. Besides the Gandhi siblings, the Congress leaders who joined them inside the AIR premises included Deepender Hooda, Charanjit Singh Channi, Praniti Shinde, K C Venugopal and Pawan Khera. Several MPs returned to the protest site after being released from detention. In a post on X, Gandhi said, Gyanesh its done bro. Time to resign. MPs from the BJD, which has not been part of the INDIA bloc, also joined the march. DMK and AAP leaders stayed away from the protest.

articleTitle: Army Subedar faces court martial for cheating civilians of Rs 51.44 lakh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: court martial case
description: The Junior Commissioned Officer (JCO) faces six charges of cheating, framed under Section 69 of the Army Act.
body_raw: A Subedar of the Corps of Electronics and Mechanical Engineers EME in the Indian Army will be facing a General Court Martial for allegedly cheating several civilians of about Rs 51.44 lakh, according to a charge sheet served on him in September. The Junior Commissioned Officer JCO, who was serving as a Subedar Clerk Inventory Management with 304 Field Workshop Company of 671 EME Battalion, attached to Headquarters 106 Infantry Brigade, faces six charges of cheating. All six charges have been framed under Section 69 of the Army Act for committing a civil offence - cheating. The charge sheet says the alleged offences came to the notice of the competent authority on September 28, 2024. At the time of the alleged offences, the Subedar was performing duties as Section In-charge, Technical Store Section, 304 Field Workshop Company. According to the particulars of the charges, the Subedar allegedly received Rs 3 lakh at field between April and May 2023 and Rs 15 lakh at Guwahati in May 2023. He is further accused of receiving Rs 5.60 lakh between August and December 2023 and Rs 10.13 lakh between September and December 2023. The remaining allegations involve receipt of Rs 3.50 lakh between August and September 2023 and Rs 14.19 lakh between December 2023 and February 2024. Directions for his trial by General Court Martial have been endorsed by Major General NS Sohal, General Officer Commanding, 71 Infantry Division. The case comes amid a series of recent court martial proceedings involving allegations of financial irregularities in the Army. In October 2025, a General Court Martial at Tibri Military Station near Gurdaspur sentenced an Army Medical Corps Subedar to seven years rigorous imprisonment and dismissal from service after finding him guilty on six charges. Three charges were under the Prevention of Corruption Act relating to disproportionate assets and three under Section 63 of the Army Act. A search had recovered Rs 8 lakh from his car and Rs 7.83 lakh from his house. Scrutiny of bank accounts also showed deposits of Rs 27.11 lakh in his account and Rs 44.27 lakh in his wifes account during his posting at a military hospital in Amritsar. Earlier that month, a General Court Martial at Fatehgarh sentenced Lieutenant Colonel Avinash Gupta of the Army Service Corps to two years rigorous imprisonment and cashiering. He was convicted on three charges under Section 52f of the Army Act relating to fraudulent transactions, including alleged misuse of railway concession vouchers issued years earlier, and one charge of unbecoming conduct. In July 2026, a Summary General Court Martial found a Major General of the Army Medical Corps, who had served as Commandant of 166 Military Hospital, Jammu, guilty on 16 of 18 charges relating to alleged irregularities and misappropriation involving medical stores worth around Rs 11 crore between August 2018 and January 2020. He was cashiered and sentenced to one years rigorous imprisonment. In August 2026, a Summary General Court Martial at Nagrota convicted Lieutenant Colonel D Maji of the Army Medical Corps on five of 14 charges arising from the same hospitals procurement of medical supplies in 2018-19. The case involved alleged projections of urgent requirements worth around Rs 3 crore. He was cashiered and sentenced to one years rigorous imprisonment.

articleTitle: 4.9 Magnitude earthquake hits Uttarakhand, tremors felt in Delhi-NCR
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Uttarakhand earthquake map (Credits: Credits: National Center for Seismology)
description: The depth of the earthquake was noted to be 13 kilometres, according to the National Center for Seismology.
body_raw: A 4.9 Magnitude earthquake hit Uttarakhands Chamoli on Tuesday night, with its tremors felt in the Delhi-NCR region. The depth of the earthquake was noted to be 13 kilometres, according to the National Center for Seismology, which characterised its status as reviewed. Delhi-NCR has experienced several noticeable earthquakes this year. On January 19, 2026, a mild 2.8-magnitude earthquake struck New Delhi, with its epicentre in North Delhi at a shallow depth of about five kilometres. Brief tremors were felt across parts of the capital, but no damage was reported. On April 3, 2026, tremors were felt in Delhi-NCR after a 5.9-magnitude earthquake struck Afghanistan. The epicentre was near Darawan, and mild shaking was also reported in Punjab, Haryana, Jammu and Kashmir and Kargil. No casualties or property damage were immediately reported. EQ of M 4.9, On 06102026 222313 IST, Lat 30.103 N, Long 79.561 E, Depth 13 Km, Location Chamoli, Uttarakhand. For more information Download the BhooKamp App  DrJitendraSingh OfficeOfDrJS tummalasrini GSureshNCS ndmaindia  - National Center for Seismology NCSEarthquake October 6, 2026 And on June 27 a stronger 6.2-magnitude earthquake struck Afghanistan, causing tremors in Delhi-NCR and other parts of northern India. The National Centre for Seismology placed its depth at approximately 215 kilometres. What to do during earthquake Here is a quick refresher from the National Disaster Management Authority NDMA on how to stay safe when the ground shakes. If youre indoors Drop, cover and hold on. Get down on the floor, take shelter under sturdy furniture and hold on until the shaking stops. If there is no shelter nearby, crouch in an inside corner and shield your head and face with your arms. Keep away from windows, glass, exterior walls and anything that could topple, such as shelves or light fixtures. If you are in bed, stay there and cover your head with a pillow. If a heavy fixture hangs above you, move carefully to a safer spot. Use a doorway only if it is close by and structurally strong. Stay inside until the shaking stops completely. Most injuries happen when people try to move around or rush out during a quake. Be prepared for power cuts, and for fire alarms and sprinklers to go off. If youre outdoors Stay where you are, but move away from buildings, trees, poles and wires that could collapse or fall. Remain in the open until the shaking ends. Many injuries occur near exterior walls and exits because of falling debris. If youre in a vehicle Pull over as soon as it is safe, avoiding overpasses, power lines and buildings. Stay inside the vehicle until the shaking stops. Afterwards, drive carefully and avoid damaged roads and bridges. If youre trapped under debris Do not light matches or kick up dust. Cover your mouth with a piece of clothing. Signal for help by tapping on a pipe or wall, or by blowing a whistle. Shout only as a last resort, since it can make you inhale dust.

articleTitle: Tried to softly bend law towards justice: CJ D K Upadhyaya as he bids farewell to Delhi High Court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Justice DK Upadhyaya
description: With CJ Upadhyaya bidding farewell to the Delhi HC, the second senior-most judge of the High Court — Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre — will now preside over as the acting Chief Justice of Delhi HC.
body_raw: Following his elevation as a judge of the Supreme Court, Delhi High Courts outgoing Chief Justice DK Upadhyaya on Tuesday remarked that he tried to softly bend the law towards justice for deserving litigants when law failed to ensure a just outcome in a case. With CJ Upadhyaya bidding farewell to the Delhi HC, the second senior-most judge of the High Court - Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre - will now preside over as the acting Chief Justice of Delhi HC. As a judge, Ive always tried to bind justice, law and compassion together. Like other judges, I came across unforeseen situations when law was not able to ensure a just outcome in the case, and it appeared isolated from justice. In such situations, I tried to softly bend the law towards justice for the deserving litigant, and to be able to do so has been a blessing for me, he said. CJ Upadhyaya, with his parent high court at Allahabad, has been in charge of Delhi HC since January 2025. Appointed as a judge of the Allahabad HC in November 2011, CJ Upadhyaya is due to retire in June 2027. Prior to Delhi HC, he also served as Chief Justice of Bombay HC. During CJ Upadhyayas tenure at HC, 85 advocates of the Delhi HC were designated as senior advocates. His tenure at Delhi HC was also marked with several important orders. Nearly two months after he took charge, HC judge Justice Yashwant Varma was embroiled in the controversy after alleged unaccounted cash was found at his official residence during a fire, in March 2025. In its aftermath, CJ Upadhyaya had submitted a report on the incident following a preliminary inquiry to then Chief Justice of India Sanjiv Khanna with the prima facie opinion that the entire matter warrants a deeper probe.

articleTitle: Expedition hopes to finally solve the Amelia Earhart mystery
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Amelia Earhart
description: Nearly 90 years after US aviator Amelia Earhart vanished over the Pacific, a new expedition to the remote island of Nikumaroro hopes a lagoon anomaly could finally reveal the fate of her missing aircraft.
body_raw: Written By Julian Ryall Amelia Earharts attempt to become the first woman to fly around the globe at the equator ended in mystery when she and her navigator, Fred Noonan, disappeared over the Pacific Ocean in July 1937. With the 90th anniversary of her disappearance on the horizon, a new expedition is setting out to finally determine what happened over the vast Pacific. This expedition has what it believes is crucial new evidence. The team from Purdue University in Indiana and the Archaeological Legacy Institute ALI is scheduled to depart for the uninhabited island of Nikumaroro on Saturday to determine if an anomaly in the islands lagoon is Earharts missing plane. Part of the low-lying Pacific island nation of Kiribati, Nikumaroro has long been considered the place where Earhart and Noonan died. The pair took off from New Guinea on July 2, 1937, on the leg to the island of Howland, where they were to refuel before continuing on to Hawaii and completing the circumnavigation in California. Something went amiss en route, however, and even though a US Coast Guard ship could hear Earharts radio transmissions and her Lockheed Electra must have been tantalizingly close, she was never found. One of the last messages said she was running on a north-south navigational line that gave her the best chance of finding land before her fuel ran out. That line went through Nikumaroro. Landing on a coral reef In 1988, researchers from the International Group for Historic Aircraft Recovery TIGHAR were the first to suggest that Earhart could have reached Nikumaroro and landed on its fringing coral reef. TIGHARs first visit to the island was in 1989, and the group has returned seven more times, turning up compelling artifacts, including lengths of aircraft aluminum and plexiglass from a windscreen. The group found a scent bottle, a zip made in Pennsylvania in the mid-1930s, parts of a pocket knife of the same brand listed in the aircraft inventory, and the heel of a womans shoe. Archive research discovered that human remains discovered on the island in 1940 were initially believed to be of Earhart or Noonan - but were lost in the chaos of the Pacific war. Despite the searches, no one has yet found the smoking gun artifact, an item that could only have come from the doomed flight. Satellite images offer fresh hope Expedition leader Rick Pettigrew, executive director of the Archaeological Legacy Institute ALI, believes the elements may have uncovered incontrovertible evidence. A powerful tropical cyclone tore through the central Pacific in 2015, shifting geographical features on the island and in its lagoon. Satellite images taken over the following years showed what might be the outline of an aircraft fuselage and wings in shallow water off the Taraia promontory. This object in the satellite images is exactly the right size to represent the fuselage and tail of the Electra, the ALI website states. It also appears to be very reflective and is likely to be metallic. It lies in very shallow water, largely covered by sediment, in a place where the current would bring an object floating into the lagoon through Tatiman Passage, the opening to the ocean and the reef. Pettigrews 17-strong team intends to focus all its efforts on the place where the images indicate debris may be located, using drone photography, remote sensing with magnetometers and sonar units. If the initial results are positive, a hydraulic dredge will excavate sediment. Once we have a sufficient portion of the object exposed, we should be able to identify it, according to the ALIs expedition plan. If it is made of aircraft aluminum and has the specific shape and rivet patterns of the Electra, we will know that we have found the remains of Earharts aircraft. In search of a smoking gun Much of the ALIs theory is based on the research and fieldwork carried out by TIGHAR, but its executive director, Ric Gillespie, is not convinced the researchers will find the smoking gun. The object visible in old satellite imagery that Pettigrew believes is aircraft wreckage does not look like aircraft wreckage, Gillespie told DW. It looks like a dead pandanus tree that was uprooted in a storm and washed up on Taraia. Pettigrew thinks the wreckage is no longer visible because it is buried in silt, Gillespie noted. He has never been to that location and does not understand that the silt there is only a few inches deep. Teams from TIGHAR searched the same location in 2001 and 2007 with metal detectors and drew blanks, he said. Yet Gillespie remains convinced that Earhart was on Nikumaroro. I think the aircraft sank immediately after being washed over the reef edge and was smashed to pieces in the surf, he said. Major components were eventually buried in underwater landslides . or grown over with coral. We have found what there is to find. Dorothy Cochrane, who has monitored progress in the search for Earhart for more than 35 years as curator at the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum in Washington, DC, and continues to do so since her recent retirement, says Earhart still holds fascination for so many people because it is the greatest unsolved mystery of the 20th and continuing into the 21st centuries. An alternative scenario She has a different view of what happened in 1937. She argues that if Earhart was nearly out of fuel while still close to Howland, it would have been impossible to fly another 640 kilometers 400 miles to Nikumaroro. Cochrane also says that items cited as evidence of a castaway on the island can be explained by other visitors and by a small settlement that existed there for several years. I believe that Earhart and Noonan were in the general vicinity of Howland Island, based on the facts of the flight, but just could not find it before they ran out of fuel, she said. Howland Island was a tiny speck in the morning light of a vast sea, she said, suggesting Earhart could not establish radio contact to guide her the last few miles to her destination. Cochrane believes the Electra lies on the seabed near Howland. Others have advanced this theory, and several searches of the area have been carried out in recent years. If Pettigrews lead pays off, however, it will conclude aviations nearly 90-year puzzle.

articleTitle: Trump suggests Iran to ‘take out’ Los Angeles, San Diego; sparks backlash in US
articleFeaturedImageAlt: trump on Iran
description: The Republican leader was swiftly criticised by California’s Democratic leaders and some fellow Republicans.
body_raw: US President Donald Trump has courted controversy for suggesting to a crowd of his supporters in the state of Nebraska that Iran could take out major cities like Los Angeles and San Diego, the two cities held by Democrats that had been a target of his administration. The Republican leader was swiftly criticised by Californias Democratic leaders and some fellow Republicans. During a political rally in Nebraska on Monday night, Trump talked about the upcoming midterm elections in November and said that he hoped to see a tremendous victory for his party.  Trump cites war costs, upcoming midterms The US President discussed American wartime economic sacrifices and suggested that high prices of fuel, fertiliser, and other products due to the war with Iran that began in February were a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, keeping our country safe. Referring to Iran, Trump said in Grand Island, Its a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, for keeping our country safe. They could take out a city. Let em take out Los Angeles, let em take out San Diego. This is a very small price to pay, and its going to be over with very soon, amid applause from the crowd. Referring to the seven-month-old war, the US President said, Its essentially almost over with. But its going to end very soon, and its going to end one way or the other. California leaders condemn Trumps remarks Californias governor and mayor were quick to criticise Trumps comments. California Governor Gavin Newsom, in an X post, said, After sending the National Guard and Marines to occupy California, Donald Trump is now saying our foreign enemies should take out Los Angeles and San Diego. He is deranged and dangerous.  Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass attacked President Trump for making the remarks, calling them irresponsible threats that could potentially compromise the safety of Americas second-largest city. The role of a president is to protect the country, not to actively threaten it and encourage attacks on American lives, Bass said. Republican leader distances himself from Trump Jim Desmond, a Republican leader running in a redrawn California district near San Diego, distanced himself from President Trumps remarks. I vehemently disagree with President Trumps comments. America must stand up to Iran and defend our interests, but the first responsibility of our Commander-in-Chief is to protect the American people and our homeland, Desmond wrote on X. White House defends Trumps comments The White House on Tuesday defended Trumps comments. The media freakout over President Trumps comments is not rooted in reality. He was clearly stating US cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran hadnt been stopped, White House Director of Communications Steven Cheung wrote in a social media post. America is safer because of the President. Iran has no nuclear, no navy, no air force, and no money.

articleTitle: Shreyas Iyer slams maiden T20I ton, leads India to 8-wicket win over West Indies in 1st T20I
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shreyas Iyer slammed maiden T20I ton during first India vs West Indies T20I. (CREIMAS)
description: Iyer scored the fastest ton by an Indian in T20Is against West Indies as India chased down 172 in just 14.4 overs with 8 wickets in hand.
body_raw: Playing a captains innings, Shreyas Iyer led from the front by slamming his maiden T20I century to lead India to a comfortable 8-wicket victory over West Indies in the first T20I at Ekana International Cricket Stadium in Lucknow on Tuesday. Iyer scored the fastest ton by an Indian in T20Is against West Indies as India chased down 172 in just 14.4 overs with 8 wickets in hand. Chasing the total, India didnt have the best of starts as they lost both openers Abhishek Sharma 21 and Sanju Samson 11 inside four overs with the scoreboard reading 35. Roston Chase picked up Abhishek in the third over, with Shimron Hetmyer taking a brilliant diving catch while running in from long-off. An over later, Sanju Samson departed, extending his lean patch since the Asian Games, as he sliced a short delivery back to Akeal Hosein, who took the catch off his own bowling. AS IT HAPPENED  INDIA VS WEST INDIES 1ST T20I HIGHLIGHTS Thereafter, skipper Shreyas Iyer and Ishan Kishan stabilised the innings with a 137-run partnership. Earlier, all-rounder Naman Dhir had a dream T20I debut, picking up three wickets with his off-spin to help India bowl out West Indies for 171. Dhir finished with impressive figures of 331, while Kuldeep Yadav also scalped 2 for 33 to help India restrict West Indies to a manageable total. Sent into bat, West Indies skipper Shai Hope started the innings in a flurry, smacking Mayank Yadav for four boundaries in the second over to set the tone.   The four boundaries forced skipper Shreyas Iyer to replace Mayank with Axar Patel in third over. Arshdeep got the first breakthrough for India, cleaning up Kamil Pooran with a pitch-up delivery. West Indies were dealt another blow in the sixth over when Shimron Hetmyer was run out while going for an unnecessary single. It turned out to be double blow for the West Indies as Axar cleaned up Rovman Powell in the sixth over with a pitch-up delivery after the right-hander went for a huge heave over square-leg. Sherfane Rutherford 56 off 34 gave the much needed impetus to West Indies innings with the left-hander hitting Kuldeep Yadav for two sixes in the ninth over and then smashing Axar for two boundaries and a six in the 11th over. With PTI inputs

articleTitle: Film City fire: AICWA seeks FIR against Pati Patni Aur Panga 2 makers, demands inquiry
articleFeaturedImageAlt: AICWA
description: AICWA has sought an FIR and inquiry into the Film City fire, alleging safety lapses on the Pati Patni Aur Panga 2 set and demanding action.
body_raw: A day after a major fire broke out at Mumbais Film City, the All Indian Cine Workers Association AICWA has approached Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, demanding a time-bound inquiry, an FIR for alleged negligence and the resignation of Film Citys managing director. In a letter dated October 6, AICWA president Suresh Shyamlal Gupta said the fire broke out at around 4 pm on October 5 on the set of Colors channels reality show Pati Patni Aur Panga Season 2 at Prime Focus Studio in Goregaon and spread to the adjoining set of Hustle. The association has also sought mandatory fire audits, on-set fire safety staff and firefighting equipment for every production at Film City, with licences cancelled for productions that fail to comply. AICWA said the fire brought shooting across much of Film City to a halt, affecting Kaun Banega Crorepati, several television serials and films, and causing losses running into lakhs of rupees. Fire on Pati Patni Aur Panga 2 set halts shooting across Film City AICWA submits letter to Chief Minister Mumbai A fire on the set of the reality show Pati Patni Aur Panga Season 2 at Dadasaheb Phalke Chitranagari Film City halted shooting across most of Film City. Shooting of KBC and many serials and films remained stopped for the entire day, and everyone involved suffered losses. The biggest blow fell on daily-wage workers, technicians and small artists. They are paid per day, so a day without shooting means a days wages lost for many of them. Producers also lost the full days set and shoot expenses. AICWA estimates that the fire caused losses running into lakhs of rupees across Film City. All Indian Cine Workers Association AICWA President Suresh Shyamlal Gupta has submitted a letter on the incident to the following Honourable Chief Minister of Maharashtra, Shri Devendra Fadnavis Honourable Labour Minister, Shri Akash Fundkar Honourable State Home Minister, Shri Yogesh Kadam Honourable State Labour Minister, Shri Ashish Jaiswal Honourable BMC Commissioner, Shri Ashwini Bhide  AICWA  AllIndianCineWorkersAssociation  PatiPatniAurPanga  Hustle  Bollywood  Filmcity   DevFadnavis  advakash  iYogeshRKadam  Ashishjaisw3Adv  AshwiniBhide  DevenBhartiIPS  ShelarAshish  ANI  PTINews  iansindia  CMOMaharashtra  sureshsgupta  - All Indian Cine Workers Association aicwaofficial October 6, 2026 AICWA demands inquiry, FIR after Film City fire In the letter addressed to Devendra Fadnavis, AICWA president Suresh Shyamlal Gupta said the blaze did not remain confined to the Pati Patni Aur Panga Season 2 set and spread to the adjoining Hustle set, putting workers and artistes in the complex at risk. AICWA has made four demands a thorough, time-bound inquiry into how the fire started, why it spread and why fire safety arrangements were allegedly not in place an FIR for negligence against the channel, producer and production house the resignation of Film Citys managing director and mandatory fire audits, trained fire safety staff and firefighting equipment at every shoot. The association has also sought cancellation of the licence of any production that fails to comply with the required safety measures. ALSO READ Fahadh Faasil says wont get half of Rs 300 cr as Bethlehem Kudumba Unit earns Rs 326 cr This is not an accident, it is criminal negligence AICWA alleged that the Pati Patni Aur Panga 2 set had been operating without adequate fire safety arrangements. There were no fire safety arrangements whatsoever on the set of Pati Patni Aur Panga Season 2, which is why the fire broke out and spread. A large number of workers and artists were working on a set that had been left completely unprotected. This is not an accident, it is criminal negligence, the letter stated. The association further alleged that Film City management was aware that sets were operating without basic safety measures. The studios stand inside Film City, and the management knew well that sets were running without basic fire safety. The Managing Director of Film City therefore bears full responsibility for this failure, AICWA said. These are allegations made by the workers body and have not yet been established through an official inquiry. Fire disrupts shooting across Film City AICWA said shooting across most of Film City remained halted for the entire day. Shoot schedules for KBC, along with several television serials and films, were affected. The association estimated that the disruption resulted in losses running into lakhs of rupees across Film City. AICWA particularly highlighted the impact on daily-wage workers, technicians and junior artists, who lose a days income when shooting is cancelled. The biggest blow fell on daily-wage workers, technicians and small artists. They are paid per day, so a day without shooting means a days wages lost for many of them. Producers also lost the full days set and shoot expenses, the association said. AICWA sends letter to multiple authorities While Fadnavis is the primary recipient of the letter, AICWA has also marked copies to several other Maharashtra authorities. These include Labour Minister Akash Fundkar, State Home Minister Yogesh Kadam, State Labour Minister Ashish Jaiswal, BMC Commissioner Ashwini Bhide and Mumbai Police Commissioner Deven Bharti. The association concluded its letter by urging the authorities to act immediately. Unless accountability is fixed at the top, these fires will keep coming, and so will the loss of innocent lives. AICWA urges you to act without delay so that the lives of cine workers are given the safety they deserve, the letter stated. What did Pati Patni Aur Panga 2 team say? Pati Patni Aur Panga 2 team told Hindustan Times that the fire broke out outside its sets and that no shooting was taking place there at the time. Yes, there was a fire outside the sets. There is no casualty. Nobody was shooting at the set of Pati Patni Aur Panga. There was no shoot happening, the team told the publication. The show is hosted by Sonali Bendre and Munawar Faruqui. Hustle 5 team confirms artists were present The fire also affected the adjoining set of MTV Hustle 5, where the grand finale was being shot. The shows team confirmed that artistes were present when the fire broke out but said everyone was safe. All the artistes were there. The fire happened suddenly. As of now, there are no casualties and everyone is safe, the team told Hindustan Times. The team added that everyone evacuated the set after the fire broke out. No casualties or injuries have been reported following the Film City fire. The exact cause of the blaze remains unknown.

articleTitle: ‘Now I don’t even look at start list’: Gulveer Singh on not fearing other runners
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gulveer Singh became the first Indian to win three middle and long-distance medals in one edition of the Asian Games. (AP)
description: India’s long-distance runner looks to level up after winning a combined five medals at the Commonwealth Games and Asiad
body_raw: There are no starting blocks in long-distance running events like 5000m and 10000m. False starts, like in the faster sprints, isnt a primary worry for a runner, but there are other fears that take its place. Indian long distance runner Gulveer Singh admits that it was only recently that he overcame the fear of the competitors around him. Pehle thoda sochta tha baaki competitors ke baare me. Earlier, I used to think about other competitors. But now I dont even look at the start list, Gulveer told The Indian Express in an interaction facilitated by SAI Media. Gulveer was one of Indias best athletes at the Asian Games 2026 with three medals - silver in 1500m, silver in 10000m and bronze in 5000m. The transformation is visible in the results. He has five major medals this year and will be eyeing the World Athletics Championships next year. Gulveers mindset has changed over the years. Now, he knows that he is operating at the same level as compared to others. So, that really helps when the athlete knows that they belong at the top level, his coach Scott Simmons had told this paper earlier. ALSO READ  5 days, 4 races, 3 medals Gulveer Singhs hectic, but productive, Asiad The other thing that has helped Gulveer is competing regularly with the top athletes who were better than him. The result you see today has come from the fact that I regularly compete with athletes who are better than me. It takes away the fear of competing against better athletes and also keeps pushing me whenever I am against these guys, Gulveer said. Late bloomer shines In the world of long-distance running, Gulveer is a late bloomer who started participating in competitions at the age of 24 after joining the Army and has never competed at the junior level. However, his rapid strides to the top echelons of Indias running depict that he was always meant to be in the space he occupies. When I started running, I had no idea that these strides would take me this far. I ran only to get selected in the army, Gulveer recalled. There is a positive to Gulveer picking up running late-he already possessed a calm mind, and the maturity that the sport needed. When I started competing, I was clear in my head about what I had to do. I think that really helped me at the international level, he said. Learning from past Gulveers participation at the World Athletics Championships in 2025 is something that helped open his eyes to the vast difference between the competition at the Asian level, and the behemoths who competed at the highest echelons of long-distance running. When I competed at the 2025 Worlds, it was my first taste of global competition. It was very different from competing at the Asian Games or Asian Championships, said Gulveer. Before competing at the World Championships in Tokyo, Gulveers only major appearances were at the Asian Games and the Asian Championships. At the Tokyo World Championships, Gulveer was well placed to qualify for the final in the mens 5000m heat but faded away at the end, losing his qualification spot. I think that was a big learning for me. I learnt there how to hold your position in a race. Long-distance running is all about the last few meters and if you fade away in that, all the hard work is gone, said Gulveer. That he learned from his mistake at the World Championships was visible in all of the races at the Commonwealth Games and Asian Games. After the Worlds, I specifically worked on my last kick and staying patient. One needs to know when that last kick has to come, if the athlete doesnt time it right, the athlete will fade away, Gulveer explained. Now, it will be some rest for Gulveer before he travels back to Colorado Springs to train under Scott Simmons for the next season. Ill be back to training soon. Once, the celebrations and felicitations are over here in India, said Gulveer. I have my eyes set on the World Championships next season and as one can see, the progression is on the right path for me at the moment.

articleTitle: 3 children suffer head injuries as ceiling collapses at government school in Udaipur
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Udaipur school ceiling collapse
description: The incident comes at a time when the state is facing increased scrutiny over the condition of schools, drawing attention of the Cockroach Janta Party whose members visited different campuses in August.
body_raw: Three children suffered head injuries after the ceiling of their classroom collapsed at a government primary school in Udaipur on Tuesday. Two other students sustained minor injuries in the incident that took place in the Bhindar area. The incident comes at a time when the state is facing increased scrutiny over the condition of schools, drawing attention of the Cockroach Janta Party CJP whose members visited campuses in different parts of Rajasthan in August. Tuesdays incident took place around 11 am at Government Primary School, Narada, under Vaniyatalai gram panchayat in the Bhindar police station area, when a portion of the plaster from a classroom ceiling suddenly came down. There were 32 children in the classroom at the time. Headmaster Lal Singh Shaktawat told The Indian Express, Class 1 students Krishna Kumari and Kartik, and Class 5 student Ganeshlal suffered head injuries. All three were taken to Bhindar Government Hospital for treatment and later sent home. Two other students sustained minor injuries. The ceiling collapsed suddenly, injuring the students. Thankfully, no one was severely injured. We sent the children back to their homes by evening. The school, which runs up to Class 5, has 37 students in all, which is why it is common for students of different classes to study in the same room. Authorities were informed of schools condition Shaktawat said the education department had earlier been informed about the poor condition of the building. The building was constructed in 2001 and had become dilapidated. We had already informed the education department about its condition. The last time the school building was repaired was in 2020, he said. Following directions from the education department and the local administration, the school building has now been locked as a precautionary measure. Classes will be shifted to a temporary location near Matajis mandir nearby. The incident comes just over a year after one of Rajasthans worst school-building tragedies. On July 25, 2025, the roof of a government school in Piplodi village of Jhalawar district collapsed, killing seven children and injuring 28 others. The National Human Rights Commission subsequently took cognizance of the incident and sought a report from the Rajasthan government, noting allegations that authorities had been informed about the buildings dilapidated condition. The safety of government schools has again emerged as a major issue in Rajasthan in recent months following the School Thik Karo campaign by the CJP. Its teams visited government schools across the state and highlighted problems ranging from unsafe and dilapidated buildings to schools functioning without proper infrastructure. Some CJP workers were also attacked while visiting a government school in Bagru. The government school at Rampura-Kanwarpura in Jaipurs Bagru area, which had been declared unsafe, was demolished after the CJP campaign highlighted its condition. The government sanctioned around Rs 18 lakh for construction of a new building.

articleTitle: Inside Ananya Panday’s Greece vacation: ‘Most beautiful five days’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ananya Panday takes a trip to Greece
description: Explore the world famous pink sands of Elafonissi Beach, photograph the striking turquoise waters at Balos Lagoon, or enjoy wild watersports at beautiful Paleokastritsa Beach.
body_raw: Ananya Pandays latest European rendezvous has set the bar pretty high for a summer getaway.While theChaand Mera Dil actor shared snapshots from her trip to Greece on Instagram, exploring tranquil waters on speedboat rides and stealing quieter moments on the beachfront, we turned to TripAdvisors top recommendations and found some must-visit attractions to add to our Greece travel bucket list.Come take a look Acropolis This ancient citadel, built in the fifth century B.C., towers over the city and is home to some of the most impressive ancient ruins, buildings, and artefacts. One of them is the Parthenon, which features the majestic ruins of an ancient Greek building known for its dignified white marble columns and perfect sense of proportion. The countrys most famous temple, it was dedicated to the goddess Athena and is considered the peak of Greek art. Elafonissi Beach Located on Cretes southwest coast, this remote beach is best known for its pink sand. The crystal-clear waters make this a popular summer vacation spot, attracting sunbathers and watersport enthusiasts alike. Plaka One of the oldest neighbourhoods in Athens, youll see Roman columns, medieval churches, and ancient landmarks like the Choragic Monument of Lysicrates-along with shops selling jewellery, clothes, ceramics, and souvenirs. Sidewalk restaurants and family-run taverns serving authentic Greek food are an added bonus. Balos Lagoon This lagoon is one of the most photographed spots on the island of Crete, with stunning turquoise waters and a panoramic landscape. Visit early in the morning to experience the lagoon at its calmest and most tranquil state. TripAdvisor suggests taking the ferry from Kissamos Port for a relaxing, convenient way to reach Belos. Paleokastritsa Beach Surrounded by lush greenery and rocky cliffs, Paleokastritsa Beach is known for its crystal-clear waters, white sandy beaches, and stunning natural beauty. The beach is also great for a variety of water sports, making it popular amongst adrenaline seekers and thrill chasers. Tours of the bay take you to the enchanting Nausicaas Cave, the famous Blue Caves, and secluded beaches accessible only by boat. The Monastery of Theotokou, overlooking the bay, is just a short distance from the beach and is considered one of the islands most important monasteries. Meteora Meteora makes for ajaw-dropping landscape in centralGreece,where six historic Eastern Orthodox monasteries sit atop massive, 400-meter-tall sandstone pillars. Meaning suspended in the air, this UNESCO World Heritage site sits near the towns of Kalabaka and Kastraki and is about 3.5 hours by train or car from Athens.

articleTitle: After nudge from selectors, Harmanpreet Kaur quits as India skipper in all formats
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down from captaincy of Indian women's team. (CREIMAS FOR BCCI)
description: The selectors felt it was time to build for the next World Cup cycle. India failed to progress to the knockouts of the T20 World Cup for the second time in a row under Harmanpreet's captaincy
body_raw: A year after leading India to the ODI World Cup, Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down as captain of the national womens cricket team in all formats - a surprise decision that she announced through an Instagram post Tuesday, a day after attending a team review meeting with BCCI officials and selectors in Guwahati. The 37-year-old also said in the post that she was ready to continue playing for the country. Now, I am ready to play for the love of the game. Captaincy ends. The journey continues, she posted. The ODI World Cup at home last year was the teams first ever ICC title. But this July, the side failed to progress to the knockout rounds of the T20 World Cup for the second time in a row, prompting the selectors to decide on a change in leadership - although Harmanpreet was keen to continue, BCCI sources told The Indian Express. The decision to move on from Harmanpreet as captain was by the selectors. After the end of the T20 World Cup, a review meeting was planned. But it took place after the Asian Games where the team won gold. Harmanpreet wanted to continue as captain, but the selectors prevailed. The selectors felt it was time to build for the next World Cup cycle. There was no question of split captaincy, the sources said. ALSO READ  Harmanpreet Kaurs real legacy is belief, not just a World Cup The Indian Express has learnt that womens team coach Amol Muzumdar, vice-captain Smriti Mandhana and Harmanpreet met separately with BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia and womens selection committee chief Amita Sharma in Guwahati. Mandhana 30 took over the captaincy reins from Harman. Harmanpreets last assignment as captain was the Asian Games campaign, where India defended its title. She captained India in five Tests, 51 ODIs and 155 T20Is, and also led the team to three Asia Cup titles. She was appointed T20 captain in 2016 and took over the reins of the ODI team in 2022 after Mithali Rajs retirement. India had reached the ODI World Cup final in 2005 and 2017 under Mithali. With Harmanpreet at the helm, India became a top contender in the international arena 2018 T20 World Cup semifinal, 2020 T20 World Cup final, 2023 T20 World Cup semifinal and, eventually, the 2025 ODI World Cup title. However, India were knocked out in the group stage of the 2024 and 2026 T20 World Cups. Not easy decision This is not an easy decision, Harmanpreet wrote on Instagram. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life. I have given everything I had to this team and to Indian womens cricket - my blood, my sweat, my time, and many times, a part of my own game and personal ambitions. There were moments when I had to put my individual performance, my own growth, and what I wanted for myself aside, because I believed the team had to come first. In an official statement, BCCI president Mithun Manhas said Harmanpreets contribution as captain will always hold a special place in the history of Indian cricket. ALSO READ  Harmanpreet will be able to bat with freedom Coach Kamaldeesh She took on the responsibility at an important stage in the growth of womens cricket and helped the Indian team build on the strong foundation laid by those who came before her. Over the years, she led India through some very important moments and helped the team compete with confidence against the best in the world. The World Cup victory in 2025 will undoubtedly be the defining achievement of her captaincy, Manhas said. Saikia also highlighted the World Cup win in his tribute. Harmanpreet, you can be immensely proud of what you have achieved as captain of India. You embraced the responsibility from the very beginning and went on to lead India through some of the most important moments in its journey, while playing an important role in the growth of Indian womens cricket, he said. You experienced the disappointment of falling short, but continued to believe in the team and its ability to achieve more. That is what made the World Cup victory in 2025 so special. You had been part of the journey for many years and eventually had the opportunity to lead India to its first womens cricket World Cup title. That will always remain one of the great moments in Indian cricket, Saikia said.

articleTitle: Harmanpreet will be able to bat with freedom: Coach Kamaldeesh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Harmanpreet Kaur with her first coach Kamaldeesh Pal Singh Sodhi (FILE & CREIMAS FOR BCCI)
description: Harmanpreet Kaur's childhood coach says she is the most valuable asset of the Indian team
body_raw: As told to Nitin Sharma Like Harmanpreet Kaur said, she always put the team first even if it affected her as a player. The captaincy also comes with a lot of stress. I am reminded of how Virat Kohli also gave up the captaincy and then flourished. I can see the same thing happening for Harman now. My mind goes to the day when I first saw Harman playing in Moga with boys. When I approached her asking if she would play for the Moga team, she told me to ask her father. Even though she had evolved as a player and then as captain, who would always back her decisions, she understood at that time that it was important to get her fathers permission. Within one year of her joining, she would lead Moga to the Inter-District title. Post the win, she would drive a motorcycle. Perhaps that was her message to her team-mates that girls can do anything. When she made her debut for the Indian team in 2009, it was rare that a girl had made her way from district team to state team to national team in a short span of three years. ALSO READ  Harmanpreet Kaurs real legacy is belief, not just a World Cup In 2012 Asia Cup final, when she was made the Indian captain for the first time, she called me and my only message to her was, Kudiye, team nu nal le chalna te stress nahi lena te team-mates layi hamesha stand lena Girl, always take the team along and dont take stress of captaincy. And always stand with your players. And thats been her mantra all these years. Initially, when she would captain the team occasionally, I would tell her to learn how MS Dhoni captained the Indian team. When India lost the 50-over World Cup final against England in 2017, she was distraught after the loss. But then when we had talked post the final, she shared how she will learn from experience. Six years later, when she got run-out in the ICC T20 Womens World Cup semi-final against Australia at Cape Town, with India needing 40 runs off 32 balls, I had a talk with her. India lost the game. I was angry about her mode of dismissal. I could sense the dejection. But she was confident that India would win a big title. And she showed that in last years ICC Womens World Cup. There was this pressure of playing in front of the home crowd too. She understood that she is one of the senior-most players in the team. And when she played that knock against Australia in the semi-final, she once again showed why her role as a batsman as well captain in the team is important. Her tactical decision in the final including giving the ball to Shafali Verma too shows how she trusts youngsters, a thing which we could see early. Post matches, she would spend time with her team-mates discussing strategies. As Harman enters the new phase in her career of playing with freedom and without the burden of captaincy, I wish her all the success. She has been the most valuable asset to the Indian womens team. Kamaldeesh Pal Singh Sodhi spoke to Nitin Sharma

articleTitle: ‘Sudden action seems bit strange’: Omar Abdullah after 150 flown out of J&K for deportation
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah
description: “If you look at it, their presence here has not really caused us any particular harm. However, it is also true that they cannot stay illegally,” the J&K CM said.
body_raw: A day after 150 alleged Bangladeshi nationals picked from across the Union Territory were airlifted to West Bengal, Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday said the sudden action seemed a bit strange. If you look at it, their presence here has not really caused us any particular harm. However, it is also true that they cannot stay illegally, he said. Omar said that Rohingyas are being unfairly targeted, adding that it is not in the hands of the UT government but the government at the Centre, who are using the police to move them out. We gave them Rohingyas refuge here, a little space, and allowed them to stay here until conditions in their country improved. Now, suddenly taking action against them seems a bit strange to me, he said. The 150 people airlifted to Bagdogra, from where they will be deported, are among 500 who were detained from different parts of the Union Territory during a survey to identify illegal immigrants. Meanwhile, speaking to reporters, Omar commended the Supreme Court for raising questions on the issue of deletion of names from voter lists. Omar said, The good thing is that questions are being raised in the Supreme Court as well, especially the deletion of names from voter lists. The SC has sought answers regarding this from the EC and the Government of India. We will have to see how far this can be corrected by the courts. The Supreme Court on Monday issued notice to the Centre and the Election Commission of India ECI on a petition accusing Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of acting in violation of the law that governs his terms of office by functioning in a unilateral manner, and seeking his removal. The notice issued by a three-judge bench, presided by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, was also directed at Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, Deputy Election Commissioner Maneesh Garg, and ECI Director General Information Technology Seema Khanna. On INDIA blocs Delhi march, he said that after the leaders met in New Delhi, a calendar was drawn out for this month. The beginning of that was for the members of Parliament from the INDIA bloc to march toward the Election Commission, and this will go on, he added. UCC will never be implemented in JK In response to a query regarding the implementation of the UCC in Jammu and Kashmir, the CM said, A Uniform Civil Code is not truly uniform until it is implemented everywhere. It will never be implemented here. He also pointed out Bihars resistance to its implementation, stating that, Similarly, there are other governments too that have said the UCC will not be applied in their states. So, this is only being implemented by the BJP. He said it is wrong that the Bharatiya Janata Party BJP is trying to implement this step by step in states where they are in power. These matters are not handled from state to state. If you have the courage, bring a legislation in Parliament, debate it and then lets see whether it passes or not. If you look at it in the true sense of a democracy, this has to be debated at the Centre. They will not introduce this law in Parliament because they do not have the numbers, he said.

articleTitle: ‘Maharashtra centre of Maoist urban network’: State defends Special Public Security Act in court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The state said the law was not vague and did not violate free speech, which is subject to reasonable restrictions under the Constitution. (File Photo)
description: Defending the law against Congress, CPI and AITUC pleas, the state says other Maoist-hit states already have similar laws that have withstood judicial scrutiny
body_raw: Maharashtra, because of its highest urban population has become center of Maoist urban network, the state government has told the Bombay High Court, defending the Maharashtra Special Public Security MSPS Act. The state did not have legal framework of public security act to ban frontal organization like other Left Wing Extremism LWE affected states Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhatisgarh, said the affidavit filed by Pritamkumar Jawale, Deputy Secretary of the state Home department. The affidavit seeks dismissal of petitions by the Congress, the Communist Party of India CPI and the All India Trade Union Congress AITUC challenging the Acts constitutional validity, and questions the petitioners legal standing. It says the law was enacted to establish a robust legal framework to prevent and tackle unlawful, subversive, and extremist activities. The petitioners contend the law curbs peaceful and legitimate dissent and gives the executive wide-ranging, arbitrary, and excessive powers to ban organisations without any judicial scrutiny or oversight. The Act lists four punishable offences being a member of an unlawful organisation, collecting funds for one, helping manage one, or carrying out an unlawful activity. It authorises the state to notify any suspected body as an unlawful organisation. Citing Elgaar Parishad and other cases, the affidavit claimed Maharashtra has the highest number of frontal organisations in the country, 64. It said Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Jharkhand had banned such groups under similar laws that withstood judicial scrutiny, so Maharashtra was empowered to enact one for local security environments. Not enacting the law, it said, would affect entitlement of security related expenditure SRE fund crucial for fighting Maoist battle in LWE-affected areas. The state said the law was not vague and did not violate free speech, which is subject to reasonable restrictions under the Constitution. It balances the fundamental liberties of citizens with the paramount duty of preserving public order and national integrity, the reply said. The state also denied that appointing a government advocate to the non-judicial advisory board was illegal. The Act bridges a critical legislative gap by allowing action before any violence or loss of life, it said, as insurgencies survive not only on ideology but they require robust logistical supply chains, safe houses, covert financial pipelines, and institutional fronts. A bench led by Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi allowed the petitioners to file a rejoinder to the affidavit and posted the matter for hearing on October 16

articleTitle: Paramount and Warner Bros are now one Hollywood giant: Skydance
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Paramount and Warner Bros are now one Hollywood giant: Skydance
description: Paramount, owned by Skydance, has completed its $81 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, with the deal officially closing on Tuesday.
body_raw: Its official Skydance-owned Paramount has closed its 81 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery. The companies completed the deal on Tuesday, ushering in a new Hollywood giant with the now shorter Skydance nametag. The merger brings two of Americas oldest moviemaking studios together. And HBO Max, titles ranging from Harry Potter to Sinners and even networks like CNN find themselves under the same roof as Paramount, CBS and the likes of Top Gun and The Godfather. All of them will come under the helm of billionaire David Ellison, and his new co-CEO Ynon Kreiz. That further concentrates power in an industry already run by just a handful of major players. Ellisons Skydance bought out Paramount for 8 billion just last year, and set its sights on Warner - an even bigger fish - very soon after. What followed erupted into a tumultuous, roughly year-long fight over Warners fate. Skydance Corp. emerges from one of the biggest tie-ups ever in the media and entertainment industry. Including billions of dollars in debt, the Warner acquisition amounted to nearly 111 billion. Today is a historic day, not just for Skydance but for our entire industry, Ellison said in a statement Tuesday. We couldnt be more excited to get to work. Heres a look at some of the key moments that got us here. Netflix vs Paramount The early days of Paramounts quest for Warner turned into a messy bidding war. Months after disclosing it was open to selling parts or even all of its business, Warner initially struck a studio and streaming deal with Netflix back in December. But Skydance-owned Paramount, which claimed Warner management never engaged meaningfully with its previous proposals, soon launched a hostile counterbid aimed at taking over the entire company - including networks like CNN and Discovery. The Hollywood giants spent much of early 2026 in a heated back-and-forth over who had a stronger offer on the table, with Warner leadership repeatedly backing Netflix as its preferred suitor. But Paramount eventually upped its offer to buy all of Warner for 31 per share, and Netflix opted to bow out of the race. Warner and Paramount inked a mutual merger agreement by late February. ALSO READ  Tom Cruise calls Digger an honour as it bombs with 20 mn opening, set to lose 150 mn The response from Hollywood Hollywood was closely watching the fight over Warners future. And from awards shows to online petitions, A-list celebrities and other creatives made their voices known. In April, thousands of movie stars, writers, directors and other professionals announced their unequivocal opposition to the Paramount-Warner merger. The open letter - which was signed by long-outspoken critics of the deal like Jane Fonda and Mark Ruffalo, as well as Hollywood heavyweights from Denis Villeneuve to J.J. Abrams - warned of fewer jobs and less choice for audiences in the United States and around the world. Meanwhile, some other stars lined up to back Paramount as Ellison reiterated his commitments to the movies. At CinemaCon this past spring, the company debuted a glossy mini movie about the studio directed by Jon M. Chu and narrated by Tom Cruise - who ended the spot atop the iconic Paramount water tower, with the words the future is paramount and the future looks pretty great from here. Director James Cameron also doubled down on his support of Ellison. The prospect of a new Warner owner also loomed over awards season this year, from BlockTheMerger pins to more subtle nods in acceptance speeches. When accepting her Emmy last month, Remarkably Bright Creatures actor Sally Field - who also signed the open letter in opposition to the Paramount-Warner deal - stressed that unique storytelling matters and we cant let those voices be silenced, or compromised or merged. Many industry critics were also outspoken when Netflixs studio and streaming deal was on the table, with particular focus on the future of movies staying in theaters. Trump and CNN Donald Trump has regularly attacked reporting he deems unfavorable at CNN most recently attempting to bar the outlet from the White House altogether. And over the course of the Warner buyout, his administration wasnt afraid to chime in about hopes for a new owner. In December - days after Paramount launched its hostile bid for Warner - the president said that CNN spread poison and lies, adding that I think the people who have run CNN for the last long period of time are a disgrace and its imperative that CNN be sold. The White House took aim again at CNN in March, over the networks coverage of the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran. At the time, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth told reporters that the sooner David Ellison takes over that network, the better. Ellison has said editorial independence will be maintained at CNN, and under a since-finalized settlement with the states, the company also agreed to form a News Editorial Independence Board. But critics point to turmoil already seen at CBS under Skydance ownership - and arent convinced this new body will move the needle much, because Ellison is set to have ample oversight over appointments. Outside this board, however, the combined company is retaining Mark Thompson as CNNs editor-in-chief. Trump has separately continued to criticise CBS coverage under Skydance ownership. Still, the president has held a long relationship with the billionaire Ellison family. Paramounts chief reportedly hosted a dinner in Washington in Trumps honour back in April, on the same day Warner shareholders gave their greenlight for the merger. And in June, just two days after the U.S. Justice Department said it wouldnt intervene in the deal, Ellison attended an Ultimate Fighting Championship match on the White House lawn for Trumps 80th birthday streamed by Paramount. Also Read - Digger Tom Cruise leans into one of his careers most remarkable performances with glee Gulf money To help fund its Warner buyout, Paramount racked up billions of dollars in financial backing from three Gulf countries Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates. The Federal Communications Commission approved the companys request for sizeable indirect ownership from those foreign investors. Paramount previously disclosed it expected those funds to indirectly own nearly 50 of equity interests - but no voting rights - of what is now the larger Skydance. But the company asked for clearance of up to 100 to account for potential future investments, which the FCC granted, citing in part that access to more capital would strengthen the broadcast industry and was therefore in the public interest. Critics - including FCCs sole Democratic Commissioner, Anna Gomez - have called the move alarming and unprecedented. They argue that amount of money opens the door to behind-the-scenes influence. The final antitrust fight Paramount cleared antitrust hurdles for its Warner acquisition from regulators worldwide over the summer, including the Trump administrations Justice Department. But in July, Democratic attorneys general from 12 states - led by Californias Rob Bonta - sued to block the merger, alleging the combined company would extinguish competition and lead to fewer choices for consumers, particularly movie theatergoers and cable customers across the U.S. The Writers Guild of America followed suit. And Paramount agreed to put its Warner buyout on ice well into next year so the challenges could head toward a larger antitrust trial. Settlement agreements emerged in September. The states terms, eventually approved by a judge, include pledges from the company to increase film production in the U.S. over the next five years, commit millions of dollars to a fund aimed at supporting workers displaced by the merger and again establish new editorial monitoring of CNN and CBS. Settling these challenges marked a key hurdle ahead of closing the deal. Critics decried the deal as capitulating to corporate pressure and said the remedies were too weak.

articleTitle: Smriti Mandhana named India women’s captain as Harmanpreet Kaur steps down
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Smriti Mandhana takes over the captaincy reign from Harmanpreet Kaur. (BCCI FOR CREIMAS)
description: Harmanpreet, who led India to the 2025 ODI World Cup title, announced earlier in the day that she was relinquishing the captaincy across formats.
body_raw: Smriti Mandhana has been appointed captain of the Indian womens cricket team, the BCCI announced on Tuesday, the day Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down from the role. Harmanpreet, who led India to the 2025 ODI World Cup title, announced earlier in the day that she was relinquishing the captaincy across formats. Today, I step down as captain of the Indian Womens Cricket Team across all formats, she wrote in a post.
