Reports said the decision followed a BCCI review meeting in Guwahati that assessed the teams performances over recent months, including Indias exit from the T20 World Cup before the semifinals. Smriti has been one of the leading figures in Indian womens cricket over the years and has played a key role in the teams progress across formats, the BCCI said in a release. It added that she has also demonstrated her leadership qualities in domestic and franchise cricket, most recently leading Royal Challengers Bengaluru to Womens Premier League titles in 2024 and 2026. ALSO READ  Harmanpreet Kaurs real legacy is belief, not just a World Cup Mandhana, who was Harmanpreets deputy, has been part of the Indian team since 2013, and the release said she brings considerable experience into the role. She will be the full-time white-ball captain from now on, the BCCI said. She has so far led India in 18 T20Is and four ODIs. The 29-year-old was the second-highest run-scorer at the 2025 World Cup, with 434 runs, and became the first Indian woman to score international hundreds in all three formats when she made a T20I century against England in June 2025. To be given the responsibility of leading India is a very special honour, Mandhana said in the release. Representing India has always meant a great deal to me, and to now have the opportunity to lead the team is something I will value deeply. I am grateful to the BCCI, the selectors, my teammates and everyone who has supported me throughout my journey and for the trust they have placed in me. She also paid tribute to her predecessor. I would also like to acknowledge Harmanpreet and the contribution she has made as captain over the years. She has led the team with great commitment and has been an important part of our journey, Mandhana said. I understand the responsibility that comes with this role and look forward to working with the team, learning along the way and giving my best to take Indian Cricket forward. Indias next assignment is a series against Zimbabwe starting on October 16. The Womens Champions Trophy follows at home in February.

articleTitle: Acidity pill Aciloc: Mundhe’s FDA shuts 3 Cadila godowns over name mix-up
articleFeaturedImageAlt: FDA licence suspended Cadila
description: Popular acidity pill Aciloc was sold in two versions with different drugs but almost identical names, says FDA
body_raw: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration FDA has cancelled the sale and distribution licences of three Cadila Pharmaceuticals Ltd godowns in Pune, Nagpur and Thane after finding that drugs with different active ingredients were being sold under deceptively similar names to Aciloc, a popular acidity medicine. Aciloc 150 and Aciloc 300 contain 150 mg and 300 mg of ranitidine. Aciloc 150 and Aciloc 300 contain a different drug altogether, famotidine, in strengths of 20 mg and 40 mg. Yet the only difference in the brand names is a  sign, the FDA said. Both reduce stomach acid and treat heartburn and ulcers. But the FDA said the similar names could lead to patients being dispensed the wrong medicine. It also found that some wholesalers who had ordered the ranitidine versions were supplied the famotidine ones. Officials said inspections were carried out in July at the companys clearing and forwarding agent CFA godowns at Bhiwandi in Thane district, Wadki in Pune and Nimji in Kalmeshwar taluka of Nagpur district, and the stock was prohibited from sale and distribution. The action followed a petition by the company in the Bombay High Court, which on August 11 directed fresh show-cause notices at all three locations. The company was given 21 days to reply in writing and a personal hearing. The companys written reply and submissions during the hearing were found unsatisfactory, following which the respective licensing authorities passed reasoned orders under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945, the FDA said. Under the rules, famotidine tablets must be sold in packs of 14. The FDA found Aciloc 150 was being sold in packs of 30 and Aciloc 300 in packs of 20. The FDA flagged another issue. Gujarats drug regulator, in a September 29 letter, cancelled manufacturing permissions for famotidine 20 mg and 40 mg tablets, with effect backdated to June 2. This was not disclosed during the show-cause and hearing proceedings, while sale and distribution continued in Maharashtra, the state FDA said. Other deficiencies cited include the absence of an inspection book, inadequate labelling of the expired-drug area, the absence of the competent person at a licensed Konkan premises and unsigned sale invoices. FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe said manufacturers have a responsibility to ensure brand names do not create confusion, and urged consumers to check the generic name and strength on medicine labels. Chemists should dispense medicines strictly according to prescriptions, he said.

articleTitle: Rajnath Singh stresses on self-reliance in aerospace sector as HAL delivers its 2,000th aero-engine
articleFeaturedImageAlt: aero-engine: Defense Minister Rajnath Singh, Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi and others during the inauguration ceremony of second Shakti Engine Manufacturing line, in Koratput. (PTI Photo)
description: Describing the engine as a significant milestone, the Defence Minister called for using it as a foundation to build an aerospace industry capable of designing, developing, manufacturing and supporting advanced propulsion systems.
body_raw: Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Tuesday called for strengthening indigenous capabilities in the design, development, testing, manufacturing and maintenance of advanced aero-engines, stressing that mastery of propulsion technology is essential for self-reliance in the aerospace and defence sector. Singh, who witnessed the delivery of the 2,000th aero-engine by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited HAL, Koraput division at Sunabeda, noted that indigenisation of components and reduced turnaround time are contributing to operational readiness and extended service life of critical defence assets. Aerospace self-reliance must extend to indigenous aero-engine capability, particularly for the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft AMCA programme. A sovereign aerospace ecosystem requires indigenous capabilities across materials, design, manufacturing, testing and Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul MRO, said Singh. He also highlighted proposed investment of around Rs 5,000 crore, indigenisation of raw materials in partnership with Mishra Dhatu Nigam Limited MIDHANI, and establishment of Indias first indigenous high-thrust engine testing facility. Urging the HAL Koraput division to raise standards in quality, productivity, indigenisation, innovation and delivery timelines, Singh described the 2,000th engine as a significant milestone and called for using it as a foundation to build an Indian aerospace industry capable of designing, developing, manufacturing and supporting advanced propulsion systems. Emphasising the need for reliable indigenous propulsion for Indias helicopter ecosystem, the defence minister stated that forces require engines that are available when needed, supported throughout their lifecycle, and upgraded with evolving technology. A long-term endeavour Aero-engine development is a long-term endeavour requiring sustained investment, specialised testing, skilled manpower and a strong industrial ecosystem, with focus on repeatable, reliable and scalable production, design, critical materials and superalloys, he added. Singh, on the occasion, hailed HALs contribution to military aviation, noting that its engines have powered frontline aircraft, including the MiG-21, MiG-27, MiG-29 and Su-30MKI since establishment of the unit in 1964. The defence minister announced that HAL is enhancing annual AL-31FP engine production capacity from 30 to 50 engines annually with an investment of Rs 335 crore. He also announced a second Shakti engine production line with an investment of Rs 218 crore. The new line will manufacture up to 100 engines annually and is scheduled to be fully established by 2028-29, catering to indigenous helicopters including Dhruv Advanced Light Helicopter ALH and Prachand Light Combat Helicopter LCH, added Singh. He also called for greater integration of MSMEs, start-ups, private industry, academia and research institutions into the propulsion ecosystem.

articleTitle: Bypoll contests: Repoll clamour in Bengal, acid test in Tamil Nadu
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rejinagar Assembly bypolls in WB
description: AJUP chief Humayun Kabir arrested by police in Rejinagar; CM Adhikari, BJP reject Oppn's allegations of vote-rigging
body_raw: The bypolls for the two Assembly constituencies in West Bengal on Tuesday saw the arrest of Aam Janata Unnayan Party AJUP chief Humayun Kabir and the Oppositions pitch for a repoll over alleged vote-rigging and other irregularities. There were no reports of any violence during polling. The Oppositions allegations were rejected by the ruling BJP and Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. The Nandigram Assembly seat in Purba Medinipur district recorded a turnout of about 80.87, while Rejinagar in Murshidabad registered about 80.07 polling, according to the Election Commission EC officials. The by-elections in the two seats were necessitated after CM Adhikari resigned from the Nandigram seat and retained his Bhabanipur constituency in Kolkata, while Humayun Kabir vacated the Rejinagar constituency and retained his Nowda seat. Soon after polling began, Kabir was arrested by the police in Rejinagar after he accused them of interfering with voting at multiple polling stations. His son Gulam Nabi Azad is the AUJP candidate from Rejinagar. The police are intimidating our workers, booth agents and voters. We will not leave the booths, Kabir told reporters before being arrested. In his home turf Nandigram, Adhikari said polling has been peaceful. In 2016, I won in Nandigram by 82,000 votes. I think this time we will cross the margin, the CM said. The Nowda MLA Kabir was arrested. Law is same for all. Even for me. I can cast my vote in my booth. I cannot visit other booths or campaign. If I break the law, I will be arrested. Later, Kabir was released by the police at around 9 pm. The Congresss Nandigram candidate Milan Pradhan however alleged that During the day genuine voters were not allowed to vote, but booths were captured by BJP agents with the help of police. Pradhan was recently arrested in old cases linked to the 2007 Nandigram land-acquisition agitation, but was later released on interim bail. The BJP has fielded Hansirani Rath, mother of Chandranath Rath-Adhikaris aide who was murdered-as its candidate in Nandigram. In Rejinagar, Congress candidate Abdullahil Kafi staged a sit-in protest near the police station alleging that booths had been captured by BJP agents. Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, the Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress TMC candidate, sent a letter to the states chief electoral officer, demanding repoll. Bengal Congress president Subhankar Sarkar also demanded a repoll in both seats. However, the BJP targeted the Opposition, saying that they want old violent polling days to return in the state. TN, Puducherry bypolls Five months after the C Joseph Vijay-led TVK stormed to power in Tamil Nadu, the state saw voting in the Madurantakam and Dharapuram Assembly bypolls, which was largely peaceful, barring EVM glitches and isolated disputes. Madurantakam recorded 86.26 turnout, compared with 87.84 in the April Assembly election, while Dharapuram registered 80.30 polling as against 86.74 earlier, as per the EC officials. Both constituencies are Scheduled Caste SC-reserved seats vacated by the AIADMK legislators who resigned within weeks of being elected as they crossed over to Vijays party. These two leaders-Maragatham Kumaravel in Madurantakam and P Sathyabama in Dharapuram-are now contesting as the TVK candidates. Facing his first major electoral test,Vijay campaigned extensively for his candidates. He spent four days campaigning in the two constituencies-two days of public rallies and two of roadshows-a substantial commitment for bypolls from a CM whose own appearances during the state Assembly elections had been relatively limited. In Kolinjivadi, Dharapuram, an election official was replaced following a complaint made by the Opposition that the official had asked an elderly woman to vote for the whistle symbol. In these bypolls, DMK supremo M K Stalin and AIADMK chief Edappadi K Palaniswami or EPS also campaigned pro-actively for their respective candidates, sharpening their attacks on Vijay. In neighbouring Puducherry, the by-election to the Thattanchavady Assembly seat recorded 80.81 polling at 6 pm. The bypoll was necessitated as the AINRC chief and CM, N Rangasamy, a BJP ally, vacated it after retaining his Mangalam seat. Nagaon LS bypoll In Assam, voting for the Nagaon Lok Sabha seat bypoll registered 76 turnout till 5 pm. The by-election was necessitated as Congress MP Pradyut Bordoloi resigned to contest, successfully, the state Assembly election from Dispur on a BJP ticket earlier this year. The contest mainly involves the candidates of the ruling BJP, the principal Opposition Congress and AIUDF chief Badruddin Ajmal. The counting of votes for all the bypolls is scheduled for October 9.

articleTitle: No classes till security assured, say SRFTI students; plan rally with Jadavpur University
articleFeaturedImageAlt: College students protest against Fee Hike in Chandigarh
description: According to the students, despite an urgent written appeal sent to Union Information & Broadcasting (I&B) Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw following violent clashes on campus, no response was received from the ministry.
body_raw: As the boycott of classes, workshops, and film shoots at the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute SRFTI in Kolkata entered its 10th day, protesting students reiterated that they will not return to academic activity till concrete security assurances are provided and warned of a mass gathering with the students of Jadavpur University and the alumni network. According to the students, despite an urgent written appeal sent to Union Information  Broadcasting IB Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw following violent clashes on campus, no response was received from the ministry. In response to escalating panic on campus, a joint delegation of student representatives from SRFTI Kolkata, the Film and Television Institute of India FTII Pune, and FTII Itanagar submitted a formal petition on October 3 to the Union Ministry requesting immediate central intervention to secure the autonomous institutes Kolkata campus. Signed by Blossom Hazarika SRFTI Students Union, Amritanshu Singh Yadav FTII Students Association, and Divyansh FTII Itanagar Students Council, the joint letter outlines four key demands for the IB Ministry. It includes deployment of adequate security personnel at vulnerable campus access points, including the main gate coordination with the West Bengal government and Kolkata Police to deny permits for public rallies near the institute implementation of preventive measures to stop outside crowds from approaching or threatening the campus and direct instructions for the SRFTI administration to maintain continuous liaison with police and student representatives until de-escalation is achieved. On Sunday, there was stone pelting two people were injured. I was one of them. I got three stitches and another student suffered a head injury, said Anamika Pal, a student representative at SRFTI. In fact, one person jumped inside the campus, and weve been constantly pelted with stones. Pal said that academic activity will remain suspended until safety guarantees are established. Till the time we are given assurance of our safety and security, we are not going to resume classes. What happened on Sunday is scary. One person jumped into the campus, but it is not difficult for many others to enter. Who will take accountability? With no official acknowledgement or safety framework provided by the IB Ministry after 10 days of disrupted academic activity, students are reaching beyond the campus perimeter to rally wider political and academic support. Classes have been off for the last 10 days, and theres no response from the IB Ministry. If we dont get support and safety from the institutions, we may go for a solidarity meeting with Jadavpur University and our alumni network, she added. Critiquing the internal response, an alumnus stated that campus officials appear more concerned about safeguarding those who are trying to disturb the peace inside the premises than the safety of the students. Neither the IB Ministry nor the local administration has issued an official security plan for the campus till the filing of this report.

articleTitle: The bone–blood sugar connection: What osteocalcin has to do with glucose control
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bone metabolism and blood sugar regulation
description: Bones are more than structural tissue. An expert explains what research reveals about the possible connection between bone metabolism and blood sugar regulation, and how strong the evidence is.
body_raw: We usually think of bones as the rigid framework that supports the body, protects organs, and stores minerals. Blood sugar regulation, meanwhile, is more commonly associated with the pancreas, liver, muscles and hormones such as insulin. But could the skeleton also have a role in how the body handles glucose? Bone is metabolically active tissue and constantly undergoes processes that build, break down and renew it. This has prompted scientists to investigate whether signals involved in bone metabolism may communicate with other parts of the body, including pathways involved in glucose regulation. The relationship appears to be more complex than simply viewing bones as structural tissue. DISCLAIMER This article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. This connection could have implications for how we understand metabolic health, particularly in people with changes in bone health or blood sugar. However, the existence of a biological link does not necessarily mean that bone health directly determines a persons blood glucose levels. An expert can help explain what is actually known, how strong the evidence is and what remains uncertain. Can bones influence blood sugar regulation? Yes, says Dr Raju Vaishya, senior consultant orthopaedic and joint replacement surgeon at Indraprastha Apollo Hospitals, New Delhi, adding, Bones are not just structural tissue they also act as an endocrine organ. Bone-forming osteoblasts produce osteocalcin, a protein that, in its undercarboxylated form, has been proposed to influence pancreatic beta-cell function, insulin secretion and insulin sensitivity. Dr Vaishya states, Experimental studies suggest osteocalcin can increase insulin production and improve glucose uptake, while insulin signalling in osteoblasts may, in turn, affect osteocalcin activation-creating a potential bonepancreas feedback loop. Bone resorption may also help release signals that influence energy metabolism. However, the human evidence is less definitive than the animal and cellular research, and osteocalcin assays and the clinically relevant form of the hormone remain areas of uncertainty. Other pathways may connect the systems indirectly, including insulin, IGF-1, adipokines, inflammatory signals and mechanical loading. So, the idea that bone metabolism can influence glucose regulation is biologically plausible, but it should not yet be interpreted as proof that changing bone metabolism will directly lower blood glucose in people. What does research show about bone health and insulin sensitivity? Research increasingly shows a two-way association between metabolic dysfunction and skeletal health, Dr Vaishya says, but the relationship is complex. People with type 2 diabetes have a higher risk of fragility fractures even when their bone mineral density is normal or relatively high. Insulin resistance, chronic hyperglycaemia, advanced glycation end-products, inflammation and changes in bone turnover may impair bone quality and microarchitecture. Conversely, the expert shares that bone-derived signals such as osteocalcin may influence glucose metabolism, although the strength of this effect in humans remains uncertain. Prediabetes and insulin resistance have also been associated with altered bone measures in observational studies, but these findings do not establish that poor bone health causes diabetes. Much of the overlap could reflect shared risk factors ageing, excess visceral fat, physical inactivity, smoking, poor diet and some medications can affect both systems. The most defensible conclusion is therefore that bone and glucose metabolism communicate biologically, while common metabolic and lifestyle factors probably explain a substantial part of their clinical association, mentions Dr Vaishya. How can people support bone and metabolic health? Quick Quiz See if you can answer this Which approach best supports both bone and metabolic health? A. Focus mainly on calcium supplements and avoid resistance training. B. Combine resistance and weight-bearing exercise with adequate nutrition, healthy weight management and good blood sugar control. C. Consume as much protein as possible to strengthen bones and muscles. D. Focus only on blood sugar control because bone health is unrelated to diabetes. Reveal the answer Correct answer B Dr Vaishya reveals that many of the same habits support both systems. Resistance and weight-bearing exercise help preserve muscle, improve insulin sensitivity and provide mechanical loading that supports bone. Adequate protein, sufficient dietary calcium and vitamin D, a healthy body weight and good glucose control are also important. People with diabetes should avoid smoking, limit excess alcohol and address fall risk. Protein intake should be individualised, particularly in people with kidney disease. Diabetes can increase fracture risk even when bone density is not low, so fracture history and other osteoporosis risk factors should also be considered. Although research suggests communication between bone and glucose metabolism, areas such as osteocalcin are still being studied and should not yet be presented as established treatments for blood sugar control. articleTitle: India squad for New Zealand series: Bhuvneshwar Kumar returns in T20Is; Jurel to lead IND A
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bhuvneshwar Kumar was called-up in India's T20I side for New Zealand tour. (Sportzpics)
description: Alongside the senior T20I squad, the BCCI also announced the India A side that will travel to New Zealand for three four-day matches against New Zealand A starting October 24.
body_raw: Veteran India pacer Bhuvneshwar Kumar made a stunning return to the national side after a four-year absence, with the Board of Control for Cricket in India BCCI including him in the T20I side for the upcoming tour of New Zealand. The 36-year-olds last international appearance for India came in a T20I against New Zealand at McLean Park in Napier on November 22, 2022. Incidentally, it is the same venue and opponent that will now mark the end of his long exile from the national setup. The decision was taken during a selection meeting held on Tuesday at the ACA Stadium in Guwahati, where the interim head of the selection committee, Pragyan Ojha, along with secretary Devajit Saikia and other selectors, finalised the T20I and India A squads. Bhuvneshwars return is seen as a major boost for Indias white-ball bowling attack, particularly given his expertise in swinging the new ball and his effectiveness during the powerplay overs. ALSO READ  Bhuvneshwar Kumar is back, four years on, with the 2027 World Cup in view The 40-day tour, which begins on October 22, will be the largest mens bilateral cricket series ever held in the country, featuring five T20Is, five ODIs, and two Test matches. The T20I leg will kick off in Christchurch, with subsequent matches in Wellington, Auckland, and Hamilton before the ODI series begins on November 4. The Test matches, scheduled for November 1923 in Wellington and November 27December 1 in Christchurch, will be crucial for both teams ICC World Test Championship final qualification. This tour also marks Indias first Test assignment in New Zealand since 2019 and their first white-ball series in the country since 2022. Alongside the senior T20I squad, the BCCI also announced the India A side that will travel to New Zealand for three four-day matches against New Zealand A starting October 24. The ODI and Test squads for the senior team will be announced later. articleTitle: Bhuvneshwar Kumar is back, four years on, with the 2027 World Cup in view
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bhuvneshwar Kumar
description: India recall the 36-year-old seamer for the T20I tour of New Zealand, and ask whether his body can take the load of ODI cricket again
body_raw: The decision to include Bhuvneshwar Kumar in the T20I squad for tour of New Zealand might have come out of the blue. But the call-up has been gathering pace over the last three months, particularly after the 36-year-olds IPL 2026, where he took 28 wickets and finished one behind Kagiso Rabada in the race for the purple cap. It was during the tour of the UK, after Harshit Rana picked up an injury again, that Bhuvneshwars name started doing the rounds. It is close to four years since Bhuvneshwar last played for India. It was not a case of him suddenly losing his place his last Test was in January 2018, his last ODI in January 2022, and by November that year he was out of the T20I set-up as well. In the domestic circuit, his appearances of late have been limited to the Syed Mushtaq Ali T20s and the IPL, where he has bowled Royal Challengers Bengaluru to successive titles. The India call-up still appeared far-fetched. But here he is again, back in Indias T20I squad for the tour of New Zealand, and not because the first-choice players are busy with other commitments. There is a big picture that Indias team management is hoping Bhuvneshwar will help complete. With India clearly short on balance, there are conversations around the possibility of making the seamer part of the 2027 World Cup. While there is little to no doubt regarding Bhuvneshwars skills and what he offers with the ball, the only question is whether his body can take the load of playing ODI cricket again. He last played the Vijay Hazare Trophy in 2023, and if he is to be considered seriously for next years World Cup in southern Africa, it is understood that India want to see where he stands in terms of fitness and whether he can take the extra load. ALSO READ  Bhuvneshwar Kumar to captain star-studded India in 2026 Hong Kong Sixes He knows it himself, and he wants another World Cup. 100 per cent. You cant beat the feeling of playing in a World Cup, whichever sport it may be, he told Jatin Saprus YouTube channel recently. My body is ready. Ive physio and trainer at home. At this moment, Im ready. Im training, but not keeping the 50-over World Cup on mind, but because I want to. If the selection happens I would be happy. If it doesnt happen, I wont be disappointed, he said. At the end of a long conversation, asked what he might have changed about his career, Bhuvneshwar paused and said where it went wrong. I would have hired the trainer and physio a while back. I wish they were there much earlier with me, he said. Whether that lack of work off the field is why successive team managements looked past him, despite what he brought to the table, is a fair question. But over the last couple of years, the work he has put in has shown in the middle. He has looked unplayable, making the new ball talk with the movement. From Sachin Tendulkar to Virat Kohli, there has been admiration for how Bhuvneshwar exposed batsmen from different eras with his movement off the new ball the wobble seam landing on the surface and moving either way, as he intended. Off the field, Bhuvneshwar appeared more spiritual, a believer in destiny. When I was young, everything was about cricket, want to play for India and take all wickets. But over the years it has changed. I dont recall a game where I went in thinking Ive to take five wickets and I did. So Im someone who believes in destiny. What is written for me will happen. My focus is always on preparation. Ive become more spiritual, he said. He had stopped thinking about comebacks, but he firmly believed he was still a player worth considering. Of course, he said when asked if he should be part of the selection conversations. Im not playing to prove anything, but Id be happy to play for India again. Ive packed my India jersey and kept it. Im emotional at the same time Im not emotional. I wont keep looking at the jersey. I wasnt hurt, and I knew what was happening. I was at peace. My family played a big part in keeping it easy. They dont say anything. They just carried on with daily routine so that played a big part for me, he said of the years he spent in the wilderness. Now, out of nowhere, Bhuvneshwar has an opening. Rarely does Indian cricket go back to a cricketer, particularly a fast bowler, it believed it had moved on from, after four long years. But then not all are Bhuvneshwar Kumar. I have changed a lot as a bowler. When I came in, Id swing, but not much of pace. Without pace, to survive in the death overs with accuracy and perfection isnt possible. I always felt Id to increase the pace, but didnt know how to do it. So the big difference now is pace. It comes with experience. There is a big difference between what I was and what Im now, he said.

articleTitle: Exchanged cash, and a ‘chemical trap’: How ACB caught a Bengal official taking Rs 20k bribe
articleFeaturedImageAlt: West Bengal ACB bribe trap
description: The arrest of a Sub-Assistant Engineer while accepting bribe in West Bengal has shed light on a new 'chemical trap' operation being used by the Anti-Corruption Bureau.
body_raw: A Sub-Assistant Engineer attached to the West Bengal State Rural Development Agency WBSRDA in Hooghly was caught red-handed by the Anti-Corruption Branch ACB while accepting a bribe of Rs 20,000 inside the Zilla Parishad Office in Chinsurah on Tuesday. The operation was initiated following a complaint lodged by a government contractor who had executed a road construction project under the Panchayat Project, valued at approximately Rs 1 crore. The work order for the project was issued in 2023, and construction was completed towards the end of 2025. Subsequently, the contractor approached the officials concerned, seeking the refund of the Earnest Money deposited during the tender process, at which point the official allegedly demanded an illegal gratification to facilitate the release of the funds. Acting on the complaint, ACB officers laid a chemical trap at the Zilla Parishad Office in Chinsurah on Tuesday. The official was intercepted on the spot while accepting a sum of Rs 20,000 from the complainant. Officers seized the entire bribe amount from the Sub-Assistant Engineer, and took him into custody. Further legal proceedings and investigation into the matter are currently underway under relevant provisions of law. In a similar incident in August this year, the ACB officials had arrested another Sub-Assistant Engineer posted at the Jamboni BDO office in Jhargram district for allegedly accepting a bribe of Rs 2 lakh. The engineer was caught red-handed inside his office during another chemical trap operation after demanding illegal gratification from a sub-contractor to clear pending bills related to the construction of a local sub-health centre. The chemical trap operation These days, the Bengal ACB has been relying on a simple chemical test to catch officials red-handed while taking bribes. Before a raid, officers dust the bribe money with phenolphthalein, an almost invisible, fine white powder that adheres to the paper without leaving any visible trace or odour. When the target accepts the cash, the chemical transfers onto their hands, unnoticed. Once the exchange takes place, ACB officers step in and simply ask the suspect to dip their fingers into a bowl of clear, colourless liquid - a basic solution of sodium carbonate. The moment the suspects hands touch the liquid, the invisible chemical reacts with the alkaline base, instantly turning the clear water into a vibrant, bright pink. The rapid colour transformation serves as irrefutable forensic evidence, proving physical possession of the marked notes even if the official denies accepting the bribe. It is done to also send a message of zero tolerance towards corruption, and that anyone caught red-handed will have to face the law, an official said.

articleTitle: Stop daily drama, learn from Modi to win people’s support: BJP to Congress
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Modi
description: Union Minister Kiren Rijiju said Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, should learn from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP on securing people’s support on the basis of work instead of relying on “drama”.
body_raw: Describing the Congress protest against the Election Commission of India as drama, the BJP Tuesday slammed the principal Opposition party and leaders of non-NDA parties who had joined it of abusing the Commission after failing to secure the mandate of the people. Union Minister Kiren Rijiju said Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, should learn from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP on securing peoples support on the basis of work instead of relying on drama. It is time to stop the drama that Rahul Gandhi ji and his colleagues keep doing daily against the Election Commission and the Supreme Court. It has been going on since 2014. In a democracy, serve the people and you will get their mandate, he said. You call the Election Commission a thief, the government a thief. This will neither serve democracy nor the rise of the Congress party again. I especially want to tell Rahul Gandhi ji Learn from Modi ji, from BJP karyakartas who continue to serve, not for their own sakes but selflessly. If you serve them, you will earn the trust of the people. Doing this drama will not help, he said. Asking the Congress to stop peddling the narrative of anti-national forces, Rijiju sought to underline that the party which ruled the country for 55 years, including two years of the Emergency, was now talking of democracy. Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said the Opposition leaders were venting their frustration over electoral defeats by levelling baseless allegations. Friends in the Opposition, the very system you are questioning is the one under which you won in Kerala. Was that victory illegitimate? You won in Karnataka. Was that victory illegitimate? You won in Himachal. Was that victory illegitimate? Opposition governments were formed in Punjab and Jharkhand. Were those victories illegitimate? he said. If you question constitutional institutions, you will commit the sin of plunging the country into the fires of anarchy. Do not commit the sin of plunging the nation into unrest and anarchy. The country and its people will never forgive you, he said. Lok Sabha MP and former Union Minister Ravi Shankar Prasad said Rahul Gandhi, Congress, and the Opposition alliance were attempting to create an atmosphere of anarchy in the country. He said the Supreme Court had held the SIR to be legally valid yet the Congress was insulting the voters of the country by blaming the Election Commission for its repeated electoral defeats. Instead of accepting the peoples verdict, the Congress is trying to undermine democratic institutions and create confusion and disorder through unfounded accusations, Prasad said. The question is whether Rahul Gandhi, the Congress party, and the Opposition alliance want anarchy in the country. Opposition leaders have gathered in Delhi and surrounded a sensitive area of the national Capital. Opposition leaders are claiming that Prime Minister Narendra Modi Ji, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, and Mohan Bhagwat have Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar under their control. This is extremely irresponsible, and we strongly condemn it, he said. He said Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge had gone even further and said that all elections should be cancelled and conducted again through ballot papers which reflects their real intention and desire. Congress leaders cannot win fair elections and, therefore, they now want a return to booth capturing, stamping, and winning elections through pressure by pouring ink into ballot boxes. They want to prevent the poor, Dalits and marginalised sections from voting in villages. This is how the Congress used to win, whether in Bihar or Uttar Pradesh, he said. Addressing the media at the party headquarters, BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra said, The Congress has been repeatedly trying to launch and re-launch Rahul Gandhi by any means necessary. When, despite numerous attempts, he failed to gain traction, the Congress and some of its allies decided that even if it meant resorting to anarchy and undermining the nations democracy, they would launch Rahul Gandhi politically at any cost. In the evening, after the Election Commission issued a statement saying no party had sought an appointment until 4 pm Tuesday and that it was later informed by police that Opposition MPs wanted a meeting at Parliament House Annexe, BJP spokesperson and Rajya Sabha MP Sudhanshu Trivedi slammed Gandhi It is clear that telling the EC anything was not his intention. Neither did he seek any appointment, and when time was given, he did not go. After that, when it was said that a representative would be sent to collect a memorandum from him, he was not ready.

articleTitle: UPSC Prelims 2027 Polity Quiz (Week 183): MCQs on removal of the Chief Election Commissioner, Mahanadi water dispute, and more
articleFeaturedImageAlt: UPSC Prelims 2027 Polity Quiz (Week 183)
description: Are you preparing for UPSC CSE 2027 Prelims? Check your progress and revise your topics through this quiz on Polity and Governance.
body_raw: UPSC Essentialsbrings to you its initiative of daily subject-wise quizzes. These quizzes are designed to help you revise some of the most important topics from the static part of the syllabus. Attempt todays subject quiz onPolity and Governanceto check your progress. As we mark the 3rd anniversary of the UPSC Essentials magazine, we thank our readers for being part of this journey. Your trust, feedback and continued support have shaped the magazine and encouraged us to keep improving with every edition. Click Here to read the UPSC Essentials magazine for September 2026. QUESTION 1 With reference to the removal of the Chief Election Commissioner CEC, consider the following statements 1. A motion for the removal of the CEC can be initiated in either House of Parliament through a notice of motion signed by at least 100 members of the Lok Sabha or 50 members of the Rajya Sabha. 2. The CEC can be removed from office only in like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court. 3. The CEC can be removed only on the ground of proven misbehavior or incapacity. How many of the statements given above are correct? a Only one b Only two c All three d None Relevance The question tests the constitutional provisions governing the appointment, tenure and removal of the Chief Election Commissioner. It is relevant to Article 324, particularly the special protection accorded to the CEC to ensure the independence of the Election Commission. Explanation - Article 3245 of the Constitution states that the CEC can be removed from office only in like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court. Hence, statement 2 is correct. - Going by Article 1244 of the Constitution, which contains the process for removing a Supreme Court judge, removal can only be on the ground of proved misbehavior or incapacity. Misbehaviour can comprise any corrupt practices or abuse of office. Over the years, courts have interpreted this to include actions which are incompatible with the office of the CEC or the CECs failure to discharge her official duties. Incapacity refers to a situation where the officer is unable to perform her duties. Hence, statement 3 is correct. - To initiate the removal of the CEC, members of both Houses must bring a notice of motion explicitly alleging misbehaviour or incapacity. To be admitted, an impeachment motion needs to be signed by at least 100 MPs in the Lok Sabha and 50 in the Rajya Sabha. They can consult people and materials to refuse or admit the motion. If the motion is admitted, an enquiry is conducted to examine the validity of the charges. This involves forming a committee to investigate evidence of misbehaviour or incapacity. Hence, statement 1 is correct. - The motion for removal must secure the support of a majority of the total membership of each House and be passed by a two-thirds majority present and voting in both Houses of Parliament. Once passed successfully, the President orders the removal of the CEC. - There is no discretion once the constitutional requirements are met, since the President acts on the advice of Parliament in this context. Therefore, option c is the correct answer. QUESTION 2 Which of the following states are involved in the Mahanadi water dispute? 1. Telangana 2. Odisha 3. Madhya Pradesh 4. Chhattisgarh Select the correct answer using the codes given below a 1 and 2 only b 2, 3 and 4 only c 2 and 4 only d 1, 2, and 4 only Relevance The question tests knowledge of inter-State river water disputes and the geographical course of the Mahanadi River. It is relevant to Indian Geography, federalism and mechanisms for resolving inter-State water disputes. Explanation - The Mahanadi water dispute between Odisha and Chhattisgarh is back in the spotlight, with the Odisha government signalling that the two BJP-ruled states are moving closer to an amicable solution, even as the Opposition BJD has called this bid an eyewash. The Mahanadi is a lifeline for millions of people in both the States. - A meeting between the two CMs was also held in July under the chairmanship of the Union Jal Shakti Minister. At the meeting, the states agreed to share data and information on their respective water requirements with the Central Water Commission. - For Odisha, the Mahanadi is more than a water-sharing dispute. The river is central to irrigation, drinking water, flood management, hydropower and the states broader negotiations with Chhattisgarh and the Centre. Therefore, option c is the correct answer. QUESTION 3 Consider the following Articles of the Constitution of India 1. Article 1943 - It grants legislatures certain privileges and immunities. 2. Article 191b - It guarantees freedom of speech and expression. Which of the articles given above isare correct? a 1 only b 2 only c Both 1 and 2 d Neither 1 nor 2 Relevance The question tests knowledge of Fundamental Rights under Article 19 and privileges and immunities of State Legislatures under Article 194. It helps strengthen understanding of constitutional provisions relating to State Legislatures and legislative privileges. Explanation - The Supreme Court will begin hearing a long-pending reference on the scope of legislative privileges, special powers and immunities enjoyed by Parliament and state legislatures to protect their functioning, and whether they can be invoked against citizens, journalists and others on breaching the privileges of the House. At the heart of the case is whether these privileges, under Articles 105 and 194 of the Constitution, can override fundamental rights such as freedom of speech and expression under Article 19. - A seven-judge Constitutional Bench comprising the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Aravind Kumar, Prashant Kumar Mishra, Joymalya Bagchi, Vipul M Pancholi, Chandrashekhar and V Mohana will hear the matter. - Article 1943 of the Constitution grants legislatures certain privileges and immunities. Article 191a guarantees freedom of speech and expression, including press freedom. The case turns on the interplay between these two rights and whether legislative privilege can override the right to free speech. Hence, 1 is correct and 2 is not correct. - Articles 14 and 21 provide for the right to equality and the right to life. The petitioners argue that when legislatures order arrests or imprisonment for alleged breaches of privilege, they affect personal liberty. According to them, any action affecting liberty must satisfy constitutional guarantees of fairness, due process and protection against arbitrariness. Therefore, option a is the correct answer. QUESTION 4 With reference to the Bye-Elections also known as bypolls, consider the following statements 1. The winner of a by-election serves a full 5-year term. 2. A bypoll is not mandatory if the remaining term of the house is less than 1 year. 3. Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, by-elections must be held within 3 months of the vacancy occurring, barring specific legal exceptions. How many of the statements given above are correct? a Only one b Only two c All three d None Relevance The question tests understanding of the constitutional and statutory framework governing by-elections in India. It is relevant to Section 151A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, including the time limit and exceptions for conducting bypolls. Explanation - Bye-Elections also known as bypolls are used to fill elected offices that have become vacant between general elections. - The elected representative serves only the remainder of the term left by the predecessor. Hence, statement 1 is not correct. - A bypoll is not mandatory if the remaining term of the house is less than 1 year, or if the Election Commission certifies that holding it is impractical due to extraordinary circumstances. Hence, statement 2 is correct. - Under Section 151A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, by-elections must be held within 6 months of the vacancy occurring, barring specific legal exceptions. Hence, statement 3 is not correct. Therefore, option a is the correct answer. Source www.eci.gov.in QUESTION 5 With reference to the Legislative Councils in India, consider the following statements 1. The total number of members in the Legislative Council of a State having such a Council shall not exceed one-half 50 per cent of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of that State. 2. The total number of members in the Legislative Council of a State shall in no case be less than forty. Which of the statements given above isare correct? a 1 only b 2 only c Both 1 and 2 d Neither 1 nor 2 Relevance The question tests knowledge of the constitutional provisions governing Legislative Councils under Article 171. It is relevant for understanding State legislature, bicameralism and constitutional provisions related to State legislatures. Explanation - The total number of members in the Legislative Council of a State having such a Council shall not exceed one-thirdof the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of that State. Hence, statement 1 is not correct. - Provided that the total number of members in the Legislative Council of a State shall in no case be less than forty. Hence, statement 2 is correct. - Of the total number of members of the Legislative Council of a State- a as nearly as may be, one-third shall be elected by electorates consisting of members of municipalities, district boards and such other local authorities in the State as Parliament may by law specify b as nearly as may be, one-twelfth shall be elected by electorates consisting of persons residing in the State who have been for at least three years graduates of any university in the territory of India or have been for at least three years in possession of qualifications prescribed by or under any law made by Parliament as equivalent to that of a graduate of any such university c as nearly as may be, one-twelfth shall be elected by electorates consisting of persons who have been for at least three years engaged in teaching in such educational institutions within the State, not lower in standard than that of a secondary school, as may be prescribed by or under any law made by Parliament d as nearly as may be, one-third shall be elected by the members of the Legislative Assembly of the State from amongst persons who are not members of the Assembly e the remainder shall be nominated by the Governor. articleTitle: CBI books OSD to Punjab CM for graft, searches Mann’s ‘camp office’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rajbir Singh Guman, an OSD to Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann
description: Searches come hours after Supreme Court agreed to hear a Punjab govt challenge to HC order directing CBI probe into corruption allegations
body_raw: The CBI on Tuesday registered a corruption case against Rajbir Singh Guman, an OSD to Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, and other senior officials and conducted searches at eight locations, including Manns camp office in Chandigarh, officials said. Mann said that the BJP has started preparing for Punjab elections and was now resorting to central agencies to target him and his government. The CBI, in a statement, said that following the orders of the Punjab and Haryana High Court, and receipt of report from the Enforcement Directorate, it has registered an FIR to investigate the allegations of corruption against OSD to Punjab Chief Minister CM and his associates for influencing and manipulating postings of officers including that of IAS and IPS officers, departmental proceedings, matters pertaining to policy formulation, administrative approvals, tender conditions, licensing matters, land use conversion matters, property disputes, revenue and land related issues in lieu of pecuniary benefits. It is also alleged that the accused public servants purportedly accessed and provided drafts of orders and policies to private persons prior to their issuance by the government, the CBI statement said, adding the agency has booked six persons, including two public servants. They include Ghuman, alleged middleman Nitin Gohal, Jitin Gohal alias Raja, Romi Raja Mahajan, Bir Devinder, RS Nagra and unknown public servants and private persons, it added. The central agency carried out raids at House No. 50, the camp office allotted to Mann under the Chief Ministers pool, where Ghuman had been staying. It also conducted searches at Ghumans residence in Gharachon in Sangrur district apart from locations in Mohali, Gurdaspur, Ludhiana, Patiala, and Jalandhar connected with the accused persons. Incriminating evidence such as laptops, mobile phones and documents have been seized. These are being scrutinized for evidence of bribery and impropriety. Further investigation in the case is in progress, read the CBI statement. The raids came hours after the Supreme Court agreed to hear a Punjab government plea challenging a Punjab and Haryana High Courts order directing the CBI to investigate Ghuman and others. The high court, in its order on Monday, had held that material shared by the ED with Punjab DGP in the matter prima facie indicated their involvement in acts of corruption, including cash for transfers and cash for favourable orders. The state filed a Special Leave Petition at around 2am in the Supreme Court against the HC order. Reacting to the development, Mann, in a post on X, said, BJP has started preparing for the Punjab elections.CBI raided my camp office. Now, ED and CBI will be misused in Punjab, so that Punjab government and I can be defamed. Seeing the love we are getting from the people, BJP is nervous, Mann said. The high court order came on on a PIL filed by advocate Nikhil Saraf, who had sought an independent probe into the matter raised by the ED with the Punjab Police in its letters to the DGP. The ED had written to the DGP seeking registration of an FIR against an alleged middleman and others, reportedly linked to the Chief Ministers Office, for allegedly influencing transfers and postings of government officials, facilitating arms licence approvals, leaking confidential government documents and securing government approvals in lieu of alleged monetary and other benefits. The EDs letters stem from a money laundering investigation linked to the submission of alleged fake consent letters for obtaining Change of Land Use CLU in a case involving a housing society. The ED had conducted searches on the premises of Nitin Gohal, Ajay Sehgal of Indian Cooperative House Building Society, the Suntec City Project and some others in May. The agency had submitted 200-page affidavit in the high court on the PIL filed by Saraf. The searches took place against the backdrop of an escalating confrontation between the Punjab government and central investigative agencies. The Mann government has repeatedly accused the Centre of using the ED and CBI to target opposition-ruled states, while the BJP has rejected such allegations and maintained that investigative agencies act independently.

articleTitle: After airlines push back, Centre pauses Mumbai airport’s flight cut plan
articleFeaturedImageAlt: mumbai airport flight cut plan
description: Adani-run CSMIA wanted to drop 265 weekly international departures from October 25 to make room for domestic flights. It must now draw up a fresh plan with regulatory approvals
body_raw: The Union government has put on hold a plan by Mumbais Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport CSMIA to cut international departures from Terminal 2 by 33 per cent, after airlines pushed back against the move, sources said. The decision came on Tuesday, the deadline the airport operator had set for airlines to choose which international flights they would give up from October 25. At a meeting chaired by Union Civil Aviation Secretary Samir Sinha on Tuesday afternoon, the Ministry of Civil Aviation directed Adani Airports Holdings Limited AAHL, which runs CSMIA, to call another meeting of all stakeholders and draw up a fresh transition plan, according to those familiar with the matter. Airlines and industry bodies, including the International Air Transport Association IATA and the Federation of Indian Airlines FIA, attended the meeting. AAHL will now seek approvals from the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security BCAS, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation DGCA and state authorities before it goes ahead with a revised plan, sources said. The airport operator had told airlines it would cut 265 weekly international departures from Terminal 2 from October 25, to make room for domestic flights moving in from Terminal 1B. Indian carriers accounted for 125 of these. IndiGo would have lost 74 flights, Air India 33, Akasa Air 11 and Air India Express seven. The remaining 140 belonged to foreign airlines. Airlines were asked to volunteer the slots they would temporarily drop by October 6. If they didnt, the operator said it would pick the slots itself based on operational considerations. This followed an earlier directive from the operator asking airlines to either move their Terminal 1B operations to Navi Mumbai International Airport NMIA or suspend them from October 25. Airlines objected, citing the impact on existing operations. IATA also sought a transparent assessment of NMIAs capacity before flights were shifted there, covering ground handling, cargo facilities, crew accommodation and connectivity. The changes are tied to the planned demolition of the northern section of Terminal 1B in January 2027. That section handles around five million passengers a year, nearly a third of Terminal 1s footfall. Redevelopment of the terminal is expected to be completed by 2029-30. The airport operator, airlines and other stakeholders will now discuss a fresh plan before any operational changes are made.

articleTitle: ‘You are licking an ice cube’: Vijay Deverakonda recalls cutting water intake for Liger
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vijay Deverakonda
description: Vijay Deverakonda’s candid account of his Liger prep reveals just how far actors can go for a shredded look
body_raw: Vijay Deverakonda recently opened up about cutting his water intake for the film Liger. I did it during Liger.where the water was cut down to make my body look shredded. It is not healthy or good at all. It starts with four or six litres of water and slowly cuts it down to 300 ml to 100 ml. 10 hours before the shoot, you dont drink water. You are licking an ice cube. Its a random t, the Ranabaali actor told Sudhir Srinivasan on his YouTube podcast. Bodybuilders and all do it. Every second from the time I was drinking 300 ml of water a day.every minute.you are like..water.water.water. When I was licking that ice cube and was not allowed water, I was sleeping thinking of water. I knew I had to go four hours without water, and then I could drink. I asked my team for coconut water and to get four litres of it. I didnt want food or anything, the 37-year-old added. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. During the conversation, he also mentioned that he has tried fasting but failed many times. Intermittent is easy. Some people fast for 48 or 72 hours. I have managed just about 24 hours fast once. I have tried six times and given up five times. Taking a leaf out of his candid admission, we asked experts about cutting water intake and how it impacts the body. From a nutrition and sports-health perspective, consultant dietitian and fitness expert Garima Goyal noted that this is not a healthy fat-loss strategy. Athletes and bodybuilders sometimes use short-term dehydration protocols before competitions or photoshoots to alter appearance, but these practices are highly context-dependent and can carry risks. The general public should not copy them as a weight-loss method. Severe water restriction causes dehydration, not meaningful fat loss. The temporary shredded appearance happens because reduced body water can make muscles and skin appear tighter and more defined, said Goyal. But the risks can be significant. Severe dehydration can lead to dizziness, weakness, headaches, low blood pressure, impaired concentration, reduced exercise performance and electrolyte disturbances. In more extreme situations, dehydration and electrolyte imbalance can affect kidney function and cardiovascular health, Goyal told indianexpress.com. What is particularly concerning for general people is that dehydration can be mistaken for successful weight loss. The number on the weighing scale may fall rapidly because water is being lost, but that does not mean the person has suddenly lost the same amount of body fat. Once normal hydration resumes, much of that weight returns, clarified Goyal. Can drinking only 100300 ml of water a day be dangerous? For most adults, that is far below normal fluid requirements, although individual needs vary. Such extreme restriction can result in significant dehydration, particularly if the person is exercising, sweating or working in a hot environment. It can also disturb the bodys electrolyte balance, which in severe cases can affect the heart and nervous system, said Dr Amit Sara, director, internal medicine, Jupiter Hospital Thane. Is licking ice or drinking coconut water enough to prevent dehydration? No, noted Dr Sarf. Licking an ice cube provides very little fluid and does not compensate for severe water restriction. Coconut water contains fluids and electrolytes, but it should not be considered a substitute for adequate hydration, particularly when someone has deliberately restricted fluids for several hours, said Dr Saraf. Extreme thirst, very little or dark-coloured urine, dizziness, confusion, unusual weakness, fainting, rapid heartbeat or inability to keep fluids down are warning signs that should not be ignored. Severe dehydration can become a medical emergency and may require prompt fluid and electrolyte replacement, said Dr Saraf. Vijays experience also highlights an important distinction looking extremely lean for a few hours is very different from being healthy and maintaining a sustainable body composition. For fat loss, the focus should remain on an appropriate calorie deficit, adequate protein, resistance training, recovery and proper hydration rather than manipulating body water. A shredded look is temporary. Dehydration is not a shortcut to sustainable fat loss, said Goyal. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine.

articleTitle: ‘Don’t sleep…’: How dentist Shota Musaev helped save flydubai captain Smit Machchhar after cockpit attack
articleFeaturedImageAlt: flydubai, smit machchhar, dentist
description: Dentist Musaev said he and other passengers rushed towards the flydubai's FZ1073 plane cockpit after hearing screams. Inside, he saw Machchhar on the floor, bleeding heavily from wounds to his head.
body_raw: Dr Shota Musaev, a Georgian dentist living in Israel, boarded flydubai flight FZ1073 as an ordinary passenger. Minutes later, after the co-pilot attacked Indian Captain Smit Machchhar in the cockpit, Musaev found himself treating the badly wounded pilot as the aircraft diverted to Saudi Arabia. Speaking to ABC News, Musaev said he and other passengers rushed towards the cockpit after hearing screams. Inside, he saw Machchhar on the floor, bleeding heavily from wounds to his head, neck and hands. How Dr Shota Musaev treated injured Indian pilot Saying that he didnt hesitate to do something, the dentist said, I think, how can I help this situation for all the passengers on the plane? How can I help? And I see one pilot on the floor, with.blood. After passengers subdued the co-pilot, Musaev turned his attention to Machchhar and treated the injured captain for about 45 minutes, according to an interview with The National. He also helped passengers restrain the attacker using headphone cables. The aircraft had been cruising at about 34,000 feet when the cockpit confrontation sent it into a steep descent before it was diverted to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. Two standby flydubai pilots who had been travelling as passengers then entered the cockpit and helped stabilise the aircraft before it landed in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.  I used T-shirts to press the wounds There was heavy bleeding from his head and left hand. I used T-shirts to press the wounds, but it the bleeding didnt stop, so I asked the stewards for ice, Dr Musaev told The National. Musaev also monitored Machchhars vital signs. At one point, he said, the captains pulse became dangerously low, prompting him to raise Machchhars feet. Later, when he noticed that the pilots lips had turned blue, he told a steward We need to land quickly. He doesnt have much more time. The Israel-based dentist added, He had very, very deep cuts and we needed many ice packets. But every time I opened the T-shirt to check the bleeding, it would bleed more. So I pressed not very hard and used ice. All through the 45 minutes, I kept the pressure on. How Musaev kept captain Machchhar conscious Dr Musaev said that he was trying to keep Captain Machchhar, who was seriously wounded in the attack by the Omani co-pilot, conscious by talking to him as he gave emergency aid to the Indian pilot. I told him, Please dont sleep, we need you. I asked how many children he had and their names. I kept telling him, Dont be afraid you will go back to your family we are landing soon.He was cut badly and would say, Im feeling hot on my hands. I kept telling him that he would be OK, Musaev said. Musaev said Machchhar repeatedly asked for help and told him he wanted to live. The captain also complained of pain in his head and a burning sensation in his hands, according to the dentist. Captain Machchhar wants to meet the dentist In a phone call with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on October 3, Machchhar said he would like to meet Musaev, who had treated him after the attack. Musaev has rejected the idea that he alone was responsible for saving Machchhar, instead crediting the passengers and crew who intervened during the crisis. Everyone in the plane is a hero, he told The National. Smit saved our lives and we saved his life. Musaev, 47, was travelling with his wife, Sigalit, from China via Dubai to Israel when he heard screams and later a call for a doctor. After the emergency landing in Tabuk, Musaev said the experience continued to affect him and his wife. He told The National that they were sleeping only about two hours a night and that he had lost three kilograms in three days.

articleTitle: Why cutting short-lived climate pollutants is a key climate priority
articleFeaturedImageAlt: SLCPs, India, climate change
description: Unlike CO₂, many short-lived climate pollutants (SLCPs) have shorter atmospheric lifetimes but can have severe effects on climate, health, and food security. What are the major sources of SLCPs, and how do they intensify these concerns for a country like India? And what efforts are underway to cut their emissions? See infographics.
body_raw: - Abhinav Rai  Short-lived climate pollutants SLCPs are responsible for up to 45 of current global warming and also contribute significantly to air pollution. Fast and immediate action on SLCPs can, therefore, help both in climate mitigation and air quality improvement. According to a 2018 Special Report on 1.5C by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change IPCC, cutting the emission of SLCPs can help avoid over half a degree of warming by 2050 and over 50 of predicted warming in the Arctic by 2050. It can also significantly reduce the risk of triggering dangerous climate tipping points, like the irreversible release of carbon dioxide and methane from thawing Arctic permafrost. But what exactly are SLCPs, where do they come from, and how do they affect the climate? Short-lived climate pollutants and their sources Short-lived climate pollutants SLCPs are also referred to as super pollutants or short-lived climate forcers SLCFs. The IPCC defines SLCFs as a group of physical and chemical compounds that have a lifespan shorter than that of carbon dioxide CO, but have significantly higher capability to increase the rate of global warming. While CO can remain in the atmosphere for hundreds of years, many SLCPs can persist in the atmosphere from a few days to two decades. The most significant SLCPs include black carbon, methane CH4, ozone O3, hydrofluorocarbons HFCs, hydrochlorofluorocarbons HCFCs and aerosols sulphate, nitrate, ammonium, carbonaceous aerosols, mineral dust, sea spray. Black carbon It is mainly a result of anthropogenic factors like incomplete combustion of biomass, burning of fossil fuels, stubble burning and forest fires. It is a strong climate-warming agent and contributes to poor air quality. The Indo-Gangetic Plain is a black carbon hotspot because of high population density, reliance on biomass burning for cooking and heating, open burning of agricultural residue or stubble burning to clear the paddy fields, and other combustion sources. Methane It is generated primarily during agricultural activities, like rice cultivation and livestock, and during the extraction and processing of fossil fuels and waste disposal. Methane has about 80 times more warming power compared to CO2 in its first 20 years in the atmosphere. It is also the second largest contributor to global warming after CO2, and a major source of tropospheric ozone O3 production. Hydrofluorocarbons HFCs HFCs are primarily used in cooling equipment such as refrigerators and air-conditioners and they can have hundreds to thousands of times greater impact on global warming compared to CO2. Although their share in GHGs is comparatively small, HFC emissions can increase with the growing demand for cooling equipment globally and especially in sub-tropical countries like India. Ozone O3 In the atmosphere, Ozone O3 can be classified into two types Stratospheric Ozone found between 10-50km above Earths surface and the tropospheric Ozone found up to 10km above Earths surface. The stratospheric ozone acts as a protective layer from the incoming ultraviolet radiation from the Sun. In contrast, tropospheric ozone is an air pollutant and a powerful greenhouse gas that adversely affects human health and reduces crop yields and agricultural productivity. O3 does not have any direct source of emission. It is produced when volatile organic compounds VOCs, methane or nitrogen oxides interact with sunlight. Impact on climate, health, and food security Black carbon, when deposited on snow or ice, darkens its colour, which reduces albedo sunlight reflecting ability and increases the absorption of more sunlight, which further warms the snowice and enhances the rate of melting. Now the cryospheric regions are warming two to three times faster than the global average. Black carbon also affects the formation of clouds and moisture transport, reducing the amount of snowfall and seasonal nourishment of glaciers. SLCPs are a significant contributor to air pollution. Black carbon is one of the most harmful components of fine particulate matter PM 2.5 air pollution. Long-term exposure to black carbon is linked to diseases such as chronic respiratory illness, asthma, pneumonia, heart disease, lung cancer, etc. About 7 million premature deaths are globally caused by problems associated with air pollution both indoor and outdoor every year, according to the Climate and Clean Air Coalition CCAC, an initiative by the United Nations Environment Program UNEP. Moreover, air pollution also reduces the growth of staple crops like rice, corn, soya and wheat. Black carbon obstructs the incoming sunlight and also disrupts rainfall patterns, affecting crop health. Indias air pollution and water-security challenge Indias air pollution levels are among the highest in the world, posing a very serious public health and economic challenge. An estimated 1.67 million deaths or 17.8 of all deaths in the country in 2019 are attributed to air pollution, according to a Lancet Planetary Health study. The study also suggested that these diseases and premature deaths caused an economic loss of around US36.8 billion, which was equivalent to 1.36 of Indias GDP at the time. In addition, a 2025 report by Clean Air Fund, backed by the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development ICIMOD, found that black carbon is accelerating the melting of glacier ice and ice sheets across the global cryosphere, including the Arctic and the Hindu Kush-Himalaya region. It found that about 60 of South Asias black carbon comes from residential fuel combustion. While more than one-fifth of Indias GDP is underpinned by the Himalayas, the accelerating glacier ice loss is also a water-security issue for the countrys glacier-fed Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra basins. According to the Global Methane Status Report 2025, India emitted 9 of total global methane emissions, the third largest globally after the US and China, where stubble burning was identified as a growing hotspot. Notably, Indias third Biennial Update Report suggests that the countrys methane emissions in 2016 largely came from agriculture 73.96, the waste sector14.46, and the energy sector 10.62. Efforts to cut SLCPs Efforts to address SLCPs are underway. For instance, a 2016 amendment to the Montreal Protocol, adopted in 1987 for protecting Earths depleting Ozone layer, called for the phase-down of hydrofluorocarbons HFCs by more than 80 by the late 2040s. India ratified this amendment, also known as the Kigali amendment, in 2021. During COP26 2021, the Global Methane Pledge initiative was launched with the aim of significantly reducing methane emissions 30 from 2020 levels by 2030, and is currently joined by 159 countries and the European Commission. However, India has not joined it yet. Two major sources of methane emissions are paddy cultivation and livestock, and India considers them as survival emissions because a large population and food security is dependent on these. In the last couple of decades, the problem of air pollution has become severe in India, especially in northern states. Several steps have been taken since the enactment of The Air Prevention and Control of Pollution Act in 1981 and notification of National Ambient Air Quality Standards NAAQS in 2009 for 12 air pollutants, including particulate matter PM10 and PM2.5, and Ozone O. These include the launch of the National Air Quality Index AQI in 2015, the Graded Response Action Plan GRAP in 2017 in the Delhi-NCR region, joining the UNEP-led CCAC in 2019 and also launching the National Clean Air Programme NCAP in 130 cities of 24 States Under NCAP, performance-linked grants are provided to the cities for implementing pollution mitigation measures. According to the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, during 2025-26, only 65 cities under NCAP a total of 130 cities have been able to check their PM2.5 levels below the standard   40 gm under NAAQS, where Delhi recorded 102 g Similarly, regarding PM10 concentrations, even though more cities showed progress than before, only 14 cities met the NAAQS  60 gm3 during 2025-26. Way forward To slow down the current rate of global warming, decarbonisation efforts remain important. But these efforts need to be complemented by rapid reductions in SLCPs. Since many SLCPs have short lifetimes, reducing their emissions can lower their atmospheric concentrations and climate impacts within years or decades. Effective reduction in SLCPs can reduce global warming up to 0.6C by 2050. Although India has taken several steps, greater attention needs to be paid to ensuring access to cleaner cooking fuel, effective management of crop residue, and reducing air pollution levels. Schemes such as Galvanising Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan GOBARdhan can be scaled up. The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, which provided over 10.5 crore LPG connections, has expanded access to cleaner fuel, but ensuring sustained refills remains an issue. For India, cutting SLCPs can deliver multiple benefits, including cleaner air, higher crop yields, and slower ice loss in the Himalaya, alongside climate mitigation. Post read questions 1. What are Short-Lived Climate Pollutants SLCPs? Discuss their major sources and their significance in addressing climate change and air pollution. 2. What is the role of black carbon in accelerating snow and glacier melt? Discuss its implications for water security in the Himalayan region. 3. How can reduction of short-lived climate pollutants contribute to Indias climate mitigation strategy? 4. Discuss the major sources of short-lived climate pollutants in India. What measures can be adopted to reduce their emissions while ensuring energy, food and livelihood security? 5. Indias efforts to tackle air pollution have significant implications for its climate objectives. Discuss with reference to NCAP, clean cooking, crop-residue management and methane reduction. Abhinav Rai is a Doctoral candidate at the Department of Geography, Delhi School of Economics, University of Delhi.
