That skill will really really take you very far. This is what I can tell you, thank you for witnessing this Everyone is running, doing one thing or the other. Just pause for a minute.  Several clips from the event instantly went viral on social media, as fans were shocked with Vidyuts technique. Master a person wrote. He is actually good bro, another commented. Wowww. Kaise kia ye, a third comment read. About Street Fighter Vidyut Jammwal is set to mark his Hollywood debut with Street Fighter. The actor will play the iconic yoga master and warrior Dhalsim. The Paramount Pictures release is set to hit the big screen in India on October 16. The film will be released in English, Hindi, Tamil and Telugu.

articleTitle: At least 12 Indian sailors injured in attacks in Black Sea, Hormuz; MEA condemns
articleFeaturedImageAlt: MEA: A motorboat travels past commercial vessels appear anchored in the Strait of Hormuz
description: The targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers and civilian infrastructure in the region must end, the MEA reiterated, and urged for the earliest restoration of navigation and commerce through international waterways.
body_raw: With Indian seafarers being injured in two separate attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and the Black Sea, the Ministry of External Affairs MEA on Tuesday condemned the incidents and expressed deep concern over the targeting of commercial shipping. Eleven Indian crew members were injured after a Panama-flagged vessel was hit by a projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday. In the other incident, at least two foreign crew members were killed and some others, including an Indian, were injured after a Russian drone strike caused a fire on a Turkish-owned civilian cargo vessel in the Black Sea on Monday. We condemn the attack earlier today on a Panama-flagged commercial vessel, MT On Peace, off the coast of Oman, where it was struck by a projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, the MEA said in a statement. Of the total crew of 19, 17 are Indian nationals. It is learnt that 12 crew members have been injured, including 11 Indian nationals, it said. With the assistance of Omani authorities, the injured crew have since been evacuated and are receiving medical treatment in Khasab, Oman. We thank the Omani authorities for their valuable support, it said. The MEA said the continuing incidents of attacks on shipping in the region remain a cause of deep concern for India. We reiterate our call for an immediate cessation of such attacks in the interests of peace and stability in the region, it said. The targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers and civilian infrastructure in the region must end, and navigation and commerce through international waterways must be restored at the earliest, the MEA said. In the other incident, the Indian Embassy in Romania reported that there were three Indian nationals among the crew members and one of them has been injured and is receiving medical attention. We have learnt of an attack today on commercial vessel MV Royad Mammadov in the Black Sea. As per preliminary information, there have been 2 casualties foreign nationals while some crew members have been injured and are undergoing medical treatment in Romania. It is further reported that there are three Indian nationals among the crew members, the mission posted on X. It said all three Indians are safe and in good health. We condemn the attack on MV Royad Mammadov in the Black Sea in which two foreign seafarers were killed and some members of the crew, including Indian nationals, injured. The injured have been rescued by Romanian authorities and are receiving medical attention. The three Indian nationals, who were part of the crew, are safe. We thank Romanian authorities for their swift action in this incident, the MEA said. India views these attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers with grave concern, it said. The targeting of traffic in international waterways is severely undermining global commerce and welfare of people across the world. We continue to call for dialogue and diplomacy to bring an end to the ongoing conflicts. Indian seafarers account for almost 12 per cent of the global maritime community. According to sources, at least nine Indian seafarers have died, one is presumed dead, and seven have been injured since the start of the West Asia crisis, until July this year. There have been at least 29 incidents of attacks on vessels carrying Indian seafarers - four involving Indian-flagged vessels and the rest involving foreign-flagged vessels. In the Black Sea, too, Indian seafarers have been victims of attacks from both Russia and Ukraine. In fact, India started actively pushing for Russia-Ukraine peace after Indian seafarers were hit by such attacks. In September 2026, India and Liberia launched a 25-nation Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers during the UN General Assembly to ensure safety and security of merchant crews and commercial shipping against targeted attacks, the MEA said. With PTI, London

articleTitle: Top 10 countries for retirement report and index 2026: How Uruguay beat Spain and Portugal to top spot
articleFeaturedImageAlt: travel
description: Top 10 countries for retirement report and index 2026 list: Know more about the world's 10 best countries for retirees seeking financial security, superior healthcare, and an exceptional lifestyle.
body_raw: Top 10 countries for retirement report and index 2026 Uruguay has been named the best country in the world for retirees, taking the No. 1 spot in the annual Global Retirement Report and Index 2026 published by Global Citizen Solutions. The overall rankings are derived from a composite score calculated across five weighted pillars quality of life, mobility and citizenship, tax, cost and investment, and administrative procedure, including processing speed and family inclusion. With a near-perfect score of 99.90, Uruguay emerged as the worlds premier retirement destination and was one of only two top-10 nations to score at least 75 in every evaluation category. Mauritius, Spain, and Costa Rica were ranked at No. 2, 3, and 4, respectively. Portugal, Paraguay, and Latvia were ranked at No. 5, 6, and 7, respectively. Andorra and Italy were ranked 8th and 9th, respectively, while Greece closed out the top 10 list. A primary driver behind Uruguays top ranking is its streamlined immigration and naturalisation pathway. Eligible applicants can apply directly for citizenship without completing a prior temporary residency period. The index also highlights Uruguays manageable monthly income requirement of 1,700, along with short routes to naturalisation three years for married applicants and five years for single applicants. According to the report, the modern concept of retirement has shifted away from simply withdrawing from active life. Patricia Casaburi, CEO of Global Citizen Solutions, noted that the concept of retirement has changed over the years. Earlier, retirement was closely tied to withdrawing from active life. But lately, retirement has become a deliberate new chapter. Casaburi added that retirement involves more than safety. Quality of life after retirement also has to be healthier, lighter in taxes, and richer in possibility than the life left behind, Casaburi said. Rank Country 1. Uruguay 2. Mauritius 3. Spain 4. Costa Rica 5. Portugal 6. Paraguay 7. Latvia 8. Andorra 9. Italy 10. Greece

articleTitle: ED summons Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann’s brother-in-law in graft case
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Defector MPs to dissenting MLAs: How AAP cracks widen on eve of Punjab polls
description: Grewal is associated with the Punjabi film industry and is linked to East Sunshine Production Pvt. Ltd. The company’s corporate records list Amardeep Grewal Singh as one of its directors.
body_raw: The Enforcement Directorate ED on Tuesday summoned Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Manns brother-in-law Amardeep Singh Grewal in connection with its probe into the alleged corrupt practices by senior officials linked to the Chief Ministers Office including cash for transfers and cash for getting favourable policies. ED had initially issued summons to Grewal for October 7, but following an appeal, he has been asked to appear at the federal agencys Delhi office on October 9, a source privy to the developments said. Grewal is associated with the Punjabi film industry and is linked to East Sunshine Production Pvt. Ltd. The companys corporate records list Grewal as one of its directors. He has been associated with various Punjabi films, including Maujaan Hi Maujaan 2023 and Snowman 2022, having overseas productionrelease linkages, an ED official said. On Monday, a the Punjab and Haryana High Court ordered the CBI to register an FIR and investigate the allegations of corruption against Punjab government officials, Rajbir Singh Ghuman an officer to special duty OSD to CM, saying the material shared by the ED prima facie substantiated the commission of cognisable offences. The Punjab government on Tuesday challenged the order in the Supreme Court. The high court order came on a PIL filed by advocate Nikhil Saraf, who sought a CBI probe into issues raised by the ED in a letter sent to Punjab Director General of Police Gaurav Yadav. The petition contended that the allegations raised serious questions about the state governments functioning and warranted an independent investigation outside the Punjab Police and Vigilance Bureau. In its communication to the DGP, the had agency sought registration of a criminal case against Ghuman and his alleged associates, Nitin Gohal and Bir Devinder. According to the communication, the three allegedly interfered in the transfer and posting of government officials, government work and tender processes. The agency also referred to material purportedly indicating attempts to influence postings, access confidential government documents and interfere in administrative approvals and other official processes.

articleTitle: ‘Seen him shouting at stars’: Raza Murad compares ‘perfectionists’ Bhansali, Raj Kapoor
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Raj Kapoor, Sanjay Leela Bhansali
description: Raza Murad recalled working with Raj Kapoor and Sanjay Leela Bhansali, saying both filmmakers are perfectionists who know how to get the best out of sensitive actors.
body_raw: Veteran actor Raza Murad, known for speaking his mind, recently took a sharp dig at the big stars of the film industry for skipping the last rites of Welcome actor Mushtaq Khan. And now, in a recent interview with Vickey Lalwani, the seasoned actor also opened up about the similarities between filmmakers Raj Kapoor and Sanjay Leela Bhansali, and why he considers both of them perfectionists. Raza Murad says Sanjay Leela Bhansali is a perfectionist Sanjay Leela Bhansali is a perfectionist, said Raza Murad. The host then asked him about reports of the filmmaker being moody and losing his temper. Responding to this, the actor said, See, about the anger, when you are consistently unable to understand what hes trying to say, then he loses his cool. Its not like he is angry right from the start. And, of course, every person has their own temperament, and that anger isnt personal, its related to work because it isnt happening properly. So, its fine, if hes getting angry. And, its not like he only loses his temper at his assistants. I have seen him shouting at bigger stars as well. When asked if he had seen Bhansali shout at Ranveer Singh, Deepika Padukone or Priyanka Chopra, Raza said, Yes, he wants what he wants, and of course, I have seen him getting angry at stars as well. Both of them are perfectionists Drawing a parallel between Bhansali and Raj Kapoor, Raza said both filmmakers wouldnt compromise when it came to their work. Speaking about how he would rate the two filmmakers, the Padmaavat actor stated, Both of them are perfectionists. They want what they want. Time, shift, money, set, dates were of least importance to them. Its okay, if it takes eight days instead of four days. And, when they are on set, they mean business. Hum kaam karne ke liye aaye hain We have come here to work. And, this has happened twice with me. Raza then recalled his first experience of working with Raj Kapoor in Prem Rog 1982. When I was working for the first time with Raj saab in Prem Rog. It was my first day, and meri kya aukaat thi unke saamne What was my status in front of him?. Despite stiff opposition from his sons stating that I wouldnt suit the role. and I was a small time actor, Raj saab said, Ye role karenge toh Raza saahab hi karenge If theres someone, who can do this role, its only Raza sir. He made me meet everyone on the set like I was some head of the state. Also Read Staff touched Bollywood stars feet Sabeer Bhatia says celeb worship shocked American guests Raza recalls similar experience with Sanjay Leela Bhansali Raza said he experienced a similar gesture from the Devdas filmmaker when he first worked with him. And the same thing happened with Sanjay Leela Bhansali, the first day when I went on his set, he also called his entire unit and introduced me to them saying, Raza saab is working with us. So, this was common in both filmmakers Raj Kapoor and Sanjay Leela Bhansali. They gave me a lot of respect and importance. He would get angry at heroines The host then asked Raza if Raj Kapoor would get angry at stars in the same way Sanjay Leela Bhansali does. The Prem Rog actor recalled, Actors are extremely sensitive but they directors know how to get work done from them. He would get angry at heroines, Kya kar rahi hai tu? Ye kya kar rahi hai? Aise mat kar What are you doing? What is this that you are doing? Dont do it. Youre not listening to me. Leave, Ill do and show it to you. He would shout the way elderly people do. And, I have never seen any heroine take offence at his anger. They used to listen to those harsh words and deliver, this was his working style. Raza also revealed that he had seen Raj Kapoor lose his temper with Padmini Kolhapure on the sets of Prem Rog and with Mandakini while shooting Ram Teri Ganga Maili 1985. Raj Kapoor would fall ill before film releases Raza further recalled how Raj Kapoor would become unwell before the release of his films. I saw Raj Kapoor saab fall ill twice, I have seen those pink lips and cheeks turn pale before any of his films release, and the moment the film would be declared a hit, he would recover. He was very concerned about RK Banner, Raj Kapoor ki film hai. Aise hi Raj Kapoor, Raj Kapoor nahi hue hai, Its a Raj Kapoor film. He didnt become Raj Kapoor by fluke, he had many qualities, shared the actor. On the debacle of Mera Naam Joker He was very upset about it. He couldnt come to terms with the reality that the film had flopped at the box office, because Sangam was also a very lengthy film, there were two intervals. But, because the times had changes, peoples mindsets had also changed, and he felt that maybe he made his autobiography. That film is a masterpiece but it happens, said Raza Murad on Raj Kapoors condition post the release of Mera Naam Joker.

articleTitle: India, Germany, Qatar & Turkiye among 7 countries interested in hosting 2036 Olympics
articleFeaturedImageAlt: India are among seven countries eyeing to get 2036 Olympics hosting rights. (FILE PHOTO)
description: India submitted their Expression of Interest to host the Games in 2024, with Ahmedabad being their city of choice to host the mega-event,
body_raw: India are among seven countries, alongside Germany, Qatar, Turkiye, and South Africa, that are interested in hosting the 2036 Olympics and have been invited to present their Games projects to the IOCs Future Host Commission next month, the International Olympic Committee IOC said on Tuesday. As per the IOC, the Games projects will be assessed on several technical factors, which include the venue master plan, athlete experience, funding strategy, political and public support, Games delivery capabilities, and legacy strategy to create long-term benefits for host communities. The Interested Parties currently in Continuous Dialogue with the IOC, with a stated interest in hosting the 2036 Olympic Games, are in alphabetical order Germany, Hungary, India, Qatar, Republic of Korea, South Africa and Turkiye, read a statement from the IOC. There are also a number of NOCs taking part in noncommittal talks with the IOC about hosting future Olympic Games beyond 2036. The Interested Parties have been invited to present their projects to the Future Host Commission in November, it added. The IOC sets out the next phase of the process for selecting the host of the 2036 Olympic Games. dhY More details ai dhY-  - IOC MEDIA iocmedia October 6, 2026 The world body, however, did not share the exact timeline for these presentations. The IOC, keeping this schedule in view, said no other Interested Parties will be considered for 2036 after October 31. India submitted their Expression of Interest to host the Games in 2024, with Ahmedabad being their city of choice to host the mega-event, which has never been held in the country before. ALSO READ  2032 Olympic emblem officially revealed after it was leaked The host selection process was subsequently halted by new IOC President Kirsty Coventry, who said fresh feedback would be taken from member nations to streamline the process. The host of the 2036 Games will be known in mid-2029, and Indias negotiations will be led by the Indian Olympic Association IOA in collaboration with the Gujarat government and with the support of the Union Sports Ministry. I was fortunate to compete at five Olympic Games, across four continents. Each had their own character. Each host brought something unique through its people, its culture and the way it chose to stage the Games, said IOC President Kirsty Coventry. But wherever the Games take place, one thing must never change athletes have to be at the heart of everything we do. As an athlete, you spend years working to make your Olympic dream come true. The experience you have when you finally reach the Olympic Games stays with you for the rest of your life. That is why, for every future host, delivering the best possible experience for the athletes must always be the starting point, she added. With PTI inputs

articleTitle: Baft-e-Hawa: Janhvi Kapoor turns heads in a 460-count Bengal muslin sari in Paris
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Janhvi Kapoor in a Baft-e-Hawa muslin sari with an ornate embellished blouse in Paris
description: Janhvi Kapoor wore a 460-count Bengal muslin sari by Pankaj S Heritage to the Business of Fashion gala in Paris. Here’s what Baft-e-Hawa means and why the historic textile is so prized.
body_raw: Janhvi Kapoor took Bengal heritage to the Business of Fashion gala in Paris, wearing an ensemble by Pankaj S Heritage. Styled by cousin sister Rhea Kapoor, Janhvi wore a 460-count Bengal muslin in Khud - Rang, or unbleached, known for its exceptionally light, airy quality. Also referred to as Baft-e-Hawa, Shabnami or Chandani, the fabric represents one of the finest traditions of Indian handwoven textiles. The sari was paired with an ornate blouse featuring polkis, garnets and emeralds, along with saraafa tassels, kiran and resham fringing. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Talking about the look, Sneha Yadav, fashion consultant, brand  image strategist, NIFT alumna, says that the design involves the tension between the simple muslin fabric and the bold blouse design. The sari possesses a near effortless feel whereas the decorated sleeves bring in formwork, workmanship and theatricality. This opposition prevents the ensemble from appearing too conventional or unduly flashy, she adds. What exactly is Baft-e-Hawa The name Baft-e-Hawa means woven air, a description that captures the fabrics extraordinary lightness. It wasnt a poetic exaggeration. It was a literal description of how the cloth felt in your hand. This was the finest Dhaka muslin we are talking about, spun exclusively from Phuti Karpas, a delicate cotton shrub that grew only along the silty banks of the Meghna River basin, in modern-day Bangladesh, says Nabanita Ghosh, Co-founder  Director, Abritee. Making this fabric required extraordinary skill and precision. According to Ghosh, the spinning happened at the most unlikely hours.Young women with exceptional eyesight worked on boats during the humid hours of dawn and dusk, when the dew and humidity kept the micro-thin threads from snapping. The skill lay in their eyes, their fingertips and their timing, she says. The beauty lies not just in the fineness of the weave, but also in the expertise required to create it and the softness and fluidity that it brought to the garment. A khud-rang, or unbleached, cloth like this leaves the weaver nowhere a slight irregularity to hide, says Ghosh. There is no dye or finishing to cover an uneven thread, so every bit of its quality comes from the hands that made it. A count like 460 sounds technical, but what it really represents is patience. What legend says The most famous story about this cloth dates to the reign of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb. Dhaka was then a Mughal hub, and its finest muslin, malmal khas, was made for the imperial court. The emperor is said to have scolded his daughter, Princess Zeb-un-Nissa, for appearing to wear nothing at all. Her reply was that she was wearing seven layers of it, says Ghosh. The story, however, has been retold and modified over generations. What gets lost in the retelling is that Baft-e-Hawa was never about transparency. It was about control, Ghosh says. Anyone can make a thin fabric. Making one that is fine, even, and still strong enough to be worn is what made it a global benchmark. The older names associated with the fabric describe it best. Shabnami, meaning dew, and Chandani, meaning moonlight, were given by people who handled this cloth and described exactly what they felt. Why the styling works With a fabric as delicate and visually distinctive as Baft-E-Hawa, adding too much ornamentation can easily overwhelm it. In Janhvis look, the relatively simple sari keeps the fabric visible, while the elaborate sleeves add structure and drama. When that delicacy is paired with a silhouette and intricate detailing, the result is a dialogue between softness and structure. That balance is what gives Janhvis look its character and makes the textile feel very relevant in a contemporary fashion context, she says. According to Yadav, this contrast helps bring a historical Indian textile into a contemporary fashion context. The sari stays closely linked with craft work, yet the styling imparts a contemporary, sculptural nature, proving that history may be read in a manner that feels present without needing to mask or recreate its roots, she says. Janhvis Paris appearance brings attention to the extraordinary craftsmanship behind one of Indias most delicate textile traditions - and shows how a historic fabric can be styled without losing its identity. A quirky touch to her Paris trip A few days back, while flying to Paris, Janhvi added a quirky touch to her fashion sense. The Peddistar wore a customised tee that said, If lost, please return to Shikhar Pahariya   View this post on Instagram   A post shared by Ena and Kim enaandkim DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to.

articleTitle: Mother brings minor son to India flouting US order, Karnataka High Court directs return
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka HC orders mother to return to US with son, Karnataka HC sends mother and son back to US, ‘Go back to US’: Karnataka HC orders mother’s return, 2-year-old US citizen to return to America, Custody battle goes back to US, Karnataka HC sends custody fight back to US, Mother and son ordered back to US
description: The mother brought her son from US to India when he was nine months old, despite US court orders, and never went back.
body_raw: The Karnataka High Court has directed an Indian mother to return to the United States with her two-year-old American citizen son, who was brought to the state when he was nine months old despite a US court order against the childs removal from Washington. The court said the mother could not have removed the child from the US courts jurisdiction and denied him the company of his father. A bench of Justices Anu Sivaraman and T P Vivekananda observed that nothing on record suggested any imminent danger to the child from his father. The bench added, The mother had removed the child. without informing the father and in violation of the orders passed. The mother could not have removed the child from the jurisdiction of the competent Family Court in the United States of America and denied the child the company of its father, the October 1 order said, adding,The mother - respondent No.4 has to go back to the United States of America, which is the place of birth of the child and the place of its ordinary residence and work out her rights in the competent Court there. The writ petitioner husband shall make all arrangements for the return of respondent No.4 as well as the minor child to the US. The order further directed the father to bear the expenses of the mother till she finds an appropriate employment and accommodation in the United States of America. Custody fight travels from US to India The man, a US citizen and permanent resident, married the woman, who is an Indian citizen, on April 2, 2022, and they lived together in America. On February 13, 2024, their son was born and became a citizen by birth. According to the case records, on learning that his wife had made arrangements to travel to India with the child and apprehending that she would remove the child without his consent, the husband approached the jurisdictional court in the US seeking protection of his custodial rights. By an order passed on November 1, 2024, the court granted a temporary protection order in favour of the husband, restrained his wife from interfering with the custody of the minor child and directed her not to remove him from the state of Washington. Despite the order, the wife travelled to India with the nine-month-old child, and they are presently residing in Bengaluru. The wife later approached the family court in Bengaluru seeking an anti-suit injunction and under the Guardians and Wards Act,1890, and sought sole custody of the child. Meanwhile, the Superior Court of Washington, Clark County directed her on March 26, 2025, to return the child to Washington and ordered that her husband shall have the child in his exclusive care. This was reiterated by order dated May 16, 2025. Alleging that his wife had failed to comply with these directions and continues to retain the child in India unlawfully, the man instituted the present petition seeking the childs return and custody. On behalf of the father, senior counsel G L Vishwanath and advocate Meena Vargued that the custody of the minor child with the wife was unlawful, since the child was removed from the US and continues to be retained in India despite the orders passed by the Superior Court of Washington, Clark County, directing his return and placing him in the exclusive care of the father. The counsel submitted that the parties had established their matrimonial home in the US, that the child is a citizen of that country, and the custody disputes are most closely connected with that jurisdiction.It was further submitted that the wife had appeared through counsel before the Superior Court of Washington and was aware of the orders passed there, which continue to remain in force. She had obstructed her husbands access to the child and initiated proceedings before the family court in Bengaluru only after removing the child to India, the counsel added. It was also submitted that the welfare and best interests of the child would be served by restoring him to the jurisdiction of the Washington court, where the custody dispute may be finally decided. US court to decide custody Advocate Sonia Rajesh, appearing for the wife, contended that the fathers plea was not maintainable since the child, who is below five years of age, has remained in the care and custody of his mother from birth, which cannot be characterised as illegal to warrant the issue of a habeas corpus writ. Denying the allegation that the child was abducted, the counsel said her journey to India was pre-planned and undertaken with the knowledge of her husband. It was also stated that the temporary protection order relied upon by the man was dismissed on June 6, 2025, by the Washington court and cannot form the basis for treating the childs custody as unlawful. The counsel added that the wife was subjected to matrimonial cruelty, repeated abandonment and financial deprivation by the childs father, and raised concerns regarding his alleged alcohol and substance abuse, parenting ability and suitability to have the childs exclusive custody. It was submitted that the child was residing lawfully in India on a valid residence visa, was safe and well cared for, and had substantially settled in India. The father has not been denied access to the child, as video calls have been facilitated and he holds a valid visa enabling him to visit the child in India. The court observed that though the mother had approached the Bengaluru court, it passed no orders granting her custody of the son. Allowing the fathers plea, the court said that all the contentions of the parties were to be decided in the proceedings before the competent court in the US.

articleTitle: Cross-voting to 2027 polls: Why Akhilesh dropped plan to put up third RS candidate
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav also alleged that poor people were being defrauded of their land in Ayodhya. (File Photo)
description: Samajwadi Party's last-minute move paves way for its two nominees and BJP’s eight candidates to get elected unopposed in October 16 UP Rajya Sabha polls
body_raw: Days after indicating that it would field its third candidate for the October 16 Rajya Sabha elections from Uttar Pradesh, the Samajwadi Party SP decided against the move Tuesday, the last day of filing nominations, paving the way for the partys two nominees and the ruling BJPs eight candidates to get elected to the Upper House unopposed. The SPs last-minute decision was driven by a combination of factors involved in its attempts to cobble together the numbers needed for a third candidates win, with the high-stakes state Assembly elections just over four months away. SP president and ex-UP chief minister Akhilesh Yadavs rethink on the matter came a day after senior party MLA Ravidas Mehrotra indicated that the party had completed formalities to put up its third candidate for the Upper House polls for 10 vacant seats from UP. On Tuesday morning, however, Akhilesh, in an X post, said, Now our eyes are not on three but on 403 seats, signalling that the party has shifted its focus to the Assembly polls due in February 2027. His move, ending week-long political suspense, made it clear that there would not be any contest between the BJP and the SP for the Rajya Sabha polls now. The BJP and the SP have enough numbers to comfortably win seven and two seats respectively. SPs calculations The SP has already fielded party general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav, who is seeking his sixth term in the Rajya Sabha, and Reliance executive Dhananjay Nathwani. Nathwani, 40, is the son of Parimal Nathwani, Director, Corporate Affairs for Reliance Industries Ltd RIL, who was re-elected to the Rajya Sabha from Jharkhand as an NDA-backed Independent in the June 2026 election, securing his fourth consecutive term in the Upper House. Currently, there are 396 MLAs in the 403-member UP Assembly, with each Rajya Sabha candidate requiring 37 first-preference votes to win. The SP has 101 MLAs. However, its effective strength is 100 as Chail MLA Puja Pal, who continues to figure in the House records as an SP member, has switched to the BJP and is currently its state vice-president. With the support of two Congress MLAs, the SP has 102 votes-nine short of the first-preference votes required to ensure the victory of its third candidate. SP sources said that the partys calculations following the BJPs decision to field its eighth candidate became a key factor in the SPs rethink. Some BJP MLAs were in touch with the SP but showed hesitance to rebel openly months before polls, sources claimed. BJP play The BJP has 255 MLAs with its NDA allies adding another 33 members Apna Dal S 13, RLD 9, SBSP 6, and NISHAD Party 5. With the support of Puja Pal, unaffiliated MLAs Manoj Pandey, Rakesh Pratap Singh, and Abhay Singh-who were expelled from the SP in June 2025 for cross-voting in the 2024 Rajya Sabha polls-and two MLAs of the Raja Bhaiyya-led Jansatta Dal Loktantrik, the NDAs effective tally stands at 294-just two short of the required 296 37 for each first-preference votes to ensure a win for all its eight candidates. The BJP named its eight candidates Monday, dropping Union Ministers Hardeep Singh Puri and B L Verma from its list. Its nominees include Dharampal Singh, Radhakant Ojha, Prakash Pal, Vidyasagar Sonkar, Gopi Krishna Pandey, Priyanka Singh Rawat, Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan and Shruti Gangwar. Assembly poll factor The BJP appears confident of managing the two additional votes required for its eighth candidate, even as the possibility of cross-voting by some NDA MLAs is not ruled out within the ruling camp too. The presence of the third SP nominee would have led to a contest for the election of 11 candidates for 10 seats. This would have led to cross-voting among the MLAs, which would have favoured the BJP more, said an SP insider. Considering the vindictive nature of the ruling camp, several of its legislators despite being unhappy were hesitant and even fearful to reveal themselves at this stage. We decided to respect their decision and instead aim for the bigger target of the 2027 elections, the party insider said. For the SP, the numbers game was tighter. Its leaders said that in the final analysis, while the party required at least nine additional first-preference votes to push through its third nominee, the BJP needed only two additional votes to secure the victory of its eighth candidate. Thus the arithmetic made the extra-candidate gamble considerably more difficult for the SP than the BJP, especially given the nature of voting in the Rajya Sabha polls. Unlike a conventional secret ballot, the Rajya Sabha elections use an open-ballot system for the MLAs, who are required to show their marked ballots to an authorised party agent. The SP leaders said this made it difficult to rely on cross-voting by even those NDA MLAs who it claimed were in touch with them. With the Assembly elections round the corner, several MLAs were said to be unwilling to risk open defiance of their parties at this stage, when the candidate selection for the 2027 polls has yet to get underway.
