articleTitle: Movers and packers ‘unload’ goods on highway, man wins Rs 73,000 payout
articleFeaturedImageAlt: packers and movers AC highway man puducherry consumer court
description: The man claimed that his 7-year-old AC went missing after the movers and packers company delivered the rest of the household articles on a highway in 2025.
body_raw: A Puducherry consumer commission has directed a movers and packers company to pay nearly Rs 73,000 to a man after it allegedly unloaded his household goods on a highway, failed to deliver his air conditioner and demanded extra money for its release. President S Mouttouvel, along with members A S Suvitha and G Arumugam, was hearing the complaint filed by a man who, following his employment transfer, was shifting his residence from Gujarat to Puducherry when the AC went missing after the rest of his household articles were delivered. Between the place of move from and place of move to as shown in Exhibit C1 Bill, the opposite party company staff had done some foul play, and thereby they have not delivered the air conditioner. It is the duty of the packers and movers to deliver all the items that were packed, the August 31 order read. AC missing, extra money demanded The man claimed that he was residing in Puducherry and required the relocation of his household essentials, including an air conditioner, from Gujarat to Puducherry due to his employment. He added that the company contacted him and offered an all-inclusive quote of Rs 25,000 for the consignment, presenting itself as a cost-effective option. The man claimed that he was impressed by the company, which had represented that it had provided services to the Air Force, Military, BSF, ITBP, Navy, all major banks, ONGC and Indian Oil, and portrayed itself as a reliable service provider. He submitted that the company, through a series of payments, collected Rs 43,000 from him, despite the agreed amount of Rs 25,000, and, during the delivery process in June 2025, refused to deliver the consignment at the specified address in Puducherry. He added that the company insisted on unloading the goods on the highway, citing reasons including that it was not allowed to enter the state, forcing him to arrange transportation of the goods from the highway to his residence. Later, he claimed that an inspection of the delivered consignment showed that his AC worth about Rs 39,999 was found missing. The man added that when he approached the company representative, they initially denied knowledge of it but later admitted that the AC was in their possession. However, the company allegedly demanded Rs 5,000 initially and later Rs 13,000 for its release. Aggrieved, he moved the commission with this complaint. No return of same AC The commission found that the company did not appear to contest the case despite receiving notice. It declined to direct the return of the same AC, noting that the AC had been purchased in 2019 and nearly seven years had passed. It held that its present condition was unknown and that returning the same AC would be of No use to the complainant. The commission also took depreciation into account and directed the company to pay 50 of the ACs value instead. It found that the complainant had established that he suffered mental agony, adding that the wrongful retention of the AC and repeated demands for additional money added to his distress. In addition to that, demanding a higher amount and repeated demanding of money, quoting some reason or the other, would have caused mental agony to the complainant, it mentioned. The commission directed the company to pay Rs 18,000 as the excess amount collected, Rs 20,000 50 of the ACs value, Rs 25,000 for mental agony and Rs 10,000 towards litigation costs. Takeaway This ruling highlights that a packers and movers company cannot demand an amount higher than what was agreed and that failure to deliver a consigned item amounts to deficiency in service. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states and union territories Puducherry 180-0425-1082 or call the National Consumer Helpline on 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: ‘Imaandar CM’ to CBI raid: Bhagwant Mann’s 2027 campaign faces a new test
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann at Fatta Maloka village during a public meeting, in Sardulgarh. (@AAPPunjab/X via PTI Photo)
description: With welfare schemes, public meetings, and digs at rivals, the Punjab CM is increasingly the face of AAP’s Assembly poll campaign.
body_raw: Imaandar CM, Lokan da CM, AAP da ikko naara, Bhagwant Mann dobara. Honest CM, peoples CM AAP has one slogan, Bhagwant Mann for the second time. As you drive down from Chandigarh to Jalandhar and then on to Kapurthala, a beaming Mann, the Punjab Chief Minister, is your constant companion, looking down at you from billboards in his trademark yellow turban. This is a far cry from late 2021, when Aam Aadmi Party AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal dominated the hoardings in Punjab, with Mann emerging later after a phone poll - Janta chunegi apna CM People will choose their CM - saw him handpicked for the top post with 93 of the votes. While other parties, except the Shiromani Akali Dal led by the Badals, remain largely non-committal about their CM face, the AAP, which swept the 2022 Assembly polls by winning 92 of 117 seats, is clearly making Mann its mascot for 2027. The flip side to this is that it puts Mann, and by extension AAP, under intense scrutiny. There was a political firestorm on Monday after the Punjab and Haryana High Court ordered a CBI probe into allegations linked to his office, following the Punjab Polices failure to act on three letters sent by the Enforcement Directorate to the Punjab DGP. The allegations involve Manns Officer on Special Duty, Rajbir Singh Ghuman, and others. On Tuesday evening, the CBI raided Ghumans residence and the CMs camp office even as the government challenged the High Court order in the Supreme Court earlier in the day. The Opposition had thought the edict would turn him into a social outcast of sorts. But Mann has remained constantly in the public eye, criss-crossing the length and breadth of the state almost every day, except for a short break in early July when he travelled to Bengaluru for what aides described as his annual wellness programme. His message changes with the audience but has two constants 300 units of free electricity a month, presented on billboards and in speeches as 600 units since bills are typically bi-monthly, and the satkar payments to women beneficiaries under the Maawan-Dheeyan Satkar Yojana that began on July 1. There is also a mandatory warning If you vote for other parties, all this will stop. Focusing on the women who have now received money for six months under the scheme, which provides Rs 1,500 a month to eligible Dalit women and Rs 1,000 to others - with the first transfers made for three months on July 1 and the second on October 1 - Mann has declared he will never let this toon-toon sound of mobile notification about money coming in stop. Kehnde Bhagwant Mann aurtan nu paise de ke sir charha reha hai . toon-toon chaldi rahegi, band nahin hon devanga. They say I am spoiling women with money. this will carry on, it wont stop. Potshots at Opposition His other favourite pitch, especially in the countryside, is the increased access to canal water under his regime, from 26 in 2022 to 86 now, and the Rs 10 lakh health insurance for all. Many billboards relay the same message, with the tagline, Jo keeta so kar ke dikhaya. He delivered what he promised. But it is his potshots at the Opposition that deliver the real sting disparaging messages cloaked in laughter. Commenting on the elevation of former India hockey captain and three-time Jalandhar Cantonment MLA Pargat Singh as Punjab Congress president on October 2, he quipped Main unhan nu hamesha Captain Sahib kehnda haan. umeed hai unhan di team vi unhan nu gend pass karegi, kyonki pass ton bina goal nahin ho sakda I always call him Captain Sahib, I hope his team will pass the ball to him so that he can score. Another favourite quip is Congress vich workers nalon vadh CM umeedwar han. Congress has more CM hopefuls than workers. At another place, he says Remember the five-point programme of Congress and Akalis Me, my son, my nephew, my brother-in-law and my sisters husband. And he almost always ends on a cautionary note Virodhi parties 2027 ton pehlan paise vi vand sakdian han. Paise le lao, par vote AAP nu pao. The Opposition parties could woo you with money, take it, but vote for AAP. The unrelenting flow of drugs is one issue where the Opposition, led by the BJP, is on the offensive. But here too, Mann plays on the front foot, reminding voters that the problem intensified during the earlier Akali Dal-BJP government and that the BJP at the Centre is responsible for manning the over-500-km international border with Pakistan, one of the routes for drug trafficking in the region. Political observers see in the billboards an AAP effort to counter the increasingly loud charge that the party is run by proxy from Delhi by Kejriwal. The billboards not only show a CM in charge but underline two things that the AAP wants voters to associate with Mann his people connect and his clean image. The flip side But its his clean image that is now under fire following the High Court order of a CBI probe. While Mann is calling it a familiar ploy by the BJP to malign him in the run-up to the Assembly polls, the Opposition is having a field day. Congress leader Partap Singh Bajwa, the Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly, said Mann cant escape blame. How is it that he was ignorant of what was transpiring in his office? The AAP government tom-toms him as an imaandaar CM. If he was so honest, why did the High Court order a CBI probe ? Punjab BJP state president Kewal Singh Dhillon went a step further and sought the CMs resignation. People in the hinterland are generally keeping an open mind. Ajaib Singh, a resident of Bagrian village in Kapurthala, who retired as a sub-inspector from the Punjab Police four months ago, says one cant say anything unless there is unassailable proof. Gurcharan Singh, a retired soldier at Bariar village, agrees. Allegations and counter-allegations are part of politics, all empty without verifiable proof. For now, though, Mann continues to do what he does best meet people with a script that he improvises on the spot to connect with them.

articleTitle: Denied pension over schizophrenia, Orissa High Court restores it for retired CRPF man
articleFeaturedImageAlt: crpf man disability pension rules orissa high court (1)
description: The petitioner was a CRPF employee who retired on medical invalidation grounds in 1999 after he was found to have schizophrenia. The authorities later rejected his disability pension saying that it was a 'non-classified' disease.
body_raw: Holding that the petitioners claim could not be rejected merely because schizophrenia was not a classified disease, the Orissa High Court has quashed a 2011 order rejecting a former CRPF personnels claim for disability pension, directing the authorities to allow the pension and release the arrears. Justice Biraja Prasanna Satapathy was dealing with a plea of a former personnel with the Central Reserve Police Force CRPF, who retired on medical grounds in 1999 due to schizophrenia with an approved 50 per cent disability pension. However, the authorities later revoked the benefit, claiming schizophrenia was non-classified and he lacked 10 years of service. Taking into account the nature of the order passed and the grounds of rejection issued, this court is of the view that since the petitioner was allowed to take retirement on the ground of invalidation because of his.schizophrenia, on the ground that such a disease is not a classified disease, the petitioners claim could not have been rejected, the court said on October 1. The ruling held that since it was clearly indicated in the order that the petitioner is entitled to get the disability pension of 50 per cent and the said order since was never modified or recalled, this court is of the view that the ground on which the petitioners claim was rejected is not sustainable in the eyes of the law. Retired due to schizophrenia The petitioner was a CRPF employee who was allowed to retire on medical invalidation in 1999 after he was found to have schizophrenia. The medical board had found him completely and permanently incapacitated for future service and recommended disability pension of 50 per cent. The CRPFs order allowing his invalidation retirement also specifically stated that he would be entitled to the pension from the date of invalidation. However, his claim for disability pension was later rejected in 2011. The authorities said schizophrenia was not a classified disease for the purpose of Extraordinary Disability Pension EOP under the CCS Pension Rules, 1972, and that he had not completed the required 10 years of qualifying service. He was told he was only entitled to service gratuity, which had already been paid. The petitioner challenged the rejection before the high court, seeking quashing of the 2011 order and release of his disability pension. Original order never recalled Order The court noted that the petitioner was allowed to retire on medical invalidation because of schizophrenia, based on the medical boards assessment that he was permanently incapacitated for further service. The 1999 retirement order specifically stated that he was entitled to 50 per cent disability pension from the date of invalidation. The high court observed that the pension claim was later rejected on the grounds that schizophrenia was not a classified disease and that the petitioner had not completed 10 years of qualifying service. It further noted that the original retirement order had never been modified or recalled. Therefore, the subsequent rejection of the pension claim was not sustainable in law and was also hit by the principle of promissory estoppel, a legal principle that allows a court to enforce a promise even when there is no formal, written contract.

articleTitle: Sonakshi Sinha, Shahid Kapoor’s driver opened a momo shop, Tukaram Mundhe shut it down
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Suraj Lama, whose momos shop was suspended by the FDA, was once a Bollywood celebrity driver.
description: Suraj Lama Momos, a popular dumpling eatery in Versova, Mumbai, had its eatery suspended by Tukaram Mundhe-led Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration.
body_raw: Tukaram Mundhe-led Maharashtra Food  Drug Administration FDA suspended the licenses of eight more eateries on Monday, as part of its intense festival season encroachment drive. These outlets included the original Andheri West branch of Suraj Lama Momos, one of the most popular momo shops of Mumbai, the eponymous owner of which has an interesting Bollywood connection. Suraj Lama was Shahid Kapoor, Sonakshi Sinhas driver Suraj Lama relocated to Mumbai at the age of 14, leaving behind his village Mirik in Darjeeling, in order to seek employment. After doing a few odd jobs, Suraj became a celebrity driver. He worked in that capacity for 25 years, including with actors Sonakshi Sinha and Shahid Kapoor, and also drove the car for leading banners like Karan Johars Dharma Productions. I worked with a lot of dedication, and saw people I worked with as my own family, but sometimes I wasnt seen as equal. It bothered me, Suraj confessed in an interview with The Indian Express a couple of years ago. He recalled an incident as the final nail in the coffin - I drove an actor to the set. There was a child who wanted to take a photo with the actor, and had been waiting for a long time. I thought of helping that child, but when I conveyed his wish to the actor, they refused. I didnt feel good, he recounted. When Suraj quit driving to sell momos The subsequent rise in app-based cab services like Ola and Uber was also a factor in Suraj going for a pivot to selling momos in 2017. He even made Sonakshi and her family taste his momos, and they approved of his skills. So, he decided to quit his job, sell his motorbike and buy a cycle, with which he started a pop-up shop. He also convinced his wife Vijayata to join him, so she also quit her job of a cook at singer KKs household. In hindsight, it was a big risk. We both were earning around Rs 30,000 each, spending half of it running our home, and saving the rest. The gamble paid off, but it could have gone in another direction as well, admitted Suraj. Since momos werent as easily available in Mumbai back then as they were in North India, Suraj got a pretty good start. Hed cycle across parts of Andheri West to sell both vegetarian and non-vegetarian momos. The demand swelled up fast, which prompted him to open a roadside eatery in Versova. In fact, when I first asked the owner of our current store to lease the space to me, he said, You wont be able to afford it, and later, he himself reached out to me, said Suraj. Even though Suraj and his wife earned Rs 30,000 each from their previous jobs, once they began selling momos, they quickly began earnings Rs 700 in a day alone. He spelled out the secret to his recipe, claiming that the momos reminded him of home. My momos are just like my mothers. I follow her recipe. I dont use preservatives or artificial colouring, he told Mid-Day in 2017. He also claims his wife, a great cook, makes delectable momos. Even though he expanded with more outlets in Malad and Kandivali, he hadnt reached other far-flung areas of high demand, including Pune, Nashik, and Gujarat. It is important to maintain quality. Today, we have a central kitchen in Mumbai, overseen entirely by my wife, with a staff of 25, preparing about 16,000 momos daily across various options. It is these momos, cooked till about 90 per cent, that go to each store, whether run by us or a franchise. Until I can do that in another city, I wont expand, said Suraj in 2024. Also Read Sanjay Dutt says his cant feel peace in India remark a scripted conversation, Shekhar Suman comments Its ironic that with so much emphasis on food quality, as he claims, Suraj Lama Momoss license was suspended by the FDA. The authority flagged lapses in the way the food was handled and stored, in sanitation, cleanliness and safeguards intended to prevent contamination. It said the violations were serious enough to take swift action against the establishment under the applicable food safety guidelines.

articleTitle: 7 die as SUV crashes into parked truck in Gujarat’s Bhavnagar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The police officer said all seven men worked in the shipbreaking yard and commuted daily from Bhavnagar to Alang, a 50-km distance.
description: The incident took place around 9.45 am near Trapaj village at the trijunction of roads leading to Bhavnagar, Talaja and Alang.
body_raw: Seven people died after an SUV travelling from Bhavnagar to Alang in Gujarat crashed into a stationary truck on Tuesday morning. All the victims worked at the Alang shipbreaking yard and were headed there when the accident took place. The incident took place around 9.45 am near Trapaj village at the trijunction of roads leading to Bhavnagar, Talaja and Alang. Manish Nakum, Deputy Superintendent of Police, told The Indian Express that six people died on the spot and one was rushed to a nearby hospital. The survivor succumbed to injuries later, said Inspector PM Desai of Alang police station. The police officer said all seven men worked in the shipbreaking yard and commuted daily from Bhavnagar to Alang, a 50-km distance. The truck driver had parked the vehicle on the service road and had gone to have snacks when the SUV hit the truck from behind, the Inspector added. The front part of the SUV was completely damaged, indicating the intensity of the crash. CCTV videos of the crash show that the impact caused the parked heavy vehicle to move forward. Visuals showed the SUVs windshield shattered and its roof damaged. The doors of the vehicle had to be forced open with iron bars to recover the victims bodies. Inspector Desai said the bodies had been sent for post-mortem and the identities of the victims would be revealed shortly after.

articleTitle: Colonial legacy of India’s policing system must end: Andhra Pradesh High Court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Andhra Pradesh High Court police policing colonial
description: Hearing six pleas alleging police interference in land or property disputes, the Andhra Pradesh High Court barred the police from adjudicating civil rights.
body_raw: The Andhra Pradesh High Court has invoked the colonial legacy of Indias policing system while calling for a shift towards people-centric and democratic policing. Referring to legal scholar Upendra Baxis observation that the colonial police survived decolonization it simply changed masters, the court said the police structure, methods and legal framework largely continued to reflect the colonial model even after Independence. Justice Maheswara Rao Kuncheam was hearing a batch of six petitions alleging police interference in civil disputes involving land, houses and other properties. The petitioners alleged that police personnel had called them to police stations, pressured them to settle disputes and interfered in matters pending before competent courts or legal forums. The common order in the six petitions was passed on October 5,restraining the police from interfering in civil disputes. Police are entrusted with the responsibility of protecting life, liberty, rights and public order, but they are not an authority above the people. Police powers are conferred by law and must be exercised fairly, reasonably and proportionately. Thus, the police must act as guardians of the constitutional principles, rather than as rulers exercising unchecked authority over citizens., the court said. The police structure, methods and legal framework largely continued to reflect the colonial model, mainly based on the Police Act, 1861, which was primarily designed to maintain order, control the population and protect the interests of the ruling authority, rather than to function as a citizen-oriented service, it added. The court said that though the British rulers were replaced by an elected Indian government, the basic institutional character of the police remained substantially unchanged. Hence, all the stakeholders contribute their respective support to change the overall existing police structures from the colonial phase to people-centric policing in the larger interest of modern Indian and turns into Democratic policing, which means a system of policing in which the police exercise their powers within the limits of law, remain accountable to constitutional and democratic institutions, and respond to the legitimate needs and rights of the people, it added. 6 pleas raised common concern The six petitions involved different disputes but raised the common issue of police allegedly interfering in civil matters already pending before competent forums. In one petition, the petitioner alleged police interference in a dispute concerning his house and pressure to vacate it. Another alleged that police had locked her house and prevented her from entering. Other petitions involved allegations that police repeatedly called parties to stations to settle disputes concerning land or property. One petitioner alleged that police threatened her to withdraw a civil suit, while another alleged that he was detained for hours and pressured to compromise in a property dispute. These were allegations made in the petitions. The State disputed them and told the court that police had not called the petitioners to the respective stations and would not interfere in civil disputes unless a cognizable offence was registered. The high court also highlighted the limited police strength in Andhra Pradesh. It noted that the state has approximately 166.18 police personnel per one lakh population, against the United Nations recommendation of 222 personnel per lakh. The court said that, given these limitations, deploying police resources in areas where they have no jurisdiction could become a futile exercise. It referred to the possibility of unjust enrichment of some police personnel through such intervention and described such conduct as illegal and unconstitutional. Police cant decide civil rights The court made it clear that the police retain their legal duty to maintain law and order, prevent crime, protect life and property, and take lawful preventive measures where there is a threat to public peace. However, those powers do not extend to deciding civil rights between private parties. The court said that once a competent judicial or quasi-judicial forum has seized a dispute, an executive authority without adjudicatory powers cannot assume the role of that forum and determine the rights of the parties. Such action would amount to acting without jurisdiction. The duty to resolve civil disputes is entrusted to the judiciary. No such power is empowered to the Police, the court said, adding that interference in pending or potential civil disputes is not within their province. DGPs guidelines draw the line The court took note of instructions issued by the Andhra Pradesh Director General of Police on October 24, 2025 concerning land disputes. The guidelines say police should not take sides or interfere in civil ownership or title disputes, while providing for preventive action where a dispute threatens public peace. The guidelines also provide for criminal cases where criminal intent or violence is evident, including trespass, cheating, forgery, assault or criminal conspiracy. The high court ultimately held that police have no jurisdiction to adjudicate upon or determine civil rights between parties. It directed the police not to interfere, adjudicate, determine or settle such rights without legal cause and ordered strict compliance with the DGPs guidelines. The parties were left free to pursue remedies before appropriate civil courts or competent forums. The court clarified that if a cognisable offence is made out, police remain free to proceed according to law. There was no order as to costs, and pending interlocutory applications were closed.

articleTitle: Gujarat couple died by suicide live on Instagram, family was among viewers
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Dahod couple live suicide, Dahod couple suicide case, Gujarat couple live suicide, Gujarat Instagram live suicide, Dahod Instagram live, young couple death Dahod, Dahod news, Gujarat suicide case, social media live tragedy, Dahod police investigation, Gujarat news, Indian Express news
description: Family members alerted the Dahod police after watching the livestream, but poor connectivity hampered efforts to locate the couple.
body_raw: At least 57 people watched a young man and a teenage girl in Gujarats Dahod as they went live on a social media platform from a forested area and allegedly took their own lives, turning a family dispute into a tragedy that unfolded in real time. Senior police officers said the incident occurred on October 4 on the outskirts of Hirapur village in Singwad, where a teenage girl, below 18, and a young man, in his early 20s, travelled roughly 20 km from their respective villages in a neighbouring taluka before starting the Instagram live. The live stream has since emerged as a crucial part of the police investigation. Poor connectivity Among those watching the couple were members of their families, who alerted the police after seeing what was unfolding. The families contacted a police station in the district, under whose jurisdiction their respective villages fall, prompting the police to mobilise teams to locate the couple. The police rushed to find them, but poor network connectivity and the challenge of pinpointing the exact location turned the response into a race they could not win. The police team was immediately dispatched, but due to network issues as well as the challenge of identifying the exact location, the two had already taken the extreme step by the time the police reached the spot, a senior officer said. A spontaneous act Karan Panna, Assistant Deputy Superintendent of Police, Limkheda division, told The Indian Express that the circumstances pointed towards family opposition to the relationship. A probe is on. Prima facie, it was a spontaneous act, and the circumstances suggest their families opposed the relationship. We are conducting an investigation after an accidental death case has been lodged. The further steps will be decided accordingly, Panna said. A team from the police station reached the spot and recovered the bodies, beginning the investigation. The bodies of the couple were sent for post-mortem examination and handed over to their families Monday for the final rites, Panna said.

articleTitle: Sanjay Dutt, 67, speaks about bond with daughter Trishala: ‘We had a disconnect’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Trishala Dutt
description: Sanjay Dutt’s candid admission about his daughter Trishala sheds light on a complicated chapter in their relationship
body_raw: Sanjay Dutt, 67, recently spoke about his 38-year-old daughter, Trishala, who lives in New York, and reflected on their bond. Now she is a big lady. She does a lot of good work there. Its beautiful. I was in New York recently. We spent a lot of time together. We talk about her work, about my work. We had a disconnect in the middle. It happened for many reasons in my case.I was not to have her custody.old story now.I have seen a massive change in her. I am very, very proud of that, Dutt told actor and host Shekhar Suman on his late-night YouTube talk show Shekhar Tonite. Behind the word disconnect lies an experience thousands of families understand intimately, psychotherapist and relationship breakthrough coach Delnna Rrajesh said. Divorce, separation, custody arrangements, legal difficulties, migration and circumstances beyond a childs control can sometimes physically separate a parent and child for years. We often discuss separation through the couples experience the marriage ended, custody was decided, homes changed. But for a child, something entirely different has happened. The relationship ended between two adults the childs family changed without the child ever choosing it. This is where we need greater psychological sensitivity. Custody determines where a child primarily lives and who has particular legal responsibilities it does not, by itself, measure the depth of a parents love or the childs attachment, shared Delnna. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. And everyday life matters enormously. Parenthood is not built only through birthdays, holidays and milestone photographs. It is built through school mornings, forgotten water bottles, fevers at midnight, homework, arguments about bedtime, car journeys, teenage moods and conversations that happen unexpectedly over dinner. When a parent and child are separated, these moments disappear. They may still love each other deeply while simultaneously grieving a relationship they are unable to fully live, Delnna told indianexpress.com. Psychology has a useful concept for some experiences of unresolved absence ambiguous loss. Unlike bereavement, where the loss itself is clear, ambiguous loss can involve someone who is still alive and emotionally significant but unavailable in the way they once were or are needed to be. In parent-child separation, the circumstances vary enormously and the concept will not describe every family, but it helps us understand why the grief can be so difficult to articulate. Nobody has died. Yet something precious may still have been lost, said Delnna. Reconciliation often becomes difficult when the parent begins by trying to correct history. That is why the goal shouldnt be to recover the lost years. The healthier task is to build the relationship that is possible now. We cannot retrieve childhood. We cannot attend yesterdays school function, wipe yesterdays tears or recreate yesterdays birthdays. But love does not belong only to the years that were lost. Where there is safety, accountability and willingness, it can also belong to the years that remain. A relationship can have a painful history without being sentenced to a painful future. Sometimes reconciliation is not about getting the past back at all. It is about refusing to let the years already lost take away the years two people may still have, said Delnna. articleTitle: KBC 18: Ayushmann Khurrana apologises to Amitabh Bachchan for calling him ‘budhau’

The two actors shared memories from the film, with Big B also praising Ayushmann. Ayushmann then jokingly apologised to the veteran actor for calling him budhau - or old man - in the film. Aapko film mein budhau kaha, I am sorry. Aap budhau nahi hain. Really life mein aap mein 84 wali koi harkat nahi hai, 24 hain aap I called you an old man in the film, I am sorry. But you are not old. In real life, there is nothing about you that is 84. You are 24, Ayushmann told him. Amitabh Bachchan then complimented Saras family, saying everyone in the Pataudi family has beautiful eyes, going all the way back to her grandfather, former cricketer Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi. While talking about Saras family, he recalled seeing Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudis mother driving an open Jaguar in Delhi. He said the confidence and attitude associated with the Pataudi family appeared to have continued across generations. Ayushmann dedicates KBC Radio tribute to Amitabh Bachchan The episode also featured a special KBC Radio segment in which Ayushmann spoke about Amitabh Bachchan in a radio-style tribute. As part of the segment, Ayushmann sang a song of Amitabh Bachchan and paid tribute to the actor during his birthday week. Sara and Ayushmann answer Rs 5 lakh question The actors continued with the quiz and reached the Rs 5 lakh question. Big B recalled an old social media post about rising petrol prices that he had written jokingly 10-15 years ago. I had written something about petrol prices rising 10-15 years ago, just as a joke. articleTitle: IIM Lucknow, TeamLease launch 11-month executive programme in Brand Management
articleFeaturedImageAlt: iim lucknow medusa campus image
description: The curriculum covers consumer insights, brand strategy and integrated communications, along with digital marketing, e-commerce, performance marketing and customer lifecycle management.
body_raw: The Indian Institute of Management IIM Lucknow has launched an 11-month Executive Programme in Brand Management in partnership with TeamLease EdTech, for working professionals seeking to build skills in brand strategy, consumer understanding, digital marketing and business decision-making. The programme comprises 132 learning hours, including 114 hours of live online learning and 18 hours through a three-day campus immersion at IIM Lucknow. The course uses case studies, business simulations, projects, assignments, faculty-led live sessions, practitioner-led masterclasses and peer learning to connect classroom concepts with business situations. Read JEE scores can get you into these IIMs undergraduate programmes after Class 12 The curriculum covers consumer insights, brand strategy and integrated communications, along with digital marketing, e-commerce, performance marketing and customer lifecycle management. Participants will also study digital consumer psychology, brand storytelling, social media and influencer branding, marketplace and quick-commerce strategy, and omnichannel growth. A key component of the programme is the use of emerging technologies in marketing. The curriculum covers AI-driven marketing and advertising and examines how AI can be used to understand consumers and support engagement with them. The programme also looks at how changing digital consumer journeys affect brand building and customer experience. The programme links marketing decisions with the financial and commercial aspects of running a brand. Participants will learn about unit economics, profitability, financial planning, valuation and governance, along with cross-functional leadership. This is intended to help professionals assess brand decisions not only from a consumer or marketing perspective but also in terms of their wider business impact. Also Read From buckets to hangers Why No-Bag Day is becoming a campus trend at IITs, IIMs The programme is designed for brand and marketing professionals, digital and growth professionals, product and business leaders, entrepreneurs, sales professionals and those aspiring to marketing leadership roles. The curriculum is structured around the changing role of brand managers, where consumer insight, digital execution, data, technology and business economics increasingly overlap. Learning is primarily delivered online, with the campus component providing an opportunity for in-person learning at IIM Lucknow. The application-oriented format includes business simulations and projects alongside academic sessions, allowing participants to apply concepts such as positioning, customer experience, digital growth and marketing economics to business situations. The programme is open to graduates, diploma holders and postgraduates. Selection will be based on the candidates academic and professional background and experience. Participants who meet the prescribed academic and attendance requirements will receive a Certificate of Successful Completion from IIM Lucknow. Admissions for the upcoming cohort are open. Details on the programme curriculum, eligibility, fee and application process are available on the programme website.

articleTitle: Jim Bakker dies at 86: Televangelist lost his multi-million empire to sex scandal, crimes
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jim Bakker death: The evangelist built a multi-million dollar empire with first wife Tammy Faye.
description: Jim Bakker Dies at 86: Infamous televangelist Jim Bakker was best known for the empire he and his first wife, Tammy Faye, built around the television show The PTL Club.
body_raw: Jim Bakker Death News Infamous televangelist Jim Bakker has died at the age of 80. While his second wife Lori Bakker didnt disclose the cause, she confirmed he was no more. It is with a broken heart that I share that my beloved husband, Jim Bakker, went home to be with the Lord this evening. He was a pioneer of Christian television, but to me, he was my husband, my best friend, and the man I was honored to walk beside through so many seasons of life and ministry, Lori said in a statement. Jim Bakker was best known for building an evangelical empire around the popular television programme The PTL Club. However, his story took a dramatic turn as sex scandals and financial crimes cost him much of his reputation and wealth. Jim Bakker and Lori Bakkerlived near Branson, Missouri, where they filmed their TV show The Jim Bakker Show since its inception in 2003. But it was Bakkers first wife Tammy Faye with whom he shot to fame. Their show fetched 13 million viewers everyday at its peak in the mid-1980s and amassed over 129 million yearly, as per AP. Their personal and professional collaborations began in college, when they began dating and dropped out to kick off their travelling ministry. Bakker preached, and Faye sang and played the accordion as they visited churches and tent revivals across the US. Televangelist Pat Robertson roped them in to launch a childrens show in 1965 and The 700 Club, a Christian talk show, in 1966. After exiting the network in 1972, Bakker formed the PTL Satellite Network in 1974, with PTL standing for Praise the Lord. Sex scandal and financial crimes galore After enjoying popularity for around 13 years, Jim Bakker admitted to a sexual encounter in 1987 with church clerk Jessica Hahn. He even paid her 265,000 from ministry funds to keep her silent. He was consequently forced to resign from his empire, with pastor and broadcaster Jerry Falwell taking over. Tammy Faye continued to stand by Bakker despite the sex scandal and subsequent fall from grace. The next year, Bakker was indicted for wire fraud, mail fraud, and conspiracy linked to PTLs finances. He was sentenced to 45 years in prison, but the jailtime was eventually reduced to eight years. Faye remained loyal to her husband even then, singing the hymn On Christ the Solid Rock I Stand at a press conference after his conviction. Also Read Fahadh Faasil says wont get half of Rs 300 cr as Bethlehem Kudumba Unit earns Rs 326 cr Finally, a few years later in 1992, Tammy Faye divorced Jim Bakker ahead of their 31st wedding anniversary. He was still in prison at the time of the separation. They had two children. After being released on parole in 1994, Bakker married Lori Bakker four years later. The couple adopted five children in 2002. Bakker became a television preacher again in the early 2000s, and was a staunch supporter of US President Donald Trump.

articleTitle: Rewilding great Indian bustards: The project and the challenges ahead
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Two male great Indian bustards (GIB) are released in Rajasthan’s Desert National Park on Sunday. (X: Bhupender Yadav)
description: For the first time, two captive-bred great Indian bustards have been released into the wild. While this experiment is indeed important, the recovery of their population still remains a long-term challenge.
body_raw: October 4 marked a significant milestone in the efforts to conserve the critically endangered great Indian bustard GIB. Two captive-bred male GIBs were released into the wild for the first time in Rajasthans Desert National Park near Jaisalmer town. The pilot release marks the first step in rewilding bustards that have been bred and raised in captivity. This is part of Project GIB which the Centre is running along with the Wildlife Institute of India and the governments of Rajasthan and Gujarat. What is the great Indian bustard and why is its population being revived? The great Indian bustard is a large, ground-dwelling bird found in savannahs, grasslands and deserts in India. Till the late 19th and early 20th century, it was spread across 11 states - from Haryana in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south, and from Rajasthan in the west to Odisha in the east. But a range of issues resulted in its decline - hunting, poaching of eggs, gradual conversion of open habitats into croplands and mining areas and, more recently, deaths due to collisions with renewable energy power lines. GIBs poor frontal vision, combined with their heavy body, makes it difficult for them to detect or avoid such infrastructure. From an estimated 1,260-1,400 in the early 1970s, the wild GIB population has now plummeted to only around 150, of which around 130 -20 are in Rajasthan. The rest are in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh - facing the risk of local extinction. To counter their decline, the Centre and the Rajasthan government launched a long-term bustard and lesser florican project in 2012-13. This project was expanded from 2014 with funding support to start a conservation breeding program. Beginning 2019, wild GIB eggs were collected from Desert National Park and surrounding areas, incubated artificially at two centres in Rajasthans Sam and Ramdevra and hand-reared. These hand-reared birds mated at these centres, giving birth to 98 birds as of now. Of these, two were released Sunday and 11 more have been earmarked for wild release. The others remain at the centres for captive reproduction. What does rewilding entail? Before initiating the rewilding process, a rewilding aviary was set up at the Ramdevra Center while a soft release facility was developed by the Wildlife Institute of India inside Desert National Park. Unlike the hand-reared birds that were used to humans, chicks aged between three and four months were released in these facilities so that they could move freely and adapt to the natural environment without human imprinting. Scientists associated with the project said the birds have been fitted with transmitters. These devices will send alerts thrice a day on their coordinates and movement pattern. Teams will also monitor them from afar. Challenges in long-term recovery The beginning of the rewilding phase, while crucial, is a challenging experiment. The released birds will face a challenge to their survival. Enclosures within Desert National Park were picked because they comprised grasslands as well as stretches free of either human or technological interruptions. While this is an experiment in Rajasthan, similar experiments would have to be carried out in range states such as Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, albeit only after habitat improvements. We can learn from the Rajasthan experience, and if this is successful, then Gujarat may do a similar pilot. However, restoration and protection of grasslands is crucial for the revival of bustards outside Rajasthan, said Gobind Sagar Bhardwaj, Director, Wildlife Institute of India. Unlike forested areas across Indias states, grassland protection has always been challenging as they are not traditionally considered protected areas in public perception. Bharadwaj said this makes them vulnerable to land-use conversion and degradation, which consequently affects the livelihoods of pastoralists and those who rear livestock. The afforestation of grasslands was red-flagged by Asad Rahmani, one of Indias foremost bustard experts and former director of Bombay Natural History Society, in the NGOs famous Hornbill magazine back in 2008. Rahmani wrote Ironically, one of the biggest threats to grasslands is not from the graziers, but from the forest department. To live up to their name, officials of the forest department consider their solemn duty to convert every grassland and even wetlands into a forest. He noted that from Gujarat to Andhra Pradesh, it was seen that forest officers decided to improve habitats by planting trees or creating waterholes in bustard habitats. Threats to GIB revival At the conclusion of a landmark case seeking protection of GIBs, the Supreme Court had, accepting the recommendations of an expert panel, ordered some broad protection measures for GIBs and their habitats in Rajasthan and Gujarat. It demarcated priority areas for the bird 14,013 sq km in Rajasthan and 740 sq km in Gujarat and ordered that 80 km of power lines in Rajasthan should be buried underground. This has to be completed between 2027 and 2028. It also ordered the creation of powerline corridors that will accommodate re-routed overhead lines. Experts have warned that rewilding will not be sustainable if these power lines cannot be buried underground soon. Limestone mining is yet another issue that threatens to affect the open and flat areas that Bustards need. The Supreme Court did not order specific measures against mining, and mine operations are proposed in the northern side of DNP, where the birds were released.

articleTitle: Retired Delhi High Court judge, family lost Rs 3.2 crore in real estate scam
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ML Varma
description: After years of delays, bounced cheques and assurances, retired Delhi High Court judge M L Varma has now approached the police. An FIR has been filed on his complaint
body_raw: Sixteen years ago, Justice M L Varma was going through his morning ritual of reading the newspaper when his eyes fell on an advertisement in a corner. The advertisement carried striking pictures of an upcoming project in Noida Sector 15, said the 84-year-old, who retired in 1991 from the Delhi High Court. It promised a high rental commercial unit. The pictures were so attractive and appealing, it looked like it was absolutely out of the world. They showed a metro station nearby, a very good sector, he added. Interested, he quickly dialled the contact number mentioned in the advertisement. He also nudged a relative to book another unit in the same project. The papers were signed at his office in Delhis Neeti Bagh, and he and his brother-in-law, Naveen Sawhney, paid Rs 3 crore. It is now 2026 and not a single brick has been laid, he said. We have been cheated out of the money. Thirteen, fourteen, fifteen years, and not a brick has been laid there, Justice Varma said. Last month, he filed a complaint at the Hauz Khas police station in Delhi against Aims Sanya Developers Private Limited, and its directors Roop Kishore Madan, Sanjay Thukral and other unknown persons. Police lodged the FIR on September 18 against unknown persons under sections of criminal conspiracy and criminal intent. A senior police officer said the investigation is underway and no arrests have been made till now. There was no response to emails sent to the builder seeking comment. The phone number registered for this project on the RERA website was not reachable. Five years of assurances and delays Varma initially had no plans to take the legal route, hoping instead that the builders would honour their commitments. It seemed like a good investment to make, to be able to earn some money later., said Varma. who enrolled as a lawyer in 1964 and is quasi-retired - he still practises and does arbitrations. The location was good and they had shown such a good picture, the brochure had made it very attractive. It would also have fetched rent, so that would have been a source of income. According to the complaint, the commercial project was to be completed within 36 months, with a grace period of six months, and was to yield high returns on investment for the investors and purchasers. As per the assurances and public advertisements, the construction of the commercial project was to commence in September 2010 and conclude by March 2014, the complaint stated, alleging that the complainants have been cheated of over Rs 3,22,34,640. After the deadline passed, Varma said he made multiple trips to the builders office in Defence Colony. He would be made to wait for hours, he said, while the builder did not show up. A few years ago, they eventually entered into a Memorandum of Understanding MoU. If there was a delay, he was supposed to give assured returns based on what the property would have fetched if it had been rented. He did not. Eventually, some years ago, we entered into an MoU. He gave advance cheques, but the cheques would bounce. That went on for five years, Varma claimed, adding that the accused paid the monthly assured returns intermittently. Eventually, when the builder stopped picking up calls in October 2025, the family decided to approach the police. He the builder induced and tricked us into buying a property which he had no intention, from day zero, of building, claimed Varmas son Satvik, a senior advocate in the Delhi High Court. Property not even demarcated Satvik said he could have understood the delay if construction had at least begun. If he had dug up the land, there could have been reasons such as a National Green Tribunal order or a ban on construction. But. the property is not even demarcated. We dont even know if it has a name now. Earlier, it was called Landmark Towers, then they changed it to Tempean Towers, he said. Varma and his wife, Nita, had persuaded Naveen to invest in the project. Naveen died two years ago after suffering from cancer for a year and a half. We could have used those resources. My father always felt that because of his mistake, my uncle lost his money as well. There was guilt and a moral dilemma, said Satvik. Varma still has the brochure of the property, which runs into multiple pages and contains elaborate maps. He asked in disbelief What could be more dishonest than this? If it can happen to someone who has been a part of the legal system for over 50 years, then what is likely to be the plight of the common man about whose misery one reads every day, who is deprived of their life savings?

articleTitle: Alcohol shop charges Rs 75 extra for beer bottle, Himachal man wins Rs 12,500 payout
articleFeaturedImageAlt: consumer court beer case
description: The commission observed that selling any packaged commodity or excisable product above its printed MRP constitutes a flagrant violation of laws.
body_raw: A consumer commission in Himachal Pradesh has directed a liquor shop and its salesman to refund Rs 75 and pay 12,500 to a customer after he was allegedly charged Rs 230 for a beer bottle carrying a maximum retail price MRP of Rs 155. President Hemanshu Mishra and members Arti Sood and Narayan Thakur observed that selling any packaged commodity or excisable product above its printed MRP constitutes a flagrant violation of the Legal Metrology Act, Consumer Protection Act, and state excise regulations. Charging above the MRP amounts to an unfair trade practice under Section 247 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, as well as a severe deficiency in service. The refusal to issue a receipt further demonstrates an intent to conceal illegal trade practices, the order read. Illegal trade practices According to the complaint, the complainant visited a liquor shop in Kangra on April 27, 2026, and purchased a bottle of beer. It was stated that the bottle carried an MRP of Rs 155, but the salesman charged him Rs 230, resulting in an overcharge of Rs 75. When the customer objected, the salesman allegedly told him that he was charging the amount on the instructions of the shop owner. The salesman also allegedly refused to issue a purchase receipt. Alleging gross deficiency in service and unfair trade practice, the complainant moved consumer commission seeking a refund and compensation. The liquor shop and its salesman did not appear before the commission after being served with notices and were proceeded against ex-parte. The commission noted that the complainants evidence therefore remained unrebutted and unchallenged. The opposite parties, despite valid service of notice, chose not to contest the complaint and opted to remain ex-parte. Consequently, the evidence adduced by the complainant remains entirely unrebutted, unchallenged, and uncontroverted. There is no legal or factual reason to disbelieve the cogent, trustworthy, and convincing evidence adduced by the complainant, it said. The commission found that the complainant had established that he was charged Rs 230 for a product bearing an MRP of Rs 155. It also noted that refusal to issue a receipt further showed an intent to conceal illegal trade practices. The commission thus allowed the complaint and directed the opposite parties to jointly and severally refund Rs 75 and awarded Rs 5,000 compensation and Rs 7,500 litigation costs. Taking note of what it described as the gravity of the illegal overcharging and the alleged defiance of excise norms by a licensed liquor vend, the commission directed that a copy of its order be sent to the Additional Commissioner, Excise and Taxation Department, Dharamshala, for strict departmental and penal action as per rules. Takeaway Sellers cannot charge consumers more than the printed MRP. Overcharging above the MRP can amount to an unfair trade practice and deficiency in service, attracting refund, compensation and litigation costs. Aggrieved consumers may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Himachal Pradesh helpline 18001808087 or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: Rs 5,000 per student: Gujarat doctor caught accepting bribe for ‘not harassing’ students
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bribery
description: Dr Rahim Ibrahim Memon, medical superintendent of the J S Chauhan Civil Hospital for allegedly seeking bribe of Rs 40,000 from 8 students.
body_raw: A government medical superintendent in Gujarat was arrested on Monday by the state Anti-Corruption Bureau ACB for seeking and receiving a bribe from medical students who were deputed to his hospital for rural service. The ACB, on Monday, booked and arrested Dr Rahim Ibrahim Memon, 59, Medical Superintendent Class-1 of the J S Chauhan Civil Hospital in Devgadh Baria, Dahod, for allegedly seeking the bribe under the pretext of not harassing the medical students during their time at the institution headed by him. A statement from the ACB on Tuesday stated, A total of eight students were appointed to J S Chauhan Government Civil Hospital, Devgadh Baria, Dahod, under the District Residency Programme DRP. The accused demanded a bribe of Rs 40,000 in total, calculated at Rs 5,000 per student, from the eight students in exchange for assigning favourable duties and ensuring they would not be harassed during their service. The incident came to light after one of the students who refused to pay the bribe approached the Gandhinagar ACB, said officials who set a trap to nab him. A team of the anti-corruption agency set a trap at the government staff quarters of the officer, who was caught red-handed while accepting a bribe of Rs 40,000 from the complainant, said the ACB. He was placed under arrest, and further investigation is underway.

articleTitle: Cracks in Mahayuti: Shiv Sena fields candidate against BJP for Pune MLC seat
articleFeaturedImageAlt: eknath-shinde
description: Tensions within Maharashtra's ruling Mahayuti alliance reached a flashpoint as Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena fielded Mangesh Chivate for the Pune Teachers’ constituency against the BJP's nominee Kaustubh Gawade.
body_raw: Disagreements within Maharashtras ruling Mahayuti alliance surfaced on the final day of nomination filings for the Legislative Council elections, as Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena Tuesday fielded Mangesh Chivate from the Pune Teachers constituency, a seat where ally BJP has already nominated its own candidate. The move raises the prospect of an internal contest within the alliance ahead of the Maharashtra Legislative Council elections scheduled for October 23. Elections are being held across five seats falling vacant as sitting members terms end on December 6. These include three Graduates constituencies Aurangabad, Pune, and Nagpur divisions, and two Teachers constituencies Amravati and Pune divisions. Following the nomination deadline, scrutiny of papers will take place on October 7, with the final date for withdrawal of candidature set for October 9. Votes will be counted on October 27. Chivate filed his nomination papers a day after Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde returned from New Delhi, where he met Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Party sources indicated that Shinde discussed Chivates candidature during the visit, particularly after the BJP fielded Kaustubh Gawade for the Pune Teachers seat. A lot can happen While expressing confidence that the BJP would agree to a resolution on candidate withdrawals, Shinde said his party remains firm on Chivates nomination. The process of filing nomination papers for the Legislative Council elections is underway, and there is still time for withdrawal. During this period, discussions will take place among leaders of Mahayuti, and a decision will be made following those talks, Shinde said. Mangesh Chivate is contesting the Pune Teachers constituency seat. After the nomination deadline ends, the withdrawal process will begin. A lot can happen during this time, he added. After receiving his official form from the party, Chivate thanked Eknath Shinde and MP Shrikant Shinde. Shiv Sena workers celebrated his nomination outside the office, lifting him on their shoulders as he held the form. I am thankful to them for picking me for the MLC seat, Chivate said, adding that he remains confident of securing a victory in the Pune Teachers constituency based on his work. Reacting to Shiv Senas move, BJP Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis acknowledged the ongoing rift over the seat. We could not reach a consensus for the Pune seat. There is still time for withdrawal. We will discuss it, Fadnavis said.

articleTitle: Francis Halzen wins Nobel Physics 2026 for IceCube and cosmic neutrinos

body_raw: Physics Nobel Prize 2026 The Nobel Prize in Physics for 2026 was announced on Tuesday by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Stockholm, and it has been awarded to Belgiums particle physicist Francis Halzen for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. The Nobel Committee, in a press release, stated that the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, conceived by Halzen, tracks neutrinos that originate in the distant cosmos. It added, The neutrino interactions that are continuously collected by IceCube will provide researchers with novel knowledge about the violent settings in which high-energy neutrinos can be created-and could even reveal previously unknown cosmic phenomena. articleTitle: Maharashtra police told CJP volunteers to skip Delhi protest, asked who’s paying: Dipke
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Abhijeet Dipke CJP mumbai protest
description: Ahead of the October 10 Jantar Mantar protest, the CJP founder called the Chandrapur police notices "dictatorship." The district's SP says they are routine before any protest.
body_raw: Cockroach Janta Party CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday accused the Maharashtra Police of trying to intimidate protesters, after police in Chandrapur issued notices to volunteers planning to join a protest at Delhis Jantar Mantar on October 10. He called the action dictatorship. A notice issued by Chandrapurs Ballarpur Police on October 5 under Section 168 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita BNSS to a CJP supporter, which Dipke shared on X, states that police had learnt he was planning to travel to New Delhi to support Dipke in the proposed march. The notice asks why he was joining the CJP agitation, who was funding his participation and what his objective was. It directs him not to take part in the Delhi protest or any agitation without permission, not to associate with violent protesters, not to post violent content on social media and not to make provocative speeches. It also directs him to follow police instructions and not obstruct public peace or law and order, and warns of preventive or criminal action if a violation leads to, or could lead to, a cognisable offence. The notice further states that Section 3713 of the Maharashtra Police Act is in force in Chandrapur district by order of the district collector to maintain law and order, and warns of legal action if he violates it and a law-and-order situation arises from his actions. At a press conference, Dipke said several volunteers had received similar notices, asking them not to join the protest and seeking details of their travel to Delhi, including who was paying for it. Somewhere or the other, the Maharashtra Police have broken our hearts. Yesterday, some of our volunteers received notices from the Chandrapur Police. They have been told not to go to the protest at Jantar Mantar. They have also been asked where the funds for their travel to Delhi are coming from, he said. If a person from Maharashtra wants to go to Delhi for a protest, what business is it of the Chandrapur Police to ask where his travel expenses are coming from? Cant a person himself buy a railway ticket worth Rs 1,000 or Rs 1,500? he asked. Chandrapur Superintendent of Police Ayush Nopany said the notices were routine. Issuing such notices before any protest or event is a routine activity. This is a prohibitory provision, and the police noticed that some people from Chandrapur were likely to travel to Delhi for the protest. We wanted to caution them against violence and provocative speeches, and remind them that they need to obtain permission from the concerned police station - in this case, the police station in Delhi and not Chandrapur, he told The Indian Express. He stressed that the notices were a preventive measure and not aimed specifically at the protesters. Dipke questioned the polices suggestion that the protest could turn violent. The notice says the protesters could become violent. How does the Chandrapur Police already know that the protest will turn violent? Has it already been planned that it will become violent? On the warning against social media posts, he said, I want to ask the Maharashtra Police to show me one video where anyone from our side has said anything that could lead to violence. I keep speaking about Gandhi and Ambedkar. Does that appear violent? Why is the Maharashtra Police behaving like the Delhi Police? When did Jantar Mantar come under the Chandrapur Police? Who are the Chandrapur Police to tell people not to participate in a protest at Jantar Mantar? he asked. Who told these officials to issue these notices? No police officer would send such notices on his own. One or two police officers should not end up bringing disrepute to the Maharashtra Police. Dipke also criticised the Mumbai Police over action against tribal students marching in Mumbai. He alleged that some students in the agitation, which he said was led by tribal activist Rahul Pawra, were detained and beaten. Criminals have reduced so much that you have started laying hands on students? he asked, questioning whether police would treat the children of influential politicians and businessmen the same way. He accused the BJP of assuming that protesters are paid to take part, and repeated his demand for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation, citing allegations of voter deletions and the Supreme Courts observations on Form 6 applications. Every Indian should demand Gyanesh Kumars resignation because our right to vote is being taken away, he said. The Form 6 row follows The Indian Express investigation that revealed objections by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi to a declaration added to the online version of Form 6, the form used to enrol new voters. The ECI has said the Supreme Court upheld the declaration, a claim legal experts have disputed, arguing the court never directly examined its validity. He said he was ready to face arrest. If you want to arrest me, arrest me. I am sitting here. Impose NSA, impose UAPA if you think that threatening us with arrest will make us remain silent. That will not happen. If you want to put me in jail, put me there. We will continue to fight to save democracy.

articleTitle: Tata feud widens, key Trust on edge as Charity Commissioner steps in
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Venu Srinivasan (left) and Vijay Singh. (File Photo/ Facebook Tata Trusts)
description: Charity Commissioner has sought a response from the trust by October 12, adding urgency to a dispute that has moved beyond differences behind closed doors.
body_raw: Pressure is mounting on the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust SDTT as the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner has sought a response to the complaints filed by Tata Sons Director and SDTT Trustees Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh, even as a separate order on the Sir Ratan Tata Trust SRTT is expected in the coming weeks. The latest move adds another layer to the increasingly bitter internal dispute within the Tata Trusts, with questions over the governance of the two principal trusts that together hold more than half of Tata Sons. The Charity Commissioners proceedings have already had a direct impact on Tata Sons, with the holding companys annual general meeting AGM adjourned after the regulators restraining order prevented SRTT from conducting its board proceedings. The Charity Commissioner had earlier issued an ex-parte order restraining SRTT from holding meetings and taking decisions while an inquiry into the composition of its board was pending. The order has effectively frozen the trusts functioning and created a procedural hurdle for Tata Sons. The SDTT now faces scrutiny on a separate front following complaints by Srinivasan and Singh. Srinivasan had sought an immediate inquiry into the administration and governance of SDTT, including the appointment and continued status of its perpetual trustees and the basis on which Noel Tata assumed and continues to hold the chairmanship of Tata Trusts. The Charity Commissioner has sought a response from the trust by October 12, adding urgency to a dispute that has moved well beyond differences behind closed doors. Trusts charitable objectives SDTT resolution targets Srinivasan Srinivasan and Singh also alleged that SDTT trustees exposed the trust and its charitable corpus to potentially significant fiscal consequences by involving the trust directly in commercial activities that, according to him, may not be incidental to its charitable objectives. He described such conduct as mismanagement of the affairs and property of SDTT and a breach of trustees duties. The dispute intensified after SDTT circulated a resolution seeking to restrain Srinivasan, in his capacity as a nominee director on the Tata Sons board, from participating in or voting on the proposed listing of Tata Sons. They termed the move an extraordinary attempt to prevent him from exercising his independent judgment and vote. He alleged that it was an attempt to neutralise his position as a trustee because his views differed from those of other trustees. He further described it as an attempt to effect a power grab within SDTT and influence the course of Tata Sons. The developments have opened a new front in the Tata Trusts internal battle at a time when the issue of Tata Sons listing has become the central fault line among trustees. The Reserve Bank of India RBI rejected Tata Sons application to remain an unregistered core investment company CIC on September 11 and directed it to comply with applicable regulations, effectively putting the company on the path towards listing. Pending decision on SRTT Meanwhile, the Charity Commissioners pending decision on SRTT remains crucial for Tata Sons. The SRTT holds a 23.56 stake in Tata Sons and its inability to convene a board meeting has prevented it from jointly nominating an authorised representative with SDTT. That nomination is critical under Tata Sons Articles of Association, which require at least five members to be personally present for quorum at the AGM, including an authorised representative jointly nominated by SDTT and SRTT. This was precisely why the Tata Sons AGM scheduled for August 18 was adjourned for want of quorum. The freeze on SRTT meant that the trust could not complete the process required to nominate its representative jointly with SDTT. The consequences extend beyond the immediate AGM. The meeting has to consider key corporate matters, including the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as a director. His current five-year term as Tata Sons chairman ends on February 20, 2027. With the Charity Commissioner now seeking a response from SDTT on the Srinivasan and Singh complaints, and an order on the SRTT proceedings expected in the coming weeks, the regulators decisions could have significant implications for the governance of the Tata Trusts as well as the functioning of Tata Sons, sources tracking the developments said.

articleTitle: ‘Like straw fire’: Quoting Nepali proverb, Sikkim High Court quashes wife’s cruelty case
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Straw fire Sikkim High Court husband wife cruelty Nepali proverb
description: The wife had lodged an FIR in 2022 alleging repeated misconduct and cruelty by her 50-year-old husband.
body_raw: Quashing criminal proceedings against a 50-year-old man after he and his wife settled their differences and resumed living together, the Sikkim High Court cited an old Nepali proverb that compares a quarrel between husband and wife to a straw fire that burns brightly but briefly. Justice Bhaskar Raj Pradhan was hearing the husbands plea to quash an FIR registered in 2022 on his 46-year-old wifes complaint alleging cruelty and repeated misconduct. He quashed the proceedings after the couple, who had been living together again for two years, reached a compromise. The criminal prosecution against the petitioner-husband be quashed to enable them to continue their life with an assurance from the petitioner that he shall conduct himself in a manner conducive to a peaceful and respectful matrimonial co-existence. An old Nepali proverb says Logne-swasniko jhagada paral ko aag whose English equivalent would be A quarrel between husband and wife is like a straw fire-it burns brightly but briefly, the October 1 order read. The husband expressed regret for his conduct and assured the court that he would maintain a peaceful and respectful relationship with his wife. Married in 2005 The court noted that the couple had married in 2005 and that the husband was facing criminal proceedings based on a complaint filed by his wife in 2022, alleging cruelty and detailing the alleged misconduct she had faced. An FIR was registered based on her complaint, and the investigation later led to the filing of a chargesheet. The husband then approached the high court, seeking to quash the FIR and criminal proceedings. He submitted a compromise signed by the couple in April this year, under which they agreed to live peacefully together, keeping their daughters well-being in mind. The husband also promised not to misbehave with or ill-treat his wife and to maintain a good relationship with her. The husbands counsel, advocate Rahul Rathi, and the wifes counsel, advocate Safal Sharma, told the court that they had personally spoken to their respective clients and believed that quashing the criminal proceedings would be in the familys best interest and give the couple a second chance. Husband regretted actions Court After interacting with the couple, the high court noted that the husband regretted his behaviour, repented his actions and sought forgiveness from his wife. It also noted that the couple had been living together for the past two years and that the husband said he had changed and was now a better person. Both of them state that they have a daughter who is 18 years old, who is living with them and they want to ensure that her happiness remains paramount, the court noted. The high court also noted that the compromise deed said the couple had considered their daughters well-being while resolving their differences and agreeing to maintain a good relationship. Accordingly, the court quashed the FIR and the criminal proceedings against the husband.

articleTitle: Freefall dating explained: Why some singles chase risky relationships for an adrenaline rush
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Freefall dating and risky relationship behaviour
description: Freefall dating, also called voltage dating, describes pursuing risky or emotionally intense romantic situations for the adrenaline rush.
body_raw: Dating trends on social media often introduce new labels for relationship behaviours that many people may already recognise. The latest to gain attention is freefall dating, also referred to as voltage dating. According to a report by VICE, the trend describes people deliberately pursuing risky or emotionally charged romantic situations, not necessarily because they are healthy or compatible, but because they create an adrenaline rush. Examples include developing feelings for a colleague or pursuing a friends former partner, where the excitement comes from the uncertainty, secrecy, or perceived risk rather than the relationship itself. While this may feel thrilling in the moment, experts suggest that these intense emotional highs can sometimes be mistaken for genuine compatibility or love. The report also notes that some singles increasingly seek reassurance from external sources, including AI and tarot readers, instead of trusting their own instincts. DISCLAIMER This article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. Intensity vs genuine attraction Counselling psychologist Athul Raj tells indianexpress.com, We tend to romanticise emotional intensity, but intensity is not a reliable measure of compatibility. In fact, uncertainty can be psychologically compelling because the brain becomes preoccupied with what feels unpredictable or incomplete. When affection is inconsistent, every moment of closeness carries disproportionate emotional significance, making the relationship feel deeper than it may actually be. That is often mistaken for chemistry. Healthy attraction looks quieter. It doesnt depend on emotional volatility to sustain interest. Instead of asking, How strongly do I feel?, a more useful question is, What is this relationship consistently bringing out in me? If the answer is persistent anxiety, hypervigilance, or the need for constant reassurance, those experiences deserve attention just as much as the attraction itself. Why relationship patterns repeat Relationship patterns rarely emerge in isolation. Raj shares that they are often shaped by earlier emotional experiences and reinforced over time. Individuals who have learned that closeness is unpredictable or has to be earned may unconsciously find themselves drawn towards similar dynamics later in life. It is less about seeking emotionally unavailable people and more about returning to a relational template that already feels familiar. He adds that the difficulty is that familiarity can create a false sense of emotional fit. Over repeated experiences, the pursuit itself begins to feel meaningful, even when the relationship offers very little emotional security. Unless people pause to examine the pattern rather than the partner, they often end up repeating the same emotional story with different individuals. Seeking reassurance outside yourself The search for reassurance is rarely about relationships alone. More often, it reflects discomfort with uncertainty. Dating requires us to make decisions without guarantees, and that ambiguity can be difficult to tolerate. External sources may provide temporary certainty, but they cannot substitute self-awareness. What I encourage people to pay attention to is not whether someone else believes the relationship will work, but whether their own lived experience consistently aligns with what they want from a partner. The quality of a relationship is revealed less by promises and more by repeated patterns of behaviour. Learning to trust those patterns is often a more reliable guide than seeking answers outside oneself, concludes Raj.
