articleTitle: Allies turned foes? Bombay HC steps into BJP vs Shiv Sena in Ulhasnagar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bombay HC ulhasnagar BJP vs Shiv Sena
description: The Mayor, a Sena Corporator, allegedly altered the UMC Commissioner's recommendations, excluding the names of S B Singh and Pradeep Ramchandani – the other BJP nominees.
body_raw: In a setback for the ruling Shiv Sena in the Ulhasnagar Municipal Corporation UMC in Thane district, the Bombay High Court on Monday halted further steps on Mayor Ashwini Kamlesh Nikams decision to recommend only two of four BJP candidates as co-opted or nominated corporators. The Mayor, a Sena Corporator, allegedly altered the UMC Commissioners recommendations, excluding the names of S B Singh and Pradeep Ramchandani-the other BJP nominees. Ramchandani, along with BJP district president Rajesh Vadhrya, had approached the court with pleas challenging the proposed nomination of councillors in the Special General Body Meeting SGBM of the UMC held on October 1, which recommended the names of only two of four BJP candidates while recommending five candidates of the Ulhasnagar Shahar Vikas Aghadi USVA - alliance dominated by the Shiv Sena. Prima facie, there appears to be substance in the contentions of the counsel for the Petitioners on whether the Mayor at all had any authorityjurisdiction under the Maharashtra Municipal Corporations Qualifications and Appointment of Nominated Councillors Rules, 2012, to reject the nominations as made, and place the names of only two candidates out of four as recommended by the Commissioner, a bench of Justices Girish S Kulkarni and Neela K Gokhale noted. In the meantime, till the adjourned date of hearing, the Municipal Secretary is restrained from taking any steps to notify andor undertake any publication of the nominated councillors as per the provisions of Rule 6 of the 2012 Rules, the HC noted. Senior advocates Birendra Saraf and Anil Y Sakhare, appearing for the petitioners, argued that while the Municipal Commissioner, under Rule 5 1 of the 2012 Rules, had recommended three USVA candidates, the Mayor placed the names of five USVA candidates before the house and thereafter, hurriedly closed the meeting with the national anthem. The long-standing BJP-Shiv Sena dispute over UMC-nominated corporators had earlier reached the High Court and Supreme Court, which ordered the convening of SGBM for the issue by October 1, after which the Mayor took a decision in question in the present pleas. It should be noted that BJP and Shiv Sena are allies in the state, but not the civic body. On October 5, the petitioners sought urgent ad-interim relief and argued that as per 2012 rules, the Mayor had no power to reject the Commissioners recommended candidates. Finding prima facie substance in petitioners contentions, the bench issued notices to the respondents, directing them to file reply affidavits by October 12.

articleTitle: Knowledge Nugget | How should you read Maharashtra’s drought?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Knowledge Nugget | How should you read Maharashtra's drought UPSC IAS, UPSC CSE, UPSC 2027
description: Maharashtra has declared drought in 265 of its 358 talukas amid an 18% rainfall deficit and prolonged dry spells across large parts of the state. What is drought, and how is it classified in India? Which parts of Maharashtra are most drought prone? Also go beyond the nugget to understand how a drought is declared in India.
body_raw: Take a look at the essential events, concepts, terms, quotes, or phenomena every day and brush up your knowledge. Heres your UPSC Current Affairs knowledge nugget for today on Drought. Knowledge Nugget Drought Subject Geography, Disaster Management Why in the news? On September 26, the Maharashtra government declared a drought in 265 out of the states 358 talukas, across its 36 districts, with Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis terming the crisis the worst the state has endured since 1972. Key takeaways 1. With no rainfall in over 20 days during the crucial kharif crop season and the Southwest monsoon receding, the crisis is expected to worsen in the summer months next year. 2. The Maharashtra government has directed all municipal corporations, municipalities, and gram panchayats to impose a minimum 10 percent water cut from October 16, citing water storage, drought-like conditions, and the possibility of El Nino-related water stress extending into next year. 3. From June 1 to September 26, Maharashtra has received 798.2 mm of rainfall against a normal 970.9 mm, a deficit of 18. 4. According to the India Meteorological Department IMD, 31 of 36 districts in Maharashtra are rain-deficient, with 20 of these facing a deficit of 25 to 58 per cent. 5. Beyond the deficit, shifting rain patterns have added to the damage in more than 100 of the states 355 drought-hit talukas, gaps between rain spells have stretched to 4060 days. 6. As a result, the main kharif crop, sown across 147 lakh hectares, has withered. Maharashtras agriculture is largely rain-fed its irrigation potential, at under 20 per cent, is much lower than in states like Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. What is drought? -Drought is a rainfall scarce period, affecting the availability of water for irrigation, drinking etc. -Ministry of Agriculture is the nodal Ministry in respect of monitoring and managing drought conditions. It classifies droughts into meteorological droughts, hydrological droughts and agricultural droughts. -Meteorological drought is classified based on rainfall deficiency w.r.t. long term average-25 or less is normal, 26-50 is moderate and more than 50 is severe. It is usually the starting point of drought conditions, indicated by prolonged dry spells. -Hydrological drought is best defined as deficiencies in surface and sub-surface water supplies leading to a lack of water for normal and specific needs. -Such conditions arise even in times of average or above average precipitation when increased usage of water diminishes the reserves. It can develop after prolonged rainfall deficiency or excessive withdrawals. -Agricultural drought is identified by 4 consecutive weeks of meteorological drought. Scarcity of water and inadequate soil moisture for normal crop growth starts affecting agricultural production. Which regions in Maharashtra are prone to drought and why? 7. Marathwada and Vidarbha, the two rain-shadow regions of the state which traditionally are drought-prone, have received very little rainfall. 8. Marathwada is particularly affected, having received 38 less rainfall than normal, while Vidarbha has a 27 deficiency. 9. The big deficit is in seven districts - Solapur, Dharashiv, Latur, Hingoli, Jalna, Beed and parts of Nanded, which are away from Godavari river - where rainfall has been just around 50 of normal. Except Solapur, all these districts fall in Marathwada region. 10. Vidarbha region is a little less affected, while western Maharashtra, which is the sugarcane and onion producing zone, is in a relatively comfortable position. Nashik district, known for onion production, has received 37 excess rainfall till now. 11. In Vidarbha, the average deficit across 11 districts is 27, with the shortfall ranging from 26 in Yavatmal to 42 in Amravati. Did you know? - A drought year is especially hard on the women. While most of them work on fields along with the men of the household, their days start much before daybreak, usually around 4 am - a relentless cycle of cooking, cleaning, tending to the children and livestock, besides spending backbreaking hours on the land they till but dont own. What are the relief measures undertaken by the Maharashtra government? 12. The declaration, under the Drought Management Code, 2016, will trigger crop-loss surveys and a package of immediate concessions, including waiver of land revenue, restructuring of crop loans, a stay on recovery of agriculture-related loans and relaxation of Viksit BharatGuarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission Gramin VBG RAM G norms. 13. The government has also provided for concessions on electricity bills for agricultural pumps, with bills for pumps up to 7.5 HP already waived and concessions to apply to pumps above that capacity. 14. Financial assistance for crop losses will be decided separately after the assessment is completed, government officials said. 15. For farmers and rural households, the immediate relief measures announced with the drought declaration include a waiver of land revenue, restructuring of crop loans and a stay on recovery of agriculture-related loans. 16. Other measures include a waiver of examination fees for school and college students, deployment of tankers for drinking water wherever required, no disconnection of electricity supply to agricultural pumps in villages declared to be facing shortages, and arrangements for foodgrains and fodder. 17. The government has also directed authorities to plan drinking water and livestock water supply and undertake water conservation works in affected areas. The measures are intended to provide immediate relief while the crop-loss assessment is carried out. 18. The extent of compensation to individual farmers will depend on the findings of the surveys and the separate government order to be issued on crop damage assistance. BEYOND THE NUGGET How is a drought declared? 1. Under the National Disaster Response Fund NDRF rules, drought declaration for kharif the monsoon cropping season, which runs from June to October requires an assessment that can begin from October 5, once the monsoon starts to withdraw. 2. For rabi, the winter cropping season from October to April, assessment can be held in March 2027. 3. There is no single definition of drought accepted across India. States have the authority to declare a drought based on local conditions. 4. But the state governments report should conform to parameters specified under NDRF norms, and disaster relief funds can be unlocked by the Centre. 5. Under NDRF rules, drought declaration is based on crop loss, the moisture adequacy index used to assess soil health, and rainfall deficit, along with decline in food production and labour migration in search of work. 6. Sowing must fall below 50 per cent of total cultivable kharifrabi area, drinking water shortage must be severe, groundwater tables must be shrinking, there must be fodder shortage, and rainfall deficit must be up to 70 per cent. Rainfall deficiency is the sole criterion for declaring drought. 3. Crop conditions, soil moisture and socio-economic indicators can also be considered in drought assessment. articleTitle: Delhi police arrests journalist over fake video targeting ACP Vivek Bhagat
articleFeaturedImageAlt: delhi protest
description: The arrest relates to a separate Cyber Police case over a video police said was fabricated; a woman journalist’s complaint against ACP Bhagat is being investigated by the Crime Branch.
body_raw: The Delhi Police Cyber Cell has arrested a 24-year-old independent journalist for allegedly circulating a fabricated video that falsely depicted ACP Vivek Bhagat engaging in sexually inappropriate conduct with a woman during the recent protests. Police said the video circulated on Instagram and Facebook was manipulated and falsely presented as CCTV footage. Bhagats photograph, name and designation were displayed alongside the purported footage, giving the impression that he was the police officer shown in the video. The Cyber Police case is separate from allegations made by a woman journalist against Bhagat, who has accused the officer of inappropriate conduct. The Crime Branch is looking into this complaint. The accused, Nadeem Ahmed Ameen, was apprehended from Haryanas Mewat region on October 5. Police said they recovered a mobile phone allegedly used to circulate the video. Police said he works as an independent journalist and operates an Instagram news account, News Aina Today. A case was registered on October 4 after police monitoring of social media platforms brought certain Instagram and Facebook reels to their notice. The reels showed a person dressed as a police officer allegedly engaging in sexually inappropriate conduct with a woman, while Bhagats photograph, name and designation were prominently displayed alongside the footage, said DCP New Delhi Sachin Sharma. The FIR was registered at the Cyber Police Station, New Delhi District. During the investigation, police traced one of the accounts involved in circulating the material - Instagram handle newsaaina0776 - to Ameen, a resident of Palwal district in Haryana. On examination, the Instagram account was found logged-in in the said device, the DCP said. Police also claimed photographs and other content connected with the alleged fabricated reel were found in the phones gallery. Ameen will be produced before a court. Further investigation is underway. According to police, Ameen is the sixth of seven brothers and is the son of a retired government Urdu lecturer. Police said he had studied up to Class 10 and had started the News Aaina Today Instagram account in April 2026. The account, they said, has around 24,000 subscribers. Larger conspiracy Police said they were also probing whether the circulation of the video was part of a larger conspiracy. An investigation is in progress to ascertain his source of funding and to verify if any larger pre-planned conspiracy was hatched in order to spread instigation and anarchy during the said protest, the DCP added. The Cyber Police is identifying other social media accounts allegedly involved in what the police described as an attempt to create a false narrative, tarnish the image of the Delhi Police, and spread disaffection and dissatisfaction against the government.

articleTitle: Gift coupon fraud: Police bust suspected Dubai-linked fake BPO in Bengaluru
articleFeaturedImageAlt: gift coupon fraud
description: The Bengaluru police initially suspected that employees were being trained to commit fraud and that SIM cards registered in other persons’ names were being used to contact and threaten potential victims.
body_raw: The Bengaluru police have detained and questioned six people after a suspected gift coupon fraud operation targeting overseas victims was uncovered on Hennur Main Road, officials said on Tuesday. The police have not identified any victims in India so far. Investigators suspect that the operation was linked to a network being run from Dubai, though the alleged Dubai connection is yet to be established. The Central Crime Branch CCB registered a case on September 26 following a tip-off that an alleged fraudulent operation was being run from a building. The police initially suspected that employees were being trained to commit fraud and that SIM cards registered in other persons names were being used to contact and threaten potential victims. Around 60 to 70 young men and women were working from the premises, which initially led investigators to suspect that it was being used as a call centre to facilitate online fraud. However, the subsequent investigation indicated that the suspected operation was linked to a gift coupon fraud targeting people outside India, the police said. Not everyone was involved. As per our interrogation, only a few people appear to have known about the activity. We have served notices to everyone and are questioning them to ascertain their roles, a senior CCB officer said. The police have also served notices on more than 60 employees who were working at the premises. Investigators have seized laptops and mobile phones and are examining the devices to determine how the suspected operation functioned and which employees were aware of the alleged fraud. The CCB is yet to establish a financial trail linking the premises to the suspected fraud, as they have not found transaction IDs or other financial details so far. The police said the investigation is continuing to establish the complete modus operandi, the roles played by the employees, and the alleged link to the Dubai-based operation.

body_raw: A cafe chain has put an aloo posto burger on its Durga Puja menu. And a section of Bengalis is incensed - perhaps understandably. The potato mashed, its edges crisped and browned, will presumably be folded into the nutty texture of poppy seed paste, pressed into a patty and tucked into a toasted bun. The umbrage, very likely, is not about the burger itself, but about seeing something intimate, pocket-friendly and comforting being recast in the language of fast food. When a dish has lived in ones home for generations, giving it a new form does risk making innovation feel like intrusion. One of the oft-repeated accounts of eastern Indias culinary history is about how posto became a part of the everyday meal. It is the story of a food born, in part, of the human instinct to make do with what is available. Cultivated in enormous quantities to supply the East India Companys extractive colonial trade, the opium poppy left its tiny white seeds behind for use in local kitchens. Soaked and ground on the shil-nora, the grainy texture of the seeds gives way to a thick, pale paste, almost creamy. The residue of an imperial cash crop was absorbed into the frugal economy of homes. It found a companion in the aloo, a traveller so completely naturalised that its foreignness now seems an affront to the spud. The potato becomes tender and absorbs the posto paste, while mustard oil gives everything a sharp nasal fragrance that softens as it meets the heat of the pan. But now the potato patty sits inside a bun where the rice ought to be. There may be lettuce, perhaps cheese, some sauce or mayonnaise or commercial mustard paste, a toasted surface where there was once steam rising from rice. The ensemble appears to belong to another vocabulary Fast, portable, assembled, engineered for eating with one hand - not licking the fingers. A caveat, however Culinary cultures can become a small place when authenticity becomes a regular test. Posto itself has never been particularly monogamous. There is jhinge posto, with ridge gourd turning soft and almost silky beneath the poppy paste dhyarosh posto, with okra imparting a slippery texture posto with broad beans and other vegetables. There are posto boras, little fritters in which the poppy seed paste crisps around the edges and stays soft within. There are preparations in which posto thickens, coats and binds. Khosha bhaja - salted strips of potato skin embedded with posto and fried until they crackle between the teeth - belongs to a culinary instinct that sees possibility in what might otherwise be thrown away. It is difficult to build a very convincing case for culinary purity in a cuisine that has spent generations finding new things to do with the same small bowl of poppy paste. Is it fair, then, to call the aloo posto in a bun a great culinary transgression? The irritation could have less to do with the burger than with what it seems to say about the food. The faint bitterness of posto rubbing against the starch of the potato, the sharp green chilli, the mustard oil opening up in the heat, the first morsel mixed into rice until everything becomes soft, pale and fragrant - they are memories of meals shared with loved ones. Comfort food has a strange relationship with innovation. We like innovation when it happens to somebody elses food - a paneer makhani or butter chicken pizza, is acceptable to us Indians, Italians balk at the pineapple pizza. We become more cautious when it reaches the foods we recognise by smell before we recognise them by sight. Perhaps that is the paradox that makes the aloo posto burger less innocent than it looks. Home food has never been a museum of fixed objects it has always been about the twists taken by every cook - described with great felicity in the Hindi phrase, haat ka khana - the liberties taken by every generation. But a restaurant changes the transaction. What is unsettling is that the posto whose flavours unfurled bite by bite on the palette is now being announced as an innovation on a festive menu. Dishes are known to wander, and yet they are never quite the prodigal child. Fast food will keep borrowing from home kitchens, and home kitchens will keep changing without much ado. For now, the burger can have its moment under the festive lights and the aloo posto is not going to be displaced from its place with the rice, mustard oil and chillies. I confess I am not averse to tasting the burger. But when the posto meets the aloo, I know I will still reach for the rice. In the years to come, though, the question may well be Will the aloo posto burger be an homage to the East Indian home? Or will it become a marker of that grandiloquent and frequent, but rarely convincing, claim that innovation arrived only yesterday at the chefs kitchen? The writer is senior associate editor, The Indian Express. kaushik.dasguptaexpressindia.com

articleTitle: IIT Ropar launches app to help children learn about plants, crops and agriculture
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The app is designed to introduce agricultural knowledge before children formally study agriculture as a subject
description: The platform is described as free, ad-free and privacy-focused, with a child-focused design aimed at keeping the digital learning environment safe and age-appropriate.
body_raw: IIT Ropars Centre of Excellence in AI for Digital Agriculture, ANNAM.AI, has launched AVNI-Grow with Nature digital learning platform designed to help children learn about plants, crops, food and agriculture through their surroundings. The web and mobile app uses artificial intelligence AI along with hands-on activities to help children identify and understand what they see around them. The platform allows children to explore crops, fruits, vegetables, spices, cereals and millets. For example, a child can use the app while looking at a plant, fruit or crop and learn more about it through AI-powered identification. The idea is to connect what children see in everyday life with basic knowledge about agriculture and food. AVNI developed by the team at IIT Ropar, is available in Hindi and English and also provides audio content for younger children. It includes daily challenges, a digital Nature Book, a Nature Gallery and a Crop Compare feature. These tools allow children to record what they learn, explore different plants and compare crops as part of their learning. The app is designed to introduce agricultural knowledge before children formally study agriculture as a subject, IIT-R said in a statement. A plant in a school garden, a fruit at home or a crop in a nearby field can become a starting point for learning about how food is grown and where it comes from. Also Read IIT Ropar announces scholarship for underprivileged students, lays foundation stone of yogic sciences centre The platform also places emphasis on learning through observation rather than only reading information. Children can explore their surroundings, identify plants and crops and gradually build a basic understanding of agriculture and nature. AVNI has been developed by Dr Mukesh Saini, Co-project Director of ANNAM.AI, IIT Ropar. The initiative is part of ANNAM.AIs work on the use of AI in agriculture and education. The platform, as per the institute is free to access, ad-free and privacy-focused, with a child-focused design aimed at keeping the digital learning environment safe and age-appropriate. ANNAM.AI is working on AI-based digital public infrastructure for Indian agriculture. AVNI extends this work into education by using AI not just to provide information but to help children learn about agriculture through direct observation and exploration. The initiative is aimed at building agricultural awareness among children at an early age, including an understanding of the plants they see, the food they eat and the role agriculture plays in producing it.

articleTitle: Swatantra Bhardwaj gets regular bail in Jantar Mantar assault case
articleFeaturedImageAlt: self-styled influencer Swatantra Bharadwaj
description: A Delhi court had earlier granted the self-styled influencer interim bail for three weeks
body_raw: A Delhi court Tuesday granted self-styled influencer Swatantra Bharadwaj regular bail in a case where he allegedly attacked the father of a student protester who had participated in the Cockroach Janta Party CJP protest in July. Additional Sessions Judge ASJ Saurabh Pratap Singh Laler of the Patiala House Court had earlier granted Bharadwaj interim bail for three weeks. ASJ Laler had then said that it would observe his conduct before considering his plea for regular bail. A detailed regular bail order is awaited. In its order granting Bharadwaj interim bail, ASJ Laler had said, Weighing all circumstances, the Court takes into account that the applicant has been in custody for a little over 10 days. a period that should have afforded him time for reflection. The case Bharadwaj had purportedly admitted to attacking the father of the student protester at Jantar Mantar in a video. He was picked up by the Crime Branch officers from his house in Bulandshahr on September 4 and brought to Delhi after securing a transit remand. On September 4, relevant sections pertaining to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Prevention of Atrocities Act, 1989 SCST Act, were added to an earlier FIR registered against Bharadwaj over the alleged attack, amid a protest by CJP supporters and the Indian Youth Congress, as well as Lok Sabha MPs Chandra Shekhar alias Azad and Rajesh Ranjan alias Pappu Yadav. The same day, another FIR was also registered under sections of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences POCSO Act, 2012, and for criminal intimidation based on the protesters complaint alleging she had received rape threats from Bhardwajs supporters. Bharadwaj had been in judicial custody since September 5 till he was granted interim bail on September 15. While granting interim bail to the accused, the court had also pulled up the police for leaving significant ground uncovered in the investigation. The investigation, as disclosed in the reply, leaves significant ground uncovered. The podcast forms the central basis of the States opposition, and its authenticity is disputed. Yet the reply does not state whether the person who manages the channel has been examined, whether the original footage has been requisitioned, or whether the electronic material has been sent for forensic examination, ASJ Laler had said in the interim bail order.

articleTitle: OpenAI is adding watermarks to ChatGPT text in the EU: Here’s what it means
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The EU AI Act requires developers and providers of AI systems to ensure that content generated by AI is machine-readable. (Express Image)
description: OpenAI is adding an invisible watermark to text generated by ChatGPT and Codex to comply with the EU AI Act's transparency rules.
body_raw: OpenAI has said that it will now add an invisible watermark to all text generated by ChatGPT and Codex in its bid to comply with the EU AI Acts transparency rules that require AI companies to make AI-generated content identifiable to other systems. The company announced its decision on Monday, October 6, in its official blog. The Sam Altman-led company said that the watermark will be rolled out in the next few weeks to eligible ChatGPT and Codex users on all plans. However, the rollout is currently limited to the EU. While the feature is off by default, developers using OpenAIs API worldwide can turn it on for select models. OpenAI said, while acknowledging that text watermarking and detection remain early technologies with significant limitations, that its phased approach reflects both the EU AI Act requirements and the technologies limitations. The company also said that it was opening applications to access its text watermark detector. However, this access will initially be limited to approved researchers and expert organisations that assist the company with evaluation and improvement of the technology. How does the watermark work? In its blog, OpenAI said that its technology named textGrain adds something it describes as an invisible statistical signal to the models word choices. Later, the detector scans for that signal to determine whether a passage contains an OpenAI watermark. OpenAI has published a paper, textGrain Entropy-Calibrated Watermarking for Language Model Text, shedding light on the inner workings of the technology. Further, OpenAI said that in its evaluations, textGrain matched or exceeded the performance of other approaches that it tested, including SythID Google DeepMinds digital watermarking tech for text. OpenAI also revealed that, along with strong performance, under ideal conditions, this technology could not guarantee reliable detection in everyday use. The company said that the detectors can make two kinds of errors-they can detect a watermark where none is present or miss a watermark that is present. Some of the key hurdles to watermark detection are that shorter or more constrained text is harder to detect, while editing text generated by AI can weaken its watermark. The limitations with watermarks OpenAI also pointed out factors that may deem watermarks inconclusive. It said that a watermark may not necessarily mean information about the extent of human judgement, editing or creativity. It does not establish any form of ownership or responsibility most importantly, it does not identify the user. It is also not a barometer to verify accuracy. The company claimed that the absence of a detected watermark does not translate to human authorship. Article 50 of the AI Act, which applies from August 2, 2026, sets out transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems, including generative and interactive AI systems and deepfakes. While providers are required to design AI systems that ensure individuals are explicitly informed whenever they interact with an AI system directly, they must add machine-readable marks to enable the detection of AI-generated or manipulated content. On the other hand, deployers of AI systems must inform users when they are exposed to emotion recognition and biometric categorisation tools, deepfakes, and text publications on matters of public interest without human review or editorial control. According to the Act, these obligations are aimed at building trust and integrity in the information ecosystem. OpenAIs latest announcement follows a similar measure taken by Anthropic in early August when it declared that it is adding invisible watermarks to text and files generated by its Claude models. Anthropic also made the announcement in its bid to comply with the EUs AI Act on Transparency Code. The company said that watermarks will be applied globally to all new models released after August 2, with plans to roll out support for older legacy models.

articleTitle: Rahul’s impromptu move, Priyanka’s negotiation skills: The INDIA march twist
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Lok Sabha LoP and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi climbs atop the barricades during the INDIA bloc MPs' march from Parliament to the ECI, demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. (Express Photo by Abhinav Saha)
description: Congress leaders have credited the Gandhis with derailing the police plan to end the protest.
body_raw: The INDIA bloc protest against the Election Commission took a surprise turn on Tuesday, thanks to Rahul Gandhi and his sister and Wayanad MP, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra.Opposition MPs were detained and pushed into buses to different police stations in Delhi. The protest was all but over when the siblings pulled off an impromptu move that even left Congress leaders confused. India News Live UpdatesRahul Gandhi, Priyankas sit-in at Doordarshan office in face-off with cops Priyanka was already seated in one of the buses, parked outside the Akashvani Bhavan, the headquarters of All India Radio, and Rahul was about to get in. Suddenly, the siblings looked at each other, and then walked past the cops and into the Akashvani Bhavan premises. The move was off the script and the police personnel initially did not know how to react. Once the Gandhis went inside, Congress leaders KC Venugopal and Pawan Khera climbed the boundary wall of Akashvani Bhavan and started raising slogans. Congress leaders Imran Pratapgarhi and Srinivas BV joined them. Most Congress leaders said they had thought the protest was over. We dont know what happened. This was not part of the plan, one of them said. According to sources in the Congress, Rahul Gandhi planned to enter the Akashvani Bhavan premises and then exit through the back gate, located opposite the Election Commission. All the other routes to the poll panels office were blocked for the rally, so the Leader of the Opposition made this plan on the go, the sources said. Once he entered the Akashvani Bhavan premises, police officers shut the back gate. So he sat here in protest, said a source. Only the two of them know what they had in mind when they walked in, said a Congress MP outside Akashvani Bhawan. At this point, the Congress leaders are still camping on the premises as top security officers talk to them. Personnel from Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force are now stationed outside the Akashvani Bhavan. A police officer said the force inside the premises was to ensure the leaders safety. Congress leaders have credited the Gandhis with derailing the police plan to end the protest. The protest would have been over if they didnt do this. Senior Congress leader Pawan Khera said in a post on X, In the morning, the India Alliance attempted to walk towards the election commission. The police forcibly stopped the MPs. Currently, Leader of Opposition Shri Rahul Gandhi and MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra along with several leaders, are sitting on a dharna inside the All India Radio premises which is next to ECI office. The Congress leaders are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, accusing him of disenfranchising voters through the Special Intensive Revision exercise to give advantage to the ruling BJP. According to highly placed sources in the Congress, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra is leading negotiations with the top police officers. Following The Indian Express investigation on the rift within the poll panel, underlining how two Election Commissioners objected on record at least 14 times in 10 months to decisions taken without their knowledge, the Election Commission acknowledged these notes, but described them as part of the panels decision-making process. However, it did not respond to any of the concerns raised by the two Commissioners, nor did it state whether or how these concerns had been addressed. Opposition leaders detained Earlier, top Opposition leaders, including Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and Trinamool Congress MPs Abhishek Banerjee and Derek OBrien, were detained as police stopped the march to the Election Commission office. The protesting MPs were taken away in buses. Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge said the opposition would continue its protest to protect voting rights and democracy. This protest will continue. We are doing this to protect your vote and your freedom. The people of the country are saying that many of their votes have been deleted and vote theft is taking place, and we are fighting and will continue to fight for their protection, he said. BJP takes a swipe Criticising the Opposition march to the Election Commission to demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumars resignation, the BJP said this was yet another attempt by the Congress and its allies to create anarchy and relaunch Rahul Gandhi. Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that the Opposition leaders are venting their frustration over electoral defeats by levelling baseless allegations. Friends in the opposition, the very system you are questioning is the one under which you won in Kerala. Was that victory illegitimate? You won in Karnataka. Was that victory illegitimate? You won in Himachal. Was that victory illegitimate? Opposition governments were formed in Punjab and Jharkhand were those victories illegitimate? the senior BJP leader asked. If you question constitutional institutions, you will commit the sin of plunging the country into the fires of anarchy. Do not commit the sin of plunging the nation into unrest and anarchy. The country and its people will never forgive you, he added. Addressing the media at the BJP headquarters, party spokesperson Sambit Patra said, The Congress has been repeatedly trying to launch and re-launch Rahul Gandhi by any means necessary. When, despite numerous attempts, he failed to gain traction, the Congress and some of its allies decided that even if it meant resorting to anarchy and undermining the nations democracy, they would launch Rahul Gandhi politically at any cost. As part of these efforts, they attacked the Indian army from time to time, the Supreme Court, Hindus, and EVMs Electronic Voting Machines. And for the last few weeks, they have been attacking the Election Commission, Patra said.

articleTitle: ‘Beyond healthy criticism’: Court orders takedown of Punjab Congress politician’s AI videos
articleFeaturedImageAlt: AI-generated videos, AI deepfake videos, Facebook AI videos, Batala Di Rajneeti, Kachi Laan, Thanedar Uncle, Punjab politics AI videos, Chandigarh court order, Punjab and Haryana High Court
description: A Chandigarh court restrains three Facebook pages from sharing AI-generated videos allegedly portraying Congress leader Amandeep Kumar negatively.
body_raw: A Chandigarh court has ordered three Facebook pages to remove AI-generated videos for allegedly maligning the reputation of Punjab Congress functionary Amandeep Kumar. The court said that the content appeared to go beyond healthy public criticism and could adversely affect the health of our democracy and the process of manufacturing of public consent. Kumar sought an interim injunction on the transmission of AI-generated videos in a civil case against the three Facebook pages. Judicial Magistrate First Class Kuldeep Singhnoted that the AI-generated scripted videos contained politically calculated material, in favour of the ruling party in Punjab, and against Kumar, who is from an opposition political party, and held that there was a prima facie case and irreparable loss and balance of convenience in favour of Kumar. The said pages appear to have a political agenda which is beyond healthy public criticism and apparently maligns the image of an individual without verified facts, knowingly. This is quite a serious act done in a very uncontrolled, casual manner, which may adversely affect the health of our democracy and the process of manufacturing of public consent, and the ruling party is responsible for controlling such acts, the October 5 order said. The order added, The other video links given by the plaintiff Kumar mentioned in this order show the apparent AI-generated scripted videos painting one person, namely Amandeep Jaintipua, negatively. Politics vs AI Amandeep Kumar, a lawyer and Congress political figure from Punjab, approached the Punjab and Haryana High Court alleging that three Facebook pages, namely Batale di Rajneeti, Kachi laan and Thanedar uncle, with substantial public reach with 2,200 followers, 1, 100 followers and 11,000 followers respectively, fabricated his visual representation through artificial intelligence and published it in a manner falsely portraying him in a body, dress and appearance, which he never adopted, posed for or consented to. Kumar stated that his reputation and public credibility are important to his political career. He acknowledged that his political actions, speeches, policies and public conduct are subject to fair public criticism and legitimate political disagreements, but objected to the false representation of him through the AI-generated content by these pages. Recently, Kumar came across highly objectionable videos and reels wherein his recognisable face and appearance have been digitally manipulated through Artificial Intelligence and shared on the said Facebook pages. The artificial content was calculated to ridicule and humiliate his character in order to malign his position. The material went to huge public exposure, reaching approximately 178 K, 180 K and 47.8 K views and public reactions. Every share of content exposes the fabricated representation to entire new audience, he stated. Advocates Harinder Deep Singh Bains, Jasdeep Singh Dhillon, Himmat Singh Bajwa and Abhay Singh Mann, appearing for the Congress leader, contended that due to the publishing of aforesaid AI-generated fake content from the referred Facebook pages, irreparable loss is being caused to Kumar, which necessitates the grant of ad-interim ex parte interim injunction putting restraint over the pages from further publishing the fabricated and morphed AI-generated content representing him on any social media platform. The counsel argued that Kumar, who is known as Amandeep Jaintipura, was a frontrunner for the elections of Members of Legislative Assembly under the Indian National Congress Party, from Batala constituency in Punjab in 2027. It was submitted that the Social India Platform referred to contains defamatory, falsely scripted AI-generated content calculated to malign his image, with content glorifying the image of the current MLA from Batala, to benefit the ruling political party. The scripted AI-generated content branded Kumar in a negative light, which is against the truth and strikes at the very fundamental right of the plaintiff concerning dignified public life, the counsel added. It was argued that it was not the case of healthy and fair criticism rather, it was cheap politics which uses the technology in an uncontrolled, unchecked and irresponsible manner. Therefore, there is a strong prima facie case, irreparable loss and balance of convenience in favour of Kumar. Interim injunction granted The court granted the interim injunction to Kumar against the Facebook pages, directing them to refrain from further disseminating, publishing, or uploading AI-generated content involving him until the next date of hearing. Further, the court granted an ad-interim ex parte injunction directing the concerned platform to disable public access to, or suspend, the pages, namely Thanedar uncle, Kachi laan, and Batale Di Rajneeti, linked to the AI-generated content against Kumar, until the next date of hearing. The matter will be next heard on October 22.

More confidence stronger body better stamina better mental well-being more comfortable in my own body more energy to keep up with my daughter and I feel like myself again. articleTitle: NYC Council hearing on AI risks: What Jacob Coxon, others told policymakers
articleFeaturedImageAlt: NYC Council hearing
description: The hearing comes at a time when the New York City Council is examining legislative proposals to require companies to disclose information about AI tools.
body_raw: Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, who quit his job last month over concerns that AI could lead to human extinction by the end of the decade, reiterated those warnings in a hearing by the New York City Council on Monday, October 5. The hearing was held to discuss the risks that AI poses to humanity. Officials from OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and Meta also appeared before the Council, but Elon Musks SpaceX was a no-show. In their testimonies, AI safety researchers who recently exited Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google DeepMind, laid out a reckless culture at the firms. They said that the biggest tech companies are racing to create technology they do not understand how to control. Meanwhile, the tech industry representatives called for greater oversight by local governments in response to mounting concerns that advanced AI systems could endanger humanity. The hearing comes at a time when the Council is examining legislative proposals to require companies to disclose information about AI tools, require third-party approval for AI systems in the city, and allow whistleblowers to receive a portion of fines from AI companies that violate laws. New York Governor Kathy Hochul has also moved to impose reporting and transparency standards around AI. Policymakers elsewhere in the US and the rest of the world are also exploring measures to strengthen AI safety. These moves have been driven by the growing fear of AI systems causing catastrophic harm, coupled with a string of hacking incidents involving AI agents behaving unexpectedly. Last month, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for an intentional slowdown of frontier AI efforts across the world to let safety research catch up. The titans of the AI industry, including OpenAIs Sam Altman, SpaceXAIs Elon Musk, and Googles Demis Hassabis, were in rare agreement. But others like Nvidias Jensen Huang and US President Donald Trump dismissed these concerns as trivial and a hoax. What happened at the NYC Council hearing? The companies run on a startup mindset Move fast, break things, fix them later. That works for a photo sharing app. It does not work for building the most powerful technology ever built, Jacob Coxon, the Anthropic former engineer who has become a leading voice for regulation, was quoted as saying by Associated Press at the Council hearing. On the current path, I think it is more likely than not that humanity loses control to these AIs and it could end in human extinction, Coxon said. A panel of AI company staffers representing tech giants OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta, also testified at the hearing. They told officials that their systems are already improving peoples daily lives and emphasised that safety was the top-most priority. Anthropic and OpenAI representatives said their advanced AI products need to be regulated. I share your commitment to ensuring that technology is developed safely and that its benefits are widely shared, said OpenAIs Morgan Dwyer. On whether the risk posed by AI could be quantified, Dwyer replied, I dont know - I also dont think it matters whether its 1 or 10 or 20 chance that something catastrophic will go wrong. None of these levels is remotely acceptable. We should not train models that we cannot make an extremely strong case that we can keep under human control. I would say that the percentage chance doesnt matter. What matters is the commitment to safety, and that is what OpenAI is committed to doing, he added. Anthropics Logan Graham told the Council that the company welcomes smart regulation and that state and local governments have a role to play in developing frameworks. AI is powerful enough that getting this wrong has real consequences, for individuals, institutions, public trust. We have to work relentlessly to do the science of mitigating the risks, he said.

articleTitle: More wait for Sewri-Worli connector as deadline pushed to May 2027

articleTitle: Trump thinks Iran behind flydubai flight cockpit attack, Vance says can’t say so
articleFeaturedImageAlt: US President Donald Trump said he personally believes Iran was behind the foiled Flydubai attack, while Vice President JD Vance has expressed caution over evidence linking Tehran to the incident.
description: Trump said he personally believes Tehran was involved in the foiled attack on an Israel-bound Flydubai flight, while JD Vance said he had seen no conclusive evidence linking Iran to the incident.
body_raw: Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance have offered differing assessments of a possible Iranian link to the flydubai cockpit attack on the Indian pilot Smit Machchhar last week, with the US President saying he personally believes Tehran was involved, while the Vice President said he had seen no conclusive evidence. Trump said he personally believed Iran was behind the foiled attack last week. I do. I personally do, he said when asked whether he believed Tehran was involved, without elaborating on how he reached that assessment. Vance, however, said that he had seen no conclusive evidence linking Iran to the incident. In terms of involvement with Iran. Thats something I defer to CIA Chief John Ratcliffe and some of the intelligence folks on, Vance told reporters before leaving on a flight to Alaska. I dont want to get ahead of any announcements there, he said. Its certainly something were looking at, but I wouldnt say Ive seen anything conclusive just yet. Asked whether he is concerned about foreign pilots flying in the US, Vance responded, saying, Anytime you have any person coming from outside the United States, youve got to be extra careful that that person is actually a good human being and is going to contribute to American society. Vance invoked the September 11 attacks while arguing that the US needs to be particularly careful about screening people entering the country. Thats the story of the 911 terrorist attack - We brought a lot of people into the United States of America who shouldnt have been here and certainly shouldnt have been flying planes, he claimed. Vance also said the flydubai suspect had a history suggesting he should not have been flying for an airline, while making clear that he was not referring to information known to US intelligence. The interesting thing about that flydubai story is we knew that guy was a problem - meaning not United States intelligence - but if you look historically, that person should not have been flying an airline, Vance continued. So were certainly looking at our procedures within the United States to make sure that people who are obviously flight risks are not getting behind the wheel of an airplane, he added. Netanyahu says too early to link Iran to flydubai incident Earlier, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said it was too early to say whether there was possible Iranian involvement in the flydubai flight incident. The UAE, which is leading the investigation into the incident, said the co-pilot attacked the flights captain, Machchhar, with the cockpits crash axe and tried to seize control of the plummeting aircraft in what it described as a terrorist attack on September 30. The attack nearly caused a crash involving 182 people on board before the captain opened the cockpit door and passengers subdued the Omani co-pilot.

articleTitle: 25 years, three times the cost: Versova-Yari Road bridge gets a December 2027 deadline
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Versova-Yari Road bridge
description: The 206-metre bridge over Kavthe creek, conceptualised in 2002 at Rs 16 crore and now pegged at Rs 48 crore, will cut a 30-minute detour between Lokhandwala and Andheri back road to under 10
body_raw: The Versova-Yari road bridge - one of suburban Mumbais much-awaited infrastructure projects is set to see the light of day in December 2027, 25 years after it was conceptualized. The 206-meter-long bridge is set to connect Lokhandwala with Andheri back road, passing over the Kavthe creek at Andheri West. At present, there is no direct connectivity between these two places, and the travel time between these two places takes 30 minutes. Meanwhile, once operational, the travel time is set to drop below 10 mins. Earlier on Monday, a team of Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation BMC officials led by Abhijit Bangar - additional municipal commissioner Projects carried out a site inspection. Following this, the private agency executing the work was told to complete the work by December next year. At present the work of erecting the pillars and columns is underway. The bridge will pass above the creek establishing a direct east-west connection between Yari Road, Panch Marg and Versova in Andheri West, an official told the Indian Express. The bridge will be Y-shaped, while the main structure will feature a 110-metre-long single-span steel basket handle arch structure. Tension rods will connect the steel arch to the bridge deck slab. The cost of this bridge has been pegged at Rs 48 crore. Initially the cost of this project was pegged at round Rs 16 crore. However, with the delay, the project saw a massive cost escalation. In 2019, members from a local housing society filed a petition with the Supreme Court stating that this project would affect mangroves therefore, it needs to be scrapped. They have also stated that the proposed alignment of this bridge was flawed. Later in August 2022, the SC quashed the stay. Following this, the project came back on track. Civic officials said that they had to acquire a slew of permissions from the forest and mangrove departments before they could go ahead with the work. As a result, the issuance of permission took more than three years, and the work could have begun last year.

articleTitle: C Raja Mohan: In Iran war, US midterm elections are the new front
articleFeaturedImageAlt: iran war, us midterms
description: For both Tehran and the White House, managing the home front can matter as much as gaining on the battlefield
body_raw: Irans Revolutionary Guards have found a new audience for their war with Donald Trump The American voter. The history of warfare tells us that weakening the adversarys domestic support can be as important as defeating its armed forces on the battlefield. In a 25-page letter last week, the Guards appealed to the honourable people of the United States to reject Trumps policies and consider peaceful coexistence with Iran. Trump, in turn, hopes that escalating military and economic pressure will force the Islamic Republic to fall in line. Coming just weeks before the midterm elections, the letter brings Tehran directly into Americas domestic political contest. With Republicans vulnerable in November, the political consequences of the Iran war are becoming harder to separate from its military course. In Tehran, too, internal struggles between advocates of negotiation and hardliners favouring confrontation are shaping the wars conduct. That brings us to the idea of the October surprise in American politics - a major event or political move that changes the national mood before the traditional voting in the first week of November. Iran helped make the phrase part of American political language during the 1980 presidential election. The Iranian Revolution of February 1979 overthrew the Shah, a close American ally. In November, militants seized the US embassy in Tehran and took its staff hostage. The crisis haunted President Jimmy Carters re-election campaign. His Republican challenger, Ronald Reagan, feared that freeing the hostages before November would rescue Carters political fortunes. Allegations that Reagans team secretly worked to delay the release remain disputed. The hostages came home as Reagan took office in January 1981. Irans upheaval had become entangled with the struggle for power in Washington. Today, Tehran hopes to exploit another American electoral moment. Trump insists the midterms do not determine his Iran policy. But the electoral calendar is now visibly intertwined with the military debate. In an interview last week, Trump said it was possible that US bombing of Iran could intensify after the November 3 elections. He has also said the war could be won right after the election - or perhaps before it. The military preparations reinforce the message. The unfolding deployment gives Trump more options if diplomacy fails - and gives Tehran reason to take his threats seriously. Setting aside the Islamic Revolutions enduring slogan, Death to America, the IRGC letter claims to have no quarrel with ordinary Americans. Its immediate target is Trump. It hopes public anxiety over the war and rising prices will weaken Republicans and create space for a more accommodating policy in Washington. The appeal could easily backfire as Republicans accuse Democrats of serving Tehrans interests. Iran is not alone in trying to exploit domestic divisions. Trump has hoped that military and economic pressure would encourage Iranians to challenge their rulers. That expectation has produced little so far. Tehrans appeal to American voters may prove equally ineffective. Both sides nevertheless see the adversarys home front as a battlefield. Meanwhile, Trump has secured an important gain at Hormuz. The recovery in Gulf oil flows has accelerated. New data show Gulf crude exports averaged about 16.3 million barrels a day in September - roughly 91 per cent of pre-war levels. This does not establish Trumps claim of total control. Iran never enjoyed uncontested sovereignty over the international waterway. Its leverage lay in making passage dangerous and expensive. Tanker attacks, higher insurance costs and uncertainty forced its adversaries to spend heavily on keeping commerce moving. Nor has the energy crisis disappeared. The problem has shifted from crude supply towards logistics and refining. Refined-product exports from the Gulf recovered to only about 60 per cent of pre-war levels in September. That distinction matters politically. More crude moving through Hormuz does not automatically mean cheaper diesel at American pumps. Crude must be transported, refined and distributed. Diesel prices have a direct effect on inflation and cost of living, a major issue in US domestic politics right now. The G7s decision, under Trumps pressure, to release 100 million barrels of crude and fuel products from emergency reserves is meant to ease this pressure. But Trumps dilemma remains. Convincing Tehran that it cannot wait him out requires a credible threat of escalation. Reassuring American voters requires avoiding an escalation that sends fuel prices soaring again. Irans letter seeks to exploit precisely that tension. Tehran faces pressures of its own. Washingtons Operation Economic Outcast is tightening the financial noose. The US has expanded sanctions from military procurement networks to Irans automotive, rail, manufacturing and steel sectors. Washington has now warned foreign financial institutions that doing business with Iran could bring sanctions without prior notice. Neither side can assume the other will crack first. The October surprise could be another military blow, a diplomatic opening, or another fuel-price shock. For India, there is a larger lesson from the US and Iranian efforts to influence each others domestic politics. Americas hopes of political change in Iran and Tehrans appeal to American voters underline an old truth Wars are fought within societies as much as between states. Managing the home front can matter as much as gaining military ground on the battlefield. The principle applies in peacetime too, especially to democracies such as India. Effective engagement with a turbulent world demands cohesion at home. Political differences are inevitable in a democracy. But a politics of winner takes all can turn those differences into debilitating domestic conflicts. That inevitably weakens the nations capacity to deal with mounting challenges abroad and the growing prospects for external meddling in its domestic affairs. The writer is contributing editor on international affairs for The Indian Express. He is professor and director at the Motwani Jadeja Institute of American Studies, Jindal Global University, Delhi

articleTitle: What happened when the lone municipality fire truck went to ‘wash’ a BJP MLA’s house in Gujarat’s Dahod

body_raw: A BJP MLA allegedly summoning a fire tender from the Devgadh Baria municipality in Dahod district to wash his house has kicked up a controversy, at a time when the states water reserves are under pressure after a deficit monsoon. The MLAs house is nearly 25 kms from the fire station which has just one fire tender. Videos of firemen spraying water on his house in absence of any fire, went viral after which the municipality took a charge from the MLA. BJP leader and President of Devgadh Baria Municipality Dharmesh Kalal confirmed that Khabad had summoned the fire tender for cleaning purpose. He clarified that the cleaning was stopped within 15 seconds as soon as officials informed the fire officer about the deployment. He also added that the municipality recovered Rs 2700 as charges from the MLA after controversy. Sources said, Khabad, a former minister was recuperating in hospital from a major surgery when the truck was summoned allegedly to wash his house in Dhanpur-Pipero area of Devgadhbaria town ahead of Diwali. Most Gujaratis take up deep cleaning of their homes during Diwali, sometimes washing them. However, the timing makes the episode harder to dismiss as Gujarat is dealing with uneven and deficient rainfall, leaving water storage in several reservoirs under pressure. Sources within the BJP say that Khabad, a four-time MLA, who recently underwent a kidney transplant surgery has been advised to observe meticulous hygiene and since he had been away for over two months for treatment, the house was locked and needed cleaning. The incident, however, has made for another awkward moment for the BJP, which has already witnessed a defeat during the recent bypolls of the Municipality following a rebellion against Kalal. eom

articleTitle: Can Ladakh grow saffron? First-ever mass plantation drive begins in Leh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ladakh saffron cultivation
description: Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena announced the planting of 90,000 saffron corms in Leh as part of Project Him Sarovar, a government initiative to reclaim lost agrarian land in Ladakh.
body_raw: Indias saffron cultivation is set to expand beyond Kashmir, with a mass plantation drive underway in Ladakhs Leh district as the Union Territory makes its first attempt to cultivate the high-value spice on a large scale. Vinai Kumar Saxena, Governor, UT Ladakh, on Sunday announced the planting of 90,000 saffron corms, weighing 800kgs, in this region that has unique high-altitude agro-climatic conditions suitable for saffron. This pioneering project has immense potential to strengthen our local economy, creating lucrative and sustainable new livelihood opportunities for our hardworking farmers, youth, and self-help groups, he said. The experiment, spread across 4,000 square metres area in Leh, is a part of Project Him Sarovar, a government initiative to reclaim lost agrarian land in Ladakh. Whats needed to grow saffron Saffron, the dried stigma of the flower, is often used in cooking, cosmetics, and for medicinal purposes. Pampore in Kashmir is well known for cultivating the finest saffron in India. The plant can be cultivated between autumn and winter, with the ideal location having minimum temperatures ranging from 8C to 10C and benefitting from light to moderate snowfall. Only corms weighing more than 10 grams bear saffron flowers, and the number of flowers depends on the size of the corm, directly affecting saffron production. On average, an acre of saffron cultivation in Pampore is known to yield a maximum of up to 2 kg of saffron. A 2024 success story The present cultivation exercise in Leh comes in the wake of a successful experimental attempt at growing saffron in Ladakh two years ago, led by researchers at the CSIR-Indian Institute of Integrative Medicine IIIM, Jammu. Botanically known as Crocus sativus, IIIM scientists had succeeded growing saffron in open fields in Leh. In 2024, the institute inked an MoU with the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council, Leh, towards setting up demonstration farms for the cultivation of medicinal, aromatic and flowering plants in Leh. Since then, the institute has been developing protocols for cultivation, processing, and post-harvest management extendable to these crops to the farmers field and is planning to introduce more crops. A welcome step Speaking to The Indian Express, C K John, a scientist formerly with Pune-based National Chemical Laboratory, said that the Ladakh experiment is a welcome step. If it is successful, this will help the farmers of the region and also contribute in increasing the countrys saffron production, he said. John had led a team that succeeded in growing saffron under greenhouse conditions in the Pune lab and has worked with farmers across Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Sikkim for experimenting and increasing the acreage of saffron cultivation in India.

articleTitle: Harmanpreet Kaur’s real legacy is belief, not just a World Cup
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Harmanpreet Kaur's last act as India captain was leading the side to their second consecutive Asian Games gold medal. (BCCI Photo)
description: Before her, India reached two ODI World Cup finals. Under her, semifinals and finals became regular, and the 2025 title came at home
body_raw: Harmanpreet Kaur ran back to complete the catch that sealed Indias 2025 ODI World Cup triumph. The captain who had carried Indian womens cricket through expectation was there at the finish. But her legacy is bigger than that trophy. Harmanpreet leaves captaincy having changed what India expects from itself. Before her, India had reached the ODI World Cup final in 2005 and 2017 under Mithali Raj. Under Harmanpreet, India became regulars at the business end of tournaments the 2018 T20 World Cup semifinal, the 2020 T20 World Cup final, the 2023 T20 World Cup semifinal and, eventually, the 2025 ODI World Cup title at home. Her biggest contribution was renewed belief. Semifinals and finals were no longer a flash-in-the-pan moment. India started to feel like they belonged there. She took over when Indian womens cricket was growing, but was still searching for consistency and belief. At the 2018 T20 World Cup, her first major tournament as captain, she announced herself with a 103 against New Zealand. It was a statement of the captain she would be aggressive, unafraid of the big stage. That intensity stayed with her. Harmanpreet was emotional, vocal and sometimes combative. Players were coming in with bigger ambitions, and her job was to build a team that believed it could compete at the highest level. Her batting, however, became less consistent as the years went by. Her strike rate was a concern. The Harmanpreet who could win a match from anywhere showed up less often. But she still produced when India needed her. In the 2025 World Cup semifinal against Australia, with India chasing a record total, Harmanpreet made 89 and helped keep the chase alive alongside Jemimah Rodrigues. A year later, in a must-win T20 World Cup game against Australia, she made 56 off 27, hitting three sixes in the final over to take India to a competitive total. Those innings offered reminders of the player India will want to see more often. In her farewell post, Harmanpreet acknowledged the cost of captaincy herself. There were moments when I had to put my individual performance, my own growth, and what I wanted for myself aside, because I believed the team had to come first, she wrote. There were difficult days too defeats, criticism, questions over her decisions. She faced them as openly as she celebrated the wins. I gave this team everything I had, she wrote. I carried the responsibility with pride. She said every difficult decision was made with one intention to make this TEAM better and to give other players the opportunity to grow, believe in themselves and become the best versions of themselves. She leaves behind a team in which Smriti Mandhana has become the batting leader, Deepti Sharma a central figure, and younger players such as N Sree Charani have emerged with confidence. It is a team that has won a World Cup and now knows what it feels like to be there. Harmanpreet wrote that she leaves captaincy with a heart full of emotions, but also with PEACE because she believes the team is in a good place. It is a team with talent, character, belief and a future that she is excited to be part of.  Her post ends Now, Im ready to play for the love of the game again. That is what Indian cricket will hope for. Without the burden of captaincy, Harmanpreet can focus on being the batter who can change a game. At 37, the hope is that giving up the captaincy brings back more of her best batting. India have a home global event, the Womens Champions Trophy, in February next year, before bigger challenges in 2028 and 2029. She says she has done her duty. She leaves the next captain with more than a World Cup trophy a team that believes it can compete on the biggest stages. Captaincy ends. The journey continues, Harmanpreet wrote. For Indian cricket, the hope is that the next chapter brings back the player who made everyone believe.

description: UPSC Mains Answer Writing GS 3: How has optogenetics enabled the establishment of causal links between neural circuits and behaviour? How do higher crude oil prices fuel inflation in India? Test your understanding, analytical ability and answer-writing skills with today's UPSC Mains practice questions.
body_raw: UPSC Essentialsbrings to you its initiative for the practice ofMains answer writing. It covers essential topics from both the static and dynamic portions of the UPSC Civil Services syllabus across various GS papers. The questions are carefully selected on the basis of their relevance to the UPSC examination and current developments, helping aspirants focus on themes that matter most for Mains. This answer-writing practice is designed as a value addition to your UPSC CSE Mains preparation. Attempt todays GS-3 questions and check your progress. As we mark the 3rd anniversary of the UPSC Essentials magazine, we thank our readers for being part of this journey. Your trust, feedback and continued support have shaped the magazine and encouraged us to keep improving with every edition. Click Here to read the UPSC Essentials magazine for September 2026. Share your views and suggestions in the comment box or write to us at manas.srivastavaindianexpress.com. QUESTION 1 The development of optogenetics represents a shift from merely observing brain activity to experimentally establishing causal relationships between neural circuits and behaviour. Discuss. QUESTION 2 How do higher crude oil prices contribute to inflationary pressures in an import-dependent economy like India? Examine the implications for monetary policy and economic growth. QUESTION 1 The development of optogenetics represents a shift from merely observing brain activity to experimentally establishing causal relationships between neural circuits and behaviour. Discuss. Relevance The question is relevant to GS Paper III Science and Technology, particularly biotechnology and advances in neuroscience. It tests the ability to assess how interdisciplinary technologies can transform modern biomedical research. It covers the application of genetic engineering and light-sensitive proteins to study specific neural circuits. NoteThis is not a model UPSC answer. It only provides you with a thought process which you may incorporate into the answers. Introduction -Peter Hegemann, Georg Nagel, and Karl Deisseroth were awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for their discoveries in light-gated ion channels and optogenetics. -The technology has altered neuroscience by allowing researchers to stimulate specific neurons with light and study the subsequent behavioral effects, rather than just monitor neural activity. Body You may incorporate some of the following points in your answer From observation to causal investigation -Earlier neuroscience relied heavily on observational and recording techniques to determine relationships between brain activity and behavior. Optogenetics provided a more precise experimental intervention. -Hegemann and Nagel discovered channelrhodopsin-2 ChR2, a light-gated ion channel, while studying the algae Chlamydomonas. -Genes that encode light-sensitive proteins can be introduced into specific types of cells, causing them to respond to specific wavelengths of light. -When light is given to the targeted cells, proteins can modify ion flow, so activating or inhibiting neuronal activity. - Researchers can thus turn specific neurons or circuits on or off and see if a specific behavior changes. This shifts the focus from which neurons are active when a behavior occurs? to does activating or inhibiting these neurons cause the behaviour? Establishing neural circuitbehaviour relationships -Optogenetics has allowed researchers to study the operation of specific brain circuits involved in pain, social behavior, thirst, food consumption, reward, attention, and memory. -For example, Deisseroths research utilized ChR2 to activate specific neurons and control mouse whisker motions. His research also modified neuronal populations connected with alertness and looked into neurons implicated in terror memories. Reactivating the identified neurons could cause fear-related behavior even when the animal was not exposed to the initial threat. Such tests give more compelling evidence of a causal association between certain brain circuits and behavior than observation alone. Conclusion -Optogenetics has transformed neuroscience from a primarily observational field to one capable of precise experimental intervention. By allowing researchers to disrupt specific neural circuits and watch the effects, it provides a powerful technique of establishing causation and may eventually lead to more tailored treatments for neurological and psychiatric illnesses. Examine the implications for monetary policy and economic growth. Relevance The question is relevant to GS Paper III Indian Economy, particularly inflation, monetary policy and external-sector vulnerabilities. It links crude oil prices with the current account, exchange rate, inflation and economic growth. NoteThis is not a model UPSC answer. It only provides you with a thought process which you may incorporate into the answers. Introduction -Higher crude oil prices pose a substantial inflationary risk to India, which relies heavily on imported energy. -An oil-price shock might thus function as a external tax on the Indian economy, influencing pricing, the external sector, and GDP growth. Body You may incorporate some of the following points in your answer How higher crude oil prices fuel inflation? -Higher global crude prices drive up the cost of fuel, diesel, LPG and other petroleum products. The recent increase in fuel costs has resulted in increased inflation in diesel, petrol, and CNG. -Costlier diesel and petrol raise transport costs, including fares and the cost of moving agricultural and industrial goods. According to the Indian Express, transport inflation increased substantially as gasoline prices surged. -Petroleum products play an essential role in industry, agriculture, logistics, and a variety of other industries. As a result, higher energy costs can affect final product prices. -Higher oil import costs increase demand for foreign currency, putting pressure on the rupee. A weakening rupee increases the cost of imported items, contributing to imported inflation. Implications for monetary policy -The RBI is facing a challenging inflation-growth trade-off. If increasing oil prices cause sustained and widespread inflation, monetary tightening may be required to control demand and keep inflation expectations from becoming entrenched. The RBIs rate-hiking process operates by increasing borrowing costs, which cools consumption and investment. -However, monetary policy is constrained in its ability to immediately address a supply-side oil shock. Raising interest rates cannot boost global oil supplies. Excessive tightening may instead impair domestic demand and investment at a time when growth is already hampered by rising input costs. Thus, the RBI must discern between a short oil shock and long-term inflationary impacts. Implications for economic growth -India imports more than 88 of its petroleum requirements persistent price hikes so significantly increase the oil import bill. Higher oil imports may increase the current account deficit and put pressure on the exchange rate. -Higher fuel and travel expenses diminish a households real disposable income and purchasing power. Higher energy costs can put a strain on government budgets, especially where fuel prices are partially sheltered from worldwide fluctuations. The Finance Ministry has warned that continued crude price hikes pose dangers to both the fiscal deficit and the current account balance. Conclusion -For an import-dependent economy, a crude-oil shock affects inflation, the external sector, and growth all at once. The policy issue is not simply to control inflation with higher interest rates, but also to combine calibrated monetary policy with structural reforms that lessen Indias reliance on imported fossil fuels.
