articleTitle: Too much screen time? Try the 20-20-20 rule to protect your eyes
articleFeaturedImageAlt: eyes
description: Prolonged screen exposure is increasingly becoming a lifestyle challenge for eye health, with digital eye strain, dry eyes and rising concerns around myopia, especially among children
body_raw: Written by By Dr Mahipal Singh Sachdev A 12-year-old boy was recently brought to our hospital by his parents after he began complaining that he could no longer see the writing clearly on his classroom board. At home, he was spending several hours on a tablet for online classes, gaming and videos, often without taking breaks. His parents initially assumed that the frequent eye rubbing and headaches were simply because he was using the screen too much. An eye examination, however, revealed myopia or short-sightedness that required correction. The case is a reminder that what may appear to be ordinary screen fatigue can sometimes signal an underlying vision problem-particularly in children. His prolonged close-up work on devices, combined with very low outdoor activity and exposure to natural light had affected vision. This may cause the eyeball to grow longer than normal, causing light to focus in front of the retina instead of directly on it. As a result, distant objects appear blurry. From the moment we wake up to check our phones to hours spent on laptops at work and evenings scrolling through social media, screens have become an inseparable part of modern life. While digital devices have transformed the way we work, learn and communicate, prolonged and uninterrupted screen use is also putting increasing demands on our eyes. One of the most common consequences of prolonged screen use is digital eye strain. People may experience dryness, burning or irritation in the eyes, blurred vision, headaches, tired eyes and difficulty focusing after spending long periods looking at a screen. A major reason is that we tend to blink less while concentrating on digital content, allowing the surface of the eye to become dry. Simply looking at a screen does not mean that our eyes are being permanently damaged. However, prolonged, uninterrupted near work can cause significant discomfort and fatigue. The solution is not necessarily to abandon technology, but to use it more responsibly. The 20-20-20 rule can make a difference One of the simplest habits is the 20-20-20 rule after every 20 minutes of screen use, look at something around 20 feet away for at least 20 seconds. Regular breaks allow the eyes to relax and can reduce symptoms of digital eye strain. Blinking consciously and frequently is equally important. Screen users should also maintain an appropriate viewing distance, reduce glare and ensure that the screen is positioned slightly below eye level. If dryness persists, an eye specialist can advise whether lubricating eye drops are appropriate. Children need special attention The concern becomes particularly important in children. Increasing time spent on near-vision activities, combined with insufficient outdoor exposure, has been associated with the growing concern around myopia, or short-sightedness. WHO guidance recommends regular breaks during near work and encouraging children to spend adequate time outdoors in daylight. Parents should therefore avoid allowing children to spend long, uninterrupted periods on phones, tablets or gaming devices. Outdoor play should be made a regular part of a childs daily routine rather than treating it as an occasional activity. Dont blame everything on blue light There is also considerable confusion around blue light. While excessive exposure to bright screens in the evening can interfere with the bodys sleep-wake cycle, current evidence does not establish that the blue light emitted by ordinary digital screens causes retinal damage or age-related macular degeneration. Digital eye discomfort is more closely associated with prolonged or improper screen use. Therefore, rather than relying solely on blue-light-blocking glasses, people should focus on the fundamentals - regular breaks, adequate blinking, appropriate screen distance, good lighting and reduced screen use before bedtime. When should you see an eye specialist? Occasional tiredness after a long day on screens is usually not a cause for alarm. However, persistent blurred vision, frequent headaches, recurrent eye pain, redness, double vision, difficulty seeing distant objects or continuing dryness should not simply be attributed to screen use. A comprehensive eye examination can identify an underlying refractive error or other eye condition that may be contributing to the symptoms. Regular eye examinations are particularly important for children, as early detection of vision problems can help prevent them from affecting learning and daily activities. Screens are here to stay, but unhealthy screen habits dont have to be. Small behavioural changes - taking regular breaks, blinking more, spending time outdoors and getting periodic eye examinations - can go a long way towards keeping our eyes comfortable and our vision healthy in an increasingly digital world. The author is Chairman  Managing Director, Centre for Sight Group of Eye Hospitals

articleTitle: When can police refuse permission for protest? Gujarat High Court to decide
articleFeaturedImageAlt: This July, as the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP’s) protest against the NEET-UG 2026 question paper leak and issues connected with the higher education system was taking Delhi by storm, 35-year-old Subodh Kumud called a similar protest in Ahmedabad.
description: Gujarat HC is hearing a petitioner whose application for protest against the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak was rejected by Ahmedabad Police at the height of the Jantar Mantar agitation in Delhi.
body_raw: Police around the country routinely refuse permission to organisations and groups to hold protests and demonstrations. The protesters sometimes go ahead anyway, contending that the refusal of permission is arbitrary. When and under what circumstances can police lawfully refuse to permit a protest? This is the question that a petitioner has asked the Gujarat High Court to clarify in an ongoing matter. The court is scheduled to take up the petition again on Wednesday October 7. What led to the petition? This July, as the Cockroach Janta Partys CJPs protest against the NEET-UG 2026 question paper leak and issues connected with the higher education system was taking Delhi by storm, 35-year-old Subodh Kumud called a similar protest in Ahmedabad. The stated intention was to express solidarity with activist Sonam Wangchuk, who had been sitting on a hunger strike at Jantar Mantar, and other protesters who were demanding the resignation of then Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. According to Kumuds petition, filed before the High Court through Advocate B S Soparkar, Kumud emailed a Form A application under the Regulations and Conduct of Assembly and Procession Ahmedabad Police Commissioner Area Rules, 1975, to police on July 17. He said that he intended to gather together about 50 people from 6 pm to 8.30 pm on July 20 in solidarity with Wangchuk, and as an extension of the Jantar Mantar protests. He said that no loudspeakers would be used. According to the petition, Kumud was called to the Ellisbridge police station on July 19 to give a statement. He was not given a copy of the statement. On July 20, the day of the intended protest, police rejected Kumuds request for permission. Kumud has said that he received the rejection by a message sent on WhatsApp, which stated that the inconvenience that the planned protest would cause to traffic and the public cannot be ignored. But the protest took place anyway, and the protesters were detained at Paldi police station for a few hours. This was also the day of the CJPs march to Parliament in Delhi, during which youth protesters stormed the heart of the capital, provoking a violent crackdown by police. Wangchuk had been removed to hospital from the Jantar Mantar site two days earlier. However, no FIR was registered against Kumud, Advocate Soparkar clarified orally in court on September 30, the last time the matter was heard. What has Kumud argued in the petition? Kumud has argued that under Rule 81 of the Regulations and Conduct of Assembly and Procession Ahmedabad Police Commissioner Area Rules, 1975, permission can be refused only on specific listed grounds, including public order, decency, and morality. He has argued that the police communication recorded no such opinion, and treated the bare possibility of traffic inconvenience as enough to invoke public order, decency, and morality. The petition has contended that this reasoning is speculative, and not a real, immediate or apprehended danger. The petition has also submitted that a Police Inspector has no power to decide a Form A application, that power lies with the Deputy Commissioner of Police, and that the petitioner has received nothing from the office of that senior officer. Going beyond the specific case of July, Kumud has asked the HC to declare that permission cannot be refused solely over possible inconvenience to vehicular traffic without a specific Rule 81 finding. He has also sought directions that persons seeking permission for assembly must not be summoned to police stations, and that applications shall be decided at least 48 hours before the scheduled event. What is the governments argument? Public Prosecutor Hardik Dave has opposed the plea in five submissions, and asked that it be rejected with costs. He has argued that the petition was infructuous, and that Kumud had ignored Rule 42 of the 1975 Rules, which requires an application not less than seven days before the event, with reasons given for any shorter notice. Dave has told the court that Kumud had applied only three days ahead of the planned event, and had given no exceptional reason for it. Dave has said that the petitioner was trying to overreach and misuse the process of the Court. According to Dave, the prayer for blanket directions for future cases cannot be granted when the existing Rules already govern the process. The state has submitted that the Rules grant the police five days for deciding applications, but prescribe no deadline for applications filed within four days of an event. Dave also submitted that the proposed venue of the protest, M J Library, is a point at which five roads converge, and the protest could have disrupted traffic and created a public-order concern.

articleTitle: G7 to release 100 million barrels of oil, diesel: Will this bring prices under control?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A tank farm at the Klesch oil refinery in in Germany's Gelsenkirchen where diesel, gasoline and heating oil are produced. (AP)
description: Diesel is among the most important petroleum fuels globally due to its use in transportation, agriculture, construction, and other industries. This also makes it the most politically sensitive fuel amid the ongoing geopolitical crises.
body_raw: Late last week, the Group of Seven G7 countries agreed to release 100 million barrels of crude oil and petroleum products from emergency reserves, including substantial volumes of diesel, amid apparent pressure from US President Donald Trump. With diesel prices at US pumps reaching record levels, the American president had been pressuring Europe to release their diesel stockpiles, and even warned that the US could ban diesel exports amid global supply tightness and soaring prices of the fuel. Following the G7 announcement, Trump - who wants to lower diesel prices ahead of the midterm polls in the US in November - announced that the US wont ban its diesel exports. Interestingly, Trump said that a diesel export ban was never really on the table, although he himself had publicly stated over the past few days that it was under consideration and that he was inclined towards it. US and European diesel prices had surged in recent weeks amid the highly constrained fuel movement through the Strait of Hormuz as well as attacks on Russias oil and gas infrastructure. Diesel supplies are tight, inventories are low and importers are scrambling to secure the fuel from geographies not impacted by conflict or chokepoint closures. Diesel is among the most important petroleum fuels globally due to its use in transportation, agriculture, construction, and other industries. This also makes it the most politically sensitive fuel amid the ongoing geopolitical crises. While these steps wont do much to deal with the structural problems that the diesel market is grappling with, they are expected to put some downward pressure on international diesel prices, at least in the short-term, according to industry experts. Diesel prices have already drifted downwards following the announcement. The extent and duration of relief will largely depend on whether global diesel flows from West Asia and Russia improve hereon. For India, these developments are broadly positive, as a lower international diesel price would help consumers, particularly bulk and industrial buyers who are supposed to pay prices in line with global rates, even as retail consumers continue to get diesel much below international prices as public sector fuel retailers are absorbing the hit for this segment. Any cool-off in diesel prices will also reduce these companies heavy under-recoveries on retail fuel sales. If bulk diesel rates decline, it would be a positive for the Indian economy as inflationary pressure would be eased to some extent. But on the flip side, higher international supply could squeeze the supernormal margins of standalone Indian refiners - who dont have much exposure to retail fuel sales - as well as large diesel exporters, which are predominantly private sector refiners like Reliance Industries and Nayara Energy. G7 decision focused on shoring up diesel supply The G7 last week agreed to coordinate, through the International Energy Agency IEA, the release of 100 million barrels of crude oil and petroleum products over four months, including front-loaded substantial diesel release in the first 20 days. The countries also agreed to examine additional diesel releases if required by market conditions. The grouping also said that it will avoid energy export restrictions among its members, while also calling on other producers to avoid export bans. Going beyond just the emergency stocks, the group has also agreed to coordinate refinery maintenance schedules so that several refineries dont shut down for maintenance simultaneously, and also called for higher refinery utilisation wherever possible, particularly to boost production of diesel, the workhorse of the global economy. The G7 wants a substantial quantity of diesel to reach the market within days, instead of being spread-out over the four-month period, which shows that the tightness in diesel flows is among the most immediate pressure points in the global energy market. But there is a limit to what reserve releases can accomplish on their own, as strategic stocks are not endless. Releasing strategic stocks of diesel is primarily a bridge to get through a period of unusually tight physical supply, rather than a solution to the underlying disruption in refinery operations, and shipping. Europe has become increasingly dependent on diesel imports from beyond the region over the past few years as it moved away from Russian fuel amid the war in Ukraine. The West Asia war has further exacerbated the supply situation for Europe, which now depends heavily on American diesel. With the decision to release emergency diesel stockpiles, the G7 is putting additional supplies in the market, while also neutralising the threat of a US diesel export ban. Trumps diesel export ban threat Amid surging cracks or margins on diesel globally, US diesel prices jumped sharply in recent weeks, reaching record levels of about 6.5 per gallon and bringing the pain of faraway wars to the American consumer. The timing is significant as the US is set to go into mid-term polls come November, and the Trump administration is evidently feeling the pressure. Diesel is politically sensitive in the US as it is not just a transportation fuel, bit also powers long-haul trucks, agricultural machinery, construction equipment, and other heavy industrial equipment. This means that a jump in diesel prices can quickly feed into consumer-level inflation. According to experts, Trumps threat appeared driven largely by the political problem created by high pump prices in the US, and was enough to set off a good measure of panic and debate in the market. The US is one of the largest diesel exporters globally, and with diesel exports from West Asia and Russia hit due to the conflicts there, American diesel exports have surged further over the past six-seven months. In August, US diesel exports averaged at record levels of about 1.6 million barrels per day bpd, up from around 1 million bpd in February, before the West Asia war began. But the simplistic assumption that restricting diesel exports would shore up supply all over the US and in turn lower prices there doesnt really hold water. That is because there are regional disparities within the US when it comes to fuel production and supply, and the fact that US pump prices are linked to international prices. According to industry participants, analysts, and experts, a ban or major restriction of US diesel exports would have affected countries that are regular importers of American diesel, leading to a further spurt in international prices of the fuel. The adverse impact wouldnt have just been beyond American shores though. Experts point out that any significant export curb was bound to lead to a reduction in refinery production rates in the US, which would hit the USs production of other fuels like petrol as well, ultimately leading to even higher fuel prices there. To that extent, any such move could have easily become counter-productive and self-defeating, and numerous petroleum industry chambers in the US had warned Washington about these risks. The US isnt one unified fuel market. Roughly 54 of the nations refining capacity is concentrated along the Gulf Coast, where refineries produce more fuel than consumers in that region use. The West Coast produces enough diesel to meet its own demand but still imports gasoline petrol and jet fuel. The East Coast, by contrast, lacks sufficient refining capacity and relies in part on diesel supplied from elsewhere - including imports, which account for about 10 of its diesel supply, trade group American Petroleum Institute API had earlier said. According to the API, which believed that a diesel export ban would break havoc at home and abroad, if US diesel exports were blocked, surplus fuel could start filling storage on the Gulf Coast, and the only way to avoid producing even more surplus diesel would be to process less crude oil. But cutting refinery runs would not reduce diesel production alone. It would also mean producing less gasoline, jet fuel and other products at a time when global fuel supplies are already tight, it had said. Exports allow US refineries to balance their systems and maximize production. An export ban would require refineries to throttle utilization to reduce diesel production to equal domestic demand. Falling utilization would result in less gasoline and jet fuel production and higher prices for those products as well. Meanwhile, areas of the US that import fuel primarily the Northeast would face higher prices for all fuels that would now be in even shorter supply globally. This could not come at a worse time for consumers as home heating oil season is about to begin, dozens of American petroleum chambers wrote in a joint representation to Trump a couple of weeks back.

articleTitle: Ban defied: Karnataka IAS officer seeks police explanation over idol immersion
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka Hassan Ganesh idol immersion row
description: Hassan Deputy Commissioner K S Lathakumari issued a notice to SP Shubhanwita for failing to prevent Ganesh idol immersions in Devigere Tank despite prohibitory orders.
body_raw: The deputy commissioner of Hassan district in Karnataka issued a notice to the superintendent of police Sunday, seeking an explanation for why Ganesh and Gowri idols were allowed to be immersed in Devigere Tank, a prominent water body, despite a district administration ban. Acting on requests from the Hassan Municipal Corporation commissioner and the tahsildar, Deputy Commissioner K S Lathakumari, an IAS officer, Saturday banned immersions in the tank, which falls under the Muzrai Department that manages temples in the state, to prevent water contamination from chemical paints, flowers, fruits, and puja materials. The prohibition order was issued under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita BNSS and Section 24 of the Water Prevention and Control of Pollution Act. Despite the ban, major public Ganesh festival organisers held massive processions led by the main town pandal. They immersed the idols in Devigere Tank near the Neerubagilu Anjaneya temple Saturday. DC Lathakumari asked SP Shubhanwita why the matter should not be referred to the competent authority for disciplinary action over alleged dereliction of duty and negligence unbecoming of a government servant. The notice highlighted that although police were empowered to book violators, no FIRs were registered and no action was taken against the organisers. The notice asked SP Shubhanwita to respond in writing immediately, failing which it will be presumed she has no explanation to offer. Copies of the notice were forwarded to the minister-in-charge of the district, the chief secretary, the regional commissioner Mysuru, and the inspector general of police southern range. Addressing the issue on Tuesday, DC Lathakumari said, There is nothing personal in the issue. Since Devigere Tank was polluted, such prohibitory orders were issued after consulting the SP as well. If some untoward incident had taken place, the district administration would have been held responsible. I was also unhappy that plaster of Paris PoP and non-eco-friendly Ganesh idols were also immersed in Devigere. JDS MLA back police officer While SP Shubhanwita was unavailable for comment, a police officer attributed the lapse to the last-minute arrival of the prohibition order. The orders were issued on Saturday morning when the massive procession had already begun. The organisers had obtained permission providing their route map and immersion place. At the last minute, it was impossible to change it, the police officer said. Hassan MLA H P Swaroop Prakash of the Janata Dal Secular backed the SP, pointing out that the pandal committee has immersed its idols in Devigere Tank for six to seven decades. The DC has threatened to initiate legal action against those who have immersed Ganesh idols in Devigere. We will have to stage a protest against the DC. We learned of the order only after the procession had begun. If the district administration is not coordinating with district agencies properly, it will be a problem, Prakash told reporters. The dispute comes weeks before the annual Hasanamba temple fair, scheduled between October 30 and November 10, which is expected to draw at least 20 lakh devotees to the district.

articleTitle: Pune water cuts from October 16? Civic body awaits state directive
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Pune, Pune Municipal Corporation, Pune water cut, Pune water cut October 16, Pune Municipal Corporation water cut, PMC water supply, Pune water shortage, Maharashtra water cut, Pune dams water storage, Khadakwasla dam, Pune drought, El Niño Pune, weekly water cuts Pune, Pune water supply news, Indian Express news
description: The Maharashtra Government has declared drought in various parts of the state, including Pune district, alerting citizens to use available water judiciously.
body_raw: A senior official of the Pune civic body said Tuesday they are likely to start weekly water cuts after the Maharashtra Government ordered local civic bodies and gram panchayats to reduce water supply by at least 10 per cent from October 16. The state government order comes amid concerns over dwindling reserves, drought-like conditions and the risk of prolonged water stress linked to El Nino. The government has declared drought in various parts of the state, including Pune district, alerting citizens to use available water judiciously. The four dams, Khadakwasla, Panshet, Varasgaon and Temghar, which supply water to Pune city, are filled to their capacity, but their water is likely to be supplied to meet the needs of drought-affected talukas of Pune district. To ensure that the available water lasts till the start of next monsoon in July next year, the Pune civic administration has prepared itself for water cuts from October 16. If there is a water cut once a week, then there will be no scarcity during summer, said Nandkishor Jagtap, in-charge of the civic water supply department, Pune Municipal Corporation PMC. However, the water cut will be considered only after written communication from the state government, Jagtap added. He said PMC Naval Kishore Ram, Mayor Manjusha Nagpure, and other senior officers are not in town, so there will be no immediate decision on a water cut. There will be a review of the situation and discussion on the water management plan before its implemented, said Jagtap. Meanwhile, the Pune civic administration has requested the Water Resource Department to reserve 21.34 TMC of water to meet the citys water demand until next monsoon. It also said that 11 villages were merged into the civic body in 2017 and 23 in 2021, increasing the population and the demand it must meet. The Pune civic body introduced water restrictions from June 15 as a precaution against a possible rainfall shortfall linked to El Nino. The cuts were temporarily lifted until July 14 to ensure adequate water availability during the annual Ashadhi Wari Palkhi processions. The decision came after heavy rains in Pune and its catchment areas boosted the water levels in the five reservoirs supplying the city to nearly 55 per cent.

articleTitle: Tamil Nadu bypolls are an early test for Vijay’s young government
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vijay
description: Both constituencies in the state are reserved seats, won in April by AIADMK candidates who subsequently resigned, joined Vijay’s TVK, and are now seeking election again under their new party’s symbol
body_raw: Five months after Tamil Nadu voters elected a new government, some of them returned to polling booths on Tuesday to answer a narrower question Whether the political movement that brought C Joseph Vijay to power has endured through its first months of governing. Voting was brisk by late morning in the two Assembly by-elections in Tamil Nadu. At 11 am, Madurantakam recorded 35.55 per cent turnout and Dharapuram 37.28 per cent. Both constituencies are reserved seats and were won in April by AIADMK candidates who resigned to join Vijays Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam TVK, and are now seeking re-election with this party. In neighbouring Puducherry, meanwhile, Thattanchavady was voting in a separate by-election necessitated by Chief Minister N Rangasamys decision to vacate the constituency after winning two seats in April. Turnout there was 19.2 per cent by 9 am, slightly above the 18.32 per cent recorded during the same first two hours in the April Assembly election. ALSO READ  Vijays river of obscenity barb to slam DMK, Udhayanidhis reels counter The Tamil Nadu contests carry a different political weight. TVK won 108 seats in April but fell short of an outright majority and formed the government with support from smaller parties. Since then, defections from the AIADMK have altered the political landscape. Madurantakams Maragatham Kumaravel and Dharapurams P Sathyabama were among the AIADMK legislators who resigned and moved to TVK. Voters are now being asked, in effect, whether their representatives moved alone. That question explains the unusual intensity of the campaign. Vijay spent four days personally campaigning in the two constituencies - two days of public rallies and two of roadshows - a substantial commitment for two by-elections from a Chief Minister whose own appearances during the April statewide campaign had been comparatively limited. For TVK, winning both seats would validate not only its candidates but the continuing movement of politicians and local organisations towards the ruling party. Losing one would give the AIADMK and DMK an opening to argue that the post-April political realignment has limits. CHECK THE LIVE UPDATES ON THE BYELECTIONS HERE. The first hours of voting offered few reliable clues. Madurantakam began sluggishly, reaching 15.99 per cent turnout around 9.30 am, before the pace accelerated. When reporters asked Kumaravel about the initially lower turnout compared with the general election, she offered a distinctly local explanation Tuesday, she said, was a day when many women visited temples. They would pray for a TVK victory and then come to vote, she said. People have the same enthusiasm as during the general election, Kumaravel said. They are coming to vote with smiling faces. The gender question has occupied TVKs calculations throughout the campaign. Women outnumber men among registered voters in both constituencies Madurantakam has 108,797 women and 104,926 men among its 213,788 voters, while Dharapuram has 116,013 women and 107,285 men among 223,306 electors. Earlier, Kumaravel said voters retained confidence in Vijay and argued that the four-month-old government needed more time to demonstrate change. Polling hitches Polling itself encountered some interruptions. In Madurantakam, electronic voting machines EVMs developed technical problems at two polling stations. At booth 26 in Sithandi, the control unit had to be replaced twice. At booth 55 in L Endathur, the ballot unit was changed after polling agents objected to a visible mark on the name of a candidate. In Dharapuram, voting at a booth in Kottapulipalayam was interrupted by an EVM malfunction, while another machine problem delayed polling at Kundadam-Manurpalayam. There were political disputes as well. At Kolinjivadi, agents objected to a polling official whom they accused of acting in favour of TVK, leading to an interruption in voting. At Veerachimangalam, AIADMK members stopped a vehicle carrying TVK functionaries from outside the constituency, alleging that they had come to distribute tokens to households. DMK and AIADMK members then argued with TVK workers. The allegations come after a campaign in which opposition parties repeatedly accused the ruling party of using money and government machinery to influence voters. TVK has denied accusations of cash distribution. Sathyabama, the TVK candidate in Dharapuram, also entered polling day dealing with a video circulating on social media that purported to show her discussing election expenditure and other matters. After voting at a school in Madukkampalayam, she said the video had been fabricated and that those responsible for releasing it had been identified. The people are clear, she said, insisting that the video would not affect the result. For the AIADMK, the identity of the TVK candidates has been central to the election. Both were elected on AIADMK tickets only months ago. Edappadi K Palaniswami has accused them of betraying the voters who elected them, while AIADMK workers have repeatedly used the word traitor during the campaign. The DMK has made much the same event into a broader democratic argument. Former CM M K Stalin described the by-elections as having been imposed on voters because elected representatives resigned and returned to seek their votes under another party. The DMK has its own stake in Tuesdays numbers. It is contesting without most of the alliance that accompanied it into the April election. Even without winning, an improvement on its previous performance would allow the party to point to the size of its independent vote after its loss of power. The Left parties, despite supporting the TVK government from outside, are contesting against it CPIMs Suganthi is in the race in Madurantakam and CPIs P Lakshmanan in Dharapuram. Naam Tamilar Katchi is also contesting both seats, making the elections five-cornered. In Puducherry, the political geometry is different. Eleven candidates are contesting in Thattanchavady, but the principal contest is among the ruling AINRC-led NDA, Congress and the DMK. Rangasamys AINRC has fielded Ashok Anand, while Congress candidate E Vinayagam has TVKs support. The DMK has fielded K Sethuselvam. For Rangasamy, the election provides an early measure of support for his four-month-old NDA government. For Vijay, the Puducherry contest places TVK in the less exposed position of supporting an ally rather than defending its own government and two defectors. The distinction is important. A general election asks voters who should govern. A by-election held five months later may be asking what they make of what has happened since. In Madurantakam and Dharapuram, even that question has an unusually literal form. Voters elected two candidates in April. The candidates changed parties. On Tuesday, the voters get to decide whether they have changed with them. Polling continues until 6 pm. Counting will take place on October 9.

articleTitle: Haramanpreet Kaur resigns as India captain: Read World Cup-winner’s full statement here
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Harmanpreet Kaur is just the third Indian captain to have won the ODI World Cup across men's and women's cricket. (AP File Photo)
description: An era has come to an end as Harmanpreet Kaur announced her resignation as India's captain in all formats.
body_raw: Harmanpreet Kaur announced that she is stepping down as Indias captain in all formats on Tuesday, thus bringing the curtains down on an illustrious stint in the position. The first and only player to have led India to victory in the Womens World Cup, Harmanpreet is Indias most succesfull captain in womens cricket and has established herself as one of the greatest cricketers of all time in the countrys history. The 37-year-old announced her resignation in a lengthy statement that she posted on her Instagram account. Here is the full text of Harmanpreets statement Today, I step down as captain of the Indian Womens Cricket Team across all formats. This is not an easy decision. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life. I have given everything I had to this team and to Indian womens cricket - my blood, my sweat, my time, and many times, a part of my own game and personal ambitions. There were moments when I had to put my individual performance, my own growth, and what I wanted for myself aside, because I believed the team had to come first. As a captain, I have had to make difficult decisions. Decisions that were not always understood, not always easy, and sometimes came at a personal cost. But every decision I made was with one intention - to make this TEAM better and to give other players the opportunity to grow, believe in themselves and become the best versions of themselves. I have seen it all. I have seen the lowest moments, the heartbreak, the criticism, the doubts and the days when nothing seemed to go our way. And I have also experienced the highest highs - the victories, the celebrations, the pride of representing our country, and the moments that made every sacrifice worth it.  leave the captaincy today with a heart full of emotions , but also with PEACE . Because I genuinely believe My team is in a good place. A team with talent, character, belief and a future that I am incredibly excited to watch and be a part of . I feel I have done my duty. I gave this team everything I had. I carried the responsibility with pride, and I will always be grateful for the privilege of leading Indian womens cricket. Now, it is time for me to turn the page. Captaincy may end today, but my love for Indian cricket never will. Thank you to every teammate, coach, support staff, management , BCCI , family members every single fan who stood by me through the highs and lows. Blood. Sweat. Sarifice. Pride. I gave it all Now, Im ready to play for the love of the game again. Captaincy ends. The journey continues.

articleTitle: Green coffee sold with unproven weight-loss claims, CCPA imposes Rs 1 lakh penalty
articleFeaturedImageAlt: green coffee weight loss benefits CCPA
description: The CCPA found a company guilty of misleading advertising after it failed to provide conclusive scientific evidence supporting its green coffee extract’s weight-loss and health claims.
body_raw: The Central Consumer Protection Authority CCPA recently ordered a health and wellness company to pay Rs 1 lakh penalty for falsely advertising and claiming that its green coffee extract products help with weight loss, blood sugar management, and detoxification. The ruling further directed the company to immediately remove the advertisement from all electronic and print media. Chief Commissioner Nidhi Khare and Commissioner Anupam Mishra were hearing a complaint filed by a consumer group alleging that certain green coffee extract products were being sold by the company as scientifically unproven weight-loss dietary supplements, which were available in many forms, such as capsules and powder. By marketing catchphrases such as helps improve insulin function which assists in blood sugar management and detoxification, the opposite party the company has falsely described the products natural attributes and intentionally exaggerated its material characteristics. This deceptive marketing strategy was engineered to exploit consumer vulnerabilities, lure undiscerning buyers through misleading representations, and distort market choices under the false pretense of wellness, the October 5 order read. In the complaint, the complainant alleged that the markets were flooded with green coffee extract products both online and offline with misleading advertisements promising weight loss. Further, it also claimed that the research carried out so far did not give any evidence-based conclusion on the positive correlation between green coffee extract and weight reduction. The CCPA sought views of the Ministry of AYUSH in the case. According to the ministry, green coffee extract products were not mentioned in any of the authoritative books of Ayurveda, Siddha, and Unani as listed in the Drugs and Cosmetics Act. The CCPA also noted that the advertisements published by the company on e-commerce platforms claimed without any proof that their products help improve insulin function, which assists in blood sugar management and detoxification. After conducting an initial inquiry into the case, the CCPA noted that the company was selling the green coffee product as a scientifically unproven weight loss dietary supplement in the form of capsules, powder, etc. However, no essence or quality of coffee was mentioned, but just weight-loss management under the name of green was advertised. Subsequently, the consumer authority came to the conclusion that a prima facie case was made out for a show cause notice to be sent to the company. In the reply to the show cause notice, the company contended that there were scientific studies conducted by research organisations where it has been proved that green coffee beans helped in weight loss, blood sugar management, and improved metabolic functions and that they had established an internal ethics and compliance committee to ensure that their advertising practices met the highest standards of ethics and compliance. Investigation The CCPA then referred the case for detailed investigation, as per which it was found that the company, which was earlier selling green coffee bean powder with misleading and exaggerated claims, continues to sell the product with identical claims on various e-commerce platforms. The report stated that the claims of the company were misleading, for which the company had not provided any independent scientific studies or clinical trial data conducted as evidence. The report observed that the research papers submitted by the company were not directly comparable to the product, as the conclusions drawn from those studies were inconclusive in nature and did not establish a clear correlation with the specific dosage or intended use of the product. The report concluded that the company was violating the Consumer Protection Act because its advertisements falsely described the product and exaggerated its characteristics to mislead and lure consumers under the labels of green, healthy, and weight loss supplements. On inquiry, the company also informed the authority that a total of 3,318 units of the product had been sold to date, and the total sale value of the product was Rs 6.54 lakh. Valid license Advocate Pratyush Kumar Yadav, appearing for the company, submitted that the company held a valid license issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India FSSAI for the manufacturesale of the product and that the ingredients used in the product were covered under the Nutraceutical Regulations. The counsel contended that the product was a nutraceutical supplement which provided nutritional and health benefits and was available in tablet form. The CCPA was further informed that the recommended dosage of the product was one tablet per day. The counsel urged that the production of the product was stopped in 2025 and the company had already begun communication with e-commerce websites for delisting of the said product. Notify me The CCPA observed that the research papers relied upon by the company cannot be seen as conclusive scientific evidence that supports the alleged weight-management benefits of the product because the studies themselves acknowledge that, owing to the limited number of available studies and the small sample sizes, the efficacy of green coffee extract could not be conclusively established. According to the authority, despite discontinuing the manufacturing of the product in 2025, the company persists in profiteering by maintaining active digital listings on e-commerce platforms and utilised the interactive notify me interfaces to sustain consumer engagement and indulged in unfair trade practice.

articleTitle: He hacked into medical body’s records to help unqualified people practice in Maharashtra
articleFeaturedImageAlt: maharashtra MMC unqualified doctors fraud
description: These applicants, whose details were changed, were students who obtained an MBBS degree abroad without clearing qualifying exams in India – necessary to practise as doctors in India.
body_raw: Maharashtra Cyber has busted an inter-state network in which a medical representative, acting as a link between pharmaceutical companies and doctors, hacked into the Maharashtra Medical Council MMC website and changed records of certain applicants to enable them to practise as doctors. Investigators also suspect that exam websites of other states may have been targeted similarly. The applicants, whose details were changed, were students who obtained MBBS degrees abroad but had not cleared the qualifying exams - the screening test conducted by the National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences NBEMS - required to practise as doctors in India. Investigators suspect the applicants paid lakhs to the accused to manipulate the MMC records into showing that they had passed the examination. How was the MMC fraud detected? The MMC approached the Maharashtra Cyber police station after detecting unauthorised access to their systems and database. During the investigation, Maharashtra Cyber found that certain foreign medical graduates who had not qualified the mandatory FMGE Screening Test also had medical registration certificates, as the MMC site showed they had cleared it. The agency then identified three accused allegedly involved in the fraudulent activity. The two accused have been identified as Varun Akhade 28 and Sanket Unhale 26, who studied in the Philippines after allegedly failing to qualify in the required local examination, Maharashtra Cyber SP Ajay Kumar Bansal said. Further investigation led Maharashtra Cyber to apprehend another person, identified as Rahul Patil, suspected to be a key operative of the inter-state gang involved in the generation and procurement of the forged documents. He charged anywhere between Rs 15-25 lakhs per applicant. An official said, We are checking if the records of any more accused have been manipulated in the MMC database. We are also checking if the accused had manipulated the database of other state medical council exams, as we have found some data of persons from other states who had paid him money. More arrests are likely in the case.

articleTitle: 70s AI photo trend: 6 Gemini prompts to give your photos a retro Indian look
articleFeaturedImageAlt: 70s retro AI Gemini trend prompts
description: To create a photo, users can upload a photograph to Gemini and describe the period, setting, mood, lighting, and photographic style they want.
body_raw: The AI photo trend is once again taking social media users back several decades. Instead of adding a vintage filter to their pictures, users are turning ordinary photographs into detailed 1970s-style scenes using AI image-generation tools such as Google Gemini. From old department stores and optical shops to rooftop photography, the trend focuses on recreating specific moments that look as though they were captured decades ago. These photos feature muted colours, film grain, imperfect exposure, faded textures, period clothing, and everyday Indian surroundings. To create one, users can upload a photograph to Gemini and describe the period, setting, mood, lighting, and photographic style they want. More detailed prompts can help create a more specific and believable result. Here are some prompts to try 1. 1973 department-store escalator Turn your photograph into a scene from the opening day of a newly installed escalator in an Indian department store. Prompt Transform my uploaded image into an entirely original Indian department-store photograph captured in 1973, on a day when a newly installed escalator has become a point of public curiosity. Preserve the persons facial identity and natural features. Place them among mirrored columns, patterned flooring, period interiors and curious shoppers. Use authentic 1970s Indian clothing, muted analogue colours, subtle film grain, slight exposure imperfections and the look of a photograph taken on a vintage film camera. 2. 1974 optical shop Give your photograph the feel of an old optical-shop picture without relying on stereotypical oversized 70s glasses. Prompt Create an entirely original Indian optical-shop photograph from 1974 using my uploaded image as the exact human reference. Preserve the persons facial identity and features. Place them inside a modest Indian optical shop surrounded by loose trial lenses, glass reflections, wooden displays and a rotating lens tray. Use realistic 1970s interiors, natural indoor lighting, faded colours, analogue film grain and subtle imperfections associated with an old printed photograph. 3. 1972 civic-wall photograph This prompt recreates the visual character of an Indian public wall from the early 1970s. Prompt Transform my uploaded image into an entirely original Indian civic-wall photograph captured in 1972. Preserve the persons identity and facial features. Place them beside a limewashed public wall featuring hand-painted lettering, uneven brush strokes, chipped paint and a drying paint edge. Recreate the atmosphere of an ordinary Indian street from the early 1970s, with period-appropriate clothing and surroundings. Make it look like an authentic analogue photograph with muted colours, natural shadows and subtle film grain. 4. 1977 rooftop photography class For something more cinematic, imagine the subject attending a photography lesson on an Indian rooftop. Prompt Create an entirely original Indian rooftop photography-learning photograph from 1977 using my uploaded image as the exact human reference. Preserve the persons facial identity and natural appearance. Place them in a small rooftop photography class with a vintage camera, grey card and basic photographic equipment. Include strong afternoon shadows, weathered terraces and authentic 1970s Indian surroundings. Give the photograph a documentary feel with muted colours, realistic analogue film grain and slight imperfections. 5. 1970s railway platform For a quintessentially Indian retro setting, transform the photograph into a railway-platform scene. Prompt Transform my uploaded image into an entirely original Indian railway-platform photograph from 1975. Preserve the persons exact facial identity and natural features. Place them on a busy Indian railway platform with period luggage, old railway signage, metal benches and passengers dressed in authentic 1970s clothing. Use warm natural light, faded colours, realistic analogue film grain, slight motion blur and the imperfect texture of a photograph printed from 35mm film. 6. 1970s neighbourhood photo Users can also recreate the feeling of an ordinary family photograph taken in an Indian neighbourhood. Prompt Create an entirely original Indian neighbourhood photograph from 1976 using my uploaded image as the exact human reference. Preserve the persons identity, facial features and natural expression. Place them outside a modest Indian home with scooters, balconies, potted plants, textured walls and everyday neighbourhood activity typical of the 1970s. Make the photograph feel candid and unstaged, as though taken by a family member on a 35mm film camera. Use slightly faded colours, subtle grain, natural lighting and authentic period details. Rather than simply asking Gemini to make this photo vintage, users can describe a particular year, location, objects, clothing, lighting and photographic style. They can then refine the generated image by asking the AI to change specific elements while retaining the subjects appearance.

articleTitle: When Jeffrey Archer called Bollywood ‘bunch of thieves’ for stealing his bestseller plots
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jeffrey Archer once accused Ladies Vs Ricky Bahl for stealing the plot of his book.
description: British author Jeffrey Archer, who died at 86 on Monday, once accused Bollywood films Ladies vs Ricky Bahl and Khudgarz of stealing the plots of his bestsellers.
body_raw: British author Jeffrey Archer, who wrote several bestselling novels, died at 86 on Monday. He died suddenly and peacefully at his home between writing sessions, as per his publisher HarperCollins. Hes already completed Adam and Eve, touted as his final novel after a publishing career of 50 years. A fan of Indian author RK Narayan, he had a rather love-hate relationship with India, particularly the Hindi film industry. When Jeffrey Archer called Bollywood a bunch of thieves Just look at your Bollywood These bunch of thieves have stolen several of my books without so much as a by your leave. Ladies Vs Ricky Bahl and Khudgarz, and several others, alleged Archer in an interview back in 2015. He was in the process of pitching his 2011 bestseller Only Time Will Tell to Hollywood and Bollywood production houses for a film adaptation. While he claimed several Hollywood companies wanted the rights of the book, he had also been looking for an Indian partner. And that does not mean some second-rate Bollywood idiot who goes around saying hes a Bollywood star producer and then he is not Its true What can I say? Such has been my Indian experience many times, he told DNA, laughing. Archer claimed that Manish Sharmas 2011 crime comedy Ladies vs Ricky Bahl was based on his 1976 bestseller Not A Penny More, Not A Penny Less, which also revolved around three people whove been conned trying to frame and get back at the conman. While Ranveer Singh played the titular character of the conman, the three peoples genders were switched to women hed wooed in order to scam them. Anushka Sharma, Dipannita Sharma, and Parineeti Chopra played the three women in Ladies vs Ricky Bahl, with the film being Parineetis acting debut. It was produced by Yash Chopras production house Yash Raj Films, and marked the reunion of Ranveer and Anushka after his 2010 acting debut, Manish Sharmas hit romantic comedy Band Baaja Baaraat. Archer also claimed that Rakesh Roshans 1987 directorial debut Khudgarz was based on his 1979 bestseller Kane and Abel. Like the book, it revolved around two feuding brothers, played by Shatrughan Sinha and Jeetendra. Co-written by Mohan Kaul and Ravi Kapoor, it was also produced by Roshan. The cast of the action film also includes Amrita Singh, Govinda, and Neelam among others. Jeffrey Archer on his official collaborations with Bollywood Despite his unpleasant encounters with Bollywood, Archer remained endlessly fascinated with India. He began selling the adaptation rights of his book officially. Producer Sheetal Talwar bought the rights to his 1984 bestseller First Among Equals and short story A La Carte from the 1988 collection A Twist in the Tale for a reported sum of Rs 1.5 crore, as per a Mumbai Mirror report. While he planned to adapt the former into a high-budget television series, that never saw light of the day. Kussh Sinha, son of Shatrughan Sinha and brother of actor Sonakshi Sinha, was supposed to make his directorial debut with that show. He ended up directing his first feature only as recently as last year with horror film Nikita Roy, starring Sonakshi in the titular role. Filmmaker Hansal Mehta was also in talks with Archer to buy the adaptation rights of Kane and Abel. However, while that never materialized either, Mehta had already directed a TV show loosely based on the book. Lakshya 1999 starred Kay Kay Menon and Sachin Khedekar among others. He wanted to remake the show into a film, starring longtime collaborator Rajkummar Rao, back in 2014. Also Read Fahadh Faasil says wont get half of Rs 300 cr as Bethlehem Kudumba Unit earns Rs 326 cr Back in 2015, Archer was even planning a book set in India, and particularly Bollywood. Consisting of eight chapters, the novel was supposed to have a Bollywood heroine at the centre. However, that book never saw light of the day either. However, Archer enjoyed massive popularity in the country, partly thanks to widespread piracy, which gave him the moniker, The Lord of the Paperbacks.

articleTitle: Naveen Patnaik’s BJD joins Opposition’s Election Commission protest
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Biju Janata Dal chief Naveen Patnaik: Ex Odisha CM has joined INDIA bloc protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
description: Protests against CEC Kumar and the Election Commission have gathered pace since the Express' report last month.
body_raw: Naveen Patnaiks Biju Janata Dal has joined opposition parties in demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar amid outrage over allegations of irregularities in the conduct of the Special Intensive Revision of stateUT voter rolls. Patnaik has sent Manas Mangraj and Sulata Deo to join protests that have erupted in central Delhi Tuesday, led by Congress MPs Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, who were briefly detained by police before being released. There is little love lost between the BJD and the Bharatiya Janata Party - in power at the centre and in Odisha - today, after the BJP thumped the BJP in the 2024 Assembly election, a loss the state party is now questioning. In the past, though, the BJD was a member of the BJP-led national alliance, i.e., from 1998-2009. Protests against CEC Kumar and the Election Commission have gathered pace since the Express report last month. An Express investigation found that Election Commissioners Vivek Joshi and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu had objected - formally and on record - 14 times in 10 months to the manner in which decisions were taken regarding the SIR. Among the 14 points raised were the allegedly illegal modification of Form 6 - to include questions about the voters parents or grandparents - and a push to centralise control of the ECINET software that manages the lists. BJD demands Gyanesh Kumars resignation On Monday BJD spokesperson Lenin Mohanty told reporters in Bhubaneswar that Gyanesh Kumar has no option but to resign and take moral responsibility. Mohanty insisted Kumar had to quit because he had lied about changes to Form 6 - that the alterations during the SIR had been approved by the Supreme Court. The court this week said it had not approved any modifications to Form 6 and sought a response from the EC and the government. Now, Kumar has no option. as Gyanesh Kumar had lied that Form 6 was approved by the Supreme Court, he has no moral right to continue but to step down, the BJD said in a statement. BJD leader Lekhashree Samantsinghar underlined that demand, declaring voters across the country, including those in Odisha, had lost trust in the EC.They EC must have done similar manipulation during the 2024 elections in Odisha by tampering with EVMs to make a particular party win the election, Samantsinghar alleged. INDIA bloc protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar Security was stepped up across the New Delhi district, and opposition MPs were stopped on the way, after which they sat on a dharna. After a face-off with the cops, they were removed from the spot and carried away in a bus. Rahul Gandhi - also the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha - was joined by Trinamool Congress leader Derek Obrien and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. Gandhi was seen adhering to Gen-Z lingo at the protest as he carried a poster that read Gyanesh, its done bro He posted the slogan on X, too, adding Its time to resign

articleTitle: Nearly 12,000 books banned in US schools; Charlotte Bronte, Margaret Atwood among those pulled
articleFeaturedImageAlt: usa bans books across public schools
description: US public schools recorded 11,982 book bans in the 2025-26 school year, the highest annual total tracked by PEN America, with Texas reporting the most removals.
body_raw: US public schools recorded almost 12,000 book bans in the 2025-2026 school year, the highest number for a single year. The count comes from a new report, Banned in the USA, released Monday during Banned Books Week, when schools and libraries hold events to draw attention to censorship. In all, 11,982 bans were logged. They affected 7,370 individual works and more than 4,000 authors, illustrators and translators, a record number of unique titles. About 34,000 bans have been counted since 2021, which suggests removals are no longer isolated cases but a steady pattern across the country. The figures come from PEN America, a free expression group that has tracked school book removals for five years. Here are some of the titles named in the findings Book Title Author Sold most banned title, 25 removals Patricia McCormick The Handmaids Tale Margaret Atwood Speak Laurie Halse Anderson Crank Ellen Hopkins The Shining Stephen King The Green Mile Stephen King Jane Eyre Charlotte Bronte Tokyo Ghoul manga series Sui Ishida Texas recorded the most bans this year, more than 8,100. The surge is linked to a state law, SB13, which bars broad categories of books from schools. Florida had held the top spot for the previous three years. Both states have passed restrictive laws, and politicians and conservative activists there have pushed for removals. A total of 114 school districts banned books, the highest number ever in a single year. Also Read NCERTs new Art textbook covers up Mohenjodaros Dancing Girl Technology appears to be playing a growing part too, as per the report. School district administrators are relying more on artificial intelligence tools to decide which books to pull. Because such tools can scan and flag many titles at once, they may help explain how the number of removals climbed so quickly alongside the new state laws. Stephen King was the most banned author for the second year in a row, with his books pulled 312 times. The most banned single title was Sold, a young adult novel about a girl from Nepal who is sold into sexual servitude. Other frequent targets include The Handmaids Tale, Speak, a prize-winning novel about a teenager who falls silent after being raped, and Crank, a novel about drug addiction. Also Read Ram Rajya, NEP, Sengol What students will learn in NCERT in Governance and Public Policy chapter The reasons behind the bans have stayed fairly consistent. Themes of race, racism, sexuality and gender identity are still the most common grounds for challenges. More than 4,500 of the banned works were on the list for the first time, from the 19th-century classic Jane Eyre to the manga series Tokyo Ghoul. The bans also reached books that young people pick up by choice. Fiction made up more than 90 of banned young adult titles, and popular manga was among them. Supporters of school libraries argue that they make ideas available to everyone, whatever their personal or political views. The report says bans limit the freedom to read and narrow the range of voices and perspectives students can see. With inputs from AP

articleTitle: Karnataka job scam: Flat purchased near Bengaluru airport by IAS officer’s kin under lens
articleFeaturedImageAlt: arrested IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar
description: Arrested IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar, the then KPSC's controller of examinations, allegedly received around Rs 1.30 crore of the Rs 1.52 crore from candidates as bribes for leaking the entrance examination for veterinary doctors.
body_raw: An apartment purchased in the name of a family member of arrested IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar in Karnataka has come under scrutiny of the Enforcement Directorate in connection with a job recruitment fraud at the Karnataka Public Service Commission KPSC, sources in Karnataka Police said. During interrogation, Basavaraj Kannale, a middleman involved in the fraud, revealed that Gangwar, the then KPSCs controller of examinations, allegedly received around Rs 1.30 crore of the Rs 1.52 crore from candidates as bribes for leaking the entrance examination of veterinary doctors conducted on January 8 and 9. Around 20 candidates allegedly paid Rs 20 lakh to Rs 40 lakh through Kannale, a close associate of Gangwar. Gangwar, 41, served as KPSCs controller of examinations from January 2024 to March 2026. The Criminal Investigation Department CID and the ED arrested Gangwar on August 29 and September 18, respectively. It was found that Gangwar used some of the proceeds of the crime to purchase an apartment in the name of the brother of the IAS officer at the Godrej Royal Woods complex near the Bengaluru International Airport at Devanahalli. The IAS officers brother and family are unaware of the flat purchased in their name in Bengaluru, and they never visited or used the property. It was used by the officer for hosting parties and other activities since it provided privacy, said police sources familiar with the probe. Gangwar has also stated before the ED that a portion of the amount he received from Kannale was used to purchase a flat in the name of his brother, apart from using the funds for buying gold jewellery for his fiance. While the investigations have tracked Rs 52 lakh in bribe amounts being funneled back to the IAS officer - through bank accounts of associates of the middleman - for the purchase of expensive pieces of gold and diamond jewellery at the Bhima Jewellery showroom in Bengaluru for the IAS officers girlfriend, the remaining amount of bribes is untraced. The ED has earlier told the court that the apartment at Devanahalli was bought with proceeds of the crimes at the KPSC. The proceeds of the recruitment frauds at the KPSC were routed through the middleman Kannale and his associates for the purchase of immovable property in the name of his brother, purchase of gold jewellery in the name of his fiance, and payment of personal expenses, a special court for PMLA cases noted last week after an ED submission. The ED has reported that an unexplained amount of Rs 26 lakh was deposited in cash between January 2025 and August 2025 in the bank accounts of a brother and sister-in-law of the IAS officer. The ED is also probing immovable assets acquired by the IAS officer - such as a semi-constructed house in Bareilly in 2025 for Rs 25 lakh, and a real estate construction business launched by his older brothers in 2025 in Uttar Pradesh for possible links to illegal gratifications at the KPSC. Gold jewellery purchases Unlike the property purchases linked to the IAS officer, the CID and ED probes have mapped the flow of Rs 52 lakh of funds from the KPSC veterinary officers recruitment fraud to Kannale and associates, and to Gangwar for jewellery purchases by his fiance. According to the investigations, gold jewellery worth Rs 29.94 lakh was purchased for Gangwars girlfriendin March 2026 at Bhima Jewellery in Bengaluru, and gold jewellery worth Rs 23 lakh was purchased again in July 2026. In both cases, the funds were provided by Kannale. The CID probe has revealed that Rs 15 lakh for the jewellery purchase in March 2026 came from a Kotak Mahindra Bank account of Balu Reddy, an associate of Kannale, and another Rs 15 lakh from the Om Lakshmi Souharda Sahakari Bank in Bidar, operated by Kannales friend Onkar Kamshetti, where aspirants transferred bribes from bank accounts. Gangwar has reportedly told investigators that he asked Kannale to buy the jewellery in July for his fiance through money transfers of Rs 8 lakh from Kannales accountant Umesh and Rs 15 lakh by Onkar Kamshetti, the vice president of the Om Lakshmi Souharda Sahakari Bank in Bidar. Gangwar has made contradictory claims that his fiance issued cheques for repayment of the cost of the gold purchases and that the jewellery purchases were a birthday gift to her. The ED is continuing investigations against the IAS officer to look at whether similar scams were also perpetrated in 12 other KPSC examinations carried out during Gangwars tenure from January 2024 to March 2026. The Karnataka High Court has ordered a SIT probe into two cases of KPSC recruitment frauds, which has been challenged by the Karnataka government in the Supreme Court on the grounds that there were no adverse remarks by the court on the CID probe into the alleged KPSC job frauds. Former KPSC chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar is also under investigation in the veterinary officers recruitment fraud as well as the recruitment of his daughter through illegal means to the post of an industrial extension officer.

articleTitle: She had a visa and made 47 trips last year, but was turned away this time
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Delhi High Court
description: The court dismissed a plea filed by a woman who had sought a written explanation as to why she was denied entry into India despite holding a valid business visa.
body_raw: The Delhi High Court recently held that possession of a visa does not create an absolute and unconditional right to enter India for a foreign national. Justice Amit Mahajan dismissed a plea filed by a woman who had sought a written explanation as to why she was denied entry into India despite holding a valid business visa. The statutory framework, therefore, does not treat the possession of a visa as creating an absolute and unconditional right of admission into India, the court observed. Why did court dismiss plea? The petitioner arrived at Delhis Indira Gandhi International Airport on March 25, 2026, along with her husband on the same flight. While her husband, who was travelling on a visa of the same category, was allowed to enter India, she was stopped at immigration and sent back to Turkmenistan the same day. She said that the authorities had neither furnished reasons for refusing her entry nor explained why she was treated differently from her husband, alleging violation of Articles 14 and 21 of the Constitution. The authorities concerned, however, told the High Court that possession of a valid visa did not create an absolute right to enter India. It said adverse inputs had been received against the woman and the immigration authority had decided to deny her entry in the interest of national security and public order. The court was informed that she had made 47 visits to India during 2025, mostly for periods of one to three days, and had travelled on both business and medical visas. It was stated that the petitioner questioned by the immigration authorities regarding the purpose of her visit, her activities and her business associations, and that the responses furnished by her were not found satisfactory and, thus the decision to deny her entry was taken. The court also examined material placed by the respondents in a sealed cover. It noted discrepancies in the petitioners parentage and spouse details and said she had no business card or invitation letter for the visit and could not provide details of the business in her home country. The court further noted that although she had obtained a business visa, she had described herself as a housewife, while the mobile number provided by her was also found to be invalid. The court observed that the entry of a foreign national in India is not a matter of enforceable right against the State but a matter of sovereign discretion. It further stated that the court, in exercise of judicial review, cannot substitute its own assessment for that of the competent authority in a matter concerning admission of a foreign national, particularly where the decision is stated to have been taken by considering confidential inputs relating to national security and public order. There is no inherent or legally enforceable right of a foreign national to seek entry into India. It is trite that the extraordinary jurisdiction of this Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India can be invoked only where there is a violation of a right. In the very dearth of any right, no writ can be issued, the court said. It therefore dismissed the womans plea.

articleTitle: ‘Royal Bengal Tiger’: How the animal got its title
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Royal bengal tiger
description: The “royal” in Royal Bengal tiger is rooted in colonial history, while the tiger's striking appearance and adaptability across India's diverse landscapes added to its mystique.
body_raw: The name Bengal tiger has a strong geographical connection. During British rule, Calcutta now Kolkata was the capital and administrative headquarters of British India, and British naturalists, hunters and officials encountered and documented tigers extensively in Bengal and surrounding forests. According to wildlife photographer Indrajit Ghorpade, this is one of the reasons the tiger came to be associated with Bengal. The British naturalists, hunters and officials predominantly encountered and documented these big cats in Bengal and nearby forests, leading them to label the animal the Bengal tiger, Ghorpade explains. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. But where did the word royal come from? Ghorpade says the honorific was added during the British colonial period, when the tigers imposing appearance and cultural symbolism fascinated those who encountered it. The exotic, fierce and striking features, stripes and colour fascinated the British, who referred to them as royal, and from Bengal as this was the capital in Calcutta, he says. Tiger skins and heads were also prized as trophies and were sent as prestigious gifts to British royal families and local dignitaries. This further strengthened the association between the tiger and royalty. Are all Royal Bengal tigers the same? Tigers adapted to various habitats, from dense jungles and mangroves to the drier regions, evolving to adapt in size and behaviour, Ghorpade says. This means a tiger living in the Sundarbans does not necessarily look or behave exactly like one in Ranthambore. Differences can occur in size, coat, colouration, diet and behaviour. Hence Ranthambore tigers and Sundarbans tigers vary and differ in size, coat, colouration and even diet, he says. How does habitat shape a tiger? Habitats determine and play a role in their size and colour. Diets vary from region to region, affecting adaptation and behaviour, Ghorpade explains. The Sundarbans, for instance, are dominated by mangrove forests and tidal waterways, creating a very different environment from the dry deciduous forests of Ranthambore. These differences dont mean that each population is a completely separate kind of tiger. Rather, they demonstrate how a highly adaptable predator can respond to very different landscapes. Tigers beyond the Indian subcontinent Apart from tigers of the subcontinent, there are subspecies across the Far East, some extinct, many vulnerable. Evolution has shaped size, colour etc., Ghorpade says. Across their range, differences in climate, habitat and prey availability have influenced how tiger populations look and behave. So, while Royal Bengal tiger is the name commonly used for Indias tigers, the reality is more nuanced. Tigers across the country share the same broad identity, but their appearance, behaviour and adaptations can vary with the landscapes they inhabit. articleTitle: Railways to pay Rs 47,000 fine 8 years after family ‘robbed’ in Mewar Express AC coach
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Uttarakhand Consumer Commission Indian Railways Robbery AC Coach Passenger Railway Police Consumer News
description: The Uttarakhand State Consumer Commission was hearing the Railways’ appeal against the district commission awarding compensation for the theft of belongings of a family during the Mewar Express journey.
body_raw: The Uttarakhand State Consumer Commission held Indian Railways liable for negligence after a family travelling in a reserved AC coach of the Mewar Express reported that thieves forcibly took away their valuables near Mathura in the early hours of July 2, 2018. The commission also upheld Rs 47,222 payout ordered by the District Consumer Commission, Dehradun. The Uttarakhand State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission president, Kumkum Rani, and member B S Manral heard an appeal filed by the Union of India and railway authorities against the May 11, 2022 order of the district commission, which had directed the Railways to pay Rs 37,222 towards the loss suffered by the complainants, Rs 25,000 towards mental agony and Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses. The negligence on the part of the railway administration and its servants is clearly proved, the state commission said on October 5, referring to the circumstances of the incident. It found that the reserved coach doors had been left open during the night and that there was no coach attendant, police personnel or TTE inside the coach when the theft occurred. The dispute arose from the familys return journey from Udaipur to New Delhi on July 1, 2018. They were travelling in the reserved AC coach of the Mewar Express and reached Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station on July 2. During the journey, when the train reached Mathura at around 4 am, the complainants said unauthorised persons entered the coach and forcibly took away the belongings of two passengers. Theft reported during early-morning journey According to the complaint, one of the persons forcibly took away a large bag belonging to Veena Dobhal, who was sleeping at her berth. The bag had been kept under her head, below the pillow. She woke up when the bag was taken and raised an alarm. Other members of the family and passengers also woke up and tried to catch the person, but he jumped from the moving train with the bag. The passengers then searched for the coach attendant, RPF personnel, and the TTE but did not find any of them available in the coach. The TTE was subsequently contacted and informed about the theft. An FIR form was filled in and later handed over to the Government Railway Police at Hazrat Nizamuddin. A Zero FIR was lodged at the railway police station at 750 am on July 2, 2018. The complainants told the commission that they had not been able to ascertain the outcome of the investigation despite their efforts. Railways blamed passengers The Railways denied negligence and argued that passengers were responsible for safeguarding luggage carried by them. It relied on the provisions of the Railways Act concerning liability for loss or damage to luggage and pointed out that the family had neither booked the luggage with the Railways nor declared that they were carrying valuables. The Railways also argued that passengers were advised inside the coach to secure their luggage with a chain and that the complainants had not followed the instruction. It maintained that reserved coaches were meant only for authorised passengers and that coach attendants and TTEs were responsible for keeping the doors closed during the night. The state commission rejected this defence in the circumstances of the case. It noted that the complainants had specifically alleged that the coach doors and the end doors of the vestibule had not been kept locked. The commission also noted that the Railways had not specifically denied this allegation and had not produced evidence from the coach attendant or TTE to establish that the doors had been kept closed. If the doors of the coach were locked  closed, there was no occasion for the unauthorised persons  miscreants to have enter into the coach and commit theft  robbery, the commission observed. It further rejected the argument that the availability of remedies under railway laws barred the consumer complaint, noting that the Consumer Protection Act provides remedies in addition to those available under other laws. The commission awarded Rs 47,222 in total, comprising Rs 37,222 compensation and Rs 10,000 litigation expenses, with 7 per cent annual interest on Rs 37,222 from July 31, 2020, until payment. Takeaway Passengers may seek compensation for valuables stolen from a reserved railway coach when they can establish that the loss resulted from negligence or misconduct by railway staff, such as failure to secure the coach or prevent unauthorised entry. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states and union territories Uttarakhand 1800-180-4188 or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance.
