articleTitle: ‘Virat Kohli can be a Bollywood actor,’ says Rahul Dravid: ‘He’s a superb mimic, done many ads’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Virat Kohli bollywood career
description: Rahul Dravid mentioned Virat Kohli's name when he was asked about cricketers who could have a career as a Bollywood actor.
body_raw: Virat Kohli is one of the most popular cricketers in the world, and as is the case with such famous sportspeople, he often faces the camera for brand endorsements. In a recent interview, former cricketer Rahul Dravid hinted that Virat could possibly have a career in front of the camera, possibly in a Bollywood film. In a chat with BBC Asian Network, Rahul was asked, Which of your teammates would make the best Bollywood actor? Abhishek Bachchan, who was also present during this interview, reminded Rahul that many cricketers had indeed been in the movies and Rahul shared, Sunil Gavaskar tried to act. Syed Kirmani tried to act, without much success. Ajay Jadeja did one film. Good thing they stuck to the cricket, he said with a laugh. When asked if Rahul would ever try his luck in the movies, he replied with a laugh, No. I know what my strengths are. Im not making a fool of myself. After a brief thought, he mentioned Virat Kohlis name and said, I think Virat has got a tremendous ability to mimic. He mimics people really well. He doesnt do it very often nowadays, but I remember him as a young kid coming into the team when we were all seniors and. Like, his ability to mimic people was absolutely superb. And he has done so many ad films. He is pretty much a pro at it. ALSO READ  Salman Khan hosts BJP youth leader at Mumbai home Touched by your warmth, simplicity At this point, the interviewer jumped in and mentioned Virats wife, Anushka Sharma, who is a Bollywood actor. She said, I am sure Anushka can give him some tips. Virat and Anushka first met each other on the set of an ad film. Since then, he has appeared in hundreds of ads. In the same chat, Dravid was also asked about his favourite Bollywood cricket film. He mentioned Ranveer Singhs 83 and Abhishek Bachchans Ghoomer, and also spoke about Aamir Khans Lagaan. Lagaan, I thought, was really good. It was a fantastic film. Previously, casting director Mukesh Chhabra, in a chat with Ranveer Allahbadia, spoke about Virats potential Bollywood career and said, He is already a great actor. He is from Delhi, he is a Punjabi. He has seen that life. He has handled success so beautifully. He has maintained himself on every level - competition, looks, fitness, mentally. He added that Virat must not join films even after he retires from his cricket career. He is also so funny. He will dance, mimic, his comic timing is great. He is doing very well in making the country proud, he should stay where he is and not join films. He should not join films even after retiring from his cricket career. He is genuinely a smart guy, not a cunning one, he said. Virat and Anushka got married in 2018 in a close-knit ceremony in Italy. The couple is now parents to their daughter, Vamika, and son, Akaay. They have been residing in the UK for a few years now.

articleTitle: What changes at IIT Bombay after student’s suicide: ‘Option to replace fans, more play areas’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: IIT Bombay student Sahil Wakode's death sparked widespread protests at the institute. (File Photo)
description: IIT Bombay suicide: Appointment of student wellness secretaries in hostels, common play areas, and replacing hostel fans are some of the proposed changes
body_raw: As students at the Indian Institute of Technology IIT Bombay and Sahil Wakodes parents continue protesting days after the students suicide on the campus, the institute has discussed proposed changes to the student wellness support system with the student representatives. With the appointment of student wellness secretaries in hostels, common play areas, new measures against exam malpractices, and replacing hostel fans, IIT Bombay is set to overhaul its student wellness support system. IIT Bombay has also announced the appointment of an associate dean for student wellness and is expected to begin a phased rollout of the proposed changes this week. The institutes Dean of Students Affairs communicated the new measures to IIT Bombay students on behalf of the director, Professor Shireesh Kedare. The new measures come on the heels of serious concerns raised by the IIT Bombay students following the suicide of Sahil Wakode. Sahil Wakode died by suicide on September 18, hours after he was allegedly found using a mobile phone during a mid-semester examination, triggering massive protests on the campus. What changes at IIT Bombay? According to the email, the institute held discussions with students and their representatives on academic, career, and wellbeing concerns to decide on a plan to ensure student wellness on the campus. Under the proposed changes, the institute is working on a system to appoint student-wellness secretaries at the hostel level and identify committees where student participation can be increased. Meetings with heads of departments with greater student participation at the department level and strengthening support available to students have been proposed. IIT Bombay has also proposed play areas in the hostels. General secretaries, sports councillors and wardens will be consulted to identify suitable spaces and understand residents concerns regarding this. The institute is also considering replacing hostel fans. While options have been identified, a final decision will be taken after students feedback. Changes to the flexy mess system have also been proposed during the meeting. On academic matters, IIT Bombay has prepared first drafts of proposed deterrent measures against the use of unfair means during examinations, which will be discussed in the emergency senate meeting. Students have been urged to participate in the surveys and consultations to stay up to date on how the institute is working on implementing the proposed changes.

articleTitle: How Kane and Abel made Jeffrey Archer a household name in India
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A portrait photograph of Jeffrey
description: Britain’s bestselling storyteller and an Indian bookshelf staple, Jeffrey Archer died suddenly and peacefully at 86, hours before his final novel, Adam and Eve, was released
body_raw: Jeffrey Archer, one of Britains most commercially successful novelists, whose page-turners remain fixtures on Indian bookshelves, died on Monday at his home in England, a day before his final novel was published. His publisher, HarperCollins, said the 86-year-old writer died suddenly and peacefully. From Kane and Abel to Adam and Eve Published in 1979, Kane and Abel-the sprawling saga of two men born on the same day in 1906, William Lowell Kane, the son of a wealthy Boston banking family, and Abel Rosnovski, a Polish immigrant who escapes a Siberian labour camp and builds a hotel empire-made Archer a household name around the world, especially in India, where the novel was, for many, their first introduction to adult fiction. His final book, Adam and Eve, out today, returns to the idea of two lives beginning on the same day at opposite ends of society a shepherds son and an earls daughter, both born on Armistice Day 1918. As the only son of an ailing journalist in Weston-super-Mare who became Baron Archer of Weston-super-Mare, Archer had lived on both ends of the spectrum. He was one of the few novelists who could claim that his life was almost as eventful as the plot of his books. He was a member of Parliament at 29, nearly bankrupt at 34, a millionaire novelist by 40 and a prisoner at 61. Everyone goes through several highs and lows in their lives, he told The Indian Express in Pune in 2016. Mine are just more public. Archer and India His books have sold more than 300 million copies and have been published in 114 countries, according to his official website, but he himself admitted that no country quite embraced him like India. From 2008 he toured almost every year, often launching books here before their British release. In 2011 he began the world tour for Only Time Will Tell in Bangalore, and Nielsen BookScan figures showed it as the fifth-bestselling novel in India that year, with more than 48,000 copies sold. Fifty million Indians have read Kane and Abel, he liked to say. In America, two to three hundred might turn up for a talk and book-signing in India its two to three thousand. He was struck by how young those crowds were. Of the 1,000 people who came to hear him in Bangalore in 2013, he said, 80 per cent were under 20. After travelling through the country and reading writers such as R K Narayan and Vikram Seth, eventually, India worked its way into his fiction. Six chapters of Cometh the Hour 2016 are set in Bombay. Indian readers were stoked to get their own cover featuring the Gateway of India. His 2010 anthology, Thereby Hangs a Tale, includes a story about a Delhi couple who fall in love at a traffic signal. Fans were hoping that Archer would also write a sprawling novel set in India, but Archer dashed down the possibility. I just dont have the knowledge, he said in 2013. I will be foolish to write about something I do not understand. While he enjoyed India and its people, he also had his moments of frustration, piracy being a sore point. In 2016, he said he found a street vendor selling a copy of Agatha Christies Passenger to Frankfurt under his name. He also accused Bollywood producers of stealing his plots, saying Rakesh Roshans Khudgarz borrowed from Kane and Abel, and Yash Raj Films Ladies vs Ricky Bahl from Not a Penny More, Not a Penny Less. They should, of course, contact my agent, he said. A life stranger than fiction Jeffrey Howard Archer was born in London on April 15, 1940. His father, William, was 64 at his birth and died when Jeffrey was a teenager. Archer later claimed his father had been a colonel in the Somerset Light Infantry. In a 1988 unauthorised biography, In for a Penny, Jonathan Mantle writes that the regiment found no connection. Archer went to Wellington School in Somerset and then to Oxford for a one-year diploma in education where he won an athletics Blue, running the 100 yards in 9.6 seconds for Britain in 1966. Archers political career began in 1966 when he was elected to the Greater London Council. In 1969, at the age of 29, he became the Conservative member of Parliament for Louth. However, in a rags-to-riches-and-back-to-rags story, a disastrous investment in a Canadian company, Aquablast, left him deep in debt, and he left the Commons in 1974. To pay what he owed, he wrote Not a Penny More, Not a Penny Less 1976, about four men swindled in a share scam who set out to win their money back. Kane and Abel followed in 1979, and there was no looking back. His newfound popularity reopened doors and brought him back into politics. Margaret Thatcher made him deputy chairman of the Conservative Party in 1985. However, he resigned in 1986 after a newspaper reported that an associate had paid money to a sex worker. Later,he sued the Daily Star over the allegations and won 500,000 in damages. He was made a life peer in 1992, and in 1999 he became the Conservative candidate for Mayor of London. However, again, he had to withdraw after a former friend revealed that Archer had asked him to provide a false alibi for the 1987 trial. He was convicted of perjury and, in 2001, sentenced to four years. His Prison Diaries He spent less than a month in Belmarsh, a high-security prison in London, before moving to Wayland in Norfolk and then North Sea Camp in Lincolnshire, before beingreleased in 2003. Writing 2,000 to 3,000 words a day in his cell, he produced A Prison Diary in three volumes Hell, Purgatory and Heaven. His first night at Wayland left him, he wrote, as low as I did during my first night at Belmarsh. I thought I had escaped from hell. So much for purgatory. After being released, he was as prolific as ever. The seven-volume Clifton Chronicles 201116 was, he said, pretty autobiographical A lot of me in Harry, my wife is Emma, my mother is Maisie. The William Warwick detective series came next. He retired from the House of Lords in 2024. Adam and Eve, about an earls daughter and a shepherds son both born on Armistice Day 1918, was always meant to be his last novel. He was signing copies for readers in London the day before he died. His detractors dismissed his prose as workmanlike, and Archer never claimed otherwise. I am not a writer, he said in Pune. I am a storyteller. I try to make people turn pages about what will happen next. Asked in 2013 what kept him going, he said The fear of stopping. I cant stop. He is survived by his wife of 60 years, Dame Mary Archer, a chemist who chaired Cambridge University Hospitals and the Science Museum Group their sons, William and James and five grandchildren. On one visit to Mumbai, a boy selling pirated books on the street asked him whether he wanted the latest Jeffrey Archer. Archer told him he was the latest Jeffrey Archer.

articleTitle: CBI probe order against Mann’s aide: Punjab takes fight to Supreme Court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Punjab CBI probe HC order Bhagwant Mann OSD
description: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has directed the CBI to probe Enforcement Directorate allegations against people linked to Bhagwant Mann’s office.
body_raw: The Punjab government has moved the Supreme Court challenging the Punjab and Haryana High Courts October 5 order directing the CBI to register a case and investigate allegations made by the Enforcement Directorate ED against people linked to Chief Minister Bhagwant Manns office. The state filed a special leave petition SLP against the high court order at 1.42 am on Tuesday. The matter is now expected to come up before the Supreme Court. We are waiting for the petition to be admitted, a government functionary said, confirming the development. The high court had on Monday directed the CBI to conduct a fair and transparent investigation into allegations contained in an ED communication to the Punjab director general of police DGP and submit its report within two months. The case is scheduled to come up before the high court on December 7. The ED had sought registration of a case against Manns Officer on Special Duty Rajbir Singh Ghuman and his alleged associates Nitin Gohal and Bir Devinder. What the ED alleged In its communication to the DGP under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act on July 30, the ED sought registration of a criminal case on the basis of material allegedly indicating cash-for-transfers and postings, influence over government policies and tenders, leakage of confidential government documents and other favours. According to the allegations cited by the ED, Ghuman, Gohal and Devinder had allegedly interfered in transfers and postings of government officials, government work and tender processes. The agency had also referred to material purportedly indicating attempts to influence postings, access confidential government documents, and interfere in administrative approvals and other official processes. What the high court said The high court order came on a PIL filed by advocate Nikhil Saraf, based on the ED communication sent to the DGP. The court noted that the communication was received in the DGPs office on August 3 and was marked to the Punjab Bureau of Investigation, but no FIR had been registered even after two months. While directing the CBI to register a case, the division bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor said the allegations would have to be tested during investigation and trial. Prima facie allegations with regard to scams including cash for transfers cash for getting favourable policies cash for tenders, and such other illegal activities corruption in high public offices have been substantiated by the ED with reference to various WhatsApp chats and other information, the bench had observed. The court, however, made it clear that it was not expressing any final view on the allegations. Merits of the allegation can only be gone into at the stage of investigationtrial and we are not required to express any definite opinion on it, it said. The bench had further held that the material supplied by the ED was not merely an expression of its opinion but was supported by material on the basis of which the agency had formed its view about possible violations of law.

articleTitle: 2032 Olympic emblem officially revealed after it was leaked
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The organising committee had an official launch on Monday, just a few days after it had to hastily convene a new conference to explain the accidental leaking ahead of schedule, the 2032 organizing committee held an official launch on Monday. (Brisbane Olympics organising committee)
description: The Olympic emblem is the crest of a pink cockatoo, an Australian bird, with the color stylized to resemble an Olympic and Paralympic flame, and a shape to resemble the host state of Queensland.
body_raw: Days after an explainer video inadvertently going live resulted in emblem of the 2032 Olympics and Paralympics getting leaked, the organisers have now officially unveiled it. The cockatoo has come out as the winner for the emblem, prevailing over the kangaroo and Koala. The Olympic emblem is the crest of a pink cockatoo, an Australian bird, with the color stylized to resemble an Olympic and Paralympic flame, and a shape to resemble the host state of Queensland. The organising committee had an official launch on Monday, just a few days after it had to hastily convene a new conference to explain the accidental leaking ahead of schedule, the 2032 organizing committee held an official launch on Monday. Brisbane 2032 vice president Tim Mander and chief marketing officer Brent Hill told the weekend news conference the accidental release was a pleasant surprise. Hill embraced the unexpected opportunity, saying the publicity has been incredible. Ahead of the community launch Monday evening in the downtown Southbank parklands, Brisbane 2032 chairman Andrew Liveris said the emblems are an opportunity to promote the unique character of a Games, inviting the world to learn more, visit, invest and be part of an event unlike any other. Lachlan Kennedy, the Brisbane sprinter who set an Australian record for the 100 meters when he ran 9.85 seconds at the Commonwealth Games at Glasgow in July, attended the emblem lauch and told local TV broadcasters I love it. I think it represents Brisbane well. Its unique, he said, I think its got soul to it. For Mikaela Cojuangco Jaworski, who heads the IOCs coordination commission for the 2032 Games, the emblems represented a vibrant expression of the nature and character of the region. The Olympics and Paralympics will be centered on the state capital, Brisbane, but cities across the state, including the Gold Coast and the Sunshine Coast, will host competitions. Australia has twice previously hosted the Summer Olympics, at Melbourne in 1956 and at Sydney in 2000. The Sydney emblem design contained representations of famous landmarks including the Sydney Opera House, the citys famous harbor and beaches, as well as boomerangs, sun and rocks. Brisbanes Lord Mayor Adrian Schrinner on Monday said the emblems are a celebration of our city, our lifestyle. They reflect the Brisbane that people know and love vibrant, resilient, connected, friendly, playful and a little bit cheeky, Schrinner said. They are also a symbol of the excitement building across our city. With just under six years to go, we are already preparing to welcome the world to Australias lifestyle capital. Organizers said First Nations elements were contained within the emblems, with cockatoos seen as messengers carrying cultural meaning and linking people to place, story and ceremony. The emblems are separate to the Games mascot, which will be revealed closer to the Games. An explainer video meant to go live after a planned ceremonial event briefly appeared on the events YouTube channel on Friday night. Screenshots of images and text soon circulated on social media. With Agency inputs

articleTitle: Namma Metro’s original fleet overhaul: What it means for Bengaluru passengers
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bengaluru Metro Namma Metro fleet overhaul BMRCL
description: Bengaluru Metro will introduce more than 20 new trains to ensure service reliability during the overhaul programme.
body_raw: In its first major overhaul since commercial operations began in 2011, Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited BMRCL is refurbishing its original fleet of 57 trains. The initiative comes as Namma Metros initial rakes have covered over 10 lakh km of service across the city. Since launching its inaugural 6.7-km stretch between M G Road and Byappanahalli on October 20, 2011, Bengalurus metro network has expanded to 96 km across the Purple Line 43.5 km, Green Line 33.5 km, and Yellow Line 19.2 km. Night-time maintenance The maintenance programme will target the 57 trains currently operating across the Purple and Green Lines. Standard mid-life overhauls are typically performed after approximately 15 years of service, ahead of more extensive life-cycle overhauls conducted later in a trains operational lifespan. BMRCL confirmed that the refurbishment will not impact daily passenger schedules. A detailed technical inspection and component replacement would be carried out. This will not affect routine journeys, as the refurbishment is being carried out during night hours, after operational hours. Also, there is rolling stock which would help withdraw the existing trains from service for maintenance, a BMRCL officer said. The maintenance involves technical assessments, followed by repairs or replacements of worn components. According to BMRCL, inspections will cover traction motors, drive systems, wheels, axles, braking assemblies, electrical equipment, wiring cables, batteries, onboard electronics, signalling, and control systems. As for passenger comfort and safety, inspections will cover air-conditioning and ventilation units, doors, passenger safety mechanisms, seats, interiors, and coach equipment. It will also cover renewal of damaged or aged safety-critical components based on technical evaluation. To maintain fleet reliability, BMRCL is inducting new rakes manufactured by the Titagarh-China Railway Rolling Stock Corporation CRRC consortium. Four new trains have already arrived, with 21 additional trains scheduled to join the Green Line fleet, providing the cushion needed for the overhaul programme. Contract awarded for Central Silk Board travelator Alongside fleet maintenance, BMRCL is advancing infrastructure upgrades at Central Silk Board station, a key interchange along the upcoming route connecting to Kempegowda International Airport KIA, with the initial Central Silk Board to K R Puram section slated for operation by 2027. BMRCL has awarded a contract worth Rs 55.48 crore to Milan Road Buildtech. The firm will handle civil and structural works for a covered travelator and an interconnected walkway at the Central Silk Board junction.

articleTitle: Orissa High Court upholds divorce over wife’s cruelty but hikes her alimony to Rs 25 lakh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Orissa High court divorce cruelty alimony rs 25 lakh wife
description: The family court granted the husband’s divorce plea in 2022 on grounds of cruelty by the wife and directed him to pay her Rs 16 lakh as permanent alimony.
body_raw: The Orissa High Court recently confirmed a couples divorce on the ground of cruelty by the wife but increased her permanent alimony from Rs 16 lakh to Rs 25 lakh. The court noted that the couple stopped living together within months of their marriage. It also held that once cruelty by the wife was established, the husbands decision to live separately could not be said to be without reasonable cause. Chief Justice Harish Tandon and Justice Chittaranjan Dash were hearing the appeal filed by the wife challenging the family courts order of May 2022. The family court had allowed the husbands plea to end the marriage and ordered him to pay Rs 16 lakh as permanent alimony. Once the course of matrimonial cruelty established against the appellant wife is taken into account, it cannot be said that the respondent husbands withdrawal from her society was without reasonable cause, the October 1 order read. Started living separately within few months The woman claimed to have married in July 2017 with her estranged husband. It was added that their marriage did not continue for long and the couple have been living separately since February 2017. The husband filed for divorce in 2020, citing cruelty. The wife opposed the plea and later filed an application seeking to resume the marriage. The family court eventually granted the husband a divorce, rejected the wifes plea to resume the marriage and ordered him to pay Rs 16 lakh as permanent alimony. Aggrieved, she filed an appeal before the Orissa High Court challenging the family courts May 2022 order. Arguments The wife, through senior advocate A Mohanty, submitted that the finding of cruelty based on the allegation that the woman was accustomed to a lavish lifestyle could not by itself constitute matrimonial cruelty. He further argued that the serious allegations made by the wife regarding demand of money, physical and mental harassment and other matrimonial misconduct had not been properly appreciated. On the contrary, the man, through advocate A K Sarangi, submitted that the matrimonial relationship had become irretrievably strained within a short period of the marriage. He added that the couple had been living separately since February 2017 and repeated efforts at reconciliation had failed. He also supported the amount awarded towards permanent alimony, based on the income and financial circumstances of the husband. Not on talking terms The high court noted that the marriage had lasted only a few months before the couple stopped living together. It also noted that the wife had admitted that although they had lived together as husband and wife until February 2017, they were not even on talking terms afterwards. The court clarified that differences in financial background, standard of living or lifestyle cannot by themselves amount to matrimonial cruelty. The relevance of these circumstances is only in understanding the actual matrimonial dynamics between the parties, it added. The court upheld the divorce, noting the long period of separation, lack of communication, repeated but unsuccessful efforts at reconciliation, serious allegations exchanged by the couple and the overall course of their relationship. It held that these circumstances amounted to mental cruelty. On alimony, the court considered the husbands income, expenses and liabilities, the wifes professional qualifications and previous employment, as well as her current unemployment. It said the amount needed a reasonable enhancement and increased the total permanent alimony to Rs 25 lakh.

articleTitle: Multiple groups, moving crowds: Why CEC protest became a challenge for Delhi Police
articleFeaturedImageAlt: delhi cec protest
description: The agitation has seen student activists, politicians and civil society members making repeated attempts to march towards ‘restricted areas’ in Central Delhi over the past four days.
body_raw: What began as a protest planned at Delhis Jantar Mantar on October 2 against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar has, over the past four days, spread across central Delhi, with multiple groups attempting to march amid prohibitory orders and the Delhi Police registering more than nine FIRs. The police response has included denying permission for the march and deploying paramilitary personnel, local police from eight police stations in the New Delhi district and personnel from the Delhi Police Reserve Battalion. All roads leading to Jantar Mantar in the New Delhi district were also fortified with barricades and police personnel. According to a police officer, the agitation has not been confined to a single conventional demonstration but has involved political parties, student organisations, activists, lawyers and other groups attempting to march towards restricted areas in central Delhi. The challenge is not merely about preventing a crowd from entering Jantar Mantar, which is already heavily fortified. It is about controlling multiple moving groups, preventing attempts to breach barricades, managing detentions and, simultaneously, dealing with a large number of people recording events on mobile phones and cameras, the officer said. httpswww.youtube.comwatch?v-Hjn02Ty0kfeatureyoutu.be Advisory for media persons The protests have also brought journalists into closer contact with police operations, prompting the police to issue an advisory on Monday. This came after three women journalists alleged that they were harassed by police personnel while covering the protests. Their complaints have been transferred to the Crime Branch for investigation. The police advisory asked journalists to carry either an identity card issued by their organisation or valid PIBDIP accreditation and, importantly, to keep it visibly displayed. Journalists were to ensure that their presence does not obstruct police operations or the movement of law-enforcement personnel. They were also asked to maintain a reasonable and safe distance during tense situations and to position themselves so that they are clearly distinguishable from protesters. Another police officer said the advisory was an attempt to create a clearer operational distinction between those covering the protest and those participating in it. Because many of those protesting also sometimes start making videos, with a mic and mobile phone camera, it becomes extremely difficult for us to distinguish between an actual journalist and activists, the officer said. Lessons from CJPs July protest The Cockroach Janta Party CJP, which staged a massive protest in July demanding the resignation of then Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak, was given permission to hold a one-day protest at Jantar Mantar. A Delhi Police officer of DCP rank handed over the permission letter to CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke at the Delhi Airport. The protesters, however, did not leave Jantar Mantar after the first day and returned for a second round of demonstrations. Delhi Police officers have acknowledged that they had underestimated the number of people who might turn up in support of the CJP. This time, the police have taken measures to prevent protesters from reaching Jantar Mantar. After the July protest ended following the resignation of Pradhan, Delhi Police officials underwent anti-protest counselling and were advised to remain calm, composed and patient while dealing with protesters and crowds. During the current protests, very few Delhi Police personnel have been seen carrying batons. Paramilitary personnel have mostly been seen carrying tear-gas shells. Many Delhi Police personnel have also been seen without name-plate badges while dealing with protesters. Sources claimed some personnel avoid wearing them because they do not want to be identified and subsequently trolled on social media.

articleTitle: Sonos Play review: A premium portable speaker that sounds superb
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sonos Play review
description: A premium portable speaker with excellent sound and smart software, the Sonos Play suits buyers already invested in the ecosystem.
body_raw: If actors have their entourage, I have a backpack full of gadgets that I may or may not use on a work trip, but I like to lug them around anyway. These days, even security staff ask me what I would do with so many devices, and I simply smile. In fact, when I was returning from San Francisco last week, a security staff member noticed the Sonos Play I had with me and asked me to play the late Dolly Partons I Will Always Love You on the speaker. I think the staff liked the Sonos Play. I am sure you may be wondering why I carry a portable speaker with me. Well, I start my day listening to music and end it with music. Hotel rooms can get lonely at times, and music helps me feel happy and comforted. The Sonos Play is portable, but depending on where you put it, the sound it produces comes close to what you hear from home speakers. But of course, Sonos Play is a very different beast designed to be mobile, but at the same time it can be part of your home entertainment system if you live within Sonos ecosystem. With a brand-new Sonos 27 operating system, a redone app and the Play portable speaker, they complement each other, and I tested them over several weeks. Heres my review of the Sonos Play. What Sonos Play  Price Rs 35,999 Differentiated design Ive been a Sonos fan since the brands inception. The way it designs its speakers and audio products reminds me of Apple in the 2000s. Sonos avoids cheaply designed products and instead uses a design language that is part Japanese and part American, with fine detailing that also has a touch of European finesse. The Play follows the design of a compact bookshelf speaker. I could see how Sonos has taken bits and pieces from the Move 2 and the Era 100 and incorporated them into the Play. What I liked about the Sonos Play is that it has a rugged feel, but you wouldnt immediately notice it. The speaker has heft its dense, and you get the sense its built with premium internals. At 1.3 kg, the Play isnt featherlight, but I had no trouble travelling with it. However, after using the Play for weeks, I feel the speaker is designed for home use, an apartment balcony, or a friends place. The speaker has a minimalist design and clean looks, and it blends effortlessly wherever you put it, whether thats a hotel room, bedroom, kitchen or living space. Its like a luxury T-shirt with no visible logos understated and a premium bespoke experience. The oval-shaped speaker, which came in black for my review unit, is also available in white. It has a rubberised top with playback buttons, volume controls, and a button to activate a voice assistant. You can choose between Sonos own voice assistant and Amazon Alexa. It also has a dedicated Bluetooth button and a hardware microphone switch to turn the microphone on or off. A small LED cluster on top indicates the connection, battery, microphone, and mute status. The Play is primarily a Wi-Fi-based speaker, but it also supports Bluetooth 5.3 for use away from home, allowing you to stream music from your phone or another device. The speaker has a large 35Wh battery that you can easily replace at home. It offers up to 24 hours of Bluetooth playback and easily lasts a full day of Wi-Fi listening at 65 per cent volume. The portable speaker sits on its wireless charging base, but can be easily lifted and carried outdoors. No cables or setup hassles needed. Sadly, the USB-C power adapter isnt, so you need to buy an 18W charger separately or greater USB-C power adaptor, which needs to be 45W to support fast charging. I used my iPhone charger, and it works, but you still need a dedicated charger just for the Play. Ecosystem advantage and the brand new Sonos 27 OS Perhaps the biggest advantage of getting the Play is its integration with the Sonos ecosystem. If you buy the Play, you can easily integrate it with the rest of your Sonos speakers and products. In my case, Sonos provided two Play units, which I grouped together just like other Sonos speakers for multi-room audio. With support for virtually any music streaming service, you can stream music over the internet and control playback through the Sonos app, Spotify Connect, or Apple AirPlay 2. You can also link two Play speakers together to create a stereo pair. And thats exactly what I did. Everything changed the moment the second Play was up and running. It took me less than 10 minutes to set up the second Play and pair the speakers. More on the audio experience later. Beyond reviewing the Play, I was keen to test the new Sonos 27 operating system and the redesigned app. The app recently received a major redesign alongside the launch of the Sonos 27 audio operating system. Adding a speaker from the get-go is easy, with the app automatically detecting it. You can also add surround speakers and subwoofers through the app with just a few taps. The app shows your entire Sonos system and, separately, your rooms. You can go into each room to add or remove speakers, and you can easily switch audio from one room to another, as long as the speakers support Sonos 27. Whats great about Sonos 27 is that it brings together your music services and controls, including Spotify, Apple Music, Bluetooth, AirPlay, voice commands, and AI assistance, under one operating system. It features Sonos Voice, which lets you ask Sonos for what you want using natural voice conversations. It also supports AI assistants such as Claude and Gemini to help you play music around your home and interact with your Sonos system. In the future, the new operating system will allow users to create their own AI agents. Sonos 27 is an interesting proposition if you already live within the Sonos ecosystem, much like many of us do within Apples ecosystem. It all comes down to how much you are willing to invest in Sonos products, because the more you add, the more youll see the advantages of Sonos 27. Exceptional audio quality The Sonos Play features three Class-H digital amplifiers, two angled tweeters, and a single mid-woofer for a balanced sound. It also supports automatic Trueplay tuning, which adjusts the EQ based on the room, while the Sonos app lets you manually tweak the bass, treble, and loudness. I spent most of my time testing the single unit of the Play, listening to music. It has that signature Sonos sound that I am familiar with, having reviewed almost every Sonos product over the past few years. But, frankly, there is no real sweet spot when it comes to the Play. What I think Sonos has nailed is that, no matter where you put the speaker in a room, you get the same sound everywhere. I cant explain how good music sounds on the Play, since its also very subjective. That said, the Play offers excellent tonal separation, well-defined mids, detailed highs, and punchy bass. Vocals sound impressive too, although I felt the speaker lacks deep bass. When I set up two Plays as a stereo pair bringing the total cost to Rs 71,998, I was immediately impressed. Using two speakers in stereo is wonderful, and the improvement in sound quality was immediately noticeable. The Play already does a great job delivering clear sound from anywhere in the room, but two speakers in stereo added a ton of detail and depth that was missing from the mono output of a single Play. Final verdict The Sonos Play sounds remarkably good for its compact size, and it looks great on a shelf or countertop. But it certainly isnt cheap. Sure, it may be one of the best-sounding portable speakers on the market, but its also smart and easy to use. With Sonos 27, the new app, long software support and a replaceable battery, Sonos is certainly moving in the right direction. The Play comes close to being the perfect portable speaker, but it still lacks spatial audio support and Dolby Atmos.

articleTitle: GST process reforms pin hope on data, tech to ensure compliance
articleFeaturedImageAlt: GST
description: Ease of doing business in focus: from no arrest, minimum sentencing removal to Rs 10,000-threshold for notices
body_raw: The GST Councils meeting on Wednesday will take up the second half of the reform exercise that was kicked off by the Goods and Services Tax GST rate cuts announced in September 2025, with officials saying the process reforms on the agenda will cement the indirect tax regime for the next half a decade or so. Officials are also of the view that systems built on technology and good quality data can help ensure correct behaviour from businesses without onerous compliance. GST rates were cleaned up last year. Now, the focus is on moving towards a stable tax system with predictability, as was the demand from the industry. It may take a year or two to stabilise and then the GST regime will only require minor tweaks for the next 5-6 years, an official said. If the proposals are approved by the Council, then the framework will be set, the official added. No arrest, notices threshold A key proposal in the process reforms that will be discussed in the Council meeting on October 8 is going to be the removal of the power to arrest by GST officers, as reported by The Indian Express on Sunday. This power, officials said, has led to the creation of unnecessary leverage over businesses even before the actual arrest stage is reached. Tax disputes will be resolved through civil consequences, namely recovery of the tax, interest for the delay, and penalty, the official said. However, prosecution will remain available, with the GST Council expected to discuss some tweaks. Additionally, the threshold for prosecution is likely to be increased from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore. The sentencing provisions are also proposed to be softened, with the minimum sentence likely to be removed altogether. This, officials said, means courts wont be bound to impose a term of imprisonment regardless of circumstances. Also, a fine will be available as an option in every case. Furthermore, it is proposed that no notice will be issued at all where the amount involved is below Rs 10,000. Crucially, this change is expected to apply to new cases as well as those pending, whether in adjudication or in the appeal phase. Such cases are about a fifth of all cases by number and a negligible part of the money. For a small business, a notice of this size costs more to answer in fees and time than the amount in dispute. Removing that category will be a real relief, and will free up officers for matters of substance, the official said. Redesign of processes The GST Council will deliberate on a wide variety of issues on October 7 that encompass all the tax dealings of an entity during its lifecycle - getting registered, filing returns and correcting them, claiming refunds, and answering demands. All four processes are proposed to be redesigned on a single principle, namely that the system should do what can be done from data and the officer should be left with what needs judgement, an official said. One major process change is set to be for the export of services, which will help align GST laws with the practice on ground. Citing the example of a testing laboratory which receives a prototype from a foreign client, tests it, sends back the report, and is paid in foreign exchange, the official explained that the place of supply followed where the work was performed. It will now follow the location of the customer, and such work therefore qualifies as an export. This opens the whole field of testing, certification, repair, calibration, research, and analysis to export treatment, and India has substantial capacity in all of them. Wednesdays GST Council meeting comes over 13 months after the last one in September 2025 which announced the major rate overhaul that saw the number of tax slabs being reduced to 5 and 18, with a 40 rate for demerit goods. There have been no meetings of the GST Council in the interim, but discussions have been ongoing to bring all stakeholders on the same page, and that takes time. What has helped is that there have not been any major concerns about revenues being adversely impacted by the rate rationalisation exercise of September 2025. This has made it easier to go ahead with the process reforms discussions at this weeks meeting.

articleTitle: World Bank raises India’s FY27 GDP growth forecast to 7.1%
articleFeaturedImageAlt: the world bank
description: The World Bank has also sounded a warning on the AI and demographic front for the South Asia region, calling for faster job creation, building old-age income support and health systems before aging pressures peak, and strengthening workforce skills.
body_raw: The World Bank has raised its GDP growth forecast for India for the current fiscal by half a percentage point to 7.1, with this rapid expansion seen driving the broader South Asia region. According to the multilateral organisations twice-yearly South Asia Economic Update, released on Tuesday, the South Asia regions GDP in 2026 is seen expanding by 6.9, up from the previous forecast of 6.3. However, excluding India, regional growth is seen 3.6, down from 4.1 earlier, mostly because of a large downward revision for Bangladesh. The World Bank expects the strong momentum in industry and services to continue, with the reforms that have been undertaken-consolidation of labour codes, Goods and Services Tax GST reforms, rationalisation of tariffs, the bankruptcy and insolvency act, and physical and digital infrastructure investments-keeping the growth potential strong. Strength in the rest of the economy is expected to make up for agricultural weakness, the World Bank said, adding that the sub-par monsoons will likely reduce agricultural output and rural demand while increasing food inflation. This will add to existing pressure from higher energy prices. In 2027-28, the World Bank expects the Indian economy to grow by 7.2. The upward revision to the growth forecast by the World Bank comes a day before the Reserve Bank of India RBI announces its interest rate decision, with economists widely expecting the Monetary Policy Committee MPC to vote in favour of a 25-basis-point increase in the repo rate to 5.5. Slated to be released at 10am on Wednesday, the MPCs statement may also show the RBI having raised its own growth forecast for 2026-27 to around 7 from 6.7. With Indias growth exceeding expectations for some time now, numerous economists and organisations have raised their forecasts in light of the rapid April-June growth rate of 7.8. On September 23, four international agencies-SP Global Ratings, Fitch Ratings, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development OECD, and the Asian Development Bank ADB-hiked their growth forecast for the current fiscal by 4080 bps to 6.97.1. Demography, AI warnings In what will concern policymakers in South Asia, the World Bank warned that the regions demographic tailwinds are beginning to fade, with growth in the working-age population seen dropping from 2.2 per year during 19602023 to 0.6 over the next 25 years. South Asias transition to an aged population is unusually compressed. Most South Asian countries will complete this transition at income levels below those at which other emerging economies even began it, the World Bank said, adding that the best policy response is to address labour markets and aging simultaneously rather than sequentially. The South Asia Economic Update report, titled Adopting AI for Growth, also noted that only 23 of Indian firms report using AI, almost half of US 43. But this comparison does not take into account the differences in the type of AI technology used or how well it is embedded in business operations. As per the World Banks AI Adoption Index-which considers factors such as purchases of AI software by firms, the number of uses of advanced AI technologies, core business functions using AI, among others-the figure for India is 0.27. This is less than a third of the US figure of 0.85. While Indian companies started adopting AI late, they have been catching up with their American counterparts over the past two years when it comes to basic AI adoption. Worryingly, the World Bank found that expected gains from AI are concentrated in a few Indian firms, with almost 75 expecting almost no productivity benefit at all. In fact, 15 of firms expect faster AI development to reduce their revenue per worker by up to 10, likely because they expect to lose market share to firms that have an advantage in deploying AI rapidly. The adoption of AI has the potential to transform South Asias development trajectory by boosting labor productivity, expanding export opportunities, and improving public service delivery. But to reap these benefits, governments need to address the foundational gaps that hold back adoption, said Franziska Ohnsorge, World Bank Group Chief Economist for Asia.

articleTitle: Noel Tata blasts 2 dissenters, repeats ‘no mandatory listing’ claim
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Tata trust
description: The four trustees of the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust launched an attack on Trusts Vice-chairmen Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh, accusing them of abandoning collective decisions, airing personal views in the media, and allegedly breaching their fiduciary duties.
body_raw: The Reserve Bank of Indias RBIs communication on Tata Sons application to surrender its registration has, rather than weakened, strengthened the position of Tata Trusts and does not ask Tata Sons to pursue a listing, Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata and three trustees said. In a letter to Trusts Vice-chairmen Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh on Monday, Noel Tata and trustees Darius Khambata, Neville N Tata and Bhaskar Bhat argued that the RBIs communication did not overturn decisions taken in 2025, as it merely declined Tata Sons application and neither mandated a listing nor prescribed any specific course of action. The four trustees said the RBIs communication instead made it more urgent to find a lawful alternative to listing that would meet the settled objective of the Trusts and Tata Sons. The proposal outlined in their letter, they said, would, if implemented, take Tata Sons outside the regulatory category on which the RBIs communication was based. The Tata Trusts did what the Board of Tata Sons asked of them. The proposal set out in the Letter gives effect to the decisions unanimously taken by SDTT and SRTT on May 28, 2025 and July 28, 2025, which both of you joined, the letter said. It was sent to the Chairman of Tata Sons for the consideration of the Board and for submission to the RBI, which is exactly the course the Board itself had agreed, they said. Far from usurping the functions of the Tata Sons board, the Trusts responded to its request, they said. Whatever view is taken of the resolutions passed at the meeting of September 17, and the Trusts position on the resolution concerning the Chairman is well known, the request for the Trusts guidance was made by Tata Sons, not by the Trusts, the letter said. The four trustees of the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust SDTT launched an attack on Srinivasan and Singh, accusing them of abandoning collective decisions, airing personal views in the media, and allegedly breaching their fiduciary duties. Credibility of opposition under question They questioned the credibility of Srinivasan and Singhs opposition to the Trusts stand on Tata Sons. The four trustees effectively tell the two vice-chairmen you cant first participate in unanimous decisions to keep Tata Sons unlisted and then champion listing without taking the matter back to the Trusts. Their accusation is summed up in one caustic phrase. The trustees referred to the two mens changed position in April 2026 as their epiphanies, saying they suddenly decided that listing was good for Tata Sons and its minority shareholders. Singh and Srinivasan had last week questioned Tata Trusts for sending Tata Sons reorganisation proposal without consulting them. Neville is the son of Noel Tata. They alleged that the two did not raise their changed position at any of the three SDTT meetings held after April. You chose not to raise your changed view for collective deliberation with your co-trustees, the trustees said, arguing that the conduct undermined the Trusts resolutions, as also the pending application made by Tata Sons to the RBI and amounted to a breach of your fiduciary duties. The letter makes clear that for the trustees, the dispute is not a mere difference of opinion. They are questioning whether Srinivasan and Singh acted consistently with their responsibilities as trustees. Past decisions on Tata Sons listing The issue stems from a series of unanimous decisions taken by the Trusts and Tata Sons over the past two years. In March 2024, the Tata Sons board, with Srinivasan and Singh then serving as Tata Trust-nominated directors, unanimously decided that Tata Sons should remain unlisted. Tata Sons repaid borrowings and redeemed preference shares aggregating about Rs 20,000 crore and applied to the RBI to surrender registration. On May 28, 2025, SDTT and Sir Ratan Tata Trust, with the participation of both Srinivasan and Singh, unanimously authorised the Tata Sons chairman to explore every available route to preserve its unlisted status, including discussions with the Shapoorji Pallonji Group. Two months later, on July 28, the two trusts again unanimously resolved that it should remain unlisted and engage with the RBI to achieve that objective. The four trustees now ask What happened to those decisions? Those resolutions have not been rescinded, they said. Nor does the record show that either Srinivasan or Singh asked the trustees to reconsider them or proposed that the Trusts should now support listing, they said. Charity Commissioner proceedings The trustees expressed significant concerns over the duos Charity Commissioner proceedings. They accused them of adopting a contradictory position demanding collective deliberation while approaching the Charity Commissioner to prevent the trust from meeting. The trustees said the duo filed complaints on September 25, seeking, among other things, directions preventing SDTT from convening meetings or acting through circular resolutions. They also sought restrictions concerning the Trust chairmans participation in Tata Sons matters and asked that the composition of the SDTT board be frozen. The response is scathing. We find it difficult. to reconcile the concern expressed in your letter, that SDTT should act only after deliberation at meetings of its trustees, the four trustees said, with the fact that the two had already asked the regulator to prevent the trustees from meeting at all. They said they would hope that, given the refreshing spirit of your letter, both complaints will now be withdrawn. Srinivasans conduct as Tata Sons director The letter also takes direct aim at Srinivasans conduct as a Tata Sons director. According to the trustees, SDTT had passed a circular resolution on September 16 asking Srinivasan not to participate in or vote on any item concerning the listing of Tata Sons. Srinivasan declined, maintaining that the Trust could not dictate how he exercised his judgment as a director. The trustees then accuse him of ignoring an earlier SDTT decision concerning the appointment of a new Tata Sons chairman. On August 13, SDTT had resolved to initiate the constitution of a Selection Committee under Article 118 of Tata Sons Articles of Association, they said. Yet, at the September 17 board meeting, Srinivasan voted for the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as chairman, despite the absence of a recommendation from the Selection Committee and against the vote of the Trust chairman. The four trustees said this effectively neutralised the affirmative rights granted to Tata Trust-nominated directors under Articles 118 and 121. The broader battle, however, is over Tata Sons future. The Trusts insist that the September 28 proposal was not an attempt to override the Tata Sons board. Rather, they said it was a response to a request made by the board itself after the RBI rejected Tata Sons application to surrender its registration. The letter ends with a clear challenge to Srinivasan and Singh if they genuinely want to protect Tata Sons, they should come forward with a better alternative to listing. If indeed you have anything constructive to offer, we would welcome your considered suggestions on means to avoid listing that are better than set out in the Letter. That challenge captures the extraordinary nature of the Tata Trusts internal battle. The dispute is no longer a quiet disagreement over corporate strategy. It has become a direct contest over fiduciary duty, institutional authority and who gets to speak for the Trusts. For the Tata Group, whose governance model has long been built around trusteeship and institutional continuity, the spectacle of trustees publicly accusing other trustees of abandoning collective decisions is deeply unsettling, said an observer. The question now is not merely whether Tata Sons will remain unlisted. It is whether the Tata Trusts can resolve a bitter internal battle over who has the authority to decide its future - and whose fiduciary duty comes first.

articleTitle: Usha Vance stumbles while carrying baby son off chopper; video goes viral
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Usha Vance falls off helicopter video
description: The moment was captured on video and has sparked debate on social media over whether anyone nearby should have stepped in to help Usha Vance.
body_raw: US Vice President J D Vances wife, Usha Vance, had a brief scare while stepping off a helicopter in Maryland Monday, appearing to lose her balance as she descended the stairs with her nine-week-old son strapped to her chest. She quickly steadied herself and appeared to reassure those around her that she and Alec Neel Vance were fine. According to USA Today, Usha appeared to stumble after taking two steps down the stairs. She regained her balance and turned towards the helicopter, seemingly indicating to her husband that she was fine. She was later seen smiling and reassuring those around her. The Irish Star reported that Usha told nearby officers, I nearly fell down the stairs. The digital news publication noted that the officers did not appear to move towards her after she stumbled. According to lip reader Nicola Hickling, she also said, Im okay, and hes fine. thank you. Vance soon joined his wife after getting off the aircraft. He was seen carrying their four-year-old daughter, Mirabel. The family was travelling to Anchorage, Alaska, where the Vice President is scheduled to headline a Republican National Committee rally in support of Republican Senator Dan Sullivans re-election campaign against Democrat Mary Peltola, according to USA Today.
